lp.tendsto_of_tendsto_toWeakSpace_one.doc:
**Schur's theorem**: along a countably generated filter, in particular for sequences, weak
convergence in ℓ¹ implies norm convergence.

groupCohomology.map_id_eq_zero_iff_of_co.signature:
groupCohomology.map_id_eq_zero_iff_of_comp_eq_resCoindToHom.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k]
  [Group G] (S : Subgroup G) {Γ : Type u} [Group Γ] {X M : Rep.{u, u, u} k G}
  {B : Rep.{u, u, u} k Γ} {f : ↥S →* Γ} (hf : Function.Bijective ⇑f) {r : Γ →* G}
  (hr : ∀ (s : ↥S), r (f s) = ↑s) (φ : Rep.res r X ⟶ B) (ψ : Rep.res S.subtype X ⟶ Rep.res f B)
  (hψ : (Rep.Hom.hom ψ).toLinearMap = (Rep.Hom.hom φ).toLinearMap) (u : X ⟶ M)
  (e : M ≅ Rep.coind.{u, u, u, u} S.subtype (Rep.res f B))
  (hu : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp u e.hom = Rep.resCoindToHom S.subtype X (Rep.res f B) ψ)
  (n : ℕ) (x : ↑(groupCohomology X n)) :
  (CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom (groupCohomology.map (MonoidHom.id G) u n)) x = 0 ↔
    (CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom (groupCohomology.map r φ n)) x = 0
groupCohomology.map_id_eq_zero_iff_of_co.doc:
**Shapiro's lemma through an identification of the subgroup.** Let `S ≤ G`, let `f : S →* Γ` be
bijective and `r : Γ →* G` restrict back to the inclusion of `S` (`r (f s) = s`), and let
`φ : Res_r X ⟶ B`. Suppose that `u : X ⟶ M`, followed by an isomorphism
`M ≅ Coind_S^G (Res_f B)`, is the adjunct of `φ` read on `S`. Then `u` kills a class of
`Hⁿ(G, X)` exactly when `φ` kills it along `r`. For the semi-local units at a place of a number
field, `Γ` is the local Galois group and `f` identifies the decomposition group with it.

ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap.linearCombinationEquiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {I : Type u_1} (R : Type u_2)
  (M : Type u_3) [TopologicalSpace I] [DiscreteTopology I] [NormedCommRing R]
  [TauCeti.NormedRing.IsTate R] [NormedAddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module R M] [IsBoundedSMul R M]
  [IsUltrametricDist M] [CompleteSpace M] [DecidableEq I] :
  ↥(lp (fun x => M) ⊤) ≃ₗᵢ[R] ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap I R →L[R] M
ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap.linearCombinati.doc:
**The universal property of `C₀(I, R)`.** Over a commutative ring admitting a multiplicative
pseudo-uniformiser, bounded families `I → M` in a complete ultrametric module correspond to
continuous linear maps `C₀(I, R) →L[R] M`, isometrically for the sup norm and the operator norm.
A family `e` is sent to its linear combination map `a ↦ ∑' i, a i • e i`, and a map `u` to its
values `u (single i 1)` at the unit coordinate vectors.

ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap.isCompletelyCon.signature:
ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap.isCompletelyContinuous_diagonalCLM_iff.{u_1, u_3} {I : Type u_1}

    Filter.Tendsto (⇑d) Filter.cofinite (nhds 0)
ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap.isCompletelyCon.doc:
**Serre's criterion for diagonal operators**: over a complete ultrametric nontrivially normed
field, a diagonal operator is completely continuous exactly when its entries tend to zero.

ZMod.unitsEquivPi.doc:
**The Chinese remainder theorem for units**: `(ℤ/n)ˣ` is the product of the unit groups
modulo the prime powers exactly dividing `n`.

ZMod.natCard_nthRoots_prime_pow_eq_natCa.doc:
**Hensel's lemma for `n`-th roots, as a count.** For `n` coprime to the prime `p`, an integer
`a` prime to `p` and `k ≠ 0`, reduction modulo `p` is a bijection from the `n`-th roots of `a`
modulo `p ^ k` to those modulo `p`; so there are equally many.

ZLattice.two_pow_div_factorial_mul_covol.signature:
ZLattice.two_pow_div_factorial_mul_covolume_le_prod_successiveMin_mul_measureReal.{u_1}

  (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E := by volume_tac) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] {K : ConvexBody E}

  2 ^ Module.finrank ℝ E / ↑(Module.finrank ℝ E).factorial * ZLattice.covolume L μ ≤
    (∏ i, ZLattice.successiveMin L K i) * μ.real ↑K
ZLattice.two_pow_div_factorial_mul_covol.doc:
**Minkowski's second theorem**, lower bound, in terms of the successive minima and with real
measures: `2ⁿ / n! · covolume L μ ≤ λ₀ ⋯ λₙ₋₁ · μ.real K`.

ZLattice.two_pow_div_factorial_mul_covol.signature:
ZLattice.two_pow_div_factorial_mul_covolume_le_prod_successiveMin_mul_measure.{u_1} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  [BorelSpace E] (L : Submodule ℤ E) [DiscreteTopology ↥L] [IsZLattice ℝ L]
  (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E := by volume_tac) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] {K : ConvexBody E}
  (hK : 0 ∈ interior ↑K) (hKs : ∀ x ∈ K, -x ∈ K) :
  ENNReal.ofReal
      (2 ^ Module.finrank ℝ E / ↑(Module.finrank ℝ E).factorial * ZLattice.covolume L μ) ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (∏ i, ZLattice.successiveMin L K i) * μ ↑K
ZLattice.two_pow_div_factorial_mul_covol.doc:
**Minkowski's second theorem**, lower bound, in terms of the successive minima. For a full
lattice `L` in a real normed space `E` of dimension `n`, a Haar measure `μ` on `E`, and a convex
body `K` symmetric about `0` with `0` in its interior, the successive minima
`λ i = successiveMin L K i` satisfy `2ⁿ / n! · covolume L μ ≤ λ₀ ⋯ λₙ₋₁ · μ K`.

ZLattice.two_pow_div_factorial_mul_covol.signature:
ZLattice.two_pow_div_factorial_mul_covolume_le_prod_mul_measure.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (L : Submodule ℤ E)
  [DiscreteTopology ↥L] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E := by volume_tac) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure]
  {K : Set E} (hK : Convex ℝ K) (h0 : 0 ∈ K) (hKs : ∀ x ∈ K, -x ∈ K) {ι : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]
  (b : Module.Basis ι ℝ E) (hbL : ∀ (i : ι), b i ∈ L) {a : ι → ℝ} (ha : ∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ a i)
  (hbK : ∀ (i : ι), b i ∈ a i • K) :
  ENNReal.ofReal
      (2 ^ Module.finrank ℝ E / ↑(Module.finrank ℝ E).factorial * ZLattice.covolume L μ) ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (∏ i, a i) * μ K
ZLattice.two_pow_div_factorial_mul_covol.doc:
**Minkowski's second theorem**, lower bound, general form. Let `L` be a discrete `ℤ`-submodule
of an `n`-dimensional real normed space `E`, `μ` a Haar measure on `E`, and `K ⊆ E` convex,
containing `0` and symmetric about it. If `b` is a basis of `E` over `ℝ` made of vectors of `L` and
the nonnegative numbers `a i` satisfy `b i ∈ a i • K`, then `2 ^ n / n! * covolume L μ ≤
(∏ i, a i) * μ K`. The basis already implies that `L` is a full lattice.

A basis attaining the successive minima `λ₀ ≤ ⋯ ≤ λₙ₋₁` of `L` with respect to `K` satisfies the
hypothesis with `a = λ`, which gives the classical form `2ⁿ / n! · covolume L μ ≤
λ₀ ⋯ λₙ₋₁ · μ K`.

ZLattice.thetaSeries.signature:
ZLattice.thetaSeries.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] (L : Submodule ℤ E)
  (τ : UpperHalfPlane) : ℂ
ZLattice.thetaSeries.doc:
The theta series `Θ_L(τ) = ∑_{v ∈ L} exp (π i ‖v‖² τ)` of `L : Submodule ℤ E`. It converges
on `ℍ` when `L` is discrete and `E` is finite-dimensional (`ZLattice.summable_thetaSeries`).

ZLattice.thetaCoset.signature:
ZLattice.thetaCoset.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] (L : Submodule ℤ E) (γ : E)
  (τ : UpperHalfPlane) : ℂ
ZLattice.thetaCoset.doc:
The theta series `θ_{γ+L}(τ) = ∑_{v ∈ L} exp (π i ‖γ + v‖² τ)` of the translate `γ + L` of
`L : Submodule ℤ E`. For `γ` in the dual lattice this is the coset theta series of the coset
`γ + L`.

ZLattice.successiveMin_pow_mul_measureRe.signature:
ZLattice.successiveMin_pow_mul_measureReal_le_two_pow_mul_covolume.{u_1} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  [BorelSpace E] (L : Submodule ℤ E) [DiscreteTopology ↥L] [IsZLattice ℝ L]
  (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E := by volume_tac) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] {K : ConvexBody E}
  (hKs : ∀ x ∈ K, -x ∈ K) (hE : 0 < Module.finrank ℝ E) :
  ZLattice.successiveMin L K ⟨0, hE⟩ ^ Module.finrank ℝ E * μ.real ↑K ≤
    2 ^ Module.finrank ℝ E * ZLattice.covolume L μ
ZLattice.successiveMin_pow_mul_measureRe.doc:
**Minkowski's first theorem on the successive minima.** For a full lattice `L` in a real normed
space `E` of positive dimension `n`, a Haar measure `μ` on `E`, and a convex body `K` symmetric
about `0`, the first successive minimum `λ₀` of `L` with respect to `K` satisfies
`λ₀ⁿ · μ.real K ≤ 2ⁿ · covolume L μ`. It follows from the upper bound of Minkowski's second
theorem, since `λ₀ ≤ λᵢ` for every `i`.

ZLattice.successiveMin.signature:
ZLattice.successiveMin.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  (L : Submodule ℤ E) (K : ConvexBody E) (i : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ E)) : ℝ
ZLattice.successiveMin.doc:
The successive minima of a `ℤ`-submodule `L` of `E` with respect to a convex body `K`, indexed
from zero: `successiveMin L K i` is the infimum of the dilation factors `t ≥ 0` for which `t • K`
contains `i + 1` vectors of `L` that are linearly independent over `ℝ`.

When no dilate of `K` contains `i + 1` independent vectors of `L` (for instance when `L` has rank
at most `i`, or when `K` is a segment containing `0` and `1 ≤ i`), the infimum is over the empty
set and `successiveMin L K i` takes the junk value `sInf ∅ = 0`; the minima then need not be
positive or monotone. For a discrete spanning lattice `L` and `0` in the interior of `K`, the
hypotheses of the main results, the set is nonempty and the infimum is attained
(`ZLattice.successiveMin_isLeast`).

ZLattice.representationNumber.signature:
ZLattice.representationNumber.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] (L : Submodule ℤ E)
  (t : ℝ) : ℕ
ZLattice.representationNumber.doc:
The representation number `r_L(t)`: the number of vectors of `L` of squared norm `t`. For a
discrete `L` in a proper space every shell is finite, so this is a genuine count.

ZLattice.prod_successiveMin_mul_measure_.signature:
ZLattice.prod_successiveMin_mul_measure_le_two_pow_mul_covolume.{u_1} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  [BorelSpace E] (L : Submodule ℤ E) [DiscreteTopology ↥L] [IsZLattice ℝ L]
  (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E := by volume_tac) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] {K : ConvexBody E}
  (hKs : ∀ x ∈ K, -x ∈ K) :
  ENNReal.ofReal (∏ i, ZLattice.successiveMin L K i) * μ ↑K ≤
    2 ^ Module.finrank ℝ E * ENNReal.ofReal (ZLattice.covolume L μ)
ZLattice.prod_successiveMin_mul_measure_.doc:
**Minkowski's second theorem**, upper bound, in terms of the successive minima. For a full
lattice `L` in a real normed space `E` of dimension `n`, a Haar measure `μ` on `E`, and a convex
body `K` symmetric about `0`, the successive minima `λ i = successiveMin L K i` satisfy
`λ₀ ⋯ λₙ₋₁ · μ K ≤ 2ⁿ · covolume L μ`. If `K` has empty interior, its measure is zero.

ZLattice.prod_successiveMin_mul_measureR.doc:
**Minkowski's second theorem**, upper bound, in terms of the successive minima and with real
measures: `λ₀ ⋯ λₙ₋₁ · μ.real K ≤ 2ⁿ · covolume L μ`.

ZLattice.prod_successiveMin_le_covolume_.doc:
**Minkowski's second theorem for bodies of measure at least `2ⁿ`.** If a convex body `K`
symmetric about `0` has `2ⁿ ≤ μ K`, then the successive minima of `L` with respect to `K` satisfy
`λ₀ ⋯ λₙ₋₁ ≤ covolume L μ`. This applies, for instance, to the central
slices of the cube `[-1, 1]ⁿ`, whose volume is at least `2ⁿ` by Vaaler's theorem.

ZLattice.prod_mul_measure_le_two_pow_mul.signature:
ZLattice.prod_mul_measure_le_two_pow_mul_covolume.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (L : Submodule ℤ E)
  [DiscreteTopology ↥L] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E := by volume_tac) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure]
  {K : Set E} (hK : Convex ℝ K) (hKs : ∀ x ∈ K, -x ∈ K) {n : ℕ} (hn : n = Module.finrank ℝ E)
  {a : Fin n → E} (haL : ∀ (i : Fin n), a i ∈ L) (ha : LinearIndependent ℝ a) {g : Fin n → ℝ}
  (hg0 : ∀ (i : Fin n), 0 ≤ g i)
  (hgap : ∀ (j : Fin n), ∀ v ∈ L, gauge K v < g j → v ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (a '' Set.Iio j)) :
  ENNReal.ofReal (∏ i, g i) * μ K ≤ 2 ^ n * ENNReal.ofReal (ZLattice.covolume L μ)
ZLattice.prod_mul_measure_le_two_pow_mul.doc:
**Minkowski's second theorem**, upper bound. Let `L` be a discrete `ℤ`-submodule of an
`n`-dimensional real normed space `E`, `μ` a Haar measure on `E`, and `K ⊆ E` convex and symmetric
about `0`. Let
`a 0, …, a (n - 1)` be `ℝ`-linearly independent vectors of `L` and `g 0, …, g (n - 1)`
nonnegative numbers such that every `v ∈ L` with `gauge K v < g j` lies in the span of
`a 0, …, a (j - 1)`. Then `(∏ i, g i) * μ K ≤ 2 ^ n * covolume L μ`.
The full independent family already implies that the discrete submodule `L` is a full lattice.

Independent lattice vectors realizing the successive minima `λ₀ ≤ ⋯ ≤ λₙ₋₁` of `L` with respect to
`K` satisfy the hypothesis with `g = λ`, which gives the classical form
`λ₀ ⋯ λₙ₋₁ · μ K ≤ 2ⁿ · covolume L μ`.

ZLattice.exists_basis_mem_smul_successiv.signature:
ZLattice.exists_basis_mem_smul_successiveMin.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] {K : ConvexBody E} [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (L : Submodule ℤ E)
  [DiscreteTopology ↥L] [IsZLattice ℝ L] (hK : 0 ∈ interior ↑K) (hsymm : ∀ x ∈ K, -x ∈ K) :
  ∃ b,
    ∀ (i : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ E)),
      ↑(b i) ∈ (max 1 ((↑↑i + 1) / 2) * ZLattice.successiveMin L K i) • ↑K
ZLattice.exists_basis_mem_smul_successiv.doc:
**A basis from the successive minima** (Cassels, Chapter V, Lemma 8). For a discrete spanning
lattice `L` and a symmetric convex body `K` with `0` in its interior, some `ℤ`-basis `b` of `L` has
`b i ∈ (max 1 ((i + 1) / 2) * successiveMin L K i) • K` for every `i`. The factor is `1` for
`i ≤ 1`, and the product of the factors is `n! / 2 ^ (n - 1)`
(`TauCeti.prod_max_one_add_one_div_two`).

ZLattice.dual.signature:
ZLattice.dual.{u} {E : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] (L : Submodule ℤ E) :
  Submodule ℤ E
ZLattice.dual.doc:
The dual lattice of `L : Submodule ℤ E`: the vectors whose inner product with every vector of
`L` is an integer. It is Mathlib's `BilinForm.dualSubmodule` of the inner product.

ZLattice.IsIntegral.thetaSeries_dual_eq_.signature:
ZLattice.IsIntegral.thetaSeries_dual_eq_sum.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] {L : Submodule ℤ E} [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [DiscreteTopology ↥L]
  [IsZLattice ℝ L] (h : ZLattice.IsIntegral L) [Fintype (ZLattice.DiscriminantGroup L)]
  (τ : UpperHalfPlane) :
  ZLattice.thetaSeries (ZLattice.dual L) τ = ∑ γ, ZLattice.thetaCosetClass L γ τ
ZLattice.IsIntegral.thetaSeries_dual_eq_.doc:
For an integral lattice `L`, the theta series of the dual lattice is the sum of the coset theta
series over the finite discriminant group `L^∨ ⧸ L`: `Θ_{L^∨} = ∑_{γ ∈ A_L} θ_γ`. The discriminant
group of an integral lattice is finite (`IsIntegral.finite_discriminantGroup`), so a `Fintype`
instance is always available.

ZLattice.IsIntegral.det_eq_card_discrimi.signature:
ZLattice.IsIntegral.det_eq_card_discriminantGroup.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  {L : Submodule ℤ E} [DiscreteTopology ↥L] [IsZLattice ℝ L] (h : ZLattice.IsIntegral L) :
  ZLattice.det L = ↑(Nat.card (ZLattice.DiscriminantGroup L))
ZLattice.IsIntegral.det_eq_card_discrimi.doc:
For an integral lattice `L`, the determinant is the order of the discriminant group
`L^∨ ⧸ L`. In particular it is a positive integer.

ZLattice.IsEven.thetaSeries_slash_T.doc:
The theta series of an even lattice is invariant under `T`, in every weight:
`Θ_L ∣[k] T = Θ_L`.

ZLattice.IsEven.thetaCoset_one_vadd.signature:
ZLattice.IsEven.thetaCoset_one_vadd.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] {L : Submodule ℤ E}
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] {γ : E} (hL : ZLattice.IsEven L) (hγ : γ ∈ ZLattice.dual L)
  (τ : UpperHalfPlane) :
  ZLattice.thetaCoset L γ (1 +ᵥ τ) =
    Complex.exp (↑Real.pi * Complex.I * ↑(‖γ‖ ^ 2)) * ZLattice.thetaCoset L γ τ
ZLattice.IsEven.thetaCoset_one_vadd.doc:
The translation law of the theta series of a coset of an even lattice: for `γ ∈ L^∨`,
`θ_{γ+L}(τ + 1) = e(q_L(γ)) θ_{γ+L}(τ)` with `e(q_L(γ)) = exp (π i ‖γ‖²)`.

ZLattice.IsEven.qExpansion_thetaSeries_c.signature:
ZLattice.IsEven.qExpansion_thetaSeries_coeff.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  {L : Submodule ℤ E} [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [DiscreteTopology ↥L]
  (hL : ZLattice.IsEven L) (m : ℕ) :
  (PowerSeries.coeff m) (UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion 1 (ZLattice.thetaSeries L)) =
    ↑(ZLattice.representationNumber L (2 * ↑m))
ZLattice.IsEven.qExpansion_thetaSeries_c.doc:
The coefficients of the `q`-expansion of the theta series of an even lattice: the `m`-th
coefficient in `q = exp (2 π i τ)` is the number `r_L(2m)` of vectors of half-norm `m`.

ZLattice.IsEven.dualGaussSum_one_one.signature:
ZLattice.IsEven.dualGaussSum_one_one.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {L : Submodule ℤ E} [DiscreteTopology ↥L]
  [IsZLattice ℝ L] {k : ℕ} (hL : ZLattice.IsEven L) (hk : Module.finrank ℝ E = 2 * k)
  [Fintype (↥(ZLattice.dual L) ⧸ (↑1 • L).submoduleOf (ZLattice.dual L))] :
  ZLattice.dualGaussSum L hL 1 1 = ↑√↑(Nat.card (ZLattice.DiscriminantGroup L)) * Complex.I ^ k
ZLattice.IsEven.dualGaussSum_one_one.doc:
**Milgram's formula.** If `L` is an even lattice and `dim E = 2k`, then
`∑_{γ ∈ L^∨/L} e(‖γ‖² / 2) = √|L^∨/L| · i^k`, where `i^k = e(n/8)` for `n = 2k`. The left side
is written as a sum over `L^∨ / 1L`; `ZLattice.dualGaussSum_one` rewrites it as a sum over the
discriminant group `L^∨/L`.

ZLattice.IsEven.signature: ZLattice.IsEven.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] (L : Submodule ℤ E) : Prop
ZLattice.IsEven.doc: A lattice is even if the squared norm of each of its vectors is an even integer.

YoungDiagram.injOn_zpow_cellContent_of_p.doc:
**Split semisimplicity separates the Jucys–Murphy eigenvalues.** Over a commutative ring
without zero divisors, if the unit `Q` is not `1` and the product `∏_{d=1}^{n} [d]_Q` of the
`Q`-integers `[d]_Q = 1 + Q + ⋯ + Q ^ (d - 1)` is nonzero, then on every Young diagram of size
less than `n` the powers `Q ^ content c` of distinct addable cells are distinct.

YoungDiagram.injOn_zpow_cellContent_iff.signature:
YoungDiagram.injOn_zpow_cellContent_iff.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] {Q : G} {n : ℕ} :
  (∀ (μ : YoungDiagram),
      μ.card < n → Set.InjOn (fun c => Q ^ YoungDiagram.cellContent c) {c | μ.IsAddable c}) ↔
    ∀ (d : ℕ), 2 ≤ d → d ≤ n → Q ^ d ≠ 1

`lutz_nagell`. It is the specialisation of the two theorems above at a short model: Mathlib's
`isCharNeTwoNF_of_isShortNF` supplies the instance, so there is nothing to discharge. No hypothesis
`Δ ≠ 0` is needed — see the module docstring.

`H¹(K, E[m])` to its additive characters with values in `ℤ/m`.

WeierstrassCurve.isInteger_or_order_two_.doc:
**Nagell–Lutz over `ℚ`**, the form the roadmap asks for: for an integral long Weierstrass
model, a nonzero torsion point has integral coordinates unless it has order exactly `2`, where the
honest bound is `4x, 8y ∈ ℤ`.

No squarefreeness hypothesis survives here. Over `ℤ` a rational prime **is** squarefree, so the
guard in the general statement discharges outright — which is why that statement carries the
hypothesis rather than a `CharZero`/unramified typeclass: the generality is free at `ℤ` and only
costs something over rings where a rational prime ramifies.

WeierstrassCurve.isInteger_of_torsion.doc:
**Nagell–Lutz, integrality half.** On an integral model in characteristic-≠-2 normal form a
nonzero torsion point has integral coordinates — with *no* order-two exception.

The long-model theorem leaves order two aside with only `4x, 8y ∈ ℤ`. Here that case collapses:
`ψ₂ = 2y`, so order two forces `y = 0`, and the curve equation then exhibits `x` as a rational root
of the monic `X³ + a₂X² + a₄X + a₆`. The `a₂` term costs nothing — the cubic is monic either
way.

**The Hasse bound** (Silverman V.1.1): an elliptic curve `E` over a field with `q` elements
satisfies `(#E(𝔽_q) - (q + 1))² ≤ 4q`, that is `|#E(𝔽_q) - (q + 1)| ≤ 2√q`, where the count
includes the point at infinity. `frobeniusTrace_sq_le_four_mul_card` is the same bound for the
trace `a_q`.

WeierstrassCurve.hasPotentialGoodReducti.doc:
**The criterion of Néron, Ogg and Shafarevich for potential good reduction** (Silverman AEC
VII.7.3). Let `W` be an elliptic curve over a nonarchimedean local field `K`, and let `ℓ` be a
prime different from the residue characteristic of `K`. Then `W` has potential good reduction
exactly when the inertia subgroup of `Gal(K^{alg}/K)` acts on the `ℓ`-adic Tate module of `W`
through a finite quotient.

`a_q` of an elliptic curve satisfies `a_q² ≤ 4q`. `hasse_bound` states the same inequality in terms
of the number of points.

elliptic curve `E` over a number field `K` is a finitely generated `ℤ`-module.

Suppose that the valuation ring of `v` is Henselian with finite residue field, for instance the
ring of integers of a nonarchimedean local field, and that Tate's algorithm, run on the integral
model of `W` with a generator `ϖ` of the maximal ideal, stops with the symbol `s`. Then the local
index the algorithm reports is `[W(F) : E₀(F)]`, the index of the subgroup of points with
nonsingular reduction.

Finiteness of the residue field is used only at nonsplit multiplicative reduction of even type
`I₂ₘ`, to find a point with singular reduction; over a general perfect residue field the index can
be `1` there.

exactly when the image of the descent map is finite.

`E(K)/2E(K)` and the image of `μ` are the same group, so finiteness of either is finiteness of
the other.

class group and finitely generated unit group.

  [∀ (p : (WeierstrassCurve.toAffine (C • W)).f.Factors),
      Monoid.FG ((WeierstrassCurve.toAffine (C • W)).ringOfIntegersFactor R p)ˣ] :
  AddGroup.FG W.Point
WeierstrassCurve.Affine.fg_point_of_vari.doc:
**The Mordell–Weil theorem** for an arbitrary Weierstrass curve: `E(K)` is finitely generated,
given an admissible change of variables `C` bringing `E` into the normal form `y² = f(x)`,
together with the finiteness hypotheses of `fg_point` for the model `C • E`. The result transfers
along the isomorphism of point groups `Point.addEquivVariableChange`.

Such a `C` exists whenever `2` is invertible in `K`, by completing the square.

WeierstrassCurve.Affine.fg_point_of_numb.doc:
**The Mordell–Weil theorem**: the group `E(K)` of `K`-rational points of an elliptic curve `E`
over a number field `K` is finitely generated.

The square on the left-hand side is completed by an admissible change of variables, possible since
`K` has characteristic zero, and the finiteness hypotheses of `fg_point` for the resulting model
are the class number theorem and Dirichlet's unit theorem.

WeierstrassCurve.Affine.fg_point.signature:

  [Height.AdmissibleAbsValues F] [Northcott Height.logHeight₁] [DecidableEq F]
  [WeierstrassCurve.IsElliptic (WeierstrassCurve.toAffine W)] (R : Type u_2) [CommRing R]
  [IsDedekindDomain R] [Algebra R F] [IsFractionRing R F] [WeierstrassCurve.IsCharNeTwoNF W]
  [∀ (p : W.f.Factors), Finite (ClassGroup (W.ringOfIntegersFactor R p))]
  [∀ (p : W.f.Factors), Monoid.FG (W.ringOfIntegersFactor R p)ˣ] : AddGroup.FG W.Point
WeierstrassCurve.Affine.fg_point.doc:
**The Mordell–Weil theorem**, general version: `E(K)` is finitely generated, for an elliptic
curve `E` given by an equation `y² = f(x)` with a monic cubic `f` (`a₁ = a₃ = 0`) over a field `K`
such that `K` has admissible absolute values with the Northcott property, `K` is the fraction
field of a Dedekind domain `R`, and for each irreducible factor `p` of `f` the integral closure of
`R` in `K[X] ⧸ (p)` has finite class group and finitely generated unit group.

For `K` a number field all of these hold; see `fg_point_of_numberField`.

The per-factor hypotheses cannot be replaced by the corresponding hypotheses on `R` itself: by a
theorem of Claborn, refined by Leedham-Green and by Clark, *every* abelian group is the class
group of the integral closure of a PID in a separable quadratic extension, so
`Finite (ClassGroup R)` gives no control over the class groups of the factors.

VonNeumannAlgebra.exists_forall_norm_sub.doc:
**The von Neumann density theorem for a generated von Neumann algebra.** An operator `x` in
the von Neumann algebra generated by a set `s` of bounded operators is a strong-operator limit of
elements of the star algebra generated by `s`: for every finite family of vectors `v i` and every
`ε > 0` there is `t ∈ StarAlgebra.adjoin ℂ s` with `‖x (v i) - t (v i)‖ < ε` for all `i`.

`[U, [V, W]] + [V, [W, U]] + [W, [U, V]] = 0`. This rearranges Mathlib's Leibniz form
`leibniz_identity_mlieBracket_apply`.

TotallyBounded.exists_tendsto_zero_subse.doc:
**Grothendieck's compactness lemma.** A totally bounded subset of a real seminormed space lies
in the closed convex hull of the range of a sequence tending to `0`.

relative Kronecker map `Hⁿ(X, A; R, M) →ₗ[k] (Hₙ(X, A; R) ⟶ M)` is bijective, for every module

TopPair.singularKronecker_bijective_of_p.doc:

ring `k`: for a projective coefficient module `R`, if the relative singular homology modules
`Hₙ(X, A; R)` of a pair are all projective, the relative Kronecker map
`Hⁿ(X, A; R, M) →ₗ[k] (Hₙ(X, A; R) ⟶ M)` is bijective in every degree, for every module `M`.

of a pair with coefficients in a field `k` is the dual of its relative singular homology,

a topological pair to the simplices subordinate to an open cover of the ambient space is a
quasi-isomorphism.

the simplices subordinate to an open cover of the ambient space does not change relative
homology.

hereditary commutative ring: a `k`-linear equivalence

`TopCat.singularKroneckerSection` and is not natural in `X`.

Kronecker map `H⁰(X; R, M) →ₗ[k] (H₀(X; R) ⟶ M)` is bijective, as no differential leaves the
degree-zero singular chains.

**The universal coefficient theorem above a projective homology module**, over a hereditary
commutative ring: for a projective coefficient module `R`, if `Hₙ(X; R)` is projective, the
Kronecker map `Hⁿ⁺¹(X; R, M) →ₗ[k] (Hₙ₊₁(X; R) ⟶ M)` is bijective, for every module `M`. The

`M`, the Kronecker map of singular cohomology is a `k`-linear equivalence
`Hⁿ(X; R, M) ≃ₗ[k] (Hₙ(X; R) ⟶ M)`.

not be natural in `X` and `Y`.

TestFunction.extDerivCLM.doc:
The **exterior derivative** of test `k`-forms on `Ω` with coefficients in `F`, as a
continuous linear map into the test `(k + 1)`-forms. It is the alternatization
`ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFinCLM` of the Fréchet derivative
`TestFunction.fderivCLM`, so pointwise it is Mathlib's `extDeriv`.

TestFunction.dualEquivDistribution.doc:
**Maps on vector-valued tests are operator-valued distributions.** For a finite-dimensional
real normed space `F` and a real normed space `V`, the continuous linear maps from the `F`-valued
test functions on `Ω` to `V` correspond to the `F →L[ℝ] V`-valued distributions on `Ω`: a map `T`
corresponds to the distribution `ψ ↦ (v ↦ T (ψ • v))`. Both spaces carry the topology of uniform
convergence on compact sets, and the correspondence is a homeomorphism for these topologies.

**Elliptic regularity for the shifted Laplacian**: for `c > 0`, a tempered distribution `f`
lies in the Sobolev space `H^{s+2}` if and only if `-Δ f + c f` lies in `H^s`.

The **resolvent of the Laplacian** `(c - Δ)⁻¹` on tempered distributions: the Fourier
multiplier with symbol `((2π)² ‖ξ‖² + c)⁻¹`. For `c > 0` it is the two-sided inverse of `-Δ + c`
(`laplacianResolvent_neg_laplacian_add_smul` and `neg_laplacian_laplacianResolvent_add_smul`);
for `c ≤ 0` the value is not meaningful.

the profinite integers to `G` that sends the generator to `x`.

edge are `q`, and all the others vanish.

homotopy category of graded `Z`-modules, by sending the standard generator at a vertex `i` to the
class of tensoring with the braid complex `Bᵢ`.

Complementary shifted Hom spaces of actual componentwise vertex projectives are in perfect
trace pairing over every commutative coefficient ring.

TauCeti.zHat.unitsEquivPiPadicInt.doc:
**The unit-group decomposition of the profinite integers.** The product decomposition
`Additive zHat ≃+* ∀ ℓ, ℤ_[ℓ]` restricts to an isomorphism of topological groups on units.

TauCeti.zHat.ringEquivPiPadicInt.doc:
**The product decomposition of the profinite integers.** The ring homomorphism from
`Additive zHat` to `∀ ℓ : Nat.Primes, ℤ_[ℓ]` with components the `ℓ`-adic components
`zHat.component ℓ` is a ring isomorphism: injective by `zHat.ext_of_component` and surjective by
`zHat.exists_forall_component_eq`. It is a homeomorphism (`zHat.continuous_ringEquivPiPadicInt`,
`zHat.continuous_ringEquivPiPadicInt_symm`), so an isomorphism of topological rings.

The inverse sends a rational-circle value to the connecting class of the unique continuous

TauCeti.zHat.cohomologicalDimensionAt_eq.doc: **The `p`-cohomological dimension of the profinite integers is one**, for every prime `p`.

**Yasui's theorem spelled out**: there are knots `K K' : S¹ → S³` with `0`-surgeries `Y`, `Y'`,
oriented compatibly with an orientation of `S³`, and an orientation-preserving homeomorphism
`Y ≃ₜ Y'`, such that `K` is smoothly concordant neither to `K'` nor to its reverse.

**The wild inertia subgroup** `P_K` of the absolute Galois group of a nonarchimedean local
field `K`: the automorphisms of the algebraic closure fixing the maximal tamely ramified extension
`K^{t}`. Through `IntermediateField.fixingSubgroupEquiv` it is `Gal(K^{alg}/K^{t})`.

TauCeti.weylDimension_eq_prod_prod_div.doc:
**The Weyl dimension formula in its quotient form**: over `ℚ`, the dimension is the product of
the term-by-term quotients `(λᵢ - λⱼ + j - i) / (j - i)`.

TauCeti.weylDenominator_eq_weylNumerator.doc:
**The Weyl denominator identity**: the Weyl denominator is the Weyl numerator of the weight
`0`,

`∏_{α > 0} (1 - e^{-α}) = ∑_{w ∈ W} sgn(w) e^{w ⬝ 0}`,

an identity in the integral group algebra of the weight space. Written without the dot action, the
right-hand side is `∑_{w ∈ W} sgn(w) e^{w(ρ) - ρ}`.

This is the case `λ = 0` of the Weyl character formula, in which the character of the trivial
module is `1`.

TauCeti.weylCoxeterHom_injective.doc:
**Tits' theorem: the braid relations are the only relations among the simple reflections.**
The canonical homomorphism from the Coxeter group of a base to the Weyl group is injective.

the dual of `TauCeti.repartitionRepresentation` to the stable subspace `Ω_F`, so that
`(σ • ω) a = ω (σ⁻¹ • a)`.

  [NeZero n] {P : MvPolynomial (Fin n) K} (hP : P ≠ 0) {r : Fin n → ℕ} (hr : ∀ (i : Fin n), 0 < r i)
  (hdeg : ∀ (i : Fin n), MvPolynomial.degreeOf i P ≤ r i) {σ : ℝ} (hσ₀ : 0 < σ) (hσ : σ ≤ 1 / 2)
  (hratio : ∀ (i j : Fin n), ↑j = ↑i + 1 → ↑(r j) ≤ σ * ↑(r i)) (β : Fin n → K)
  (hβ :
    ∀ (i : Fin n),
      σ⁻¹ * (P.logHeight + 4 * ↑n * ↑(r 0) * ↑(Module.finrank ℚ K)) ≤

**Roth's lemma** (Pottmeyer, Theorem 3.4.1). Let `P ≠ 0` be a polynomial in `n ≥ 1`
variables over a number field `K`, with partial degrees `deg_{Xᵢ} P ≤ rᵢ` for positive weights
`rᵢ` satisfying `rᵢ₊₁ ≤ σ rᵢ`, where `0 < σ ≤ 1 / 2`. If
`σ⁻¹ (h(P) + 4 n r₀ [K : ℚ]) ≤ rᵢ h(βᵢ)` for every `i`, then the index of `P` at `β` with
weights `r` is at most `2 n σ ^ (1 / 2 ^ (n - 1))`. Heights are relative logarithmic heights.

                  ∫⁻ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ioo 0 1, ∫⁻ (x : E), ‖v t x‖ₑ ^ p.toReal ∂↑(ν t) = A}
TauCeti.wassersteinEDist_rpow_eq_sInf_li.doc:
**The Benamou–Brenier formula, as an infimum.** For `1 ≤ p < ∞` and probability measures `μ₀`,
`μ₁` on a finite-dimensional real normed space, `W_p (μ₀, μ₁) ^ p` is the infimum of the
`p`-actions `∫₀¹ ∫ ‖vₜ‖ ^ p dνₜ dt` of the curves `t ↦ νₜ` of finite measures, narrowly continuous
on `[0, 1]` and joining `μ₀` to `μ₁`, solving the continuity equation with velocity `v` on
`(0, 1)`. Both sides may be infinite.

TauCeti.wassersteinEDist_one_eq_lintegra.signature:
TauCeti.wassersteinEDist_one_eq_lintegral_enorm_cdf_sub (μ ν : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ)

TauCeti.wassersteinEDist_one_eq_lintegra.doc:
**The one-dimensional Kantorovich formula.** The Wasserstein distance at exponent one of two
probability laws on `ℝ` is the area between their cumulative distribution functions.

TauCeti.wassersteinEDist_one_eq_iSup_of_.signature:

TauCeti.wassersteinEDist_one_eq_iSup_of_.doc:
**Kantorovich–Rubinstein duality on a compact space.** For probability measures on a compact
pseudometric space whose open sets are measurable, the `1`-Wasserstein distance is the supremum
of the differences of expectations of the `1`-Lipschitz real functions.

**Kantorovich–Rubinstein duality, normalized at a basepoint.** Under the hypotheses of
`TauCeti.wassersteinEDist_one_eq_iSup`, the supremum may be taken over the `1`-Lipschitz real
functions vanishing at any prescribed point `x₀`: subtracting a constant does not change a
difference of expectations under two probability measures.

**Kantorovich–Rubinstein duality.** For probability measures with finite first moments on a
second-countable pseudometric space whose measurable structure is standard Borel and contains the
open sets — in particular on a Polish metric space with its Borel σ-algebra — the
`1`-Wasserstein distance is the supremum of the differences of expectations of the `1`-Lipschitz
real functions.

TauCeti.volume_setOf_tendsto_circleMap_n.signature:

**Fatou's lemma on circles.** If `log⁺ ‖f‖⁻¹` is integrable on the circles about `c` of
radii `ρ n`, and its circle averages there are at most `B`, then the angles in one period along
which `f (circleMap c (ρ n) θ)` tends to `0` through nonzero values form a null set.

TauCeti.volume_rpow_add_volume_rpow_le.doc:
**Brunn–Minkowski inequality** for nonempty Lebesgue-measurable sets
in a positive-dimensional real inner product space. The sum has its outer volume and
need not be measurable or have finite volume.

TauCeti.vitali_of_tendsto.signature:
TauCeti.vitali_of_tendsto.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]
  {Ω A : Set ℂ} [ProperSpace E] {F : ℕ → ℂ → E} (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hconn : IsPreconnected Ω)

TauCeti.vitali_of_tendsto.doc:
**Vitali's theorem with prescribed pointwise values.** Under the hypotheses of `vitali`, if
the sequence converges pointwise on `A` to a specified function `g`, its locally uniform
holomorphic limit agrees with `g` throughout `A`.

No regularity of `g` away from `A` is assumed or concluded; when `A` is all of `Ω` the limit is
`g` itself, which is
`TauCeti.tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_of_isLocallyBoundedOn_of_forall_tendsto`.

TauCeti.vitali.signature:
TauCeti.vitali.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] {Ω A : Set ℂ}

  (hF : ∀ (n : ℕ), DifferentiableOn ℂ (F n) Ω) (hb : TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn F Ω) (hAΩ : A ⊆ Ω)

TauCeti.vitali.doc:
**Vitali's convergence theorem.** Let `Ω` be an open preconnected subset of `ℂ`. A locally
bounded sequence of holomorphic maps from `Ω` into a proper complex normed space `E` (for instance
`ℂ`) which converges pointwise on a subset `A ⊆ Ω` having an accumulation point in `Ω` converges
locally uniformly on `Ω` to a holomorphic map.

The pointwise limit on `A` need not be supplied: its existence is enough to determine the
holomorphic limit uniquely.

TauCeti.vietaHom_eq_comp_esymmSubst.doc:
**Vieta's formulas**, in the form the symmetric descent uses: if `f` is the product of the
linear factors attached to `x`, then substituting the signed coefficients of `f` is the same as
substituting the elementary symmetric polynomials and evaluating at `x`.

TauCeti.vertexStrongConnectivity_le_arcC.signature:
TauCeti.vertexStrongConnectivity_le_arcConnectivity.{u, v} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v} :
  TauCeti.vertexStrongConnectivity Q ≤ TauCeti.arcConnectivity Q
TauCeti.vertexStrongConnectivity_le_arcC.doc:
**The directed Whitney inequality**, numerical form: the vertex strong connectivity is at most
the arc connectivity.

TauCeti.vermaCentralCharacter_eq_iff.signature:
TauCeti.vermaCentralCharacter_eq_iff.{v} {K : Type} {L : Type v} [Field K] [CharZero K]

TauCeti.vermaCentralCharacter_eq_iff.doc:
**Harish-Chandra's theorem on central characters**: two weights `lam` and `mu` have the same
central character, `χ_lam = χ_mu`, exactly when `mu` lies in the dot orbit of `lam`, that is
`mu = w · lam = w (lam + ρ) - ρ` for an element `w` of the Weyl group.

TauCeti.vanKampenWide_hom_ext.signature:
TauCeti.vanKampenWide_hom_ext.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] {ι : Type u_2}

TauCeti.vanKampenWide_hom_ext.doc:
**Uniqueness in the Seifert--van Kampen theorem for a family.** If the interiors of the sets
`U i ∋ x` cover `X` and their pairwise intersections are path connected, then two homomorphisms out
of `π₁(X, x)` which agree on the image of every `π₁(U i, x)` are equal.

TauCeti.vanKampenWideLift_surjective.signature:
TauCeti.vanKampenWideLift_surjective.{u_1, u_2} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] {ι : Type u_2}

  Function.Surjective ⇑(TauCeti.vanKampenWideLift U x hxU)
TauCeti.vanKampenWideLift_surjective.doc:
**The generation half of van Kampen's theorem for a family.** Every loop class is the image
of an element of the indexed free product when all pairwise intersections of the cover members
are path connected.

TauCeti.vanKampenWideEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.vanKampenWideEquiv.{u_1, u_2} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] {ι : Type u_2}

TauCeti.vanKampenWideEquiv.doc:
**The Seifert--van Kampen theorem for a family with a simply connected common pairwise
intersection.** If the interiors of the path-connected sets `U i` cover `X`, all of them contain
the simply connected set `C ∋ x`, and two distinct members meet inside `C`, then the canonical
homomorphism from the free product of the groups `π₁(U i, x)` to `π₁(X, x)` is an isomorphism.
Its underlying homomorphism is `vanKampenWideLift`.

TauCeti.vanKampenLift_bijective.signature:

TauCeti.vanKampenLift_bijective.doc:
**The based Seifert--van Kampen theorem for a simply connected overlap.**

If the interiors of two path-connected sets cover `X`, their intersection is simply connected,
and both contain the basepoint, then the canonical homomorphism from the free product of their
fundamental groups to the fundamental group of `X` is bijective.

TauCeti.universalGSpaceStandardHomotopyE.signature:

TauCeti.universalGSpaceStandardHomotopyE.doc:
**Milnor's join resolution is homotopy equivalent to the standard resolution**, by a homotopy
equivalence whose forward map is the explicit join-to-standard chain map. Its homotopy inverse is
the lift of the identity of the trivial representation from the standard resolution to the join
resolution.

TauCeti.unifIntegrable_of_lintegral_ofRe.doc:
**De la Vallée Poussin's criterion.** A family of a.e. strongly measurable functions with
`∫ Φ(‖f i‖) ≤ C < ∞` for a superlinear `Φ` is uniformly integrable.

TauCeti.two_mul_sq_measureReal_sub_le_kl.signature:

**Pinsker's inequality for events**, with natural logarithms. The extended-valued right

**Young's inequality for real inner products**: for every weight `ε > 0`,
`2 ⟪x, y⟫ ≤ ε ‖x‖² + ε⁻¹ ‖y‖²`.

TauCeti.twoPiHermiteHilbertBasis.signature:
TauCeti.twoPiHermiteHilbertBasis.{u_1} (𝕜 : Type u_1) [RCLike 𝕜] :

**The rescaled Hermite functions are a Hilbert basis of `L²(ℝ)`.** This is the Hermite basis in

`TauCeti.hilbertBasisOfOrthogonalSystem`, run at the weight `e^{-2πx²}` and the polynomials

times the interval-integral coefficients of `g`.

TauCeti.tsum_star_integral_normalizedChe.doc:
**Parseval's identity for the Chebyshev cosine basis** (polarized form): the inner product of
`f` and `g` is the sum of the conjugated measure-integral coefficients of `f` times the
measure-integral coefficients of `g`.

TauCeti.tsum_one_div_pow_wildExponent_tw.doc:
**Serre's mass formula for the quadratic extensions of `ℚ_2`**:
`∑_{L ∈ σ_{ℚ_2}(2)} 2 ^ (-c(L)) = 2 · 2⁻¹ + 4 · 2⁻² = 2`.

the line `Re s = c`, the truncated Perron integral of the series is the series of the truncated
Perron kernels at the ratios `x / n`.

TauCeti.trace_heckeTCuspLevelOne_eq_neg_.signature:
TauCeti.trace_heckeTCuspLevelOne_eq_neg_hurwitzClassNumber_sub_min {k : ℤ} {w : ℕ} (hk : k = ↑w + 2)
  (hw : Even w) (hw₀ : w ≠ 0) (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] :
  (LinearMap.trace ℂ (CuspForm (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.mapGL ℝ).range k))
      (TauCeti.heckeTCuspLevelOne k n) =
    (-∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc (-4 * ↑n) (4 * ↑n) with t ^ 2 ≤ 4 * ↑n,
            ↑(TauCeti.hurwitzClassNumber (4 * ↑n - t ^ 2).toNat) *
              Polynomial.eval (↑t) (Polynomial.dickson 2 (↑n) w)) /
        2 -
      (∑ p ∈ n.divisorsAntidiagonal, ↑(min p.1 p.2) ^ (w + 1)) / 2
TauCeti.trace_heckeTCuspLevelOne_eq_neg_.doc:
**The Eichler–Selberg trace formula at level one.** For even `k = w + 2 ≥ 4` and `n ≥ 1`, the
trace of `Tₙ` on the cusp forms of weight `k` on `SL(2, ℤ)` is

`tr(Tₙ | S_k) = -½ ∑_{t² ≤ 4n} H(4n - t²) P_k(t, n) - ½ ∑_{dd' = n} min(d, d')^(k-1)`,

with Hurwitz class numbers normalized by `H(0) = -1/12` and `P_k(t, n) = (dickson 2 n w).eval t`.
The sum over `t` runs over the integers with `t² ≤ 4n`, written as a filter of `[-4n, 4n]`.

  (htight : MeasureTheory.UnifTight (fun i => ↑↑↑i) p mu) : TotallyBounded S
TauCeti.totallyBounded_of_comp_add_sub_o.doc:
**The Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criterion.** For `1 ≤ p < ∞`, a family `S` of `Lᵖ`
functions is totally bounded as soon as it is bounded in `Lᵖ`, its translation increments are
uniformly small in `Lᵖ`, and it is uniformly tight in the sense of `MeasureTheory.UnifTight`.

Dropping either of the last two hypotheses breaks the conclusion: on `ℝ` the concentrating family
`n ^ (1/p) 1_{[0, 1/n]}` satisfies all but the smallness of translations, and the escaping family
`f(· - n)` of translates of a single nonzero `f` satisfies all but tightness, and neither is
totally bounded.

TauCeti.totallyBounded_of_comp_add_sub_o.doc:
**The Fréchet--Kolmogorov criterion for a family vanishing almost everywhere off a fixed bounded
set**, the form that Rellich--Kondrachov for `W^{1,p}_0(Ω)` consumes. For such functions the
tightness hypothesis is automatic, so an `Lᵖ`-bounded family whose translation increments are
uniformly small in `Lᵖ` is totally bounded.

TauCeti.totalVariationOn_eq_lintegral_pe.doc:
**The coarea formula for total variation.** For `u` locally integrable on `Ω`, against an
additive Haar measure, the total variation of `u` is the integral of the perimeters of its
superlevel sets: `|Du|(Ω) = ∫_ℝ P({u > t}; Ω) dt`, finite or infinite.

TauCeti.totalVariationOn.signature:
TauCeti.totalVariationOn.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E)
  (Ω : TopologicalSpace.Opens E) (u : E → ℝ) : ENNReal
TauCeti.totalVariationOn.doc:
The **total variation** of `u : E → ℝ` on the open set `Ω`, relative to the measure `μ`:
the extended supremum of `∫ div φ * u ∂μ` over test vector fields `φ ∈ 𝓓(Ω, E)` with
`‖φ x‖ ≤ 1` everywhere. For `μ` an additive Haar measure this is the variation `|Du|(Ω)` of the
distributional derivative of `u` on `Ω`, defined by duality.

TauCeti.torusWeightSeries.doc:
The local multiplicity series `f_(σ, i) ∈ ℤ⟦X⟧` attached to an embedded square-zero
pseudoholomorphic torus with determinant sign `σ` (`true` for `+`, `false` for `-`) and with
`i` negative signs among its three nontrivially twisted normal operators. The positive series
are `1 / (1 - X)`, `1 + X`, `(1 + X) / (1 + X ^ 2)` and `(1 + X) (1 - X ^ 2) / (1 + X ^ 2)`,
and each negative series is the inverse of the positive series with the same index. The weight
of the torus with multiplicity `m` is the coefficient `coeff m (torusWeightSeries σ i)`.

TauCeti.torusFamilyProjection.signature:
TauCeti.torusFamilyProjection.{u_4, u_5, u_6} {Y : Type u_4} {Λ : Type u_5} [AddCommGroup Λ]
  {E : Type u_6} [AddCommGroup E] (P : Y → Λ →ₗ[ℤ] E) : AddAction.orbitRel.Quotient Λ (Y × E) → Y
TauCeti.torusFamilyProjection.doc:
The projection `(Y × E)/Λ → Y` of the family of tori to its parameter space, descended from
`Prod.fst` along the period translation action.

TauCeti.torusFamilyHomeomorphProd.signature:
TauCeti.torusFamilyHomeomorphProd.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {Y : Type u_1} {Λ : Type u_2}

TauCeti.torusFamilyHomeomorphProd.doc:
**The global trivialization** of a continuous family of full lattices. For a `ℤ`-basis `b`
of `Λ` indexed by `ι`, the map `[y, v] ↦ (y, [F_y⁻¹ v])`, with `F_y⁻¹` the coordinate map of the
period basis at `y`, is a homeomorphism from the orbit space of the period translation action to
the product of `Y` with the fixed torus `ℝ^ι/ℤ^ι`. It lies over `Y`
(`TauCeti.fst_torusFamilyHomeomorphProd`), and on each fibre it is induced by the real linear
isomorphism `F_y⁻¹`.

TauCeti.torusFamilyFiberHomeomorph.doc:
The canonical identification of the translation quotient at `y` with the literal fibre
of the total period quotient. It sends `[v]` to `[y, v]` and needs no lattice basis.

TauCeti.topologicallyGenerates_iff_fratt.doc:
**Burnside's basis theorem, dense spanning form.** A set topologically generates a
profinite pro-`p` group exactly when the span of its image in the Frattini quotient is dense.

TauCeti.topologicallyGenerates_iff_fratt.signature:
TauCeti.topologicallyGenerates_iff_frattiniQuotient_span_eq_top.{u_1} {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)]

  (Subgroup.closure s).topologicalClosure = ⊤ ↔

TauCeti.topologicallyGenerates_iff_fratt.doc:
**Burnside's basis theorem, spanning form.** If the Frattini quotient is finite, a set
topologically generates a profinite pro-`p` group exactly when its images span that quotient
over `𝔽_p`.

TauCeti.topologicallyGenerates_iff_fratt.signature:
TauCeti.topologicallyGenerates_iff_frattiniQuotient.{u} {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)]
  {G : Type u} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G]

TauCeti.topologicallyGenerates_iff_fratt.doc:
**Burnside's basis theorem, generation form.** A set topologically generates a profinite
pro-`p` group if and only if its image topologically generates the Frattini quotient.

TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRank_le_rank.signature:
TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRank_le_rank_continuousZModDual.{u} {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)]

  [TotallyDisconnectedSpace W] [hW : _root_.Module (ZMod p) (Additive W)] :
  TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRank W ≤ Module.rank (ZMod p) (TauCeti.continuousZModDual p W)
TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRank_le_rank.doc:
**Burnside's basis theorem, cardinal form: the lower bound.** A profinite group whose additive
copy is an `𝔽_p`-vector space is topologically generated by a dual family of a basis of its
continuous `𝔽_p`-dual, and such a dual family converges to `1`.

TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat_le_o.signature:
TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat_le_of_openSubgroup_of_finiteIndex.{u} {G : Type u} [Group G]
  [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] (hG : TauCeti.IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated G)
  (U : OpenSubgroup G) [(↑U).FiniteIndex] :
  TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat ↥↑U ⋯ ≤
    1 + (↑U).index * (TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat G hG - 1)
TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat_le_o.doc:
**The Schreier bound.** Let `U` be an open subgroup of finite index in a topologically
finitely generated topological group `G`. Then `U` is topologically finitely generated
(`TauCeti.IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated.of_openSubgroup_of_finiteIndex`), and
`d(U) ≤ 1 + [G : U] * (d(G) - 1)`, with subtraction in `ℕ`. This is the topological form of
Schreier's index formula `Subgroup.rank_le_one_add_index_mul_rank_sub_one`. The bound is sharp:
finite-index subgroups of nontrivial finitely generated discrete free groups attain it, by the
Nielsen–Schreier theorem.

TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat_le_o.signature:
TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat_le_of_openSubgroup.{u} {G : Type u} [Group G]
  [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G]
  (hG : TauCeti.IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated G) (U : OpenSubgroup G) :
  TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat ↥↑U ⋯ ≤
    1 + (↑U).index * (TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat G hG - 1)
TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat_le_o.doc:
**The Schreier bound for open subgroups of a compact group.** Every open subgroup `U` of a
topologically finitely generated compact group `G` is topologically finitely generated
(`TauCeti.IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated.of_openSubgroup`), with
`d(U) ≤ 1 + [G : U] * (d(G) - 1)`.

TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat_abso.signature:
TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat_absoluteGaloisGroup (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (K : Type)
  [Field K] [ValuativeRel K] [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] [Algebra ℚ_[p] K]

  TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat (Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K) hG = Module.finrank ℚ_[p] K + 2
TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat_abso.doc:
**The generator rank of a local absolute Galois group** (NSW (7.4.1)). For a finite extension
`K` of `ℚ_p`, the absolute Galois group `G_K` needs exactly `[K : ℚ_p] + 2` topological
generators. A witness of topological finite generation is
`TauCeti.isTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated_fieldAbsoluteGaloisGroup`.

TauCeti.topologicalClosure_closure_eq_to.signature:
TauCeti.topologicalClosure_closure_eq_top_iff_quotient_profiniteFrattini.{u} {G : Type u} [Group G]
  [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G]

TauCeti.topologicalClosure_closure_eq_to.doc:
**Generation modulo the Frattini subgroup.** A set topologically generates a profinite
group if and only if its image topologically generates the quotient by the Frattini subgroup.

TauCeti.toeplitz_comp_sub_toeplitz_eq_ne.signature:
TauCeti.toeplitz_comp_sub_toeplitz_eq_neg_classicalHankel_comp_classicalHankel
  (a b : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℂ ⊤ AddCircle.haarAddCircle)) :

    -TauCeti.classicalHankel a ∘SL
        TauCeti.classicalHankel ((MeasureTheory.Lp.compMeasurePreserving (fun t => -t) ⋯) b)
TauCeti.toeplitz_comp_sub_toeplitz_eq_ne.doc:
**Classical Toeplitz product identity.** The product defect is minus the product of
the classical Hankel operator of the left symbol and that of the reflected right symbol.

TauCeti.toRelativeCWComplex.doc:
**A classical relative CW complex in a Hausdorff space is a categorical relative CW complex.**
The inclusion of the base `D` into `C` is the transfinite composition of the inclusions of the
skeleta `skeletonLT C n`, and the step from `skeletonLT C n` to `skeletonLT C (n + 1)` attaches
the `n`-cells of `C` along their attaching maps.  The body is exposed so that the `n`-th space is
the skeleton `skeletonObj C n` and the cells attached at step `n` are `cell C n` by definition.

TauCeti.toReal_transportCost_eq_sSup.signature:
TauCeti.toReal_transportCost_eq_sSup.{u, v} {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
  [CompactSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [OpensMeasurableSpace X] [PseudoMetricSpace Y]
  [CompactSpace Y] [MeasurableSpace Y] [OpensMeasurableSpace Y] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure X}
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure Y} {c : X × Y → ℝ} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] (hc : Continuous c) (hc0 : ∀ (z : X × Y), 0 ≤ c z) :
  (TauCeti.transportCost (fun z => ENNReal.ofReal (c z)) μ ν).toReal =
    sSup
      {r |
        ∃ φ ψ,
          Continuous φ ∧
            Continuous ψ ∧
              (∀ (x : X) (y : Y), φ x + ψ y ≤ c (x, y)) ∧ TauCeti.kantorovichDualValue μ ν φ ψ = r}
TauCeti.toReal_transportCost_eq_sSup.doc:
**Strong Kantorovich duality for probability measures**, read as an equality between the
primal value and the supremum of the dual values over the continuous potentials.

TauCeti.toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_bijective_.signature:
TauCeti.toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_bijective_of_isSimpleRing.{u_1, u_2} (R : Type u_1) [Ring R]
  (M : Type u_2) [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module R M] [IsSimpleRing R] [IsSemisimpleModule R M]
  [Nontrivial M] [Module.Finite (Module.End R M) M] :
  Function.Bijective ⇑(Module.toModuleEnd (Module.End R M) M)
TauCeti.toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_bijective_.doc:
**The double centralizer theorem for a simple ring.** A nontrivial semisimple module over a
simple ring is automatically faithful. If it is finite over its endomorphism ring `D`, it presents
`R` as `Module.End D M`.

TauCeti.toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_bijective.signature:
TauCeti.toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_bijective.{u_1, u_2} (R : Type u_1) [Ring R] (M : Type u_2)
  [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module R M] [IsSemisimpleModule R M] [FaithfulSMul R M]
  [Module.Finite (Module.End R M) M] : Function.Bijective ⇑(Module.toModuleEnd (Module.End R M) M)
TauCeti.toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_bijective.doc:
**The double centralizer theorem.** Let `M` be a faithful semisimple `R`-module which is finite
over its endomorphism ring `D = Module.End R M`. Then the natural map `R → Module.End D M` is
bijective: `R` is exactly the ring of `D`-linear endomorphisms of `M`.

This sharpens Mathlib's `Module.Finite.toModuleEnd_moduleEnd_surjective` from surjectivity to
bijectivity; the extra input is faithfulness, which is what makes the map injective.

TauCeti.thue_gap_principle.signature:
TauCeti.thue_gap_principle {α : ℂ} (hd : 2 ≤ (minpoly ℚ α).natDegree) {κ : ℝ}
  (hκ : ↑(minpoly ℚ α).natDegree / 2 + 1 < κ) :
  ∃ C lam,
    1 ≤ C ∧
      1 ≤ lam ∧
        ∀ (ξ₁ ξ : ℚ),
          ‖↑ξ₁ - α‖ ≤ Height.mulHeight₁ ξ₁ ^ (-κ) →
            C ≤ Height.mulHeight₁ ξ₁ →
              ‖↑ξ - α‖ ≤ Height.mulHeight₁ ξ ^ (-κ) →
                Height.mulHeight₁ ξ ≤ Height.mulHeight₁ ξ₁ ^ lam
TauCeti.thue_gap_principle.doc:
**Thue's gap principle** (Evertse, Theorem 6.14). Let `α` be a complex algebraic number of
degree `d ≥ 2` and let `κ > d / 2 + 1`. There are constants `C ≥ 1` and `λ ≥ 1` such that for
all rationals `ξ₁` and `ξ` with `|ξ₁ - α| ≤ H(ξ₁) ^ (-κ)`, `H(ξ₁) ≥ C` and
`|ξ - α| ≤ H(ξ) ^ (-κ)`, the heights satisfy `H(ξ) ≤ H(ξ₁) ^ λ`. The degree hypothesis
already forces `α` to be algebraic.

TauCeti.thue_approximation_real.signature:
TauCeti.thue_approximation_real {α : ℝ} (hd : 2 ≤ (minpoly ℚ α).natDegree) {κ : ℝ}
  (hκ : ↑(minpoly ℚ α).natDegree / 2 + 1 < κ) : {ξ | |↑ξ - α| ≤ Height.mulHeight₁ ξ ^ (-κ)}.Finite
TauCeti.thue_approximation_real.doc:
**Thue's approximation theorem** for real `α`. Let `α` be a real algebraic number of degree
`d ≥ 2` and let `κ > d / 2 + 1`. Then only finitely many rationals `ξ` satisfy
`|ξ - α| ≤ H(ξ) ^ (-κ)`. This is a variant of Evertse, Theorem 6.9, rather than that statement
verbatim: every degree `d ≥ 2` is allowed.

TauCeti.thue_approximation.signature:
TauCeti.thue_approximation {α : ℂ} (hd : 2 ≤ (minpoly ℚ α).natDegree) {κ : ℝ}
  (hκ : ↑(minpoly ℚ α).natDegree / 2 + 1 < κ) : {ξ | ‖↑ξ - α‖ ≤ Height.mulHeight₁ ξ ^ (-κ)}.Finite
TauCeti.thue_approximation.doc:
**Thue's approximation theorem**, for complex `α`. Let `α` be a complex algebraic number of
degree `d ≥ 2` and let `κ > d / 2 + 1`. Then only finitely many rationals `ξ` satisfy
`|ξ - α| ≤ H(ξ) ^ (-κ)`. This is a variant of Evertse, Theorem 6.9, rather than that statement
verbatim: here `α` may be complex and every degree `d ≥ 2` is allowed.

TauCeti.thickPart.signature:
TauCeti.thickPart.{u_1, u_2} (G : Type u_1) {X : Type u_2} [Group G] [PseudoMetricSpace X]
  [MulAction G X] (ε : ℝ) : Set X
TauCeti.thickPart.doc:
The **`ε`-thick part** of an action on a metric space: the points moved a distance at least
`ε` by every nonidentity element. For `0 < ε` it excludes every point with nontrivial
stabilizer.

TauCeti.tfae_forall_exists_dvd_sub_pow.signature:
TauCeti.tfae_forall_exists_dvd_sub_pow.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A] (π : A) {p : ℕ}

  (h : π ^ p ∣ ↑p) :
  [∀ (x : A), ∃ y, π ^ p ∣ x - y ^ p, ∀ (x : A), ∃ y, ↑p ∣ x - y ^ p,
      ∀ (x : A), ∃ y, π * ↑p ∣ x - y ^ p].TFAE
TauCeti.tfae_forall_exists_dvd_sub_pow.doc:
**The Frobenius surjectivity criterion** (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, *Integral p-adic Hodge
theory*, Lemma 3.9). In a `π`-adically complete and separated ring `A` with `π ^ p ∣ p`, the
following are equivalent: every element of `A` is a `p`-th power modulo `π ^ p`, modulo `p`, and
modulo `π p`.

TauCeti.tensorMultiplicity_eq_sum_weylSi.signature:
TauCeti.tensorMultiplicity_eq_sum_weylSign_mul_formalCharacter_coeff.{u, v} {K : Type u}
  {L : Type v} [Field K] [CharZero K] [IsAlgClosed K] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L]
  [LieAlgebra.IsKilling K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] {H : LieSubalgebra K L} [H.IsCartanSubalgebra]

`lam`, `mu`, and `nu`, `c^nu_{lam mu} = ∑_{w ∈ W} sgn(w) · [e^{nu - w ⬝ lam}] ch L(mu)`.

This is the Brauer–Klimyk formula
`TauCeti.isotypicMultiplicity_tensor_eq_sum_weylSign_mul_formalCharacter_coeff` for
`M = L(mu)`.

TauCeti.tensorMultiplicity_eq_coeff_form.signature:
TauCeti.tensorMultiplicity_eq_coeff_formalCharacter_mul_weylNumerator.{u, v} {K : Type u}
  {L : Type v} [Field K] [CharZero K] [IsAlgClosed K] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L]
  [LieAlgebra.IsKilling K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] {H : LieSubalgebra K L} [H.IsCartanSubalgebra]
  (b : (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H).Base)
  [Fintype ↥(LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H).weylGroup] {lam mu nu : Module.Dual K ↥H}
  (hlam : TauCeti.IsDominantIntegral b lam) (hmu : TauCeti.IsDominantIntegral b mu)
  (hnu : TauCeti.IsDominantIntegral b nu) :
  ↑(TauCeti.tensorMultiplicity b lam mu nu) =
    (TauCeti.formalCharacter K (↥H) (TauCeti.irreducibleQuotient b mu) *
          TauCeti.weylNumerator (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H) b lam).coeff
      nu
TauCeti.tensorMultiplicity_eq_coeff_form.doc:
**The Racah–Speiser formula, in group-algebra form**: for dominant integral weights `lam`,
`mu`, and `nu`, the tensor multiplicity `c^nu_{lam mu}` of `L(nu)` in `L(lam) ⊗ L(mu)` is the
coefficient at `nu` of `ch L(mu) · N(lam)`.

This is the Brauer–Klimyk formula
`TauCeti.isotypicMultiplicity_tensor_eq_coeff_formalCharacter_mul_weylNumerator` for
`M = L(mu)`.

TauCeti.tendsto_truncatedPerron_LSeries_.signature:
TauCeti.tendsto_truncatedPerron_LSeries_natCast {f : ℕ → ℂ} {c : ℝ} {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N)
  (hc : 0 < c) (h : LSeriesSummable f ↑c) :

**The arithmetic Perron formula at an integer endpoint.**  At `x = N` the truncated integral
tends to the sum of `f` below `N` together with half of the endpoint term.

to the series of sharp steps `∑' n, f n * perronStep (x / n)`.  This holds at every positive `x`,

**Šmulian's theorem**, relative form: every sequence in a relatively weakly compact subset of
a real or complex normed space has a subsequence converging weakly to some point of the space.

  {v : ℕ → T → X} {K : T → Set X} (hvK : ∀ (k : ℕ) (t : T), v k t ∈ K t)
  (hK :

  (hω : ∀ (t : T), Filter.Tendsto (ω t) (nhds t) (nhds 0)) :

TauCeti.tendsto_subseq_of_limsup_edist_l.doc:
**A refined Arzelà–Ascoli theorem** (Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré, Proposition 3.3.1). Let `l y` be
the filter of an auxiliary convergence `y_n ⇀ y` on a weak extended metric space `X`, for which
the distance is jointly sequentially lower semicontinuous. The topology of `X` need not be
induced by its extended distance; the auxiliary convergence is specified only by `l`. Let
`v k : T → X` be maps on a separable space `T` such that

* at each time `t`, the values `v k t` lie in a set `K t` in which every sequence has a
  `⇀`-convergent subsequence;
* `limsup_k d(v k s, v k t) ≤ ω s t`, where `ω t s → 0` as `s → t`.

Then a subsequence `v (ψ n)` converges pointwise for `⇀` to a map `u : T → X` with
`d(u s, u t) ≤ ω s t`. The maps `v k` need not be continuous.

TauCeti.tendsto_integral_cpow_mul_I_smul.signature:
TauCeti.tendsto_integral_cpow_mul_I_smul_atTop.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]

TauCeti.tendsto_integral_cpow_mul_I_smul.doc:
**Riemann--Lebesgue on a vertical line**: the integral of `f` against the oscillating factor
`x ^ (i t)` tends to `0` as `x → ∞`.

No hypothesis is needed on `f`. A limit along `atTop` only sees `x > 0`, and there the factor
`x ^ (i t)` has modulus `1`, so the integrand is integrable exactly when `f` is; when `f` is not
integrable both the left-hand side and the limit are `0`. (For `x ≤ 0` the equivalence fails —
at `x = 0` the integrand vanishes almost everywhere, and for `x < 0` the branch of the complex
power contributes a factor of modulus `exp (-π t)` — but those scales are irrelevant here.)

`μ` be a finite measure, and let the almost-everywhere measurable maps `T n, T₀ : X → Y` have

preconnected open set `U`, monotone at each point of `U` and bounded above at some point `x₀ ∈ U`.

`xᵢ = μᵢ + n - i`, the dimension is

TauCeti.sw2_eq_add_galoisEvens_add_cup_o.signature:

  (σ : L →ₐ[K] SeparableClosure K) (hfin : Module.finrank K L = 2) (a : Lˣ) {m n : ℕ}
  {t : Fin m → Kˣ} {b : Fin n → Kˣ}
  (ht :
    QuadraticMap.Equivalent (QuadraticMap.traceTransfer K QuadraticMap.sq)
      (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares K fun i => ↑(t i)))
  (hb :
    QuadraticMap.Equivalent (QuadraticMap.traceTransfer K (↑a • QuadraticMap.sq))
      (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares K fun i => ↑(b i))) :
  TauCeti.sw2 b =
    TauCeti.sw2 t + TauCeti.galoisEvens K L σ hfin (TauCeti.kummerClass a) +
      (((TauCeti.trivialF2TopPairing (TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup K)).cup 1 1) (TauCeti.sw1 t))
        ((CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom (TauCeti.galoisCor K L σ 1)) (TauCeti.kummerClass a))

**The relative Stiefel–Whitney formula in degree two, on diagonal presentations of the trace
forms**: for a quadratic extension `L/K` and `a ∈ Lˣ`, if `Tr_*⟨1⟩ ≅ ⟨t₁, …, tₘ⟩` and
`Tr_*⟨a⟩ ≅ ⟨b₁, …, bₙ⟩`, then `w₂(b) = w₂(t) + N^{Ev}((a)) + w₁(t) ∪ cor (a)`, with the Evens
norm and the corestriction taken along any `K`-embedding `σ` of `L` into a separable closure of
`K`. No regularity hypothesis is needed: isometry with a diagonal form with unit coefficients
already makes both trace forms regular.

      (((TauCeti.trivialF2TopPairing (TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup K)).cup 1 1)

Théorème 2 in degree two): for a quadratic extension `L/K`, which is separable as `2` is
invertible, and `a ∈ Lˣ` with Kummer class `(a) ∈ H¹(G_L, 𝔽₂)`,

```text
w₂(Tr_*⟨a⟩) = w₂(Tr_*⟨1⟩) + N^{Ev}((a)) + w₁(Tr_*⟨1⟩) ∪ cor (a),
```

where the Evens norm `N^{Ev}` and the corestriction `cor` are taken along any `K`-embedding `σ`
of `L` into a separable closure of `K`. The two sides are the classes of the regular forms
`y ↦ Tr_{L/K}(a y²)` and `y ↦ Tr_{L/K}(y²)` on `L`; their regularity is a hypothesis.

forms**: for a finite extension `L/K` and `a ∈ Lˣ`, if `Tr_*⟨1⟩ ≅ ⟨t₁, …, tₘ⟩` and

TauCeti.surjective_inclusionInDoubleDual.doc:
**Milman–Pettis theorem.** A uniformly convex Banach space is reflexive: its canonical map
into the continuous bidual is surjective.

TauCeti.supSeminorm.signature:
TauCeti.supSeminorm.{u_1, u_2} (K : Type u_1) [NontriviallyNormedField K] {A : Type u_2}

TauCeti.supSeminorm.doc:
The supremum seminorm `|f|sup` of `f : A`: the supremum of its absolute values `|f(x)|` at
the maximal ideals `x` of `A`. It is zero on the zero algebra, which has no maximal ideals.

TauCeti.summatory_mul_rpow_neg_le.signature:
TauCeti.summatory_mul_rpow_neg_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} (N : ι → ℕ) [Northcott N]
  (hN : ∀ (i : ι), 1 ≤ ↑(N i)) (w : ι → ℝ) {C α β x : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hβα : β ≠ α) (hx : 1 ≤ x)
  (hC : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 1 x, TauCeti.summatory N w t ≤ C * t ^ β) :
  TauCeti.summatory N (fun i => w i * ↑(N i) ^ (-α)) x ≤
    C * x ^ (β - α) + α * C * ((x ^ (β - α) - 1) / (β - α))
TauCeti.summatory_mul_rpow_neg_le.doc:
**A negative-power Abel bound.** Suppose every index has `N`-value at least `1`, and the
partial sums of a real weight `w` are at most `C * t ^ β` on `[1, x]`. Twisting the weight by
`(N i) ^ (-α)` with `α ≥ 0` gives partial sums at most
`C x ^ (β - α) + α C (x ^ (β - α) - 1) / (β - α)`.

For `β > α` this is `O(x ^ (β - α))`, and for `β < α` it is bounded uniformly in `x`. No sign
condition is imposed on `w`: only its partial sums are controlled.

TauCeti.summatory_mul_le_of_summatory_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} (N : ι → ℕ) [Northcott N] {a : ℝ}

  (hC : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc a x, TauCeti.summatory N w t ≤ C)
  (hg_diff : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc a x, DifferentiableAt ℝ g t)
  (hg_int : MeasureTheory.IntegrableOn (deriv g) (Set.Icc a x) MeasureTheory.volume)
  (hg_deriv : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc a x, deriv g t ≤ 0) (hg_nonneg : 0 ≤ g x) :
  TauCeti.summatory N (fun i => w i * g ↑(N i)) x ≤ C * g a
TauCeti.summatory_mul_le_of_summatory_le.doc:

let `g` be nonincreasing on `[a, x]` with `0 ≤ g x`.  If the summatory function of a real weight `w`
is at most `C` at every cutoff in `[a, x]`, then the summatory function at `x` of the twisted weight
`i ↦ w i * g (N i)` is at most `C * g a`.

No sign condition is imposed on `w` or on `C`: only the partial sums of `w` are controlled.

**Taylor's formula with divided-difference remainder.** For every function `f` and every `n`,
`f b = Σ_{j<n} (b - a)^j • c_j + (b - a)^n • q_n b`, where `c_j = (swap dslope a)^[j] f a` and
`q_n = (swap dslope a)^[n] f`. This is `n` applications of `f b = f a + (b - a) • dslope f a b`.
When the `c_j` vanish this is Mathlib's `pow_sub_smul_iterate_dslope_of_zero`.

TauCeti.subsingleton_setOf_mem_contactSe.doc:
**The twist theorem at a point.** Suppose the cost is twisted at `x`: the map
`y ↦ Dₓ c (x, y)` is injective on the set of `y` for which the section `c (·, y)` is
differentiable at `x`. If the potential is differentiable at `x`, finite near `x`, and satisfies
the dual constraint near `x`, and the cost sections of the contact partners of `x` are
differentiable at `x`, then `x` has at most one contact partner.

homotopy groups `π_ k X x` are trivial.

TauCeti.sub_one_mul_padicValNat_factoria.signature:
TauCeti.sub_one_mul_padicValNat_factorial_pow (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (k : ℕ) :

TauCeti.sub_one_mul_padicValNat_factoria.doc:
**Legendre's formula for `(pᵏ)!`.** Since `pᵏ` has base-`p` digit sum one,
`(p - 1) v_p((pᵏ)!) = pᵏ - 1`.

TauCeti.sub_le_fenchelConjugate.signature:
TauCeti.sub_le_fenchelConjugate.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [AddCommMonoid E]

TauCeti.sub_le_fenchelConjugate.doc:
**The Fenchel–Young inequality**, in the form that holds with no hypothesis: every point of `E`
bounds the conjugate from below.

TauCeti.sub_algebraMap_eq_sum_mul_sub_al.signature:

TauCeti.sub_algebraMap_eq_sum_mul_sub_al.doc:
**Hadamard's identity in the algebra of smooth functions.** A pointwise factorization of
`g - g x` through the functions `c i`, with coefficients `a i`, is an identity between the bundled
smooth maps themselves, the constants appearing as the images of `algebraMap`.

This is the pointwise-to-bundled transport: the hypothesis speaks of values, the conclusion of
elements of `C^n⟮I, M; 𝕜⟯`, and the two are related by evaluation being a ring homomorphism.

TauCeti.strictCohomologicalDimensionLE_i.signature:
TauCeti.strictCohomologicalDimensionLE_iff_forall_openSubgroup.{u} {p : ℕ} {G : Type u} [Group G]

TauCeti.strictCohomologicalDimensionLE_i.doc:
**The strict cohomological dimension through integral coefficients** (NSW (3.3.4)), as
vanishing predicates. For a profinite group `G` and a prime `p`,
`StrictCohomologicalDimensionLE p G n` holds if and only if `CohomologicalDimensionLE p G n` holds
and the `p`-primary component of `Hⁿ⁺¹(U, ℤ)` vanishes for every open subgroup `U`, the integers
carrying the trivial action.

TauCeti.steinerSymmetrization.signature:
TauCeti.steinerSymmetrization.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  (e : E) (he : ‖e‖ = 1) (s : Set E) : Set E
TauCeti.steinerSymmetrization.doc:
Steiner symmetrization along the unit direction `e`, centered on its orthogonal hyperplane.
The section of length `ℓ` is the open centered interval of radius `ℓ / 2`; this includes
empty intervals for `ℓ = 0` and the whole line for `ℓ = ∞`.

TauCeti.stdPeterWeylBasis.signature:
TauCeti.stdPeterWeylBasis.{u_1, u_2} (𝕜 : Type u_1) (G : Type u_2) [RCLike 𝕜] [IsAlgClosed 𝕜]

  [BorelSpace G] :
  HilbertBasis ((i : TauCeti.IrrepClass 𝕜 G) × Fin i.model.dim × Fin i.model.dim) 𝕜
    ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp 𝕜 2 (TauCeti.haarProb G))
TauCeti.stdPeterWeylBasis.doc:
**The Peter-Weyl theorem, unconditionally.** The normalized matrix coefficients of the models
chosen in the unitary equivalence classes are a Hilbert basis of `L²(G)`, indexed by
`Σ i, Fin (IrrepClass.model i).dim × Fin (IrrepClass.model i).dim`. No skeleton is assumed:
`isIrrepSkeleton_model` supplies one.

`TauCeti.coe_stdPeterWeylBasis` identifies the elements of this basis with
`TauCeti.peterWeylFamily IrrepClass.model`.

TauCeti.standardPolytabloidBasis.signature:
TauCeti.standardPolytabloidBasis (μ : YoungDiagram) :
  Module.Basis (TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau μ) ℚ ↥(TauCeti.spechtSubrepresentation μ).toSubmodule
TauCeti.standardPolytabloidBasis.doc:
**The standard basis theorem.**  The polytabloids of the standard `μ`-tableaux are a basis of
the Specht module `S^μ`: they are linearly independent by
`TauCeti.linearIndependent_polytabloid` and they span by
`TauCeti.spechtSubrepresentation_eq_span_standard`.

TauCeti.standardCount_mul_prod_factorial.signature:
TauCeti.standardCount_mul_prod_factorial_betaNumber (μ : YoungDiagram) {r : ℕ}
  (hr : μ.colLen 0 ≤ r) :
  TauCeti.standardCount μ * ∏ i ∈ Finset.range r, (μ.betaNumber r i).factorial =
    μ.card.factorial *
      ∏ k ∈ Finset.range r, ∏ l ∈ Finset.Ico (k + 1) r, (μ.betaNumber r k - μ.betaNumber r l)
TauCeti.standardCount_mul_prod_factorial.doc:
**The Frobenius determinant formula** for the number `f^μ` of standard Young tableaux of shape
`μ`: for any bound `r` on the number of rows, `f^μ` times the product of the factorials of the
beta-numbers is `μ.card !` times the product of their differences over the ordered pairs of rows.

The differences are differences of natural numbers, and are truncated at no ordered pair: the
beta-numbers strictly decrease across `k < l < r`.

This is the multiplicative form of `f^μ = n ! * ∏_{k < l} (β_k - β_l) / ∏_k β_k !`, and carries no
division obligation.

TauCeti.sq_setAverage_norm_le_setAverage.doc:
**Jensen's inequality for the square of a mean.** On a set `s` of finite nonzero measure, the
square of the mean of `‖g‖` is at most the mean of `‖g‖²`.

TauCeti.sq_norm_sub_sub_mul_sq_norm_one_.signature:
TauCeti.sq_norm_sub_sub_mul_sq_norm_one_sub_conj_mul (a z : ℂ) (t : ℝ)
  (hD : 1 - t ^ 2 * ‖a‖ ^ 2 ≠ 0) :
  ‖z - a‖ ^ 2 - t ^ 2 * ‖1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z‖ ^ 2 =
    (1 - t ^ 2 * ‖a‖ ^ 2) *
      (‖z - TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicCenter a t‖ ^ 2 - TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicRadius a t ^ 2)
TauCeti.sq_norm_sub_sub_mul_sq_norm_one_.doc:
**The Apollonius identity for the Moebius factor.** For every `z : ℂ`,

`‖z - a‖ ^ 2 - t ^ 2 * ‖1 - conj a * z‖ ^ 2`
`  = (1 - t ^ 2 * ‖a‖ ^ 2)`
`      * (‖z - pseudoHyperbolicCenter a t‖ ^ 2 - pseudoHyperbolicRadius a t ^ 2)`.

Both sides are real quadratics in `z.re` and `z.im` with the same leading coefficient
`1 - t ^ 2 * ‖a‖ ^ 2`, and the definitions of `TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicCenter` and
`TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicRadius` are exactly what completes the square. No hypothesis is placed on
`z`, and the disc hypothesis on `a` enters only through the nonvanishing of the denominator.

TauCeti.sq_le_mul_one_add_div_pow_of_sq_.signature:
TauCeti.sq_le_mul_one_add_div_pow_of_sq_le_mul_sub {D d e : ℕ → ℝ} {τ τ' A : ℝ} (hτ : 0 < τ)
  (hττ' : 4 * τ ≤ τ') (hD0 : D 0 = 0) (hD : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 ≤ D n)
  (htri : ∀ (n : ℕ), D (n + 1) ≤ D n + d n) (hstep : ∀ (n : ℕ), d n ^ 2 ≤ 2 * τ * (e n - e (n + 1)))
  (hcoer : ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 * τ' * (A - e n) ≤ D n ^ 2) (n : ℕ) :
  D n ^ 2 ≤ 2 * τ' * (e 0 - A) * (1 + 8 * τ / τ') ^ n
TauCeti.sq_le_mul_one_add_div_pow_of_sq_.doc:
**Discrete Grönwall bound under coercivity.** Let `D n ≥ 0` with `D 0 = 0` grow by steps
`D (n + 1) ≤ D n + d n` whose squared lengths are paid for by an energy `e`,
`d n ² ≤ 2τ (e n - e (n + 1))`, and let the energy satisfy the coercivity bound
`2τ' (A - e n) ≤ D n ²`, where `4τ ≤ τ'`. Then `D n ² ≤ 2τ' (e 0 - A) (1 + 8τ / τ')ⁿ`.

With `c = τ + τ' / 4`, the quantity `N n = D n ² + 2c (e n - A)` dominates `D n ² / 2` by the
coercivity bound, and grows at most by the factor `1 + 8τ / τ'` per step by the triangle
inequality, Young's inequality and the energy decrease along a step.

TauCeti.spectralRadius_eq_gelfandRadius_.signature:
TauCeti.spectralRadius_eq_gelfandRadius_toLp_inr.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [NonUnitalNormedRing A]
  [NormedSpace ℂ A] [IsScalarTower ℂ A A] [SMulCommClass ℂ A A] [CompleteSpace A] (a : A) :
  spectralRadius ℂ a = ENNReal.ofReal (gelfandRadius (WithLp.toLp 1 ↑a))
TauCeti.spectralRadius_eq_gelfandRadius_.doc:
**Gelfand's formula** in a nonunital complex Banach algebra: the spectral radius of `a`,
computed from its quasispectrum, is the Gelfand radius of its image in the ℓ¹ unitization.

TauCeti.spechtSubrepresentation_le_or_le.signature:
TauCeti.spechtSubrepresentation_le_or_le_orthogonal (μ : YoungDiagram)
  (U : Subrepresentation (TauCeti.permutationModule (TauCeti.shapePartition μ)).ρ) :
  TauCeti.spechtSubrepresentation μ ≤ U ∨
    U ≤ TauCeti.orthogonalSubrepresentation (TauCeti.spechtSubrepresentation μ)
TauCeti.spechtSubrepresentation_le_or_le.doc:
**James's submodule theorem.**  A subrepresentation `U` of the Young permutation module `M^μ`
either contains the Specht module `S^μ` or is orthogonal to it for the tabloid form.

The dichotomy is whether some column antisymmetrizer `b_t` fails to annihilate some vector of `U`.
If it does fail, the value is a nonzero multiple of the polytabloid `e_t` and lies in `U`, so `U`
contains the orbit of `e_t`, which spans `S^μ`.  If every `b_t` annihilates every vector of `U`,
then self-adjointness of `b_t` moves it off each polytabloid `e_t = b_t · {t}` and onto the vector
of `U`, where it vanishes.

After identifying tensor-induced trivial `𝔽₂` coefficients with the ambient trivial
coefficient object, the class of an invariant diagonal cocycle does not depend on the transversal.

**The Evens norm of a cocycle**: for a homogeneous cocycle `z` of degree `n` of the total
coinduced resolution of `A`, fixed by `U`, the class in `H^{l n}(G, Ind⊗ A)` of its diagonal

`TauCeti.smoothTensorInducedGradedResolutionContraction` for some order on the cosets; by
`TauCeti.smoothTensorInducedDiagonalClass_eq` it does not depend on that order.

TauCeti.smoothCommHopfAlgProperty_of_cha.signature:
TauCeti.smoothCommHopfAlgProperty_of_charZero.{u, v} (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharZero k]
  (H : CommHopfAlgCat k) [Algebra.FiniteType k ↑H] : TauCeti.smoothCommHopfAlgProperty k H
TauCeti.smoothCommHopfAlgProperty_of_cha.doc:
**Cartier's theorem**: a finite-type commutative Hopf algebra over a field of characteristic
zero is smooth. Equivalently, every affine group scheme of finite type over such a field is
smooth.

TauCeti.slodowySlice.signature:
TauCeti.slodowySlice.{u_1, u_2} (R : Type u_1) {L : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [LieRing L]
  [LieAlgebra R L] (e f : L) : AffineSubspace R L
TauCeti.slodowySlice.doc:
**The Slodowy slice** `e + ker (ad f)`, as an affine subspace of `L`. When `(h, e, f)` is an
`sl₂` triple in a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero, its direction
`ker (ad f)` is complementary to `[L, e]` (`IsSl2Triple.isCompl_range_ad_e_ker_ad_f`). For `f = 0`,
in particular in the degenerate case `e = f = 0`, it is all of `L`
(`TauCeti.slodowySlice_zero_right`).

TauCeti.skolemNoether.signature:
TauCeti.skolemNoether.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (K : Type u_1) {A : Type u_2} {B : Type u_3} [Field K]
  [Ring A] [Algebra K A] [Ring B] [Algebra K B] [IsSimpleRing A] [FiniteDimensional K A]
  [Algebra.IsCentral K B] [IsSimpleRing B] (f g : B →ₐ[K] A) : ∃ u, ∀ (x : B), g x = ↑u * f x * ↑u⁻¹
TauCeti.skolemNoether.doc:
**The Skolem-Noether theorem.** Two `K`-algebra homomorphisms `f g : B →ₐ[K] A` from a
finite-dimensional **central simple** `K`-algebra `B` to a finite-dimensional **simple** `K`-algebra
`A` are conjugate: there is a unit `u` of `A` with `g x = u * f x * u⁻¹` for all `x : B`.

Finite-dimensionality of `B` is not among the hypotheses: it follows from them, because `f` is
injective, `B` being simple and `A` nontrivial. The proof does use it, to make `B ⊗[K] Aᵐᵒᵖ`
Artinian, and with it the classification of modules that produces the conjugating isomorphism.

TauCeti.singularCubicalHomologyNatIso.signature:
TauCeti.singularCubicalHomologyNatIso.{u} (k : Type u) [Ring k] (n : ℕ) :
  (TauCeti.singularChains k).comp
      (HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) n) ≅
    (TauCeti.normalizedCubicalChainComplex k).comp
      (HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) n)
TauCeti.singularCubicalHomologyNatIso.doc:
**Cubical singular homology is naturally isomorphic to singular homology**, as functors on
topological spaces.

TauCeti.singularChainsResolution.signature:
TauCeti.singularChainsResolution.{u} (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (E : TopCat) (G : Type u) [Group G]
  [MulAction G ↑E] [ContinuousConstSMul G ↑E] [IsCancelSMul G ↑E] [ContractibleSpace ↑E] :
  CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution (Rep.trivial k G k)
TauCeti.singularChainsResolution.doc:
**The singular chains of a contractible free `G`-space are a projective resolution** of the
trivial representation of `G` over `k`: `G` acts freely on singular simplices, so the terms are
free over the group ring, and the augmented singular chain complex of a contractible space is
exact.

TauCeti.simplyConnectedSpace_sphere.signature:
TauCeti.simplyConnectedSpace_sphere.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  (h : 2 < Module.rank ℝ E) (c : E) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) : SimplyConnectedSpace ↑(Metric.sphere c r)
TauCeti.simplyConnectedSpace_sphere.doc:
Every sphere of nonnegative radius in a real normed space of rank greater than two is
simply connected.

TauCeti.simplyConnectedSpace_of_interior.signature:
TauCeti.simplyConnectedSpace_of_interior_union.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X]
  {A B : Set X} (hCover : interior A ∪ interior B = Set.univ) (hAB : IsPathConnected (A ∩ B))
  [SimplyConnectedSpace ↑A] [SimplyConnectedSpace ↑B] : SimplyConnectedSpace X
TauCeti.simplyConnectedSpace_of_interior.doc:
**Two-set van Kampen criterion for simple connectedness.** A space covered by the interiors of
two simply connected sets with path-connected intersection is simply connected.

TauCeti.simple_indFDRep_ofLinearCharacte.signature:
TauCeti.simple_indFDRep_ofLinearCharacter_iff_of_conj_eq_inv.{u} {k G : Type u} [Field k] [Group G]

TauCeti.simple_indFDRep_ofLinearCharacte.doc:
**The Mackey criterion for a linear character of an inverted subgroup of index two:** the
induced representation is irreducible exactly when some value of `χ` is not a square root of `1`.
Conjugation by any element outside `N` inverts it, by
`TauCeti.conj_eq_inv_of_notMem_of_index_two`, so `{}^s χ = χ⁻¹` for every such `s` and the
criterion becomes the single condition `χ ≠ χ⁻¹`.  The inversion hypothesis is asked of the one
outside element `s` only.

TauCeti.simple_indFDRep_ofLinearCharacte.doc:
**The Mackey irreducibility criterion for an induced linear character.**  For a normal
subgroup `N ◁ G` and a linear character `χ : N →* kˣ`, the induced representation `Ind_N^G χ` is
irreducible exactly when **no element of `G` outside `N` stabilizes `χ`**: for every `s ∉ N` some
`x ∈ N` has `χ (s x s⁻¹) ≠ χ x`.

The irreducibility of `χ` itself, which the general criterion also asks for, is automatic: a line
has no proper nonzero subrepresentation.

TauCeti.simple_indFDRep_iff_of_normal.doc:
**The Mackey irreducibility criterion for a normal subgroup.** If `H ◁ G`, then the
representation induced from `A` is irreducible exactly when `A` is irreducible and none of its
conjugates `{}^s A`, for `s ∉ H`, is isomorphic to `A`.

TauCeti.simple_indFDRep_iff_doubleCoset.doc:
**The Mackey irreducibility criterion.** The representation induced from `A` is irreducible
exactly when `A` is irreducible and every double coset `HsH` other than `H` itself, read at its
chosen representative, is Mackey disjoint. Algebraic closure supplies scalar Schur.

**The Mackey irreducibility criterion, elementwise.** The disjointness condition of
`TauCeti.simple_indFDRep_iff_doubleCoset` may equally be asked of every element `s ∉ H` rather than
of one chosen representative of every nonidentity double coset.

The signed checked representation of the braid group on the word space `(Fin n → ι) →₀ R`:
the elementary braid `σ i` acts by the signed checked R-matrix on the strands `i` and `i + 1`.
