R-matrix is the Jimbo R-matrix at the parameter `-s`, rescaled by `-s`, on the alphabet with the
reversed order: it is the conjugate of `(-s) • T_{-s}` on `(Fin n → ιᵒᵈ) →₀ R` by the relabelling
of words along `ι ≃ ιᵒᵈ`.

TauCeti.signedCheckedR_braid.doc:
The braid relation for signed checked R-matrices on two pairs of strands sharing the strand
`k`, the Yang-Baxter equation for the signed checked R-matrix.

  (hxy : x - θ₂ * y ≠ 0) :
  (θ₁ - θ₂) / (θ₁ - θ₀) * ((x - θ₀ * y) / (x - θ₂ * y)) +
      (θ₂ - θ₀) / (θ₁ - θ₀) * ((x - θ₁ * y) / (x - θ₂ * y)) =
    1
TauCeti.siegel_identity.doc:
**Siegel's identity.** For `θ₁ ≠ θ₀` and `x - θ₂ y ≠ 0` in a field,
`(θ₁ - θ₂) / (θ₁ - θ₀) · (x - θ₀ y) / (x - θ₂ y) + (θ₂ - θ₀) / (θ₁ - θ₀) · (x - θ₁ y) / (x - θ₂ y)`
equals `1`. Applied to the linear factors of a binary form, it turns a Thue equation into unit
equations.

  (i : V → E) (x : V) (ν : E) : Module.End ℝ V
TauCeti.shapeOperator.doc:
The **shape operator** `S_ν` of `i : V → E` at `x` in the direction `ν`: the endomorphism of
`V` with `⟪Di(x) (S_ν v), Di(x) w⟫ = ⟪ν, B(v, w)⟫` for all `v` and `w`, where `B` is the second
fundamental form. It is defined when `Di(x)` is injective, so that the induced metric
`⟪Di(x) v, Di(x) w⟫` is nondegenerate, and is `0` otherwise.

locally integrable on a convex open set `Ω` and let `S ⊆ Ω` have finite positive measure. Then
`∫_Ω |u - ⨍_S u| ≤ (∫_{Ω - Ω} ‖h‖) / μ(S) · |Du|(Ω)`. Both sides may be infinite.

compactly supported `C¹` function `g` and a direction `v`, the integral of `∂_v g` over the
half-space `{x | ⟪x, ν⟫ < c}` is the integral of `g` over the boundary hyperplane against
`(n - 1)`-dimensional Hausdorff measure, weighted by the normal component `⟪v, ν⟫` of `v`.

TauCeti.setIntegral_rect_eq_setIntegral_.doc:
**The fundamental theorem of calculus in the second coordinate.** The integral of a
continuous partial derivative `φ = ∂₂ Φ` over the rectangle `[a₁, b₁] × [a₂, b₂]` is the integral
over `[a₁, b₁]` of the difference of the values of `Φ` on the two horizontal sides.

**The fundamental theorem of calculus in the first coordinate.** The integral of a continuous
partial derivative `φ = ∂₁ Φ` over the rectangle `[a₁, b₁] × [a₂, b₂]` is the integral over
`[a₂, b₂]` of the difference of the values of `Φ` on the two vertical sides.

TauCeti.setIntegral_normalHalfSpace_fder.doc:
**The divergence theorem on a half-space.** For a compactly supported `C¹` function `g` on
`ℝ × E` and a direction `v`, the integral of the directional derivative `∂_v g` over the half-space
`{x | a < x.fst}` is the boundary integral of `g` over `{a} × E`, weighted by `⟪v, -e₁⟫ = -v.fst`,
the normal component of `v` along the outward unit normal.

TauCeti.semilocallySimplyConnectedSpace_.doc:
**A path-connected, locally path-connected space is semilocally simply connected if and only
if it admits a simply connected covering space.**

The forward direction is the universal-cover construction, the reverse direction is
`TauCeti.SemilocallySimplyConnectedSpace.of_isCoveringMap`; surjectivity of the covering map is
automatic here, by `IsCoveringMap.comp_subtypeVal_pathComponent_surjective`, because the base is
path-connected and a simply connected total space is nonempty.

TauCeti.semilocalEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.semilocalEquiv.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K] (L : Type u_2) [Field L]
  [NumberField L] [Algebra K L]
  (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) :
  TensorProduct K (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.adicCompletion K v)
      L ≃ₐ[IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.adicCompletion K v]
    (w : { w // w.asIdeal.LiesOver v.asIdeal }) →
      IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.adicCompletion L ↑w
TauCeti.semilocalEquiv.doc:
**The semi-local decomposition** `K_v ⊗[K] L ≃ₐ[K_v] ∏_{w ∣ v} L_w`: completing `L` at the
finitely many places above a finite place `v` of `K` decomposes the scalar extension of `L` to
`K_v` into the product of those completions.

TauCeti.semianalyticAt_iff_exists_iUnion.signature:
TauCeti.semianalyticAt_iff_exists_iUnion.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] {s : Set E} {x : E} :
  TauCeti.SemianalyticAt s x ↔
    ∃ U ∈ nhds x,
      ∃ m k f g,
        (∀ (i : Fin m), AnalyticOnNhd ℝ (f i) U) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin m) (j : Fin k), AnalyticOnNhd ℝ (g i j) U) ∧
            s ∩ U = (⋃ i, {y | f i y = 0} ∩ ⋂ j, {y | 0 < g i j y}) ∩ U
TauCeti.semianalyticAt_iff_exists_iUnion.doc:
**Equivalence of presentations.** A set is semianalytic at `x` if and only if, on some
neighbourhood `U` of `x`, it agrees with a finite union of sets
`{y | f y = 0 ∧ 0 < g₁ y ∧ ⋯ ∧ 0 < gₖ y}` with `f, g₁, …, gₖ` analytic on `U`.

TauCeti.selfStabilizationOrdinal_eq_iSup.doc:
The least simultaneous stabilization level is the supremum of the orbit ranks
of all finite tuples. This holds for arbitrary structures.

TauCeti.scott_isomorphism.signature:
TauCeti.scott_isomorphism.{u, v, w, w'} {L : FirstOrder.Language}
  [Countable ((k : ℕ) × L.Functions k)] [Countable ((k : ℕ) × L.Relations k)] (M : Type w)
  [L.Structure M] [Countable M] :
  ∃ σ,
    FirstOrder.Language.SentenceInf.Realize σ M ∧
      ∀ (N : Type w') [inst : L.Structure N] [Countable N],
        FirstOrder.Language.SentenceInf.Realize σ N ↔ Nonempty (L.Equiv M N)
TauCeti.scott_isomorphism.doc:
**Scott's isomorphism theorem.** In a countable language, every countable structure `M` has
an `Lω₁ω` sentence that `M` satisfies and that holds in a countable structure, in any universe,
exactly when that structure is isomorphic to `M`.

Function symbols are allowed: the sentence is the back-translation of the Scott sentence of the
graph expansion of `M`.

TauCeti.schwarzRearrangement.signature:
TauCeti.schwarzRearrangement.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E) (f : E → ENNReal) (x : E) : ENNReal
TauCeti.schwarzRearrangement.doc:
The **Schwarz rearrangement** of `f : E → ℝ≥0∞` with respect to `μ`: the radially
nonincreasing function whose superlevel set `{t < f*}` is `{x | μ (ball 0 ‖x‖) < μ {t < f}}`.
For an additive Haar measure on a nontrivial finite-dimensional real normed space, this is the
centered open ball of the same measure when `μ {t < f}` is finite, and the whole space when it is
infinite.

TauCeti.schurPoly_mul_alternant.signature:
TauCeti.schurPoly_mul_alternant.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] {σ : Type u_2} [Fintype σ]
  {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) (hμ : (YoungDiagram.ofPartition μ).colLen 0 ≤ Fintype.card σ) :
  TauCeti.schurPoly σ R μ *
      (MvPolynomial.rename ⇑(Fintype.equivFin σ).symm)
        (TauCeti.alternant (Fin (Fintype.card σ)) R fun j => Fintype.card σ - 1 - ↑j) =
    (MvPolynomial.rename ⇑(Fintype.equivFin σ).symm)
      (TauCeti.alternant (Fin (Fintype.card σ)) R fun j =>
        (YoungDiagram.ofPartition μ).betaNumber (Fintype.card σ) ↑j)
TauCeti.schurPoly_mul_alternant.doc:
**Jacobi's bialternant formula for partitions.** In a finite alphabet `σ`, ordered by
`Fintype.equivFin σ`, the Schur polynomial of `μ` times the renamed staircase alternant equals
the renamed alternant of the beta-numbers of its Young diagram.

TauCeti.schurPoly_eq_det_hsymmInt.signature:
TauCeti.schurPoly_eq_det_hsymmInt.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] {σ : Type u_2} [Fintype σ]
  [DecidableEq σ] {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) {r : ℕ} (hr : μ.parts.card ≤ r) :
  TauCeti.schurPoly σ R μ =
    (Matrix.of fun i j =>
        TauCeti.hsymmInt σ R (↑((YoungDiagram.ofPartition μ).rowLen ↑i) - ↑↑i + ↑↑j)).det
TauCeti.schurPoly_eq_det_hsymmInt.doc:
**The Jacobi--Trudi identity for partitions.**  In a finite alphabet `σ`, the Schur polynomial
of a partition `μ` is `det (h_{μᵢ - i + j})_{0 ≤ i, j < r}` for every `r` at least the number of
parts of `μ`, where `μᵢ` is the `i`-th largest part (`0` past the last part) and `h_m = 0` for
`m < 0`.

TauCeti.scalarCurvature_sphereRoundMetri.signature:
TauCeti.scalarCurvature_sphereRoundMetricOfRadius.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] {n : ℕ} [Fact (Module.finrank ℝ E = n + 1)] {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r)
  (p : ↑(Metric.sphere 0 1)) :
  (TauCeti.sphereRoundMetricOfRadius r hr).scalarCurvature p = ↑n * (↑n - 1) / r ^ 2
TauCeti.scalarCurvature_sphereRoundMetri.doc:
**Scalar curvature of the round sphere.** The round `n`-sphere of radius `r` has scalar
curvature `n (n - 1) / r²`.

TauCeti.sUnitsRatMulEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.sUnitsRatMulEquiv {S : Finset ℕ} (hS : ∀ p ∈ S, Nat.Prime p) :
  ↥({v | ↑(Rat.HeightOneSpectrum.primesEquiv v) ∈ S}.unit ℚ) ≃* ℤˣ × Multiplicative (↥S → ℤ)
TauCeti.sUnitsRatMulEquiv.doc:
**The structure of the rational `S`-units.** If `S` consists of primes, the map
`x ↦ (sign x, (v_p(x))_{p ∈ S})` is an isomorphism from the rational `S`-units to
`ℤˣ × Multiplicative (S → ℤ)`; its inverse sends `(ε, z)` to `ε ∏_{p ∈ S} p ^ z_p`
(`TauCeti.coe_sUnitsRatMulEquiv_symm_apply`).

TauCeti.rpow_lintegral_le_measure_univ_r.signature:
TauCeti.rpow_lintegral_le_measure_univ_rpow_mul.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace α]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {u : α → ENNReal} (hu : AEMeasurable u μ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) :
  (∫⁻ (x : α), u x ∂μ) ^ r ≤ μ Set.univ ^ (r - 1) * ∫⁻ (x : α), u x ^ r ∂μ
TauCeti.rpow_lintegral_le_measure_univ_r.doc:
**Hölder's inequality in extended-valued `∫⁻` form**, raised to the power `r`: the `L¹`
integral of `u : α → ℝ≥0∞` is controlled by its `L^r` integral at the cost of the factor
`μ univ ^ (r - 1)`.  Stated for an `ℝ≥0∞`-valued `u`, so a norm-valued application passes
`fun x => ‖f x‖ₑ` and needs only that this composite is measurable.

On a finite measure space this is the nesting `L^r ⊆ L¹`; for a general `μ` it is only the
displayed inequality, which does not by itself give that inclusion.  No finiteness is assumed, and
the bound is not vacuous when `μ univ = ∞`: arithmetic in `ℝ≥0∞` makes the right-hand side `0`
rather than `∞` whenever `∫⁻ ‖f‖ₑ ^ r = 0`, and the inequality still holds there because `f` then
vanishes almost everywhere.

TauCeti.roundSphereVolume_eq_two_mul_pi_.doc: **The area of the unit round sphere**: `|Sⁿ| = 2 π ^ ((n + 1) / 2) / Γ((n + 1) / 2)`.

TauCeti.rouche_windingNumber_comp.signature:
TauCeti.rouche_windingNumber_comp {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
  (hγ : TauCeti.IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
  (hfa : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, AnalyticAt ℂ f (γ t)) (hga : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, AnalyticAt ℂ g (γ t))
  (hs : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, ‖f (γ t) - g (γ t)‖ < ‖f (γ t)‖) :
  TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber (f ∘ γ) a b 0 = TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber (g ∘ γ) a b 0
TauCeti.rouche_windingNumber_comp.doc:
**Rouché's theorem as an equality of image winding numbers**, classical form. Under
`‖f (γ t) - g (γ t)‖ < ‖f (γ t)‖` along a closed piecewise-`C¹` curve, the image curves `f ∘ γ`
and `g ∘ γ` wind equally often about the origin. This is the special case of
`TauCeti.rouche_symm_windingNumber_comp` obtained by discarding the nonnegative summand
`‖g (γ t)‖`.

TauCeti.rouche_symm_windingNumber_comp.signature:
TauCeti.rouche_symm_windingNumber_comp {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
  (hγ : TauCeti.IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
  (hfa : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, AnalyticAt ℂ f (γ t)) (hga : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, AnalyticAt ℂ g (γ t))
  (hs : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, ‖f (γ t) - g (γ t)‖ < ‖f (γ t)‖ + ‖g (γ t)‖) :
  TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber (f ∘ γ) a b 0 = TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber (g ∘ γ) a b 0
TauCeti.rouche_symm_windingNumber_comp.doc:
**Rouché's theorem as an equality of image winding numbers, symmetric form** — the "dog on a
leash" statement. If `f` and `g` are analytic along a closed piecewise-`C¹` curve `γ` and never
point in opposite directions there, the image curves `f ∘ γ` and `g ∘ γ` wind equally often about
the origin.

Read through `TauCeti.argumentPrinciple_windingNumber_of_analyticOnNhd`, this is the geometric face
of `TauCeti.rouche_symm_nullHomologous_of_analyticOnNhd`; on its own it is *stronger*, since apart
from analyticity at each point of the curve — `AnalyticAt`, hence on some neighbourhood of that
point — only the behaviour of the two functions **along the curve** enters: no single ambient open
set carrying both, no confinement of the zeros to a finite set, and no null-homology. That is
because the equality of the two logarithmic-derivative integrals is already forced by the
hypothesis: it
puts `g / f` in `Complex.slitPlane`, where `Complex.log` is a single-valued primitive. It is only
in *counting* the winding that those extra hypotheses are needed.

TauCeti.rouche_symm_nullHomologous_of_an.signature:
TauCeti.rouche_symm_nullHomologous_of_analyticOnNhd {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ}
  {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f U) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g U)
  (hfS : ∀ z ∈ U, f z = 0 → z ∈ S) (hgS : ∀ z ∈ U, g z = 0 → z ∈ S)
  (hγ : TauCeti.IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) (hγU : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
  (hnull : TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous γ a b U)
  (hs : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, ‖f (γ t) - g (γ t)‖ < ‖f (γ t)‖ + ‖g (γ t)‖) :
  ∑ z ∈ S, TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber γ a b z * ↑(analyticOrderNatAt f z) =
    ∑ z ∈ S, TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber γ a b z * ↑(analyticOrderNatAt g z)
TauCeti.rouche_symm_nullHomologous_of_an.doc:
**Rouché's theorem for a null-homologous cycle**, holomorphic form. Let `f` and `g` be analytic
on an open set `U` with all their zeros in a finite set `S`, and let `γ` be a closed piecewise-`C¹`
curve in `U`, null-homologous in `U`, along which `‖f (γ t) - g (γ t)‖ < ‖f (γ t)‖ + ‖g (γ t)‖`.
Then `f` and `g` have the same zero count enclosed by `γ`, each zero counted with its multiplicity
and with the winding number of `γ` about it.

The curve is not required to miss `S`: the hypothesis already forces both functions to be zero-free
along it, so it may run through the non-zeros that `S` happens to list. This is the holomorphic
specialization of `TauCeti.rouche_symm_nullHomologous`, with the orders read off by
`analyticOrderNatAt` instead of supplied by the caller.

TauCeti.rouche_symm_nullHomologous.signature:
TauCeti.rouche_symm_nullHomologous {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
  {ordf ordg : ℂ → ℤ} (hU : IsOpen U) (hfoff : ∀ z ∈ U, z ∉ S → AnalyticAt ℂ f z ∧ f z ≠ 0)
  (hgoff : ∀ z ∈ U, z ∉ S → AnalyticAt ℂ g z ∧ g z ≠ 0)
  (hfmero : ∀ s ∈ S, s ∈ U → MeromorphicAt f s) (hgmero : ∀ s ∈ S, s ∈ U → MeromorphicAt g s)
  (hford : ∀ s ∈ S, s ∈ U → meromorphicOrderAt f s = ↑(ordf s))
  (hgord : ∀ s ∈ S, s ∈ U → meromorphicOrderAt g s = ↑(ordg s)) (hγ : TauCeti.IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b)
  (hγU : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U) (hclosed : γ a = γ b) (hγoff : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, γ t ∉ ↑S)
  (hnull : TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous γ a b U)
  (hs : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, ‖f (γ t) - g (γ t)‖ < ‖f (γ t)‖ + ‖g (γ t)‖) :
  ∑ z ∈ S, TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber γ a b z * ↑(ordf z) =
    ∑ z ∈ S, TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber γ a b z * ↑(ordg z)
TauCeti.rouche_symm_nullHomologous.doc:
**Rouché's theorem for a null-homologous cycle, symmetric form** (Estermann). Let `f` and `g`
be meromorphic on an open set `U`, analytic and non-vanishing off a finite set `S`, of orders
`ordf` and `ordg` on `S`, and let `γ` be a closed piecewise-`C¹` curve in `U`, null-homologous in
`U`, missing `S`, and satisfying `‖f (γ t) - g (γ t)‖ < ‖f (γ t)‖ + ‖g (γ t)‖` along its length.
Then `f` and `g` enclose the same number of zeros minus poles, each counted with its multiplicity
*and* with the winding number of `γ` about it.

The hypothesis is the strict form of the triangle inequality `‖f z - g z‖ ≤ ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖`, so it
says exactly that `f` and `g` never point in *opposite* directions along the curve; it is symmetric
in the two functions and strictly weaker than the classical `‖f (γ t) - g (γ t)‖ < ‖f (γ t)‖`.

Exactly as in `TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple_nullHomologous`, points of `S` outside `U` are
harmless rather than excluded — null-homology makes their winding number, hence their contribution
on either side, vanish — so the meromorphy and order hypotheses are conditional on membership in
`U`, and `S` may list ordinary points, of order `0`.

`TauCeti.rouche_symm` is the circle case, proved separately: see the section introduction for how
the two interfaces differ and what recovering the disc statement from this one would take.

TauCeti.rouche_symm_exists_eq_zero_iff.signature:
TauCeti.rouche_symm_exists_eq_zero_iff {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ}
  (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (Metric.closedBall c R)) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (Metric.closedBall c R))
  (hs : ∀ z ∈ Metric.sphere c R, ‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖) :
  (∃ z ∈ Metric.ball c R, f z = 0) ↔ ∃ z ∈ Metric.ball c R, g z = 0
TauCeti.rouche_symm_exists_eq_zero_iff.doc:
**Rouché's theorem as a zero-detection principle**, symmetric form. Under the hypothesis
`‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖` on the bounding circle, `f` has a zero in the open disc if and only
if `g` does. This is how Rouché is normally used: to import a zero of a comparison function.

TauCeti.rouche_symm.signature:
TauCeti.rouche_symm {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (Metric.closedBall c R))
  (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (Metric.closedBall c R))
  (hs : ∀ z ∈ Metric.sphere c R, ‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖) :
  ∑ᶠ (z : ℂ) (_ : z ∈ Metric.ball c R), analyticOrderNatAt f z =
    ∑ᶠ (z : ℂ) (_ : z ∈ Metric.ball c R), analyticOrderNatAt g z
TauCeti.rouche_symm.doc:
**Rouché's theorem, symmetric form** (Estermann). If `f` and `g` are holomorphic on the closed
disc `closedBall c R` and `‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖` at every point `z` of the bounding circle,
then `f` and `g` have the same number of zeros in `ball c R`, each counted with multiplicity. The
hypothesis forces both functions to be zero-free on the circle, hence of finite order throughout
the disc, so every zero is genuinely counted.

The hypothesis is the strict form of the triangle inequality `‖f z - g z‖ ≤ ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖`, so it
says exactly that `f z` and `g z` never point in *opposite* directions on the circle. It is
symmetric in `f` and `g` and strictly weaker than the classical `‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖` of
`TauCeti.rouche`.

The counts are the canonical finitely supported sums `∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt · z`;
no finiteness witness appears in the statement.

TauCeti.rouche_nullHomologous.signature:
TauCeti.rouche_nullHomologous {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
  (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f U) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g U)
  (hfS : ∀ z ∈ U, f z = 0 → z ∈ S) (hgS : ∀ z ∈ U, g z = 0 → z ∈ S)
  (hγ : TauCeti.IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) (hγU : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
  (hnull : TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous γ a b U)
  (hs : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, ‖f (γ t) - g (γ t)‖ < ‖f (γ t)‖) :
  ∑ z ∈ S, TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber γ a b z * ↑(analyticOrderNatAt f z) =
    ∑ z ∈ S, TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber γ a b z * ↑(analyticOrderNatAt g z)
TauCeti.rouche_nullHomologous.doc:
**Rouché's theorem for a null-homologous cycle**, classical form. Under
`‖f (γ t) - g (γ t)‖ < ‖f (γ t)‖` along the curve, `f` and `g` enclose the same winding-weighted
number of zeros. This is the special case of
`TauCeti.rouche_symm_nullHomologous_of_analyticOnNhd` obtained by discarding the nonnegative
summand `‖g (γ t)‖`.

TauCeti.rouche_exists_eq_zero_iff.signature:
TauCeti.rouche_exists_eq_zero_iff {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ}
  (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (Metric.closedBall c R)) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (Metric.closedBall c R))
  (hs : ∀ z ∈ Metric.sphere c R, ‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖) :
  (∃ z ∈ Metric.ball c R, f z = 0) ↔ ∃ z ∈ Metric.ball c R, g z = 0
TauCeti.rouche_exists_eq_zero_iff.doc:
**Rouché's theorem as a zero-detection principle**, classical form: under
`‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖` on the bounding circle, `f` has a zero in the open disc if and only if `g`
does.

TauCeti.rouche_add_windingNumber_comp.signature:
TauCeti.rouche_add_windingNumber_comp {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
  (hγ : TauCeti.IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
  (hfa : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, AnalyticAt ℂ f (γ t)) (hga : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, AnalyticAt ℂ g (γ t))
  (hs : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, ‖g (γ t)‖ < ‖f (γ t)‖) :
  TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber (f ∘ γ) a b 0 =
    TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber ((fun w => f w + g w) ∘ γ) a b 0
TauCeti.rouche_add_windingNumber_comp.doc:
**Rouché's theorem as an equality of image winding numbers, additive form.** A holomorphic
perturbation `g` dominated by `f` along a closed piecewise-`C¹` curve does not change how often the
image winds about the origin. This is the phrasing that names the "dog on a leash" picture: the
walker `f ∘ γ` and the dog `(f + g) ∘ γ`, on a leash shorter than the walker's distance from the
lamppost at the origin, circle it the same number of times.

It is the special case of `TauCeti.rouche_windingNumber_comp` for the pair `f`, `f + g`.

TauCeti.rouche_add_nullHomologous.signature:
TauCeti.rouche_add_nullHomologous {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
  (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f U) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g U)
  (hfS : ∀ z ∈ U, f z = 0 → z ∈ S) (hsumS : ∀ z ∈ U, f z + g z = 0 → z ∈ S)
  (hγ : TauCeti.IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) (hγU : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
  (hnull : TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous γ a b U)
  (hs : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, ‖g (γ t)‖ < ‖f (γ t)‖) :
  ∑ z ∈ S, TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber γ a b z * ↑(analyticOrderNatAt f z) =
    ∑ z ∈ S, TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber γ a b z * ↑(analyticOrderNatAt (fun w => f w + g w) z)
TauCeti.rouche_add_nullHomologous.doc:
**Rouché's theorem for a null-homologous cycle**, additive form: a holomorphic perturbation `g`
dominated by `f` along the curve does not change the winding-weighted number of zeros enclosed.
This is the phrasing of most textbooks, and the one that reads the zeros of a perturbed function
off the unperturbed one.

TauCeti.rouche_add_exists_eq_zero_iff.doc:
**Rouché's theorem as a zero-detection principle**, additive form: a holomorphic perturbation
`g` dominated by `f` on the bounding circle neither creates nor destroys zeros inside, so `f` has a
zero in the open disc if and only if `f + g` does. This is the phrasing that reads a zero of a
perturbed function off the unperturbed one, the existence counterpart of `TauCeti.rouche_add`.

TauCeti.rouche_add.doc:
**Rouché's theorem**, in the additive phrasing of most textbooks: a holomorphic perturbation
`g` that is dominated by `f` on the bounding circle does not change the number of zeros inside.

TauCeti.rouche.signature:

TauCeti.rouche.doc:
**Rouché's theorem** for a disc, classical form. If `f` and `g` are holomorphic on the closed
disc `closedBall c R` and `‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖` at every point `z` of the bounding circle, then `f`
and `g` have the same number of zeros in `ball c R`, each counted with multiplicity.

This is the special case of `TauCeti.rouche_symm` obtained by discarding the nonnegative summand
`‖g z‖` from the symmetric hypothesis.

dimension of a finite-type affine group `G` is the dimension of the centralizer `C_G(x)` of an
element `x` of its Lie algebra `𝔤` plus the rank of `ad x`, the dimension of `[𝔤, x]`.

TauCeti.riesz_lemma_translate.doc:
**Riesz's lemma**, translated form: for a closed submodule `F`, a vector `x` and `r < 1`, some
`y ∈ F` satisfies `r * ‖x - y‖ ≤ ‖x - y - z‖` for every `z ∈ F`, so `x - y` is almost as far from
`F` as its norm. For `x ∈ F` one may take `y = x`.

TauCeti.riesz_lemma_of_norm_lt_of_lt.doc:
**Riesz's lemma** relative to a larger subspace: if `F` is a closed subspace properly contained
in a subspace `G`, then `G` contains a vector of norm at most `R` at distance at least `1`
from `F`.

differential `ω`, multiplication by `ω` is a `k`-linear isomorphism `L(W - D) ≃ Ω_F(D)`.

open proper subset `Ω` of `ℂ` is the source of an open partial homeomorphism whose target is the
open unit disc. The map and its inverse are holomorphic and conformal throughout their respective
domains.

TauCeti.riemannMapping_of_hasHolomorphic.doc:
**The Riemann mapping theorem for domains with holomorphic square roots.** A connected open
proper subset `Ω` of `ℂ` on which every nowhere-zero holomorphic function has a holomorphic square
root admits a holomorphic bijection onto the open unit disc, with nonvanishing derivative
throughout `Ω`.

The square roots are all that the Koebe argument needs of `Ω`; simply connected open sets have them
(`IsSimplyConnected.hasHolomorphicSquareRoots`), which gives `TauCeti.riemannMapping`.

TauCeti.riemannMapping_normalized.doc:
**The Riemann mapping theorem, normalized.** A nonempty, simply connected, open, proper subset
`Ω` of `ℂ` with a base point `z₀` carries a holomorphic bijection onto the open unit disc that
sends `z₀` to `0` with positive real derivative there, and that map is unique: any other one agrees
with it on `Ω`.

This is the pinned-down form of `TauCeti.riemannMapping`, which asserts existence only.

`ℂ`, regarded as a subtype, is homeomorphic to `Complex.UnitDisc`.

The homeomorphism is induced by the holomorphic bijection supplied by `TauCeti.riemannMapping`;
its forward and inverse formulas are
`DifferentiableOn.toHomeomorphOfBijOn_apply` and
`DifferentiableOn.toHomeomorphOfBijOn_symm_apply`.

TauCeti.riemannMapping.doc:
**The Riemann mapping theorem.** A simply connected open proper subset `Ω` of `ℂ` admits a
holomorphic bijection onto the open unit disc, with nonvanishing derivative throughout `Ω`.

Existence only: the map is not asserted to be unique, and no normalization is imposed.

and `Φ : (ℝ × ℝ) × ℝ → M` a `C²` homotopy from `Φ(·, 0)` to `Φ(·, 1)`. The integral of `Φ^* φ`

edges count positively, the left and top edges negatively.

TauCeti.realize_scottSentenceAt_iff.{u, v, w, w', o} {L : FirstOrder.Language} [L.IsRelational]

  (hα : α < Ordinal.omega 1) (hs : TauCeti.SelfStabilizesCompletely M α) (N : Type w')
  [L.Structure N] [Countable N] :
  FirstOrder.Language.SentenceInf.Realize (TauCeti.scottSentenceAt M α) N ↔ Nonempty (L.Equiv M N)
TauCeti.realize_scottSentenceAt_iff.doc:
At a countable internally stabilizing level, the Scott sentence of a countable structure `M`
holds in a countable structure exactly when that structure is isomorphic to `M`.

TauCeti.realize_scottFormula_iff_bfEquiv.doc:
A tuple in any structure satisfies the canonical Scott formula exactly when it is
back-and-forth equivalent to the original tuple at that countable ordinal.

TauCeti.rank_jacobiMatrixAt_dehomogenize.signature:
TauCeti.rank_jacobiMatrixAt_dehomogenize_div.{u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_3} {K : Type u_4} [Field K]
  [Finite ι] {n : ℕ} (i : Fin (n + 1)) {p : ι → MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) K} {d : ι → ℕ}
  (hp : ∀ (k : ι), (p k).IsHomogeneous (d k)) {b : Fin (n + 1) → K} (hi : b i ≠ 0)
  (hb : ∀ (k : ι), (MvPolynomial.eval b) (p k) = 0) :
  (TauCeti.jacobiMatrixAt (fun k => (TauCeti.dehomogenize i) (p k)) fun j =>
        b (i.succAbove j) / b i).rank =
    (TauCeti.jacobiMatrixAt p b).rank
TauCeti.rank_jacobiMatrixAt_dehomogenize.doc:
**The Jacobian criterion in a ratio chart**: at a common zero `b` of a family of homogeneous
equations with `b i ≠ 0`, the Jacobian matrix of the dehomogenized equations at the coordinate
ratios `b (i.succAbove j) / b i` has the same rank as the Jacobian matrix of the homogeneous
equations at `b`.

TauCeti.range_localCyclotomicCharacter_e.signature:
TauCeti.range_localCyclotomicCharacter_eq_of_ringEquiv.{u_1, u_2} (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)]
  {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {K' : Type u_2} [Field K'] (e : K ≃+* K') :
  (TauCeti.localCyclotomicCharacter p K).range = (TauCeti.localCyclotomicCharacter p K').range
TauCeti.range_localCyclotomicCharacter_e.doc:
**The image of the cyclotomic character is an invariant of the field.** An isomorphism of fields
induces an isomorphism of absolute Galois groups, and the cyclotomic character of the target is the
character of the source read through it (`TauCeti.localCyclotomicCharacter_map`); hence the two
characters have the same image in `ℤ_pˣ`.

TauCeti.range_brauerActionOrth_two_eq_ce.signature:
TauCeti.range_brauerActionOrth_two_eq_centralizer_of_sq_add_sq_eq_one.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K]
  (n : ℕ) (h2 : 2 ≠ 0) {c s : K} (hcs : c ^ 2 + s ^ 2 = 1) (hc : c ≠ 0) (hs : s ≠ 0) :
  (TauCeti.brauerActionOrth K n 2).range =
    Subalgebra.centralizer K (Set.range ⇑((TauCeti.stdOrthogonalRep K n).tensorPower 2))
TauCeti.range_brauerActionOrth_two_eq_ce.doc:
**Brauer duality on the tensor square.** Over a field `K` with `2 ≠ 0` that has a point
`(c, s)` of the unit circle with `c ≠ 0` and `s ≠ 0`, the image of the Brauer algebra `B₂(n)` in
the endomorphisms of `(Kⁿ)^{⊗2}` is the commutant of the diagonal action of the orthogonal group:
an operator commuting with every `g ⊗ g` is a combination of the identity, the flip of the two
tensor factors and the cup-cap generator.

TauCeti.range_brauerActionOrth_two_eq_ce.signature:
TauCeti.range_brauerActionOrth_two_eq_centralizer_of_noZeroDivisors.{u} (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
  (n : ℕ) [NoZeroDivisors R] (h2 : 2 ≠ 0) (hrot : ∃ c s, c ^ 2 + s ^ 2 = 1 ∧ c * s ≠ 0) :
  (TauCeti.brauerActionOrth R n 2).range =
    Subalgebra.centralizer R (Set.range ⇑((TauCeti.stdOrthogonalRep R n).tensorPower 2))
TauCeti.range_brauerActionOrth_two_eq_ce.doc:
**Brauer duality for the orthogonal group on two strands.** Over a commutative ring without
zero divisors in which `2 ≠ 0` and which contains a point `(c, s)` of the unit circle with
`c * s ≠ 0`, the operators on `Rⁿ ⊗ Rⁿ` commuting with the diagonal action of the orthogonal
group are exactly the image of the Brauer algebra `B₂(n)`: the combinations of the identity, the
flip of the two factors, and the contraction-expansion `x ⊗ y ↦ (x ⬝ᵥ y) • ∑ᵢ eᵢ ⊗ eᵢ`.

Some point of the circle with `c * s ≠ 0` is needed when `n = 2`: over `ZMod 3` the orthogonal
group of the plane consists of the signed permutation matrices, which commute with the projection
onto the span of `e₀ ⊗ e₀` and `e₁ ⊗ e₁`, and that projection is not in the image.

TauCeti.range_brauerActionOrth_two_eq_ce.signature:
TauCeti.range_brauerActionOrth_two_eq_centralizer.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [CharZero K]
  (n : ℕ) :
  (TauCeti.brauerActionOrth K n 2).range =
    Subalgebra.centralizer K (Set.range ⇑((TauCeti.stdOrthogonalRep K n).tensorPower 2))
TauCeti.range_brauerActionOrth_two_eq_ce.doc:
**Brauer duality on the tensor square in characteristic zero.** Over a field of
characteristic zero, the image of the Brauer algebra `B₂(n)` in the endomorphisms of `(Kⁿ)^{⊗2}`
is the commutant of the diagonal action of the orthogonal group.

TauCeti.ramificationIndex_sub_one_le_dif.signature:
TauCeti.ramificationIndex_sub_one_le_differentExponent.{u_1, u_2} (K : Type u_1) (L : Type u_2)
  [Field K] [ValuativeRel K] [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] [Field L]
  [ValuativeRel L] [TopologicalSpace L] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField L] [Algebra K L]
  [ValuativeExtension K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L] :
  TauCeti.ramificationIndex K L - 1 ≤ TauCeti.differentExponent K L
TauCeti.ramificationIndex_sub_one_le_dif.doc: **The first half of Dedekind's different theorem**: `e(L/K) - 1 ≤ d(L/K)`.

TauCeti.ramificationIdx_sub_one_le_multi.signature:
TauCeti.ramificationIdx_sub_one_le_multiplicity_differentIdeal.{u_1, u_2} (A : Type u_1)
  {B : Type u_2} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsDedekindDomain A] [IsDedekindDomain B]
  [Module.IsTorsionFree A B] [Module.Finite A B]
  [Algebra.IsSeparable (FractionRing A) (FractionRing B)] {p : Ideal A} [p.IsMaximal] (hp : p ≠ ⊥)
  (P : Ideal B) [P.IsPrime] [P.LiesOver p] :
  P.ramificationIdx A - 1 ≤ multiplicity P (differentIdeal A B)
TauCeti.ramificationIdx_sub_one_le_multi.doc:
**Dedekind's different theorem, first part, as a bound on the exponent**: the multiplicity of
a prime `P` over a nonzero prime `p` in the different ideal is at least `e(P ∣ p) - 1`.

TauCeti.ramificationIdx_le_multiplicity_.signature:
TauCeti.ramificationIdx_le_multiplicity_differentIdeal_iff.{u_1, u_2} (A : Type u_1) {B : Type u_2}
  [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsDedekindDomain A] [IsDedekindDomain B]
  [Module.IsTorsionFree A B] [Module.Finite A B]
  [Algebra.IsSeparable (FractionRing A) (FractionRing B)] {p : Ideal A} [p.IsMaximal] (hp : p ≠ ⊥)
  (P : Ideal B) [P.IsMaximal] [P.LiesOver p] :
  P.ramificationIdx A ≤ multiplicity P (differentIdeal A B) ↔
    ¬Algebra.IsSeparable (A ⧸ p) (B ⧸ P) ∨ ↑(P.ramificationIdx A) = 0
TauCeti.ramificationIdx_le_multiplicity_.doc:
**Dedekind's different theorem, second part, as a bound on the exponent**: the multiplicity
of `P` in the different ideal is at least `e(P ∣ p)` exactly when the residue extension is
inseparable or `e(P ∣ p)` vanishes in the residue field `A ⧸ p`.

TauCeti.quotientWildInertiaSubgroupEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.quotientWildInertiaSubgroupEquiv.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [ValuativeRel K]
  [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] :
  ↥(TauCeti.inertiaSubgroup K) ⧸
      (TauCeti.wildInertiaSubgroup K).subgroupOf (TauCeti.inertiaSubgroup K) ≃ₜ*
    TauCeti.PrimeToPTateModule
      (ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField ↥(ValuativeRel.valuation K).integer)) (AlgebraicClosure K)
TauCeti.quotientWildInertiaSubgroupEquiv.doc:
**Tame inertia is the prime-to-`p` Tate module**: the tame character induces an isomorphism
of topological groups `I_K / P_K ≃ₜ* ℤ̂^{(p')}(1)` from the tame inertia group, the quotient of
the inertia subgroup by the wild inertia subgroup.

TauCeti.quinticF20Spec_specialize_X_pow_.signature:
TauCeti.quinticF20Spec_specialize_X_pow_five_add_C_mul_X_add_C.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R]
  (a b : R) :
  TauCeti.quinticF20Spec.specialize R
      (Polynomial.X ^ 5 + Polynomial.C a * Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C b) =
    Polynomial.X ^ 6 + Polynomial.C (8 * a) * Polynomial.X ^ 5 +
              Polynomial.C (40 * a ^ 2) * Polynomial.X ^ 4 +
            Polynomial.C (160 * a ^ 3) * Polynomial.X ^ 3 +
          Polynomial.C (400 * a ^ 4) * Polynomial.X ^ 2 +
        Polynomial.C (512 * a ^ 5 - 3125 * b ^ 4) * Polynomial.X +
      Polynomial.C (256 * a ^ 6 - 9375 * a * b ^ 4)
TauCeti.quinticF20Spec_specialize_X_pow_.doc:
**Dummit's formula for the resolvent of a quintic trinomial.** Over every commutative ring,
the specialization of the quintic `F₂₀` specification at `X⁵ + aX + b` is
`X⁶ + 8aX⁵ + 40a²X⁴ + 160a³X³ + 400a⁴X² + (512a⁵ - 3125b⁴)X + (256a⁶ - 9375ab⁴)`.

TauCeti.quasiIso_cyclicCochainComplexToT.signature:
TauCeti.quasiIso_cyclicCochainComplexToTotal.{u, u_1, u_2} (R : Type u_1) (A : Type u)
  (M : Type u_2) [CommRing R] [NonUnitalSemiring A] [_root_.Module R A] [IsScalarTower R A A]
  [SMulCommClass R A A] [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module R M] [Algebra ℚ R] :
  QuasiIso (TauCeti.cyclicCochainComplexToTotal R A M)
TauCeti.quasiIso_cyclicCochainComplexToT.doc:
Over a ring containing `ℚ`, the inclusion of Connes' cyclic cochain complex into the total
complex of the cyclic bicomplex is a quasi-isomorphism: cyclic cohomology defined by cyclic cochains
is the cohomology of the total cyclic bicomplex.

TauCeti.quasiIso_cubicalCrossProduct.signature:
TauCeti.quasiIso_cubicalCrossProduct.{u} (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (X Y : TopCat) :
  QuasiIso (TauCeti.cubicalCrossProduct k X Y)
TauCeti.quasiIso_cubicalCrossProduct.doc:
**The cubical Eilenberg–Zilber theorem**: the cross product of normalized cubical chains
`N(X; k) ⊗ N(Y; k) ⟶ N(X × Y; k)` is a quasi-isomorphism.

TauCeti.qTheta.signature: TauCeti.qTheta.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NormedField 𝕜] (q w : 𝕜) : 𝕜
TauCeti.qTheta.doc:
The **theta product** `θ_q(w) = (w; q)_∞ (q w⁻¹; q)_∞`, written as
`(1 - w) ∏_{n ≥ 1} (1 - qⁿ w) (1 - qⁿ w⁻¹)`. The product converges for `‖q‖ < 1`; otherwise the
value is a junk value. With `q = e^{2π i τ}` and `w = e^{2π i (r₁ τ + r₂)}` it is the product in
the Siegel function `g_r(τ)`.

TauCeti.puiseuxField.not_completeSpace.doc:
**The Puiseux field is not complete.** The partial sums of `∑ j, t ^ ((j + 1) + 1 / (j + 2))`
form a Cauchy sequence without a limit.

TauCeti.puiseuxField.mem_level_factorial.signature:
TauCeti.puiseuxField.mem_level_factorial_of_aeval_eq_zero.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  [∀ (n : ℕ+), HasEnoughRootsOfUnity K ↑n] {p : Polynomial (LaurentSeries K)} (hp : p ≠ 0)
  {x : ↥(TauCeti.puiseuxField K)} (hx : (Polynomial.aeval x) p = 0) :
  x ∈ TauCeti.puiseuxField.level K p.natDegree.factorial.toPNat'
TauCeti.puiseuxField.mem_level_factorial.doc:
If `K` contains all roots of unity, then a Puiseux series that is a root of a nonzero
polynomial of degree `d` over `K⸨X⸩` lies in level `d!`. Thus all roots of such a polynomial lie in
a common level.

TauCeti.puiseuxField.levelGalEquivRootsO.signature:
TauCeti.puiseuxField.levelGalEquivRootsOfUnity.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] (d : ℕ+)
  [HasEnoughRootsOfUnity K ↑d] :
  Gal(↥(TauCeti.puiseuxField.level K d)/LaurentSeries K) ≃* ↥(rootsOfUnity (↑d) K)
TauCeti.puiseuxField.levelGalEquivRootsO.doc:
If the coefficient field has a primitive `d`-th root of unity, then the Galois group of the
level-`d` subfield of the Puiseux field over `K⸨X⸩` is the group of `d`-th roots of unity of `K`.
The inverse is `levelKummer` (`TauCeti.puiseuxField.levelGalEquivRootsOfUnity_symm_apply`).

TauCeti.puiseuxField.levelCoconeIsColimi.doc:
The Puiseux field is the colimit of the ramified Laurent levels in `CommAlgCat K`.

Equivalently, every compatible family of `K`-algebra maps from the levels factors uniquely
through the bounded-denominator Puiseux series field.

TauCeti.puiseuxField.kummer_injective.doc:
**Faithfulness.** Distinct points of the Tate module act by distinct automorphisms of the
Puiseux field: the automorphism attached to `ζ` sends `t ^ (1 / n)` to `ζₙ t ^ (1 / n)`.

TauCeti.puiseuxField.instIsAlgClosure.signature:
TauCeti.puiseuxField.instIsAlgClosure.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] [CharZero K] :
  IsAlgClosure (LaurentSeries K) ↥(TauCeti.puiseuxField K)
TauCeti.puiseuxField.instIsAlgClosure.doc:
Over an algebraically closed field `K` of characteristic zero, the Puiseux field is an
algebraic closure of the Laurent-series field `K⸨X⸩`.

TauCeti.puiseuxField.exists_isRoot_level.signature:
TauCeti.puiseuxField.exists_isRoot_levelEmbedding.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K]
  [CharZero K] {P : Polynomial ↥(TauCeti.puiseuxField K)} (hP : P.degree ≠ 0) :
  ∃ n y, P.IsRoot ((TauCeti.puiseuxField.levelEmbedding K n) y)
TauCeti.puiseuxField.exists_isRoot_level.doc:
**Newton–Puiseux theorem.** Over an algebraically closed field `K` of characteristic zero,
every nonconstant polynomial over the Puiseux field has a root lying in a single ramified level.

TauCeti.psumPart_eq_sum_spechtCharValue_.signature:
TauCeti.psumPart_eq_sum_spechtCharValue_smul_schurPoly.{u_1, u_2} {n : ℕ} {σ : Type u_1} [Fintype σ]
  (R : Type u_2) [CommRing R] (ρ : n.Partition) :
  MvPolynomial.psumPart σ R ρ = ∑ l, TauCeti.spechtCharValue l ρ • TauCeti.schurPoly σ R l
TauCeti.psumPart_eq_sum_spechtCharValue_.doc:
**Frobenius's formula**: the power-sum product of a partition `ρ` of `n` expands in the Schur
polynomials as `p_ρ = ∑_{λ ⊢ n} χ^λ(ρ) s_λ`, the coefficients being the column of `ρ` in the
character table of `Sₙ`. This holds in every finite alphabet and over every commutative ring; the
Schur polynomials of the partitions with more parts than the alphabet has letters vanish.

TauCeti.psumPartBasis.signature:
TauCeti.psumPartBasis.{u_1, u_2} (σ : Type u_1) [Fintype σ] (R : Type u_2) [CommRing R]
  [Algebra ℚ R] {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ Fintype.card σ) :
  Module.Basis n.Partition R ↥(TauCeti.symmetricHomogeneousSubmodule σ R n)
TauCeti.psumPartBasis.doc:
**The power-sum basis**: over a `ℚ`-algebra and in an alphabet of at least `n` letters, the
power-sum products `p_μ` of the partitions `μ` of `n` form a basis of the symmetric polynomials of
degree `n`.

TauCeti.profiniteFrattini.signature: TauCeti.profiniteFrattini.{u} (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : Subgroup G
TauCeti.profiniteFrattini.doc:
The **Frattini subgroup** `Φ(G)` of a topological group: the intersection of its maximal open
subgroups. For a profinite group this is the Frattini subgroup of Ribes–Zalesskii; with the
discrete topology it is Mathlib's `frattini` (`TauCeti.profiniteFrattini_eq_frattini`).

TauCeti.principalUnitsEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.principalUnitsEquiv {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {f : ℕ} (hf : 0 < f) (hf₂ : p = 2 → 2 ≤ f)
  {w : ℤ_[p]ˣ} (hw : w ∈ TauCeti.unitsPrincipal p f) (hw' : w ∉ TauCeti.unitsPrincipal p (f + 1)) :
  Multiplicative ℤ_[p] ≃ₜ* ↥(TauCeti.unitsPrincipal p f)
TauCeti.principalUnitsEquiv.doc:
**The principal units are a copy of `ℤ_p`.** For `f ≥ 1`, with `f ≥ 2` when `p = 2`, and a
unit `w` of exact level `f`, the `p`-adic power map `l ↦ w ^ l` is a topological group
isomorphism from the additive group of `ℤ_[p]` onto `U^(f) = 1 + p ^ f ℤ_p`. It is onto because
`w` topologically generates `U^(f)`, and injective because `w` has infinite order.

TauCeti.primeNumberTheoremTransfer.signature:
TauCeti.primeNumberTheoremTransfer.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  {S : Set (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K))} {δ : ℝ}
  (B : TauCeti.PrimeBoundaryRemainder K S δ) :
  ((fun x => TauCeti.primePsi K S x - δ * x) =o[Filter.atTop] fun x => x) ∧
    ((fun x => TauCeti.primeTheta K S x - δ * x) =o[Filter.atTop] fun x => x) ∧
      (fun x => TauCeti.primeCount K S x - δ * TauCeti.Real.logIntegral x) =o[Filter.atTop] fun x =>
        x / Real.log x
TauCeti.primeNumberTheoremTransfer.doc:
**Prime-number-theorem transfer from exact boundary data.**  The three conclusions are,
respectively, the von Mangoldt-weighted prime-power asymptotic, the logarithmically weighted prime
asymptotic after removing higher powers, and the unweighted prime-counting asymptotic after Abel
summation.  The error-term formulation includes residue zero.

TauCeti.primeIdealTheorem_of_boundary.signature:
TauCeti.primeIdealTheorem_of_boundary.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (B : TauCeti.PrimeBoundaryRemainder K Set.univ 1) :
  (Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (TauCeti.primePsi K Set.univ) fun x => x) ∧
    (Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (TauCeti.primeTheta K Set.univ) fun x => x) ∧
      Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (TauCeti.primeCount K Set.univ) TauCeti.Real.logIntegral
TauCeti.primeIdealTheorem_of_boundary.doc:
**The conditional prime ideal theorem.**  Boundary data for all prime ideals with residue one
give the standard asymptotic equivalences for `ψ`, `ϑ`, and `π`.

TauCeti.primeIdealTheorem.signature:
TauCeti.primeIdealTheorem.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [NumberField K] :
  (Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (TauCeti.primePsi K Set.univ) fun x => x) ∧
    (Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (TauCeti.primeTheta K Set.univ) fun x => x) ∧
      Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (TauCeti.primeCount K Set.univ) TauCeti.Real.logIntegral
TauCeti.primeIdealTheorem.doc:
**The prime ideal theorem.** For a number field `K`, Chebyshev's functions satisfy
`ψ_K(x) ~ x` and `ϑ_K(x) ~ x`, and the number `π_K(x)` of prime ideals of norm at most `x`
satisfies `π_K(x) ~ Li(x)`.

TauCeti.primeCount_univ_isEquivalent_div.signature:
TauCeti.primeCount_univ_isEquivalent_div_log.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [NumberField K] :
  Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (TauCeti.primeCount K Set.univ) fun x => x / Real.log x
TauCeti.primeCount_univ_isEquivalent_div.doc: **The prime ideal theorem, in the form `π_K(x) ~ x / log x`.**

TauCeti.presentedProP.oneRelator_q_eq_ze.signature:
TauCeti.presentedProP.oneRelator_q_eq_zero_iff_mem_topologicalClosure_commutator.{u} {p : ℕ}
  [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {X : Type u} (r : TauCeti.freeProP p X) (x₀ : X) (w : X → ℤ_[p])
  (hw : w x₀ = 1) (q : ℤ_[p])
  (hr : Multiplicative.toAdd ((TauCeti.freeProP.exponentSum p X) r) = q • w) [Finite X] :
  q = 0 ↔ r ∈ (commutator (TauCeti.freeProP p X)).topologicalClosure
TauCeti.presentedProP.oneRelator_q_eq_ze.doc:
**The torsion-free case of the structure theorem.** The coordinate `q` of the exponent vector
`exponentSum r = q • w`, `w x₀ = 1`, of the relator vanishes exactly when `r` lies in the closed
commutator subgroup of the free pro-`p` group; then the factor `ℤ_p ⧸ q ℤ_p` of
`oneRelatorAbelianizationEquiv` is `ℤ_p` and `G^{ab} ≅ ℤ_p^X` is torsion-free.

TauCeti.presentedProP.oneRelatorAbeliani.signature:
TauCeti.presentedProP.oneRelatorAbelianizationEquiv.{u} {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {X : Type u}
  (r : TauCeti.freeProP p X) (x₀ : X) (w : X → ℤ_[p]) (hw : w x₀ = 1) (q : ℤ_[p])
  (hr : Multiplicative.toAdd ((TauCeti.freeProP.exponentSum p X) r) = q • w) [Finite X] :
  TopologicalAbelianization (TauCeti.presentedProP p X {r}) ≃ₜ*
    Multiplicative (({ x // x ≠ x₀ } → ℤ_[p]) × ℤ_[p] ⧸ Ideal.span {q})
TauCeti.presentedProP.oneRelatorAbeliani.doc:
**The abelianization structure theorem for one-relator pro-`p` groups.** Let
`G = presentedProP p X {r}` be the pro-`p` group on a finite type `X` with the single relator `r`,
and write the exponent vector of `r` as `exponentSum r = q • w` with `w x₀ = 1`. Then

`G^{ab} ≃ₜ* ℤ_p^{X ∖ {x₀}} × ℤ_p ⧸ q ℤ_p`

as topological groups, the isomorphism sending the class of the generator at `x ≠ x₀` to the
coordinate vector at `x` and the class of the generator at `x₀` to `(-w, 1)`. When `q ≠ 0` the
factor `ℤ_p ⧸ q ℤ_p` is finite cyclic and is the torsion subgroup of `G^{ab}`; when `q = 0` it is
`ℤ_p` and `G^{ab} ≅ ℤ_p^X` is torsion-free.

TauCeti.pow_ramificationIdx_dvd_differen.signature:
TauCeti.pow_ramificationIdx_dvd_differentIdeal_iff.{u_1, u_2} (A : Type u_1) {B : Type u_2}
  [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsDedekindDomain A] [IsDedekindDomain B]
  [Module.IsTorsionFree A B] [Module.Finite A B]
  [Algebra.IsSeparable (FractionRing A) (FractionRing B)] {p : Ideal A} [p.IsMaximal] (hp : p ≠ ⊥)
  (P : Ideal B) [P.IsMaximal] [P.LiesOver p] :
  P ^ P.ramificationIdx A ∣ differentIdeal A B ↔
    ¬Algebra.IsSeparable (A ⧸ p) (B ⧸ P) ∨ ↑(P.ramificationIdx A) = 0
TauCeti.pow_ramificationIdx_dvd_differen.doc:
**Dedekind's different theorem, second part** (Stichtenoth, Theorem 3.5.1(b) and
Corollary 3.5.5): for a maximal ideal `P` of `B` over a nonzero maximal ideal `p` of `A`, the power
`P ^ e(P ∣ p)` divides the different ideal exactly when `P` is not tame, that is, when the residue
extension at `P` is inseparable or `e(P ∣ p)` vanishes in the residue field `A ⧸ p`.

Together with Mathlib's `pow_sub_one_dvd_differentIdeal`, the different exponent at `P` is
therefore `e(P ∣ p) - 1` at the tame primes and at least `e(P ∣ p)` at all others.

TauCeti.pow_pow_totient_eq_self.signature:
TauCeti.pow_pow_totient_eq_self.{u_1} {M : Type u_1} [Monoid M] {q n : ℕ} (hq : q.Coprime n) {x : M}
  (hx : x ^ n = 1) : x ^ q ^ n.totient = x
TauCeti.pow_pow_totient_eq_self.doc:
**Euler's theorem on an `n`-th root of unity**: if `x ^ n = 1` in a monoid and `q` is prime to
`n`, then `x ^ q ^ φ(n) = x`, since `q ^ φ(n) ≡ 1 [MOD n]`.

TauCeti.pow_mul_eval_hasseDeriv_multicho.signature:
TauCeti.pow_mul_eval_hasseDeriv_multichoose_X_add_one_pow_mem_range_intCast {k : ℕ} {L : ℤ}

      Polynomial.eval (↑x) ((Polynomial.hasseDeriv m) (Ring.multichoose (Polynomial.X + 1) k ^ l)) ∈
    Set.range Int.cast
TauCeti.pow_mul_eval_hasseDeriv_multicho.doc:
**Baker's denominator bound.** If each of `1, …, k` divides the integer `L`, then for every
integer `x` and all `l, m`,

`L ^ m Δ(x; k, l, m) = L ^ m (1 / m!) (d / dx) ^ m (Δ(x; k) ^ l)`

is an integer.

TauCeti.pow_mul_eval_hasseDeriv_map_mult.signature:
TauCeti.pow_mul_eval_hasseDeriv_map_multichoose_X_add_one_comp_C_mul_X_mem_range_intCast.{u_1}
  {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [CharZero K] {k : ℕ} {L : ℤ} (hL : ∀ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, ↑j ∣ L) (q : ℤ)
  {x : K} (hx : ↑q * x ∈ Set.range Int.cast) (m : ℕ) :
  ↑L ^ m *
      Polynomial.eval x
        ((Polynomial.hasseDeriv m)
          (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℚ K)
            ((Ring.multichoose (Polynomial.X + 1) k).comp (Polynomial.C ↑q * Polynomial.X)))) ∈
    Set.range Int.cast
TauCeti.pow_mul_eval_hasseDeriv_map_mult.doc:
**Baker's denominator bound at points of a scaled lattice.** Let `K` be a field of
characteristic zero, `q` an integer and `x ∈ K` with `q x` an integer, and let `L` be an integer
divisible by each of `1, …, k`. Then for every `m`,

`L ^ m (1 / m!) (d / dx) ^ m Δ(q x; k)`

is an integer. Here `Δ(q X; k)` is mapped to `K[X]` and differentiated in `X`. For `q = 1` and
`x` integral this is the case `l = 1` of
`TauCeti.pow_mul_eval_hasseDeriv_multichoose_X_add_one_pow_mem_range_intCast`.

TauCeti.pow_dvd_differentIdeal_iff_of_is.signature:
TauCeti.pow_dvd_differentIdeal_iff_of_isCoprime.{u_1, u_2} (A : Type u_1) {B : Type u_2}

TauCeti.pow_dvd_differentIdeal_iff_of_is.doc:
**Dedekind's different theorem at a prime power with a coprime complement.** If
`p · B = P ^ e * Q` with `P ^ e` and `Q` coprime and `p ≠ ⊥`, then `P ^ e` divides
`differentIdeal A B` exactly when the residue extension at `P` is inseparable or `e` vanishes in
the residue field `A ⧸ p`.

TauCeti.poincarePolynomial_map.signature:
TauCeti.poincarePolynomial_map.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {B : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} [Group W]

  (e : W ≃* H) : TauCeti.poincarePolynomial (cs.map e) = TauCeti.poincarePolynomial cs
TauCeti.poincarePolynomial_map.doc:
**The Poincaré polynomial is invariant under transporting the Coxeter system along a group
isomorphism**, since the length function is (`TauCeti.length_map`). The hypothesis `[Finite H]`
follows from `[Finite W]`, but is needed to state the left-hand side.

TauCeti.poincarePairing.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {E : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]

TauCeti.poincarePairing.doc:
The Poincaré pairing `H^k_dR(M) → H^l_c(M) → ℝ` on an oriented boundaryless manifold of
dimension `k + l`, sending classes `[φ]` and `[ψ]` to `∫_M φ ∧ ψ`. It is the wedge product
`H^k_dR(M) → H^l_c(M) → H^(k+l)_c(M)` followed by integration.

TauCeti.pivotalIsoApp_rightDual.signature:
TauCeti.pivotalIsoApp_rightDual.{v, u} {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C]

TauCeti.pivotalIsoApp_rightDual.doc:
**The Freyd–Yetter identity**: the component of the pivotal isomorphism at `Xᘁ` is the mate
of the inverse of its component at `X`.

TauCeti.pivotalBalancedEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.pivotalBalancedEquiv.{v, u} (C : Type u) [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C]
  [CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory C] [CategoryTheory.BraidedCategory C]
  [CategoryTheory.RigidCategory C] : TauCeti.PivotalCategory C ≃ TauCeti.BalancedCategory C
TauCeti.pivotalBalancedEquiv.doc:
Pivotal structures on a braided rigid category correspond to balanced structures via
`θ_X = φ_X ≫ u_X⁻¹`, with inverse `φ_X = θ_X ≫ u_X`.

TauCeti.piHilbertBasis.doc:
**The `Fintype`-indexed product Hilbert basis.** Pointwise products of coordinatewise Hilbert
bases form a Hilbert basis of `L²(Measure.pi μ)`, indexed by the dependent function type.

TauCeti.peterWeylBasis.signature:
TauCeti.peterWeylBasis.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {G : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_3} [RCLike 𝕜]
  [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] [MeasurableSpace G]
  [BorelSpace G] [IsAlgClosed 𝕜] {models : ι → TauCeti.IrrepModel 𝕜 G}
  (h : TauCeti.IsIrrepSkeleton models) :
  HilbertBasis ((i : ι) × Fin (models i).dim × Fin (models i).dim) 𝕜
    ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp 𝕜 2 (TauCeti.haarProb G))
TauCeti.peterWeylBasis.doc:
**The Peter-Weyl theorem.** For a skeleton of the unitary dual of a compact group,
the normalized matrix coefficients `√(dim V_i) · (models i)_{ab}` are a Hilbert basis of `L²(G)`,
indexed by `Σ i, Fin (models i).dim × Fin (models i).dim`.

Algebraic closedness of the scalars is Schur's lemma, and enters through the orthonormality half.

TauCeti.perronFormula_of_forall_absNorm_.signature:
TauCeti.perronFormula_of_forall_absNorm_ne.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  {f : TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction K} {x c : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (hc : 0 < c)
  (hoff :
    ∀ (I : ↥(nonZeroDivisors (Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)))), ↑(Ideal.absNorm ↑I) ≠ x)
  (h : LSeriesSummable ⇑((TauCeti.normCoeff K) f) ↑c) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun T =>
      (↑(2 * Real.pi))⁻¹ *
        ∫ (t : ℝ) in -T..T,
          LSeries (⇑((TauCeti.normCoeff K) f)) (↑c + ↑t * Complex.I) *
            TauCeti.perronIntegrand x c t)
    Filter.atTop (nhds (TauCeti.idealSummatory K f x))
TauCeti.perronFormula_of_forall_absNorm_.doc:
**The Perron formula off the norms.**  If `x > 0` is not the absolute norm of a nonzero ideal,
the truncated Perron integral tends to the inclusive ideal sum `∑_{N(I) ≤ x} f(I)`.

TauCeti.perronFormula_natCast.signature:
TauCeti.perronFormula_natCast.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  {f : TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction K} {c : ℝ} {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (hc : 0 < c)
  (h : LSeriesSummable ⇑((TauCeti.normCoeff K) f) ↑c) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun T =>
      (↑(2 * Real.pi))⁻¹ *
        ∫ (t : ℝ) in -T..T,
          LSeries (⇑((TauCeti.normCoeff K) f)) (↑c + ↑t * Complex.I) *
            TauCeti.perronIntegrand (↑N) c t)
    Filter.atTop (nhds (TauCeti.idealSummatory K f ↑N - ((TauCeti.normCoeff K) f) N / 2))
TauCeti.perronFormula_natCast.doc:
**The Perron formula at an integer endpoint.**  At `x = N` the truncated Perron integral tends
to the inclusive ideal sum `∑_{N(I) ≤ N} f(I)` less half of the norm coefficient at `N`: every
ideal of norm exactly `N` enters with half weight.

TauCeti.perronFormula.signature:
TauCeti.perronFormula.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  {f : TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction K} {x c : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (hc : 0 < c)
  (h : LSeriesSummable ⇑((TauCeti.normCoeff K) f) ↑c) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun T =>
      (↑(2 * Real.pi))⁻¹ *
        ∫ (t : ℝ) in -T..T,
          LSeries (⇑((TauCeti.normCoeff K) f)) (↑c + ↑t * Complex.I) *
            TauCeti.perronIntegrand x c t)
    Filter.atTop
    (nhds (∑ I ∈ TauCeti.idealsLE K x, f I * TauCeti.perronStep (x / ↑(Ideal.absNorm ↑I))))
TauCeti.perronFormula.doc:
**The arithmetic Perron formula for ideal sums.**  Where the `L`-series of the norm
coefficients of `f` converges absolutely on the line `Re s = c`, the truncated Perron integral
tends, as the height grows, to the ideal sum `∑_{N(I) ≤ x} f(I)` in which each ideal of norm
exactly `x` carries half weight.  The two readings of this limit are
`TauCeti.perronFormula_of_forall_absNorm_ne` and `TauCeti.perronFormula_natCast`.

TauCeti.periodBasis.signature:
TauCeti.periodBasis.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {Y : Type u_1} {Λ : Type u_2} [AddCommGroup Λ]
  {E : Type u_3} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (P : Y → Λ →ₗ[ℤ] E)

  (hinj : ∀ (y : Y), Function.Injective ⇑(P y)) (y : Y) : Module.Basis ι ℝ E
TauCeti.periodBasis.doc:
The **period basis** at `y`: the periods `P y (b i)` of a `ℤ`-basis `b` of `Λ`, viewed as a
real basis of `E`. They form a `ℤ`-basis of the full lattice `LinearMap.range (P y)`, hence a real
basis of `E`. Its inverse coordinate map `x ↦ ∑ i, x i • P y (b i)` is the real linear
isomorphism `ℝ^ι ≃ E` carrying the standard lattice `ℤ^ι` onto the periods at `y`.

TauCeti.perimeter.signature:
TauCeti.perimeter.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E)
  (Ω : TopologicalSpace.Opens E) (s : Set E) : ENNReal
TauCeti.perimeter.doc:
The **perimeter** of a set `s` in the open set `Ω`, relative to the measure `μ`: the total
variation of the indicator of `s` on `Ω`. For a null-measurable `s` it is the extended supremum
of `∫_s div φ ∂μ` over test vector fields `φ ∈ 𝓓(Ω, E)` with `‖φ x‖ ≤ 1` everywhere
(`TauCeti.perimeter_eq_iSup`).

TauCeti.pathIntegral_mextDeriv_ofFunctio.signature:
TauCeti.pathIntegral_mextDeriv_ofFunction.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {E : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2}

TauCeti.pathIntegral_mextDeriv_ofFunctio.doc:
**The fundamental theorem of calculus for line integrals.** The line integral of the
differential of a `C¹` function along a `C¹` curve is the difference of the values of the
function at the endpoints.

TauCeti.pathIntegral_mextDeriv.doc:
**The fundamental theorem of calculus for line integrals**, for a `C¹` form `ψ` of degree
zero: the line integral of `dψ` along a `C¹` curve is the difference of the values of `ψ` at the
endpoints.

TauCeti.pathIntegral.signature:
TauCeti.pathIntegral.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {E : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3}
  {F : Type u_4} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace H]

  [NormedSpace ℝ F] (φ : TauCeti.RoughForm I M F 1) (γ : ℝ → M) (a b : ℝ) : F
TauCeti.pathIntegral.doc:
The integral of a `1`-form `φ` along a curve `γ : ℝ → M` over the oriented interval `a..b`:
the interval integral of `φ` evaluated on the velocity of `γ`.

TauCeti.pathClassIntegral_mextDeriv_ofFu.signature:
TauCeti.pathClassIntegral_mextDeriv_ofFunction.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {E : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2}

TauCeti.pathClassIntegral_mextDeriv_ofFu.doc:
**The fundamental theorem of calculus for path classes.** The integral of the differential of
a `C²` function along a path class is the difference of the values of the function at the
endpoints.

TauCeti.pathClassIntegral_mextDeriv.signature:
TauCeti.pathClassIntegral_mextDeriv.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {E : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2}

TauCeti.pathClassIntegral_mextDeriv.doc:
**The fundamental theorem of calculus for path classes**, for a `C²` form `ψ` of degree zero:
the integral of `dψ` along a path class is the difference of the values of `ψ` at the
endpoints.

TauCeti.partitionCumulant_eq_prod_freeCu.signature:
TauCeti.partitionCumulant_eq_prod_freeCumulant.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2}
  {α : Type u_3} [LinearOrder α] {s : Finset α} [CommRing R] [Monoid A] (φ : A → R) (a : α → A)

TauCeti.partitionCumulant_eq_prod_freeCu.doc:
The free cumulants are *multiplicative*: the free cumulant of a noncrossing partition is the
product of the free cumulants of the words read along its parts, `κ_π(a) = ∏_{B ∈ π} κ_B(a)`.

TauCeti.padicValNat_factorial_eq_add_sum.signature:
TauCeti.padicValNat_factorial_eq_add_sum (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (n h : ℕ) :

    padicValNat p (n / p ^ h).factorial + ∑ k ∈ Finset.range h, n / p ^ (k + 1)
TauCeti.padicValNat_factorial_eq_add_sum.doc:
**Legendre's formula, truncated at level `h`.** The `p`-adic valuation of `n!` exceeds that of
`⌊n / pʰ⌋!` by `∑_{k = 1}^{h} ⌊n / pᵏ⌋`.

TauCeti.padicCompletionUnitsNormCokernel.signature:
TauCeti.padicCompletionUnitsNormCokernelEquiv.{u_1} (p : ℕ) (K : Type) [Field K] [ValuativeRel K]
  [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] (L : Type u_1) [Field L] [Algebra K L]
  [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hpK : ↑p ≠ 0) {m : ℕ}

    Additive (TauCeti.powerClassQuotient (Abelianization Gal(L/K)) (p ^ m))
TauCeti.padicCompletionUnitsNormCokernel.doc:
**The cokernel of the completed norm** `A(L) → A(K)` is `Gal(L/K)^ab / (Gal(L/K)^ab)^(p^m)`,
the maximal `p`-quotient of `Gal(L/K)^ab`, once `p ^ m` contains the full power of `p` dividing
`#Gal(L/K)^ab`. The isomorphism is induced by the completed norm residue map
(`TauCeti.padicCompletionUnitsNormCokernelEquiv_mk`).

TauCeti.padicCompletionUnitsEquivAbelian.signature:
TauCeti.padicCompletionUnitsEquivAbelianizationProP (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (K L : Type)
  [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] [ValuativeRel L] [TopologicalSpace L]

    TauCeti.abelianizationProP p (TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup K) ↑(TauCeti.galoisSubgroup K L ι)
TauCeti.padicCompletionUnitsEquivAbelian.doc:
**Local reciprocity for `A(L)`.** If `V ≤ G_K` is the subgroup fixing the image of a finite
extension `L/K` under `ι : L →ₐ[K] Kˢ`, then the multiplicative `p`-adic completion `A(L)` of
`Lˣ` is canonically isomorphic to `V^ab(p)`, the maximal pro-`p` quotient of the topological
abelianization of `V`.

TauCeti.outerAction.signature:
TauCeti.outerAction.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [Group E] [TopologicalSpace E] (N : Subgroup E) [N.Normal]
  [SeparatelyContinuousMul E] : E ⧸ N →* TauCeti.ContinuousOut ↥N
TauCeti.outerAction.doc:
The **outer action** of `E ⧸ N` on a normal subgroup `N`: the class of `e` acts by the outer
class of conjugation by `e` (`outerAction_mk`). It is well defined because conjugation by an
element of `N` is inner.

TauCeti.orthogonalComplement_iSup_eigens.signature:
TauCeti.orthogonalComplement_iSup_eigenspaces_convolutionOperator_eq_bot.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1}

  [MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G] (k : C(G, 𝕜)) (hk : ∀ (g : G), k g⁻¹ = (starRingEnd 𝕜) (k g)) :

TauCeti.orthogonalComplement_iSup_eigens.doc:
**The spectral theorem for a symmetric convolution operator:** its eigenspaces span a dense
subspace of `L²(G)`, in the sense that their supremum has trivial orthogonal complement. Together
with `finiteDimensional_eigenspace_convolutionOperator` this says that `L²(G)` is exhausted, up to
the kernel of the operator, by finite-dimensional translation-invariant subspaces.

TauCeti.one_le_natDenominator_pow_mul_ho.signature:

**Evertse's lower bound for the conjugates of an algebraic number.** Let `z` be a nonzero
algebraic number of degree `d` in a field of characteristic zero and `w` a complex conjugate of
`z`. Then `den(z) ^ d * house(z) ^ (d - 1) * ‖w‖ ≥ 1`.

TauCeti.one_le_natDenominator_pow_mul_ho.signature:
TauCeti.one_le_natDenominator_pow_mul_house_pow_mul_norm {z : ℂ} (hz : IsAlgebraic ℚ z)
  (hz0 : z ≠ 0) :

TauCeti.one_le_natDenominator_pow_mul_ho.doc:
**Evertse's lower bound.** A nonzero algebraic number `z ∈ ℂ` of degree `d` satisfies
`den(z) ^ d * house(z) ^ (d - 1) * ‖z‖ ≥ 1`.

TauCeti.one_add_norm_sq_rpow_le_mul_sub.signature:
TauCeti.one_add_norm_sq_rpow_le_mul_sub.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] (s : ℝ)
  (x y : E) :

TauCeti.one_add_norm_sq_rpow_le_mul_sub.doc:
**Peetre's inequality**, in the form `⟨x⟩ ^ s ≤ 2 ^ (|s| / 2) ⟨x - y⟩ ^ |s| ⟨y⟩ ^ s` for every
real `s`.

TauCeti.one_add_norm_add_sq_rpow_le_mul.signature:
TauCeti.one_add_norm_add_sq_rpow_le_mul.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [SeminormedAddGroup E] (s : ℝ)
  (x y : E) :
  (1 + ‖x + y‖ ^ 2) ^ (s / 2) ≤ 2 ^ (|s| / 2) * (1 + ‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (s / 2) * (1 + ‖y‖ ^ 2) ^ (|s| / 2)
TauCeti.one_add_norm_add_sq_rpow_le_mul.doc:
**Peetre's inequality.** For every real `s`, the Japanese bracket `⟨x⟩ = (1 + ‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (1/2)`
satisfies `⟨x + y⟩ ^ s ≤ 2 ^ (|s| / 2) ⟨x⟩ ^ s ⟨y⟩ ^ |s|`.

TauCeti.one_add_norm_add_sq_rpow_le.signature:

TauCeti.one_add_norm_add_sq_rpow_le.doc:
**Peetre's inequality, subadditive form.** The Japanese bracket weight
`(1 + ‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (s / 2)` is subadditive up to a constant: for `s ≥ 0`,
`(1 + ‖x + y‖ ^ 2) ^ (s / 2) ≤ 2 ^ s ((1 + ‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (s / 2) + (1 + ‖y‖ ^ 2) ^ (s / 2))`.

TauCeti.ofReal_neg_pow_mul_addHaar_ball_.signature:
TauCeti.ofReal_neg_pow_mul_addHaar_ball_le_mul_mongeAmpereMeasure.{u_1} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  [BorelSpace E] {Ω : Set E} {u : E → ℝ} [Nontrivial E] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E)
  [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] [DecidablePred fun x => x ∈ Ω] (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩ : Bornology.IsBounded Ω)
  (hu : ConvexOn ℝ Ω u) (hc : ContinuousOn u (closure Ω)) (hfr : ∀ x ∈ frontier Ω, 0 ≤ u x) {x₀ : E}
  (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ Ω) :
  ENNReal.ofReal (-u x₀) ^ Module.finrank ℝ E * μ (Metric.ball 0 1) ≤
    2 ^ (Module.finrank ℝ E + 1) *
        ENNReal.ofReal (Metric.diam Ω ^ (Module.finrank ℝ E - 1) * Metric.infDist x₀ Ωᶜ) *
      (TauCeti.mongeAmpereMeasure μ fun x => if x ∈ Ω then ↑(u x) else ⊤) Ω
TauCeti.ofReal_neg_pow_mul_addHaar_ball_.doc:
**The Aleksandrov maximum principle.** Let `Ω` be a bounded open convex subset of a real inner
product space `E` of finite dimension `n ≥ 1`, and let `u` be convex on `Ω`, continuous on its
closure, and nonnegative on its frontier. Then at every `x₀ ∈ Ω`,

  `max (-u x₀) 0 ^ n * μ (ball 0 1) ≤ 2 ^ (n + 1) * diam Ω ^ (n - 1) * dist(x₀, ∂Ω) * MA_u(Ω)`,

where `dist(x₀, ∂Ω)` is the distance from `x₀` to the complement of `Ω` and `MA_u` is the
Aleksandrov Monge–Ampère measure of `u` (extended by `⊤` off `Ω`) with respect to the additive
Haar measure `μ`. When `MA_u(Ω)` is finite, this bounds the negative part `max (-u x₀) 0` above
on `Ω` and shows that `max (-u x₀) 0 = O(dist(x₀, ∂Ω) ^ (1 / n))` as `x₀` approaches the
boundary.

TauCeti.ofReal_mul_measure_compl_closedB.signature:
TauCeti.ofReal_mul_measure_compl_closedBall_le_wassersteinEDist.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} {p : ENNReal}
  [PseudoMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [SecondCountableTopology X]
  [Fact (1 ≤ p)] (x : X) (μ : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure X) (r : ℝ) :
  ENNReal.ofReal r * ↑μ (Metric.closedBall x r)ᶜ ≤
    TauCeti.wassersteinEDist p (MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac x) ↑μ
TauCeti.ofReal_mul_measure_compl_closedB.doc:
**Markov's inequality for the Wasserstein distance from a Dirac law.** For a probability
measure `μ` and a radius `r`, the mass of `μ` outside the closed ball of radius `r` about `x`,
multiplied by `r`, is at most `W_p (δ_x, μ)`, for every exponent `1 ≤ p`.

TauCeti.ofReal_mgf_sub_integral_le_linte.signature:
TauCeti.ofReal_mgf_sub_integral_le_lintegral.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

  (hfm : Measurable f) (hfi : MeasureTheory.Integrable f μ) {t : ℝ}
  (hint : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (t * (f x - ∫ (y : Ω), f y ∂μ))) μ)
  (hneg : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-t * f x)) μ) :
  ENNReal.ofReal (ProbabilityTheory.mgf (fun x => f x - ∫ (y : Ω), f y ∂μ) μ t) ≤

TauCeti.ofReal_mgf_sub_integral_le_linte.doc:
**Symmetrization by Jensen's inequality.** For a probability measure `μ`, the moment
generating function of `f - 𝔼 f` at `t` is at most `∫∫ exp (t (f x - f y)) dμ(x) dμ(y)`.

TauCeti.ofReal_integral_sub_integral_le_.signature:
TauCeti.ofReal_integral_sub_integral_le_wassersteinEDist_one.{u} {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X]
  {μ ν : MeasureTheory.Measure X} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] {f : X → ℝ} (hf : LipschitzWith 1 f)
  (hμ : MeasureTheory.Integrable f μ) (hν : MeasureTheory.Integrable f ν) :

TauCeti.ofReal_integral_sub_integral_le_.doc:
**Kantorovich–Rubinstein weak duality.** The difference of the expectations of an integrable
`1`-Lipschitz real function under two measures is at most their `1`-Wasserstein distance. No
measurability of the ground distance and no finiteness of the measures is needed.

TauCeti.ofReal_cdf_sub_le_measure.doc:
**The Fréchet–Hoeffding bound on a quadrant.** Every transport plan of two real laws gives the
quadrant `Iic a ×ˢ Ioi b` mass at least `cdf μ a - cdf ν b`: the pairs with first coordinate at most
`a` carry mass `cdf μ a`, and at most `cdf ν b` of it has second coordinate at most `b`.

TauCeti.oddOrthogonalWeylDimension_eq_pr.signature:
TauCeti.oddOrthogonalWeylDimension_eq_prod_prod_div (n : ℕ) (μ : YoungDiagram) :
  ↑(TauCeti.oddOrthogonalWeylDimension n μ) =
    ∏ i ∈ Finset.range n,
      (↑(μ.rowLen i) + ↑n - ↑i - 1 / 2) / (↑n - ↑i - 1 / 2) *
        ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ico (i + 1) n,
          ((↑(μ.rowLen i) + ↑n - ↑i - 1 / 2) ^ 2 - (↑(μ.rowLen j) + ↑n - ↑j - 1 / 2) ^ 2) /
            ((↑n - ↑i - 1 / 2) ^ 2 - (↑n - ↑j - 1 / 2) ^ 2)
TauCeti.oddOrthogonalWeylDimension_eq_pr.doc:
**The Weyl dimension formula for `SO (2n + 1)` in its product form**: over `ℚ`, with
`lᵢ = μᵢ + n - i - 1/2` and `rᵢ = n - i - 1/2` the entries of `μ + ρ` and of `ρ`, the dimension is

`∏_{i < n} lᵢ / rᵢ · ∏_{i < j < n} (lᵢ² - lⱼ²) / (rᵢ² - rⱼ²)`.

TauCeti.numberField_CoefficientField.signature:

TauCeti.numberField_CoefficientField.doc: **The coefficient field of a newform of weight at least two is a number field.**

TauCeti.nsmul_smul_fixingSubgroupKummerE.signature:

twist.** If `g ∈ G_K` acts on `μₙ` as the `k`th power map and the `K`-endomorphism `τ` of `L`

with `μₙ^{⊗ -1} ⊗ Lˣ ⧸ (Lˣ)ⁿ` as a module over `G_K ⧸ N`.

TauCeti.not_isTopologicalGroup_restricte.doc:
The restricted product `Πʳ n : ℕ, [Multiplicative ℚ, ⊥]` is not a topological group: the
hypothesis `Fact (∀ i, IsOpen (A i))` of Mathlib's `RestrictedProduct.isTopologicalGroup` cannot be
dropped.

TauCeti.not_isPreconnected_compl_union_o.signature:
TauCeti.not_isPreconnected_compl_union_of_not_isPreconnected_inter {S T : Set ℂ} (hS : IsClosed S)
  (hT : IsClosed T) (hSc : IsPreconnected S) (hTc : IsPreconnected T)
  (hSTb : Bornology.IsBounded (S ∩ T)) (hST : ¬IsPreconnected (S ∩ T)) : ¬IsPreconnected (S ∪ T)ᶜ
TauCeti.not_isPreconnected_compl_union_o.doc:
**Janiszewski's second theorem.** If two closed preconnected subsets `S`, `T` of the plane have
a bounded intersection that is not preconnected, then their union separates the plane: the
complement of `S ∪ T` is not preconnected.

TauCeti.not_isPreconnected_compl_range_s.signature:
TauCeti.not_isPreconnected_compl_range_sphere.{w, u} {F : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup F]
  [NormedSpace ℝ F] {E : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  {h : ↑(Metric.sphere 0 1) → ↑(Metric.sphere 0 1)}
  (hEF : Module.finrank ℝ F = Module.finrank ℝ E + 1) (hc : Continuous h)
  (hi : Function.Injective h) : ¬IsPreconnected (Set.range h)ᶜ
TauCeti.not_isPreconnected_compl_range_s.doc:
**The Jordan–Brouwer separation theorem, connected form.** The complement of the image of a
continuous injection of the unit sphere of a finite-dimensional real normed space `E` into the unit
sphere of a real normed space of dimension `dim E + 1` is not preconnected.

TauCeti.not_infEquivAt_nat_int_sumLex_in.doc:
**Elementary equivalence is strictly weaker than infinitary equivalence.** The countable
orders `ℤ` and `ℤ ⊕ₗ ℤ` are elementarily equivalent (`elementarilyEquivalent_int_sumLex_int`),
but some `L_{ω₁ω}` sentence distinguishes them. A fortiori they are not `L_{∞ω}`-equivalent, since
`TauCeti.InfEquivW.infEquivAt` turns `L_{∞ω}`-equivalence into agreement at `ℕ`.

TauCeti.not_hochschildVanishesAt_four_zi.signature:
TauCeti.not_hochschildVanishesAt_four_zigzagStrictAInfinityAlgebra.{u, w} {k : Type w} [CommRing k]
  {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} [Finite V] {hns : ∀ (i : V), ∃ j, G.Adj i j} [Nontrivial k]
  {δ : Fin 4 → G.Dart} (hδ : Function.Injective δ) {v : V}
  (hv : ∀ (i : Fin 4), (δ i).toProd.2 = v) :
  ¬(TauCeti.zigzagStrictAInfinityAlgebra k hns).HochschildVanishesAt
      ⟨4, TauCeti.not_hochschildVanishesAt_four_zigzagStrictAInfinityAlgebra._proof_1⟩
TauCeti.not_hochschildVanishesAt_four_zi.doc:
**The quartic Hochschild cohomology `HH^{4, -2}` of a zigzag algebra is nonzero** when four
distinct darts of `G` have a common head, that is when some vertex has four distinct neighbours,
over every nontrivial commutative ring: some Hochschild cocycle of the strict zigzag algebra of
suspended degree one, concentrated on words of length four, is not the Hochschild differential of
a cochain of degree zero.

TauCeti.not_forall_alternatingGroup_le_o.signature:
TauCeti.not_forall_alternatingGroup_le_of_isPreprimitive_of_isCycle_mem_of_card_support_eq :
  ¬∀ (α : Type) [inst : Fintype α] [inst_1 : DecidableEq α] (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)),
      MulAction.IsPreprimitive (↥G) α →
        ∀ g ∈ G,
          g.IsCycle →
            Nat.Prime g.support.card → g.support.card = Nat.card α → alternatingGroup α ≤ G
TauCeti.not_forall_alternatingGroup_le_o.doc:
**Jordan's theorem fails in degree `p`.** A primitive permutation group of degree `n`
containing a cycle of prime length `p` need not contain the alternating group when `p = n`: the
affine group `AGL(1, 5)` is primitive on five points and contains a `5`-cycle. This shows that the
bound `p + 3 ≤ n` of `TauCeti.alternatingGroup_le_of_isPreprimitive_of_isCycle_mem` cannot be
weakened to `p ≤ n`.

TauCeti.not_forall_alternatingGroup_le_o.signature:
TauCeti.not_forall_alternatingGroup_le_of_isPreprimitive_of_isCycle_mem_of_card_support_add_one_eq :
  ¬∀ (α : Type) [inst : Fintype α] [inst_1 : DecidableEq α] (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)),
      MulAction.IsPreprimitive (↥G) α →
        ∀ g ∈ G,
          g.IsCycle →
            Nat.Prime g.support.card → g.support.card + 1 = Nat.card α → alternatingGroup α ≤ G
TauCeti.not_forall_alternatingGroup_le_o.doc:
**Jordan's theorem fails in degree `p + 1`.** A primitive permutation group of degree `n`
containing a cycle of prime length `p` need not contain the alternating group when `p + 1 = n`:
the affine group `AGL(1, 8)` of the field with eight elements is primitive on eight points and
contains a `7`-cycle. This shows that the bound `p + 3 ≤ n` of
`TauCeti.alternatingGroup_le_of_isPreprimitive_of_isCycle_mem` cannot be weakened to
`p + 1 ≤ n`.

TauCeti.not_exists_eLpNorm_le_const_mul_.signature:
TauCeti.not_exists_eLpNorm_le_const_mul_eLpNorm_fderiv.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] {p : ENNReal} {k : ℕ∞} (hp₀ : p ≠ 0) :
  ¬∃ C,
      ∀ (u : E → ℝ),
        ContDiff ℝ (↑k) u →
          HasCompactSupport u →
            MeasureTheory.eLpNorm u p μ ≤ ↑C * MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (fderiv ℝ u) p μ
TauCeti.not_exists_eLpNorm_le_const_mul_.doc:
**No Poincaré inequality holds on the whole space.** There is no constant `C` with
`‖u‖_p ≤ C ‖Du‖_p` for every compactly supported `Cᵏ` function `u`, for any order `k ≤ ∞`
and any `p ≠ 0`, including `p = ∞`. In particular, the inequality fails even when restricted
to smooth test functions.

Compare `MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv`, which supplies such a constant once every
`u` is supported in one fixed bounded set; the proof here shows that hypothesis cannot be
dropped.

TauCeti.not_continuous_restrictedProduct.doc:
The inverse of the splitting `restrictedProductSum` of a restricted product over a sum of index
types is not continuous in general: for `Πʳ k : ℕ ⊕ ℕ, [Multiplicative ℚ, ⊥]`, with the trivial,
non-open, reference subgroup at every index, it is a discontinuous bijection. The openness
hypothesis of `continuous_restrictedProductSum_symm` therefore cannot be dropped.

TauCeti.norm_truncatedPerron_LSeries_sub.signature:
TauCeti.norm_truncatedPerron_LSeries_sub_sum_le {f : ℕ → ℂ} {x c T : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (hc : 0 < c)
  (hT : 0 < T) (hoff : ∀ (n : ℕ), f n ≠ 0 → x ≠ ↑n) (h : LSeriesSummable f ↑c) :
  ‖((↑(2 * Real.pi))⁻¹ *
          ∫ (t : ℝ) in -T..T, LSeries f (↑c + ↑t * Complex.I) * TauCeti.perronIntegrand x c t) -
        ∑ n ∈ Finset.Ico 1 ⌈x⌉₊, f n‖ ≤
    ∑' (n : ℕ), ‖f n‖ * ((x / ↑n) ^ c / (Real.pi * T * |Real.log (x / ↑n)|))
TauCeti.norm_truncatedPerron_LSeries_sub.doc:
**The off-norm arithmetic Perron formula.**  When `x` is not a natural number at which `f` is
nonzero, the truncated integral differs from the sharp partial sum `∑_{n < x} f n` by at most the
series of the smoothed-step kernel errors, a series that absolute convergence on the line makes
summable.

TauCeti.norm_truncatedPerron_LSeries_nor.signature:
TauCeti.norm_truncatedPerron_LSeries_normCoeff_sub_idealSummatory_le.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  [NumberField K] {f : TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction K} {x c T : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (hc : 0 < c)
  (hT : 0 < T)
  (hoff :
    ∀ (I : ↥(nonZeroDivisors (Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)))), ↑(Ideal.absNorm ↑I) ≠ x)
  (h : LSeriesSummable ⇑((TauCeti.normCoeff K) f) ↑c) :
  ‖((↑(2 * Real.pi))⁻¹ *
          ∫ (t : ℝ) in -T..T,
            LSeries (⇑((TauCeti.normCoeff K) f)) (↑c + ↑t * Complex.I) *

    ∑' (n : ℕ), ‖((TauCeti.normCoeff K) f) n‖ * ((x / ↑n) ^ c / (Real.pi * T * |Real.log (x / ↑n)|))
TauCeti.norm_truncatedPerron_LSeries_nor.doc:
**The truncated Perron formula off the norms.**  If `x > 0` is not the absolute norm of a
nonzero ideal, then at every positive height `T` the truncated Perron integral differs from the
inclusive ideal sum `∑_{N(I) ≤ x} f(I)` by at most the series of the smoothed-step kernel errors at
the ratios `x / n`.

TauCeti.norm_testFunctionLp_le_mul_norm_.signature:
TauCeti.norm_testFunctionLp_le_mul_norm_gradientTestFunctionLp.{u_1} {E : Type u_1}
  [MeasurableSpace E] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [BorelSpace E] {mu : MeasureTheory.Measure E} [mu.IsAddHaarMeasure]
  {Omega : TopologicalSpace.Opens E} {p : ENNReal} [Fact (1 ≤ p)] {pstar : ENNReal}
  (hpstar : pstar ≠ ⊤) (hexp : pstar⁻¹ + (↑(Module.finrank ℝ E))⁻¹ = p⁻¹)
  (phi : TestFunction Omega ℝ ⊤) :
  ‖TauCeti.testFunctionLp pstar phi‖ ≤
    ↑(MeasureTheory.SNormLESNormFDerivOfEqConst ℝ mu p.toReal) *
      ‖TauCeti.gradientTestFunctionLp p phi‖
TauCeti.norm_testFunctionLp_le_mul_norm_.doc:
**The Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev inequality between test-function classes.** If `1 ≤ p`
and the Sobolev conjugate `p⋆ ≠ ∞` satisfies `1/p⋆ + 1/n = 1/p`, where `n = dim E`, then every test
function `φ` on `Ω` satisfies `‖φ‖_{p⋆} ≤ C ‖∇φ‖_p` for its classes in `L^{p⋆}(Ω)` and
`Lᵖ(Ω, E)`, with Mathlib's constant `MeasureTheory.SNormLESNormFDerivOfEqConst`. This is the
bound along which a map defined on test functions by the gradient norm extends to its completion.

TauCeti.norm_summatory_mul_cpow_le_of_su.signature:

**An imaginary-power Abel bound.** Suppose every index has `N`-value at least `1`, and the
partial sums of `w` are bounded by `C * t ^ θ` on `[1, x]` for a positive exponent `θ`. Twisting
the weight by `(N i) ^ (-z)` with `Re z = 0` preserves that exponent, at the cost of the explicit
factor `1 + ‖z‖ / θ`.

spaces are almost orthogonal in the sense that `∑ j ∈ s, √‖(T i)† ∘L T j‖ ≤ A` and
`∑ j ∈ s, √‖T i ∘L (T j)†‖ ≤ A` for every `i ∈ s`, then `‖∑ i ∈ s, T i‖ ≤ A`.

TauCeti.norm_sq_one_sub_conj_mul_sub_nor.signature:
TauCeti.norm_sq_one_sub_conj_mul_sub_norm_sq_sub (z w : ℂ) :

**Poincaré defect identity (norm form).** The difference of the squared norms of the Moebius
denominator and numerator factors is the product of the two hyperbolic defects:
`‖1 - conj w * z‖ ^ 2 - ‖z - w‖ ^ 2 = (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2) * (1 - ‖w‖ ^ 2)`.

`‖F z‖ ≤ D₁ D₂ A T ^ D₁ exp (D₂ ‖λ‖ T) (3 R / T) ^ (L ^ 2)`.

TauCeti.norm_le_mul_three_mul_div_pow.signature:

**Schwarz's lemma with prescribed zeros**, in the form `M * (3 * R / T) ^ ∑ x ∈ s, k x`. If
`f` is analytic on a neighbourhood of `closedBall c T`, bounded by `M` on `sphere c T`, and
vanishes to order at least `k x` at each point `x` of a finite set `s ⊆ closedBall c R`, where
`3 * R ≤ T`, then `‖f z‖ ≤ M * (3 * R / T) ^ ∑ x ∈ s, k x` on `closedBall c R`.

TauCeti.norm_le_mul_prod_div_pow.doc:
**Schwarz's lemma with prescribed zeros.** If `f` is analytic on a neighbourhood of
`closedBall c T`, bounded by `M` on `sphere c T`, and vanishes to order at least `k x` at each
point `x` of a finite set `s ⊆ ball c T`, then on `closedBall c T`
`‖f z‖ ≤ M * ∏ x ∈ s, (‖z - x‖ / (T - ‖x - c‖)) ^ k x`.

TauCeti.norm_iteratedFDeriv_heatKernel_c.signature:
TauCeti.norm_iteratedFDeriv_heatKernel_convolution_le_of_holderWith.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1}
  {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] {g : E → F} {M t : ℝ} [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
