**Hölder bounds on the derivatives of a heat convolution.** If `g` is bounded and `α`-Hölder
with constant `H`, then for `m ≥ 1` and `t > 0`,
`‖D^m (K_t ⋆ g)(x)‖ ≤ H ∫ ‖D^m K_t(z)‖ ‖z‖^α dz`. By
`TauCeti.exists_integral_norm_iteratedFDeriv_heatKernel_mul_rpow_le` the right side is
`O(H t^((α - m) / 2))`, which for `m = 2` is integrable in time near `t = 0` when `α > 0`.

TauCeti.norm_inverse_one_sub_sub_one.signature:
TauCeti.norm_inverse_one_sub_sub_one.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [NormedRing R] [NormOneClass R]
  [HasSummableGeomSeries R] [IsUltrametricDist R] {x : R} (hx : ‖x‖ < 1) :
  ‖Ring.inverse (1 - x) - 1‖ = ‖x‖
TauCeti.norm_inverse_one_sub_sub_one.doc:
**Ultrametric Neumann estimate.** In a normed ring with `‖1‖ = 1`, convergent geometric
series and an ultrametric norm, `‖(1 - x)⁻¹ - 1‖ = ‖x‖` whenever `‖x‖ < 1`.

TauCeti.norm_inverse_one_sub.signature:
TauCeti.norm_inverse_one_sub.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [NormedRing R] [NormOneClass R]
  [HasSummableGeomSeries R] [IsUltrametricDist R] {x : R} (hx : ‖x‖ < 1) :
  ‖Ring.inverse (1 - x)‖ = 1
TauCeti.norm_inverse_one_sub.doc:
**Ultrametric Neumann estimate.** In a normed ring with `‖1‖ = 1`, convergent geometric
series and an ultrametric norm, the inverse of `1 - x` has norm one whenever `‖x‖ < 1`.

TauCeti.norm_heatCauchyPotential_sub_hea.doc:
**The temporal Hölder estimate of the Cauchy heat potential.** If `g` is continuous and
`α`-Hölder with constant `H`, its Cauchy potential `u` satisfies
`‖u(t, x) - u(s, x)‖ ≤ H M_α |t - s|^(α/2)`, where `M_α = ∫ ‖y‖^α K_1(y) dy` is
`TauCeti.heatKernelMoment`.

TauCeti.norm_fderiv_le_of_forall_mem_bal.doc:
**Cauchy's estimate on a ball in a complex normed space.** If `f` is holomorphic on
`ball c r` and bounded there by `M`, then `‖fderiv ℂ f c‖ ≤ 2 * M / r`.

TauCeti.norm_det_mul_max_norm_le.signature:
TauCeti.norm_det_mul_max_norm_le.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NormedField 𝕜] (a b a' b' x y : 𝕜) :
  ‖a * b' - b * a'‖ * max ‖x‖ ‖y‖ ≤
    (‖a‖ + ‖b‖ + ‖a'‖ + ‖b'‖) * (‖a * x + b * y‖ + ‖a' * x + b' * y‖)
TauCeti.norm_det_mul_max_norm_le.doc:
**Cramer's rule bound** for two linear forms `L = a x + b y` and `L' = a' x + b' y` in two
variables: the determinant `D = a b' - b a'` satisfies
`‖D‖ max(‖x‖, ‖y‖) ≤ (‖a‖ + ‖b‖ + ‖a'‖ + ‖b'‖) (‖L‖ + ‖L'‖)`.

TauCeti.norm_deriv_lt_one_of_not_injOn.signature:
TauCeti.norm_deriv_lt_one_of_not_injOn.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]

  (hgd : DifferentiableOn ℂ g (Metric.ball c R))
  (hgm : Set.MapsTo g (Metric.ball c R) (Metric.closedBall (g c) R))
  (hgi : ¬Set.InjOn g (Metric.ball c R)) : ‖deriv g c‖ < 1
TauCeti.norm_deriv_lt_one_of_not_injOn.doc:
**Strict Schwarz lemma, equal radii.** A holomorphic map of `ball c R` into
`closedBall (g c) R` that is **not** injective has `‖deriv g c‖ < 1`.

TauCeti.norm_deriv_lt_div_of_not_injOn.signature:
TauCeti.norm_deriv_lt_div_of_not_injOn.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]
  [StrictConvexSpace ℝ E] {g : ℂ → E} {c : ℂ} {R₁ R₂ : ℝ} (hR₁ : 0 < R₁) (hR₂ : 0 < R₂)
  (hgd : DifferentiableOn ℂ g (Metric.ball c R₁))
  (hgm : Set.MapsTo g (Metric.ball c R₁) (Metric.closedBall (g c) R₂))
  (hgi : ¬Set.InjOn g (Metric.ball c R₁)) : ‖deriv g c‖ < R₂ / R₁
TauCeti.norm_deriv_lt_div_of_not_injOn.doc:
**Strict Schwarz lemma.** A holomorphic map of `ball c R₁` into `closedBall (g c) R₂` that is
**not** injective has `‖deriv g c‖ < R₂ / R₁`.

Both radii must be positive: for `R₂ = 0` the map is constant, so it is not injective and the
strict bound fails.

TauCeti.norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_clos.doc:
**Cauchy's estimate, uniformly on a ball.** If `f` is holomorphic on an open set `U` containing
`closedBall c (2 * r)` and `‖f‖ ≤ M` on that closed ball, then `‖deriv f z‖ ≤ M / r` at *every*
point `z` of `ball c r`, not just at the centre.

Halving the radius is what leaves room to recentre `norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_norm_le`
at an arbitrary `z ∈ ball c r`: the ball `closedBall z r` is still inside `closedBall c (2 * r)`.

**Cauchy's estimate on a closed ball.** If `f` is holomorphic on an open set `U` containing
`closedBall c r` and `‖f‖ ≤ M` on that closed ball, then `‖deriv f c‖ ≤ M / r`.

This is Mathlib's `Complex.norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_sphere_norm_le` with its `DiffContOnCl`
hypothesis and its bound on the boundary circle both supplied from a sup bound on a closed ball
inside the domain of holomorphy, which is the form the family estimates below consume.

TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_l.signature:
TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_le {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Metric.ball 0 1))

  ‖deriv f z‖ / (1 - ‖f z‖ ^ 2) ≤ 1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2)
TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_l.doc:
**The infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick inequality.** A holomorphic self-map `f` of the open
unit disc contracts the Poincaré metric: at every point `z` of the disc,
`‖deriv f z‖ / (1 - ‖f z‖ ^ 2) ≤ 1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2)`.

TauCeti.norm_convolutionLp_le.signature:
TauCeti.norm_convolutionLp_le.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace E]
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [BorelSpace E]

TauCeti.norm_convolutionLp_le.doc:
**Young's inequality** for convolution with an integrable kernel:
`‖k ⋆ f‖_p ≤ ‖k‖₁ ‖f‖_p` for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, as a bound on the operator norm.

TauCeti.norm_add_rpow_add_norm_sub_rpow_.signature:
TauCeti.norm_add_rpow_add_norm_sub_rpow_le.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]

TauCeti.norm_add_rpow_add_norm_sub_rpow_.doc:
**The pointwise Clarkson inequality.** For `2 ≤ q` and vectors `a`, `b` of a normed group
satisfying the parallelogram identity,
`‖a + b‖ ^ q + ‖a - b‖ ^ q ≤ 2 ^ (q - 1) * (‖a‖ ^ q + ‖b‖ ^ q)`.

TauCeti.nontrivial_deRhamCohomology_circ.doc: The first de Rham cohomology of the circle is nontrivial.

TauCeti.nonempty_linearEquiv_of_projecti.doc:
**Swan's theorem for `ℤ_p[G]`** (NSW (5.6.10)(ii)). Two finitely generated projective
`ℤ_p[G]`-modules with isomorphic rationalizations are isomorphic.

TauCeti.nonempty_lazardDelineation_of_la.signature:
TauCeti.nonempty_lazardDelineation_of_lazardProjection {n d : ℕ}

**Lazard lifting of a family.** Over a preconnected analytic submanifold on which the Lazard
projection of a family with respect to an irreducible basis is valuation-invariant, the family has
a Lazard delineation. Its members may be nullified at points of the base.

TauCeti.nonempty_layerTateModule.signature:
TauCeti.nonempty_layerTateModule.{u} (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (K L : Type u) [Field L] [Field K]

TauCeti.nonempty_layerTateModule.doc:
**Existence of the Tate module of a finite layer** (NSW (5.6.5) and the proof of (7.4.1)). For
a finite Galois extension `L/K` of `p`-adic fields there is a finitely generated
`ℤ_p[Gal(L/K)]`-module of projective dimension at most one which is an extension of the
augmentation ideal by `A(L)`.

TauCeti.nonempty_continuousMulEquiv_piPa.signature:
TauCeti.nonempty_continuousMulEquiv_piPadicInt.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [ValuativeRel K]
  [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] :

        (TauCeti.wildInertiaSubgroup K).subgroupOf (TauCeti.inertiaSubgroup K) ≃ₜ*
      Multiplicative

          ℤ_[↑↑ℓ]))
TauCeti.nonempty_continuousMulEquiv_piPa.doc:
**Tame inertia is `∏_{ℓ ≠ p} ℤ_ℓ`**: the tame inertia group `I_K/P_K` is isomorphic, as a
topological group, to the product of the additive groups of `ℓ`-adic integers over the primes `ℓ`
different from the residue characteristic `p`. Up to a choice of an isomorphism `ℤ_ℓ(1) ≃ ℤ_ℓ` for
each `ℓ` (`TauCeti.PadicTateTwist.nonempty_continuousAddEquiv`), it is the tame character
`I_K/P_K ≃ ℤ̂^{(p')}(1)` (`TauCeti.quotientWildInertiaSubgroupEquiv`) followed by the
decomposition of `ℤ̂^{(p')}(1)` into its `ℓ`-adic components
(`TauCeti.PrimeToPTateModule.continuousMulEquivPiPadicTateTwist`).

TauCeti.nonempty_continuousMulEquiv_iwas.signature:
TauCeti.nonempty_continuousMulEquiv_iwasawaGroup.{u} (K : Type u) [Field K] [ValuativeRel K]
  [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] :
  Nonempty (TauCeti.tameQuotient K ≃ₜ* TauCeti.IwasawaGroup K)
TauCeti.nonempty_continuousMulEquiv_iwas.doc:
**Iwasawa's theorem**: the tame quotient of the absolute Galois group of `K` is isomorphic, as
a topological group, to the profinite group `⟨σ, τ | σ τ σ⁻¹ = τ ^ q⟩`.

TauCeti.nonempty_continuousMulEquiv_free.signature:
TauCeti.nonempty_continuousMulEquiv_freeProP_of_not_mu (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (K : Type)

  [ValuativeExtension ℚ_[p] K] (hmu : ¬∃ ζ, IsPrimitiveRoot ζ p) :

    (TauCeti.absoluteGaloisGroupProP p K ≃ₜ* TauCeti.freeProP p (Fin (Module.finrank ℚ_[p] K + 1)))
TauCeti.nonempty_continuousMulEquiv_free.doc:
**Shafarevich's theorem.** If a finite compatible extension `K` of `ℚ_[p]` contains no
primitive `p`th root of unity, its maximal pro-`p` Galois group `G_K(p)` is the free pro-`p` group
on `[K : ℚ_[p]] + 1` generators.

TauCeti.nonempty_continuousLinearEquiv_z.signature:
TauCeti.nonempty_continuousLinearEquiv_zeroAtInfty_nat_of_dense_span.{u, v} {K : Type v}
  [NontriviallyNormedField K] [CompleteSpace K] {E : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace K E] [IsUltrametricDist E] [CompleteSpace E] (hE : ¬FiniteDimensional K E)
  {v : ℕ → E} (hv : Dense ↑(Submodule.span K (Set.range v))) :
  Nonempty (E ≃L[K] ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap ℕ K)
TauCeti.nonempty_continuousLinearEquiv_z.doc:
An infinite-dimensional ultrametric Banach space of countable type (some sequence has dense
span) over a complete nontrivially normed field is continuously linearly equivalent to
`C₀(ℕ, K)`.

TauCeti.nonempty_center_algEquiv_conjCla.signature:
TauCeti.nonempty_center_algEquiv_conjClasses.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {G : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [Fintype K] [Group G] [Finite G] (hexp : ∀ (g : G), g ^ Fintype.card K = g) :
  Nonempty (↥(Subalgebra.center K (MonoidAlgebra K G)) ≃ₐ[K] ConjClasses G → K)
TauCeti.nonempty_center_algEquiv_conjCla.doc:
**The good-splitting structure theorem for a finite coefficient field.** The centre of `K[G]`
is `K`-algebra isomorphic to the functions on the conjugacy classes of `G`.

The indexing is by cardinality only: the canonical indexing of the factors is by the maximal ideals
of the centre (`TauCeti.centerAlgEquivPi`), which `TauCeti.card_maximalSpectrum_center` counts.

TauCeti.nonempty_algEquiv_real_or_quater.signature:
TauCeti.nonempty_algEquiv_real_or_quaternion.{u_1} (D : Type u_1) [DivisionRing D] [Algebra ℝ D]
  [Algebra.IsCentral ℝ D] [FiniteDimensional ℝ D] :
  Nonempty (D ≃ₐ[ℝ] ℝ) ∨ Nonempty (D ≃ₐ[ℝ] Quaternion ℝ)
TauCeti.nonempty_algEquiv_real_or_quater.doc:
**Frobenius' theorem.** A finite-dimensional division algebra over `ℝ` with centre `ℝ` is
`ℝ`-isomorphic either to `ℝ` or to the Hamilton quaternions `ℍ[ℝ]`.

This is the classification to use when nothing is known about `D` beyond the hypotheses. If
`finrank ℝ D = 4` is already in hand, `TauCeti.nonempty_algEquiv_quaternion_of_finrank_eq_four`
gives the quaternion isomorphism directly, with no disjunction to discharge.

TauCeti.nonUnitalJacobson.signature:
TauCeti.nonUnitalJacobson.{u_1, u_2} (R : Type u_1) (A : Type u_2) [CommRing R] [NonUnitalRing A]
  [_root_.Module R A] [IsScalarTower R A A] [SMulCommClass R A A] : TwoSidedIdeal A
TauCeti.nonUnitalJacobson.doc: The Jacobson radical of a nonunital algebra, defined through its external unitization.

TauCeti.noetherCharge_eq_of_eulerLagrang.signature:
TauCeti.noetherCharge_eq_of_eulerLagrange.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]

  (hs : IsOpen s) (hs' : IsPreconnected s) (hq : ∀ t ∈ s, HasDerivAt q (v t) t)
  (hEL :
    ∀ t ∈ s,
      HasDerivAt (fun s => fderiv ℝ (fun u => L s (q s, u)) (v s))
        (fderiv ℝ (fun y => L t (y, v t)) (q t)) t)
  (hL : ∀ t ∈ s, DifferentiableAt ℝ (L t) (q t, v t)) (hξ : ∀ t ∈ s, DifferentiableAt ℝ ξ (t, q t))
  (hB : ∀ t ∈ s, DifferentiableAt ℝ B (t, q t))
  (hsym : ∀ t ∈ s, TauCeti.lagrangianVariation L ξ t (q t, v t) = (fderiv ℝ B (t, q t)) (1, v t))

  TauCeti.noetherCharge L ξ B t₀ (q t₀, v t₀) = TauCeti.noetherCharge L ξ B t₁ (q t₁, v t₁)
TauCeti.noetherCharge_eq_of_eulerLagrang.doc:
**Noether's theorem.** Let `q` solve the Euler–Lagrange equations with velocity `v` on an open
preconnected set of times `s`, and suppose that, at every time of `s`, the infinitesimal variation
of `L` under `ξ` along the solution is the total time derivative of the gauge term `B`. Then the
Noether charge takes the same value at all times of `s`.

TauCeti.noRetraction_diskBoundary.doc:
**The no-retraction theorem**: the boundary sphere `∂Dⁿ` of the disk is not a retract of
the disk `Dⁿ`. That is, there are no maps `i : ∂Dⁿ ⟶ Dⁿ` and `r : Dⁿ ⟶ ∂Dⁿ` with `i ≫ r = 𝟙`;
in particular the boundary inclusion `TopCat.diskBoundaryInclusion n` has no retraction. This
includes `n = 0`, where the boundary is empty.

TauCeti.ne_zero_of_eqOn_dedekindZeta.doc:
**The Dedekind zeta function has no zeros on the line `Re s = 1` away from its pole.** If `f`
agrees with `ζ_K` on `Re s > 1` and is complex differentiable at a point `s ≠ 1` with `Re s = 1`,
then `f s ≠ 0`. By `exists_differentiableOn_eq_dedekindZeta_sub`, such an `f` exists: the
meromorphic continuation of `ζ_K`.

TauCeti.ncard_isomorphic_mul_natCard_alg.signature:
TauCeti.ncard_isomorphic_mul_natCard_algEquiv.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [ValuativeRel K]
  [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] {n : ℕ}
  {L : IntermediateField K (SeparableClosure K)} (hL : L ∈ TauCeti.totallyRamifiedOfDegree K n) :
  {M | M ∈ TauCeti.totallyRamifiedOfDegree K n ∧ Nonempty (↥L ≃ₐ[K] ↥M)}.ncard *
      Nat.card Gal(↥L/K) =
    n
TauCeti.ncard_isomorphic_mul_natCard_alg.doc:
**The orbit count** ([Serre 1978, Remarque 3°]): for `L ∈ σ_K(n)`, the isomorphism class of `L`
inside `σ_K(n)` has `n / #Aut_K(L)` members, in multiplied form. The extension `L / K` is separable
of degree `n`, so it has `n` embeddings into `SeparableClosure K`; their images are the members of
the class, and the embeddings with a given image form a torsor under `Aut_K(L)`.

TauCeti.natCast_le_mahlerExponent.signature:
TauCeti.natCast_le_mahlerExponent {n : ℕ} {ξ : ℝ}
  (hξ : ¬(IsAlgebraic ℚ ξ ∧ (minpoly ℚ ξ).natDegree ≤ n)) : ↑n ≤ TauCeti.mahlerExponent n ξ
TauCeti.natCast_le_mahlerExponent.doc:
**Dirichlet's lower bound for Mahler's exponent.** If `ξ` is not algebraic of degree at
most `n`, then `w_n(ξ) ≥ n`.

TauCeti.natCard_zerothHomotopy_sphere_co.signature:
TauCeti.natCard_zerothHomotopy_sphere_compl_range_eq_two.{w, u} {F : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup F]

  (hEF : Module.finrank ℝ F = Module.finrank ℝ E + 1) (hc : Continuous h)
  (hi : Function.Injective h) : Nat.card (ZerothHomotopy ↑(Set.range h)ᶜ) = 2
TauCeti.natCard_zerothHomotopy_sphere_co.doc:
**The Jordan–Brouwer separation theorem.** The complement of the image of a continuous injection
of the unit sphere of a finite-dimensional real normed space `E` into the unit sphere of a real
normed space of dimension `dim E + 1` has exactly two path components (Hatcher,
*Algebraic Topology*, Corollary 2B.2).

TauCeti.natCard_nsmul_permK0_quotient_to.signature:
TauCeti.natCard_nsmul_permK0_quotient_top_eq_sum_artinCoeff.{u} (k G : Type u) [Field k] [Group G]

TauCeti.natCard_nsmul_permK0_quotient_to.doc: **Artin's signed permutation identity in the exact Grothendieck group over every field.**

TauCeti.natCard_nsmul_one_eq_sum_artinCo.signature:
TauCeti.natCard_nsmul_one_eq_sum_artinCoeff_indK0.{u} (k G : Type u) [Field k] [Group G]

  Nat.card G • 1 = ∑ᶠ (C : Subgroup G), (C.artinCoeff * ↑(Nat.card ↥C)) • (TauCeti.indK0 k C) 1
TauCeti.natCard_nsmul_one_eq_sum_artinCo.doc:
**Artin's identity in `G₀(k[G])` over every field**, written as induction of the unit
from subgroups. No division by the group order is required.

TauCeti.natCard_nsmul_eq_sum_artinCoeff_.signature:
TauCeti.natCard_nsmul_eq_sum_artinCoeff_indK0_resK0.{u} (k G : Type u) [Field k] [Group G]

TauCeti.natCard_nsmul_eq_sum_artinCoeff_.doc:
**Artin's induction identity for every virtual class over every field.** Multiplying by
`|G|` expresses a class as the Artin-coefficient sum of its induced restrictions.

TauCeti.natCard_monoidHom_le.signature:
TauCeti.natCard_monoidHom_le.{u_1, u_2} (G : Type u_1) (M : Type u_2) [MulOneClass G] [Finite G]
  [CommRing M] [IsDomain M] : Nat.card (G →* M) ≤ Nat.card G
TauCeti.natCard_monoidHom_le.doc:
**Dedekind's bound.** A finite monoid `G` has at most `#G` homomorphisms into a domain `M`,
since they are linearly independent in the `M`-module `G → M` of rank `#G`.

TauCeti.natCard_le_eighty_four_mul_genus.signature:
TauCeti.natCard_le_eighty_four_mul_genus_sub_one_of_not_dvd.{u, v} {k : Type u} {F : Type v}
  [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F] [PerfectField k] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p]
  (hF : TauCeti.IsFunctionField k F) (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F) (G : Subgroup Gal(F/k))
  [Finite ↥G] (hgenus : 2 ≤ TauCeti.genus k F) (hp : ¬p ∣ Nat.card ↥G) :
  Nat.card ↥G ≤ 84 * (TauCeti.genus k F - 1)
TauCeti.natCard_le_eighty_four_mul_genus.doc:
**The Hurwitz bound for a group of order prime to the characteristic** (Stichtenoth,
Exercise 3.18): over a perfect constant field of characteristic `p`, a finite group `G` of
automorphisms of a function field of genus `g ≥ 2` with `p ∤ |G|` has order at most `84 (g - 1)`.

The ramification index of a place of `F` over the fixed field divides `|G|`, by the fundamental
identity for the Galois extension `F / F^G`, so it too is prime to `p` and every place is tame
(`TauCeti.Place.isTame_iff_not_dvd_ramificationIdx`).

TauCeti.natCard_le_eighty_four_mul_genus.signature:
TauCeti.natCard_le_eighty_four_mul_genus_sub_one_of_charZero.{u, v} {k : Type u} {F : Type v}

  (hgenus : 2 ≤ TauCeti.genus k F) : Nat.card ↥G ≤ 84 * (TauCeti.genus k F - 1)
TauCeti.natCard_le_eighty_four_mul_genus.doc:
**The Hurwitz bound in characteristic zero** (Stichtenoth, Exercise 3.18): a finite group of
automorphisms of a function field of genus `g ≥ 2` with exact constant field of characteristic zero
has order at most `84 (g - 1)`.  No tameness hypothesis is needed: every place is tame
(`TauCeti.Place.isTame_of_charZero`).

TauCeti.natCard_le_eighty_four_mul_genus.signature:
TauCeti.natCard_le_eighty_four_mul_genus_sub_one.{u, v} {k : Type u} {F : Type v} [Field k]
  [Field F] [Algebra k F] (hF : TauCeti.IsFunctionField k F) (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F)
  (G : Subgroup Gal(F/k)) [Finite ↥G] (hgenus : 2 ≤ TauCeti.genus k F)
  (htame :
    ∀ (P : TauCeti.Place k F), TauCeti.Place.IsTame k (↥(IntermediateField.fixedField G)) P) :
  Nat.card ↥G ≤ 84 * (TauCeti.genus k F - 1)
TauCeti.natCard_le_eighty_four_mul_genus.doc:
**The Hurwitz bound** (Stichtenoth, Exercise 3.18): a finite group `G` of automorphisms of a
function field of genus `g ≥ 2`, every place of which is tame over the fixed field, has order at
most `84 (g - 1)`.

TauCeti.mycielski_prod.signature:
TauCeti.mycielski_prod.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [TopologicalSpace.IsCompletelyMetrizableSpace X] [PerfectSpace X] [Nonempty X] {M : Set (X × X)}
  (hM : IsMeagre M) :
  ∃ f, Continuous f ∧ Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ (x y : ℕ → Bool), x ≠ y → (f x, f y) ∉ M
TauCeti.mycielski_prod.doc:
**Mycielski's theorem, binary case.** A meagre subset `M` of `X × X`, for a nonempty perfect
completely metrizable space `X`, misses every pair `(f x, f y)` with `x ≠ y` for some continuous
injection `f` of Cantor space into `X`.

TauCeti.mycielski.signature:
TauCeti.mycielski.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [TopologicalSpace.IsCompletelyMetrizableSpace X] [PerfectSpace X] [Nonempty X] (k : ℕ → ℕ)
  (R : (n : ℕ) → Set (Fin (k n) → X)) (hR : ∀ (n : ℕ), IsMeagre (R n)) :
  ∃ f,
    Continuous f ∧
      Function.Injective f ∧
        ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Fin (k n) → ℕ → Bool), Function.Injective a → f ∘ a ∉ R n
TauCeti.mycielski.doc:
**Mycielski's theorem.** Let `X` be a nonempty perfect completely metrizable space, for
example a nonempty perfect Polish space, and let `R n` be a meagre set of `k n`-tuples of points
of `X` for each `n`. There is a continuous injection `f` of Cantor space into `X` such that for
every `n` and every injective tuple `a` of `k n` points of Cantor space, `f ∘ a ∉ R n`.

TauCeti.mvfderiv_det_apply.signature:
TauCeti.mvfderiv_det_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
  [CompleteSpace 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_3}
  [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H} {M : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace H M] {n : Type u_5} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : M → Matrix n n 𝕜} {x : M}
  (hA : ∀ (i j : n), (MDiffAt fun y => A y i j) x) (hdet : IsUnit (A x).det)
  (v : TangentSpace I x) :
  ((d% fun y => (A y).det) x) v =
    (A x).det * ((A x)⁻¹ * Matrix.of fun i j => ((d% fun y => A y i j) x) v).trace
TauCeti.mvfderiv_det_apply.doc:
**Jacobi's formula on a manifold.** If the entries of a matrix-valued function `A` are
differentiable at `x` and `A x` has invertible determinant, then along a tangent vector `v` the
derivative of `det A` is `det (A x) * trace ((A x)⁻¹ * dA (v))`, where `dA (v)` is the matrix of
the derivatives of the entries of `A` along `v`.

TauCeti.multiplicity_differentIdeal_eq_r.signature:
TauCeti.multiplicity_differentIdeal_eq_ramificationIdx_sub_one_iff.{u_1, u_2} (A : Type u_1)
  {B : Type u_2} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsDedekindDomain A] [IsDedekindDomain B]
  [Module.IsTorsionFree A B] [Module.Finite A B]
  [Algebra.IsSeparable (FractionRing A) (FractionRing B)] {p : Ideal A} [p.IsMaximal] (hp : p ≠ ⊥)
  (P : Ideal B) [P.IsMaximal] [P.LiesOver p] :
  multiplicity P (differentIdeal A B) = P.ramificationIdx A - 1 ↔
    Algebra.IsSeparable (A ⧸ p) (B ⧸ P) ∧ ↑(P.ramificationIdx A) ≠ 0
TauCeti.multiplicity_differentIdeal_eq_r.doc:
**Dedekind's different theorem, the tame case, as an exponent**: the multiplicity of `P` in
the different ideal is exactly `e(P ∣ p) - 1` when the residue extension is separable and
`e(P ∣ p)` is nonzero in the residue field `A ⧸ p`.

TauCeti.mul_preprojectiveHilbertSeries_e.signature:
TauCeti.mul_preprojectiveHilbertSeries_eq_one_of_two_mul_le_sum.{u, v, w, u_1} (k : Type w)
  {Q : Type u} [Field k] [Quiver Q] [Fintype Q] [(i j : Q) → Fintype (i ⟶ j)] [DecidableEq Q]
  {S : Type u_1} [CommRing S] [LinearOrder S] [IsStrictOrderedRing S] {δ : Q → S}
  (hδ : ∀ (i : Q), 0 < δ i)
  (hδle : ∀ (i : Q), 2 * δ i ≤ ∑ j, ↑(Fintype.card (i ⟶ j) + Fintype.card (j ⟶ i)) * δ j) :
  ((1 + PowerSeries.X ^ 2) • 1 -
        PowerSeries.X •
          Matrix.of fun v w =>
            ↑(Fintype.card (Quiver.Symmetrify.of.obj w ⟶ Quiver.Symmetrify.of.obj v))) *
      TauCeti.preprojectiveHilbertSeries k Q =
    1
TauCeti.mul_preprojectiveHilbertSeries_e.doc:
**The Hilbert series identity for a quiver with a superadditive weight.** Let `δ` be a weight
on the vertices of a finite quiver `Q` over a strictly ordered commutative ring, positive with

```text
2 δ_i ≤ ∑_j (#(i ⟶ j) + #(j ⟶ i)) δ_j
```

at every vertex. No hypothesis on the sinks of `Q` is needed: the matrix Hilbert series `H` of `Π`
satisfies `((1 + X²) I - X A) H = I` for `A_{v,w} = #(w ⟶ v)` the arrow-count matrix of the doubled
quiver.

TauCeti.mul_preprojectiveHilbertSeries_e.signature:
TauCeti.mul_preprojectiveHilbertSeries_eq_one.{u, v, w} (k : Type w) {Q : Type u} [Field k]
  [Quiver Q] [Fintype Q] [(i j : Q) → Fintype (i ⟶ j)] (hQ : ∀ (u : Q), ∃ w, Nonempty (u ⟶ w))
  [DecidableEq Q] :
  ((1 + PowerSeries.X ^ 2) • 1 -
        PowerSeries.X •
          Matrix.of fun v w =>
            ↑(Fintype.card (Quiver.Symmetrify.of.obj w ⟶ Quiver.Symmetrify.of.obj v))) *
      TauCeti.preprojectiveHilbertSeries k Q =
    1
TauCeti.mul_preprojectiveHilbertSeries_e.doc:
**The Hilbert series identity for a quiver without sinks.** If every vertex of `Q` is the tail
of an arrow and `A_{v,w} = #(w ⟶ v)` is the arrow-count matrix of the doubled quiver, then
`((1 + X²) I - X A) H = I` for the matrix Hilbert series `H` of `Π`.

TauCeti.mul_measure_lt_maximalFunction_l.signature:
TauCeti.mul_measure_lt_maximalFunction_le.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [ENorm F] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] (f : E → F)
  (t : ENNReal) :
  t * μ {x | t < TauCeti.maximalFunction μ f x} ≤ 4 ^ Module.finrank ℝ E * ∫⁻ (x : E), ‖f x‖ₑ ∂μ
TauCeti.mul_measure_lt_maximalFunction_l.doc:
**The Hardy–Littlewood maximal inequality**, the weak-type `(1,1)` bound: the measure of the
set where the maximal function exceeds `t`, multiplied by `t`, is at most `4 ^ n` times the `L¹`
norm of `f`, with `n` the dimension of the space.

No integrability hypothesis is needed: the bound is vacuous when `∫⁻ x, ‖f x‖ₑ ∂μ = ∞`.

TauCeti.mul_measure_le_of_forall_exists_.signature:
TauCeti.mul_measure_le_of_forall_exists_ball.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E} [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] {t : ENNReal} {S : Set E} {R : ℝ}
  {g : E → ENNReal}
  (hS :
    ∀ x ∈ S, ∃ r ∈ Set.Ioc 0 R, t * μ (Metric.ball x r) ≤ ∫⁻ (y : E) in Metric.ball x r, g y ∂μ) :
  t * μ S ≤ 4 ^ Module.finrank ℝ E * ∫⁻ (y : E), g y ∂μ
TauCeti.mul_measure_le_of_forall_exists_.doc:
**The Vitali covering estimate.** If every point of `S` is the centre of a ball of radius at
most `R` on which `∫⁻ g` is at least `t` times the measure of the ball, then
`t * μ S ≤ 4 ^ n * ∫⁻ g`, with `n` the dimension of the space.

The factor `4 ^ n` is the cost of passing from a pairwise disjoint subfamily of those balls to its
fourfold enlargement, which still covers `S`.

TauCeti.mul_integral_norm_sq_eq_four_pi_.signature:
TauCeti.mul_integral_norm_sq_eq_four_pi_mul_abs_signedArea_iff {a b : ℝ} {γ γ' : ℝ → ℂ}
  (hab : a < b) (hγ : AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval γ a b)
  (hγ' : ∀ᵐ (t : ℝ), t ∈ Set.uIoc a b → HasDerivAt γ (γ' t) t) (hγab : γ a = γ b)
  (hL2 : MeasureTheory.MemLp γ' 2 (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ioc a b))) :
  (b - a) * ∫ (t : ℝ) in a..b, ‖γ' t‖ ^ 2 = 4 * Real.pi * |TauCeti.signedArea γ a b| ↔
    ∃ c w,
      (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc a b, γ t = c + w * Complex.exp (2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I * ↑t / (↑b - ↑a))) ∨
        ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc a b, γ t = c + w * Complex.exp (-(2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I * ↑t / (↑b - ↑a)))
TauCeti.mul_integral_norm_sq_eq_four_pi_.doc:
**Equality in the area–energy inequality.** For an absolutely continuous closed plane curve
with square-integrable derivative, `(b - a) ∫ₐᵇ ‖γ'‖² = 4π |signedArea γ a b|` exactly when `γ`
is constant or traverses a circle once at constant angular speed, in either orientation.

TauCeti.mul_exp_integral_le_of_mul_le_de.signature:
TauCeti.mul_exp_integral_le_of_mul_le_deriv {g k : ℝ → ℝ} {s t : ℝ} (hst : s ≤ t)
  (hg : MonotoneOn g (Set.Icc s t)) (hgs : 0 ≤ g s)
  (hk : IntervalIntegrable k MeasureTheory.volume s t)
  (h : ∀ᵐ (σ : ℝ), σ ∈ Set.Ioo s t → k σ * g σ ≤ deriv g σ) :
  g s * Real.exp (∫ (σ : ℝ) in s..t, k σ) ≤ g t
TauCeti.mul_exp_integral_le_of_mul_le_de.doc:
**Grönwall's inequality for monotone functions, almost-everywhere form.** Let `g` be monotone
on `[s, t]` with `g s ≥ 0`. If `k g ≤ g'` at almost every point of `(s, t)`, for an interval
integrable `k`, then `g s · exp (∫ₛᵗ k) ≤ g t`. No continuity of `g` is needed.

TauCeti.mul_burkholderPhi_le.signature:
TauCeti.mul_burkholderPhi_le {p : ℝ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) {x y : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hy : 0 ≤ y) :

TauCeti.mul_burkholderPhi_le.doc:
**The scalar Bellman majorization estimate.** For `2 ≤ p` and `x, y ≥ 0`,
`((p - 1) ^ (p - 1) / p ^ (p - 2)) Φ_p(x, y) ≤ (p - 1) ^ p x ^ p - y ^ p`.

TauCeti.mulVec_surjective_jacobiMatrixAt.signature:
TauCeti.mulVec_surjective_jacobiMatrixAt_iff_exists_eval_pderiv_ne_zero.{u_2, u_3, u_4}
  {σ : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_3} {K : Type u_4} [Field K] [Unique ι] [Fintype σ]

equation has full rank at a point exactly when some partial derivative of the equation is nonzero
there.

an open set of `ℂ` and conservative there (its integrals over the boundaries of rectangles in the

set `Ω ⊆ ℂ` into a proper complex normed space `E` has a subsequence converging locally uniformly

result applies to scalar-valued holomorphic maps.

TauCeti.monodromy_theorem_of_free_homotopy.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]

TauCeti.monodromy_theorem_of_free_homoto.doc:
**The monodromy theorem for a free homotopy of paths.** Let `h` be a continuous map of the
square, read as a family of paths `h (t, ·)` whose *endpoints are allowed to move*, and suppose a
family of germs continues along each of those paths. If the initial germs — the germ of `f t 0` at
`h (t, 0)` — themselves continue along the initial edge `t ↦ h (t, 0)`, then the terminal germs
continue along the terminal edge `t ↦ h (t, 1)`.

This is the monodromy theorem in the form the deck-group and covering-space consumers need: the
continuation of a germ across a homotopy is itself a continuation, along the path the far endpoint
sweeps out. Nothing is assumed rel endpoints; `TauCeti.monodromy_theorem` is the special case in
which both edges are constant, where "continues along a constant path" degenerates to "carries one
germ throughout".

  f t 1 =ᶠ[nhds z₁] f 0 1
TauCeti.monodromy_theorem.doc:
**The monodromy theorem.** Let `h` be a homotopy rel endpoints between two paths from `z₀` to
`z₁` in `ℂ`, and suppose a germ at `z₀` continues along every path `h (t, ·)` of the homotopy,
all the continuations starting from that one germ. Then they all end at one and the same germ at
`z₁`: the result of the continuation depends on the path only through its homotopy class.

This is the rel-endpoints case of `TauCeti.monodromy_theorem_of_free_homotopy`, whose homotopy is
allowed to move the endpoints and whose conclusion is correspondingly a continuation along the
path the terminal point sweeps out rather than a single germ at `z₁`.

finite-dimensional real normed space `E` of dimension `n`, a compactly supported smooth `n`-form

finite-dimensional real normed space `E` of dimension `n`, a compactly supported smooth `n`-form is
the exterior derivative of a compactly supported form if and only if its integral vanishes.

lies in the old subspace. It is a sum, over the primes `p ∣ N`, of forms of the same nebentypus
supported on the multiples of `p`, and each of those is old.

convex hull of the permutation orbit of `w` exactly when `x` is majorized by `w`: every prefix
sum of `x` is at most the corresponding prefix sum of `w`, and the total sums agree.

TauCeti.mem_convexHull_range_comp_perm_i.doc:
**Rado's theorem.** For antitone `w`, a tuple `x` lies in the convex hull of the permutation
orbit of `w` exactly when `x` is majorized by `w`: the prefix sums of the decreasing
rearrangement of `x` are at most those of `w`, and the total sums agree.

TauCeti.mem_connectedComponentIn_of_hasC.signature:
TauCeti.mem_connectedComponentIn_of_hasContinuousLogOn {K : Set ℂ} {a b : ℂ} (hK : IsClosed K)

  b ∈ connectedComponentIn Kᶜ a
TauCeti.mem_connectedComponentIn_of_hasC.doc:
**Borsuk's separation theorem.** If the Borsuk map `z ↦ (z - a) / (z - b)` of two points
outside a bounded closed set `K ⊆ ℂ` has a continuous logarithm on `K`, then `K` does not separate
them: `b` lies in the connected component of `a` in `Kᶜ`.

That the two points lie outside `K` is not assumed: the Borsuk map vanishes at `a` and, by the
division convention, at `b` as well, so a logarithm on `K` already excludes both from `K`.

This is the converse of `TauCeti.hasContinuousLogOn_sub_div_sub`, and the direction that fails
without boundedness — the real axis separates `i` from `-i` while carrying a logarithm of their
Borsuk map.

`p = n / (n - 1)`. Every null-measurable set `s` of finite measure satisfies
`μ(s) ^ (1/p) ≤ C P(s; E)`, where `1/p = 1 - 1/n`, `P(s; E)` is the perimeter of `s` in the whole
space, finite or infinite, and `C` is the constant `MeasureTheory.eLpNormLESNormFDerivOneConst μ p`
of the Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev inequality.

**The dyadic John–Nirenberg inequality** for any additive Haar measure: the superlevel
set at `2ⁿ⁺¹ N M` has measure at most `2⁻ᴺ` times the cube measure.

of a matrix-valued function `S` from a fixed matrix `A` is integrable with integral at most `v`,
then the measure of the event where some entry deviates by more than `η > 0` is at most
`ENNReal.ofReal (card m * card n * v / η²)`.

TauCeti.measure_essentialBoundary.doc: **Lebesgue's density theorem.** The essential boundary of a null-measurable set is null.

normalized on the integer box, the Eisenstein region has volume `q ^ (-n) (1 - q⁻¹)` for
`0 < n`, where `q = Nat.card 𝓀[K]`.

interval over which the imaginary part of the represented function is continuous up to the real
axis and vanishes there.  Continuity is asked for on the closed rectangle of any positive height

TauCeti.measurableSet_graph_iff_measurab.doc:
**The Borel graph theorem.** A map between standard Borel spaces is measurable if and only if
its graph is measurable.

**The Borel graph theorem for partial maps.** The graph of `f` on `s`, for standard Borel
spaces `X` and `Y`, is measurable if and only if `s` is measurable and `f` is measurable on
`s`.

TauCeti.meas_gt_le_div_sq_of_integral_sq.signature:

**The uncentered Chebyshev inequality.** If `Y²` is integrable with `∫ Y² ≤ v` and `0 < η`,
then the set where `Y` exceeds `η` has measure at most `v / η²`.

TauCeti.meas_ge_le_integral_norm_sq_div_.doc:
**Chebyshev's inequality for the second moment.** For any measure, if `‖Y‖²` is integrable
and `0 < c`, the set where `‖Y‖` is at least `c` has measure at most `(∫ ‖Y‖²) / c²`. Unlike
`ProbabilityTheory.meas_ge_le_variance_div_sq`, `Y` is not centered at its mean.

**Riemann's removable singularity theorem on complex curves.** A map between complex curves
that is continuous at `x` and holomorphic at every point of a punctured neighbourhood of `x` is
holomorphic at `x`. This is Mathlib's
`Complex.differentiableOn_compl_singleton_and_continuousAt_iff` read in charts.

TauCeti.mayerVietorisShortComplex_shortE.signature:

**The Mayer–Vietoris short exact sequence of de Rham complexes.** On a Hausdorff σ-compact
manifold modelled on a finite-dimensional space, the Mayer–Vietoris short complex of two open
subsets is short exact.

**The Galois group of the maximal unramified extension is the profinite integers.** This
continuous multiplicative equivalence sends arithmetic Frobenius to `zHat.gen`.

**Nakayama's lemma in coordinates.** Elements of `𝔪` whose gradients span `κⁿ` generate
`𝔪`.

relations, evaluating a reduced word depends only on the element it represents. No square
relations are required of the generators.

TauCeti.map_add_eq_add_hessianAverage.doc:
**Taylor's formula to second order**, with the remainder written as the averaged Hessian
evaluated twice on the increment.

TauCeti.manifoldMorseIndex_norm_sq_sub_t.doc:
**Milnor's index bound on a smooth affine complete intersection.** On the common zero set in
`ℂ^σ` of a polynomial family with surjective Jacobian at every common zero, every critical point of
the Euclidean squared distance from a point `a` has real Morse index at most the complex dimension
`|σ| - |ι|` of the zero set.

TauCeti.mahlerMeasure_eq_one_iff.signature:
TauCeti.mahlerMeasure_eq_one_iff.{u_1} {F : Type u_1} [Field F] [CharZero F] {x : F}

TauCeti.mahlerMeasure_eq_one_iff.doc:
**Kronecker's theorem.** An algebraic element has Mahler measure `1` exactly when it is zero
or a root of unity.

TauCeti.mahlerMeasure.signature: TauCeti.mahlerMeasure.{u_1} {F : Type u_1} [Field F] [CharZero F] (x : F) : ℝ
TauCeti.mahlerMeasure.doc:
The *Mahler measure* `M(x)` of `x`: the Mahler measure of its primitive minimal polynomial
`F_x`, mapped to `ℂ[X]`. For algebraic `x` this is `a₀ ∏ max(1, |x⁽ⁱ⁾|)` over the complex
conjugates of `x` (`mahlerMeasure_eq_leadingCoeff_mul_prod`); for transcendental `x` it is `1`.

TauCeti.macbeathHom_injective_of_locally.signature:
TauCeti.macbeathHom_injective_of_locallyFinite.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {X : Type u_2} [Group G]

  [LocallyPathConnectedSpace X] [SimplyConnectedSpace X] (hPc : IsClosed P) (hP : IsConnected P)

TauCeti.macbeathHom_injective_of_locally.doc:
**Macbeath's theorem for a tile.** If the translates of a closed connected set `P` are
locally finite and cover a simply connected, locally path-connected pseudometric space on which `G`
acts isometrically, then every relation among the Macbeath generators of `P` is a consequence of
the Macbeath relations of `P`.

TauCeti.macbeathEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.macbeathEquiv.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {X : Type u_2} [Group G] [MulAction G X] {U : Set X}

TauCeti.macbeathEquiv.doc:
**Macbeath's theorem.** If the translates of a path-connected open set `U` cover a simply
connected space `X`, then `G` is presented by the Macbeath generators and relations of `U`.

TauCeti.lsCategoryCount_univ_le_totalCri.doc:
**The Lusternik–Schnirelmann theorem.** On a compact boundaryless manifold `M`, the
Lusternik–Schnirelmann count of `M` is at most the number of critical points of any smooth
function on `M`. The critical points may be degenerate; if there are infinitely many, their count
is `⊤`.

TauCeti.lsCategoryCount_univ_le_minCriti.signature:
TauCeti.lsCategoryCount_univ_le_minCriticalCount.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {H : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace H]
  {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} {M : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
  [I.Boundaryless] [CompactSpace M] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [T2Space M] [IsManifold I (↑⊤) M] :
  TauCeti.lsCategoryCount M Set.univ ≤ TauCeti.minCriticalCount I M
TauCeti.lsCategoryCount_univ_le_minCriti.doc:
**The Lusternik–Schnirelmann lower bound for `c(M)`.** On a compact boundaryless manifold,
every smooth function has at least as many critical points as the Lusternik–Schnirelmann count of
`M`, so `c(M)` is bounded below by that count.

TauCeti.lsCategoryCount_univ_le_encard_c.doc:
**The Lusternik–Schnirelmann bound on a compact open part.** If `C` is a compact open subset
of a boundaryless manifold `M`, for instance a connected component of a compact manifold, then the
Lusternik–Schnirelmann count of `C`, as a space in its own right, is at most the number of critical
points in `C` of a function `f` that is smooth on `C`. The critical points may be degenerate; if
there are infinitely many in `C`, their count is `⊤`.

Summed over the finitely many components of a compact manifold `M`, using
`TauCeti.lsCategoryCount_univ_eq_finsum_connectedComponents` and
`TauCeti.totalCriticalCount_eq_finsum_connectedComponents`, these bounds recover
`TauCeti.lsCategoryCount_univ_le_totalCriticalCount`.

TauCeti.lsCategoryCount_sublevel_le_enca.signature:
TauCeti.lsCategoryCount_sublevel_le_encard.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] {H : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} {M : Type u_3}
  [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] {f : M → ℝ} [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [T2Space M]
  [I.Boundaryless] [IsManifold I (↑⊤) M] (hf : ContMDiff I (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ) (↑⊤) f)
  {t b : ℝ} (htb : t < b) (hb : IsCompact {x | f x ≤ b})
  (hfin : (TauCeti.criticalPoints I f ∩ {x | f x ≤ b}).Finite) :
  TauCeti.lsCategoryCount M {x | f x ≤ t} ≤ (TauCeti.criticalPoints I f ∩ {x | f x ≤ t}).encard
TauCeti.lsCategoryCount_sublevel_le_enca.doc:
**The Lusternik–Schnirelmann bound on sublevels.** Let `f` be smooth and `t < b`, and suppose
that the sublevel `{f ≤ b}` is compact and contains only finitely many critical points of `f`. Then
the Lusternik–Schnirelmann count of `{f ≤ t}` is at most the number of critical points of `f` in
`{f ≤ t}`. The critical points may be degenerate.

TauCeti.loopChainAlgebra.signature:
TauCeti.loopChainAlgebra.{u_1, u_2} (B : Type u_1) [TopologicalSpace B] (b : B) (R : Type u_2)
  [CommRing R] : Type (max u_2 u_1)
TauCeti.loopChainAlgebra.doc:
The **chain algebra of the Moore loop space**: `C_*(Ω_b B; R)`, the normalized cubical chains
of the Moore loops at `b`, with the Pontryagin product.

TauCeti.log_normalizedValuationWithZero_.signature:
TauCeti.log_normalizedValuationWithZero_zpow_sub_one_le.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  [ValuativeRel K] [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] {x : Kˣ} {M i : ℕ}
  (hi0 : i ≠ 0) (hM : x ^ M ∈ TauCeti.unitFiltration K i) (hM1 : x ^ M ≠ 1) {b : ℤ}
  (hb : ↑b.natAbs ≠ 0)
  (hi :
    ∀ (ℓ : ℕ),
      Nat.Prime ℓ →
        ∀ (hℓK : ↑ℓ ≠ 0), ℓ ∣ b.natAbs → TauCeti.natCastValuation K ℓ hℓK < (ℓ - 1) * i) :

    ((TauCeti.normalizedValuationWithZero K) (↑x ^ M - 1)).log +
      ↑(TauCeti.natCastValuation K b.natAbs hb)
TauCeti.log_normalizedValuationWithZero_.doc:
**The one-factor estimate, explicit form.** Let `x ∈ Kˣ` have a power `x ^ M ≠ 1` in a
positive-depth step `U(K,i)`, and let `b` be an integer with `(|b| : K) ≠ 0` such that
`v_K(ℓ) < (ℓ - 1) * i` for every prime `ℓ ∣ b`. Then

`v_K(x ^ b - 1) ≤ v_K(x ^ M - 1) + v_K(|b|)`.

TauCeti.lintegral_rpow_maximalFunction_l.signature:
TauCeti.lintegral_rpow_maximalFunction_le.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [ENorm F] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] {f : E → F}
  (hf : AEMeasurable (fun x => ‖f x‖ₑ) μ) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 < p) :
  ∫⁻ (x : E), TauCeti.maximalFunction μ f x ^ p ∂μ ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (2 * p * 2 ^ (p - 1) / (p - 1)) * 4 ^ Module.finrank ℝ E *
      ∫⁻ (x : E), ‖f x‖ₑ ^ p ∂μ
TauCeti.lintegral_rpow_maximalFunction_l.doc:
**The Hardy–Littlewood maximal inequality**, the strong-type `(p, p)` bound for `1 < p < ∞`,
as an inequality between the integrals `∫⁻ ‖·‖ₑ ^ p`:

`∫⁻ (M f) ^ p ∂μ ≤ (2 * p * 2 ^ (p - 1) / (p - 1)) * 4 ^ n * ∫⁻ ‖f‖ₑ ^ p ∂μ`.

The constant degenerates as `p → 1`, as it must in positive dimension, where `M` is not bounded on
`L¹`.

TauCeti.lintegral_rpow_lintegral_mul_le_.doc:
**Young's inequality for integral kernels.** Let `1 ≤ p ≤ q` and let `r` be the exponent with
`1/p + 1/r = 1 + 1/q`. If the `r`-th powers of the kernel `k` have row integrals
`∫⁻ y, k x y ^ r ∂ν` at most `A` for almost every `x` and column integrals `∫⁻ x, k x y ^ r ∂μ`
at most `B` for almost every `y`, then the integral operator with kernel `k` satisfies
`∫⁻ x, (∫⁻ y, k x y * g y ∂ν) ^ q ∂μ ≤ A ^ (q (1 - 1/p)) * B * (∫⁻ y, g y ^ p ∂ν) ^ (q / p)`.

The kernel need only be a.e. measurable: the proof applies the measurable case to a measurable
modification of `k`, which agrees with `k` on almost every row and on almost every column.
For `p = q` this is Schur's test, `TauCeti.lintegral_rpow_lintegral_mul_le`.

TauCeti.lintegral_mul_le_of_inv_add_inv_.signature:
TauCeti.lintegral_mul_le_of_inv_add_inv_eq.{u_1} {β : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace β]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure β} {k g : β → ENNReal} (hk : AEMeasurable k ν) (hg : AEMeasurable g ν)
  {p q r : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (hpq : p ≤ q) (hr : p⁻¹ + r⁻¹ = 1 + q⁻¹) :
  ∫⁻ (y : β), k y * g y ∂ν ≤
    (∫⁻ (y : β), k y ^ r * g y ^ p ∂ν) ^ q⁻¹ * (∫⁻ (y : β), k y ^ r ∂ν) ^ (1 - p⁻¹) *
      (∫⁻ (y : β), g y ^ p ∂ν) ^ (p⁻¹ - q⁻¹)
TauCeti.lintegral_mul_le_of_inv_add_inv_.doc:
**Hölder's inequality for Young's exponents.** Let `1 ≤ p ≤ q` and let `r` be the exponent with
`1/p + 1/r = 1 + 1/q`. Then
`∫⁻ k g ≤ (∫⁻ k ^ r g ^ p) ^ (1/q) (∫⁻ k ^ r) ^ (1 - 1/p) (∫⁻ g ^ p) ^ (1/p - 1/q)`.

This is Hölder's inequality with the three exponents `1/q`, `1 - 1/p` and `1/p - 1/q`, which add
up to `1`, applied to the factorization
`k g = (k ^ r g ^ p) ^ (1/q) (k ^ r) ^ (1 - 1/p) (g ^ p) ^ (1/p - 1/q)`.

TauCeti.lintegral_mul_le_lintegral_schwa.doc:
**Hardy--Littlewood rearrangement inequality.** For two nonnegative a.e.-measurable
functions on a finite-dimensional real normed space, Schwarz rearrangement can only increase the
integral of their product. The statement includes infinite integrals and dimension zero.

TauCeti.lintegral_enorm_sub_setAverage_r.signature:
TauCeti.lintegral_enorm_sub_setAverage_rpow_le_of_convex.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  [BorelSpace E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [CompleteSpace F]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E} [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] {u : E → F} {Ω S : Set E} (hΩ : IsOpen Ω)
  (hΩc : Convex ℝ Ω) (hb : Bornology.IsBounded Ω) (hu : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 u Ω) (hS : S ⊆ Ω)
  (hS₀ : μ S ≠ 0) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) :
  ∫⁻ (x : E) in Ω, ‖u x - ⨍ (y : E) in S, u y ∂μ‖ₑ ^ p ∂μ ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal
        ((μ.real (Metric.ball 0 1) * Metric.diam Ω ^ (Module.finrank ℝ E + 1) / μ.real S) ^ p) *
      ∫⁻ (y : E) in Ω, ‖fderiv ℝ u y‖ₑ ^ p ∂μ
TauCeti.lintegral_enorm_sub_setAverage_r.doc:
**The Poincaré–Wirtinger inequality on a convex domain**, in `∫⁻` form. If `u` is `C¹` on a
bounded convex open set `Ω` and `S ⊆ Ω` has positive measure, then for `1 ≤ p` the `p`-th power
of the deviation of `u` from its mean over `S` has integral over `Ω` at most `C ^ p` times the
integral of `‖Du‖ ^ p` over `Ω`, where `C = μ(B(0, 1)) * (diam Ω) ^ (n + 1) / μ(S)` and `n` is
the dimension of the space.

TauCeti.lintegral_enorm_rpow_le_of_suppo.signature:
TauCeti.lintegral_enorm_rpow_le_of_support_subset_Icc.{u_1} {F : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup F]
  {g : ℝ → F} {a b : ℝ} [NormedSpace ℝ F] {g' : ℝ → F} (hg : ∀ (t : ℝ), HasDerivAt g (g' t) t)
  (hg' : Continuous g') (hsupp : Function.support g ⊆ Set.Icc a b) {r : ℝ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) :
  ∫⁻ (t : ℝ), ‖g t‖ₑ ^ r ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((b - a) ^ r) * ∫⁻ (t : ℝ), ‖g' t‖ₑ ^ r
TauCeti.lintegral_enorm_rpow_le_of_suppo.doc:
**The one-dimensional Poincaré inequality**, in the `∫⁻` form the Fubini argument below
consumes: a `C¹` function on `ℝ` that vanishes outside `Set.Icc a b` satisfies
`∫ ‖g‖^r ≤ (b - a)^r ∫ ‖g'‖^r` for every `1 ≤ r`. The endpoints may be in either
order: an empty or degenerate interval carries only the zero function.

The two ingredients are the fundamental theorem of calculus, which bounds `‖g t‖` by the total
variation `∫ ‖g'‖` over the interval, and the nesting `L^r ⊆ L^1` of the `Lᵖ` scale on the
finite measure space `Set.Ioc a b`, which converts that `L^1` bound into an `L^r` one at the cost
of the factor `(b - a)^{r-1}`.

`F` need not be complete.

TauCeti.lintegral_enorm_rpow_le_lintegra.signature:
TauCeti.lintegral_enorm_rpow_le_lintegral_sharpMaximalFunction_rpow.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1}
  [Fintype ι] {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [CompleteSpace F] [Nonempty ι]
  {f : (ι → ℝ) → F} (hf : MeasureTheory.Integrable f MeasureTheory.volume) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 < p) :
  ∫⁻ (x : ι → ℝ), ‖f x‖ₑ ^ p ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (2 ^ (p + 1) * 2 ^ ((p + 2 * ↑(Fintype.card ι) + 2) * p)) *
      ∫⁻ (x : ι → ℝ), TauCeti.sharpMaximalFunction MeasureTheory.volume f x ^ p
TauCeti.lintegral_enorm_rpow_le_lintegra.doc:
**The Fefferman–Stein inequality**, as an inequality between the integrals `∫⁻ ‖·‖ₑ ^ p`.
For `1 < p < ∞` and integrable `f` on `ℝⁿ = ι → ℝ`, `n ≥ 1`,

`∫ ‖f‖^p ≤ 2^(p + 1) 2^((p + 2n + 2) p) ∫ (f^#)^p`,

where `f^#` is the sharp maximal function for balls in the sup distance.

TauCeti.lintegral_add_mul_klDiv_eq_mul_k.doc:
**The Gibbs identity.** For probability measures `μ` and `ν`, a cost `c` finite
`μ.prod ν`-almost everywhere, and a positive temperature `ε`, every probability measure `π` on
`X × Y` satisfies `∫ c dπ + ε * klDiv π (μ ⊗ ν) = ε * klDiv π R - ε * log Z`, where
`Z = ∫ e^{-c/ε} d(μ ⊗ ν)` and `R = Z⁻¹ e^{-c/ε} (μ ⊗ ν)` is the Gibbs measure, written as the
tilted measure `(μ.prod ν).tilted fun z ↦ -((c z).toReal / ε)`. Both sides may be `∞`.

TauCeti.lintegral_Lp_lintegral_le.doc:
**Minkowski's integral inequality.** For `1 ≤ p` and a jointly a.e. measurable
`f : α → β → ℝ≥0∞`, the `Lᵖ(μ)` seminorm of `x ↦ ∫⁻ y, f x y ∂ν` is at most the integral over `ν`
of the `Lᵖ(μ)` seminorms of the functions `x ↦ f x y`:
`(∫⁻ x, (∫⁻ y, f x y ∂ν) ^ p ∂μ) ^ (1 / p) ≤ ∫⁻ y, (∫⁻ x, f x y ^ p ∂μ) ^ (1 / p) ∂ν`.

TauCeti.linearIndependent_exp.signature:
TauCeti.linearIndependent_exp.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} (u : ι → ↥(integralClosure ℚ ℂ))
  (u_inj : Function.Injective u) :
  LinearIndependent ↥(integralClosure ℚ ℂ) fun i => Complex.exp ↑(u i)
TauCeti.linearIndependent_exp.doc:
**The Lindemann–Weierstrass theorem**, in Baker's form. The exponentials of pairwise distinct
algebraic numbers are linearly independent over the field `integralClosure ℚ ℂ` of algebraic
numbers.

TauCeti.lieDerivForm_eq_curryLeft_extDer.doc:
**Cartan's formula** `L_V ω = ι_V dω + d (ι_V ω)`, where the interior product `ι_V` inserts
`V` into the first slot.

TauCeti.lieDerivFormWithin_eq_curryLeft_.signature:
TauCeti.lieDerivFormWithin_eq_curryLeft_extDerivWithin_add.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1}

TauCeti.lieDerivFormWithin_eq_curryLeft_.doc:
**Cartan's formula** within a set, `L_V ω = ι_V dω + d (ι_V ω)`, where the interior product
`ι_V` inserts `V` into the first slot.

TauCeti.lieDerivEndomorphism_apply_sub_a.signature:
TauCeti.lieDerivEndomorphism_apply_sub_apply.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2}
  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {A : E → E →L[𝕜] E} {x : E}
  {X : E → E} (hA : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 A x) (hX : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 X x)
  (hsq : ∀ (u : E), (A x) ((A x) u) = -u) (w : E) :
  (TauCeti.lieDerivEndomorphism (fun y => (A y) (X y)) A x) w -
      (A x) ((TauCeti.lieDerivEndomorphism X A x) w) =
    ((fderiv 𝕜 A x) ((A x) (X x))) w - ((fderiv 𝕜 A x) ((A x) w)) (X x) +

      (A x) (((fderiv 𝕜 A x) (X x)) w)
TauCeti.lieDerivEndomorphism_apply_sub_a.doc:
**Nijenhuis–Lie-derivative identity**: if `A x` squares to `-1`, then for every differentiable
vector field `X`, the derivative `DX(x)` cancels out of `(L_{A X} A)(x) w - A x ((L_X A)(x) w)`,
leaving the pointwise Nijenhuis expression of `A` on `(X x, w)`.

TauCeti.leviForm.signature:
TauCeti.leviForm.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℂ V] (f : V → ℝ) (x : V) :
  V →ₗ⋆[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ
TauCeti.leviForm.doc:
The **Levi form** of a real function `f` at `x`: the sesquilinear form
`(D²f(x)(v, w) + D²f(x)(I • v, I • w) + I * (D²f(x)(I • v, w) - D²f(x)(v, I • w))) / 4`,
conjugate-linear in `v` and complex-linear in `w`. Its matrix entries in holomorphic coordinates
are the Wirtinger derivatives, with the arguments reversed: for `C²` `f` and coordinate vectors
`e_j`, `leviForm f x (e_k) (e_j) = ∂²f / ∂z_j ∂(conj z_k)`.

TauCeti.length_quotient_lsmul_le_finrank.signature:
TauCeti.length_quotient_lsmul_le_finrank_mul_ord.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A]
  [IsDomain A] {K : Type u_2} [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] {V : Type u_3}
  [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module K V] [_root_.Module A V] [IsScalarTower A K V]
  [IsNoetherianRing A] [Ring.KrullDimLE 1 A] [Module.Finite K V] (M : Submodule A V) (a : A)
  (ha : a ≠ 0) :
  Module.length A (↥M ⧸ ((LinearMap.lsmul A ↥M) a).range) ≤ ↑(Module.finrank K V) * Ring.ord A a
TauCeti.length_quotient_lsmul_le_finrank.doc:
**Krull–Akizuki's length bound.** For any `A`-submodule `M` of a finite-dimensional
`K`-vector space `V` — finitely generated or not — and any nonzero `a : A`,
`length (M ⧸ aM) ≤ dim_K V * ord_A a`.

TauCeti.leechLattice.doc:
**The Leech lattice**, glued from the Golay Construction B lattice along the order-two
subgroup generated by the odd shift `(-3/2, 1/2, …, 1/2)`. Its carrier is the union of the
Construction B lattice and its translate by the shift, by `mem_leechLattice_carrier_iff`.

TauCeti.le_mul_exp_of_le_add_mul_integra.signature:
TauCeti.le_mul_exp_of_le_add_mul_integral {φ : ℝ → ℝ} {a b c K : ℝ}
  (hφ : ContinuousOn φ (Set.Icc a b)) (hK : 0 ≤ K)
  (h : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc a b, φ t ≤ c + K * ∫ (s : ℝ) in a..t, φ s) (t : ℝ) :
  t ∈ Set.Icc a b → φ t ≤ c * Real.exp (K * (t - a))
TauCeti.le_mul_exp_of_le_add_mul_integra.doc:
**Grönwall's inequality, integral form.** If `φ` is continuous on `[a, b]`, `0 ≤ K` and
`φ t ≤ c + K ∫ₐᵗ φ` for every `t ∈ [a, b]`, then `φ t ≤ c exp (K (t - a))` on `[a, b]`.

TauCeti.le_add_fenchelConjugate.signature:
TauCeti.le_add_fenchelConjugate.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [AddCommMonoid E]

TauCeti.le_add_fenchelConjugate.doc:
**The Fenchel–Young inequality** in additive form, `⟪x, y⟫ ≤ f x + f⋆ y`, valid whenever
neither summand is `⊥`; the second summand is `⊥` only when `f ≡ ⊤`.

TauCeti.lcm_pow_mul_eval_hasseDeriv_mult.signature:
TauCeti.lcm_pow_mul_eval_hasseDeriv_multichoose_X_add_one_pow_mem_range_intCast (k l m : ℕ)

**Baker's denominator bound**, classical form: for every integer `x` and all `l, m`,
`lcm(1, …, k) ^ m Δ(x; k, l, m)` is an integer.

TauCeti.laplaceTransform_conv.signature:
TauCeti.laplaceTransform_conv (μ ν : MeasureTheory.Measure NNReal) [MeasureTheory.SFinite μ]

TauCeti.laplaceTransform_conv.doc:
**The Laplace transform turns convolution into multiplication.** The identity needs no
finiteness or integrability hypothesis: under the junk-value convention for non-integrable
Bochner integrals it holds for all s-finite measures and every real parameter `t`.

TauCeti.kummerIso.signature:

it), for `n` invertible in `K`. It is `TauCeti.kummerClassMap`, which is injective since the
kernel of the Kummer map is `(Kˣ)ⁿ` and surjective by Hilbert 90.

TauCeti.kummerCup_padicTwo.doc:
**The Gram formula for the Kummer cup over `ℚ₂`.** In square-class coordinates along
`-1`, `2`, `5`, the cup is `x₀ y₀ + x₁ y₂ + x₂ y₁` times the nonzero class
`(-1) ∪ (-1)`. The scalar lies in `ZMod 2`.

TauCeti.kronecker_approximation_nat.doc:
**Kronecker's approximation theorem with positive multipliers.** If `1` and the real numbers
`αᵢ` satisfy no nontrivial integer relation, that is, if they are linearly independent over `ℚ`,
then for every `θ ∈ ℝ^ι` and `ε > 0` there are infinitely many natural numbers `n`, hence
arbitrarily large positive ones, each with some `x ∈ ℤ^ι` such that `|n αᵢ - xᵢ - θᵢ| ≤ ε` for
every `i`.

TauCeti.kronecker_approximation.doc:
**Kronecker's approximation theorem.** If `1` and the real numbers `αᵢ` satisfy no
nontrivial integer relation, that is, if they are linearly independent over `ℚ`, then for every
`θ ∈ ℝ^ι` and `ε > 0` there are infinitely many integer pairs `(x, y)`, `x ∈ ℤ^ι`, `y ∈ ℤ`, with
`|y αᵢ - xᵢ - θᵢ| ≤ ε` for every `i`.

TauCeti.krausLocalCondition_iff_exists_i.signature:
TauCeti.krausLocalCondition_iff_exists_integralModel.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R]
  {K : Type u_2} [Field K] [Algebra R K] {c₄ c₆ : K} [Invertible 2] [Invertible 3] [IsLocalRing R] :
  TauCeti.KrausLocalCondition R c₄ c₆ ↔
    ∃ W, WeierstrassCurve.IsIntegral R W ∧ W.c₄ = c₄ ∧ W.c₆ = c₆ ∧ W.Δ ≠ 0
TauCeti.krausLocalCondition_iff_exists_i.doc:
**Kraus's local criterion.** For a local ring `R` with an algebra map to a field `K` in which
`2` and `3` are invertible, the pair `(c₄, c₆)` is the pair of `c`-invariants of a nonsingular
Weierstrass equation with coefficients in `R` exactly when Kraus's local condition holds.

The correspondence is concrete in both directions: a witness of `KrausLocalCondition` is a change
of variables carrying `ofCInvariants c₄ c₆` to an equation with coefficients in `R`, and that
transform is the model the equivalence produces.

TauCeti.krausGlobalCondition_iff_exists_.signature:
TauCeti.krausGlobalCondition_iff_exists_integralModel.{u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_2} [Field K]
  {c₄ c₆ : K} {O : Type u_3} [CommRing O] [IsDedekindDomain O] [Algebra O K] [IsFractionRing O K]
  [Invertible 2] [Invertible 3] [Nonempty (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum O)] :
  TauCeti.KrausGlobalCondition O c₄ c₆ ↔
    ∃ W, WeierstrassCurve.IsIntegral O W ∧ W.c₄ = c₄ ∧ W.c₆ = c₆ ∧ W.Δ ≠ 0
TauCeti.krausGlobalCondition_iff_exists_.doc:
**Kraus's global criterion.** Let `O` be a Dedekind domain with fraction field `K`, in which
`2` and `3` are invertible, and assume `O` has a height-one prime, as the ring of integers of a
number field does. Then the pair `(c₄, c₆)` is the pair of `c`-invariants of a nonsingular
Weierstrass equation with coefficients in `O` exactly when Kraus's local condition holds at every
height-one prime.

The equation produced is the `(b₂/12, a₁/2, a₃/2)`-transform of `ofCInvariants c₄ c₆` for elements
`a₁`, `b₂`, `a₃` of `O` approximating the local witnesses modulo `12`. Without a height-one prime
the condition is vacuous and the statement fails, since nothing then forces `c₄³ ≠ c₆²`.

TauCeti.koszulComplex.homologyZeroEquivS.doc:
**Zeroth Koszul homology of a finite sequence**: for `x = (xᵢ)` in `R`, the Koszul complex of
the functional `v ↦ ∑ᵢ vᵢ xᵢ` has `H₀ ≃ R ⧸ (xᵢ)`.

TauCeti.koszulComplex.exactAt_of_isWeakl.doc:
**The Koszul complex of a weakly regular sequence is acyclic in positive degrees**: if
`x = (x₀, …, xₙ₋₁)` is a weakly regular sequence in `R`, then `Hₖ₊₁(K(x)) = 0` for every `k`.
With `homologyZeroEquivSpan`, the complex of finite free modules `K(x)` resolves
`R ⧸ (x₀, …, xₙ₋₁)`.

integrable against both `γ` and `π`, with the same integral. Then
`klDiv γ R = klDiv γ π + klDiv π R`.

TauCeti.ker_vanKampenWideLift.doc:
**The relations half of van Kampen's theorem for a family.** The kernel of the canonical map
from the indexed free product is exactly the normal closure of the common-intersection
relators.

TauCeti.ker_toeplitz_eq_bot_or_ker_adjoi.doc:
**Coburn's alternative.** For a nonzero essentially bounded symbol `a`, either the Toeplitz
operator `T_a` or its adjoint has trivial kernel.

TauCeti.ker_lift_eq_normalClosure_macbea.doc:
**Macbeath's theorem for a tile**, as a description of the relations: under the hypotheses
of `TauCeti.macbeathHom_injective_of_locallyFinite`, the kernel of the evaluation of words in
the Macbeath generators of `P` is the normal closure of the Macbeath relations of `P`.

TauCeti.ker_lift_eq_normalClosure_macbea.doc:
**Macbeath's theorem**, as a description of the relations: if the translates of a
path-connected open set `U` cover a simply connected space, then the kernel of the evaluation of
words in the Macbeath generators of `U` is the normal closure of the Macbeath relations.

TauCeti.kepler_sq_eq_neg_two_mul_mul_mul.signature:

TauCeti.kepler_sq_eq_neg_two_mul_mul_mul.doc:
**Vieta's formula for the Kepler product of turning points.** If `r₁ ≠ r₂` are nonzero
turning points of a Kepler orbit with `m ≠ 0`, then `ℓ² = -2 m E r₁ r₂`.

TauCeti.kepler_radialPeriod.signature:
TauCeti.kepler_radialPeriod {m κ ℓ E r₁ r₂ : ℝ} (hm : 0 < m) (hℓ : ℓ ≠ 0) (h₁ : 0 < r₁)
  (hlt : r₁ < r₂) (hr₁ : 2 * m * (E + κ / r₁) = ℓ ^ 2 / r₁ ^ 2)
  (hr₂ : 2 * m * (E + κ / r₂) = ℓ ^ 2 / r₂ ^ 2) :
  TauCeti.radialPeriod m (fun r => -κ / r) ℓ E r₁ r₂ =
    2 * Real.pi * √(m / κ) * ((r₁ + r₂) / 2) ^ (3 / 2)
TauCeti.kepler_radialPeriod.doc:
**Kepler's third law.** Between two distinct turning points `0 < r₁ < r₂` of a Kepler orbit
with `ℓ ≠ 0`, the radial period is `2π √(m / κ) a^(3/2)` for the semi-major axis
`a = (r₁ + r₂) / 2`.

TauCeti.kepler_kappa_eq.signature:
TauCeti.kepler_kappa_eq {m κ ℓ E r₁ r₂ : ℝ} (hm : m ≠ 0) (h₁ : r₁ ≠ 0) (h₂ : r₂ ≠ 0) (hne : r₁ ≠ r₂)
  (hr₁ : 2 * m * (E + κ / r₁) = ℓ ^ 2 / r₁ ^ 2) (hr₂ : 2 * m * (E + κ / r₂) = ℓ ^ 2 / r₂ ^ 2) :
  κ = -E * (r₁ + r₂)
TauCeti.kepler_kappa_eq.doc:
**Vieta's formula for the Kepler sum of turning points.** If `r₁ ≠ r₂` are nonzero turning
points of a Kepler orbit with `m ≠ 0`, then `κ = -E (r₁ + r₂)`; equivalently, for `E ≠ 0` the
semi-major axis `(r₁ + r₂) / 2` is `κ / (-2 E)`.

TauCeti.karp_theorem_at.doc:
**Karp's theorem at a common carrier.** Structures in a relational language that are both
coded into `κ` are potentially isomorphic exactly when they satisfy the same infinitary sentences
with carrier `κ`.

TauCeti.karp_theorem.doc:
**Karp's theorem.** Structures in a relational language are potentially isomorphic exactly when
they satisfy the same infinitary sentences. The converse uses the carrier `M ⊕ N`.

TauCeti.jordanHolderMultiplicity_vertexP.signature:
TauCeti.jordanHolderMultiplicity_vertexProjectiveModuleFG_eq_card_path.{v, w} (k : Type (max v w))

TauCeti.jordanHolderMultiplicity_vertexP.doc:
**The Cartan path-count formula.** The multiplicity of `Sᵢ` in the vertex projective `Pⱼ`
is the number of oriented paths from `j` to `i`. With simples in rows and projectives in columns,
these are the entries of the Cartan matrix of a finite acyclic path algebra.

TauCeti.janiszewski.signature:
TauCeti.janiszewski {a b : ℂ} {S T : Set ℂ} (hS : IsClosed S) (hT : IsClosed T)

TauCeti.janiszewski.doc:
**Janiszewski's theorem.** If two bounded closed subsets `S`, `T` of the plane have preconnected
intersection and neither separates `a` from `b`, then their union does not separate them either.

TauCeti.jacobiMatrixAt_mulVec_self.doc:
**Euler's identity** for the Jacobian matrix of a family of homogeneous polynomials: applied
to the point itself, it returns each equation's value scaled by its degree.

TauCeti.iwasawaHomeomorph_symm_toGL.doc:
**The Iwasawa decomposition of `GL n ℝ` restricts to `SL n ℝ`**: the factors in `GL n ℝ` of a
matrix of determinant one are the images under `toGL` of its factors in `SL n ℝ`.

`s ⊗ T ↦ T s` is an isomorphism of `A`-modules `S ⊗[k] (S →ₗ[A] M) ≃ₗ[A] M`, with `A` acting on
the left factor.

TauCeti.isotypicMultiplicity_tensor_eq_s.signature:
TauCeti.isotypicMultiplicity_tensor_eq_sum_weylSign_mul_formalCharacter_coeff.{u, v, w} {K : Type u}
  {L : Type v} [Field K] [CharZero K] [IsAlgClosed K] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L]
  [LieAlgebra.IsKilling K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] {H : LieSubalgebra K L} [H.IsCartanSubalgebra]
  (b : (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H).Base) {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module K M]

TauCeti.isotypicMultiplicity_tensor_eq_s.doc:
**The Brauer–Klimyk formula, expanded over the Weyl group**: for dominant integral weights
`lam` and `nu` and a finite-dimensional `L`-module `M`, the multiplicity of `L(nu)` in
`L(lam) ⊗ M` is `∑_{w ∈ W} sgn(w) · [e^{nu - w ⬝ lam}] ch M`.

TauCeti.isotypicMultiplicity_tensor_eq_c.signature:
TauCeti.isotypicMultiplicity_tensor_eq_coeff_formalCharacter_mul_weylNumerator.{u, v, w}
  {K : Type u} {L : Type v} [Field K] [CharZero K] [IsAlgClosed K] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L]
  [LieAlgebra.IsKilling K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] {H : LieSubalgebra K L} [H.IsCartanSubalgebra]
  (b : (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H).Base) {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module K M]

  [Fintype ↥(LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H).weylGroup] {lam nu : Module.Dual K ↥H}
  (hlam : TauCeti.IsDominantIntegral b lam) (hnu : TauCeti.IsDominantIntegral b nu) :
  ↑(LieModule.isotypicMultiplicity K L (TensorProduct K (TauCeti.irreducibleQuotient b lam) M)
        (TauCeti.irreducibleQuotient b nu)) =

          TauCeti.weylNumerator (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H) b lam).coeff

TauCeti.isotypicMultiplicity_tensor_eq_c.doc:
**The Brauer–Klimyk formula, in group-algebra form**: for dominant integral weights `lam` and
`nu` and a finite-dimensional `L`-module `M`, the multiplicity of `L(nu)` in `L(lam) ⊗ M` is the

This combines Weyl-alternating inversion
(`TauCeti.coeff_formalCharacter_mul_weylDenominator_eq_isotypicMultiplicity`) on `L(lam) ⊗ M`,
multiplicativity of formal characters (`TauCeti.formalCharacter_tensor`), and the Weyl character
formula `ch L(lam) · Δ = N(lam)`.

TauCeti.isotropicOscillator_sq_eq_sq_mul.signature:

TauCeti.isotropicOscillator_sq_eq_sq_mul.doc:
**Vieta's formula for the isotropic oscillator, product of squared turning points.** If
`r₁, r₂` are nonzero turning points of an isotropic oscillator with `m ≠ 0` and `r₁² ≠ r₂²`,

TauCeti.isotropicOscillator_energy_eq.doc:
**Vieta's formula for the isotropic oscillator, sum of squared turning points.** If `r₁, r₂`
are nonzero turning points of an isotropic oscillator with `m ≠ 0` and `r₁² ≠ r₂²`, then

TauCeti.isZLattice_fullUnitLattice.doc:
**Dirichlet's unit lattice theorem, with all places retained.** The logarithmic image of
the units is a full integral lattice in the sum-zero hyperplane.

TauCeti.isWeakHomotopyEquivalence_cwAppr.doc:
**CW approximation** (Hatcher, Proposition 4.13). For a path-connected space `X`, the map
`TauCeti.cwApproximationMap X x` from the CW complex `TauCeti.cwApproximation X x` to `X` is a weak
homotopy equivalence.

TauCeti.isVertexStrong_iff_exists_paths.signature:
TauCeti.isVertexStrong_iff_exists_paths.{u, v} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v} {k : ℕ}

      ∀ ⦃s t : V⦄,

TauCeti.isVertexStrong_iff_exists_paths.doc:
**Menger's theorem for vertex-strong arrow families.** An arrow family on a finite vertex type
is `k`-vertex-strong exactly when it has more than `k` vertices and any two distinct vertices `s`
and `t` are joined by `k` distinct directed paths pairwise sharing no vertex other than `s` and
`t`. When there are arrows from `s` to `t`, one of these paths may be a single arrow.

TauCeti.isUnimodular_leechLattice.doc: **The Leech lattice is unimodular**, being glued along a Lagrangian subgroup.

TauCeti.isSuperfluous_smul_top_of_isNilp.signature:
TauCeti.isSuperfluous_smul_top_of_isNilpotent.{u, v} {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [Semiring R]

TauCeti.isSuperfluous_smul_top_of_isNilp.doc:
**Nakayama's lemma for a nilpotent ideal.** If `I` is a nilpotent ideal then `I • M` is
superfluous in `M`.

Unlike `TauCeti.isSuperfluous_jacobson`, which asks the submodule lattice of `M` to be coatomic
(for instance `M` finitely generated) and takes the radical of `M`, nilpotence of `I` buys the
conclusion for an arbitrary module: a submodule `K` with `I • M ⊔ K = ⊤` absorbs `I ^ k • M` into
`I ^ (k + 1) • M` for every `k`, and a power of `I` vanishes.

**Burnside's `pᵃqᵇ` theorem**: a finite group of order `pᵃqᵇ`, for primes `p` and `q`, is
solvable.

**Burnside's `pᵃqᵇ` theorem**, in the form the induction runs in: a finite group whose order
divides a product of two prime powers is solvable.

quintic over a field.  If the specialization of Dummit's `F₂₀` resolvent is separable, then

field.

TauCeti.isSeqCompact_toWeakSpace_of_isCo.doc:
**Šmulian's theorem**: in a real or complex normed space, a weakly compact set is weakly
sequentially compact. Neither completeness nor separability of the space is assumed.

TauCeti.isSemialgebraic_iff_definable_ri.signature:

**Tarski's theorem for the real field.** A subset of `σ → ℝ` is semialgebraic if and only if
it is definable with parameters in the field `ℝ`, that is, in the language of rings with its usual
interpretation.

TauCeti.isSemialgebraic_iff_definable_ri.doc:
**Tarski's theorem in the field language.** Given projection closure, a subset of `σ → R` is
semialgebraic if and only if it is definable in the language of rings with parameters from `R`.

TauCeti.isRiemannRochDivisor_weilDiffere.doc:
**The Riemann–Roch theorem** (Stichtenoth, Theorem 1.5.15), for the divisor `(ω)` itself:
the divisor of a nonzero Weil differential is a Riemann–Roch divisor for the genus.

**The Riemann–Roch theorem** (Stichtenoth, Theorem 1.5.15): the divisor of a nonzero Weil
differential is a Riemann–Roch divisor for the genus.

TauCeti.isRepresentationFinite_pathAlgeb.signature:
TauCeti.isRepresentationFinite_pathAlgebra_iff_titsForm_posDef.{u, v, w} (k : Type u) (Q : Type v)

**Gabriel's theorem for path algebras.** For a finite connected quiver with finitely many paths,
the path algebra is representation-finite exactly when the Tits form is positive definite.

TauCeti.isPushout_fundamentalGroupoidOn.signature:
TauCeti.isPushout_fundamentalGroupoidOn.{u} {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] {A B S : Set X}

    (TauCeti.FundamentalGroupoidOn.map (ContinuousMap.inclusion ⋯) ⋯)
    (TauCeti.FundamentalGroupoidOn.map (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A) ⋯)
    (TauCeti.FundamentalGroupoidOn.map (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal B) ⋯)
TauCeti.isPushout_fundamentalGroupoidOn.doc:
**The two-set van Kampen theorem for fundamental groupoids on a set of basepoints.** If the
interiors of `A` and `B` cover `X` and the set `S` meets every path component of `A`, of `B`
and of `A ∩ B`, then the square of fundamental groupoids on `S` induced by the inclusions of
`A ∩ B` into `A` and `B` and of `A` and `B` into `X` is a pushout in the category of groupoids.

TauCeti.isPushout_fundamentalGroupoid.{u} {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] {A B : Set X}

    (FundamentalGroupoid.map (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A))
    (FundamentalGroupoid.map (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal B))
TauCeti.isPushout_fundamentalGroupoid.doc:
**The two-set van Kampen theorem for fundamental groupoids.** If the interiors of `A` and `B`
cover `X`, the square of fundamental groupoids induced by the inclusions of `A ∩ B` into `A` and
`B` and of `A` and `B` into `X` is a pushout in the category of groupoids.

TauCeti.isPushout_fundamentalGroup.signature:
TauCeti.isPushout_fundamentalGroup.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] {A B : Set X} {x : X}
  (hCover : interior A ∪ interior B = Set.univ) (hA : IsPathConnected A) (hB : IsPathConnected B)
  (hAB : IsPathConnected (A ∩ B)) (hxA : x ∈ A) (hxB : x ∈ B) :
  CategoryTheory.IsPushout (GrpCat.ofHom (FundamentalGroup.map (ContinuousMap.inclusion ⋯) ⟨x, ⋯⟩))

    (GrpCat.ofHom (FundamentalGroup.map (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A) ⟨x, hxA⟩))
    (GrpCat.ofHom (FundamentalGroup.map (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal B) ⟨x, hxB⟩))
TauCeti.isPushout_fundamentalGroup.doc:
**The based Seifert--van Kampen theorem.** If the interiors of `A` and `B` cover `X`, the sets
`A`, `B` and `A ∩ B` are path connected, and all three contain the basepoint `x`, then the square
of fundamental groups induced by the inclusions of `A ∩ B` into `A` and `B` and of `A` and `B`
into `X` is a pushout of groups. That is, `π₁(X, x)` is the free product of `π₁(A, x)` and
`π₁(B, x)` amalgamated over `π₁(A ∩ B, x)`.

TauCeti.isPotentiallyONable_of_discrete_norm.{u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_3} [NormedCommRing R]

TauCeti.isPotentiallyONable_of_discrete_.doc:
**Serre's potential orthonormalisation theorem.** Every Banach module over a complete
ultrametric norm-one commutative ring with discrete scalar norms and field residue ring is
continuously linearly equivalent to a native model space `C₀(I, R)`. In particular this applies
to complete discretely normed fields. The index type need not be countable.

TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_exists.doc:
**Bochner's theorem on a discrete abelian group.** A function on a discrete abelian group is
positive definite if and only if it is the Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a finite inner regular
measure on the Pontryagin dual.

and only if it is the moment sequence `φ n = ∫ zⁿ dμ(z)` of a finite positive measure on the unit
circle.

Objectwise congruence invariance is independent of an equivariant presentation of
the category. Only the forward functor of the equivalence needs a specified lineator.

TauCeti.isONable_iff_free_residueModule.{u_4, u} {R : Type u_4} [NormedCommRing R]

commutative ring with a multiplicative pseudo-uniformiser `ϖ`, let `M` be a complete ultrametric
module with contractive scalar action. If the norms of the ring and of `M` take their values in
`‖ϖ‖ ^ ℤ ∪ {0}`, then `M` is orthonormalisable exactly when its residue module is free over the

TauCeti.isNullSet_image_of_not_isRegular.doc:
**Sard's theorem at the sharp regularity, in codimension at most two.** Let `M` be a
boundaryless Lindelöf manifold modelled on a space of dimension `m` and `N` a manifold modelled on
a space of dimension `n`, with `m ≤ n + 2`. If `f` is `C^k` at every point of `s` with `k > m - n`,
and no point of `s` is regular, then `f '' s` is null in `N`.

**Sard's theorem in arbitrary dimensions.** Let `M` be a boundaryless Lindelöf manifold
modelled on a space of dimension `m`. If `f` is `C^k` at every point of `s` with `k ≥ m² + 1`, and
no point of `s` is regular, then `f '' s` is null in `N`, whatever the dimension of `N`.

**Sard's theorem in equal dimensions**, for a set of non-regular points. Let `M` and `N` be
real manifolds whose finite-dimensional models have the same dimension, with `M` Lindelöf. If `f`
is differentiable at every point of `s` and no point of `s` is regular, then `f '' s` is null in
`N`.

TauCeti.isNullSet_image_of_finrank_lt_fi.doc:
**Sard's theorem when the source has smaller dimension.** If the model of `M` has smaller
dimension than the model of `N` and `f` is differentiable at every point of `s`, then `f '' s` is
null in `N`. Both manifolds may have boundary or corners.

TauCeti.isNullSet_image_criticalPoints.doc:
**Sard's theorem in equal dimensions.** The critical values of a differentiable map from a
Lindelöf manifold to a manifold whose finite-dimensional model has the same dimension form a
null set.

TauCeti.isNilpotent_ad_lie_of_lie_lie_eq.doc:
**Jacobson's lemma** for the adjoint representation. In a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over
a field of characteristic zero, if `⁅e, ⁅e, a⁆⁆ = 0` then `ad ⁅e, a⁆` is nilpotent. In particular
every element of `ker (ad e) ⊓ [e, L]` is `ad`-nilpotent.

TauCeti.isNilpotent_ad_isSemisimple_ad_u.signature:
TauCeti.isNilpotent_ad_isSemisimple_ad_unique.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] [LieModule.IsFaithful K L L] [PerfectField K]
  {n₁ s₁ n₂ s₂ : L} (hn₁ : IsNilpotent ((LieAlgebra.ad K L) n₁))
  (hs₁ : ((LieAlgebra.ad K L) s₁).IsSemisimple) (hn₂ : IsNilpotent ((LieAlgebra.ad K L) n₂))
  (hs₂ : ((LieAlgebra.ad K L) s₂).IsSemisimple) (hc₁ : ⁅n₁, s₁⁆ = 0) (hc₂ : ⁅n₂, s₂⁆ = 0)
  (h : n₁ + s₁ = n₂ + s₂) : n₁ = n₂ ∧ s₁ = s₂
TauCeti.isNilpotent_ad_isSemisimple_ad_u.doc:
**Abstract Jordan decomposition, uniqueness.** In a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with
trivial center over a perfect field, if `n₁ + s₁ = n₂ + s₂` where `⁅nᵢ, sᵢ⁆ = 0`, `ad nᵢ` is
nilpotent and `ad sᵢ` is semisimple, then `n₁ = n₂` and `s₁ = s₂`.

TauCeti.isNashAt_iff_exists_isSemialgebr.signature:
TauCeti.isNashAt_iff_exists_isSemialgebraicOn.{u_1} {σ : Type u_1} [Fintype σ] {f : (σ → ℝ) → ℝ}
  {x : σ → ℝ} :

      ∃ U,
        IsOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ TauCeti.IsSemialgebraic U ∧ TauCeti.IsSemialgebraicOn (fun y x => f y) U
TauCeti.isNashAt_iff_exists_isSemialgebr.doc:
**The local Nash graph criterion.** A scalar function is a Nash germ at `x` exactly when
it is analytic there and its graph is semialgebraic on some open semialgebraic neighbourhood.

TauCeti.isMeagre_image_of_not_isRegularP.doc:
**Sard's theorem, in Baire category form.** The image of a Lindelöf set of critical points
at which a map is smooth is meagre. Both manifolds are finite-dimensional and without boundary;
their dimensions may differ. Smoothness is required in the ambient manifold at points of `s`,
not merely within `s`.

TauCeti.isMeagre_image_criticalPoints_of.signature:
TauCeti.isMeagre_image_criticalPoints_of_isFredholm.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
  [CompleteSpace E] [CompleteSpace F] {U : Set E} [LindelofSpace ↑U] {f : E → F} {n : WithTop ℕ∞}
  (hf : ∀ x ∈ U, ContDiffAt ℝ n f x) (hFred : ∀ x ∈ U, (fderiv ℝ f x).IsFredholm)
  (hn :
    ∀ x ∈ U,
      ↑(Module.finrank ℝ ↥(↑(fderiv ℝ f x)).ker * Module.finrank ℝ ↥(↑(fderiv ℝ f x)).ker + 1) ≤
        n) :
  IsMeagre (f '' (U ∩ {x | ¬Function.Surjective ⇑(fderiv ℝ f x)}))
TauCeti.isMeagre_image_criticalPoints_of.doc:
**The Sard--Smale theorem.** The critical values of a sufficiently smooth Fredholm map on a
Lindelöf subset of a Banach space form a meagre set. The subset need not be open; smoothness
is assumed at each of its points in the ambient space. Every subset of a separable Banach space
is Lindelöf.

Sard's theorem itself is false in infinite dimensions, and "measure zero" has no meaning there;
what survives is that the Fredholm condition confines the failure of regularity to a
finite-dimensional direction, in which the finite-dimensional theorem applies fibrewise.

The regularity threshold is the pointwise one of
`TauCeti.exists_mem_nhds_isClosed_isNowhereDense_image_criticalPoints`: at each point `C^k` with
`k ≥ (dim ker)² + 1`. In particular `n = ∞` needs no side condition.

TauCeti.isManifold_symChartedSpace.signature:
TauCeti.isManifold_symChartedSpace.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace α] [T2Space α]

  IsManifold (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ (Fin n → ℂ)) ⊤ (Sym α n)
TauCeti.isManifold_symChartedSpace.doc:
**The symmetric power of a complex curve is a complex analytic manifold.** For a Hausdorff
one-dimensional complex manifold `α`, the elementary-symmetric charts of `Sym α n` have analytic
transition maps, so `TauCeti.symChartedSpace` makes `Sym α n` an analytic manifold modelled on
`Fin n → ℂ`.

TauCeti.isLocalRing_end_of_indecomposabl.signature:
TauCeti.isLocalRing_end_of_indecomposable.{v, u, u_1} {C : Type u}

TauCeti.isLocalRing_end_of_indecomposabl.doc:
**Fitting's lemma: an indecomposable object has a local endomorphism ring**, in an
idempotent-complete linear category over a commutative Artinian ring `R` when the endomorphisms of
the object are finitely generated over `R`, for instance in a Hom-finite linear category over a
field. Indecomposability leaves `0` and `1` as the only idempotents of `End X`
(`TauCeti.idempotent_eq_zero_or_id_of_indecomposable`).

TauCeti.isLocalDiffeomorph_of_mfderiv_eq.doc:
**The inverse function theorem for manifolds**, global form: a `C^n` map (`1 ≤ n`) from a
boundaryless source manifold, all of whose differentials are continuous linear equivalences, is a
`C^n` local diffeomorphism.

TauCeti.isLocalDiffeomorph_of_deriv_ne_z.doc:
**The inverse function theorem in one variable**: a `C^n` function `𝕂 → 𝕂`, `1 ≤ n`, whose
derivative vanishes nowhere is a `C^n` local diffeomorphism.

TauCeti.isLocalDiffeomorphAt_of_mfderiv_.doc:
**The inverse function theorem for manifolds.** If `f` is `C^n` on an open set `s` with
`1 ≤ n`, `x` belongs to `s` and is an interior point, and the differential at `x` is a
continuous linear equivalence, then `f` is a `C^n` local diffeomorphism at `x`.

Mathlib's `Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/LocalDiffeomorph.lean` lists this implication as a TODO.

TauCeti.isLimitLocalHomologySystemCone.signature:
TauCeti.isLimitLocalHomologySystemCone.{w} {Λ : Type w} [Ring Λ] (N : ModuleCat Λ) (M E : Type w)
  [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [ChartedSpace E M] [CompactSpace M] {n : ℕ} (hn : Module.finrank ℝ E = n) :
  CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit (TauCeti.localHomologySystemCone N M E n)
TauCeti.isLimitLocalHomologySystemCone.doc:
**The top homology of a compact manifold is the module of parallel families of local
classes.** For a compact Hausdorff space modelled on a real normed space of finite dimension `n`,
the restrictions `Hₙ(M, M ∖ M; N) ⟶ Hₙ(M, M ∖ {x}; N)` exhibit `Hₙ(M, M ∖ M; N)` as the limit of
the local homology system: every transport-invariant family of local classes is the family of
restrictions of exactly one class.

TauCeti.isLeast_lintegral_isContinuityEq.signature:
TauCeti.isLeast_lintegral_isContinuityEquation.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [BorelSpace E]
  {μ₀ μ₁ : MeasureTheory.Measure E} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ₀]
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ₁] {p : ENNReal} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (hp_top : p ≠ ⊤)
  (hfin : TauCeti.wassersteinEDist p μ₀ μ₁ ≠ ⊤) :

    {A |
      ∃ ν v,
        TauCeti.IsContinuityEquation (fun t => ↑(ν t)) v 0 1 ∧
          ContinuousOn ν (Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
            ↑(ν 0) = μ₀ ∧

TauCeti.isLeast_lintegral_isContinuityEq.doc:
**The Benamou–Brenier formula.** For `1 ≤ p < ∞` and probability measures `μ₀`, `μ₁` on a
finite-dimensional real normed space at finite Wasserstein distance, `W_p (μ₀, μ₁) ^ p` is the
least `p`-action `∫₀¹ ∫ ‖vₜ‖ ^ p dνₜ dt` of a curve `t ↦ νₜ` of finite measures, narrowly
continuous on `[0, 1]` and joining `μ₀` to `μ₁`, solving the continuity equation with velocity `v`
on `(0, 1)`. The minimum is attained by the displacement interpolation of an optimal coupling.

primal value `∞`, in which case the continuous dual values are unbounded rather than attaining a
