**The Mayer–Vietoris isomorphism of a sphere.** The reduced Mayer–Vietoris connecting
morphism `Hₖ₊₁(S) ⟶ H_redₖ(S ∖ {p, -p})` of the cover of the unit sphere `S` by the complements of
`p` and `-p` is an isomorphism in every degree, since both complements are contractible.

are projective.

chains.

`D u x = f (x, u x)` with `u p.1 = p.2`.

lifting function.

  TauCeti.IsDemushkin p G ↔

TauCeti.isDemushkin_iff_nondegenerate_de.doc:
**Labute's criterion.** Let `F` be the free pro-`p` group on a finite type `X`, let `r ∈ Φ(F)`,
and let `G ≅ ⟨X ∣ r⟩`. Then `G` is a Demushkin group exactly when `X` is nonempty and the degree-one
form of the class of `r` in `gr_1(F)` is nondegenerate.

TauCeti.isDemushkin_absoluteGaloisGroupP.signature:
TauCeti.isDemushkin_absoluteGaloisGroupProP_of_mu (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (K : Type) [Field K]
  [ValuativeRel K] [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K]
  (hmu : ∃ ζ, IsPrimitiveRoot ζ p) : TauCeti.IsDemushkin p (TauCeti.absoluteGaloisGroupProP p K)
TauCeti.isDemushkin_absoluteGaloisGroupP.doc:
**Demushkin's theorem**: the maximal pro-`p` quotient `G_K(p)` of the absolute Galois group of
a nonarchimedean local field `K` containing a primitive `p`th root of unity is a Demushkin group.

TauCeti.isCompl_eisensteinSubspace_range.signature:
TauCeti.isCompl_eisensteinSubspace_range_cuspToModFormCharSpace {N k : ℕ} [NeZero N]
  (χ : (ZMod N)ˣ →* ℂˣ) (hk : 3 ≤ ↑k) :
  IsCompl (TauCeti.eisensteinSubspace χ hk) (TauCeti.cuspToModFormCharSpace (↑k) χ).range
TauCeti.isCompl_eisensteinSubspace_range.doc:
**The cusp–Eisenstein decomposition of `M_k(N, χ)`**: in weight `k ≥ 3`, the span of the
Eisenstein series of nebentypus `χ` is a complement of the image of `S_k(N, χ)` in `M_k(N, χ)`.

TauCeti.isCompact_setOfPred_isMultiCoupl.doc:
**Prokhorov's theorem for multi-couplings.** The multi-couplings of finitely many tight
probability measures form a weakly compact set: it is tight, hence relatively compact, and
closed.

TauCeti.isCompact_closure_toWeakSpace_of.doc:
**Grothendieck's lemma.** In a real or complex Banach space, a set has weakly compact closure
if, for every `ε > 0`, each of its points lies within norm distance `ε` of a fixed weakly compact
set.

TauCeti.isCompact_closure_range_of_isLoc.doc:
**Montel's theorem, relative-compactness form.** A locally bounded family of holomorphic
maps of an open set `Ω ⊆ ℂ` into a proper complex normed space `E` restricts to a relatively
compact family in the space `C(↥Ω, E)` of continuous maps with the compact-open topology.

The sequential selection theorem `TauCeti.montel` follows from this compactness result.
Properness of `E` is essential: a bounded family of constant maps can fail to be relatively
compact in an infinite-dimensional target.

TauCeti.isCompact_closure_range_iff_isLo.doc:
**Montel's theorem as an equivalence.** For a family of holomorphic maps of an open set
`Ω ⊆ ℂ` into a proper complex normed space `E`, being locally bounded on `Ω` and being relatively
compact in `C(↥Ω, E)` are the same condition.

TauCeti.isCompact_closure_of_isTightMeas.signature:
TauCeti.isCompact_closure_of_isTightMeasureSet_of_mass_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace α]
  [TopologicalSpace α] [T2Space α] [BorelSpace α] {S : Set (MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure α)}
  {C : NNReal} (hTight : MeasureTheory.IsTightMeasureSet {x | ∃ μ ∈ S, ↑μ = x})
  (hmass : ∀ μ ∈ S, μ.mass ≤ C) : IsCompact (closure S)
TauCeti.isCompact_closure_of_isTightMeas.doc:
**Prokhorov's theorem for finite measures.** A tight set of finite measures with uniformly
bounded total mass has compact closure in the topology of weak convergence.

This is the finite-measure counterpart of Mathlib's `isCompact_closure_of_isTightMeasureSet`
for probability measures.

TauCeti.isColimitFundamentalGroupWideCoc.signature:
TauCeti.isColimitFundamentalGroupWideCocone.{u_1, u_2} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X]
  {ι : Type u_2} {U : ι → Set X} {C : Set X} {x : X} (hU : ∀ (y : X), ∃ i, U i ∈ nhds y)

TauCeti.isColimitFundamentalGroupWideCoc.doc:
**The Seifert--van Kampen theorem for a family with a common pairwise intersection.** If the
interiors of the path-connected sets `U i` cover `X`, all of them contain the path-connected set
`C ∋ x`, and two distinct members meet inside `C`, then `π₁(X, x)` is the wide pushout in the
category of groups of the groups `π₁(U i, x)` over `π₁(C, x)`, along the maps induced by the
inclusions.

TauCeti.isAutomatic_iff_finite_kernel.signature:
TauCeti.isAutomatic_iff_finite_kernel.{u} {k : ℕ} {Δ : Type u} {a : ℕ → Δ} [NeZero k] (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
  TauCeti.IsAutomatic k a ↔ (TauCeti.kernel k a).Finite
TauCeti.isAutomatic_iff_finite_kernel.doc:
**Eilenberg's theorem**: for `2 ≤ k`, a sequence is `k`-automatic if and only if its
`k`-kernel is finite.

TauCeti.isActionStationary_iff_eulerLagr.signature:
TauCeti.isActionStationary_iff_eulerLagrange.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] {L : ℝ → E × E → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} {n : WithTop ℕ∞} {q : ℝ → E} (hn : 2 ≤ n)
  (hn' : n ≤ ↑⊤) (hq : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, ContDiffAt ℝ n q t)
  (hL : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (Function.uncurry L) (t, q t, deriv q t)) :
  TauCeti.IsActionStationary n L q a b ↔
    ∀ t ∈ Set.uIoo a b,
      HasDerivAt (fun s => fderiv ℝ (fun u => L s (q s, u)) (deriv q s))
        (fderiv ℝ (fun y => L t (y, deriv q t)) (q t)) t
TauCeti.isActionStationary_iff_eulerLagr.doc:
**Hamilton's principle of stationary action.** For `2 ≤ n ≤ ∞`, let `q` be `C^n` at every
point of `[a, b]` and let `L` be jointly `C²` along `q`. Then `q` is a stationary point of the
action of `L` among `C^n` variations with fixed endpoints between `a` and `b` exactly when it
solves the Euler–Lagrange equations `d/dt ∂_v L(t, q, q') = ∂_q L(t, q, q')` at every time strictly
between `a` and `b`.

TauCeti.inverseRegularizedGamma.doc:
The inverse `P⁻¹(s, u)` of the regularized lower incomplete gamma function in its argument.

For positive `s` this is the quantile of the Gamma law with shape `s` and rate `1`. For
nonpositive `s` it is `0`; the quantile itself supplies the value `0` outside `0 < u < 1`.

TauCeti.inv_card_le_simultaneousExponent.signature:
TauCeti.inv_card_le_simultaneousExponent.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (θ : ι → ℝ) :
  (↑(Fintype.card ι))⁻¹ ≤ TauCeti.simultaneousExponent θ
TauCeti.inv_card_le_simultaneousExponent.doc:
**Dirichlet's lower bound for the simultaneous exponent.** Every family of `n` real numbers
has simultaneous exponent at least `1 / n`. For the empty family both sides are `⊤`.

TauCeti.intervalIntegral_ofReal_cpow_neg.signature:
TauCeti.intervalIntegral_ofReal_cpow_neg_sub_one {u v : ℝ} (hu : 0 < u) (hv : 0 < v) (z : ℂ) :
  ∫ (x : ℝ) in u..v, ↑x ^ (-z - 1) = ∫ (t : ℝ) in Real.log u..Real.log v, Complex.exp (-z * ↑t)
TauCeti.intervalIntegral_ofReal_cpow_neg.doc:
**Substitution `x = exp t`.** For `0 < u` and `0 < v`, the integral of `x ^ (-z - 1)` over
`[u, v]` is the truncated Laplace transform `∫ t in log u..log v, exp (-z t)` of the constant
function `1`.

TauCeti.internalScottRank_lt_omega_one.signature:
TauCeti.internalScottRank_lt_omega_one.{u, v, w} {L : FirstOrder.Language} [L.IsRelational]
  {M : Type w} [L.Structure M] [Countable M] : TauCeti.internalScottRank M < Ordinal.omega 1
TauCeti.internalScottRank_lt_omega_one.doc:
Every countable structure has internal Scott rank below the first uncountable ordinal.
The relational language need not be countable.

TauCeti.internalEnergy_map_smul_add_smul.signature:
TauCeti.internalEnergy_map_smul_add_smul_gradient_le.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  (ρ : MeasureTheory.Measure E) [ρ.IsAddHaarMeasure] {f : E → EReal} {U : ℝ → ℝ} [Nontrivial E]
  (hU0 : U 0 = 0)
  (hc : ConvexOn ℝ (Set.Ioi 0) fun s => s ^ Module.finrank ℝ E * U (s ^ Module.finrank ℝ E)⁻¹)
  (ha : AntitoneOn (fun s => s ^ Module.finrank ℝ E * U (s ^ Module.finrank ℝ E)⁻¹) (Set.Ioi 0))
  (hf : Convex ℝ {p | f p.1 ≤ ↑p.2}) (hbot : ∀ (x : E), f x ≠ ⊥) {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E}
  [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite μ] (hμ : μ.AbsolutelyContinuous ρ)
  (hμD : ∀ᵐ (x : E) ∂μ, x ∈ interior {x | f x ≠ ⊤}) (h₀ : TauCeti.internalEnergy U ρ μ ≠ ⊥)

        μ) ≤
    ↑(1 - t) * TauCeti.internalEnergy U ρ μ +
      ↑t *
        TauCeti.internalEnergy U ρ (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (gradient fun x' => (f x').toReal) μ)
TauCeti.internalEnergy_map_smul_add_smul.doc:
**McCann's displacement convexity of internal energies.** Let `E` be a real inner product space
of finite dimension `n ≥ 1` with an additive Haar measure `ρ`, and let `U : ℝ → ℝ` satisfy
`U 0 = 0` and McCann's condition: `s ↦ sⁿ U(s⁻ⁿ)` is convex and nonincreasing on `(0, ∞)`. Let
`f : E → EReal` be convex (convex real epigraph, never `⊥`), with real representative `F`, and let
`μ` be a σ-finite measure, absolutely continuous with respect to `ρ` and carried by the interior of
the effective domain of `f`. Then the internal energy is convex along the interpolation
`μₜ = (Tₜ)₊ μ`, `Tₜ x = (1 - t) • x + t • ∇F x`:
`𝓤(μₜ) ≤ (1 - t) 𝓤(μ) + t 𝓤((∇F)₊ μ)` for `t ∈ [0, 1]`, provided neither endpoint has energy `⊥`.
The endpoint `(∇F)₊ μ` need not be absolutely continuous; its singular part is charged at the
recession constant `U'(∞)`.

TauCeti.intermediateFieldEquivClosedSubg.signature:
TauCeti.intermediateFieldEquivClosedSubgroup.{u_1, u_2} {F : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Field F]

TauCeti.intermediateFieldEquivClosedSubg.doc:
**The fundamental theorem of Galois theory in the ambient model.** For a normal extension
`E/F` the closed subgroups of `Gal(E/F)` correspond, inclusion-reversingly, to the intermediate
fields of the separable closure `separableClosure F E / F`; an intermediate field of `E` outside
the separable closure has the same fixing subgroup as its separable part.

TauCeti.interior_image_criticalPoints_eq.doc:
**The Morse--Sard theorem at the sharp regularity, in codimension at most two**, in the form
that carries no measure-theoretic data: if `finrank ℝ E ≤ finrank ℝ F + 2` and the map is `C^n`
at every point of `U` with `finrank ℝ E - finrank ℝ F < n`, then the critical values taken on `U`
have empty interior.

TauCeti.interior_image_criticalPoints_eq.signature:
TauCeti.interior_image_criticalPoints_eq_empty.{u, v} {E : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {F : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ F] {U : Set E} {f : E → F} {n : WithTop ℕ∞}
  (hf : ∀ x ∈ U, ContDiffAt ℝ n f x) (hk : ↑(Module.finrank ℝ E * Module.finrank ℝ E + 1) ≤ n) :
  interior (f '' (U ∩ {x | ¬Function.Surjective ⇑(fderiv ℝ f x)})) = ∅
TauCeti.interior_image_criticalPoints_eq.doc:
**The Morse--Sard theorem**, in the form that carries no measure-theoretic data: the critical
values taken on a set where the map is sufficiently smooth at every point have empty interior.
The measure structure used to prove it is chosen inside the proof, so the target here carries no
`MeasurableSpace` instance; this is the shape in which Sard is fed to the fibrewise step of the
Sard--Smale theorem, where the target is a complement subspace with no measurable structure of
its own.

TauCeti.integral_trace_fderiv_mul_indica.signature:
TauCeti.integral_trace_fderiv_mul_indicator_eq_integral_inner_outerNormal.{u_1} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  [BorelSpace E] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E} {Ω : TopologicalSpace.Opens E} {s : Set E}
  (hu : MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrableOn (s.indicator 1) (↑Ω) μ)
  (hfin :
    ∀ (K : Set E),
      IsCompact K → K ⊆ ↑Ω → ∃ U, K ⊆ ↑U ∧ TauCeti.totalVariationOn μ U (s.indicator 1) ≠ ⊤)
  {φ : E → E} (hφ : ContDiff ℝ 1 φ) (hc : HasCompactSupport φ) (hs : tsupport φ ⊆ ↑Ω) :
  ∫ (x : E), (LinearMap.trace ℝ E) ↑(fderiv ℝ φ x) * s.indicator 1 x ∂μ =
    ∫ (y : ↥Ω),
      inner ℝ (φ ↑y) (TauCeti.outerNormal μ Ω s ↑y) ∂TauCeti.variationMeasure μ Ω (s.indicator 1)
TauCeti.integral_trace_fderiv_mul_indica.doc:
**The Gauss–Green formula, `Dχ_s = -ν_s |Dχ_s|`.** For a set `s` of locally finite perimeter
in `Ω`, the outer normal `ν_s` represents the distributional derivative of the indicator against
the perimeter measure: `∫_s div φ dμ = ∫ ⟪φ, ν_s⟫ d|Dχ_s|` for every `C¹` vector field `φ` with
compact support in `Ω`, where `div φ = tr (Dφ)`.

TauCeti.integral_posDef_multivariateGamm.signature:
TauCeti.integral_posDef_multivariateGamma {p : ℕ} {a : ℝ} (ha : (↑p - 1) / 2 < a) :
  ∫ (A : ↥(selfAdjoint.submodule ℝ (Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ))) in {A | (↑A).PosDef},

TauCeti.integral_posDef_multivariateGamm.doc:
**The multivariate Gamma integral.** For `((p : ℝ) - 1) / 2 < a`, the integral of
`(det A) ^ (a - (p + 1) / 2) * exp (-trace A)` over the cone of positive-definite symmetric
`p × p` matrices, against `TauCeti.symmetricLebesgue p`, is `Γ_p(a)`.

TauCeti.integral_norm_sum_sq_of_pairwise.signature:
TauCeti.integral_norm_sum_sq_of_pairwise_indepFun.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2}

  (hindep : (↑s).Pairwise fun i j => ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (X i) (X j) μ) :

TauCeti.integral_norm_sum_sq_of_pairwise.doc:
**Bienaymé's identity for random vectors.** If the random vectors `X i`, `i ∈ s`, in a real
Hilbert space are square-integrable, centered and pairwise independent, then the expected squared
norm of their sum is the sum of their expected squared norms.

TauCeti.integral_norm_sub_average_sq_le.signature:
TauCeti.integral_norm_sub_average_sq_le.{u_1} {a b : ℝ} {V : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup V]

  (hf : AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval f a b)

TauCeti.integral_norm_sub_average_sq_le.doc:
**Wirtinger's inequality.** An absolutely continuous function on `[a, b]` with `f a = f b`,
valued in a finite-dimensional real inner product space and with square-integrable
almost-everywhere derivative, deviates from its mean in `L²` by at most `(b - a) / (2π)` times
the `L²` norm of its derivative.

TauCeti.integral_norm_sub_average_sq_eq_.signature:

  (hf : AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval f a b)
  (hff' : ∀ᵐ (t : ℝ), t ∈ Set.uIoc a b → HasDerivAt f (f' t) t) (hfab : f a = f b)
  (hf' : MeasureTheory.MemLp f' 2 (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ioc a b))) :
  ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, ‖f x - ⨍ (y : ℝ) in a..b, f y‖ ^ 2 =

TauCeti.integral_norm_sub_average_sq_eq_.doc:
**Equality in Wirtinger's inequality.** Equality holds exactly when, on `[a, b]`, the function
is its mean plus a first harmonic `cos (2π t / (b - a)) • u + sin (2π t / (b - a)) • v`.

TauCeti.integral_norm_rpow_neg_finrank_m.doc:
**Radial fundamental theorem of calculus.** For a `C¹` function `f` with compact support on a
nontrivial finite-dimensional real normed space of dimension `d`,
`∫ ‖x‖ ^ (-d) * f' x x ∂μ = -(d * μ (ball 0 1)) * f 0`.

In the language of distributions, `div (x / ‖x‖ ^ d) = d μ(ball 0 1) δ₀`.

TauCeti.integral_inner_sub_integral_le.doc:
**The quadratic Fenchel–Young inequality in mean.** Let `X` and `Y` be square-integrable
random vectors, where the law of `X` has covariance matrix `A * T * A` for a positive-semidefinite
matrix `A`. Then the correlation of the centred variable `X - 𝔼 X` with `Y` is at most
`(𝔼 ⟪A Y, Y⟫ + tr (A * T)) / 2`.

TauCeti.integral_fderiv_sub_fderiv_Icc.signature:
TauCeti.integral_fderiv_sub_fderiv_Icc {U : Set (ℝ × ℝ)} {fs ft : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ × ℝ}

TauCeti.integral_fderiv_sub_fderiv_Icc.doc:
**Green's theorem on a rectangle.** For a one-form `f_s ds + f_t dt` that is `C¹` over an
open neighbourhood of a rectangle `[a₁, b₁] × [a₂, b₂]`, the integral of its exterior derivative
`∂_s f_t - ∂_t f_s` over the rectangle is its integral over the positively oriented boundary.

TauCeti.integral_exp_neg_mul_sin_lt.signature:
TauCeti.integral_exp_neg_mul_sin_lt (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) :

TauCeti.integral_exp_neg_mul_sin_lt.doc: **Jordan's integral bound.** For `c > 0`, `∫₀^π e^{-c sin θ} dθ < π / c`.

**Lebesgue decomposition of the BV derivative.** The distributional derivative is the sum
of the density `acDerivativeDensity μ Ω u ν` against `ν` and the polar field against the singular
part of `|Du|`. Both pairings are integrable because the test field has compact support.

TauCeti.integralTopForm_mpullback_Icc_eq.doc:
For `a < b`, the line integral of a continuous real `1`-form along a `C¹` curve is the
canonical oriented integral over `[a, b]` of the pullback of the form along the curve.

TauCeti.integralTopForm_mextDeriv.signature:

  [ChartedSpace (EuclideanHalfSpace (n + 1)) M]

  (o : TauCeti.Manifold.Orientation (modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace (n + 1)) M (Fin (n + 1)))
  {φ : TauCeti.RoughForm (modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace (n + 1)) M ℝ n}

TauCeti.integralTopForm_mextDeriv.doc:
Stokes' theorem for a compactly supported C1 form on an oriented smooth manifold with
boundary. The boundary carries its outward-first orientation.

TauCeti.integralClosure.isNoetherianRing.signature:
TauCeti.integralClosure.isNoetherianRing.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]

  (K : Type u_3) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] [_root_.Module K L]
  [IsScalarTower A K L] [Module.Finite K L] : IsNoetherianRing ↥(integralClosure A L)
TauCeti.integralClosure.isNoetherianRing.doc:
**Krull–Akizuki for Mathlib's `integralClosure`.** The specialisation of
`TauCeti.IsIntegralClosure.isNoetherianRing` to the integral closure of `A` in `L` as a
subalgebra.

TauCeti.integral2_slice_sub_eq_sides.doc:
**Stokes' formula on the boundary of a cube** for a closed two-form `ψ` that is C¹ on
`(ℝ × ℝ) × ℝ`: its integrals over the top and bottom faces `[a, b] × {1}` and `[a, b] × {0}`
differ by the signed sum of its integrals over the four side faces, each parametrized by the
direction of its edge followed by the last coordinate. All integrals are iterated integrals over
oriented intervals, so the corners `a` and `b` may come in either order.

The proof applies Stokes' formula on the rectangle to the cylinder homotopy `h ψ`, whose exterior
derivative is the difference of the top and bottom slices of the closed form `ψ`.

TauCeti.instHasSemialgebraicProjectionsR.doc:
**The Tarski–Seidenberg theorem.** The projection of a semialgebraic subset of `ℝ ^ (n + 1)`
forgetting the coordinate `0` is semialgebraic. So quantifier elimination, the identification of
semialgebraic sets with definable sets, and the image and composition laws of semialgebraic
functions, which assume `HasSemialgebraicProjections`, hold over `ℝ` unconditionally.

TauCeti.instCWComplexCellularClassifying.signature:
TauCeti.instCWComplexCellularClassifyingSpace.{u} {S : Type u} (R : Set (FreeGroup S)) :
  Topology.CWComplex Set.univ
TauCeti.instCWComplexCellularClassifying.doc:
**The cellular classifying space is a CW complex.** Its cells are those of the presentation
complex, one `0`-cell, one `1`-cell for each generator and one `2`-cell for each relator, together
with the cells of dimension at least `3` attached to kill the higher homotopy groups
(`TauCeti.killHomotopyGroupsCWComplexCellEquiv`).

TauCeti.injective_freeGroup_lift_transve.doc:
**Sanov's theorem.** The matrices `[[1, 2], [0, 1]]` and `[[1, 0], [2, 1]]` freely generate
a free subgroup of rank two of `SL(2, ℤ)`. This is the case `R = ℤ`, `c = d = 2` of
`injective_freeGroup_lift_transvection_of_two_le_abs`.

TauCeti.injective_freeGroup_lift_transve.signature:
TauCeti.injective_freeGroup_lift_transvection_of_two_le_abs.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R]
  [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] {c d : R} (hc : 2 ≤ |c|) (hd : 2 ≤ |d|) :
  Function.Injective
    ⇑(FreeGroup.lift
        ![Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.transvection ⋯ c, Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.transvection ⋯ d])
TauCeti.injective_freeGroup_lift_transve.doc:
**Sanov's theorem**, in the general form over a linearly ordered commutative ring `R`: for
`c, d : R` with `2 ≤ |c|` and `2 ≤ |d|`, the matrices `[[1, c], [0, 1]]` and `[[1, 0], [d, 1]]`
freely generate a free subgroup of rank two of `SL(2, R)`.

TauCeti.infinite_totallyRamifiedOfDegree.signature:
TauCeti.infinite_totallyRamifiedOfDegree_iff_or_tsum_eq_top.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  [ValuativeRel K] [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
  (TauCeti.totallyRamifiedOfDegree K n).Infinite ↔
    ringChar K = ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField ↥(ValuativeRel.valuation K).integer) ∧
        ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField ↥(ValuativeRel.valuation K).integer) ∣ n ∨
      ∑' (L : ↑(TauCeti.totallyRamifiedOfDegree K n)),
          1 /
            ↑(Nat.card (IsLocalRing.ResidueField ↥(ValuativeRel.valuation K).integer)) ^
              (↑L).wildExponent =
        ⊤
TauCeti.infinite_totallyRamifiedOfDegree.doc:
**Serre's finiteness dichotomy, relative to the weighted count**: for `0 < n`, `σ_K(n)` is
infinite exactly when `K` has equal characteristic `p`, the residue characteristic, with `p ∣ n`,
or the weighted count `∑_{L ∈ σ_K(n)} q ^ (-c(L))` of Serre's mass formula is infinite. Since the
mass formula makes that count `n`, the second alternative never occurs.

TauCeti.infinite_totallyRamifiedOfDegree.signature:
TauCeti.infinite_totallyRamifiedOfDegree_iff.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [ValuativeRel K]
  [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
  (TauCeti.totallyRamifiedOfDegree K n).Infinite ↔

      ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField ↥(ValuativeRel.valuation K).integer) ∣ n
TauCeti.infinite_totallyRamifiedOfDegree.doc:
**Serre's finiteness dichotomy**: for `0 < n`, there are infinitely many totally ramified
degree-`n` subextensions of a separable closure of `K` exactly when `K` has equal
characteristic `p`, the residue characteristic, and `p ∣ n`.

TauCeti.infinite_totallyRamifiedOfDegree.signature:
TauCeti.infinite_totallyRamifiedOfDegree.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [ValuativeRel K]
  [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hnK : ↑n = 0) :
  (TauCeti.totallyRamifiedOfDegree K n).Infinite
TauCeti.infinite_totallyRamifiedOfDegree.doc:
**Infinitely many totally ramified extensions in equal characteristic.** If `0 < n` and
`(n : K) = 0`, that is, `K` has characteristic `p > 0` with `p ∣ n`, then `σ_K(n)` is infinite:
its discriminant exponents are unbounded.

TauCeti.infinite_simultaneousApproximati.signature:
TauCeti.infinite_simultaneousApproximationDenominators_inv_card.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι]
  (θ : ι → ℝ) : (TauCeti.simultaneousApproximationDenominators θ (↑(Fintype.card ι))⁻¹).Infinite
TauCeti.infinite_simultaneousApproximati.doc:
**Dirichlet's theorem, infinitely many denominators.** For every finite family `θ`,
infinitely many positive integers `q` admit integers `pᵢ` with `|q θᵢ - pᵢ| ≤ q ^ (-1 / n)` for
every `i`, where `n` is the number of coordinates.

TauCeti.infinite_linearFormApproximation.doc:
**Dirichlet's theorem for one linear form, infinitely many solutions.** If `1` and the
`n ≥ 1` real numbers `θᵢ` satisfy no nontrivial integer relation, then every exponent `w < n` has
infinitely many solutions `0 < |x₀ + ∑ i, xᵢ θᵢ| ≤ ‖x‖ ^ (-w)`, with the sup norm taken over all
coordinates of `x`.

TauCeti.inertiaDegree_mul_ramificationIn.signature:
TauCeti.inertiaDegree_mul_ramificationIndex_sub_one_le_discriminantExponent.{u_1, u_2}

TauCeti.inertiaDegree_mul_ramificationIn.doc:
**The first half of Dedekind's different theorem, for the discriminant**: the discriminant
exponent is at least `f(L/K) · (e(L/K) - 1)`.

TauCeti.index_square_le_of_closure_eq_to.signature:
TauCeti.index_square_le_of_closure_eq_top.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [CommGroup G] {S : Finset G}
  (hS : Subgroup.closure ↑S = ⊤) : (Subgroup.square G).index ≤ 2 ^ S.card
TauCeti.index_square_le_of_closure_eq_to.doc:
In a commutative group generated by a finite set `S`, the subgroup of squares has index at
most `2 ^ S.card`. The quotient by the squares is an elementary abelian `2`-group spanned by
the image of `S`.

TauCeti.indecomposable_iff_isLocalRing_e.signature:
TauCeti.indecomposable_iff_isLocalRing_end.{u, v} {A : Type u} [Ring A] (M : ModuleCat A)
  (hM : IsFiniteLength A ↑M) : CategoryTheory.Indecomposable M ↔ IsLocalRing (CategoryTheory.End M)
TauCeti.indecomposable_iff_isLocalRing_e.doc:
**Fitting's lemma, categorically**: an object of `ModuleCat A` whose underlying module has
finite length is indecomposable exactly when its ring of endomorphisms in the category is local.

TauCeti.hyperbolicSixSpinEquivSpecialLin.signature:
TauCeti.hyperbolicSixSpinEquivSpecialLinear.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [NeZero 2] :
  ↥(spinGroup (TauCeti.splitEvenForm K 3)) ≃* Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 4) K
TauCeti.hyperbolicSixSpinEquivSpecialLin.doc:
**The Spin group of three hyperbolic planes is `SL₄(K)`.** This is
`TauCeti.spinGroupEquivSpecialLinearGroupOfFinrankEqSix` for the canonical split polarization, so a
Spin element goes to the matrix of its even half-spin action in
`TauCeti.spinSixHalfSpinStandardBasis`. By `TauCeti.coe_hyperbolicSixSpinEquivSpecialLinear_apply`
it is the restriction of `TauCeti.hyperbolicSixEvenUnitaryEquivGeneralLinear` to Spin, so `Spin(Q)`
is the determinant-one subgroup of the reverse-unitary group `U(C₀, σ) ≅ GL₄(K)`. Over `ℚ`, three
hyperbolic planes give the split rational six-dimensional form, with `U(C₀, σ) ≅ GL₄(ℚ)` and
`Spin(Q) ≅ SL₄(ℚ)`.

TauCeti.hyperbolicLength_comp_le.signature:
TauCeti.hyperbolicLength_comp_le {γ γ' : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
  (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Metric.ball 0 1))
  (hmaps : Set.MapsTo f (Metric.ball 0 1) (Metric.ball 0 1)) (hγ : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc a b))
  (hderiv : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIoo a b, HasDerivAt γ (γ' t) t) (hγ' : ContinuousOn γ' (Set.uIcc a b))
  (hmem : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, ‖γ t‖ < 1) :
  TauCeti.hyperbolicLength (f ∘ γ) a b ≤ TauCeti.hyperbolicLength γ a b
TauCeti.hyperbolicLength_comp_le.doc:
**Schwarz--Pick for the Poincaré length.** Post-composing a path in the open unit disc with a
holomorphic self-map of the disc does not increase its hyperbolic length. This is the infinitesimal
Schwarz--Pick inequality `TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_le` integrated along the path, in
the same way as `TauCeti.hyperbolicLength_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_comp` integrates its equality
case; the path is asked to be `C¹` on its parameter interval, as in
`TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_le_hyperbolicLength`, so that both density-weighted speeds are
integrable, which is what `TauCeti.densityLength_le_densityLength` spends to turn the pointwise
comparison of the two integrands into a comparison of the two lengths.

TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_map_le.signature:
TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_map_le {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Metric.ball 0 1))
  (hmaps : Set.MapsTo f (Metric.ball 0 1) (Metric.ball 0 1)) {z w : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ Metric.ball 0 1)
  (hw : w ∈ Metric.ball 0 1) : TauCeti.hyperbolicDist (f z) (f w) ≤ TauCeti.hyperbolicDist z w
TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_map_le.doc:
**Schwarz--Pick, distance form.** A holomorphic self-map of the complex unit disc does not
increase the hyperbolic distance.

TauCeti.hurwitz_injOn.signature:
TauCeti.hurwitz_injOn.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} {l : Filter ι} {Ω : Set ℂ} {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ}
  (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hconn : IsPreconnected Ω) (hF : ∀ᶠ (i : ι) in l, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) Ω)
  (hconv : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F g l Ω) (hinj : ∃ᶠ (i : ι) in l, Set.InjOn (F i) Ω) :
  Set.InjOn g Ω ∨ ∃ v, ∀ z ∈ Ω, g z = v
TauCeti.hurwitz_injOn.doc:
**Hurwitz's theorem for injectivity.** On a connected open set, a locally uniform limit of
functions that are holomorphic for all sufficiently large `i` and *injective* for infinitely many
`i` is either injective or constant.

This is the form the Riemann mapping theorem consumes: it is what keeps the extremal map injective
in the limit. Both alternatives genuinely occur — for `ι = ℕ` and `l = atTop`, the injective maps
`F n z = z / (n + 1 : ℂ)` converge locally uniformly to the constant `0`.

TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula_ratFunc.signature:
TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula_ratFunc.{u, v} {k : Type u} {F : Type v} [Field k] [Field F]
  [Algebra k F] [Algebra (RatFunc k) F] [IsScalarTower k (RatFunc k) F]
  [FiniteDimensional (RatFunc k) F] [Algebra.IsSeparable (RatFunc k) F]
  (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F) :
  2 * ↑(TauCeti.genus k F) - 2 =
    -2 * ↑(Module.finrank (RatFunc k) F) + TauCeti.Divisor.degree (TauCeti.Divisor.different k F ⋯)
TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula_ratFunc.doc:
**The Hurwitz genus formula over a rational subfield** (Stichtenoth, Corollary 3.4.14): for a
finite separable extension `F` of the rational function field `k(x)` with exact constant field
`k`, `2g - 2 = -2 [F : k(x)] + deg Diff(F / k(x))`.

TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula_geometricD.signature:
TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula_geometricDegree.{u, u', v, v'} {k : Type u} {k' : Type u'}
  {F : Type v} {F' : Type v'} [Field k] [Field k'] [Field F] [Field F'] [Algebra k k'] [Algebra k F]
  [Algebra k' F'] [Algebra F F'] [Algebra k F'] [IsScalarTower k k' F'] [IsScalarTower k F F']
  [FiniteDimensional F F'] [Algebra.IsSeparable F F'] [FiniteDimensional k k']
  [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'] (hF : TauCeti.IsFunctionField k F)
  (hF' : TauCeti.IsFunctionField k' F') (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F)
  (hex' : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k' F') :
  2 * ↑(TauCeti.genus k' F') - 2 =
    ↑(TauCeti.geometricDegree F k' F') * (2 * ↑(TauCeti.genus k F) - 2) +
      TauCeti.Divisor.degree (TauCeti.Divisor.different k' F' hF)
TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula_geometricD.doc:
**The Hurwitz genus formula through the geometric degree** (Stichtenoth, Theorem 3.4.13): under
the hypotheses of `TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula`,
`2g' - 2 = n(F'/F) · (2g - 2) + deg Diff(F'/F)`, where `n(F'/F) = [F' : F k']` is the geometric
degree.

TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula.signature:
TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula.{u, u', v, v'} {k : Type u} {k' : Type u'} {F : Type v} {F' : Type v'}
  [Field k] [Field k'] [Field F] [Field F'] [Algebra k k'] [Algebra k F] [Algebra k' F']
  [Algebra F F'] [Algebra k F'] [IsScalarTower k k' F'] [IsScalarTower k F F']
  [FiniteDimensional F F'] [Algebra.IsSeparable F F'] [FiniteDimensional k k']
  [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'] (hF : TauCeti.IsFunctionField k F)
  (hF' : TauCeti.IsFunctionField k' F') (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F)
  (hex' : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k' F') :
  ↑(Module.finrank k k') * (2 * ↑(TauCeti.genus k' F') - 2) =
    ↑(Module.finrank F F') * (2 * ↑(TauCeti.genus k F) - 2) +
      ↑(Module.finrank k k') * TauCeti.Divisor.degree (TauCeti.Divisor.different k' F' hF)
TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula.doc:
**The Hurwitz genus formula** (Stichtenoth, Theorem 3.4.13): for a finite separable extension
`F' / k'` of the function field `F / k`, both with exact constants and with `k' / k` finite
separable, `[k' : k] · (2g' - 2) = [F' : F] · (2g - 2) + [k' : k] · deg Diff(F'/F)`.

TauCeti.hurwitz_forall_ne_or_forall_eq.signature:
TauCeti.hurwitz_forall_ne_or_forall_eq.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} {l : Filter ι} {Ω : Set ℂ}
  {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ} (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hconn : IsPreconnected Ω)
  (hF : ∀ᶠ (i : ι) in l, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) Ω) (hconv : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F g l Ω)
  {v : ℂ} (hne : ∃ᶠ (i : ι) in l, ∀ z ∈ Ω, F i z ≠ v) : (∀ z ∈ Ω, g z ≠ v) ∨ ∀ z ∈ Ω, g z = v
TauCeti.hurwitz_forall_ne_or_forall_eq.doc:
**Hurwitz's theorem for an omitted value**, dichotomy form. On a connected open set, a locally
uniform limit of functions that are holomorphic for all sufficiently large `i` and avoid the value
`v` for infinitely many `i` either avoids `v` everywhere or is constantly `v`.

The dichotomy is genuine: for `ι = ℕ` and `l = atTop`, the functions `F n z = v + 1 / (n + 1 : ℂ)`
avoid `v` on any `Ω` and converge locally uniformly to the constant `v`.

TauCeti.hurwitz_forall_ne.signature:
TauCeti.hurwitz_forall_ne.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} {l : Filter ι} {Ω : Set ℂ} {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ}
  {g : ℂ → ℂ} (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hconn : IsPreconnected Ω)
  (hF : ∀ᶠ (i : ι) in l, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) Ω) (hconv : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F g l Ω)
  {v : ℂ} (hne : ∃ᶠ (i : ι) in l, ∀ z ∈ Ω, F i z ≠ v) (hnc : ¬∀ z ∈ Ω, g z = v) (z : ℂ) :
  z ∈ Ω → g z ≠ v
TauCeti.hurwitz_forall_ne.doc:
**Hurwitz's theorem for an omitted value.** If `F i` is holomorphic on `Ω` for all sufficiently
large `i` and avoids the value `v` there for infinitely many `i` (frequently along `l`), and the
locally uniform limit `g` is not constantly `v`, then `g` avoids `v` as well.

Contrapositive of `TauCeti.hurwitz_eventually_exists_eq`: a point where `g` took the value `v`
would force `F i` to take it too.

TauCeti.hurwitz_eventually_exists_eq_zer.signature:
TauCeti.hurwitz_eventually_exists_eq_zero.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} {l : Filter ι} {Ω : Set ℂ}
  {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ} [l.NeBot] (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hconn : IsPreconnected Ω)
  (hF : ∀ᶠ (i : ι) in l, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) Ω) (hconv : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F g l Ω)
  {z₀ : ℂ} (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ Ω) (hgz₀ : g z₀ = 0) (hnc : ¬∀ z ∈ Ω, g z = 0) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∀ᶠ (i : ι) in l, ∃ z ∈ Ω ∩ Metric.ball z₀ ε, F i z = 0
TauCeti.hurwitz_eventually_exists_eq_zer.doc:
**Hurwitz's theorem: zeros of the limit are limits of zeros.** If `g` is the locally uniform
limit on a connected open `Ω` of functions `F i` that are holomorphic for all sufficiently large
`i`, is not identically zero, and vanishes at `z₀ ∈ Ω`, then every ball about `z₀` contains a zero
of `F i` for all sufficiently large `i`.

The hypothesis that `g` is not identically zero cannot be dropped: for `ι = ℕ` and `l = atTop`,
the constant functions `F n z = 1 / (n + 1 : ℂ)` are holomorphic and nowhere zero and converge
locally uniformly to `g = 0`, which vanishes at every `z₀`, yet no `F n` has a zero anywhere.

Note that the ball is *not* assumed to lie in `Ω`; the zero produced is located in
`Ω ∩ ball z₀ ε`.

TauCeti.hurwitz_eventually_exists_eq.signature:
TauCeti.hurwitz_eventually_exists_eq.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} {l : Filter ι} {Ω : Set ℂ} {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ}
  {g : ℂ → ℂ} [l.NeBot] (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hconn : IsPreconnected Ω)
  (hF : ∀ᶠ (i : ι) in l, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) Ω) (hconv : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F g l Ω)

  ∀ᶠ (i : ι) in l, ∃ z ∈ Ω ∩ Metric.ball z₀ ε, F i z = v
TauCeti.hurwitz_eventually_exists_eq.doc:
**Hurwitz's theorem: values of the limit are limits of values.** If `g` is the locally uniform
limit on a connected open `Ω` of functions `F i` that are holomorphic for all sufficiently large
`i`, is not constantly `v`, and takes the value `v` at `z₀ ∈ Ω`, then every ball about `z₀`
contains a point where `F i` takes the value `v`, again for all sufficiently large `i`.

This is `TauCeti.hurwitz_eventually_exists_eq_zero` for the translated family `F i - v`, and the
form the injectivity corollary `TauCeti.hurwitz_injOn` consumes.

TauCeti.hurwitz.signature:
TauCeti.hurwitz.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} {l : Filter ι} {Ω : Set ℂ} {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ}

TauCeti.hurwitz.doc:
**Hurwitz's theorem.** On a connected open set, a locally uniform limit of functions that are
holomorphic for all sufficiently large `i` and nowhere zero for infinitely many `i` is itself
either nowhere zero or identically zero.

This is the value `v = 0` of `TauCeti.hurwitz_forall_ne_or_forall_eq`. The dichotomy is genuine:
for `ι = ℕ` and `l = atTop`, the constant functions `F n z = 1 / (n + 1 : ℂ)` on any `Ω` converge
locally uniformly to `0`, so the second alternative cannot be dropped.

TauCeti.house_eq_one_iff.signature:
TauCeti.house_eq_one_iff.{u_1} {F : Type u_1} [Field F] [CharZero F] {x : F} (hx : IsIntegral ℤ x) :
  TauCeti.house x = 1 ↔ ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ x ^ n = 1
TauCeti.house_eq_one_iff.doc:
**Kronecker's theorem.** An algebraic integer has house `1` exactly when it is a root of
unity.

TauCeti.hopfLax_norm_rpow_add_add_smul_l.signature:
TauCeti.hopfLax_norm_rpow_add_add_smul_le.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E]

  TauCeti.hopfLax (fun x => ‖x‖ ^ p) φ (t + h) (x + h • w) ≤
    TauCeti.hopfLax (fun x => ‖x‖ ^ p) φ t x + h * ‖w‖ ^ p
TauCeti.hopfLax_norm_rpow_add_add_smul_l.doc:
**The Hopf–Lax subsolution inequality for the `p`-th power cost.** In a real seminormed space,
for `1 ≤ p` and `φ` bounded below, `u (t + h, x + h w) ≤ u (t, x) + h ‖w‖ ^ p` for `t > 0` and
`h ≥ 0`.

TauCeti.hopfLax_add_add_smul_le.signature:
TauCeti.hopfLax_add_add_smul_le.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module ℝ E]

  (hLc : ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ L) (ht : 0 < t) (hh : 0 ≤ h) (x w : E) :
  TauCeti.hopfLax L φ (t + h) (x + h • w) ≤ TauCeti.hopfLax L φ t x + h * L w
TauCeti.hopfLax_add_add_smul_le.doc:
**The Hopf–Lax subsolution inequality.** For a convex Lagrangian `L`, moving from `(t, x)` at
velocity `w` for time `h ≥ 0` raises the Hopf–Lax value by at most `h L w`:
`u (t + h, x + h w) ≤ u (t, x) + h L w` for `t > 0`.

TauCeti.homotopyOperator.signature:
TauCeti.homotopyOperator.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {E : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3}
  {F : Type u_4} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace H]

      (k + 1)) :
  TauCeti.RoughForm I M F k
TauCeti.homotopyOperator.doc:
The **homotopy operator** on forms on the cylinder `M × [0, 1]`: the `k`-form
`x ↦ ∫₀¹ φ(x, t)(∂ₜ, (·, 0)) dt` on `M` built from a `(k + 1)`-form `φ` on `M × [0, 1]`, where
`∂ₜ = (0, 1)` is the unit time vector and tangent vectors of `M` enter through
`ContinuousLinearMap.inl`. Equivalently `h φ = ∫₀¹ ιₜ^*(∂ₜ ⌟ φ) dt` for the slices
`ιₜ x = (x, t)`. For a `C¹` form with values in a Banach space on a `C²` manifold,
`d (h φ) + h (d φ) = ι₁^* φ - ι₀^* φ`
(`TauCeti.mextDeriv_homotopyOperator_add_homotopyOperator_mextDeriv`).

TauCeti.homotopyGroupMulAction.signature:
TauCeti.homotopyGroupMulAction.{u_1, u_2} {N : Type u_1} [Fintype N] {X : Type u_2}
  [TopologicalSpace X] {x : X} : MulAction (FundamentalGroup X x) (HomotopyGroup N X x)
TauCeti.homotopyGroupMulAction.doc:
**The fundamental group at `x` acts on every homotopy group based at `x`**, an element of
`π₁(X, x)` acting by transport around the loop it represents.

The action is a left action: transport composes covariantly and `FundamentalGroup.mul_def`
reverses the order of concatenation, so the two reversals cancel.

TauCeti.homologyEulerChar_cellularChainC.signature:
TauCeti.homologyEulerChar_cellularChainComplex.{w} {X : Type w} [TopologicalSpace X] {D : Set X}
  (C : Set X) [Topology.RelCWComplex C D] [T2Space X] {k : Type w} [DivisionRing k]

  HomologicalComplex.homologyEulerChar (TauCeti.cellularChainComplex C M) =
    ↑(Module.finrank k ↑M) * TauCeti.cwEulerChar C
TauCeti.homologyEulerChar_cellularChainC.doc:
**Euler--Poincaré for a finite relative CW complex.**  The alternating sum of the dimensions
of the cellular homology groups of a finite relative CW complex, with coefficients in a
finite-dimensional module `M`, is `dim M` times the alternating count of its cells.

TauCeti.hom_eq_zero_of_isEmpty_linearEqu.doc:
**Schur's lemma, vanishing form.** A linear map between simple modules is zero if the two
modules are not linearly equivalent.

The `IsEmpty` hypothesis is the constructive form of saying that no equivalence exists.

TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.quotie.doc:
The sheaf of holomorphic functions on the normalization which have matching values on each
fibre of the quotient map. For paired node flags this is the normalization construction of the
structure sheaf of a nodal curve.

TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.isFrac.signature:
TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.isFractionRing_meromorphicGerms (a : ℂ) :
  IsFractionRing
    ↑((TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ ℂ) ℂ).presheaf.stalk a)
    ↥(TauCeti.meromorphicGerms ℂ a)
TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.isFrac.doc:
The field of meromorphic germs at `a : ℂ` is the fraction field of the ring of holomorphic
germs at `a`.

TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.exists.signature:
TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.existsUnique_weierstrassPreparation {E : Type}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] [FiniteDimensional ℂ E] {x₀ : E} {w₀ : ℂ}
  {f :
    ↑((TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ (E × ℂ)) (E × ℂ)).presheaf.stalk
        (x₀, w₀))}
  (hf :
    (PowerSeries.map
          (IsLocalRing.residue
            ↑((TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ E) E).presheaf.stalk x₀)))
        ((TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.verticalPowerSeries x₀ w₀) f) ≠
      0) :
  ∃! pu,
    pu.1.IsDistinguishedAt
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal
          ↑((TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ E) E).presheaf.stalk x₀)) ∧
      IsUnit pu.2 ∧ f = (TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.evalVertical x₀ w₀) pu.1 * pu.2
TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.exists.doc:
**Weierstrass preparation theorem in holomorphic stalks.** Every holomorphic germ `f` at
`(x₀, w₀)` whose vertical power series has nonzero image in `(𝒪_{E, x₀} ⧸ 𝔪_{x₀})⟦X⟧` admits a
unique factorization `f = evalVertical x₀ w₀ P * u` into a distinguished polynomial `P` over
`𝒪_{E, x₀}` and a unit germ `u` at `(x₀, w₀)`.

TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.exists.signature:
TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.existsUnique_weierstrassDivision {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E]

    ↑((TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ (E × ℂ)) (E × ℂ)).presheaf.stalk
        (x₀, w₀))}
  (hf :
    (PowerSeries.map
          (IsLocalRing.residue
            ↑((TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ E) E).presheaf.stalk x₀)))
        ((TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.verticalPowerSeries x₀ w₀) f) ≠
      0)
  (g :
    ↑((TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ (E × ℂ)) (E × ℂ)).presheaf.stalk
        (x₀, w₀))) :
  ∃! qr,
    ((TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.verticalPowerSeries x₀ w₀) g).IsWeierstrassDivision
      ((TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.verticalPowerSeries x₀ w₀) f)
      ((TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.verticalPowerSeries x₀ w₀) qr.1) qr.2
TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.exists.doc:
**Weierstrass division theorem in holomorphic stalks.** Given germs `f` and `g` at `(x₀, w₀)`
such that the vertical power series of `f` has nonzero image in `(𝒪_{E, x₀} ⧸ 𝔪_{x₀})⟦X⟧`, there
exist unique `q ∈ 𝒪_{E × ℂ, (x₀, w₀)}` and `r ∈ (𝒪_{E, x₀})[X]` forming a Weierstrass division of
`g` by `f`.

TauCeti.holderWith_of_contDiff_of_finran.signature:
TauCeti.holderWith_of_contDiff_of_finrank_lt.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  [BorelSpace E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E}
  [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] {u : E → F} {p : NNReal} [CompleteSpace F] (hu : ContDiff ℝ 1 u)
  (hp : ↑(Module.finrank ℝ E) < p) (hDu : MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (fderiv ℝ u) (↑p) μ ≠ ⊤) :
  HolderWith
    ((2 ^ (Module.finrank ℝ E + 1) / (↑(Module.finrank ℝ E) * μ.real (Metric.ball 0 1)) *
            (↑(Module.finrank ℝ E) * μ.real (Metric.ball 0 1) * (↑p - 1) /
                (↑p - ↑(Module.finrank ℝ E))) ^
              (1 - 1 / ↑p) *
          2 ^ (1 - ↑(Module.finrank ℝ E) / ↑p)).toNNReal *
      (MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (fderiv ℝ u) (↑p) μ).toNNReal)
    (1 - ↑(Module.finrank ℝ E) / p) u
TauCeti.holderWith_of_contDiff_of_finran.doc:
**Morrey's inequality, Hölder form.** If `u` is `C¹` on the whole space, `p` exceeds the
dimension `n` of the space, and the derivative of `u` lies in `Lᵖ`, then `u` is Hölder continuous
of exponent `1 - n / p`, with constant
`2 ^ (n + 1) / (n ω) * K ^ (1 - 1 / p) * 2 ^ (1 - n / p) * ‖Du‖_{Lᵖ}`, where `ω = μ(B(0, 1))`
and `K = n ω (p - 1) / (p - n)`.

TauCeti.holderWith_heatDuhamelPotential.doc:
**The value-field parabolic Hölder estimate for the Duhamel potential.** If the forcing
is jointly measurable and its spatial slices on `[0,T]` are bounded by `M` and `α`-Hölder with
constant `H`, where `0 < α ≤ 2`, then its Duhamel potential is parabolically `α`-Hölder on the
closed slab, with constant `T H (1 + M_α) + M max(1,T)`. Here `M_α` is the heat-kernel moment.
No temporal continuity of the forcing is assumed.

TauCeti.holderWith_heatCauchyPotential.doc:
**The parabolic Hölder estimate of the Cauchy heat potential.** If `g` is continuous and
`α`-Hölder with constant `H`, its Cauchy potential is `α`-Hölder on parabolic space-time, whose
distance is `‖x - x'‖ + √|t - s|`, with constant `H (1 + M_α)`. Here
`M_α = ∫ ‖y‖^α K_1(y) dy` is `TauCeti.heatKernelMoment`, which depends only on `α` and the
dimension. Continuity is automatic when `α > 0` (`HolderWith.continuous`).

TauCeti.hilbertSymbol_productFormula.signature:
TauCeti.hilbertSymbol_productFormula.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K] (a b : Kˣ) :
  (∏ᶠ (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)),
        TauCeti.hilbertSymbol (v.unitAtFinitePlace a) (v.unitAtFinitePlace b)) *
      ∏ w, TauCeti.hilbertSymbol ((TauCeti.unitAtRealPlace w) a) ((TauCeti.unitAtRealPlace w) b) =
    1
TauCeti.hilbertSymbol_productFormula.doc:
**Hilbert's product formula.** For `a, b ∈ Kˣ` in a number field `K`, the product of the
norm-equation Hilbert symbols `(a_v, b_v)_v` over the finite places and of the real Hilbert symbols
`(a_w, b_w)_w` over the real places of `K` is `1`.

TauCeti.hilbertSymbol_padicTwo.signature:
TauCeti.hilbertSymbol_padicTwo {a b : ℚ_[2]ˣ} {α β : ℤ} {u v : ℤ_[2]ˣ} (ha : ↑a = 2 ^ α * ↑↑u)
  (hb : ↑b = 2 ^ β * ↑↑v) :
  TauCeti.hilbertSymbol a b =
    (-1) ^
      (TauCeti.serreEps u * TauCeti.serreEps v + ↑α * TauCeti.serreOmega v +
        ↑β * TauCeti.serreOmega u)
TauCeti.hilbertSymbol_padicTwo.doc:
**Serre's formula for the Hilbert symbol over `ℚ_2`.** For `a = 2 ^ α u` and `b = 2 ^ β v`
with `u, v` units of `ℤ_2`,

`(a, b) = (-1) ^ (ε(u) ε(v) + α ω(v) + β ω(u))`,

with the exponent computed in `ZMod 2`.

TauCeti.hilbertSymbolForm.signature:
TauCeti.hilbertSymbolForm.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [ValuativeRel K] [TopologicalSpace K]
  [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] [Invertible 2] :
  LinearMap.BilinForm (ZMod 2) (TauCeti.SquareClassGroup K)
TauCeti.hilbertSymbolForm.doc:
**The Hilbert symbol as a bilinear form over `𝔽₂`.** Over a nonarchimedean local field in which
`2` is invertible, the Hilbert symbol on square classes, read in `ZMod 2` through the dictionary
`+1 ↦ 0`, `-1 ↦ 1`, is a `ZMod 2`-bilinear form on `Kˣ/(Kˣ)²`. Its sign is the symbol
(`TauCeti.hilbertSign_hilbertSymbolForm`).

TauCeti.hilbertBasisOfWeightedMeasure.signature:
TauCeti.hilbertBasisOfWeightedMeasure.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {α : Type u_2}
  [MeasurableSpace α] (f : ℕ → α → ℝ) (w : α → ℝ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α}
  (hwnn : ∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂μ, 0 ≤ w x) (hwm : AEMeasurable w μ) (hc : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < c n)
  (horth : ∀ (m n : ℕ), ∫ (x : α), f m x * f n x * w x ∂μ = if m = n then c n else 0)
  (hmem :
    ∀ (n : ℕ),
      MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun x => (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (f n x / √(c n))) 2
        (μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x)))
  (hcomplete : (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range (TauCeti.bareNormalizedLp f w c hmem)))ᗮ = ⊥) :
  HilbertBasis ℕ 𝕜 ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp 𝕜 2 (μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x)))
TauCeti.hilbertBasisOfWeightedMeasure.doc:
**The weighted-measure basis.** The normalized bare functions, orthonormal by the
orthogonality relation and complete by hypothesis, form a Hilbert basis of `L²(w·μ)` — the textbook
statement that a family of orthogonal functions is an orthonormal basis of its own weighted `L²`
space.

TauCeti.hilbert90.signature:
TauCeti.hilbert90.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] :
  CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero
    (continuousCohomology 1
      (TauCeti.ofDiscreteModule ℤ (TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup K) (TauCeti.UnitsCoeff K)))
TauCeti.hilbert90.doc:
**Hilbert 90 for the absolute Galois group**, stated for Mathlib's canonical continuous
cohomology: `H¹(G_K, (Kˢ)ˣ) = 0` (NSW (6.2.1)). This is the form in which the vanishing feeds
the canonical all-degree theory, where it makes the Kummer map `Kˣ → H¹(G_K, μₙ)` surjective for
`n` positive and invertible in `K`.

TauCeti.hermiteHilbertBasis.signature:
TauCeti.hermiteHilbertBasis.{u_1} (𝕜 : Type u_1) [RCLike 𝕜] :
  HilbertBasis ℕ 𝕜 ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp 𝕜 2 MeasureTheory.volume)
TauCeti.hermiteHilbertBasis.doc:
**The Hermite functions are a Hilbert basis of `L²(ℝ)`.** Orthonormality comes from the
weighted-measure machinery and completeness from moment determinacy
(`TauCeti.orthogonal_span_range_bareNormalizedLp_eq_bot`), applied to the exact-degree family
`Hₙ(x√2)` against the Gaussian weight `e^{-x²}`.

TauCeti.hermiteAnnihilationCLM_comp_herm.signature:
TauCeti.hermiteAnnihilationCLM_comp_hermiteCreationCLM_sub_hermiteCreationCLM_comp_hermiteAnnihilationCLM :
  TauCeti.hermiteAnnihilationCLM ∘SL TauCeti.hermiteCreationCLM -
      TauCeti.hermiteCreationCLM ∘SL TauCeti.hermiteAnnihilationCLM =
    ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (SchwartzMap ℝ ℝ)
TauCeti.hermiteAnnihilationCLM_comp_herm.doc:
**Canonical Commutation Relation (CCR) for the Hermite ladder operators.**
`[a, a†] = a ∘L a† - a† ∘L a = id`.

TauCeti.heatSemigroup_sub_eq_integral.signature:
TauCeti.heatSemigroup_sub_eq_integral.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  [BorelSpace E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [CompleteSpace F] {p : ENNReal}
  [Fact (1 ≤ p)] {φ : E → F} (hp : p ≠ ⊤) (hφ : ContDiff ℝ 2 φ) (hc : HasCompactSupport φ)
  {f g : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp F p MeasureTheory.volume)} (hf : ↑↑f =ᵐ[MeasureTheory.volume] φ)
  (hg : ↑↑g =ᵐ[MeasureTheory.volume] Laplacian.laplacian φ) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
  ((TauCeti.heatSemigroup hp).realOperator t) f - f =
    ∫ (s : ℝ) in Set.Ioc 0 t, ((TauCeti.heatSemigroup hp).realOperator s) g
TauCeti.heatSemigroup_sub_eq_integral.doc:
**Duhamel's formula for the heat semigroup.** Let `φ` be of class `C²` with compact support,
and let `f, g ∈ Lᵖ` be the classes of `φ` and `Δ φ`. Then for `t > 0`,
`e^{tΔ} f - f = ∫₀ᵗ e^{sΔ} g ds` as `Lᵖ`-valued integrals.

TauCeti.heatSemigroupBUC_sub_eq_integral.doc:
**Duhamel's identity in supremum norm.** For bounded uniformly continuous `C²` data `f`
with bounded first and second derivatives and bounded uniformly continuous Laplacian `g`,
`e^{tΔ} f - f = ∫₀ᵗ e^{sΔ} g ds` as a Banach-valued integral.

TauCeti.heatKernel_convolution_sub_eq_in.signature:
TauCeti.heatKernel_convolution_sub_eq_integral.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F]
  [NormedSpace ℝ F] {t : ℝ} [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [CompleteSpace F] {φ : E → F}
  (hφ : ContDiff ℝ 2 φ) (hc : HasCompactSupport φ) (ht : 0 < t) (x : E) :
  MeasureTheory.convolution (TauCeti.heatKernel t) φ (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ)
        MeasureTheory.volume x -
      φ x =
    ∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t,
      MeasureTheory.convolution (TauCeti.heatKernel s) (Laplacian.laplacian φ)
        (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) MeasureTheory.volume x
TauCeti.heatKernel_convolution_sub_eq_in.doc:
**Duhamel's formula for the heat equation.** For `φ` of class `C²` with compact support and
`t > 0`, `(K_t ⋆ φ)(x) - φ(x) = ∫₀ᵗ (K_s ⋆ Δ φ)(x) ds` at every point `x`.

TauCeti.heatDuhamelPotential_eq_integral.signature:
TauCeti.heatDuhamelPotential_eq_integral.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  [BorelSpace E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [CompleteSpace F] {f : ℝ → E → F}
  {M t : ℝ} {H α : NNReal} (hf : MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable (Function.uncurry f))
  (hfM : ∀ᵐ (s : ℝ) ∂MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ioo 0 t), ∀ᵐ (y : E), ‖f s y‖ ≤ M)
  (hH : ∀ᵐ (s : ℝ) ∂MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ioo 0 t), HolderWith H α (f s)) (hα : 0 < α)
  (ht : 0 ≤ t) (x : E) :
  TauCeti.heatDuhamelPotential f t x =
    ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..t, Laplacian.laplacian (TauCeti.heatDuhamelPotential f σ) x + f σ x
TauCeti.heatDuhamelPotential_eq_integral.doc:
**Duhamel's principle in integrated form.** Let `f` be jointly measurable and essentially
bounded on `(0, t) × E`, with `f(s, ·)` `α`-Hölder for almost every `0 < s < t`, where `α > 0`.
Then the Duhamel potential `w` satisfies `w(t, x) = ∫₀ᵗ (Δw(σ, x) + f(σ, x)) dσ`.

TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder_onIoi.signature:
TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder_onIoi (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
  TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f ↔ ∃ μ, TauCeti.RepresentsLaplaceOnIoi μ f
TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder_onIoi.doc:
**The Hausdorff--Bernstein--Widder theorem on the open half-line.** A function is completely
monotone on `(0, ∞)` if and only if it is the Laplace transform of a positive measure on `ℝ≥0`,
integrable against the exponential kernel at every positive parameter.

Compare `TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder`, which adds continuity at `0` to the hypotheses and
gets a *finite* measure in return.

TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder_diffe.signature:
TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder_difference (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
  TauCeti.IsDifferenceCompletelyMonotone f ∧ ContinuousWithinAt f (Set.Ici 0) 0 ↔
    ∃ μ, TauCeti.RepresentsLaplace μ f
TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder_diffe.doc:
**The Hausdorff--Bernstein--Widder theorem in finite-difference form.** A function has
alternating mixed forward differences and is right-continuous at zero if and only if it is the
Laplace transform of a finite positive measure on `ℝ≥0`.

Compare `TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder`, which states the same representation equivalence
using the derivative-based complete-monotonicity hypothesis.

TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder.signature:
TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
  TauCeti.IsContinuousCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f ↔ ∃ μ, TauCeti.RepresentsLaplace μ f
TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder.doc:
**Hausdorff--Bernstein--Widder theorem**, finite-measure version on `ℝ≥0`.

A function is continuous on `[0, ∞)` and completely monotone on `(0, ∞)` if and only if it is
the Laplace transform of a finite positive measure on `ℝ≥0`.

TauCeti.hausdorffMeasure_image_eq_zero_o.signature:
TauCeti.hausdorffMeasure_image_eq_zero_of_iteratedFDeriv_eq_zero.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1}
  {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
  {f : E → F} {k : ℕ} {s : Set E} [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F]
  {U : Set E} [Nontrivial E] (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : ContDiffOn ℝ (↑k) f U) (hsU : s ⊆ U) (hk : 0 < k)
  (hzero : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ (i : ℕ), 1 ≤ i → i ≤ k → iteratedFDeriv ℝ i f x = 0) :
  (MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure (↑(Module.finrank ℝ E) / ↑k)) (f '' s) = 0
TauCeti.hausdorffMeasure_image_eq_zero_o.doc:
**Sard's lemma on the flat stratum, in Hausdorff measure.** Let `f` be `C^k` on an open set
`U` of a nontrivial finite-dimensional real normed space, with `0 < k`, and let `s ⊆ U` be a set
at each point of which every iterated derivative of order `1 ≤ i ≤ k` vanishes. Then `f '' s` has
`finrank ℝ E / k`-dimensional Hausdorff measure zero.

TauCeti.hasSum_sq_frequency_mul_sq_fouri.signature:
TauCeti.hasSum_sq_frequency_mul_sq_fourierCoeffOn {a b : ℝ} {f f' : ℝ → ℂ} (hab : a < b)
  (hf : AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval f a b)
  (hff' : ∀ᵐ (t : ℝ), t ∈ Set.uIoc a b → HasDerivAt f (f' t) t) (hfab : f a = f b)
  (hf' : MeasureTheory.MemLp f' 2 (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ioc a b))) :
  HasSum (fun n => (2 * Real.pi * ↑n / (b - a)) ^ 2 * ‖fourierCoeffOn hab f n‖ ^ 2)
    ((b - a)⁻¹ * ∫ (t : ℝ) in a..b, ‖f' t‖ ^ 2)
TauCeti.hasSum_sq_frequency_mul_sq_fouri.doc:
**Parseval's energy identity** for an absolutely continuous closed complex curve with
square-integrable derivative. Each frequency contributes its squared frequency times the
squared norm of the corresponding Fourier coefficient.

TauCeti.hasSum_chebyshevT_expansion.signature:
TauCeti.hasSum_chebyshevT_expansion.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜]
  (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp 𝕜 2 Polynomial.Chebyshev.measureT)) :
  HasSum
    (fun n =>
      (∫ (x : ℝ),
          (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (TauCeti.normalizedChebyshevT n x) *
            ↑↑f x ∂Polynomial.Chebyshev.measureT) •
        TauCeti.normalizedChebyshevTLp 𝕜 n)
    f
TauCeti.hasSum_chebyshevT_expansion.doc:
**The Chebyshev expansion.** Every `f ∈ L²(measureT)` is the sum of its normalized
Chebyshev-polynomial series.

TauCeti.hasPrekopaLeindler_volume.doc:
The **Prékopa–Leindler inequality** on a finite-dimensional real inner product space, such as
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`: its volume has the Prékopa–Leindler property at every weight
`0 ≤ θ ≤ 1`.

TauCeti.hasLaurentSeriesOnAnnulus_of_dif.doc:
**Laurent's theorem on an open concentric annulus (with countable exceptional set).**
Let `0 ≤ r` and `r < ρ` with `ENNReal.ofReal ρ < R` (allowing `r = 0` for punctured disks and
`R = ⊤` for exteriors of closed disks or `ℂ \ {c}`). If `f : ℂ → E` is continuous on the open
annulus `Metric.eball c R \ Metric.closedBall c r` and complex-differentiable outside a countable
set `s`, then `f` has the convergent Laurent series with coefficients `circleLaurentCoeff f c ρ`
throughout `Metric.eball c R \ Metric.closedBall c r`.

TauCeti.hasFoelnerSets_iff_not_paradoxic.signature:
TauCeti.hasFoelnerSets_iff_not_paradoxical_univ.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] :
  TauCeti.HasFoelnerSets G ↔ ¬TauCeti.Paradoxical G Set.univ
TauCeti.hasFoelnerSets_iff_not_paradoxic.doc:
**Tarski's alternative**, topology-free form: a group has Følner sets exactly when it is not
paradoxical for its left regular action.

TauCeti.hasFoelnerSets_iff.signature:
TauCeti.hasFoelnerSets_iff.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [DecidableEq G] :
  TauCeti.HasFoelnerSets G ↔
    ∀ (K : Finset G) (ε : ℝ),
      0 < ε → ∃ F, F.Nonempty ∧ ∀ g ∈ K, ↑(symmDiff (g • F) F).card < ε * ↑F.card
TauCeti.hasFoelnerSets_iff.doc:
A group has Følner sets exactly when for every finite `K ⊆ G` and every `ε > 0` there is a
finite nonempty `F ⊆ G` with `|gF △ F| < ε · |F|` for all `g ∈ K`.

TauCeti.hasFDerivAt_timeDeriv_of_continu.signature:
TauCeti.hasFDerivAt_timeDeriv_of_continuousWithinAt.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] {u : E → ℝ → F}
  {v w : E → ℝ → E →L[ℝ] F} {g : E → F} {s : Set ℝ} {x : E} {t : ℝ} (hs : Convex ℝ s) (ht : t ∈ s)
  (hst : UniqueDiffWithinAt ℝ s t)
  (hv : ∀ᶠ (p : E × ℝ) in nhds x ×ˢ nhdsWithin t s, HasFDerivAt (fun x => u x p.2) (v p.1 p.2) p.1)
  (hw : ∀ᶠ (p : E × ℝ) in nhds x ×ˢ nhdsWithin t s, HasDerivWithinAt (v p.1) (w p.1 p.2) s p.2)
  (hwc : ContinuousWithinAt (fun p => w p.1 p.2) (Set.univ ×ˢ s) (x, t))
  (hg : ∀ᶠ (y : E) in nhds x, HasDerivWithinAt (u y) (g y) s t) : HasFDerivAt g (w x t) x
TauCeti.hasFDerivAt_timeDeriv_of_continu.doc:
**Peano's theorem on mixed partial derivatives**, differentiating a time derivative in space.
Let `u : E → ℝ → F`, let `s ⊆ ℝ` be convex, and let `t ∈ s` be a point at which derivatives within
`s` are unique. Suppose that near `x` in space and near `t` within `s`, the spatial derivative of
`u(·, τ)` at `y` is `v(y, τ)`, and that `v(y, ·)` has time derivative `w(y, τ)` within `s`, with
`w` jointly continuous at `(x, t)`. If `g y` is the time derivative of `u(y, ·)` within `s` at `t`
for every `y` near `x`, then `g` is differentiable at `x` with derivative `w(x, t)`: the spatial
derivative of `∂ₜu` exists and equals `∂ₜ D_y u`.

TauCeti.hasDerivWithinAt_spatialDeriv_of.doc:
**Peano's theorem on mixed partial derivatives**, differentiating a spatial derivative in
time. Let `u : E → ℝ → F`, let `s ⊆ ℝ` be convex, and let `t ∈ s`. Suppose that `v τ` is the
spatial derivative of `u(·, τ)` at `x` for `τ ∈ s` near `t`, and that near `x` in space and near
`t` within `s`, `u(y, ·)` has time derivative `g(y, τ)` within `s`, whose spatial derivative is
`w(y, τ)`, with `w` jointly continuous at `(x, t)`. Then `v` has time derivative `w(x, t)` within
`s` at `t`: the time derivative of `D_y u` exists and equals `D_y ∂ₜu`.

TauCeti.hasDerivAt_noetherCharge.signature:
TauCeti.hasDerivAt_noetherCharge.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  {L : ℝ → E × E → ℝ} {ξ : ℝ × E → E} {B : ℝ × E → ℝ} {q v : ℝ → E} {t : ℝ}
  (hq : HasDerivAt q (v t) t)
  (hEL :
    HasDerivAt (fun s => fderiv ℝ (fun u => L s (q s, u)) (v s))
      (fderiv ℝ (fun y => L t (y, v t)) (q t)) t)
  (hL : DifferentiableAt ℝ (L t) (q t, v t)) (hξ : DifferentiableAt ℝ ξ (t, q t))
  (hB : DifferentiableAt ℝ B (t, q t))
  (hsym : TauCeti.lagrangianVariation L ξ t (q t, v t) = (fderiv ℝ B (t, q t)) (1, v t)) :
  HasDerivAt (fun s => TauCeti.noetherCharge L ξ B s (q s, v s)) 0 t
TauCeti.hasDerivAt_noetherCharge.doc:
**Noether's theorem**, pointwise in time. Let `q` have velocity `v t` at `t` and satisfy the
Euler–Lagrange equation `d/dt ∂_v L(t, q, v) = ∂_q L(t, q, v)` there. If at `t` the infinitesimal
variation of `L` under `ξ` is the total time derivative `DB_(t, q)(1, v)` of the gauge term `B`
along the curve, then the Noether charge has derivative zero at `t`.

TauCeti.hasContinuousLogOn_sub_div_sub_i.signature:
TauCeti.hasContinuousLogOn_sub_div_sub_iff {K : Set ℂ} {a b : ℂ} (hK : IsClosed K)
  (hKb : Bornology.IsBounded K) :
  TauCeti.HasContinuousLogOn (fun z => (z - a) / (z - b)) K ↔ b ∈ connectedComponentIn Kᶜ a
TauCeti.hasContinuousLogOn_sub_div_sub_i.doc:
**The Borsuk criterion.** For two points outside a bounded closed set `K ⊆ ℂ`, the Borsuk map
`z ↦ (z - a) / (z - b)` has a continuous logarithm on `K` exactly when `K` fails to separate the
two points; both sides already force `a` and `b` outside `K`. The easy direction is
`TauCeti.hasContinuousLogOn_sub_div_sub`, the hard one
`TauCeti.mem_connectedComponentIn_of_hasContinuousLogOn`.

TauCeti.hasCentralRadical_iff_isCompl_ce.signature:
TauCeti.hasCentralRadical_iff_isCompl_center_derivedSeries.{u, v} (K : Type u) (L : Type v)
  [Field K] [CharZero K] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] :
  LieAlgebra.HasCentralRadical K L ↔
    IsCompl (LieAlgebra.center K L) (LieAlgebra.derivedSeries K L 1) ∧
      LieAlgebra.IsSemisimple K ↥(LieAlgebra.derivedSeries K L 1)
TauCeti.hasCentralRadical_iff_isCompl_ce.doc:
**The structure theorem for reductive Lie algebras.** Over a field of characteristic zero, a
finite-dimensional Lie algebra is reductive (its solvable radical is its centre) if and only if it
is the direct sum of its centre and its derived ideal, with the derived ideal semisimple.

The reverse implication only uses the second conjunct: semisimplicity of the derived ideal alone
implies reductivity, through `TauCeti.hasCentralRadical_of_hasTrivialRadical_derivedSeries`, and
hence the first conjunct. The first conjunct alone is not enough: the semidirect product
`sl₂ ⋉ K²` with the standard module has trivial centre and is its own derived ideal, so it
satisfies the first conjunct without being reductive.

TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_perronSolution.signature:
TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_perronSolution.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {Ω : Set E} {g : E → ℝ} [MeasurableSpace E]
  [BorelSpace E] (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hb : Bornology.IsBounded Ω) (hg : BddAbove (g '' frontier Ω))
  (hne : (TauCeti.perronFamily Ω g).Nonempty) :
  InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd (TauCeti.perronSolution Ω g) Ω
TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_perronSolution.doc:
**Perron's theorem.** Let `Ω` be a bounded open set, let `g` be bounded above on
`frontier Ω`, and suppose the Perron family of `g` is nonempty. Then the Perron solution
`TauCeti.perronSolution Ω g` is harmonic in `Ω`.

In Perron's setting of bounded boundary data the family is nonempty by
`TauCeti.perronFamily_nonempty`.

TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_iff_weaklyHarmonic.doc:
**Weyl's lemma for continuous functions.** A function continuous on the open set `Ω` is
harmonic on `Ω` if and only if it is weakly harmonic there: `∫ Δφ • u ∂μ = 0` for every test
function `φ ∈ 𝓓(Ω)`.

TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_iSup_of_monotone.signature:
TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_iSup_of_monotone.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {ι : Type u_2} [SemilatticeSup ι] [Nonempty ι]
  {F : ι → E → ℝ} {U : Set E} (hU : IsOpen U) (hUc : IsPreconnected U)
  (hF : ∀ (i : ι), InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd (F i) U)
  (hmono : ∀ x ∈ U, Monotone fun i => F i x) {x₀ : E} (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ U)
  (hbdd : BddAbove (Set.range fun i => F i x₀)) :
  InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd (fun x => ⨆ i, F i x) U
TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_iSup_of_monotone.doc:
**The limit in Harnack's convergence theorem is harmonic.** Let `F` be a family of functions
harmonic on a preconnected open set `U`, monotone at each point of `U` and bounded above at some
point `x₀ ∈ U`. Then its pointwise supremum is harmonic on `U`.

TauCeti.harishChandraLinearIso.signature:
TauCeti.harishChandraLinearIso.{v} {K : Type} {L : Type v} [Field K] [CharZero K] [IsAlgClosed K]
  [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L] [LieAlgebra.IsKilling K L] [FiniteDimensional K L]
  {H : LieSubalgebra K L} [H.IsCartanSubalgebra] [LieModule.IsTriangularizable K (↥H) L]
  (b : (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H).Base) :
  ↥(Subalgebra.center K (UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra K L)) ≃ₐ[K] ↥(TauCeti.linearInvariants H)
TauCeti.harishChandraLinearIso.doc:
**The linear Harish-Chandra isomorphism** `Z(U(L)) ≃ₐ[K] S(H)^W`: the linear Harish-Chandra
projection `TauCeti.hcProjectionLinear b`, with its values in the Weyl invariants.

TauCeti.groupHomology.indIso_inv_comp_ma.signature:
TauCeti.groupHomology.indIso_inv_comp_map_counit_assoc.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G]
  [DecidableEq G] (S : Subgroup G) (B : Rep.{u, u, u} k G) (n : ℕ) {Z : ModuleCat k}
  (h : groupHomology B n ⟶ Z) :
  CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (groupHomology.indIso S (Rep.res S.subtype B) n).inv
      (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
        (groupHomology.map (MonoidHom.id G) ((Rep.indResAdjunction k S.subtype).counit.app B) n)
        h) =
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
      (groupHomology.map S.subtype (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id (Rep.res S.subtype B)) n) h
TauCeti.groupHomology.indIso_inv_comp_ma.doc:
**Corestriction through Shapiro's lemma.** For a `G`-representation `B`, the inverse of
Shapiro's isomorphism `Hₙ(G, Ind_S^G Res_S B) ≅ Hₙ(S, Res_S B)` followed by the map induced by the
counit `Ind_S^G Res_S B ⟶ B` of induction–restriction is corestriction
`Hₙ(S, Res_S B) ⟶ Hₙ(G, B)`.

TauCeti.groupHomology.indIso_inv_comp_ma.signature:
TauCeti.groupHomology.indIso_inv_comp_map_counit.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G]
  [DecidableEq G] (S : Subgroup G) (B : Rep.{u, u, u} k G) (n : ℕ) :
  CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (groupHomology.indIso S (Rep.res S.subtype B) n).inv
      (groupHomology.map (MonoidHom.id G) ((Rep.indResAdjunction k S.subtype).counit.app B) n) =
    groupHomology.map S.subtype (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id (Rep.res S.subtype B)) n
TauCeti.groupHomology.indIso_inv_comp_ma.doc:
**Corestriction through Shapiro's lemma.** For a `G`-representation `B`, the inverse of
Shapiro's isomorphism `Hₙ(G, Ind_S^G Res_S B) ≅ Hₙ(S, Res_S B)` followed by the map induced by the
counit `Ind_S^G Res_S B ⟶ B` of induction–restriction is corestriction
`Hₙ(S, Res_S B) ⟶ Hₙ(G, B)`.

TauCeti.groupHomology.indIso_inv.signature:
TauCeti.groupHomology.indIso_inv.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] [DecidableEq G]
  (S : Subgroup G) (A : Rep.{u, u, u} k ↥S) (n : ℕ) :
  (groupHomology.indIso S A n).inv =
    groupHomology.map S.subtype ((Rep.indResAdjunction k S.subtype).unit.app A) n
TauCeti.groupHomology.indIso_inv.doc:
**The inverse of Shapiro's isomorphism in homology is corestriction of the unit.** The
inverse of the isomorphism `Hₙ(G, Ind_S^G A) ≅ Hₙ(S, A)` of `groupHomology.indIso` is the
change-of-group map along `S ≤ G` induced by the unit `A ⟶ Res_S Ind_S^G A`, `a ↦ 1 ⊗ a`,
of induction–restriction. The `DecidableEq G` instance is the one used by Mathlib's `indIso`;
keeping it caller-supplied ensures that this equality rewrites the caller's isomorphism.

TauCeti.groupCohomologyOddEquivTorsionBy.signature:
TauCeti.groupCohomologyOddEquivTorsionBy (T : Type) [AddCommGroup T] (m : ℕ) [NeZero m] (i : ℕ)
  (hi : Odd i) :
  ↑(groupCohomology ((AddEquiv.refl T).cyclicRep ⋯) i) ≃ₗ[ℤ] ↥(Submodule.torsionBy ℤ T ↑m)
TauCeti.groupCohomologyOddEquivTorsionBy.doc:
**Odd-degree cohomology of the trivial action.** When `C_m` acts trivially on `T`, its
cohomology in odd degree is the `m`-torsion `T[m]`: the class of a norm-zero element `x`
corresponds to `x` itself.

TauCeti.groupCohomology.map_unit_comp_co.signature:
TauCeti.groupCohomology.map_unit_comp_coindIso_hom.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G]
  (S : Subgroup G) (B : Rep.{u, u, u} k G) (n : ℕ) :
  CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
      (groupCohomology.map (MonoidHom.id G) ((Rep.resCoindAdjunction k S.subtype).unit.app B) n)
      (groupCohomology.coindIso (Rep.res S.subtype B) n).hom =
    groupCohomology.map S.subtype (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id (Rep.res S.subtype B)) n
TauCeti.groupCohomology.map_unit_comp_co.doc:
**Restriction through Shapiro's lemma.** For a `G`-representation `B`, the map induced by the
unit `B ⟶ Coind_S^G Res_S B` of restriction–coinduction, followed by Shapiro's isomorphism, is
restriction `Hⁿ(G, B) ⟶ Hⁿ(S, Res_S B)`.

TauCeti.groupCohomology.map_resCoindToHo.signature:
TauCeti.groupCohomology.map_resCoindToHom_comp_coindIso_hom.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k]
  [Group G] (S : Subgroup G) (A : Rep.{u, u, u} k ↥S) {B : Rep.{u, u, u} k G}
  (f : Rep.res S.subtype B ⟶ A) (n : ℕ) :

      (groupCohomology.coindIso A n).hom =
    groupCohomology.map S.subtype f n
TauCeti.groupCohomology.map_resCoindToHo.doc:
**Shapiro's isomorphism on an adjunct.** For a `G`-representation `B` and a morphism
`f : Res_S B ⟶ A`, the map induced by the adjunct `B ⟶ Coind_S^G A` of `f`, followed by Shapiro's
isomorphism, is the change-of-group map `Hⁿ(G, B) ⟶ Hⁿ(S, A)` induced by `f` along `S ≤ G`.

TauCeti.groupCohomology.isZero_of_isZero.signature:
TauCeti.groupCohomology.isZero_of_isZero_sylow.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] [Finite G]

  (h :
    ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)],

TauCeti.groupCohomology.isZero_of_forall.signature:
TauCeti.groupCohomology.isZero_of_forall_isPGroup.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G]
  [Finite G] (A : Rep.{u, u, u} k G) {q : ℕ}
  (h₁ :
    ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (S : Subgroup G),
      IsPGroup p ↥S → CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (groupCohomology (Rep.res S.subtype A) (q + 1)))
  (h₂ :
    ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (S : Subgroup G),
      IsPGroup p ↥S → CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (groupCohomology (Rep.res S.subtype A) (q + 2)))
  (S : Subgroup G) (n : ℕ) :
  CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (groupCohomology (Rep.res S.subtype A) (n + 1))
TauCeti.groupCohomology.isZero_of_forall.doc:
**Tate's cohomological triviality criterion** for ordinary cohomology (Milne II 3.10). Let `G`
be a finite group and `A` a representation of `G`. If `H^{q+1}(S, A)` and `H^{q+2}(S, A)` vanish
for every subgroup `S` of `G` of prime-power order, then `Hⁿ⁺¹(S, A)` vanishes for every
subgroup `S` of `G` and every `n`.

TauCeti.groupCohomology.coindIso_hom_com.signature:
TauCeti.groupCohomology.coindIso_hom_comp_corestriction.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G]
  (S : Subgroup G) [S.FiniteIndex] (A : Rep.{u, u, u} k G) (n : ℕ) :
  CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (groupCohomology.coindIso (Rep.res S.subtype A) n).hom
      (TauCeti.groupCohomology.corestriction S A n) =
    groupCohomology.map (MonoidHom.id G) ((Rep.coindResAdjunction k S).counit.app A) n
TauCeti.groupCohomology.coindIso_hom_com.doc:
**Corestriction through Shapiro's lemma.** Precomposed with Shapiro's isomorphism
`Hⁿ(G, Coind_S^G Res_S A) ≅ Hⁿ(S, Res_S A)`, corestriction is the map induced by the trace
`Coind_S^G Res_S A ⟶ A`, the counit of `Rep.coindResAdjunction`.

TauCeti.groupCohomology.averagingHomotop.signature:
TauCeti.groupCohomology.averagingHomotopy.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] [Fintype G]
  [Invertible ↑(Fintype.card G)] (A : Rep.{u, u, u} k G) :
  Homotopy (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id (groupCohomology.inhomogeneousCochains A))
    (TauCeti.groupCohomology.averageCochainMap A)
TauCeti.groupCohomology.averagingHomotop.doc:
**The averaging contraction.** The identity of the complex of inhomogeneous cochains is
homotopic to the averaging projection onto the invariants placed in degree `0`, through the
homotopy whose component from degree `n + 1` to degree `n` is `(-1)^(n+1)` times the average

`L((m - 1) (y)_∞)`, so this is the case `F₀ = k(x)` of
`TauCeti.genus_le_one_add_finrank_mul_genus_sub_one_add_degree`.

and a unit `x` modulo `gcd(g, N / g)`. The cusp `γ • ∞` corresponds to the label of `γ`

local field `K` and `a ∈ Lˣ`, the Evens norm `N^{Ev}((a)) ∈ H²(G_K, 𝔽₂)`, taken along any

morphisms from the tensor product of the representatives of `S` and `T` to the representative of
`U`. Over an algebraically closed field, with finite-dimensional morphism spaces, it is the
multiplicity of `U` in `S ⊗ T` (`TauCeti.fusionCoeff_eq_simpleMultiplicities`).

elementary: it is the product of six block unipotent matrices,
`u ⊕ u⁻¹ = U(u) L(-u⁻¹) U(u) U(-1) L(1) U(-1)`.

class function with the restricted one.

`TauCeti.frobenius_reciprocity`, but no representation is involved here: the identity is a
double count over `G × G` and holds for arbitrary class functions.

the restricted character.

`TauCeti.ClassFunction.characterPairing`.  The hypothesis `hG` is what makes the normalizing factors
meaningful; it also supplies the invertibility of `Nat.card S`.

**Freudenthal's multiplicity formula.** Let `M` be a finite-dimensional module generated by a
highest weight vector of weight `λ`. Then for every linear form `μ` on the Cartan subalgebra,

`(⟨λ + ρ, λ + ρ⟩ - ⟨μ + ρ, μ + ρ⟩) · dim Mμ = 2 ∑_{α > 0} ∑_{j ≥ 1} dim M_{μ + jα} · ⟨μ + jα, α⟩`,

the inner sum running over the `α`-string above `μ` with the rung `μ` itself removed; the double
sum is `TauCeti.freudenthalRHS`.

`λ`; solved for `dim Mμ` it is `TauCeti.coeff_formalCharacter_eq_freudenthalRHS_div`.

and Remark 2). Let `r ∈ Φ(F)` be a relator of the free pro-`2` group on an odd number `n` of
generators presenting a Demushkin group. Then the image of the canonical character of `⟨X ∣ r⟩` is
`{±1}`, or `n ≥ 3` and the image is `{±1} × U^(f)` for some `f ≥ 2`. At rank one the image is
`{±1}`, the odd word at every level reading `x₁²` there.

free pro-`p` group `F` on a finite linearly ordered type with the same class `ρ ∈ gr_1(F)` and the
same exponent vector `v = exponentSum r`, and suppose that for every `m ≥ 1` each element of
`λ_{m+1}(F)` lying in the closed commutator subgroup `K` has class `δ_ρ(⟦ω⟧)` for a family

automorphism of `F` carries `r` to `w`.

relator, which keeps the deviations in `K` along the approximation. The hypothesis on the
corrections is the constrained form of the span statement that `Im δ_ρ` contains the class of
every element of `λ_{m+1}(F) ∩ K`; it is assumed here, not established.
