The free cumulant of a word is the sum over the noncrossing partitions `π` of its block
moments weighted by the Möbius function, `κ_s(a) = ∑_{π ∈ NC(s)} μ(π, 1_s) φ_π(a)`.

TauCeti.freeCumulant.signature:
TauCeti.freeCumulant.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {α : Type u_3} [LinearOrder α]
  [CommRing R] [Monoid A] (φ : A → R) (a : α → A) (s : Finset α) : R
TauCeti.freeCumulant.doc:
The *free cumulant* `κ_s(a)` of the word `(a_i)_{i ∈ s}`: the cumulant of the partition of
`s` into one part. For `s = Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)` with `n ≥ 1` this is the `n`-th free
cumulant `κ_n(a₁, …, aₙ)`; for `s = ∅` it is the meaningless value `1`.

TauCeti.fourier_twoPiHermiteFunctionLp.signature:
TauCeti.fourier_twoPiHermiteFunctionLp (n : ℕ) :
  FourierTransform.fourier (TauCeti.twoPiHermiteFunctionLp ℂ n) =
    (-Complex.I) ^ n • TauCeti.twoPiHermiteFunctionLp ℂ n
TauCeti.fourier_twoPiHermiteFunctionLp.doc:
**The Fourier eigenrelation for the unitary Fourier transform of `L²(ℝ; ℂ)`.** The `n`-th
rescaled Hermite function is an eigenvector of `MeasureTheory.Lp.fourierTransformₗᵢ` with
eigenvalue `(-i)ⁿ`.

TauCeti.fourier_twoPiHermiteFunction.signature:
TauCeti.fourier_twoPiHermiteFunction (n : ℕ) :
  (FourierTransform.fourier fun x => ↑(TauCeti.twoPiHermiteFunction n x)) = fun x =>
    (-Complex.I) ^ n * ↑(TauCeti.twoPiHermiteFunction n x)
TauCeti.fourier_twoPiHermiteFunction.doc:
**Fourier eigenfunction theorem.** For Mathlib's `exp (-2πixξ)` convention, the rescaled
Hermite function `Φₙ(x) = √(√(2π)) ψₙ(√(2π)x)` has eigenvalue `(-i)ⁿ`.

TauCeti.formalCharacter_mul_weylDenomina.doc:
**The Weyl character formula.** For a finite-dimensional module `M` generated by a highest
weight vector of weight `lam`, the formal character of `M` times the Weyl denominator is the Weyl
numerator of `lam`:
`ch M · ∏_{α>0} (1 - e^{-α}) = ∑_{w ∈ W} sgn(w) e^{w(lam + ρ) - ρ}`.

Both sides are alternating for the dot action and supported in `lam - Q⁺`, so
`TauCeti.formalCharacter_mul_weylDenominator_eq_of_forall_coeff_isDominantIntegral_eq` reduces the
identity to the coefficients at the dominant integral weights. There both sides are `1` at `lam`
and `0` elsewhere: on the left by the two coefficient computations above and
`coeff_formalCharacter_mul_weylDenominator_eq_one_of_isHighestWeightVector_of_lieSpan_eq_top`,
on the right because the dot orbit of a dominant integral weight is free and meets the dominant
integral weights only at `lam`.

Such an `M` is irreducible, by
`TauCeti.isIrreducible_of_isHighestWeightVector_of_lieSpan_eq_top`, so this is the character of
`L(lam)`; it is stated for `M` itself so that no identification with `L(lam)` is needed to use
it.

TauCeti.formalCharacter_coeff_eq_kostant.signature:
TauCeti.formalCharacter_coeff_eq_kostantMultiplicity.{u, v, w} {K : Type u} {L : Type v} [Field K]
  [CharZero K] [IsAlgClosed K] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L] [LieAlgebra.IsKilling K L]
  [FiniteDimensional K L] {H : LieSubalgebra K L} [H.IsCartanSubalgebra] {M : Type w}
  [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module K M] [LieRingModule L M] [LieModule K L M] [FiniteDimensional K M]
  [Fintype ↥(LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H).weylGroup]
  {b : (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H).Base} {lam : Module.Dual K ↥H} {v : M}
  (hv : TauCeti.IsHighestWeightVector b lam v) (hgen : LieSubmodule.lieSpan K L {v} = ⊤)
  (mu : Module.Dual K ↥H) :
  (TauCeti.formalCharacter K (↥H) M).coeff mu =
    (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H).kostantMultiplicity b lam mu
TauCeti.formalCharacter_coeff_eq_kostant.doc:
**Kostant's multiplicity formula**, read off the formal character: for a finite-dimensional
module generated by a highest weight vector of weight `lam`, the coefficient of `ch M` at `mu` is
`∑_{w ∈ W} sgn(w) P(w ⬝ lam - mu)`.

It is the Weyl character formula `ch M · Δ = N(lam)` read one coefficient at a time.

TauCeti.forall_reachableWithout_iff_exis.signature:
TauCeti.forall_reachableWithout_iff_exists_paths.{u, v} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v} {s t : V}
  [Finite V] [∀ (x y : V), Finite (Q x y)] (k : ℕ) :
  (∀ (F : Finset ((x : V) × (y : V) × Q x y)), F.card < k → TauCeti.ReachableWithout (↑F) s t) ↔
    ∃ P, (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧ Pairwise fun i j => (P i).arrows.Disjoint (P j).arrows
TauCeti.forall_reachableWithout_iff_exis.doc:
**Menger's theorem for arrow-disjoint directed paths, predicate form.** For vertices `s` and
`t` of a finite arrow family, `t` stays reachable from `s` after deleting any fewer than `k` arrows
exactly when there are `k` directed `s`–`t` paths, no two of which traverse a common arrow.

TauCeti.forall_reachableAvoiding_iff_exi.signature:
TauCeti.forall_reachableAvoiding_iff_exists_paths.{u, v} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v} {s t : V}
  [Finite V] (hst : s ≠ t) (hadj : IsEmpty (Q s t)) (k : ℕ) :
  (∀ (X : Finset V), s ∉ X → t ∉ X → X.card < k → TauCeti.ReachableAvoiding Q (↑X) s t) ↔
    ∃ P, (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧ Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)
TauCeti.forall_reachableAvoiding_iff_exi.doc:
**Menger's theorem for internally vertex-disjoint directed paths, predicate form.** Let `s ≠ t`
be vertices of an arrow family on a finite vertex type, with no arrow from `s` to `t`. Then `t`
stays reachable from `s` after deleting any fewer than `k` vertices other than `s` and `t` exactly
when there are `k` directed `s`–`t` paths pairwise sharing no vertex other than `s` and `t`.

TauCeti.forall_preprojectiveKoszulLeft_i.signature:
TauCeti.forall_preprojectiveKoszulLeft_injective_iff.{u, w} (k : Type w) [Field k] {V : Type u}
  {G : SimpleGraph V} [Finite V] (hG : G.Connected) (o : TauCeti.DoubledQuiver.Orientation G) :
  (∀ (v : TauCeti.DoubledQuiver.OrientedQuiver G o),
      Function.Injective ⇑(TauCeti.preprojectiveKoszulLeft k v)) ↔
    ¬∃ t, t.Valid ∧ Nonempty (G ≃g TauCeti.diagramGraph t.cartanMatrix)
TauCeti.forall_preprojectiveKoszulLeft_i.doc:
**The Koszulity dichotomy for preprojective algebras of oriented graphs**: for a connected
finite simple graph `G` and any orientation `o` of `G`, the left Koszul differential of
`Π_k(OrientedQuiver G o)` is injective at every vertex if and only if `G` is not isomorphic to the
diagram of any valid Dynkin type.

TauCeti.forall_not_isMixedSeparator_iff_.signature:
TauCeti.forall_not_isMixedSeparator_iff_exists_paths.{u, v} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v}
  {s t : V} [Finite V] [Fintype (Q s t)] (hst : s ≠ t) (k : ℕ) :
  (∀ (X : Finset V), X.card < k → ¬TauCeti.IsMixedSeparator X (TauCeti.arrowFinset Q s t) s t) ↔
    ∃ P,
      Function.Injective P ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k ⊕ Q s t), (P i).IsPath) ∧ Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)
TauCeti.forall_not_isMixedSeparator_iff_.doc:
**Menger's theorem for internally vertex-disjoint directed paths between possibly adjacent
terminals, predicate form.** Let `s ≠ t` be vertices of an arrow family on a finite vertex type,
with finitely many arrows from `s` to `t`. Then `t` stays reachable from `s` after deleting every
arrow from `s` to `t` and any fewer than `k` vertices other than `s` and `t` exactly when there is a
family of distinct directed `s`–`t` paths indexed by `Fin k ⊕ Q s t`, pairwise sharing no vertex
other than `s` and `t`.

TauCeti.forall_isNashAt_apply_iff_exists.signature:
TauCeti.forall_isNashAt_apply_iff_exists_isSemialgebraicOn.{u_1, u_2} {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2}
  [Fintype σ] [Fintype τ] {g : (σ → ℝ) → τ → ℝ} {x : σ → ℝ} :
  (∀ (i : τ), TauCeti.IsNashAt (fun y => g y i) x) ↔
    AnalyticAt ℝ g x ∧ ∃ U, IsOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ TauCeti.IsSemialgebraicOn g U
TauCeti.forall_isNashAt_apply_iff_exists.doc:
**The local Nash graph criterion for maps.** The coordinates of a map between
finite-dimensional coordinate spaces are Nash germs at `x` exactly when the map is analytic at `x`
and its graph is semialgebraic on some open semialgebraic neighbourhood of `x`.

TauCeti.forall_isDomain_and_isIntegrally.signature:
TauCeti.forall_isDomain_and_isIntegrallyClosed_iff_satisfiesSerreR_one_and_satisfiesSerreS_two.{u}
  {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
  (∀ (p : Ideal R) [inst : p.IsPrime],
      IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p)) ↔
    Ring.SatisfiesSerreR 1 R ∧ Module.SatisfiesSerreS 2 R R
TauCeti.forall_isDomain_and_isIntegrally.doc:
**Serre's criterion for normality.** A Noetherian ring is normal, that is, every localization
at a prime is an integrally closed domain, if and only if it satisfies `(R_1)` and `(S_2)`.
Stacks, Lemma 10.157.4 (031S).

TauCeti.forall_exists_reachableWithout_i.signature:
TauCeti.forall_exists_reachableWithout_iff_exists_paths.{u, v} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v}
  [Finite V] [∀ (x y : V), Finite (Q x y)] {A B : Finset V} (k : ℕ) :
  (∀ (F : Finset ((x : V) × (y : V) × Q x y)),
      F.card < k → ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, TauCeti.ReachableWithout (↑F) a b) ↔
    ∃ a b P,
      (∀ (i : Fin k), a i ∈ A) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), b i ∈ B) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
            (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ v ∈ (P i).vertices, v ≠ a i → v ≠ b i → v ∉ A ∧ v ∉ B) ∧
              Pairwise fun i j => (P i).arrows.Disjoint (P j).arrows
TauCeti.forall_exists_reachableWithout_i.doc:
**Menger's theorem for arrow-disjoint directed paths between vertex sets, predicate form.** Let
`A` and `B` be sets of vertices of a finite arrow family. After deleting any fewer than
`k` arrows, some vertex of `B` stays reachable from some vertex of `A` exactly when there are `k`
directed paths, each from a vertex of `A` to a vertex of `B` with its other vertices in neither `A`
nor `B`, no two of which traverse a common arrow.

TauCeti.forall_exists_reachableAvoiding_.signature:
TauCeti.forall_exists_reachableAvoiding_iff_exists_paths.{u, v} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v}
  [Finite V] (A B : Finset V) (k : ℕ) :
  (∀ (X : Finset V), X.card < k → ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, TauCeti.ReachableAvoiding Q (↑X) a b) ↔
    ∃ a b P,
      (∀ (i : Fin k), a i ∈ A) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), b i ∈ B) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
            (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ v ∈ (P i).vertices, v ≠ a i → v ≠ b i → v ∉ A ∧ v ∉ B) ∧
              Pairwise fun i j => (P i).vertices.Disjoint (P j).vertices
TauCeti.forall_exists_reachableAvoiding_.doc:
**Menger's theorem for vertex-disjoint directed paths between vertex sets, predicate form.** Let
`A` and `B` be sets of vertices of an arrow family on a finite vertex type. After deleting any fewer
than `k` vertices, some vertex of `B` stays reachable from some vertex of `A` exactly when there
are `k` pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths, each from a vertex of `A` to a vertex of `B` with
its other vertices in neither `A` nor `B`.

TauCeti.forall_exists_isLinear_zigzagGra.doc:
**The Koszulity dichotomy for zigzag algebras**: for a connected finite simple graph `G` on at
least two vertices, every graded vertex simple of `ZigzagAlgebra k G` admits a linear graded
projective resolution if and only if `G` is not isomorphic to the diagram of any valid Dynkin
type.

TauCeti.forall_exists_isLinear_iff_bigra.signature:
TauCeti.forall_exists_isLinear_iff_bigradedExtPoincareMatrix_isDiagonal.{uk, uA, uI} {k : Type uk}
  [Field k] {A : Type uA} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] {𝒜 : ℤ → Submodule k A} [GradedAlgebra 𝒜]
  [CategoryTheory.HasExt (TauCeti.GradedModuleCat 𝒜)] {I : Type uI} [IsSemisimpleRing ↥(𝒜 0)]
  [Module.Finite k A] (S : I → (TauCeti.gradedFiniteModules 𝒜).FullSubcategory)
  (hS : TauCeti.IsExhaustiveGradedSimpleFamily S)
  (hSzero : ∀ (i : I) (p : ℤ), p ≠ 0 → (S i).obj.grading.piece ℤ p = ⊥)
  (h :
    TauCeti.IsGradedEulerAdmissibleOn (TauCeti.gradedFiniteModules 𝒜)
      (TauCeti.gradedFiniteModules 𝒜))
  (hneg : ∀ p < 0, 𝒜 p = ⊥) {b : ℕ}
  (hb :
    ∀ (i j : I),
      TauCeti.IsGradedExtBoundedBy (TauCeti.GradedModuleCat.shift 𝒜) (S i).obj (S j).obj b) :
  (∀ (i : I), ∃ r, r.IsLinear) ↔
    ∀ (i j : I),
      TauCeti.Bigraded.IsDiagonal (TauCeti.bigradedExtPoincareMatrix (fun i => (S i).obj) ⋯ b i j)
TauCeti.forall_exists_isLinear_iff_bigra.doc:
**Bigraded Ext detects linear resolutions over a semisimple degree-zero part.** Suppose that
`A` is finite-dimensional and nonnegatively graded, with semisimple degree-zero part. For an
exhaustive family of finite simple modules concentrated in degree zero, every simple admits a
linear graded projective resolution if and only if every entry of the full bigraded Ext Poincare
matrix has diagonal support.

Unlike `TauCeti.forall_isLinear_iff_bigradedExtPoincareMatrix_isDiagonal`, this statement does not
take a preselected family of minimal resolutions: their existence, with finite-dimensional terms,
follows from semisimplicity of the degree-zero part.

TauCeti.flat_frobeniusRootIdeal.signature:
TauCeti.flat_frobeniusRootIdeal.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] {p : ℕ} [ExpChar R p]
  [PerfectRing R p] [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (f : R) :
  Module.Flat R ↥(TauCeti.frobeniusRootIdeal R p f)
TauCeti.flat_frobeniusRootIdeal.doc: **Frobenius-root ideals are flat**, also when `R` has zero divisors.

TauCeti.fixingSubgroup_discrField.signature:
TauCeti.fixingSubgroup_discrField.{u, v} {F : Type u} [Field F] {E : Type v} [Field E] [Algebra F E]
  {f : Polynomial F} [Fact (Polynomial.map (algebraMap F E) f).Splits] (hsep : f.Separable)
  (hchar : ringChar F ≠ 2) : (TauCeti.discrField f E).fixingSubgroup = TauCeti.evenAutSubgroup f E
TauCeti.fixingSubgroup_discrField.doc:
**The comparison theorem, from the other side.** Away from characteristic `2`, the
automorphisms of a splitting extension that fix the discriminant field of a separable
polynomial are exactly those acting on its roots by an even permutation. Unlike
`TauCeti.fixedField_evenAutSubgroup`, this needs no normality of the extension.

TauCeti.fixedField_evenAutSubgroup.signature:
TauCeti.fixedField_evenAutSubgroup.{u, v} {F : Type u} [Field F] {E : Type v} [Field E]
  [Algebra F E] {f : Polynomial F} [Fact (Polynomial.map (algebraMap F E) f).Splits] [IsGalois F E]
  (hsep : f.Separable) (hchar : ringChar F ≠ 2) :
  IntermediateField.fixedField (TauCeti.evenAutSubgroup f E) = TauCeti.discrField f E
TauCeti.fixedField_evenAutSubgroup.doc:
**The comparison theorem.** In a Galois splitting extension, and away from characteristic `2`,
the discriminant field of a separable polynomial is the field fixed by the automorphisms
acting on the roots by an even permutation.

TauCeti.finsum_traceResidue_kaehlerBasis.signature:
TauCeti.finsum_traceResidue_kaehlerBasisOfSeparating_coord_eq_zero.{u_1, u_2} {k : Type u_1}
  {F : Type u_2} [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F] [PerfectField k]
  (hF : TauCeti.IsFunctionField k F) (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F)
  [∀ (P : TauCeti.Place k F), Algebra.IsSeparable k P.ResidueField] (t : TauCeti.Place k F → F)
  (ht : ∀ (P : TauCeti.Place k F), P.ord (t P) = 1)
  [∀ (P : TauCeti.Place k F), Algebra.IsSeparable (↥k⟮t P⟯) F] (ω : Ω[F⁄k]) :
  have htr := ⋯;
  ∑ᶠ (P : TauCeti.Place k F),
      (P.traceResidue ⋯) (((TauCeti.kaehlerBasisOfSeparating ⋯).coord ()) ω) =
    0
TauCeti.finsum_traceResidue_kaehlerBasis.doc:
**The residue theorem over a perfect field** (Stichtenoth, Corollary 4.3.3 and
Remark 4.3.7(d)): over a perfect exact constant field, choose a prime element `t_P` at each place
`P`. Then the trace residues of a Kähler differential `ω` sum to zero,
`∑_P Tr_{F_P/k} res_{P,t_P} (ω / dt_P) = 0`, a sum with finitely many nonzero terms
(`TauCeti.finite_support_traceResidue_kaehlerBasisOfSeparating_coord`). This is the residue
theorem for Weil differentials `TauCeti.finsum_traceResidue_coord_eq_zero` at `u = 1`, applied to
the Weil differential attached to `ω`. Unlike `TauCeti.finsum_kaehlerResidueOfPerfectField_eq_zero`,
places of every degree contribute, so this applies over finite fields.

TauCeti.finsum_residue_adicOfIrreducible.signature:
TauCeti.finsum_residue_adicOfIrreducible_X_sub_C_of_isAlgClosed.{u_1} {k : Type u_1} [Field k]
  [IsAlgClosed k] (z : RatFunc k) :
  ∑ᶠ (a : k), ((TauCeti.Place.adicOfIrreducible ⋯).residue ⋯ ⋯) z =
    ((TauCeti.Place.infty k).residue ⋯ ⋯) (RatFunc.X ^ 2 * z)
TauCeti.finsum_residue_adicOfIrreducible.doc:
**The residue theorem for `k(x)` over an algebraically closed field** (Stichtenoth,
Corollary 4.3.3, for `k(x)`): `∑_{a ∈ k} res_{P_a, x - a} (z) = res_{P_∞, x⁻¹} (x² z)` for every
rational function `z`.

TauCeti.finsum_residue_adicOfIrreducible.signature:
TauCeti.finsum_residue_adicOfIrreducible_X_sub_C.{u_1} {k : Type u_1} [Field k] {z : RatFunc k}
  (hz : ∀ (P : TauCeti.Place k (RatFunc k)), P.degree ≠ 1 → z ∈ P.integers) :
  ∑ᶠ (a : k), ((TauCeti.Place.adicOfIrreducible ⋯).residue ⋯ ⋯) z =
    ((TauCeti.Place.infty k).residue ⋯ ⋯) (RatFunc.X ^ 2 * z)
TauCeti.finsum_residue_adicOfIrreducible.doc:
**The residue theorem for `k(x)`** (Stichtenoth, Corollary 4.3.3, for `k(x)`): if every pole
of `z` is a rational place, then the residues of `z dx` over `ℙ¹(k)` sum to zero, in the form
`∑_{a ∈ k} res_{P_a, x - a} (z) = res_{P_∞, x⁻¹} (x² z)`.

The hypothesis is needed: over `ℚ`, `z = 2x / (x² - 2)` is integral at every place `P_a`, so the
left side vanishes, while `res_{P_∞, x⁻¹} (x² z) = 2`; the missing residue sits at the place of
`x² - 2`, which has degree two.

TauCeti.finsum_repartitionDualComponent_.signature:
TauCeti.finsum_repartitionDualComponent_eq_zero.{u_1, u_2} {k : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [Field k]
  [Field F] [Algebra k F] (hF : TauCeti.IsFunctionField k F)
  {ω : Module.Dual k ↥(TauCeti.repartitionSpace k F)} (hω : ω ∈ TauCeti.weilDifferentialSpace k F)
  (x : F) : ∑ᶠ (P : TauCeti.Place k F), (TauCeti.repartitionDualComponent ω P) x = 0
TauCeti.finsum_repartitionDualComponent_.doc:
**The abstract residue theorem** (Stichtenoth, (1.45)): the local components of a Weil
differential sum to zero on every function of `F`.

The constant repartition of `x` lies in the diagonal copy of `F` inside `A_F`, on which every Weil
differential vanishes, and its entry at every place is `x`.  Stichtenoth states the case `x = 1`;
no hypothesis on the constant field `k` is needed, and no residue map has been constructed.

TauCeti.finsum_kaehlerResidueOfPerfectFi.doc:
**The residue theorem** (Stichtenoth, Corollary 4.3.3): over an algebraically closed field,
the residues of a Kähler differential `ω` at the places of `F` sum to zero,
`∑_P res_P (ω) = 0`. Every place is rational here, and only finitely many residues are nonzero
(`TauCeti.finite_support_kaehlerResidueOfPerfectField`).

Over a field that is not algebraically closed the rational places do not suffice: over `ℚ`, the
differential `2x / (x² - 2) dx` of `ℚ(x)` has residue zero at every rational place `x = a` and
residue `-2` at infinity; the missing residue sits at the place of `x² - 2`, which is not rational
(see `TauCeti.finsum_residue_adicOfIrreducible_X_sub_C`). Over a perfect field the trace residues
at the places of every degree sum to zero
(`TauCeti.finsum_traceResidue_kaehlerBasisOfSeparating_coord_eq_zero`).

TauCeti.finsum_finrank_singularHomology_.signature:
TauCeti.finsum_finrank_singularHomology_of_finite_cwComplex.{w} {X : Type w} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [T2Space X] (C : Set X) [Topology.CWComplex C] {k : Type w} [DivisionRing k] (M : ModuleCat k)
  [Module.Finite k ↑M] [Topology.RelCWComplex.Finite C] :
  ∑ᶠ (i : ℕ),
      (-1) ^ i *
        ↑(Module.finrank k
            ↑(((AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat k) i).obj M).obj ↧↑C)) =

TauCeti.finsum_finrank_singularHomology_.doc:
**Euler--Poincaré for ordinary singular homology.** For a finite CW complex with
finite-dimensional coefficients over a division ring, the alternating homology dimensions
equal the coefficient dimension times the alternating cell count.

TauCeti.finsum_finrank_singularHomology_.signature:
TauCeti.finsum_finrank_singularHomology_complexBasePair.{w} {X : Type w} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [T2Space X] {D : Set X} (C : Set X) [Topology.RelCWComplex C D] {k : Type w} [DivisionRing k]

TauCeti.finsum_finrank_singularHomology_.doc:
**Euler--Poincaré for relative singular homology.** For a finite relative CW complex,
the alternating sum of the dimensions of relative singular homology is the coefficient
dimension times the alternating count of relative cells. Both sums have finite support.

TauCeti.finrank_weightSpace_eq_kostantMu.signature:

Weyl module of a dominant weight `λ` has dimension `∏_{i < j} (λᵢ - λⱼ + j - i) / (j - i)`, the

```text
dim e_v Π_{m+2} e_i + dim e_v Π_m e_i = ∑_w #(w ⟶ v) dim e_w Π_{m+1} e_i + dim K_m(i, v),
```

the sum running over the arrows of the doubled quiver into `v`, where `K_m(i, v)` is the space of
`y ∈ e_v Π_m e_i` killed by the reverse `b*` of every arrow `b` into `v`, the kernel of the left
map of the Koszul complex of `S_v`.

null-measurable set `G` lies in a set `F` of finite volume, then in dimension `n ≥ 1`

      TauCeti.coweightPairing (lam + TauCeti.weylVector (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H) b) i
TauCeti.finrank_mul_prod_coweightPairing.doc:
**The Weyl dimension formula, division-free.** For a finite-dimensional module `M` generated
by a highest weight vector of weight `lam`,

`dim M · ∏_{α>0} ⟨ρ, α^∨⟩ = ∏_{α>0} ⟨lam + ρ, α^∨⟩`,

an identity of integers, the coroot pairings being those of the integral weights `ρ` and
`lam + ρ`.

TauCeti.finrank_mul_finrank_centralizer_.signature:
TauCeti.finrank_mul_finrank_centralizer_of_isSimpleRing_tensorProduct_mulOpposite.{u_1, u_2}
  {K : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} [Field K] [Ring A] [Nontrivial A] [Algebra K A]
  [FiniteDimensional K A] (B : Subalgebra K A) [IsSimpleRing (TensorProduct K (↥B) Aᵐᵒᵖ)] :
  Module.finrank K ↥B * Module.finrank K ↥(Subalgebra.centralizer K ↑B) = Module.finrank K A
TauCeti.finrank_mul_finrank_centralizer_.doc:
**The dimension count behind the centralizer theorem**, asking only for what it uses: that `A`
is finite-dimensional and nonzero over the field `K` — so that the factor of `finrank K A` cancelled
at the end is nonzero — and that the ring `R = B ⊗[K] Aᵐᵒᵖ` acting on `A` is simple. Then

  `finrank K B * finrank K C_A(B) = finrank K A`.

Simplicity of `R` is the only algebraic hypothesis on `B` and on `A`, and there is more than one way
to supply it: `TauCeti.finrank_mul_finrank_centralizer` has it from `B` central simple and `A`
simple, while `TauCeti.finrank_mul_finrank_centralizer_of_isField` has it from `B` a subfield and
`A` central simple.

TauCeti.finrank_mul_finrank_centralizer.signature:
TauCeti.finrank_mul_finrank_centralizer.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} [Field K] [Ring A]
  [Algebra K A] [IsSimpleRing A] [FiniteDimensional K A] (B : Subalgebra K A)
  [Algebra.IsCentral K ↥B] [IsSimpleRing ↥B] :
  Module.finrank K ↥B * Module.finrank K ↥(Subalgebra.centralizer K ↑B) = Module.finrank K A
TauCeti.finrank_mul_finrank_centralizer.doc:
**The centralizer theorem.** For a central simple `K`-subalgebra `B` of a finite-dimensional
simple `K`-algebra `A`, the dimensions of `B` and of its centralizer are complementary:

  `finrank K B * finrank K C_A(B) = finrank K A`.

This is the dimension count of
`TauCeti.finrank_mul_finrank_centralizer_of_isSimpleRing_tensorProduct_mulOpposite`, whose one
algebraic hypothesis — simplicity of `B ⊗[K] Aᵐᵒᵖ` — `IsSimpleRing.tensorProduct` supplies
from `B` central simple and `Aᵐᵒᵖ` simple.

TauCeti.finrank_linearMap_pi_eq_natCard.doc:
**The multiplicity theorem for a product of simple modules.**  The dimension of the space of
`A`-linear maps from a simple module `S` into a finite product of simple modules counts the
factors isomorphic to `S`.

TauCeti.finrank_linearMap_eq_zero_of_isE.signature:
TauCeti.finrank_linearMap_eq_zero_of_isEmpty_linearEquiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {k : Type u_1}
  {A : Type u_2} {S : Type u_3} {N : Type u_4} [CommSemiring k] [Nontrivial k] [Ring A]
  [Algebra k A] [AddCommGroup S] [_root_.Module A S] [IsSimpleModule A S] [AddCommGroup N]
  [_root_.Module k N] [_root_.Module A N] [IsScalarTower k A N] [IsSimpleModule A N]
  (h : IsEmpty (S ≃ₗ[A] N)) : Module.finrank k (S →ₗ[A] N) = 0
TauCeti.finrank_linearMap_eq_zero_of_isE.doc:
**Schur's lemma, vanishing form, in dimensions.**  Between inequivalent simple modules the
hom space is trivial, hence of dimension zero.

Schur's lemma is normally read with a field of scalars, but this half of it does not need one.
The conclusion is a statement about the zero module, whose `Module.finrank` vanishes over any
nontrivial commutative semiring, and that is all `k` is asked to be here. So the result is
available wherever the simple modules live over an algebra, without first arranging a field to
measure the hom space in.

TauCeti.finrank_linearMap_eq_natCard_of_.doc:
**The multiplicity theorem.**  If `M` decomposes as a finite direct sum of simple modules
`N i`, then the dimension of the space of `A`-linear maps from a simple module `S` into `M` is
the number of factors isomorphic to `S`.

Only the right-hand side mentions the decomposition, so this is the statement that the
multiplicity of `S` in `M` is an invariant of `M`; see
`TauCeti.natCard_eq_natCard_of_linearEquiv_pi`.

TauCeti.finrank_eq_prod_coweightPairing_.signature:
TauCeti.finrank_eq_prod_coweightPairing_div.{u, v, w} {K : Type u} {L : Type v} [Field K]
  [CharZero K] [IsAlgClosed K] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L] [LieAlgebra.IsKilling K L]
  [FiniteDimensional K L] {H : LieSubalgebra K L} [H.IsCartanSubalgebra] {M : Type w}
  [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module K M] [LieRingModule L M] [LieModule K L M] [FiniteDimensional K M]
  {b : (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H).Base} {lam : Module.Dual K ↥H} {v : M}
  (hv : TauCeti.IsHighestWeightVector b lam v) (hgen : LieSubmodule.lieSpan K L {v} = ⊤) :
  ↑(Module.finrank K M) =
    ∏ i ∈ TauCeti.posRootsFinset (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H) b,
      ↑(TauCeti.coweightPairing (lam + TauCeti.weylVector (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H) b)
            i) /
        ↑(TauCeti.coweightPairing (TauCeti.weylVector (LieAlgebra.IsKilling.rootSystem H) b) i)
TauCeti.finrank_eq_prod_coweightPairing_.doc:
**The Weyl dimension formula.** For a finite-dimensional module `M` generated by a highest
weight vector of weight `lam`,

`dim M = ∏_{α>0} ⟨lam + ρ, α^∨⟩ / ⟨ρ, α^∨⟩`,

the product running over the positive roots, with `ρ` the Weyl vector of the base and
`⟨·, α^∨⟩` the integer coroot pairing `TauCeti.coweightPairing`. Such an `M` is irreducible, so
this is the dimension of `L(lam)` for every dominant integral weight `lam` at which `L(lam)` is
nonzero.

TauCeti.finprod_hilbertSymbol_padic_mul_.doc:
**Hilbert's product formula over `ℚ`.** For `a, b ∈ ℚˣ`, the product over the primes `ℓ` of the
Hilbert symbols `(a, b)_ℓ` computed in `ℚ_ℓ`, times the Hilbert symbol `(a, b)_∞` computed in `ℝ`,
is `1`.

**Northcott's theorem for the Mahler measure.** In a field of characteristic zero, there are

TauCeti.finite_setOf_absMulHeight₁_le.signature:

**Northcott's theorem for the absolute height.** In a field of characteristic zero there are

TauCeti.finiteDimensional_preprojectiveA.signature:
TauCeti.finiteDimensional_preprojectiveAlgebra_orientedQuiver_iff.{u_1, u_2} (k : Type u_1)

TauCeti.finiteDimensional_preprojectiveA.doc:
**The finite/infinite dichotomy for preprojective algebras of oriented graphs**: for a
connected finite simple graph `G` and any orientation `o` of `G`, the preprojective algebra
`Π_k(OrientedQuiver G o)` is finite-dimensional over `k` if and only if `G` is isomorphic to the
diagram of a valid Dynkin type.

TauCeti.fibrationLocalSystem.signature:
TauCeti.fibrationLocalSystem.{u, u_1} {E B : Type u} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B]

`F'` of the Moore-path replacement, a right DG module over `C_*(Ω_b B; R)` through the strict

TauCeti.fenchelConjugate_innerₗ_fenchelC.doc:
**The Fenchel–Moreau theorem on a complete real inner product space.** A function
`f : G → EReal` with convex real epigraph that is lower semicontinuous and never takes the value
`⊥` is the conjugate of its conjugate for the inner product pairing.

TauCeti.fenchelConjugate_flip_fenchelCon.signature:

  {B : E →ₗ[ℝ] F →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ} (hB : ∀ (ℓ : E →L[ℝ] ℝ), ∃ y, ∀ (x : E), (B x) y = ℓ x)

TauCeti.fenchelConjugate_flip_fenchelCon.doc:
**The Fenchel–Moreau theorem, with its converse.** For a pairing `B` that represents every
continuous linear functional on `E` and makes every functional `x ↦ B x y` continuous, a function
`f : E → EReal` equals its biconjugate exactly when it has convex real epigraph, is lower
semicontinuous, and either never takes the value `⊥` or is identically `⊥`.

TauCeti.fenchelConjugate_flip_fenchelCon.signature:
TauCeti.fenchelConjugate_flip_fenchelConjugate_eq.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup E]

  [LocallyConvexSpace ℝ E] {f : E → EReal} {F : Type u_2} [AddCommGroup F] [_root_.Module ℝ F]

TauCeti.fenchelConjugate_flip_fenchelCon.doc:
**The Fenchel–Moreau theorem.** Let the pairing `B` represent every continuous linear
functional on the locally convex space `E`. If `f : E → EReal` has convex real epigraph, is lower
semicontinuous and never takes the value `⊥`, then `f` equals its biconjugate `f⋆⋆`, the second
conjugate being taken for the transposed pairing.

closed-ball maximum and the sphere has the corresponding weak inequality.

**Prokhorov's theorem along an ultrafilter, for measures carried by a compact set.** Finite
measures eventually carried by a compact set `K`, with mass eventually at most `C`, converge along
an ultrafilter to a finite measure carried by `K`.

containing a field whose maximal ideal `𝔪` is finitely generated has a coefficient field `s` and
is a quotient of the power series ring over its residue field in `spanFinrank 𝔪` variables, by a

complete local ring containing a field, and let a finite family `x` generate its maximal ideal.
Then `R` has a coefficient field `s`, and there is a surjective ring homomorphism from the power
series ring over the residue field onto `R` that is `s` on constants and sends each variable
`X i` to `x i`. Such a surjection exists for every coefficient field
(`MvPowerSeries.exists_surjective_ringHom_of_isAdicComplete`).

TauCeti.exists_sum_smul_norm_sub_lt_of_t.doc:
**Mazur's lemma**, with explicit finite coefficients: every tail of a weakly convergent
sequence admits a convex combination within any positive norm distance of its weak limit.

of natural numbers satisfying the strong Morse inequalities

`(cᵢ - cᵢ₋₁ + ⋯ ± c₀) - (bᵢ - bᵢ₋₁ + ⋯ ± b₀)` in the `i`-th strong inequality for `i < n`, and
zero for `i ≥ n`.

TauCeti.exists_signInvariant_mcCallumPro.signature:
TauCeti.exists_signInvariant_mcCallumProjection_stackCells_not_signInvariant
  (polynomialGCD : NormalizedGCDMonoid (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℝ)) :
  ∃ f S,
    {f}.IsSquarefreeBasis {f} ∧
      TauCeti.IsSemialgebraic S ∧
        TauCeti.IsAnalyticSubmanifold 1 S ∧
          IsConnected S ∧
            (∀ x ∈ S, Polynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval x) f ≠ 0) ∧
              (∀ q ∈ {f}.mcCallumProjection {f},
                  TauCeti.SignInvariant (fun x => (MvPolynomial.eval x) q) S) ∧
                (∃ q ∈ {f}.mcCallumProjection {f}, ∃ x ∈ S, ∃ y ∈ S, q.orderAt x ≠ q.orderAt y) ∧
                  ∀ (k : ℕ) (θ : Fin k → ↑S → ℝ),
                    (∀ (x : ↑S), StrictMono fun i => θ i x) →
                      ∃ E ∈ TauCeti.stackCells S θ,
                        ¬TauCeti.SignInvariant
                            (fun y =>
                              (MvPolynomial.eval y) ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv ℝ 2).symm f))
                            E
TauCeti.exists_signInvariant_mcCallumPro.doc:
**Sign-invariance of the McCallum projection does not suffice for lifting.** In
`Finset.IsSquarefreeBasis.exists_isSemialgebraicStack_signInvariant_of_mcCallumProjection`, the
hypothesis that the McCallum projection is order-invariant on the base cannot be weakened to
sign-invariance, even for a nonnullified squarefree basis over a connected semialgebraic
analytic submanifold. So a lower level of a CAD that is merely sign-invariant for the projection
cannot replace an order-invariant one.

Explicitly, let `f = (T - 1)² (T - 1 - x₀²) + x₁`, a monic cubic in the distinguished variable
`T` over `ℝ[x₀, x₁]`, and let `S ⊆ ℝ ^ 2` be the line `x₁ = 0`. As `f` is squarefree, it is its
own squarefree basis. Over `S` its coefficients `1`, `-(3 + x₀²)`, `3 + 2 x₀²` and `-(1 + x₀²)`
have constant signs, its content is `1`, and its discriminant vanishes, because each fibre
`(T - 1)² (T - 1 - x₀²)` has a double root. So the McCallum projection of `{f}` is sign-invariant
on `S`, and some member of it has nonconstant order on `S`; since the other members do not vanish
on `S`, this is the discriminant. But the fibre has the two roots `1` and `2` over `(1, 0)` and
the single root `1` over the origin. In the coordinates `(T, x₀, x₁)`, every cell of a stack over
`S` lies over all of `S`, so the cells through the zeros `(1, 1, 0)` and `(2, 1, 0)` of `f` would
both contain its only zero `(1, 0, 0)` over the origin, hence coincide, and then also contain
`(3 / 2, 1, 0)`, where `f` is negative. So no stack over `S`, given by pointwise strictly
increasing functions, continuous or not, has `f` sign-invariant on each cell.

TauCeti.exists_setLIntegral_exp_mul_norm.doc:
**The John–Nirenberg inequality on Euclidean balls.** There are constants `A > 0` and `C`,
depending only on the dimension `n`, such that the following holds for every additive Haar
measure `μ` on `ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ ι`. Let `f : ℝⁿ → E` be integrable on the ball `B(x₀, R)`,
with mean oscillation `⨍_B ‖f - f_B‖ ≤ M` on every ball `B ⊆ B(x₀, R)`. If `σ M ≤ A`, then on the
concentric ball `B' = B(x₀, R / (2√n))`,

`∫_{B'} exp (σ ‖f - f_{B'}‖) ≤ C |B'|`.

TauCeti.exists_setLIntegral_exp_mul_mul_.doc:
**Moser's crossover estimate.** There are constants `A > 0` and `C`, depending only on the
dimension `n`, such that the following holds for every additive Haar measure `μ` on
`ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ ι`. Let `f : ℝⁿ → ℝ` be integrable on the ball `B(x₀, R)`, with mean
oscillation `⨍_B |f - f_B| ≤ M` on every ball `B ⊆ B(x₀, R)`. If `|σ| M ≤ A`, then on the
concentric ball `B' = B(x₀, R / (2√n))`,

`(∫_{B'} exp (σ f)) (∫_{B'} exp (-σ f)) ≤ C |B'|²`.

For `f = log u`, with `u` positive, this compares the averages of `u^σ` and of `u^(-σ)` over `B'`:
it is the step of Moser's proof of the Harnack inequality that links the bounds for positive
powers of a supersolution to those for its negative powers.

TauCeti.exists_setLIntegral_enorm_le_mul.doc:
**De la Vallée Poussin's criterion, quantitative form.** If `Φ` is superlinear and the
functions `f i` satisfy the uniform bound `∫ Φ(‖f i‖) ≤ C < ∞`, then for every `ε > 0` there is
a finite `T` with `∫_s ‖f i‖ ≤ T μ(s) + ε` for every index `i` and every set `s`.

TauCeti.exists_roth_auxiliary_polynomial.signature:

  ∃ P,
    P ≠ 0 ∧

TauCeti.exists_roth_auxiliary_polynomial.doc:
**Roth's auxiliary polynomial** (Pottmeyer, Theorem 2.6.5). Let `α` be an algebraic number
of degree `d` in a field of characteristic zero, and let `b ≥ 1` be an integer such that `b α` is
integral over `ℤ`. Let `ε ≥ 0` and let `ι` be a finite set of `n` variables with
`2 d ≤ exp (ε² n / 2)`. For all positive integers `rᵢ`, `i ∈ ι`, there is a nonzero
`P ∈ ℤ[Xᵢ : i ∈ ι]` with `deg_{Xᵢ} P ≤ rᵢ`, whose index at `(α, …, α)` with weights `r` is at
least `(n / 2) (1 - ε)`, and whose coefficients have absolute value at most
`(12 b max(1, ⌈α⌉)) ^ (∑ᵢ rᵢ)`, where `⌈α⌉` is the house of `α`.

TauCeti.exists_riemannianEDist_le_mul_ex.doc:
**A trajectory converging to a nondegenerate critical point converges exponentially fast in
the Riemannian distance.** If the maximal integral curve `γ` of `-grad f` through `x` exists for
all positive time and converges to a nondegenerate critical point `p`, then the Riemannian
distance from `γ t` to `p` is at most `C * exp (-μ * t)` for some `μ, C > 0` and all large `t`.
This is the manifold counterpart, for an arbitrary `C¹` metric, of the vector-space theorem
`IsIntegralCurveOn.exists_norm_sub_le_mul_exp_atTop`.

TauCeti.exists_residueFieldSection.{u_1, u_2} (k : Type u_1) (R : Type u_2) [Field k] [CommRing R]

TauCeti.exists_residueFieldSection.doc:
**Cohen's theorem: a complete local ring containing a field has a coefficient field.** If the
complete local ring `R` is an algebra over some field `k`, then reduction `R → ResidueField R` has
a ring homomorphism section. When `k` is perfect, `TauCeti.residueFieldSection k R` is even a
`k`-algebra section. In general a `k`-linear section need not exist.

TauCeti.exists_representsLaplace_of_isDi.doc:
**The existence half of the Hausdorff--Bernstein--Widder theorem in finite-difference form.**
A function right-continuous at zero all of whose mixed forward differences with nonnegative steps
have the sign `(-1)ⁿ` is the Laplace transform of a finite positive measure on `ℝ≥0`.

TauCeti.exists_representsLaplace_of_isCo.signature:
TauCeti.exists_representsLaplace_of_isContinuousCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi {f : ℝ → ℝ}
  (hf : TauCeti.IsContinuousCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f) : ∃ μ, TauCeti.RepresentsLaplace μ f
TauCeti.exists_representsLaplace_of_isCo.doc:
**Existence half of the Hausdorff--Bernstein--Widder theorem**: a function continuous on
`[0, ∞)` and completely monotone on `(0, ∞)` is the Laplace transform of a finite positive
measure on `ℝ≥0`.

TauCeti.exists_representsLaplace_of_isCo.signature:
TauCeti.exists_representsLaplace_of_isCompletelyMonotone {f : ℝ → ℝ}
  (hcm : TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone f) : ∃ μ, TauCeti.RepresentsLaplace μ f
TauCeti.exists_representsLaplace_of_isCo.doc:
**Bernstein's theorem, existence half.** A completely monotone function on `[0, ∞)` is the
Laplace transform of a finite positive measure on `ℝ≥0`.

Uniqueness of that measure is not asserted here; it is `TauCeti.RepresentsLaplace.unique`, and
the two combine in the Hausdorff--Bernstein--Widder theorem.

TauCeti.exists_regular_lineDeriv_ofFun_a.doc:

measures.** If every compact `K ⊆ Ω` has an open neighbourhood `U` on which `u` has finite total
variation, then for every direction `v` there are regular measures `ν₁` and `ν₂` on `Ω` with
`∂_v u (φ) = ∫ φ dν₁ - ∫ φ dν₂` for every test function `φ`, where `∂_v u` is the derivative of
the distribution `Distribution.ofFun Ω u μ ⊤`. If `u` is locally integrable on `Ω`, this is the
distributional derivative of `u`, `∂_v u (φ) = -∫ ∂_v φ * u`; otherwise `Distribution.ofFun` is
zero by convention and the statement is trivial. The measures are finite on compact subsets of
`Ω` but need not be finite.

**The regular-fibre theorem.** A regular fibre over an interior value of a `C^m` map,
`m ≥ 1`, from a finite-dimensional boundaryless real manifold to a finite-dimensional real
manifold admits a `C^m` manifold structure of dimension `dim M - dim N`, with its subspace
topology, for which the inclusion is a `C^m` smooth embedding and has tangent image `ker df`.
No separation or countability assumptions are needed, and an empty fibre is allowed.

TauCeti.exists_quiver_admissibleIdeal_mo.doc:
**Gabriel's presentation theorem.** Every finite-dimensional algebra `A` over an algebraically
closed field `k` is Morita equivalent to a bound quiver algebra: there are a finite quiver `Q`
and an admissible ideal `I` of the path algebra `kQ` such that `A` is Morita equivalent to
`kQ ⧸ I`. The algebra `kQ ⧸ I` is isomorphic to the basic corner `eAe` of `A`
(`TauCeti.IsSemiperfectRing.exists_isIdempotentElem_full_isBasic_corner`), presented by
`TauCeti.IsBasic.exists_surjective_pathAlgebra_isAdmissibleIdeal_ker`.

TauCeti.exists_probabilityMeasure_of_ten.doc:
**Lévy's continuity theorem, including existence.** If the characteristic functions of a
sequence of probability measures converge pointwise to a function continuous at zero, there is
a unique probability measure with that characteristic function, and the sequence converges
weakly to it. Continuity is required only at zero; normalization of the limit follows from the
probability measures in the sequence.

**Uniform bound for inverse period maps.** For a basis `b` of `Λ`, the real linear maps
`x ↦ ∑ i, x i • P y (b i)` are bounded below by one constant `c > 0` as `y` ranges over a
compact set: `c * ‖x‖ ≤ ‖∑ i, x i • P y (b i)‖`.

**Belyi's degree reduction.** Every finite set `S` of elements algebraic over a perfect field
`F`, such as a finite subset of `AlgebraicClosure ℚ`, is carried into `F` by a polynomial
`q ∈ F[X]` with `q′ ≠ 0`, in particular nonconstant, whose critical values in every field
extension of `F` also lie in `F`.

TauCeti.exists_polynomial_aeval_mem_crit.signature:

TauCeti.exists_polynomial_aeval_mem_crit.doc:
**Polynomial Belyification of algebraic numbers.** Every finite set `S` of elements algebraic
over `ℚ` in a field `K`, such as a finite subset of `AlgebraicClosure ℚ`, is carried into
`{0, 1}` by a nonconstant polynomial `q` with rational coefficients whose critical values, in
every field of characteristic zero, lie in `{0, 1}`.

TauCeti.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_sum.signature:
TauCeti.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_sum_eq.{u, v} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v} {s t : V}

  ∃ k P X,
    (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
      (∀ (v : V), v ≠ s → v ≠ t → {i | v ∈ (P i).vertices}.card ≤ c v) ∧

TauCeti.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_sum.doc:
**Vertex-capacitated Menger's theorem for directed paths.** Let `s ≠ t` be vertices of an arrow
family on a finite vertex type, with no arrow from `s` to `t`, and let `c v` be a capacity on every
vertex. Some family of `k` directed `s`–`t` paths, in which every vertex `v` other than `s` and `t`
lies on at most `c v` members, and some set `X` of vertices avoiding `s` and `t`, whose deletion
leaves `t` unreachable from `s`, satisfy `∑ v ∈ X, c v = k`. By
`TauCeti.card_le_sum_of_not_reachableAvoiding`, the family is then largest and the separator of
least weight.

TauCeti.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_car.doc:
**Menger's theorem for internally vertex-disjoint directed paths.** Let `s ≠ t` be vertices of
an arrow family on a finite vertex type, with no arrow from `s` to `t`. Some family of `k` distinct
directed `s`–`t` paths, pairwise sharing no vertex other than `s` and `t`, and some set of `k`
vertices avoiding `s` and `t`, whose deletion leaves `t` unreachable from `s`, exist. By
`TauCeti.card_le_card_of_not_reachableAvoiding`, the family is then largest and the separator
smallest.

TauCeti.exists_paths_setSeparator_sum_eq.signature:
TauCeti.exists_paths_setSeparator_sum_eq.{u, v} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v} [Finite V]
  [DecidableEq V] (c : V → ℕ) (A B : Finset V) :
  ∃ k a b P X,
    (∀ (i : Fin k), a i ∈ A) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin k), b i ∈ B) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ v ∈ (P i).vertices, v ≠ a i → v ≠ b i → v ∉ A ∧ v ∉ B) ∧

TauCeti.exists_paths_setSeparator_sum_eq.doc:
**Vertex-capacitated Menger's theorem for directed paths between vertex sets.** Let `A` and `B`
be sets of vertices of an arrow family on a finite vertex type, and let `c v` be a capacity on every
vertex. Some family of `k` directed paths, the `i`-th from `a i ∈ A` to `b i ∈ B` with its other
vertices in neither `A` nor `B`, in which every vertex `v` lies on at most `c v` members, and some
set `X` of vertices meeting every walk from a vertex of `A` to a vertex of `B` satisfy
`∑ v ∈ X, c v = k`. By `TauCeti.card_le_sum_of_forall_not_reachableAvoiding`, the family is then
largest and the separator of least weight.

TauCeti.exists_paths_setSeparator_card_e.doc:
**Menger's theorem for vertex-disjoint directed paths between vertex sets.** Let `A` and `B` be
sets of vertices of an arrow family on a finite vertex type. Some family of `k` pairwise
vertex-disjoint directed paths, the `i`-th from `a i ∈ A` to `b i ∈ B` with its other vertices in
neither `A` nor `B`, and some set of `k` vertices meeting every walk from a vertex of `A` to a
vertex of `B` exist. By `TauCeti.card_le_card_of_forall_not_reachableAvoiding`, the family is then
largest and the separator smallest.

TauCeti.exists_paths_setArrowSeparator_c.doc:
**Menger's theorem for arrow-disjoint directed paths between vertex sets.** Let `A` and `B` be
disjoint sets of vertices of a finite arrow family. Some family of `k` directed paths, the `i`-th
from `a i ∈ A` to `b i ∈ B` with its other vertices in neither `A` nor `B`, no two of which
traverse a common arrow, and some set of `k` arrows whose deletion leaves no vertex of `B` reachable
from a vertex of `A` exist. By `TauCeti.card_le_card_of_forall_not_reachableWithout`, the family
is then largest and the set of arrows smallest.

TauCeti.exists_paths_isMixedSeparator_ca.doc:
**Menger's theorem for internally vertex-disjoint directed paths between possibly adjacent
terminals.** Let `s ≠ t` be vertices of an arrow family on a finite vertex type, with finitely many
arrows from `s` to `t`. For some `k`, there are a family of distinct directed `s`–`t` paths indexed
by `Fin k ⊕ Q s t`, pairwise sharing no vertex other than `s` and `t`, whose member indexed by an
arrow `e` from `s` to `t` is the path consisting of `e`, and a set `X` of `k` vertices, avoiding `s`
and `t`, whose deletion together with that of every arrow from `s` to `t` leaves `t` unreachable
from `s`. By `TauCeti.card_le_card_add_card_of_isMixedSeparator`, the family is then largest and
the separator smallest.

TauCeti.exists_paths_arrowSeparator_card.doc:
**Menger's theorem for arrow-disjoint directed paths.** For distinct vertices `s` and `t` of a
finite arrow family, some family of directed `s`–`t` paths, no two of which traverse a common
arrow, has as many members as some set of arrows whose deletion leaves `t` unreachable from `s`.
By `TauCeti.card_le_card_of_not_reachableWithout`, the family is then largest and the set of
arrows smallest.

TauCeti.exists_pathCycleDecomposition.doc:
**Path–cycle decomposition.** Every nonnegative arrow assignment `f` on a finite arrow family
is a sum of positively weighted directed paths, each from a vertex of negative excess to a vertex
of positive excess, and positively weighted directed cycles. The number of components is at most
the number of arrows on which `f` is positive, and if the values of `f` lie in an additive subgroup
`H`, then so do all weights.

TauCeti.exists_parametric_morse_chart.doc:
**The parametric Morse lemma, as a local chart.** The chart has a product source containing
`(a, 0)`, preserves the base parameter in both directions, and fixes the zero section. Its
quadratic equation uses the vertical Hessian on that same zero section. The base and the fiber
are Banach spaces, so the ordinary inverse function theorem applies to their product.

TauCeti.exists_openPartialHomeomorph_of_.doc:
**The Nash inverse function theorem.** A map with Nash coordinate germs and invertible
Fréchet derivative at `a` restricts, inside any prescribed neighbourhood, to a local
homeomorphism with open semialgebraic source and target and semialgebraic graphs in both
directions. Every coordinate of the map and its inverse is Nash throughout those domains.
Empty coordinate index types are allowed.

TauCeti.exists_openPartialHomeomorph_fde.doc:
**The straightening theorem** (flow-box theorem). A `C^n` vector field `w`, `1 ≤ n`, defined
near a point `a` of a finite-dimensional real normed space, with `w a ≠ 0`, is constant in suitable
`C^n` coordinates: there is an open partial homeomorphism `φ`, `C^n` on its source with `C^n`
inverse on its target, such that `a ∈ φ.source` and `dφ_y (w y) = w a` for every `y ∈ φ.source`.

TauCeti.exists_one_le_pow_mul_norm_gelfo.doc:
**Liouville's lower bound for Gelfond's values** (Karatarakis–Wiedijk, §3). Let `K` be a
number field of degree `h`, `α, β, γ ∈ K`, `m ∈ ℕ` and `c ∈ ℝ`. There is `c₂ ≥ 1` with the
following property. Let `q ^ 2 = 2 m n`, `r ≥ n` and `t₀ ≤ m`, and let
`η_{ab} ∈ 𝓞 K`, `a, b < q`, have house at most `c ^ n n ^ ((n + 1) / 2)`, as for Gelfond's
auxiliary function. If
`ρ = ∑_{a, b} η_{ab} ((a + 1) + (b + 1) β) ^ r α ^ ((a + 1) t₀) γ ^ ((b + 1) t₀)` is nonzero, then
`1 ≤ c₂ ^ r r ^ ((h - 1) r) |σ ρ|` for every embedding `σ : K →+* ℂ`. In particular
`|σ ρ| ≥ c₂ ^ (-r) r ^ (-(h - 1) (r + 1))`.

TauCeti.exists_nullified_mcCallumProjection_orderAt_ne

            (Finset.map (MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv ℝ 3).toEmbedding {f}).IsIrreducibleBasis B →
              (∀
                  q ∈
                    (Finset.map (MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv ℝ 3).toEmbedding {f}).mcCallumProjection
                      B,
                  ∀ x ∈ C, ∀ y ∈ C, q.orderAt x = q.orderAt y) ∧
                (∀ b ∈ B, ∀ x ∈ C, Polynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval x) b = 0) ∧

                    (∀ (x : ↑C), StrictMono fun i => θ i x) →

TauCeti.exists_nullified_mcCallumProject.doc:
**McCallum lifting fails over positive-dimensional nullifying cells.** The hypothesis of
`TauCeti.exists_isSemialgebraicStack_orderAt_eq_of_mcCallumProjection` that no basis member is
nullified over a cell with more than one point cannot be dropped, even over a connected
semialgebraic analytic submanifold on which the McCallum projection is order-invariant.

Explicitly, let `f = X₂ (X₀ + 1) + X₃ X₁`, a polynomial in the distinguished variable `X₀` and the
base coordinates `X₁, X₂, X₃`, and let `C ⊆ ℝ ^ 3` be the line of base points `x` with
`x₁ = x₂ = 0`. As a polynomial in `X₀`, `f` is linear with coprime coefficients `X₂` and
`X₂ + X₃ X₁`, each of which vanishes to order one at every point of `C`; its content and
discriminant are units. So for every irreducible basis `B` of `{f}`, every element of the McCallum
projection has constant order on `C`, while every member of `B` is nullified over `C`. But `f` has
order at least two at the point `(-1, 0, 0, 0)` above `C`, and order one at every point above
`C` where `X₀ ≠ -1` or `X₁ ≠ 0`. Since every cell of a stack over `C` lies over the whole of `C`,
no stack over `C`, given by pointwise strictly increasing functions, continuous or not, has `f`
order-invariant on each cell.

TauCeti.exists_nsmul_hyperbolicClass_add.doc:
**Witt decomposition** (Lam I.4.1), existence: every isometry class of regular forms is the
orthogonal sum of a number of hyperbolic planes and an anisotropic class.

TauCeti.exists_notMem_nsmul_mem_smul_sub.doc:
**The trivial-filtration theorem, relative form.** For a `G`-stable subgroup `N ≠ ⊤` of a
finite discrete `p`-primary additive group `M` with a continuous action of a pro-`p` group `G`,
there is `x ∉ N` with `p • x ∈ N` whose class modulo `N` is fixed by `G`: the quotient `M ⧸ N`,
with the induced action `AddSubgroup.quotientDistribMulAction`, contains a copy of `𝔽_p` with
trivial action.

TauCeti.exists_norm_lt_and_forall_apply_.doc:
**Helly's criterion.** Let `f i` be finitely many continuous linear functionals on `E`, let
`c i` be scalars and let `0 ≤ M`. For every `ε > 0` some `x : E` with `‖x‖ < M + ε` satisfies
`f i x = c i` for every `i` if and only if `‖∑ i, a i * c i‖ ≤ M * ‖∑ i, a i • f i‖` for all
scalars `a i`.

of a bounded `α`-Hölder function with constant `H` is `O(H τ^((α - 2)/2))`, uniformly in the

`1 < p < ∞`. There is a constant `C` such that for every operator `A` on `ℝ × E` with

near a point `x` is, on a neighbourhood of `x`, the exterior derivative of a `C^r` form defined on
the whole manifold. The manifold may have boundary or corners.

The coefficient space is complete: with values in the finitely supported sequences there is a
smooth closed `1`-form on `ℝ` with no local primitive. Finite dimensionality of the model and the
Hausdorff property are used only to cut the local primitive off by a smooth bump function.

**Brauer's local lemma.** For every prime `p` there is a function `ψ : G → ℕ`, none of whose
values is divisible by `p`, whose cast to `k` is an `A`-combination of virtual characters induced
from `p`-elementary subgroups, for every subring `A` of `k` containing the `|G|`-th roots of
unity. It is the sum, over the conjugacy classes of `p`-regular elements `s`, of `orderOf s` times
the induced `p`-section indicator of `s`: at `y` only the class of the `p`-free part of `y`
contributes, and its contribution is prime to `p`.

TauCeti.exists_mem_orientedGS_of_not_isM.doc:
**Miller's independence lemma.** If every word extends to a word of `S`, then every
non-meagre subset of Cantor space with the Baire property contains both ends of an oriented
edge of `orientedGS S`.

**Sard--Smale, locally.** Near a point where a sufficiently smooth map has Fredholm
derivative there is a neighbourhood on which the critical values form a closed nowhere dense set.
The neighbourhood can be taken inside any prescribed neighbourhood `U` of the point, so the
conclusion can be confined to a region on which `f` is known to be the map of interest.

Completeness of the target enters through Smale's local properness lemma, which supplies the
compactness used to prove that the local critical-value image is closed.

The regularity threshold `(dim ker)² + 1` is the one inherited from the finite-dimensional
Morse--Sard theorem `TauCeti.interior_image_criticalPoints_eq_empty`, which the fibrewise step
applies to the obstruction slice, a map out of `ker (fderiv ℝ f a)`.

space to the nonempty closed subsets of a Polish space, which is weakly measurable in the sense that
`{z | M z ∩ U ≠ ∅}` is measurable for every open `U`, has a measurable selection.

and let `μ` be a curve in `P_p(X)`, absolutely continuous on `[a, b]` with finite `p`-action,

continuous paths, whose law at each time `t ∈ [a, b]` is `μ t`, whose expected `p`-action is the
`p`-action of `μ`, and whose averaged speed is the metric speed of `μ`:
`|μ'|(t) ^ p = ∫ |γ'|(t) ^ p dη` at almost every `t ∈ [a, b]`.

that is, a finite extension of `ℚ_[p]`. For every fixed `α ∈ K` there is a constant `C`,
depending on `α` and `K`, such that

`ker (a ∘ fst) = ker a × B` onto `ker (b ∘ snd) = A × ker b`.

TauCeti.exists_linearEquiv_and_isCompl_b.doc:

indecomposable submodules, and let `N` be a direct summand of `M` whose endomorphism ring is local
(so in particular `N` is nonzero). Then `N` is isomorphic to one of the `Q i₀`, and can be exchanged
for it: `N` and the remaining summands `⨆ j ≠ i₀, Q j` are complementary in `M`.

The locality of `Module.End A N` is what Fitting's lemma
`TauCeti.isLocalRing_end_of_isIndecomposable` supplies when `M` has finite length.

homomorphism `sl (Fin 2) K →ₗ⁅K⁆ L` into a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of
characteristic zero, and `φ'` any Lie algebra homomorphism agreeing with `φ` at the raising element
`E₀₁` (it is then injective too). Some automorphism `ψ` of `L` in the subgroup
`TauCeti.expAdSubgroup K e` attached to their common value `e` satisfies `ψ ∘ φ = φ'`.

**The Levi decomposition.** Over a field of characteristic zero, a finite-dimensional Lie
algebra is the semidirect sum of its solvable radical and a semisimple Lie subalgebra acting on
the radical by the adjoint action.

TauCeti.exists_leviComplement.doc:
**Levi's theorem.** Over a field of characteristic zero, the solvable radical of a
finite-dimensional Lie algebra has a complementary Lie subalgebra, a Levi complement.

  (hd : d ∈ IsManifold.maximalAtlas (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ F) 1 N)
  (hc : c ∈ IsManifold.maximalAtlas (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ K) 1 P) (hu : u.1 ∈ e.source)

  (hinv :
    (fderiv ℂ (fun q => ↑c (G (↑e.symm q.1, ↑d.symm q.2))) (↑e u.1, ↑d u.2) ∘SL
        ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℂ E F).IsInvertible) :
  ∃ ψ,
    (∀ᶠ (p : M × P) in nhds (u.1, G u), MDiffAt ψ p) ∧
      ψ (u.1, G u) = u.2 ∧

TauCeti.exists_jointImplicitFunction_of_.doc:
**The joint holomorphic implicit function theorem in charts.** Suppose `G : M × N → P` is
holomorphic near `u`, and the partial derivative in the `N` coordinate of its representative in
holomorphic charts `e`, `d`, `c` is invertible at `u`. There is a solution `ψ : M × P → N`,
holomorphic near `(u.1, G u)`, taking that point to `u.2`. Near `(u, G u)`, the equation
`G (z, v) = w` is equivalent to `ψ (z, w) = v`. In particular solutions sufficiently near `u.2`
are unique. Only the parameter and unknown model spaces need be assumed finite-dimensional;
invertibility of the partial derivative forces the level model to have the same dimension as
the unknown model. No separation or global countability assumptions are needed.

**The joint holomorphic implicit function theorem.** Let `G : E₁ × E₂ → F` be complex
differentiable near `u`, with invertible partial derivative `∂₂G(u) : E₂ →L[ℂ] F`. Then there is a
map `ψ : E₁ × F → E₂`, holomorphic (indeed analytic) near `(u.1, G u)`, with `ψ (u.1, G u) = u.2`
and `G (z, ψ (z, w)) = w` near `(u.1, G u)`; moreover, for `(z, v)` near `u` and `w` near `G u`,
`G (z, v) = w` holds exactly when `ψ (z, w) = v`. One choice of `ψ` is
`HasStrictFDerivAt.jointImplicitFunctionOfProdDomain`, and any two maps with these properties
agree near `(u.1, G u)`
(`HasStrictFDerivAt.eventuallyEq_jointImplicitFunctionOfProdDomain_of_continuousAt`).

TauCeti.exists_isTubularNeighborhood_nor.doc:
**Tubular neighbourhood theorem** for a compact `C²` embedded submanifold of a Euclidean
space, as `IsTubularNeighborhood` data: for some `ε > 0`, the normal vectors of length less than
`ε`, in the total space of the normal bundle, are mapped by `(x, v) ↦ f x + v` homeomorphically
onto an open subset of `V`. The model-fibre parameter of `Bundle.TotalSpace` is taken to be `V`,
which contains every fibre.

TauCeti.exists_isManifold_transverseFibe.doc:
**The transverse fibre-product theorem.** The actual equal-value subtype of two transverse
`C^n` maps, `n ≥ 1`, is a `C^n` manifold of dimension `dim X + dim Y - dim N` with its
subspace topology. Its inclusion is a smooth embedding, and its tangent image consists of
pairs whose images under the two differentials agree. Empty fibre products are allowed;
no separation or countability hypotheses are needed.

TauCeti.exists_isKantorovichOptimalTrans.doc:
**Brenier's theorem with the inverse map.** Let `μ` and `ν` be probability measures on a
finite-dimensional real inner product space `E`, both absolutely continuous with respect to an
additive Haar measure, and suppose the optimal cost for `‖x - y‖ ^ 2 / 2` is finite. Then there is
a convex, lower semicontinuous `u : E → EReal` that never takes the value `⊥` such that `u` is
finite near `μ`-almost every point and its Legendre–Fenchel conjugate `u⋆` is finite near
`ν`-almost every point, both with differentiable real representatives there, and:

* the gradient `∇ u` is an optimal transport map from `μ` to `ν`;
* the gradient `∇ u⋆` is an optimal transport map from `ν` to `μ`;
* the two maps are inverse to each other, `∇ u⋆ ∘ ∇ u = id` `μ`-almost everywhere and
  `∇ u ∘ ∇ u⋆ = id` `ν`-almost everywhere.

The almost everywhere uniqueness of the optimal maps and plans in each direction is recorded
separately, in `TauCeti.exists_isKantorovichOptimalTransportMap_gradient` and
`TauCeti.IsOptimalCoupling.unique`.

TauCeti.exists_isKantorovichOptimalTrans.doc:
**Brenier's theorem.** Let `μ` and `ν` be probability measures on a finite-dimensional real
inner product space `E`, with `μ` absolutely continuous with respect to an additive Haar measure,
and suppose the optimal cost for `‖x - y‖ ^ 2 / 2` is finite, as it is for laws with finite second
moment (`TauCeti.transportCost_norm_sub_sq_div_two_ne_top`). Then there is a convex, lower
semicontinuous `u : E → EReal` that never takes the value `⊥`, is finite near `μ`-almost every
point and has differentiable real representative there, such that the gradient
`T = ∇ (fun x => (u x).toReal)`:

* is an optimal transport map from `μ` to `ν`, attaining the Kantorovich value;
* induces the unique optimal plan: a plan is optimal exactly when it is the graph plan of `T`;
* is the unique optimal transport map up to `μ`-almost everywhere equality.

TauCeti.exists_isJordanCurve_superset_cl.doc:
**The bounded-image form of the small-Jordan-curve theorem.** A holomorphic injection of a
disc onto a bounded domain has finite Dirichlet integral by the conformal area formula, so for
every positive tolerance and radius bound, some closed image crosscut can be chosen on a Jordan
curve in the closure of the image domain whose diameter is at most the tolerance.

This is the form used for the Riemann map of a bounded Jordan domain.

**The existence theorem of the classification of Demushkin groups, even rank** (Labute,
Theorem 1 and Remark 2; Serre, Theorem 3.2). Let `n` be even and let `A ≤ ℤ_pˣ` be a closed pro-`p`
subgroup with `(A : A^p) < p ^ n` as supernatural numbers. Then there is a Demushkin group of rank
`n`, presented on `n` generators by a single relator `r`, which has exactly one continuous
character with the prescription property, and that character has image `A`.

in rank two, where `(A : A²) = 4`; every other closed pro-`p` subgroup is realized in every even
rank `n ≥ 2`. The pro-`p` hypothesis on `A` is used for odd `p`, where it places `A` inside the
principal units `1 + pℤ_p`; every closed subgroup of `ℤ_2ˣ` is pro-`2`.

equivalence** (Labute, Theorem 1 and Remark 2; Serre, Theorem 3.2). Let `n` be even and let

`TauCeti.exists_isDemushkin_range_demushkinCharacter_eq_iff_of_odd`, this is the full list of the

finite measure `μ` and a measure `ν` on `E` for the cost `d(x, y) ^ p`, at finite Wasserstein
distance `W_p (μ, ν)`. Then the displacement interpolation, the laws `μₜ` of
`(1 - t) • x + t • y` under `π`, solves the continuity equation on `(0, 1)` with a velocity field
of `p`-action at most `W_p (μ, ν) ^ p`: `∫₀¹ ∫ ‖vₜ‖ ^ p dμₜ dt ≤ W_p (μ, ν) ^ p`.

**Weyl's complete reducibility theorem.** Over a field of characteristic zero, every Lie
submodule of a finite-dimensional module over a Lie algebra with nondegenerate Killing form has a
complement, so the module is a direct sum of irreducibles.

The `sl₂` case, `TauCeti.exists_isCompl_of_toLieSubalgebra_eq_top`, is the rank-one instance of
the same argument, run with the concrete Casimir operator of an `sl₂` triple.

**Hoffman's circulation theorem.** A bounded circulation exists exactly when every vertex
set has total lower bound entering it at most the total upper bound leaving it.

**The cellular approximation theorem** (Hatcher, Theorem 4.8). Every map `f : C → C'` of
relative CW complexes sending the base `D` into the base `E` is homotopic, relative to `D`, to a
cellular map.

TauCeti.exists_isCellular_homotopic.doc:
**The cellular approximation theorem for CW complexes** (Hatcher, Theorem 4.8). Every map of
CW complexes is homotopic to a cellular map.

squarefree basis of `F` is well-oriented, there is a sign-invariant CAD for `F` with analytic
cells. Its base CAD is order-invariant for that projection. No restriction is imposed on
nullification of the top-level basis, including over positive-dimensional base cells.

TauCeti.exists_isCAD_signInvariant.doc:
**Existence of adapted cylindrical algebraic decompositions.** For every finite set `F` of
real polynomials in `n` variables there is a cylindrical algebraic decomposition of `ℝ ^ n` on
each cell of which every member of `F` is sign-invariant.

TauCeti.exists_isCAD_orderAt_eq_of_isMcC.doc:
**Correctness of McCallum's projection.** A finite family of real polynomials that is
well-oriented in McCallum's sense has a cylindrical algebraic decomposition into analytic
submanifolds, on each cell of which every member of the family has constant ambient order.

TauCeti.exists_isCAD_lazardValuationRein.doc:
**Validity of Lazard's projection.** Every finite family of real polynomials in `n`
variables has a cylindrical algebraic decomposition of `ℝ ^ n` into analytic submanifolds on
each cell of which every member has constant Lazard valuation, when the coordinates are read in
reverse order, from the coordinate added first by the cylindrical structure to the one added
last. Every member is also sign-invariant on each cell. No well-orientedness hypothesis is
imposed, and members may be nullified over base cells of positive dimension.

the origin, then `X ∩ quadraticSublevelUnionCell ε` is a strong deformation retract of `X`: there
is a retraction of `X` onto it, and a homotopy in `X` from this retraction to the identity which
fixes `X ∩ quadraticSublevelUnionCell ε`. Both are restrictions of
`TauCeti.quadraticHandleRetraction ε` and `TauCeti.quadraticHandleDeformation ε`.

nondegenerate Killing form over a field of characteristic zero, `e` is the image of the raising
element `E₀₁` under an injective Lie algebra homomorphism `sl (Fin 2) K →ₗ⁅K⁆ L` if and only if
`e ≠ 0` and `ad e` is nilpotent.

**The matrix form of the Ado–Iwasawa theorem.** Every finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a
field embeds in `𝔤𝔩_n = Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K` for some `n`. Over `ℝ` this is the embedding
consumed by the integration of a real Lie algebra to a Lie group.

TauCeti.exists_injective_freeGroup_SL.doc:
**Free groups of countable rank are linear over `ℤ`.** Every free group on a countable basis
embeds in `SL(2, ℤ)`.

**The Riemann map of a Jordan domain extends to a homeomorphism of the

constant `C`, depending only on `α` and the dimension, such that the Hessian `D² w(t, ·)` is

there is a constant `C`, depending only on `α` and the dimension, such that at every point `x`
the Hessian `t ↦ D² w(t, ·)(x)` is `α/2`-Hölder in time on `[0, T]` with constant `C H`, whenever

with constant `H` for almost every `0 < s < T`. Neither the bound on `f` nor the horizon `T`
enters the estimate. Together with

`α`-Hölder estimate of `D² w` on the slab `E × [0, T]`, for `0 < α < 1`.

orthogonal in the sense that `∑ j, √‖(T i)† ∘L T j‖ ≤ A` and `∑ j, √‖T i ∘L (T j)†‖ ≤ A` for
every `i`, the sums over `j` being taken over arbitrary finite sets. Then for every `x` the
series `∑ i, T i x` converges unconditionally, and its sum is a bounded operator of norm at
most `A`.

extension `K` of `ℚ_p`, every finite quotient of `G_K` through which the commutator subgroup of

repetitions are allowed: the quotient may have fewer than `[K : ℚ_p] + 2` elements.

**Miller's independence lemma**, for the simple graph: if `S` is dense, then every
non-meagre subset of Cantor space with the Baire property contains two adjacent points of
`gSGraph S`.

TauCeti.exists_fourierMultiplierCLM_eq_a.doc:
**The Mihlin–Hörmander multiplier theorem on `Lᵖ`.** Let `V` be a real inner product space of
finite dimension `n ≥ 1`, let `2N > n` and `1 < p < ∞`. There is a constant `C` such that for
every symbol `m` of temperate growth satisfying Mihlin's condition of order `N` with constant `A`,

`‖D^k m ξ‖ ≤ A / ‖ξ‖ ^ k` for every `k ≤ N` and every `ξ ≠ 0`,

the Fourier multiplier `𝓕⁻ (m • 𝓕 f)` of the tempered distribution of any `f ∈ Lᵖ(V, F)` is an
`Lᵖ` function `g` with `‖g‖_p ≤ C A ‖f‖_p`.

TauCeti.exists_forall_dual_pos_iff.doc:
**Gordan's theorem.** Some linear functional is strictly positive on every vector of a finite
family exactly when the only nonnegative linear relation among the vectors is the trivial one.

TauCeti.exists_forall_apply_eq_smul.signature:
TauCeti.exists_forall_apply_eq_smul.{u, v, w} (K : Type u) [Field K] (L : Type v) [LieRing L]
  [LieAlgebra K L] (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module K M] [LieRingModule L M]
  [LieModule K L M] [LieModule.IsIrreducible K L M] [IsAlgClosed K] [FiniteDimensional K M]
  (f : M →ₗ⁅K,L⁆ M) : ∃ c, ∀ (m : M), f m = c • m
TauCeti.exists_forall_apply_eq_smul.doc:
**Schur's lemma for Lie modules.** Over an algebraically closed field, a morphism of a
finite-dimensional irreducible `L`-module to itself is multiplication by a scalar: an eigenvalue
exists, and the corresponding eigenspace is a nonzero Lie submodule, hence everything.

TauCeti.exists_forall_abs_apply_sub_le_o.signature:
TauCeti.exists_forall_abs_apply_sub_le_of_forall_neg_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_1}
  {κ : Type u_2} {K : Type u_3} {V : Type u_4} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module K V]
  [LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K] [Finite ι] [Finite κ] [FiniteDimensional K V]
  (a : ι → Module.Dual K V) (b : κ → Module.Dual K V) :
  ∃ C,
    0 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (c : K),
        0 ≤ c →
          ∀ (w : V),
            (∀ (j : ι), -c ≤ (a j) w) →
              ∃ w', (∀ (j : ι), 0 ≤ (a j) w') ∧ ∀ (k : κ), |(b k) (w - w')| ≤ C * c
TauCeti.exists_forall_abs_apply_sub_le_o.doc:
**Hoffman's error bound for a polyhedral cone.** Let `a j` be finitely many functionals on a
finite-dimensional space. There is a constant `C` such that every `w` with `-c ≤ a j w` for all
`j`, where `0 ≤ c`, lies within `C * c` of the cone `{w' | ∀ j, 0 ≤ a j w'}`, as measured by
finitely many prescribed functionals `b k`. The constant `C` is nonnegative.

TauCeti.exists_foldr_markoffVieta_eq.signature:
TauCeti.exists_foldr_markoffVieta_eq {x : Fin 3 → ℤ} (hx : x ∈ TauCeti.positiveMarkoffTriples) :
  ∃ l, List.foldr TauCeti.markoffVieta 1 l = x
TauCeti.exists_foldr_markoffVieta_eq.doc:
**Markoff's theorem.** Every positive Markoff triple `x` is obtained from `(1, 1, 1)` by a
finite word in the Vieta moves: `x = R_{i₁} (R_{i₂} ⋯ (R_{i_k} (1, 1, 1)))`. No coordinate
permutation is needed.

TauCeti.exists_finset_deriv_eq_zero.signature:
TauCeti.exists_finset_deriv_eq_zero {f : ℝ → ℝ} {Z : Finset ℝ} (hZ : Z.Nonempty)
  (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (Z.min' hZ) (Z.max' hZ))) (hfZ : ∀ x ∈ Z, f x = 0) :
  ∃ Z',
    Z'.card + 1 = Z.card ∧
      (∀ z ∈ Z', deriv f z = 0) ∧
        (∀ z ∈ Z', ∃ x ∈ Z, ∃ y ∈ Z, x < z ∧ z < y) ∧
          ∀ x ∈ Z, ∀ y ∈ Z, x < y → ∃ z ∈ Z', x < z ∧ z < y
TauCeti.exists_finset_deriv_eq_zero.doc:
**Rolle's theorem for finitely many zeros.** If a function `f : ℝ → ℝ`, continuous between
the smallest and largest points of a nonempty finite set `Z`, vanishes on `Z`, then `deriv f`
vanishes on a finite set `Z'` with one point fewer that separates the points of `Z`: every point of
`Z'` lies strictly between two points of `Z`, and strictly between any two points of `Z` lies a
point of `Z'`.

TauCeti.exists_finset_card_smul_symmDiff.doc:
**Reiter implies Følner.** If a nonnegative finitely supported function `p` on `X` satisfies
`∑_{g ∈ K} ∑_x |p (g⁻¹ • x) - p x| < ε · ∑_x p x`, then some finite nonempty set `F ⊆ X` satisfies
`|g • F ∆ F| < ε |F|` for every `g ∈ K`.

TauCeti.exists_filtration_of_isProP.signature:
TauCeti.exists_filtration_of_isProP.{u_1, u_2} {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {G : Type u_1}
  [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] {M : Type u_2} [AddCommGroup M] [TopologicalSpace M]
  [DiscreteTopology M] [DistribMulAction G M] [ContinuousSMul G M] [Finite M]
  (hG : TauCeti.IsProP p G) (htors : IsAddPGroup p M) :
  ∃ N,
    N 0 = ⊥ ∧
      Monotone N ∧
        (∀ (i : ℕ), padicValNat p (Nat.card M) ≤ i → N i = ⊤) ∧
          (∀ (i : ℕ) (g : G), ∀ x ∈ N i, g • x ∈ N i) ∧
            (∀ i ≤ padicValNat p (Nat.card M), Nat.card ↥(N i) = p ^ i) ∧
              ∀ i < padicValNat p (Nat.card M),
                ∃ x,
                  N (i + 1) = N i ⊔ AddSubgroup.zmultiples x ∧
                    x ∉ N i ∧ p • x ∈ N i ∧ ∀ (g : G), g • x - x ∈ N i
TauCeti.exists_filtration_of_isProP.doc:
**The trivial-filtration theorem.** A finite discrete `p`-primary additive group `M` with a
continuous action of a pro-`p` group `G` has a `G`-stable increasing chain of subgroups
`N 0 = ⊥ ≤ N 1 ≤ …` reaching `⊤` after `padicValNat p (Nat.card M)` steps, the composition
length of `M`, and constant at `⊤` from there on, with `|N i| = p ^ i` along the way. Each step
adjoins an element `x` with `x ∉ N i`, `p • x ∈ N i` and `g • x - x ∈ N i` for every `g`, so
every factor `N (i + 1) ⧸ N i` is a copy of `𝔽_p` with trivial `G`-action.

TauCeti.exists_faithful_weightedPBWRepre.signature:

  ∃ N b w,
    ∃ (hbracket :
      ∀ (i j k : Fin (Module.finrank K L)), w k < w i + w j → (b.repr ⁅b i, b j⁆) k = 0),
      0 < N ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin (Module.finrank K L)), 0 < w i ∧ w i < N) ∧
          Module.Finite K (UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra K L ⧸ b.weightedPBWIdeal w hbracket N) ∧
            Function.Injective ⇑(b.weightedPBWRepresentation w hbracket N) ∧
              ∀ (x : L), (b.weightedPBWRepresentation w hbracket N) x ^ N = 0
TauCeti.exists_faithful_weightedPBWRepre.doc:
**Birkhoff's theorem on a weighted PBW quotient.** A finite-dimensional nilpotent Lie
algebra has a faithful left-multiplication representation on a finite-dimensional weighted
enveloping quotient, with one positive nilpotence bound for all acting operators.
The basis, weights, and cutoff are supplied by the conclusion, in every characteristic.

TauCeti.exists_faithful_preserving_ad_ni.signature:
TauCeti.exists_faithful_preserving_ad_nilpotence_charZero.{u, v} (K : Type u) (L : Type v) [Field K]

    ∃ (_ : FiniteDimensional K V),
      ∃ ρ,
        Function.Injective ⇑ρ ∧
          ∀ (x_3 : L), IsNilpotent ((LieAlgebra.ad K L) x_3) → IsNilpotent (ρ x_3)
TauCeti.exists_faithful_preserving_ad_ni.doc:
**Hochschild's strengthening of Ado's theorem in characteristic zero.** A finite-dimensional
Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero has a faithful finite-dimensional representation
that preserves nilpotence of the adjoint action: every `ad`-nilpotent element acts nilpotently.

For semisimple `L` the nilradical is zero, so the nilpotence clause of
`TauCeti.exists_faithful_nilrepresentation_charZero` is empty there, while this one still
constrains every `ad`-nilpotent element.

TauCeti.exists_faithful_preserving_ad_ni.signature:
TauCeti.exists_faithful_preserving_ad_nilpotence.{u, v} (K : Type u) (L : Type v) [Field K]
