TauCeti.exists_faithful_preserving_ad_ni.doc:
**Hochschild's strengthening of the Ado–Iwasawa theorem.** A finite-dimensional Lie algebra
over an arbitrary field has a faithful finite-dimensional representation that preserves
nilpotence of the adjoint action: every `ad`-nilpotent element acts nilpotently.

TauCeti.exists_faithful_nilrepresentatio.signature:
TauCeti.exists_faithful_nilrepresentation_charZero.{u, v} (K : Type u) (L : Type v) [Field K]
  [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] [CharZero K] :
  ∃ V x x_1,
    ∃ (_ : FiniteDimensional K V),
      ∃ ρ, Function.Injective ⇑ρ ∧ ∀ x_3 ∈ TauCeti.LieAlgebra.nilradical K L, IsNilpotent (ρ x_3)
TauCeti.exists_faithful_nilrepresentatio.doc:
**Ado's theorem in characteristic zero, with nilpotence on the nilradical.** A
finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero has a faithful
finite-dimensional representation in which every element of the nilradical acts nilpotently.

TauCeti.exists_faithful_nilrepresentatio.signature:
TauCeti.exists_faithful_nilrepresentation.{u, v} (K : Type u) (L : Type v) [Field K] [LieRing L]
  [LieAlgebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] :
  ∃ V x x_1,
    ∃ (_ : FiniteDimensional K V),
      ∃ ρ, Function.Injective ⇑ρ ∧ ∀ x_3 ∈ TauCeti.LieAlgebra.nilradical K L, IsNilpotent (ρ x_3)
TauCeti.exists_faithful_nilrepresentatio.doc:
**The Ado–Iwasawa theorem with nilpotence on the nilradical.** A finite-dimensional Lie
algebra over an arbitrary field has a faithful finite-dimensional representation in which every
element of the nilradical acts nilpotently.

TauCeti.exists_eventually_hasFDerivAt_of.doc:
**The local Frobenius theorem.** Let `E` and `F` be finite-dimensional real normed spaces and
let `f : E × F → (E →L[ℝ] F)` be `C^(n+1)` near `(x₀, y₀)`, for instance `C¹`. If `f` satisfies the
Frobenius integrability condition near `(x₀, y₀)`, then the total differential equation
`D u x = f (x, u x)` has a local solution `u` with `u x₀ = y₀`, which is `C^(n+1)` at `x₀`.

TauCeti.exists_equivariant_chart_target_.signature:
TauCeti.exists_equivariant_chart_target_eq_sumOfConjugatesInnerSublevel_of_contMDiffAt.{u_1, u_2,
    u_3, u_4}
  {E : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} {G : Type u_4} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H}
  [I.Boundaryless] [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [Group G] [Fintype G] [MulAction G M]
  [ContinuousConstSMul G M] {y : M} (hsmooth : ∀ (g : G), ContMDiffAt I I 1 (fun x => g • x) y)
  (hy : ∀ (g : G), g • y = y) {s : Set M} (hs : s ∈ nhds y) :
  ∃ σ e c,
    0 < c ∧
      y ∈ e.source ∧
        ↑e y = 0 ∧
          e.source ⊆ s ∧
            e.target =
                (ContRepresentation.toRepresentation ℝ G E σ).sumOfConjugatesInnerSublevel c ∧
              IsPreconnected e.source ∧
                (∀ (g : G), ∀ z ∈ e.source, g • z ∈ e.source ∧ ↑e (g • z) = (σ g) (↑e z)) ∧
                  ∀ (g : G),
                    (σ g = 1 ↔ g ∈ TauCeti.MulAction.germKernel G y) ∧
                      (σ g = 1 ↔ ∀ z ∈ e.source, g • z = z)
TauCeti.exists_equivariant_chart_target_.doc:
**The linear local model at a fixed point.** Let a finite group `G` act continuously on a
finite-dimensional real manifold without boundary, fixing `y`, by maps that are `C¹` at `y`.
Inside any neighbourhood `s` of `y` there is a chart `e` sending `y` to `0` whose domain is
`G`-invariant and preconnected and whose target is a positive strict sublevel set of a
`σ`-invariant inner product, in which `G` acts linearly through a continuous representation `σ`.
Every element of `G` is retained, including those acting trivially: `g` acts as the identity near
`y`, that is, lies in the germ kernel at `y`, exactly when `σ g = 1`, and exactly when `g` fixes
every point of the domain of `e`.

TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_isLo.signature:
TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_isLocalRing_end.{u, v, w, x} {A : Type u} [Ring A] {M : Type v}
  [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module A M] {ι : Type w} {κ : Type x} [Finite ι] [Finite κ]
  {P : ι → Submodule A M} {Q : κ → Submodule A M} (hP : iSupIndep P) (hPt : ⨆ i, P i = ⊤)
  (hPloc : ∀ (i : ι), IsLocalRing (Module.End A ↥(P i))) (hQ : iSupIndep Q) (hQt : ⨆ j, Q j = ⊤)
  (hQind : ∀ (j : κ), TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule A ↥(Q j)) :
  ∃ e, ∀ (i : ι), Nonempty (↥(P i) ≃ₗ[A] ↥(Q (e i)))
TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_isLo.doc:
**The Krull-Schmidt theorem**, in Azumaya's generality: if a module is the internal direct sum
of a finite family of submodules with local endomorphism rings, and also of a finite family of
indecomposable submodules, then the two families are matched by a bijection of their index sets
under which corresponding summands are isomorphic.

Each summand of the first family is automatically indecomposable, by
`TauCeti.isIndecomposableModule_of_isLocalRing_end`; for a module of finite length the converse
holds too, which is `TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_iSupIndep` below.

TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_iSup.doc:
**The Krull-Schmidt theorem.** Two decompositions of a module of finite length into
indecomposable submodules are matched by a bijection of their index sets under which corresponding
summands are isomorphic.

The index types need not carry finiteness instances: independence and the nonzero summands force
them to be finite because the ambient module is Noetherian.

Fitting's lemma makes the endomorphism ring of each summand local, as needed by
`TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_isLocalRing_end`. Existence of such a decomposition is
`TauCeti.exists_indecomposable_decomposition`.

TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_fins.doc:
**The Krull-Schmidt theorem**, in the `Finset` packaging that
`TauCeti.exists_indecomposable_decomposition` produces: two `Finset`s of indecomposable submodules
each presenting the module as an internal direct sum are matched by a bijection under which
corresponding summands are isomorphic.

TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_dire.doc:
**The Krull-Schmidt theorem for external direct sums**, in Azumaya's generality: if a module is
isomorphic to a finite direct sum of modules with local endomorphism rings, and also to a finite
direct sum of indecomposable modules, then the two families are matched by a bijection of their
index sets under which corresponding summands are isomorphic.

No finiteness hypothesis on `M` is needed; for a module of finite length Fitting's lemma supplies
the locality hypothesis, which is `TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_directSum` below.

TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_dire.signature:
TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_directSumEquiv.{u, w, x, y, z} {A : Type u} [Ring A]
  {ι : Type w} {κ : Type x} {N : ι → Type y} [(i : ι) → AddCommGroup (N i)]
  [(i : ι) → _root_.Module A (N i)] {Q : κ → Type z} [(j : κ) → AddCommGroup (Q j)]
  [(j : κ) → _root_.Module A (Q j)] [Finite ι] [Finite κ]
  (e : (DirectSum ι fun i => N i) ≃ₗ[A] DirectSum κ fun j => Q j)
  (hN : ∀ (i : ι), IsLocalRing (Module.End A (N i)))
  (hQ : ∀ (j : κ), TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule A (Q j)) :
  ∃ f, ∀ (i : ι), Nonempty (N i ≃ₗ[A] Q (f i))
TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_dire.doc:
**The Krull-Schmidt theorem for two abstract families of summands**: a direct sum of modules
with local endomorphism rings that is isomorphic to a direct sum of indecomposable modules has its
summands matched by a bijection of the index sets.

This is `TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_directSum_of_isLocalRing_end` with the ambient module
taken to be the first direct sum; it is the form to use when no ambient module is in play.

**The Krull-Schmidt theorem for external direct sums.** Two decompositions of a module of finite
length as a direct sum of indecomposable modules are matched by a bijection of their index sets
under which corresponding summands are isomorphic.

`TauCeti.exists_linearEquiv_directSum_isIndecomposableModule` supplies such a decomposition, and
`TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_iSupIndep` is the same statement for families of submodules of
`M`. Neither theorem requires finiteness instances on the index types.

TauCeti.exists_equiv_iso_of_iso_biproduc.doc:
**The Krull-Schmidt theorem for biproducts in `ModuleCat A`.** If an object of finite length is
isomorphic to a finite biproduct of indecomposable objects in two ways, the two families of
summands are matched by a bijection of their index sets under which corresponding summands are
isomorphic.

`TauCeti.exists_indecomposable_iso_biproduct` supplies such an isomorphism, and
`TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_directSum` is the same statement for external direct sums of
modules.

TauCeti.exists_equiv_iso_of_biproduct_is.signature:
TauCeti.exists_equiv_iso_of_biproduct_iso.{u, v} {A : Type u} [Ring A] {ι κ : Type} [Finite ι]

  [IsArtinian A ↑(⨁ P)] (e : ⨁ P ≅ ⨁ Q) (hP : ∀ (i : ι), CategoryTheory.Indecomposable (P i))

TauCeti.exists_equiv_iso_of_biproduct_is.doc:
**The Krull-Schmidt theorem with no ambient object**: an isomorphism between two finite
biproducts of indecomposable objects of finite length matches their summands by a bijection of the
index sets.

TauCeti.exists_eq_sum_mul_of_forall_mul_.doc:
**The Ikeda--Nakayama annihilator criterion**, for a right self-injective ring: if every `r`
with `a i * r = 0` for all `i` also satisfies `x * r = 0`, then `x` lies in the left ideal
generated by the `a i`.

**The Ikeda--Nakayama annihilator criterion**, for a left self-injective ring: if every `r`
with `r * a i = 0` for all `i` also satisfies `r * x = 0`, then `x` lies in the right ideal
generated by the `a i`.

  {f g : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hg : DifferentiableOn ℂ g U) (hfi : Set.InjOn f U)
  (hgi : Set.InjOn g U) (hfimage : f '' U = Metric.ball 0 1) (hgimage : g '' U = Metric.ball 0 1) :
  ∃ u a, Set.EqOn g (fun z => ↑u * ((f z - ↑a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) ↑a * f z))) U
TauCeti.exists_eqOn_unitDiscStandardAuto.doc:
**Uniqueness in the Riemann mapping theorem, up to a disc automorphism.** If `f` and `g` are
holomorphic injections from an open set `U` onto the open unit disc, then there are `u` on the
unit circle and `a` in the unit disc such that

`g z = u * (f z - a) / (1 - conj a * f z)`

for every `z ∈ U`.

TauCeti.exists_eqOn_const_mul_add_iff_lo.doc:
**Rigidity of the pre-Schwarzian derivative.** Two holomorphic functions with nonvanishing
derivatives on a domain have equal pre-Schwarzian derivatives exactly when one is obtained from
the other by postcomposition with `w ↦ a * w + b` for a nonzero constant `a`.

TauCeti.exists_eLpNorm_lineDerivOp_lineD.doc:
**The Calderón–Zygmund estimate for a second directional derivative.** Let `v, w ∈ ℝⁿ` and
`1 < p < ∞`. There is a constant `C` with

`‖∂_v ∂_w u‖_{Lᵖ} ≤ C ‖Δu‖_{Lᵖ}`

for every Schwartz function `u` on `ℝⁿ` with values in a complex Hilbert space.

data. Let `c` be a dilation factor, `M` a bound on operator norms and `B`, `B'` cancellation
constants, all finite. Then for every `1 < p < ∞` there is a constant `C` with the following
property. Let `T` be a bounded linear operator on `L²(ℝⁿ)` of Hilbert space valued functions with
`‖T‖ ≤ M`, such that `T` and its adjoint satisfy the cancellation condition with dilation factor
`c` and constants `B` and `B'`. Then `‖T f‖_p ≤ C ‖f‖_p` for every `f ∈ L²`.

**The Calderón–Zygmund theorem on an inner product space under Hörmander's condition**, strong
type `(p, p)` for `1 < p < ∞`, with a constant depending only on the data. Let `V` be a
finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension `n ≥ 1`, let `M`, `B` and `B'` be finite,
and let `1 < p < ∞`. There is a constant `C` with the following property. Let `T` be a bounded
linear operator on `L²(V)` of Hilbert space valued functions with `‖T‖ ≤ M`. Suppose that `T` and
its adjoint `T†` are given off the support of their argument by kernels `k` and `k'`: for every
compact set `s` and every `f` vanishing off `s`, `T f x = ∫ k x y (f y) dy` (respectively
`T† f x = ∫ k' x y (f y) dy`) for almost every `x ∉ s`. Suppose that both kernels satisfy
**Hörmander's condition**

`∫_{‖x - y'‖ > 2 ‖y - y'‖} ‖k x y - k x y'‖ dx ≤ B` and
`∫_{‖x - y'‖ > 2 ‖y - y'‖} ‖k' x y - k' x y'‖ dx ≤ B'` for all `y`, `y'`.

uniformly to families of operators, such as the truncations of a Fourier multiplier.

There is a constant `C` with `‖D²u‖_{Lᵖ} ≤ C ‖Δu‖_{Lᵖ}` for every real Schwartz function `u` on
`V`.

second Fréchet derivative of `u`.

dimension `n ≥ 1`, let `N` be an integer with `2N > n`, and let `1 < p < ∞`. There is a constant

does not depend on `m` or `A`.

TauCeti.exists_diffeomorph_eventually_co.doc:
**Moser's lemma**, local form. Let `ω₀`, `ω₁` be closed `C^r` two-forms (`r ≥ 1`) on an open
subset `W` of a finite-dimensional real normed space, with `ω₁ - ω₀ = dα` on `W` for a `C^r`
one-form `α` vanishing at `x₀ ∈ W`. If `ω₀` and `ω₁` agree at `x₀` and are nondegenerate there,
then some `C^r` diffeomorphism `ψ` of the space pulls `ω₁` back to `ω₀` on a neighbourhood of `x₀`.
Moreover `ψ` fixes, near `x₀`, every point at which `α` vanishes; in particular `ψ x₀ = x₀`.

**Darboux's theorem.** A closed `C^r` two-form `ω` (`r ≥ 1`) on an open subset of a
finite-dimensional real normed space, nondegenerate at `x₀`, is constant in suitable coordinates
near `x₀`: there is a `C^r` diffeomorphism `ψ` of the space fixing `x₀` such that the pullback
`ψ^* ω` equals the constant form `ω(x₀)` on a neighbourhood of `x₀`.

depending only on `E` and `μ`, with the following property. Let `u` be convex on an open set `Ω`,
with `λ μ ≤ MA_u ≤ Λ μ` on `Ω` for the Monge–Ampère measure of `u` extended by `⊤` off `Ω` and

of `D`, with any supporting slope, is bounded with closure inside `Ω`. Consider a family of
sections `S i = S(c i, h i)`, `i ∈ t`, with centres `c i ∈ Ω`, supporting slopes `ℓ i`, positive
heights with `4 θ h i ≤ H` and `2 θ² h i ≤ H`, and `S i ⊆ D`. Then there is a countable subfamily

measure of the union of the whole family:
`μ (⋃ i ∈ t, S i) ≤ √(A (2 θ²)ⁿ Λ / λ) μ (⋃ j ∈ s, S j)`, where `n = finrank ℝ E`.

**The Vitali covering lemma for sections.** There is a constant `C`, depending only on `E`
and `μ`, with the following property. Let `u` be convex on an open set `Ω`, with
`λ μ ≤ MA_u ≤ Λ μ` on `Ω` for the Monge–Ampère measure of `u` extended by `⊤` off `Ω` and
`0 < λ`, and write `θ = 1 + C Λ / λ`. Suppose that every section of height `H` centred at a point
of `D`, with any supporting slope, is bounded with closure inside `Ω`. Consider a family of
sections `S i = S(c i, h i)`, `i ∈ t`, with centres `c i ∈ Ω`, supporting slopes `ℓ i`, positive

`j ∈ s`.

TauCeti.exists_cost_eq_finiteMultiDualVa.doc:
**Finite multi-marginal Kantorovich duality.** For a nonempty finite family of finite
spaces, the primal and dual problems have the same value and both attain it.

pseudometric spaces, a continuous nonnegative cost, and every `ε > 0`, there is a pair of
*continuous* potentials satisfying the Kantorovich constraint whose value is within `ε` of the
primal transport cost. Together with weak duality this closes the duality gap.

TauCeti.exists_continuousOn_eq_forall_me.doc:
**Carathéodory's existence theorem for linear equations.** Let `M : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E` be almost
everywhere strongly measurable and essentially bounded on `(a, b)`, and let `F : ℝ → E` be
integrable on `(a, b)`. Then the linear equation `x' = M(t) x + F(t)` with `x(a) = x₀` has a
solution in Carathéodory's sense: a curve `x` continuous on `[a, b]` with `x a = x₀` and
`x t = x₀ + ∫ s in a..t, (M s (x s) + F s)` for every `t ∈ [a, b]`.

TauCeti.exists_continuousOn_closedBall_e.doc:
**Carathéodory's continuity theorem.** A holomorphic injection of a disc onto a bounded region
whose boundary is locally connected extends continuously to the closed disc.

No injectivity is claimed for the extension on the circle, and none is needed for continuity.

TauCeti.exists_continuousOn_closedBall_e.doc:
**Carathéodory's continuity theorem, as a characterization.** A holomorphic injection of a disc
onto a bounded region extends continuously to the closed disc if and only if the boundary of the
region is locally connected.

**Carathéodory's continuity theorem on the upper half-plane.** Let `Ω` be a bounded simply
connected open subset of `ℂ` with locally connected frontier, and let `p ∈ frontier Ω`. Then a
Riemann map from the upper half-plane onto `Ω` extends continuously to the real axis and tends to
`p` at infinity.

The finite real boundary values lie in `frontier Ω` and, together with `p`, cover that frontier.
No injectivity is asserted on the real axis: distinct boundary parameters can have the same value
when the frontier is locally connected but is not a Jordan curve.

TauCeti.exists_continuousOn_bijOn_upperH.doc:
**Carathéodory's theorem on the closed upper half-plane for an unbounded Jordan domain.**  Let
`U` be a connected open subset of `ℂ`, and suppose that the frontier of `U` together with the
point at infinity is a Jordan curve of the Riemann sphere, so that `U` is unbounded.  Then there is
a map which is continuous on the closed upper half-plane, holomorphic on the open upper half-plane,
a bijection from the open upper half-plane onto `U`, from the closed upper half-plane onto
`closure U` and from the real line onto `frontier U`, and which
tends to infinity at infinity within the closed half-plane.

TauCeti.exists_contDiff_conjWirtingerDer.doc:
**The Dolbeault lemma on the plane.** Every `Cⁿ` function `f : ℂ → W`, `n ≥ 1`, is `\bar∂ g`
for a `Cⁿ` function `g`; no support condition on `f` is needed.

TauCeti.exists_contDiffOn_conjWirtingerD.doc:
**The Dolbeault lemma on a disc.** Let `f` be `Cⁿ`, `n ≥ 1`, on the open disc `eball c R`
of radius `R ≤ ∞`. Then there is a function `g`, `Cⁿ` on the disc, with `\bar∂ g = f` on the
disc.

**The Dolbeault lemma on a disc of real radius.** If `f` is `Cⁿ`, `n ≥ 1`, on `ball c R`,
there is a function `g`, `Cⁿ` on `ball c R`, with `\bar∂ g = f` there.

TauCeti.exists_complete_self_stabilization.{u, v, w} {L : FirstOrder.Language} [L.IsRelational]

TauCeti.exists_complete_self_stabilizati.doc:
A countable structure stabilizes below `ω₁`. Only its tuples are counted; the language
may be uncountable.

TauCeti.exists_comp_eq_and_topologicalCl.doc:
**Gaschütz's lifting lemma, generator-rank form.** Along a continuous surjection `f : G →* H`
from a topologically finitely generated profinite group onto a Hausdorff group, a topologically
generating `n`-tuple of `H` lifts to a topologically generating `n`-tuple of `G` whenever `n` is at
least the topological generator rank of `G`.

**Gaschütz's lifting lemma for profinite groups.** Along a continuous surjection `f : G →* H`
from a profinite group onto a Hausdorff group, an `ι`-tuple that topologically generates `H` lifts
to an `ι`-tuple that topologically generates `G`, provided `G` is topologically generated by some
`ι`-tuple, with `ι` finite.

TauCeti.exists_circleLIntegral_sq_lt.doc:
**Wolff's lemma.** If `2 π` times the plane integral of `g ^ 2` is smaller than
`c * log (R / r)`, then some circle of radius `ρ` strictly between `r` and `R` has
`circleLIntegral g ζ ρ ^ 2 < c`.

Since `log (R / r)` grows without bound as the annulus is made longer while the plane integral
stays fixed, this makes the circle integral arbitrarily small at arbitrarily small radii: a weight
of finite square integral cannot have a large circle integral on every circle about `ζ`.

  ∃ ρ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 R, TauCeti.circleLIntegral g ζ ρ < c
TauCeti.exists_circleLIntegral_lt_of_lin.doc:
**Wolff's lemma in the limit: a weight of finite square integral has small circle integrals at
arbitrarily small radii.** If `∫⁻ z, g z ^ 2` is finite then for every threshold `c ≠ 0` and every
bound `R > 0` there is a radius `ρ` below `R` with `circleLIntegral g ζ ρ < c`.

The threshold that `TauCeti.exists_circleLIntegral_sq_lt` asks to be beaten is
`2 π ∫⁻ z, g z ^ 2 / log (R / r)`, which for a finite square integral falls to `0` as the annulus
`Ioo r R` is made logarithmically longer; here the outer radius is the prescribed bound `R` and the
inner one `R * exp (-L)` is pushed towards `0`, which is what confines the radius produced to
`Ioo 0 R`. The reduction to a finite threshold is the passage to `min c 1`, and the square is undone
by monotonicity of squaring on `ℝ≥0∞`.

There is no companion statement for a *fixed* small radius: see
`TauCeti.liminf_circleLIntegral_nhdsGT_eq_zero` for the sharp form, a lower limit rather than a
limit.

**Wolff's lemma, area form.** On a measurable subset `s` of the domain of holomorphy on which
`f` is injective the Dirichlet integral is the area of `f '' s`, so a radius with `ℓ ρ ^ 2 < c`
exists as soon as `2 π * area (f '' s) < c * log (R / r)`.

TauCeti.exists_circleImageLength_sq_lt.doc:
**Wolff's lemma.** If `2 π` times the Dirichlet integral of `f` over `s` is smaller than
`c * log (R / r)`, then some circle of radius `ρ` between `r` and `R` has `ℓ ρ ^ 2 < c`.

Since `log (R / r)` grows without bound as the annulus is made longer while the Dirichlet integral
stays fixed, this makes `ℓ` arbitrarily small at arbitrarily small radii; for a holomorphic `f`
that is the geometric statement that a map of finite Dirichlet integral cannot keep every circular
arc about `ζ` long.

TauCeti.exists_chart_mfderiv_eq_const.doc:
**The straightening theorem** [Lee, Thm. 9.22]. Let `v` be a vector field on a `C^n` manifold
with finite-dimensional boundaryless model, `C^m` on a neighbourhood of `x`, with `1 ≤ m`,
`m + 1 ≤ n` and `v x ≠ 0`. Then some chart `e` of the `C^m` maximal atlas whose domain contains `x`

TauCeti.exists_bijOn_const_mul_schwarzCh.doc:
**The Schwarz--Christoffel theorem for polygonal domains with several ends.**  Let `U` be a
simply connected, unbounded open set, with a point `q` outside its closure, whose frontier is a
finite union of closed segments and closed rays.  Suppose that `U` coincides near each frontier
point other than the distinct vertices `v i` with an open half-plane, and near the vertex `v i` with
the open sector of opening `(e i + 1) * π` at `v i`, where `e i ∈ (-1, 1)`.  Suppose finally that
far out `U` is covered by pairwise disjoint ends `E k ⊆ U`, each either the far part of a sector of
opening `(-e' k - 1) * π` with `e' k ∈ (-3, -1)`, a half-strip between two parallel sides with
`e' k = -1`, or the far part of the exterior of a closed half-strip with `e' k = -3`.

Then there are distinct real prevertices `a i` of the vertices and `a' k` of the ends, and
constants `A ≠ 0` and `B`, such that `z ↦ A * F z + B` maps the upper half-plane bijectively onto
`U`, where `F` is the normalized Schwarz--Christoffel primitive for these prevertices and the
turning exponents `e i` and `e' k`.  The Schwarz--Christoffel vertex at `a i` is sent to `v i`, and
near `a' k` the map takes its values in the end `E k`.

**The Schwarz--Christoffel theorem for a polygonal Jordan domain whose end is the exterior of
a half-strip.**  Let `U` be a connected open set whose frontier, together with the point at
infinity, is a Jordan curve of the Riemann sphere.  Suppose that `U` coincides near each frontier
point other than the distinct vertices `v i` with an open half-plane, near the vertex `v i` with
the open sector of opening `(e i + 1) * π` at `v i`, where `e i ∈ (-1, 1)`, and far from a point
`c` with the exterior of the closed half-strip `{0 ≤ re ((z - c) / b), 0 ≤ im ((z - c) / b) ≤ π}`:
so `U` has a further vertex at infinity, of opening `2 * π`, between two parallel sides pointing
the same way.  Then there are distinct real prevertices `a i` and constants `A ≠ 0` and `B` such
that `z ↦ A * F z + B` maps the upper half-plane bijectively onto `U`, where `F` is the normalized

that the Schwarz--Christoffel vertex at `a i`, the limit of `F` at `a i`, is sent to `v i`.  The
prevertex of the vertex at infinity is the point at infinity of the half-plane.

corners of angles `(e i + 1) * π`, straight sides away from those corners, and a sector of opening

holomorphic inverse: `Function.invFunOn f Ω` is holomorphic on the disc and inverts `f` on both

TauCeti.exists_analytic_delineation_of_o.doc:
**Analytic delineability from constant discriminant order.** A polynomial with nonzero
fibers of constant degree over a preconnected analytic submanifold, whose nonzero formal
discriminant has constant ambient order on the base, has a global delineation with intrinsically
analytic root functions. Each root function is represented by an ambient function whose values
off the base are immaterial. Along each root section, the polynomial, viewed as a polynomial in
all `n + 1` variables, has constant ambient order of vanishing.

No preservation of the formal degree or nonvanishing of the discriminant values is required.
Multiple roots are allowed, and their fiber multiplicities are constant.

TauCeti.exists_analyticOnNhd_prod_eqOn.doc:
**The Riemann extension theorem across a coordinate hyperplane.** Let `U ⊆ V` and `s ⊆ ℂ` be
open. If `f` is analytic on `U × (s \ {c})` and, when `c ∈ s`, each slice `z ↦ f (w, z)`, for
`w ∈ U`, is bounded on a punctured neighbourhood of `c`, then some `g` analytic on `U × s` agrees
with `f` on `U × (s \ {c})`. Such a `g` is unique on `U × s` by
`eqOn_prod_of_eqOn_prod_diff_singleton`.

TauCeti.existsUnique_vanKampenDesc.doc:
**The based van Kampen theorem for a neighborhood cover, in universal-property form.**
Pairwise compatible homomorphisms out of the fundamental groups of the cover members extend
uniquely to the ambient fundamental group. Repeated indices in the triple-intersection
hypothesis imply path connectedness of the double intersections and individual members. No
common pairwise intersection is required, and the target can be any monoid.

TauCeti.existsUnique_transitiveGroupLabe.doc:
A transitive subgroup of the symmetric group on five points carries exactly one label, one of
`5T1`, …, `5T5`.

TauCeti.existsUnique_toeplitz_eq_iff_adj.doc:
**Brown–Halmos theorem.** A bounded operator `T` on Hardy space is a Toeplitz operator `T_a`
for a unique essentially bounded symbol `a` if and only if `S† T S = T`, where `S = T_z` is the
forward shift.

TauCeti.existsUnique_lie_eq_and_lie_eq_n.doc:
**Morozov's lemma**. Let `ad e` be nilpotent, `⁅h, e⁆ = 2 • e` and `h ∈ [e, L]`, over a field
of characteristic zero. Then there is a unique `f` with `⁅e, f⁆ = h` and `⁅h, f⁆ = -(2 • f)`.
The case `h = 0` is allowed.

TauCeti.existsUnique_isSl2Triple_of_isNi.doc:
**Morozov's lemma** for `sl₂` triples. Let `ad e` be nilpotent, `⁅h, e⁆ = 2 • e`, `h ≠ 0` and
`h ∈ [e, L]`, over a field of characteristic zero. Then there is a unique `f` such that `(h, e, f)`
is an `sl₂` triple.

TauCeti.existsUnique_isPos_reflection_sm.doc:
**A cover of `W / W_λ` has a unique positive root label.** If `y` is covered by `x` in the
Bruhat order of the minimal coset representatives of the stabilizer of the dominant weight `λ`,
there is exactly one positive root `β` with `y λ = s_β (x λ)`.

TauCeti.existsUnique_eq_smul_lazardCocyc.doc:
**The symmetric 2-cocycle lemma**, with uniqueness: for `n ≥ 2`, a homogeneous symmetric
additive 2-cocycle of degree `n` over any commutative ring is `r • C_n` for a unique `r`.

TauCeti.existsUnique_eq_hazewinkelFormal.doc:
**Universality of Hazewinkel's formal group law over `ℚ`-algebras**: a formal group law over a
`ℚ`-algebra whose logarithm has no terms outside the degrees `pⁿ` is Hazewinkel's formal group law
of a unique family `v`.

TauCeti.existsUnique_dynkinType.doc:
**The Cartan-Killing classification, existence and uniqueness of the Dynkin type.** Every
irreducible reduced crystallographic finite root system has a unique valid `DynkinType`.

TauCeti.exactForms_succ_eq_closedForms_n.doc:
**The Poincaré lemma on a normed space.** Every closed smooth real form of positive degree
on `E` is the exterior derivative of a smooth form.

TauCeti.eventually_residual_exists_isMan.doc:
**Generic regular zeros.** For a residual set of parameters `l`, the zeros of `s (·, l)`
form a `C^n` manifold of dimension the index `d`, with a `C^n` immersion into `M` whose tangent
spaces are the kernels of the linearizations in the `M` direction.

TauCeti.eventually_finsum_analyticOrderN.signature:
TauCeti.eventually_finsum_analyticOrderNatAt_ball_eq.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} {l : Filter ι}
  {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (Metric.closedBall c r))

  (hconv : TendstoUniformlyOn F g l (Metric.sphere c r)) (hne : ∀ z ∈ Metric.sphere c r, g z ≠ 0) :
  ∀ᶠ (i : ι) in l,
    ∑ᶠ (z : ℂ) (_ : z ∈ Metric.ball c r), analyticOrderNatAt (F i) z =
      ∑ᶠ (z : ℂ) (_ : z ∈ Metric.ball c r), analyticOrderNatAt g z
TauCeti.eventually_finsum_analyticOrderN.doc:
**Hurwitz's theorem, counting form.** Let `g` and — for all sufficiently large `i` — the `F i`
be analytic on a closed disc `closedBall c r`, let `F i → g` uniformly on the
bounding circle `sphere c r`, and let `g` not vanish on that circle. Then for all sufficiently
large `i`, `F i` has exactly as many zeros in `ball c r` as `g` does, counted with multiplicity.

No ambient domain enters: a locally uniform limit on an open `Ω` supplies the uniform convergence
on any circle with `closedBall c r ⊆ Ω`, via
`tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_iff_tendstoUniformlyOn_of_compact`.

TauCeti.eventually_exists_hasFDerivAt_if.signature:
TauCeti.eventually_exists_hasFDerivAt_iff_eventually_isFrobeniusIntegrableAt.{u} {E F : Type u}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ F] {n : ℕ∞} {f : E × F → E →L[ℝ] F} {s : Set (E × F)}
  {p₀ : E × F} (hf : ContDiffOn ℝ (↑n + 1) f s) (hs : s ∈ nhds p₀) :

    ∀ᶠ (p : E × F) in nhds p₀, TauCeti.IsFrobeniusIntegrableAt f p
TauCeti.eventually_exists_hasFDerivAt_if.doc:
**The Frobenius theorem for total differential equations.** Let `E` and `F` be
finite-dimensional real normed spaces and let `f : E × F → (E →L[ℝ] F)` be `C^(n+1)` near `p₀`,
for instance `C¹`. The total differential equation `D u x = f (x, u x)` has a local solution
through every point near `p₀` if and only if `f` satisfies the Frobenius integrability condition
near `p₀`.

TauCeti.eventually_eventually_right_of_m.doc:
**One half of the Kuratowski–Ulam theorem.** If `X` is second countable and `s` is comeagre
in `X × Y`, then comeagrely many sections `(·, y) ⁻¹' s` are comeagre.

TauCeti.eventually_eventually_left_of_me.doc:
**One half of the Kuratowski–Ulam theorem.** If `Y` is second countable and `s` is comeagre
in `X × Y`, then comeagrely many sections `(x, ·) ⁻¹' s` are comeagre.

TauCeti.eventuallyEq_of_eventually_hasFD.signature:

  {f : E × F → E →L[ℝ] F} {u₁ u₂ : E → F} {x₀ : E} {K : NNReal} {s : Set (E × F)}
  (hs : s ∈ nhds (x₀, u₁ x₀)) (hf : LipschitzOnWith K f s)
  (hu₁ : ∀ᶠ (x : E) in nhds x₀, HasFDerivAt u₁ (f (x, u₁ x)) x)
  (hu₂ : ∀ᶠ (x : E) in nhds x₀, HasFDerivAt u₂ (f (x, u₂ x)) x) (h₀ : u₁ x₀ = u₂ x₀) :
  u₁ =ᶠ[nhds x₀] u₂
TauCeti.eventuallyEq_of_eventually_hasFD.doc:
**Uniqueness in the local Frobenius theorem.** Two solutions of the total differential
equation `D u x = f (x, u x)` near `x₀` taking the same value at `x₀` agree near `x₀`, as soon as
`f` is Lipschitz near `(x₀, u₁ x₀)`. Neither integrability nor finite dimensionality is needed:
along each ray from `x₀` both solutions solve the same ordinary differential equation.

TauCeti.eventuallyConst_separatingSpace.doc:
**Sinclair's stability lemma.** Let `E n` and `F` be Banach spaces, let
`R n : E (n + 1) → E n` be continuous linear maps, and let `T n : E n →ₗ F` be linear maps, not
assumed continuous, with `T (n + 1) = T n ∘ R n`, so that `T n = T 0 ∘ R 0 ∘ ⋯ ∘ R (n - 1)`.
Then the decreasing sequence of separating spaces of the `T n` is eventually constant.

          ((↑n - 1 - ↑i) ^ 2 - (↑n - 1 - ↑j) ^ 2)
TauCeti.evenOrthogonalWeylDimension_eq_p.doc:
**The Weyl dimension formula for `SO (2n)` in its product form**: over `ℚ`, with
`lᵢ = μᵢ + n - 1 - i` and `rᵢ = n - 1 - i` the entries of `μ + ρ` and of `ρ`, the dimension is

`∏_{i < j < n} (lᵢ² - lⱼ²) / (rᵢ² - rⱼ²)`.

TauCeti.eulerChar_eq_finsum_finrank_sing.doc:
**Euler--Poincaré** for a space of finite CW type: its Euler characteristic is the alternating
sum of the dimensions of its singular homology over any division ring.

TauCeti.eulerChar_eq_finsum_finrank_sing.doc:
**Euler--Poincaré in cohomology** for a space of finite CW type: its Euler characteristic is
the alternating sum of the dimensions of its singular cohomology over any field.

TauCeti.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_sphere.signature:
TauCeti.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_sphere.{u_2} {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]

A sphere of radius `r > 0` in an `n`-dimensional real inner product space has
`(n - 1)`-dimensional Hausdorff measure `n ω_n r ^ (n - 1)`, where `ω_n` is the volume of the
unit ball.

TauCeti.etvDist_sq_le_two_mul_mass_mul_k.signature:
TauCeti.etvDist_sq_le_two_mul_mass_mul_klDiv.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace α]

**Pinsker's inequality** for finite measures of equal mass, using Mathlib's total variation
distance `etvDist`, the signed-measure norm. If their common mass is `M`, this says
`‖μ - ν‖² ≤ 2 * M * klDiv μ ν`. There is no finiteness assumption on relative entropy.

TauCeti.etvDist_sq_le_two_mul_klDiv.signature:

TauCeti.etvDist_sq_le_two_mul_klDiv.doc:
**Pinsker's inequality** for probability measures, with natural logarithms and no

`dTV(μ, ν) = sup_s |μ s - ν s|`, so the bound is equivalently `2 * dTV(μ, ν)² ≤ klDiv μ ν`.

TauCeti.etale_aeval_of_basis.signature:

TauCeti.etale_aeval_of_basis.doc:
**The Jacobian criterion for étaleness.** If `T` is smooth over `R` and the differentials
`d aᵢ` of finitely many elements `aᵢ` of `T` form a basis of `Ω[T⁄R]`, then `T` is étale over the
polynomial ring `R[Xᵢ]` via `Xᵢ ↦ aᵢ`.

TauCeti.esymm_mem_adjoin_psum.signature:
TauCeti.esymm_mem_adjoin_psum.{u_1, u_2} (σ : Type u_1) [Fintype σ] (R : Type u_2) [CommRing R]

TauCeti.esymm_mem_adjoin_psum.doc:
**Newton's identities express `eₖ` through the power sums**: over a `ℚ`-algebra the elementary
symmetric polynomial `eₖ` is a polynomial in the power sums `p₁, …, pₖ`.

TauCeti.essentialInterior_ae_eq.signature:
TauCeti.essentialInterior_ae_eq.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MetricSpace α] [MeasurableSpace α]

TauCeti.essentialInterior_ae_eq.doc:

TauCeti.eqOn_const_mul_schwarzChristoffe.doc:
**The Schwarz--Christoffel formula.**  Let `f` be holomorphic with nonvanishing derivative on
the upper half-plane.  Assume that away from the distinct real prevertices `a i` its boundary
values run along affine lines with the upper half-plane on one side, and that each `a i` is
carried to a vertex of one of four kinds:
* a finite vertex: `f` opens the sector of angle `(e i + 1) * π` at `f (a i)`, with boundary values
  on the two bounding rays, where `-1 < e i < 1`;
* a vertex at infinity of opening `β * π` with `0 < β < 2`, where `e i = -β - 1`: the inverted map
  `b / (f - c)` extends across `a i` with value `0`, opens the sector of angle `β * π` there, and
  has its other boundary values on the two bounding rays;
* a vertex at infinity between two parallel sides, where `e i = -1`: the exponential
  `exp ((f - c) / b)` extends across `a i` with value `0`, injectively, with real boundary values
  and upper half-plane values above the axis;
* a vertex at infinity of opening `2 * π`, where `e i = -3`: `f` is continuous and injective on
  the closed upper half-disc about `a i` with `a i` removed, tends to infinity at `a i`, and far
  out the image of the open upper half-disc is the exterior of the closed half-strip
  `{0 ≤ re ((w - c) / b), 0 ≤ im ((w - c) / b) ≤ π}`.

Assume finally that `z * f''(z) / f'(z)` has a finite limit as `z` tends to infinity in the upper
half-plane.  Then throughout the upper half-plane

`f z = (f'(z₀) / integrand(z₀)) * F z + f z₀`,

where `F` is the normalized Schwarz--Christoffel primitive for the data `a` and `e`.  So `f` is an
affine image of `F`, and the two constants are read off from the value and derivative of `f` at
the normalization point `z₀`.

star-convex about `x` and contained in `closedBall x D`, and `p` exceeds the dimension `n` of the
space, then for every `S ⊆ Ω` of positive measure the deviation of `u x` from the mean of `u`
over `S` is at most `D ^ n / (n μ(S)) * K ^ (1 - 1 / p) * D ^ (1 - n / p)` times the `Lᵖ(Ω)`
norm of the derivative of `u`, where `K = n μ(B(0, 1)) (p - 1) / (p - n)`.

`d ^ n / (n μ(S)) * K ^ (1 - 1 / p) * d ^ (1 - n / p)` times the `Lᵖ(Ω)` norm of the derivative

TauCeti.enorm_setAverage_rpow_le.doc:
**Hölder's bound on an average**, in `∫⁻` form: the `q`-th power of the average of `f` over a
set `s` is at most `(μ s)⁻¹` times the integral of `‖f‖ ^ q` over `s`.
The single factor `(μ s)⁻¹` is what survives after the `q`-th power of the normalization
`(μ s)⁻¹` cancels against the `(μ s) ^ (q - 1)` of Hölder's inequality.
No measurability or integrability hypothesis is needed, since a function not integrable on `s`
has average zero.

  ‖⨍ (y : α) in s, f y ∂mu‖ₑ ≤ mu s ^ (-p.toReal⁻¹) * MeasureTheory.eLpNorm f p (mu.restrict s)
TauCeti.enorm_setAverage_le.doc:
**Hölder's bound on an average**: the average of `f` over a set `s` is at most
`μ s ^ (-1/p)` times the `Lᵖ` seminorm of `f` on `s`. At `p = 1` this is the
bound by the average of `‖f‖`, and the volume factor sharpens as `p` grows because a larger
exponent controls the mass of `s` more efficiently. No measurability or integrability hypothesis
is needed, since a function not integrable on `s` has average zero.

**Hölder's inequality** for the integral of a product: `‖∫ u v‖ ≤ ‖u‖_p ‖v‖_q` for Hölder
conjugate exponents `p` and `q`.

**Hölder's inequality** for the integral of an inner product: `‖∫ ⟪u, v⟫‖ ≤ ‖u‖_p ‖v‖_q` for
Hölder conjugate exponents `p` and `q`.

TauCeti.endAlgEquivSelfOfIsSimpleModule.signature:
TauCeti.endAlgEquivSelfOfIsSimpleModule.{u, v, w} {k : Type u} {A : Type v} {S : Type w} [Field k]

TauCeti.endAlgEquivSelfOfIsSimpleModule.doc:
**Schur's lemma over an algebraically closed field.** The endomorphism ring of a
finite-dimensional simple module over a `k`-algebra is the field `k` itself.

Mathlib's `IsSimpleModule.algebraMap_end_bijective_of_isAlgClosed` proves that every such
endomorphism is a scalar; this packages that bijection as an algebra equivalence. Finite
dimensionality is needed: an infinite-dimensional simple module can have a larger division
endomorphism ring.

The equivalence involves no choices: it is the inverse of the structure map `k → End A S`, which
Schur's lemma proves bijective. Its inverse is therefore `algebraMap` on the nose, and the scalar
attached to an endomorphism is characterized by
`TauCeti.endAlgEquivSelfOfIsSimpleModule_smul`.

TauCeti.endAlgEquivOfSimple.signature:
TauCeti.endAlgEquivOfSimple.{w, v, u} (k : Type w) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Type u}
  [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [CategoryTheory.Linear k C]
  [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasKernels C] (X : C) [CategoryTheory.Simple X]
  [FiniteDimensional k (X ⟶ X)] : CategoryTheory.End X ≃ₐ[k] k
TauCeti.endAlgEquivOfSimple.doc:
**Schur's lemma** as an identification of algebras: the endomorphisms of a simple object `X`
with finite-dimensional endomorphisms over an algebraically closed field `k` are the scalars
`k`. This is the inverse of the structure map `algebraMap k (End X)`, `c ↦ c • 𝟙 X`.

TauCeti.elementarilyEquivalent_int_sumLe.doc: `ℤ` and `ℤ ⊕ₗ ℤ` satisfy the same first-order sentences in the language of orders.

TauCeti.eisensteinSet.signature: TauCeti.eisensteinSet.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [ValuativeRel K] (n : ℕ) : Set (Fin n → K)
TauCeti.eisensteinSet.doc:
The Eisenstein region in the space `Fin n → K` of coefficient vectors of monic polynomials of
degree `n`: every coefficient has valuation below `1`, and the constant term of `monicOfCoeff a`
has valuation at least that of every element of valuation below `1`. For `0 < n` the constant term
is `a 0`, which then has the valuation of a uniformizer; for `n = 0` it is `1`, and the region is
the whole one-point space. When `𝒪[K]` is a discrete valuation ring,
`TauCeti.mem_eisensteinSet_iff_exists_isEisensteinAt` identifies these with the coefficient vectors
of the polynomials over `𝒪[K]` that are Eisenstein at `𝓂[K]`.

`TauCeti.edist_sq_le_of_forall_mem_moreauYosidaResolvent`, the piecewise constant interpolant

As `τ → 0` this becomes a `1/2`-Hölder bound on bounded time intervals.

**The Poincaré–Wirtinger inequality on a convex domain.** If `u` is `C¹` on a bounded convex
open set `Ω` and `S ⊆ Ω` has positive measure, then for `1 ≤ p < ∞` the `Lᵖ(Ω)` seminorm of the
deviation of `u` from its mean over `S` is at most `μ(B(0, 1)) * (diam Ω) ^ (n + 1) / μ(S)` times
the `Lᵖ(Ω)` seminorm of the derivative of `u`, where `n` is the dimension of the space.

**The Hardy–Littlewood maximal inequality**, the strong-type `(p, p)` bound for `1 < p < ∞`,
in terms of representative-level `Lᵖ` seminorms.

Together with `TauCeti.maximalFunction_le_eLpNormEssSup` (the case `p = ∞`) and
`TauCeti.mul_measure_lt_maximalFunction_le` (the weak-type substitute at `p = 1`), this gives the
representative-level strong estimate for the maximal function. The resulting finiteness statement
is recorded by
`TauCeti.eLpNorm_maximalFunction_lt_top` below.

`n ≥ 2` and let `p = n / (n - 1)`. Every integrable `u : E → ℝ` satisfies `‖u‖_p ≤ C |Du|(E)`,
where `|Du|(E)` is the total variation of `u` on the whole space, finite or infinite, and `C` is
the constant `MeasureTheory.eLpNormLESNormFDerivOneConst μ p` of the `C¹` Gagliardo–Nirenberg–
Sobolev inequality `MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_one`.

function satisfies `‖u‖ₚ ≤ (n ωₙ^(1/n))⁻¹ |Du|(E)` for `p = n / (n - 1)`.

altogether, since `f^#` vanishes for constant `f`; and positive dimension is needed, since in
dimension `0` every ball is the whole space and `f^#` vanishes identically.

**The Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev inequality for integrable functions.** Let `E` have
dimension `n ≥ 2` and let `p = n / (n - 1)`. Every integrable `C¹` function `u` satisfies
`‖u‖_p ≤ C ‖Du‖₁`, with `‖Du‖₁` finite or infinite, where `C` is the constant
`MeasureTheory.eLpNormLESNormFDerivOneConst μ p` of the compactly supported case
`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_one`.

TauCeti.eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_of_sup.doc:
**The Poincaré inequality on a slab.** A `C¹` function on `ℝ^{n+1}` that vanishes outside
the slab `{x | x i ∈ Set.Icc a b}` satisfies `‖u‖_p ≤ (b - a) ‖Du‖_p` for every `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`.

Only the width of the slab enters the constant: neither the dimension nor the exponent nor the
shape of the region where `u` lives has any effect. In particular that region need not be
bounded — being trapped between two parallel hyperplanes is enough — and the hypothesis cannot
be dropped, by `TauCeti.not_exists_eLpNorm_le_const_mul_eLpNorm_fderiv`.

This is the estimate that passes to `W^{1,p}_0(Ω)` by density of `C_c^∞(Ω)`, for any `Ω`
contained in such a slab. The endpoints may be in either order: an empty slab carries only the
zero function.

radius `R` satisfies `‖u‖_p ≤ 2R ‖Du‖_p` for every `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`.

This is the shape the estimate takes on a bounded domain: any `Ω ⊆ Metric.ball c R` sits inside a
slab of width `2R`, so the constant may be taken to be twice the radius. It is not the optimal
constant — for the ball the sharp one is smaller — but it is explicit and depends on nothing but
`R`.

shows no such bound holds uniformly over all compactly supported functions.

vectors `b_t · q`, so one of those is nonzero and the shape of `t` dominates `μ`.

be real numbers, `n = |κ| ≥ 1`, such that `∑ⱼ αⱼ yⱼ` is an integer for an integer vector `y`

`|∑ⱼ αⱼ yⱼ - x| ≤ ‖y‖ ^ (-n)`, where `‖y‖` is the sup norm.

TauCeti.dimH_image_le_of_iteratedFDeriv_.doc:
**Sard's lemma on the flat stratum, in Hausdorff dimension.** A `C^{k+1}` map divides the
Hausdorff dimension of a set of points at which all iterated derivatives of order `1 ≤ i ≤ k`
vanish by `k + 1`.

The Hölder bound of `TauCeti.holderOnWith_of_iteratedFDeriv_eq_zero` only holds near a given point,
where the `(k+1)`-st derivative is bounded, so the countably stable local form
`dimH_image_le_of_locally_holder_on` is what applies.

TauCeti.differentiable_intervalIntegral_.doc:
**Truncated Laplace transforms are entire.** If `f` is interval integrable on `[a, b]`, then
`z ↦ ∫ t in a..b, f t * exp (-z t)` is complex differentiable everywhere.

TauCeti.differentiableOn_schwarzReflecti.signature:
TauCeti.differentiableOn_schwarzReflection_of_symmetric {f : ℂ → ℂ} {Ω : Set ℂ} (hΩopen : IsOpen Ω)

TauCeti.differentiableOn_schwarzReflecti.doc:
**Schwarz reflection principle (real axis).** On a conjugation-symmetric open set `Ω`, if `f`
is continuous on the closed upper part, holomorphic on the open upper part, and real-valued on
the real axis of `Ω`, then the explicit reflection extension `schwarzReflection f` is holomorphic
on all of `Ω` — in particular across the real axis.

The gluing calculus (continuity everywhere, holomorphy off the axis, the conjugation symmetry) is
`Reflection/Basic.lean`; the missing holomorphy at the axis is Painlevé removability,
`differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_im_ne_zero`.

TauCeti.differentiableOn_lineSchwarzRefl.doc:
**Schwarz reflection principle across an affine line, holomorphy form.** Let the source line
be `p + a * ℝ`, with `a ≠ 0`. Suppose an open domain `Ω` is invariant under reflection in this
line. If `f` is continuous on the closed positive side, holomorphic on the open positive side,
and its boundary values have real target coordinate, then `lineSchwarzReflection p a q b f` is
holomorphic throughout `Ω`.

The side and boundary conditions are expressed in the affine coordinates `(z - p) / a` and
`(f z - q) / b`. The target direction `b` need not be nonzero for holomorphy: when `b = 0`, the
conclusion is the constant function with value `q`. The packaged reflection theorem below assumes
`b ≠ 0` to obtain branch agreement and target-line symmetry.

TauCeti.differentiableOn_integral_mul_ce.doc:
**Holomorphy of the Laplace transform.** If `f` is bounded on `[0, ∞)`, its Laplace transform
`z ↦ ∫ t in Ici 0, f t * exp (-z t)` is complex differentiable on the half-plane `0 < re z`.

TauCeti.differentiableOn_circleSchwarzReflection_of_symmetric {Ω : Set ℂ} {c d : ℂ} {r s : ℝ}
  {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hr : 0 < r) (hs : 0 < s) (hΩ : IsOpen Ω)

TauCeti.differentiableOn_circleSchwarzRe.doc:
**Schwarz reflection principle across a circle.** Let `Ω` be an open set invariant under
reflection in the source circle. If `f` is continuous on the closed inside part, holomorphic on
the open inside part, sends the source-circle boundary into the
target circle, and avoids the target centre in the punctured interior, then its explicit
circle-reflection extension is holomorphic throughout `Ω`.

The target-centre avoidance is exactly the non-pole condition for reflection in the target
circle.

TauCeti.differentiableOn_and_re_nonneg_i.signature:

TauCeti.differentiableOn_and_re_nonneg_i.doc:
**The Herglotz representation theorem**, as a characterization: a function on the unit disc
is holomorphic with nonnegative real part if and only if it is the Herglotz transform of a finite
positive measure on the unit circle plus an imaginary constant.

nonzero in `L`, the different exponent of `L/K` is at most `e(L/K) − 1 + v_L(e(L/K))`.

then `d(L/K) = ∑_{i < N} (#G_i - 1)`.

TauCeti.differentExponent_eq_ramificatio.doc:
**Dedekind's different theorem, the tame case**: `d(L/K) = e(L/K) - 1` exactly when `L/K` is
tamely ramified.

TauCeti.differentExponent_eq_finsum_lowe.signature:
TauCeti.differentExponent_eq_finsum_lowerRamificationGroup.{u_1, u_2} (K : Type u_1) (L : Type u_2)

**Hilbert's formula for the different exponent**: for a finite Galois extension `L/K` of
nonarchimedean local fields, `d(L/K) = ∑_{i ≥ 0} (#G_i - 1)`, where `G_i` is the `i`-th lower
ramification group. The sum is finite because the filtration is eventually trivial.

TauCeti.diagramSchurPoly_mul_alternant.signature:
TauCeti.diagramSchurPoly_mul_alternant.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (N : ℕ) (μ : YoungDiagram)
  (hμ : μ.colLen 0 ≤ N) :
  (TauCeti.diagramSchurPoly N R μ * TauCeti.alternant (Fin N) R fun j => N - 1 - ↑j) =
    TauCeti.alternant (Fin N) R fun j => μ.betaNumber N ↑j
TauCeti.diagramSchurPoly_mul_alternant.doc:
**Jacobi's bialternant formula.**  For a Young diagram `μ` with at most `N` rows, the Schur
polynomial `s_μ` in the alphabet `Fin N` times the Vandermonde alternant `a_δ`, `δ_j = N - 1 - j`,
is the alternant `a_{λ+δ}` of the row lengths `λ_j = μ.rowLen j` shifted by the staircase:
`s_μ · a_δ = a_{λ+δ}`.  This is the division-free form of `s_μ = a_{λ+δ} / a_δ`.

The row bound is necessary: for a taller shape `s_μ` vanishes, while the right-hand side, which
only sees the first `N` rows, need not.

TauCeti.diagramSchurPoly_eq_det_hsymmInt.signature:
TauCeti.diagramSchurPoly_eq_det_hsymmInt.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (N : ℕ)
  (μ : YoungDiagram) {r : ℕ} (hr : μ.colLen 0 ≤ r) :
  TauCeti.diagramSchurPoly N R μ =
    (Matrix.of fun i j => TauCeti.hsymmInt (Fin N) R (↑(μ.rowLen ↑i) - ↑↑i + ↑↑j)).det
TauCeti.diagramSchurPoly_eq_det_hsymmInt.doc:
**The Jacobi--Trudi identity.**  The Schur polynomial of a Young diagram `μ` in the alphabet
`Fin N` is the determinant `det (h_{μᵢ - i + j})_{0 ≤ i, j < r}` of complete homogeneous symmetric
polynomials, for every `r` at least the number of rows of `μ`.  The index `μᵢ - i + j` is an
integer, and `h_m = 0` for `m < 0` (`TauCeti.hsymmInt`).

There is no condition relating `N` to `μ`: when `μ` has more than `N` rows, both sides vanish.

TauCeti.diagramSchurPoly_eq_det_esymmInt.signature:
TauCeti.diagramSchurPoly_eq_det_esymmInt.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (N : ℕ)
  (μ : YoungDiagram) {r : ℕ} (hr : μ.rowLen 0 ≤ r) :
  TauCeti.diagramSchurPoly N R μ =
    (Matrix.of fun i j => TauCeti.esymmInt (Fin N) R (↑(μ.colLen ↑i) - ↑↑i + ↑↑j)).det
TauCeti.diagramSchurPoly_eq_det_esymmInt.doc:
**The dual Jacobi--Trudi identity.**  The Schur polynomial of a Young diagram `μ` in the
alphabet `Fin N` is the determinant `det (e_{μ'ᵢ - i + j})_{0 ≤ i, j < r}` of elementary symmetric
polynomials, where `μ'ᵢ` is the length of the `i`-th column, for every `r` at least the number of
columns of `μ`.  The index `μ'ᵢ - i + j` is an integer, and `e_m = 0` for `m < 0`
(`TauCeti.esymmInt`).

TauCeti.diagonalChain_iff_equivalent.signature:

TauCeti.diagonalChain_iff_equivalent.doc:
**Witt's chain theorem** in its nontrivial range: two diagonal forms of rank at least two are
isometric if and only if their coefficient families are connected by a diagonal chain.

module is the underlying cochain complex of `M`.

**The differential graded Yoneda lemma** in degree zero: a morphism of differential graded
right modules out of the free rank-one module is the same thing as a degree-zero cycle of `M`.

TauCeti.dgYonedaEquiv.signature:

closed degree-zero elements of `F(X)`.  A transformation goes to the image of the identity of `X`
under its component at `X` (`TauCeti.dgYonedaEquiv_apply_coe`), and a closed element `x` goes to
the transformation sending `g : Y ⟶ X` to `F(g)(x)` (`TauCeti.dgApp_dgYonedaEquiv_symm_v`).

right-module cochains of degree `p` out of the free rank-one module with the degree-`p` part of
`M`.  The inverse sends `x` to right multiplication `a ↦ x * a`.

**The DG Yoneda lemma**: evaluation at the identity of `X` is an isomorphism from the Hom
complex of right DG modules `Hom(Hom(-, X), F)` to the complex `F(X)`.

TauCeti.dgRepresentableHomEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.dgRepresentableHomEquiv.{v} (R : Type v) [CommRing R] {C : Type v} [TauCeti.DGCategory R C]

(`TauCeti.dgApp_dgRepresentableHomEquiv_symm_v`).

TauCeti.det_submatrix_hsymmToeplitz.signature:
TauCeti.det_submatrix_hsymmToeplitz.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} (σ : Type u_1) [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ]

polynomials.** A minor of `(h_{j - i})` on the rows `ρ (p)` and the columns `π (p)` is the
complementary minor of `((-1)^{j - i} e_{j - i})`, on the rows `π (m)` and the columns `ρ (m)`,
signed by `π` and `ρ`.

TauCeti.det_mul_transpose_eq_sum_plucker.signature:
TauCeti.det_mul_transpose_eq_sum_plucker_mul.{u_1, u_3} {R : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_3} [CommRing R]

`∑ₖ x i k * y j k` is the sum over the `p`-element subsets `s` of `ι` of the products of the
Plücker coordinates of `x` and `y` at `s`. For `p > #ι` both sides vanish.

TauCeti.det_mul_conjTranspose_eq_sum_plu.doc:
**The Cauchy–Binet formula, Hermitian form.** Over a commutative star ring, the determinant
of the Hermitian Gram matrix `∑ₖ x i k * star (x j k)` of a family is the sum of the products of
its Plücker coordinates with their conjugates.

TauCeti.dense_setOf_stabilizer_eq_ker_of.doc:
**The principal part of a finite smooth action.** For a finite group acting by `C¹` maps on a
preconnected Hausdorff manifold without boundary, the points whose stabilizer is the kernel of the
action form a dense set. The action need not be faithful: elements acting trivially are retained
in every stabilizer, and generically they are the only ones. The set is also open, by
`TauCeti.isOpen_setOf_stabilizer_eq_ker`.

TauCeti.dense_setOf_stabilizer_eq_ker.signature:

TauCeti.dense_setOf_stabilizer_eq_ker.doc:
**Generic stabilizer of a finite linear action.** For a finite group acting linearly and
continuously on a Hausdorff topological module over a ring in which `0` is a limit of units, for
instance a finite-dimensional real vector space, the points whose stabilizer is the kernel of the
action form a dense set. The action need not be faithful. The set is also open, by
`TauCeti.isOpen_setOf_stabilizer_eq_ker`.

TauCeti.dense_setOf_exists_norm_apply_eq.doc:
**The Bishop–Phelps theorem.** The continuous linear functionals on a Banach space which
attain their norm on the closed unit ball are norm dense in the dual.

TauCeti.dense_representativeSubmodule.signature:
TauCeti.dense_representativeSubmodule.{u_1, u_2} (𝕜 : Type u_1) (G : Type u_2) [RCLike 𝕜] [Group G]

  Dense ↑(TauCeti.representativeSubmodule 𝕜 G)
TauCeti.dense_representativeSubmodule.doc:
**The Peter-Weyl density theorem.** The representative ring `𝓡(G)` of a compact group is
uniformly dense in `C(G, 𝕜)`. Hausdorffness is not needed: the mollifiers the proof runs on are
built without it.

**Sard--Smale**, in the form transversality arguments consume: the regular values of a
sufficiently smooth Fredholm map restricted to a Lindelöf subset are dense, being the complement
of a meagre set in a Baire space. The regularity threshold is that of
`TauCeti.isMeagre_image_criticalPoints_of_isFredholm`.

TauCeti.denseRange_mul_sub_intCast.doc:
**Kronecker's theorem, density form.** If `1` and the real numbers `αᵢ` satisfy no
nontrivial integer relation, that is, if they are linearly independent over `ℚ`, then the
points `(y αᵢ - xᵢ)ᵢ`, for `y ∈ ℤ` and `x ∈ ℤ^ι`, are dense in `ℝ^ι`.

square to order `2 v_K(2) + 1` is a square, so the defect exponent of a nonsquare unit is at most
`2 v_K(2)`. In odd residue characteristic the bound is `0`.

    ↑↑σ =
      TauCeti.RoughForm.extendByZero (U ⊔ V)
        (TauCeti.mextDeriv fun y => ρ (TopologicalSpace.Opens.inclusion ⋯ y) • ↑↑φ y)) :
  (TauCeti.deRhamCohomology.mayerVietorisδ I U V k) ((TauCeti.deRhamCohomology.mk I k) φ) =
    (TauCeti.deRhamCohomology.mk I (k + 1)) σ
TauCeti.deRhamCohomology.mayerVietorisδ_.doc:
**The Mayer–Vietoris connecting map through a cut-off function.** Let `ρ` be a smooth function
on `U ⊔ V` supported in `V` such that `1 - ρ` is supported in `U`, and let `φ` be a closed form on
`U ⊓ V`. If `σ` is the closed form on `U ⊔ V` extending `d(ρ φ)` by zero
(`TauCeti.exists_closedForms_coe_eq_extendByZero_mextDeriv`), then the connecting map sends the
class of `φ` to the class of `σ`.

TauCeti.deRhamCohomology.map_eq_of_homot.doc:
**Homotopy invariance of de Rham cohomology.** If `F : M × [0, 1] → M'` is a smooth
homotopy from `f` to `g`, then `f` and `g` induce the same map on de Rham cohomology. The source
`M` may have boundary or corners.

TauCeti.cyclicTwoCohomPolynomialEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.cyclicTwoCohomPolynomialEquiv.{u} (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
  [IsTopologicalGroup G] [DiscreteTopology G] (hG : Nat.card G = 2) :
  Polynomial (ZMod 2) ≃ₐ[ZMod 2] TauCeti.gradedCohomF2 G
TauCeti.cyclicTwoCohomPolynomialEquiv.doc:
The canonical graded mod-two cohomology algebra of an order-two discrete group is a
polynomial algebra, with `X` sent to its nontrivial character in degree one.

TauCeti.cyclicModuleRootPowProjectiveRes.signature:
TauCeti.cyclicModuleRootPowProjectiveResolution.{u} (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (n i : ℕ) :
  CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution

        Ideal.span {MulOpposite.op (AdjoinRoot.root (Polynomial.X ^ n) ^ i)})
TauCeti.cyclicModuleRootPowProjectiveRes.doc:
**The periodic free resolution of `M_i` over `R[X]/(X ^ n)`.** With `x` the class of `X`
and `M_i = A ⧸ (x ^ i)`, the complex
`⋯ ⟶ A --x^(n-i)--> A --x^i--> A --x^(n-i)--> A --x^i--> A ⟶ M_i ⟶ 0` is a projective
resolution of `M_i`.

TauCeti.cyclicConnectingEquiv.doc:
**The connecting isomorphism `H¹(C_m, T) ≃ H²(C_m, Λ)`.** When multiplication by `m` is
bijective on `E`, for instance when `E` is a real vector space, the cohomology of `E` vanishes in
positive degrees and the connecting homomorphism of `0 → Λ → E → T → 0` is an isomorphism.

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.selfEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.selfEquiv.{u, u_1} (R : Type u) (M : Type u_1) [CommRing R]

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.selfEquiv.doc:
If multiplication by `2` is injective on `M`, then `HCⁿ(R; M) ≅ M` in every even degree `n`,
by the class of the product cochain. In particular `HC²ᵏ(ℂ) ≅ ℂ`.

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.oddPairing_matr.doc:
**Stabilization of the odd pairing**: enlarging an invertible matrix `u` to the block diagonal
matrix `u ⊕ 1` does not change its odd pairing.

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.oddPairing.signature:
TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.oddPairing.{u_1, u_2} {A : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Ring A] [Algebra ℂ A]

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.oddPairing.doc:
**Connes' odd pairing** `⟨[u], [φ]⟩ = (1 + i)⁻¹ 2⁻ⁿ Γ(n/2 + 1)⁻¹ φ(u⁻¹ - 1, u - 1, …, u - 1)`
of an invertible `u` with cyclic cohomology classes of odd degree `n = 2m + 1`.

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.matrixExtension.signature:
TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.matrixExtension.{u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {R : Type u_4} {A : Type u_5}

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.matrixExtension.doc:
The map `HCⁿ(A; M) → HCⁿ(Matrix ι ι A; M)` on cyclic cohomology induced by matrix extension of
cyclic cocycles.

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.evenPairing_uni.signature:
TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.evenPairing_units_conj.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2}
  {M : Type u_3} [Field R] [CharZero R] [Ring A] [Algebra R A] [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module R M]

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.evenPairing_uni.doc:
**Conjugation invariance of the even pairing.** Conjugating an idempotent by a unit does not
change its even pairing with cyclic cohomology.

TauCeti.cycleCocycle.doc: The character of a cycle, as a cyclic cocycle.

TauCeti.cwComplexPreimage.signature:
TauCeti.cwComplexPreimage.{u} {E B : Type u} [TopologicalSpace B] {p : E → B} (C : Set B)
  [TopologicalSpace E] [Topology.CWComplex C] [T2Space B] (hp : IsCoveringMap p) :
  Topology.CWComplex (p ⁻¹' C)
TauCeti.cwComplexPreimage.doc:
**A CW structure lifts along a covering map.** If `C` is a CW complex in the Hausdorff space
`B` and `p : E → B` is a covering map, then `p ⁻¹' C` is a CW complex in `E`. Its `n`-cells are the
pairs of an `n`-cell of `C` and a point of `E` over the centre of that cell
(`TauCeti.cellPreimageEquiv`); the characteristic map of such a pair is the lift of the
characteristic map of the cell through `p` sending the centre to the chosen point.

TauCeti.curry_le_residual.signature:
TauCeti.curry_le_residual.{u_1, u_2} {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [TopologicalSpace Y] [SecondCountableTopology Y] :
  (residual X).curry (residual Y) ≤ residual (X × Y)
TauCeti.curry_le_residual.doc:
**One half of the Kuratowski–Ulam theorem.** If `Y` is second countable, every comeagre subset
of `X × Y` has comeagre sections `(x, ·) ⁻¹' s` over a comeagre set of `x`.

TauCeti.cup_kummerClass_eq_zero_iff.signature:
TauCeti.cup_kummerClass_eq_zero_iff.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Invertible 2] (a b : Kˣ) :
  (((TauCeti.trivialF2TopPairing (TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup K)).cup 1 1) (TauCeti.kummerClass a))
        (TauCeti.kummerClass b) =
      0 ↔
    ∃ x y, ↑b = x ^ 2 - ↑a * y ^ 2
TauCeti.cup_kummerClass_eq_zero_iff.doc:
**The cup-norm theorem.** For units `a` and `b` of a field in which `2` is invertible, the cup
product `(a) ∪ (b) ∈ H²(G_K, 𝔽₂)` of their Kummer classes vanishes if and only if the norm
equation `b = x² - a y²` has a solution in `K`.

TauCeti.cup_kummerClass_eq_hilbertSymbol.signature:
TauCeti.cup_kummerClass_eq_hilbertSymbol_smul.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K] [ValuativeRel K]
  [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] [Invertible 2] {c e : Kˣ}
  (hce : TauCeti.hilbertSymbol c e = -1) (a b : Kˣ) :
  (((TauCeti.trivialF2TopPairing (TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup K)).cup 1 1) (TauCeti.kummerClass a))
      (TauCeti.kummerClass b) =
    TauCeti.additiveIntUnitsAddEquiv (Additive.ofMul (TauCeti.hilbertSymbol a b)) •
      (((TauCeti.trivialF2TopPairing (TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup K)).cup 1 1)
          (TauCeti.kummerClass c))
        (TauCeti.kummerClass e)
TauCeti.cup_kummerClass_eq_hilbertSymbol.doc:
**A Kummer cup over a local field is its Hilbert symbol times a fixed nonzero cup**: if
`(c, e)_K = -1`, then `(a) ∪ (b) = ε • ((c) ∪ (e))`, where `ε ∈ ZMod 2` is `0` if `(a, b)_K = 1`
and `1` if `(a, b)_K = -1`.

TauCeti.criticalHessian.signature:
TauCeti.criticalHessian.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {E : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace H] [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace H M] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) :
  TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] ℝ
TauCeti.criticalHessian.doc:
The **critical Hessian** of a real function `f` at a point `x` of a manifold: the second
derivative at `extChartAt I x x` of the coordinate expression of `f` in the preferred extended
chart, as a bilinear form on the tangent space at `x`.

Like `TauCeti.manifoldMorseIndex`, the definition makes sense at every point and carries no
regularity hypotheses. At a critical point of a `C²` function on a manifold without boundary it is
intrinsic: `TauCeti.criticalHessian_apply_eq_of_mem_maximalAtlas` computes it in an arbitrary chart
there. At a noncritical point it depends on the preferred chart, and on a manifold with boundary
or corners it may also depend on the chart inverse outside `range I`.

TauCeti.countable_infEquivAt_nat_iff_iso.doc:
**Karp's theorem for countable structures.** Countable structures in a relational language are
isomorphic exactly when they satisfy the same `L_{ω₁ω}` sentences, the infinitary sentences whose
conjunctions and disjunctions are indexed by `ℕ`.

TauCeti.convexSection.signature:
TauCeti.convexSection.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module ℝ E] (Ω : Set E)
  (u : E → ℝ) (x : E) (ℓ : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (h : ℝ) : Set E
TauCeti.convexSection.doc: The section of `u` on `Ω` at `x`, with slope `ℓ` and strict height `h`.

TauCeti.convexOn_of_midpoint.signature:
TauCeti.convexOn_of_midpoint.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module ℝ E]
  [TopologicalSpace E] [IsTopologicalAddGroup E] [ContinuousSMul ℝ E] {s : Set E} {f : E → ℝ}
  (hs : Convex ℝ s) (hf : ContinuousOn f s)
  (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, f (midpoint ℝ x y) ≤ (f x + f y) / 2) : ConvexOn ℝ s f
TauCeti.convexOn_of_midpoint.doc:
**Jensen's theorem.** On a convex subset of a real topological vector space, a continuous
function that is midpoint convex is convex.

TauCeti.continuous_restrictedProductSum_.signature:
TauCeti.continuous_restrictedProductSum_symm_of_principal.{u₁, u₂, v, w} {ι₁ : Type u₁}

  {T : Set (ι₁ ⊕ ι₂)} (hT₁ : Filter.comap Sum.inl (Filter.principal T) = 𝓕₁)
  (hT₂ : Filter.comap Sum.inr (Filter.principal T) = 𝓕₂) :
  Continuous ⇑(TauCeti.restrictedProductSum U hT₁ hT₂).symm
TauCeti.continuous_restrictedProductSum_.doc:
For a principal filter on `ι₁ ⊕ ι₂` the inverse of the splitting is continuous for every
reference family, so that the splitting is a homeomorphism: the target is a principal stage,
whose topology is induced from the product.

TauCeti.continuous_rationalDiagonal.signature:
TauCeti.continuous_rationalDiagonal.{u, v, w} {ι : Type u} {G : ι → Type v} [(i : ι) → Group (G i)]
  {Γ : Type w} [MulOneClass Γ] [TopologicalSpace Γ] [(i : ι) → TopologicalSpace (G i)]
  (φ : (i : ι) → Γ →* G i) (U : (i : ι) → Subgroup (G i))
  (h : ∀ (γ : Γ), ∀ᶠ (i : ι) in Filter.cofinite, (φ i) γ ∈ U i)

  (huniform : ∀ (γ : Γ), ∀ i ∈ S, (φ i) γ ∈ U i) : Continuous ⇑(TauCeti.rationalDiagonal φ U h)
TauCeti.continuous_rationalDiagonal.doc:
The diagonal is continuous when the coordinate maps are continuous and there is one cofinite
set of indices at which every `γ` is integral. Pointwise eventual integrality alone builds the
map but is not enough for continuity, because the restricted-product topology is finer than the
topology induced from the full product.

TauCeti.continuous_outerAction.signature:
TauCeti.continuous_outerAction.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [Group E] [TopologicalSpace E] {N : Subgroup E}
  [N.Normal] [IsTopologicalGroup E] [CompactSpace ↥N] : Continuous ⇑(TauCeti.outerAction N)
TauCeti.continuous_outerAction.doc:
For compact `N`, the outer action `E ⧸ N → ContinuousOut N` is continuous for the quotient
topologies.

TauCeti.continuous_eval_and_not_continuo.signature:
TauCeti.continuous_eval_and_not_continuous_rationalDiagonal_range_coeMonoidHom.{u, v} {ι : Type u}
  {G : ι → Type v} [(i : ι) → Group (G i)] [(i : ι) → TopologicalSpace (G i)]
  [∀ (i : ι), DiscreteTopology (G i)] (hG : {i | Nontrivial (G i)}.Infinite) :
  (∀ (i : ι),

    ¬Continuous

            (fun i => (Pi.evalMonoidHom G i).comp RestrictedProduct.coeMonoidHom.range.subtype)
            (fun x => ⊥) ⋯)
TauCeti.continuous_eval_and_not_continuo.doc:
The uniform integrality set in `continuous_rationalDiagonal` cannot be dropped. Take
discrete groups with trivial reference subgroups, infinitely many of them nontrivial, and for `Γ`
the range of the coercion from the restricted product to the full product, that is, the finitely
supported elements, with the topology induced from the full product. The coordinate maps are
continuous and every element of `Γ` is eventually integral (it is the coercion of an element of
the restricted product), but the diagonal is not continuous:
it would make the restricted-product topology the one induced from the full product,
contradicting `not_isInducing_coe_bot`.

TauCeti.continuous_continuousConnesB.signature:
TauCeti.continuous_continuousConnesB.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (𝕜 : Type u_1) (A : Type u_2) (M : Type u_3)

TauCeti.continuous_continuousConnesB.doc: Connes' operator is continuous for bounded convergence of cochains.

TauCeti.continuous_awayDecomposition_sym.signature:
TauCeti.continuous_awayDecomposition_symm.{u, v} {ι : Type u} {G : ι → Type v}
  [(i : ι) → Group (G i)] (S : Set ι) (hS : S.Finite) (U : (i : ι) → Subgroup (G i))

TauCeti.continuous_awayDecomposition_sym.doc:
The inverse of the decomposition is continuous when the reference subgroups away from `S` are
open; the reference subgroups at `S` play no role, since the finite factor carries no integrality
condition. Together with `continuous_awayDecomposition` this makes the decomposition a
homeomorphism for such families.

TauCeti.continuous_and_isPositiveDefinit.signature:
TauCeti.continuous_and_isPositiveDefiniteSub_of_integral_fourierAtom_eq.{u_1} {V : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V]
  [BorelSpace V] {F : V → ℂ} (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure V) [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ]
  (hrep : ∀ (v : V), F v = ∫ (q : V), TauCeti.fourierAtom v q ∂μ) :
  Continuous F ∧ TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub F
TauCeti.continuous_and_isPositiveDefinit.doc:
**Converse half of Bochner's theorem.** The Fourier-convention transform of a finite Borel
measure is continuous and positive definite.

TauCeti.continuous_and_isPositiveDefinit.signature:
TauCeti.continuous_and_isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_existsUnique_innerRegular_pontryaginMeasureTransform_eq.{u_1}
  {G : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalAddGroup G]

TauCeti.continuous_and_isPositiveDefinit.doc:
**Bochner's characterization without countability assumptions.** A function on a locally
compact abelian group is continuous and positive definite if and only if it is the
Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a unique finite inner regular measure on the Pontryagin dual.

TauCeti.continuousDerivationsEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.continuousDerivationsEquiv.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] :
  LaurentSeries K ≃ₗ[LaurentSeries K] ↥(TauCeti.continuousDerivations K)
TauCeti.continuousDerivationsEquiv.doc:
**The continuous derivations of `K⸨X⸩` form a free module of rank one** with basis the formal
derivative `D`: the equivalence sends `a` to `a • D`, and its inverse evaluates a derivation at the
parameter `X`.

TauCeti.continuousCyclicCochains.signature:
TauCeti.continuousCyclicCochains.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (R : Type u_1) (A : Type u_2) (M : Type u_3)
  [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid A] [_root_.Module R A] [TopologicalSpace A] [AddCommGroup M]
  [_root_.Module R M] [SMulCommClass R R M] [TopologicalSpace M] [ContinuousConstSMul R M]
  [ContinuousAdd M] (n : ℕ) : Submodule R (A [×n + 1]→L[R] M)
TauCeti.continuousCyclicCochains.doc: The submodule of jointly continuous cochains satisfying the signed cyclic relation.

TauCeti.continuesInside_iff_exists_analy.signature:
TauCeti.continuesInside_iff_exists_analyticOnNhd.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E] {U : Set ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {f₀ : ℂ → E} (hUo : IsOpen U)
  (hUc : IsSimplyConnected U) (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ U) :
  TauCeti.ContinuesInside f₀ U z₀ ↔ ∃ F, AnalyticOnNhd ℂ F U ∧ F =ᶠ[nhds z₀] f₀
TauCeti.continuesInside_iff_exists_analy.doc:
**The monodromy theorem, in two-way form.** On a simply connected open set `U`, a germ at a
point `z₀ ∈ U` continues along every path in `U` from `z₀` if and only if it is the germ of a
function analytic on all of `U`.

The forward direction is `TauCeti.ContinuesInside.exists_analyticOnNhd`; the reverse is the
observation that a holomorphic function is its own continuation.

TauCeti.continuedLFunctionOfWeight_ne_ze.signature:
TauCeti.continuedLFunctionOfWeight_ne_zero_of_hasCancellation_sq.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  [NumberField K] {χ : TauCeti.UnitaryIdealWeight K} (hχ : TauCeti.HasCancellation χ)
  (hχ₂ : TauCeti.HasCancellation (χ ^ 2)) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 ≤ s.re) :
  TauCeti.continuedLFunctionOfWeight χ s ≠ 0
TauCeti.continuedLFunctionOfWeight_ne_ze.doc:
**Nonvanishing when the square also cancels.** If a unitary weight `χ` and its pointwise
square `χ ^ 2` both have cancellation, the continued L-function of `χ` has no zeros on the closed
half-plane `Re s ≥ 1`.

TauCeti.continuedLFunctionOfWeight.signature:
TauCeti.continuedLFunctionOfWeight.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (χ : TauCeti.UnitaryIdealWeight K) (s : ℂ) : ℂ
TauCeti.continuedLFunctionOfWeight.doc:
**The continued L-function of a unitary weight**, defined by partial summation:
`s * ∫_{1}^{∞} (∑_{N(I) ≤ t} χ(I)) t ^ (-(s + 1)) dt`.

On `Re s > 1` it is the norm-regrouped L-series of `χ`
(`TauCeti.continuedLFunctionOfWeight_eq_LSeries`); under `TauCeti.HasCancellation χ` it is
holomorphic on `Re s > 1 - 1 / [K : ℚ]` (`TauCeti.differentiableOn_continuedLFunctionOfWeight`).
Where the integral does not converge it takes the junk value of Mathlib's Bochner integral.

TauCeti.contMDiff_orbitRelQuotientMap.doc:
For free properly discontinuous actions by `C^n` maps on `C^n` manifolds and `m ≤ n`, a
`C^m` map carrying one action to the other along `σ` induces a `C^m` map of orbit spaces.

TauCeti.contMDiff_orbitRelQuotientLift_i.signature:
TauCeti.contMDiff_orbitRelQuotientLift_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7, u_8} {G : Type u_1}

TauCeti.contMDiff_iff_mdifferentiable.doc:
A map between complex manifolds is `C^n`, for any `n ≠ 0`, if and only if it is
holomorphic.

For a boundaryless model on a finite-dimensional complex space, the `C^m` and `C^n` groupoids
agree whenever `m` and `n` are nonzero.

of exponent `-1` give the principal logarithm of their fractional-linear ratio, after
scaling by their separation and translating by the value at the base point.

in `ℂ^N`: a line belongs to it when every polynomial of the family vanishes at every vector of
the line. The line of `L` is `L.submodule`, which is the underlying submodule of
`Projectivization.equivSubmodule ℂ (Fin N → ℂ) L`.

**The lattice form of Weyl's theorem**: the Lie submodules of a finite-dimensional module over

TauCeti.compactlySupportedDeRhamCohomolo.doc:
Integration `H^n_c(M) → ℝ` over an oriented boundaryless manifold, induced by integrating
compactly supported closed top forms.

The map on compactly supported de Rham cohomology induced by extension by zero along an

Compactly supported de Rham cohomology is the categorical homology of the compactly

  (hα : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 1, extDeriv α (ψ t x) = ω₁ (ψ t x) - ω₀ (ψ t x))
  (hX :

**Moser's identity.** Let `ω₀`, `ω₁` be forms that are closed along the orbit `t ↦ ψₜ x`,
`t ∈ [0, 1]`, with `ω₁ - ω₀ = dα` there. If `ψₜ` moves along a time-dependent field `Xₜ` with
`ι_{Xₜ} ((1 - t) • ω₀ + t • ω₁) = -α` near the orbit, and the derivative of `ψₜ` at `x` solves the
variational equation, then `ψ₁^* ω₁ = ψ₀^* ω₀` at `x`.

TauCeti.coinduction.signature:
TauCeti.coinduction.{w, u₁, u, u_1} {R : Type u₁} {A : Type u} [Ring R] [Ring A] (f : R →+* A)

The *coinduction* of `R`-modules to smooth `A`-modules along `f : R →+* A`: the smooth part of
the coextension of scalars `Hom_R(A, V)`, which is the module of continuous `R`-linear maps
`A → V` when the `J i` form a basis of neighborhoods of `0`
(`TauCeti.mem_smoothPart_coextendScalars_iff_continuous`).

TauCeti.coeff_rayTorusWeightSeries.doc:
**Independent-component expansion** of the ray series: its `n`-th coefficient is the sum,
over all configurations `l` of total class `n • A₀` (the elements of
`s.weightedFinsuppAntidiag m n`), of the products of the local weights
`w_(σ c, i c)(l c)`.

TauCeti.coeff_inv_smul_𝔾ₐ_toPowerSeries_.signature:
TauCeti.coeff_inv_smul_𝔾ₐ_toPowerSeries_mem.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [CommRing K] {p : ℕ}
  [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {σ : K →+* K} {s : ℕ → K} {A : Subring K} (hσ : Set.MapsTo ⇑σ ↑A ↑A)
  (hσp : ∀ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, σ a - a ^ p = ↑p * b) (hs : ∀ (i : ℕ), ↑p * s i ∈ A)

TauCeti.coeff_inv_smul_𝔾ₐ_toPowerSeries_.doc:
**Hazewinkel's functional equation lemma.** Let `f = b₁ X + ⋯` be a formal coordinate over `K`
whose linear coefficient `b₁` is a unit of `A`, and suppose that `f` satisfies the functional
equation. Then the formal group law `f⁻¹(f(X) + f(Y))` with logarithm `f`, the transport
`f⁻¹ • 𝔾ₐ` of the additive formal group law, has all its coefficients in `A`.

TauCeti.closedZpowers_lieExp_eq_top_iff.signature:
TauCeti.closedZpowers_lieExp_eq_top_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] {H : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} {G : Type u_3}
  [TopologicalSpace G] [ChartedSpace H G] [Group G] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [LieGroup I (↑⊤) G]

TauCeti.closedZpowers_lieExp_eq_top_iff.doc:
**Kronecker's criterion**: `lieExp X` is a topological generator of a connected commutative
Lie group if and only if `Λ + ℤ X` is dense in the Lie algebra, `Λ` the kernel of the
exponential.

TauCeti.closedSubgroup_units_two_classif.signature:
TauCeti.closedSubgroup_units_two_classification {A : Subgroup ℤ_[2]ˣ} (hA : IsClosed ↑A)
  (hA' : A ≠ ⊥) :
  (∃ f, 2 ≤ f ∧ A = TauCeti.unitsPrincipal 2 f) ∨
    (∃ f, 2 ≤ f ∧ A = TauCeti.unitsPlusMinus f) ∨
      A = Subgroup.zpowers (-1) ∨
        ∃ f u, 2 ≤ f ∧ ↑u = -1 + 2 ^ f ∧ A = (Subgroup.zpowers u).topologicalClosure
TauCeti.closedSubgroup_units_two_classif.doc:
**Labute's classification of the closed subgroups of `ℤ_2ˣ`.** Every nontrivial closed
subgroup of `ℤ_2ˣ` is a principal unit group `U^(f)` with `f ≥ 2`, a subgroup
`V^(f) = {±1} × U^(f)` with `f ≥ 2`, the subgroup `{±1}`, or a twisted subgroup `U^[f]` with
`f ≥ 2`, generated by `-1 + 2 ^ f`. The four families are pairwise distinct and faithfully indexed
by `f`: `unitsPrincipal_inj`, `unitsPlusMinus_inj`, `topologicalClosure_zpowers_two_eq_iff` and
the `ne` lemmas above.

TauCeti.clifford_restrict_character.signature:
TauCeti.clifford_restrict_character.{u, v} {k : Type u} {G : Type v} [Field k] [Group G]
  {N : Subgroup G} [N.Normal] [Finite G] [IsAlgClosed k] (hG : IsUnit ↑(Nat.card G)) (W : FDRep k G)
  [CategoryTheory.Simple W] :
  ∃ V,
    ∃ (_ : CategoryTheory.Simple V),
      ∃ e reps,
        e ≠ 0 ∧
          (∀ (g : G), ∃! r, r ∈ reps ∧ g⁻¹ * r ∈ TauCeti.inertia V) ∧
            ∀ (n : ↥N), W.character ↑n = ↑e * ∑ g ∈ reps, (TauCeti.conjNormalFDRep g V).character n
TauCeti.clifford_restrict_character.doc:
**Clifford's theorem, character form.**  The character of the restriction of an irreducible
representation to a normal subgroup is a positive common multiple of the sum of the distinct
conjugates of a fixed irreducible constituent, indexed by representatives of the left cosets of its
inertia group.  The finite set `reps` is a genuine left transversal for the inertia group: for every
`g`, it contains a unique `r` with `g⁻¹ * r ∈ inertia V`.

The hypothesis on `Nat.card G` is Maschke's condition.  Algebraic closure makes `k` a splitting
field, so irreducible characters form an orthonormal basis and their pairings compute
multiplicities.

TauCeti.classifyingSpaceSingularHomology.signature:
TauCeti.classifyingSpaceSingularHomologyIsoGroupHomology.{u} (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (G : Type u)

    groupHomology (Rep.trivial k G k) n
TauCeti.classifyingSpaceSingularHomology.doc:
**The singular homology of the classifying space is group homology**: for every group `G`,
the singular homology `Hₙ(BG; k)` of Milnor's classifying space with coefficients in a
commutative ring `k` is Mathlib's group homology `Hₙ(G, k)` of the trivial representation. It
comes from the free resolution of `k` by the singular chains of `universalGSpace G`.

TauCeti.classifyingSpaceSingularCohomolo.signature:
TauCeti.classifyingSpaceSingularCohomologyIsoGroupCohomology.{u} (k : Type u) [CommRing k]
  (G : Type u) [Group G] (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module k M] (n : ℕ) :
