    groupCohomology (Rep.trivial k G M) n
TauCeti.classifyingSpaceSingularCohomolo.doc:
**The singular cohomology of the classifying space is group cohomology**: for every group
`G`, the singular cohomology `Hⁿ(BG; M)` of Milnor's classifying space with coefficients in a
module `M` over a commutative ring `k` is Mathlib's group cohomology `Hⁿ(G, M)` of the trivial
representation `M`. It comes from the free resolution of `k` by the singular chains of
`universalGSpace G`.

TauCeti.circleLIntegral_sq_le.signature:
TauCeti.circleLIntegral_sq_le {g : ℂ → ENNReal} (ζ : ℂ) (ρ : ℝ)
  (hg :
    AEMeasurable (fun θ => g (circleMap ζ ρ θ))
      (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ioo (-Real.pi) Real.pi))) :
  TauCeti.circleLIntegral g ζ ρ ^ 2 ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (2 * Real.pi * ρ) * TauCeti.circleLIntegral (fun z => g z ^ 2) ζ ρ
TauCeti.circleLIntegral_sq_le.doc:
**Cauchy–Schwarz on a circle.** The square of the circle integral of `g` is at most
`2 π ρ` — for `ρ > 0` the circumference of the circle — times the circle integral of `g ^ 2`.

Only the angular trace of `g` along the circle at hand need be measurable; nothing is assumed of
`g` off that circle. Both sides vanish for a nonpositive radius, so no positivity is assumed.

TauCeti.chebyshevTHilbertBasis.signature:
TauCeti.chebyshevTHilbertBasis.{u_1} (𝕜 : Type u_1) [RCLike 𝕜] :

**The Chebyshev `T` polynomials are a Hilbert basis of `L²(measureT)`.** Orthonormality is
`orthonormal_normalizedChebyshevTLp`; completeness is
`orthogonal_span_normalizedChebyshevTLp_eq_bot`.

TauCeti.chebyshevTEnvelopeHilbertBasis.signature:
TauCeti.chebyshevTEnvelopeHilbertBasis.{u_1} (𝕜 : Type u_1) [RCLike 𝕜] :

TauCeti.chebyshevTEnvelopeHilbertBasis.doc:
**The Chebyshev envelope functions are a Hilbert basis of `L²((-1, 1]; dx)`.** It is the
weight-in-the-function normalization, assembled from the same bridge as the weight-in-the-measure
basis `TauCeti.chebyshevTHilbertBasis`: orthonormality from the Chebyshev orthogonality relation,
completeness from moment determinacy applied to the exact-degree family `Tₙ`.

TauCeti.character_resFDRep_indFDRep_mack.signature:
TauCeti.character_resFDRep_indFDRep_mackey.{u} {k G : Type u} [Field k] [Group G] {H K : Subgroup G}

TauCeti.character_resFDRep_indFDRep_mack.doc:
**The Mackey decomposition formula, character form.**  For a finite-dimensional representation
`A` of a finite-index subgroup `H` and an element `x` of a subgroup `K`, the character of
`Res_K (Ind_H^G A)` at `x` is the sum, over the double cosets `K \ G / H`, of the characters of
the Mackey summands.

The character of `Ind_H^G A` at `x : K`, read on `G`, is
the same number: `FDRep.character_actionRes` is a `simp` lemma rewriting the left-hand side into
it.

TauCeti.chainsDesc_pathClassIntegral_mex.doc:
**Stokes' theorem on singular `1`-chains.** The integral of `dψ` along a singular `1`-chain is
the evaluation of the `0`-form `ψ` on its boundary.

TauCeti.cerfTheorem_iff_natCard_zerothHo.doc:
**Cerf's theorem as a count of path components.** Cerf's theorem holds exactly when the
diffeomorphism group of `S³` has two path components.

TauCeti.centralizer_span_range_map_const.signature:
TauCeti.centralizer_span_range_map_const_eq_range_permTensorActionAlgHom.{u_1} {k : Type u_1}
  {n d : ℕ} [Field k] [NeZero ↑d.factorial] :
  Subalgebra.centralizer k ↑(Submodule.span k (Set.range fun f => PiTensorProduct.map fun x => f)) =
    (TauCeti.permTensorActionAlgHom k n d).range
TauCeti.centralizer_span_range_map_const.doc:
**Schur-Weyl duality.** Over a field in which `d !` is nonzero, the commutant of the diagonal
operators `f^{⊗d}` on `(kⁿ)^{⊗d}`, taken over all endomorphisms `f` of `kⁿ`, is exactly the image
of the group algebra `k[S_d]` acting by permuting the tensor factors.

Together with `TauCeti.coe_centralizer_range_permTensorActionAlgHom_eq_span_range_map_const`, which
computes the commutant in the other direction, this says that the symmetric-group image and the
span of the diagonal operators are each other's commutants. The general linear group acts through
the invertible `g^{⊗d}`. The downstream theorem
`TauCeti.toSubmodule_range_tensorPowerRep_asAlgebraHom_eq_span_range_map_const` proves that these
span the same subalgebra, and
`TauCeti.centralizer_range_tensorPowerRep_asAlgebraHom_eq_range_permTensorActionAlgHom` gives the
resulting commutant of the image of `k[GLₙ]`.

TauCeti.centralizer_range_tensorPowerRep.signature:
TauCeti.centralizer_range_tensorPowerRep_eq_range_permTensorActionAlgHom.{u_1} {k : Type u_1}
  {n d : ℕ} [Field k] [Infinite k] [NeZero ↑d.factorial] :
  Subalgebra.centralizer k (Set.range ⇑(TauCeti.tensorPowerRep k n d)) =
    (TauCeti.permTensorActionAlgHom k n d).range
TauCeti.centralizer_range_tensorPowerRep.doc:
**Schur-Weyl duality for the group ranges:** the commutant of the general-linear group action
is the image of `k[S_d]`.

TauCeti.centralizer_range_tensorPowerRep.signature:
TauCeti.centralizer_range_tensorPowerRep_asAlgebraHom_eq_range_permTensorActionAlgHom.{u_1}
  {k : Type u_1} {n d : ℕ} [Field k] [Infinite k] [NeZero ↑d.factorial] :
  Subalgebra.centralizer k (Set.range ⇑(TauCeti.tensorPowerRep k n d).asAlgebraHom) =

finite-dimensional and nonnegatively graded, its degree-zero part is semisimple, the chosen

occur in the public statement.

then `(#x)² < 4 · #y`.

the sum running over the irreducible characters of `G`.

TauCeti.card_le_linearFormExponent.doc:

`θᵢ` satisfy no nontrivial integer relation, that is, if they are linearly independent over `ℚ`,
then the linear-form exponent of `θ` is at least `n`.

**The Hurwitz bound for the whole automorphism group**: over a constant field of characteristic
zero, a function field of genus `g ≥ 2` whose automorphism group is finite has
`|Aut(F / k)| ≤ 84 (g - 1)`.

TauCeti.card_add_orbitCount_le_length_ad.signature:

the number of points plus the number of cycles of its product is at most the length of `L`
plus twice the number of orbits of the group generated by `L`.

This is the disconnected form of `TauCeti.card_add_orbitCount_le_length_add_two`: each orbit
of the generated group is one connected component of the transposition graph.

TauCeti.card_add_orbitCount_le_length_ad.doc:
**Hurwitz's transposition bound.** If a list of transpositions generates a group acting
transitively on a finite type, its length is at least the number of points plus the number of
cycles of its product, minus two. Equivalently,
`Nat.card α + orbitCount L.prod ≤ L.length + 2`.

TauCeti.card_add_orbitCount_add_two_le_l.doc:
**Hurwitz's transposition bound with a defect.** Let `L ++ Equiv.swap a b :: M` be a list of
transpositions in which the factor `Equiv.swap a b` joins two points `a` and `b` that the group
generated by the later factors `M` already connects, but that lie in different cycles of the
product of `M`. Then the bound
`TauCeti.card_add_orbitCount_le_length_add_two_mul_card_orbits` is not attained: it holds with
`2` to spare.

For the surface of a ribbon graph or permutation triple, such a factor merges two cycles of the
product without joining two components, and so raises the genus.

TauCeti.brownBicollaring.doc:
**Brown's bicollaring theorem:** every locally flat embedding of the standard `n`-sphere
in the standard `(n + 1)`-sphere is globally bicollared, including `n = 0`.

subspace `V` of an arbitrary real normed space has a fixed point.

nonempty compact convex subset of a finite-dimensional real normed space has a fixed point. The

finite Galois `L ⊆ Kˢ` goes to the continuous class of the inflation of that cocycle; see
`brauerCohomologyEquiv_unique`.

Scalar extension of any two-torsion Brauer class corresponds under `ι` to
restriction of its mod-two Galois cohomology class.

TauCeti.braidEquivalent_of_isReduced_wor.doc:
**Matsumoto's theorem, relational form.** Two reduced words representing the same element
of a Coxeter group are connected by braid moves.

TauCeti.bochner_probabilityMeasure.signature:
TauCeti.bochner_probabilityMeasure.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup V]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] (F : V → ℂ) :

      MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧ ∀ (v : V), F v = ∫ (q : V), TauCeti.fourierAtom v q ∂μ
TauCeti.bochner_probabilityMeasure.doc:
**Bochner's theorem for normalized functions.** A function is continuous, positive definite
and normalized by `F 0 = 1` if and only if it is the Fourier-convention transform of a unique
*probability* measure; this is the characteristic-function form of the theorem. Normalization is
part of the equivalence: a probability representation forces `F 0 = 1`.

TauCeti.bochner_posSemidef.signature:
TauCeti.bochner_posSemidef.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] (F : V → ℂ) :
  (Continuous F ∧ Matrix.PosSemidef fun a b => F (a - b)) ↔
    ∃! μ, MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ ∧ ∀ (v : V), F v = ∫ (q : V), TauCeti.fourierAtom v q ∂μ
TauCeti.bochner_posSemidef.doc:
**Bochner's theorem, kernel form.** The subtraction kernel `(a, b) ↦ F (a - b)` of a
continuous function is positive semidefinite if and only if `F` is the Fourier-convention
transform of a unique finite Borel measure. This is `TauCeti.bochner` read through the
PD-function ↔ PD-kernel correspondence `TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_posSemidef`.

TauCeti.bochner_euclideanSpace.signature:
TauCeti.bochner_euclideanSpace (d : ℕ) (F : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℂ) :
  Continuous F ∧ TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub F ↔

          F v = ∫ (q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), TauCeti.fourierAtom v q ∂μ
TauCeti.bochner_euclideanSpace.doc:
**Bochner's theorem on `ℝᵈ`**: the specialization of `bochner` to Euclidean space. A
function on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` is continuous and positive definite if and only if it is
the Fourier transform of a unique finite positive measure.

TauCeti.bochner_charFun_real.signature:
TauCeti.bochner_charFun_real (F : ℝ → ℂ) :
  Continuous F ∧ TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub F ↔
    ∃! μ,
      MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ ∧
        ∀ (x : ℝ), F x = ∫ (ξ : ℝ), Complex.exp (↑x * ↑ξ * Complex.I) ∂μ
TauCeti.bochner_charFun_real.doc:
**Bochner's theorem on the real line**, in its classical form: a function `F : ℝ → ℂ` is
continuous and positive definite if and only if `F x = ∫ ξ, exp (i x ξ) dμ(ξ)` for a unique
finite Borel measure `μ` on `ℝ`.

TauCeti.bochner_charFun_probabilityMeasu.signature:
TauCeti.bochner_charFun_probabilityMeasure.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup V]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] (F : V → ℂ) :

    ∃! μ, MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧ MeasureTheory.charFun μ = F
TauCeti.bochner_charFun_probabilityMeasu.doc:
**The Bochner–Khinchin theorem.** A function `F` on a finite-dimensional real inner-product
space is continuous, positive definite and normalized by `F 0 = 1` if and only if it is the
characteristic function of a unique Borel probability measure.

TauCeti.bochner_charFun.signature:
TauCeti.bochner_charFun.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] (F : V → ℂ) :
  Continuous F ∧ TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub F ↔
    ∃! μ, MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ ∧ MeasureTheory.charFun μ = F
TauCeti.bochner_charFun.doc:
**Bochner's theorem, characteristic-function form.** A function `F` on a finite-dimensional
real inner-product space is continuous and positive definite if and only if it is the
characteristic function `v ↦ ∫ q, exp (i⟪q, v⟫) ∂μ` of a unique finite Borel measure `μ`.

TauCeti.bochnerMeasure.signature:
TauCeti.bochnerMeasure.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] (F : V → ℂ) : MeasureTheory.Measure V
TauCeti.bochnerMeasure.doc:
**The representing measure of Bochner's theorem**: the unique finite Borel measure whose
Fourier-convention transform is `F`, when `F` is continuous and positive definite, and the zero
measure otherwise.

TauCeti.bochner.signature:
TauCeti.bochner.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] (F : V → ℂ) :
  Continuous F ∧ TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub F ↔

TauCeti.bochner.doc:
**Bochner's theorem.** A function `F` on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space is
continuous and positive definite if and only if it is the Fourier-convention transform
`v ↦ ∫ q, fourierAtom v q ∂μ` of a unique finite Borel measure `μ`. Bochner (1932); Rudin,
*Fourier Analysis on Groups*, Theorem 1.4.3.

one uniquely parametrized regular boundary value makes the primitive a bijection onto the

TauCeti.bcr_zero_spatial_iff_hausdorff_b.signature:
TauCeti.bcr_zero_spatial_iff_hausdorff_bernstein_widder (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
  (TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD fun x => ↑(f ↑x.1)) ∧
      (Continuous fun x => ↑(f ↑x.1)) ∧ Bornology.IsBounded (Set.range fun x => ↑(f ↑x.1)) ↔
    TauCeti.IsContinuousCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f
TauCeti.bcr_zero_spatial_iff_hausdorff_b.doc:
**The zero-spatial BCR theorem is the Hausdorff--Bernstein--Widder theorem.**

For a real function `f`, the bounded, continuous positive-definite condition on
`(t, _) ↦ f t : ℝ≥0 × PUnit → ℂ` holds exactly when `f` is continuous on `[0, ∞)` and completely
monotone on `(0, ∞)`.

TauCeti.bcr_semigroup_bochner.signature:
TauCeti.bcr_semigroup_bochner.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] (F : NNReal × V → ℂ) :
  TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD F ∧ Continuous F ∧ Bornology.IsBounded (Set.range F) ↔
    ∃! μ, TauCeti.RepresentsLaplaceFourier μ F
TauCeti.bcr_semigroup_bochner.doc:
**The Berg--Christensen--Ressel representation theorem** (Berg--Christensen--Ressel 4.1.13).
A function on the involutive semigroup `ℝ≥0 × V`, for `V` a finite-dimensional real inner-product
space, is positive definite, continuous and bounded **if and only if** it is the Laplace--Fourier
transform of a unique finite measure on `ℝ≥0 × V`:

`F (t, a) = ∫ (p, q), exp (-t p) * exp (-2πi⟪a, q⟫) dμ (p, q)`.

The forward direction is `TauCeti.exists_representsLaplaceFourier` together with the transform
injectivity of `TauCeti.RepresentsLaplaceFourier.unique`; the converse direction is the elementary
fact that such a transform is positive definite, continuous, and bounded by the total mass.

TauCeti.badlyApproximable_of_natDegree_m.doc:
**Liouville's theorem in degree two.** A real number whose minimal polynomial over `ℚ` has
degree `2` is badly approximable.

TauCeti.awayDecomposition.signature:
TauCeti.awayDecomposition.{u, v} {ι : Type u} {G : ι → Type v} [(i : ι) → Group (G i)] (S : Set ι)
  (hS : S.Finite) (U : (i : ι) → Subgroup (G i)) :
  TauCeti.RestrictedProductGroup U ≃*
    TauCeti.RestrictedProductGroupWithFactor ((i : ↑S) → G ↑i) fun j => U ↑j
TauCeti.awayDecomposition.doc:
For a finite set `S` of indices, the decomposition of a restricted product as the plain
product of the factors at `S` times the restricted product away from `S`, coordinatewise the
identity in both directions: `x` goes to `((x i)_{i ∈ S}, (x i)_{i ∉ S})`, and `(y, z)` goes to
the element with coordinate `y ⟨i, _⟩` at `i ∈ S` and `z ⟨i, _⟩` at `i ∉ S`.

It is the composite of the reindexing along `Equiv.sumCompl (· ∈ S)`, the splitting over the sum
`S ⊕ {i // i ∉ S}`, and the collapse of the restricted product over the finite index type `S`.

TauCeti.artinSchreier_genus_formula.signature:
TauCeti.artinSchreier_genus_formula.{u, u', v, v'} {k : Type u} {k' : Type u'} {F : Type v}
  {F' : Type v'} [Field k] [Field k'] [Field F] [Field F'] [Algebra k k'] [Algebra k F]
  [Algebra k' F'] [Algebra F F'] [Algebra k F'] [IsScalarTower k k' F'] [IsScalarTower k F F']
  (hF : TauCeti.IsFunctionField k F) (hF' : TauCeti.IsFunctionField k' F') (p : ℕ)
  [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP F p] {y : F'} {u : F} (hgen : F⟮y⟯ = ⊤)
  (hy : y ^ p - y = (algebraMap F F') u) (S : Finset (TauCeti.Place k F))
  (m : TauCeti.Place k F → ℕ)
  (hpole : ∀ P ∈ S, ∃ w, P.ord (u - (w ^ p - w)) = -↑(m P) ∧ ¬↑p ∣ P.ord (u - (w ^ p - w)))
  (hreg : ∀ P ∉ S, ∃ w, u - (w ^ p - w) ∈ P.integers) [Algebra.IsSeparable k k']
  (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F) (hex' : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k' F')
  (hu : ∀ (w : F), w ^ p - w ≠ u) :
  ↑(Module.finrank k k') * (2 * ↑(TauCeti.genus k' F') - 2) =
    ↑p * (2 * ↑(TauCeti.genus k F) - 2) + (↑p - 1) * ∑ P ∈ S, (↑(m P) + 1) * ↑P.degree
TauCeti.artinSchreier_genus_formula.doc:
**The Artin--Schreier genus formula**, cross-multiplied for a possible constant-field
extension. The representatives may vary with the place. Pole orders are weighted by residue
field degrees, not by the number of poles.

TauCeti.apply_prod_ofFn_eq_sum_prod_free.doc:
The *moment–cumulant formula* for a word `a₁, …, aₙ` with `n ≥ 1` in multiplicative form:
`φ (a₁ * ⋯ * aₙ) = ∑_{π ∈ NC(n)} ∏_{B ∈ π} κ_B(a₁, …, aₙ)`.

TauCeti.apply_add_eq_zero_of_le_div_sub_.signature:
TauCeti.apply_add_eq_zero_of_le_div_sub_rpow_mul_rpow {φ : ℝ → ℝ} {k₀ M α β : ℝ} (hM : 0 < M)
  (hα : 0 < α) (hβ : 1 < β) (hφ : ∀ (h : ℝ), k₀ ≤ h → 0 ≤ φ h) (hanti : AntitoneOn φ (Set.Ici k₀))
  (hrec : ∀ (k h : ℝ), k₀ ≤ k → k < h → φ h ≤ (M / (h - k)) ^ α * φ k ^ β) :
  φ (k₀ + M * φ k₀ ^ ((β - 1) / α) * 2 ^ (β / (β - 1))) = 0
TauCeti.apply_add_eq_zero_of_le_div_sub_.doc:
**Stampacchia's lemma.** Let `φ` be nonnegative and antitone on `[k₀, ∞)`, with

`φ h ≤ (M / (h - k)) ^ α * φ k ^ β` whenever `k₀ ≤ k < h`,

for constants `M > 0`, `α > 0` and `β > 1`. Then `φ (k₀ + d) = 0`, where
`d = M * φ k₀ ^ ((β - 1) / α) * 2 ^ (β / (β - 1))`.

TauCeti.analyticSet_graph_iff_measurable.signature:
TauCeti.analyticSet_graph_iff_measurable.{u_1, u_2} {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2}

TauCeti.analyticSet_graph_iff_measurable.doc:
**The Borel graph theorem, analytic form.** A map between Polish spaces is measurable if and
only if its graph is analytic.

**`D_h ≤ p S_{h+1}`.** The dual stage norm at level `h` is at most `p` times the Gauss norm at
the radius `r_{h+1}`, provided the latter is the supremum of a bounded family.

TauCeti.amenable_iff_not_paradoxical_uni.signature:
TauCeti.amenable_iff_not_paradoxical_univ.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]

TauCeti.amenable_iff_not_paradoxical_uni.doc:
**Tarski's alternative**: a discrete group is amenable exactly when it is not paradoxical for
its left regular action.

TauCeti.amenable_iff_forall_finset_exist.signature:

TauCeti.amenable_iff_forall_finset_exist.doc:
Finite-intersection criterion: a topological group is amenable exactly when every finite
family of invariance equations `m (L_g f) = m f` is satisfied by some mean.

TauCeti.alternatingGroup_le_of_isPreprim.signature:

**Jordan's theorem for a cycle of prime length** (Wielandt, Theorem 13.9). A primitive
permutation group of degree at least `p + 3` that contains a cycle of prime length `p` contains
the alternating group.

TauCeti.algebraicIndependent_exp.signature:

**The Lindemann–Weierstrass theorem**, algebraic independence form. If the algebraic numbers
`u i` are linearly independent over `ℕ` (equivalently, over `ℚ`), then their exponentials are
algebraically independent over the field `integralClosure ℚ ℂ` of algebraic numbers.

The normed-field structure on an algebraic extension `M` of a nonarchimedean local field `K`
given by the spectral norm of `M/K` with respect to the normalized absolute value of `K`.

product space is almost everywhere strongly measurable exactly when it is weakly measurable, that

or zero, according to whether the point lies in the set.

finite-dimensional real inner product space with an additive Haar measure `μ`, and let
`F x = (f x).toReal`. At `μ`-almost every point `x` of the effective domain, `F` has a
second-order Taylor expansion
`F x' = F x + ⟪∇F x, x' - x⟫ + ⟪A (x' - x), x' - x⟫ / 2 + o(‖x' - x‖ ^ 2)`
with a positive operator `A`, the only positive operator giving such an expansion.

TauCeti.ae_existsUnique_isPositive_foral.doc:
**Alexandrov's theorem for the subdifferential.** Let `f : E → EReal` be convex (convex real
epigraph, never `⊥`) on a finite-dimensional real inner product space with an additive Haar measure
`μ`. At `μ`-almost every point `x` of the effective domain, the subdifferential of `f` is
differentiable with a positive derivative `A`: every subgradient `y'` of `f` at a point `x'` near
`x` satisfies `y' = ∇F x + A (x' - x) + o(‖x' - x‖)`, where `F x = (f x).toReal`. The operator `A`
is the only positive operator with this expansion; uniqueness among all operators is
`eq_of_forall_mem_subdifferential_norm_sub_le`.

real epigraph and never take the value `⊥`, on a finite-dimensional real normed space `E` with an
additive Haar measure `μ`. Then at `μ`-almost every point `x` of the effective domain, `f` is
finite on a neighbourhood of `x` and its real representative `x ↦ (f x).toReal` is
differentiable at `x`.

TauCeti.addHaar_image_eq_zero_of_not_surjective_fderivWithin.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1}

spaces of equal dimension. If `f` is differentiable along `s` with derivative `f'`, and `f'` is

space and may carry unrelated norms and Haar measure normalizations.

TauCeti.addHaar_image_eq_zero_of_iterate.signature:
TauCeti.addHaar_image_eq_zero_of_iteratedFDeriv_eq_zero_of_finrank_le_mul.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1}

set `U` of a finite-dimensional real normed space, and let `s ⊆ U` be a set at each point of which
every iterated derivative of order `1 ≤ i ≤ k` vanishes. If `finrank ℝ E ≤ k * finrank ℝ F` and

`C^{k+1}` to `C^k`, while the dimension hypothesis tightens from
`finrank ℝ E < (k + 1) * finrank ℝ F` to `finrank ℝ E ≤ k * finrank ℝ F`.

TauCeti.addHaar_image_eq_zero_of_iterate.signature:
TauCeti.addHaar_image_eq_zero_of_iteratedFDeriv_eq_zero.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}

  {k : ℕ} {s : Set E} [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ F] [MeasurableSpace F]
  [BorelSpace F] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure F) [ν.IsAddHaarMeasure] {U : Set E} (hU : IsOpen U)
  (hf : ContDiffOn ℝ (↑(k + 1)) f U) (hsU : s ⊆ U)
  (hzero : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ (i : ℕ), 1 ≤ i → i ≤ k → iteratedFDeriv ℝ i f x = 0)

TauCeti.addHaar_image_eq_zero_of_iterate.doc:
**Sard's lemma on the flat stratum.** Let `f` be `C^{k+1}` on an open set `U` of a
finite-dimensional real normed space, and let `s ⊆ U` be a set at each point of which every
iterated derivative of order `1 ≤ i ≤ k` vanishes. If `finrank ℝ E < (k + 1) * finrank ℝ F`, then
`f '' s` has additive Haar measure zero.

This is the slice of finite-dimensional Sard that higher regularity buys: for a fixed pair of
dimensions with positive-dimensional target, the hypothesis holds as soon as `k` is large enough.

TauCeti.addHaar_image_eq_zero_of_fderiv_.doc:
**Sard's theorem on the locus where the derivative vanishes, at the sharp regularity, in
codimension at most two.** Let `f` be a map between finite-dimensional real normed spaces with
nontrivial target and `finrank ℝ E ≤ finrank ℝ F + 2`, and let `s` be a set at each point of
which `f` is `C^n` and the Fréchet derivative of `f` vanishes. If
`finrank ℝ E - finrank ℝ F < n`, then `f '' s` has additive Haar measure zero.

TauCeti.addHaar_image_eq_zero_of_fderiv_.signature:
TauCeti.addHaar_image_eq_zero_of_fderiv_eq_zero.{u_1, u_2} {F : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup F]
  [NormedSpace ℝ F] [FiniteDimensional ℝ F] [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F] [Nontrivial F]
  (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure F) [ν.IsAddHaarMeasure] {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {f : E → F} {s : Set E} {n : WithTop ℕ∞}
  (hk : ↑(Module.finrank ℝ E * Module.finrank ℝ E + 1) ≤ n) (hf : ∀ x ∈ s, ContDiffAt ℝ n f x)
  (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, fderiv ℝ f x = 0) : ν (f '' s) = 0
TauCeti.addHaar_image_eq_zero_of_fderiv_.doc:
**Sard's theorem on the locus where the derivative vanishes.** Let `f` be a map between
finite-dimensional real normed spaces with nontrivial target, and let `s` be a set at each point
of which `f` is `C^n` and the Fréchet derivative of `f` vanishes. If
`((finrank ℝ E * finrank ℝ E + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞ω) ≤ n`, then `f '' s` has additive Haar measure zero.

No relation between the two dimensions is required, beyond a nontrivial (positive-dimensional)
target: the vanishing of the derivative, rather than a dimension count, is what the higher
derivatives are used against. The smoothness bound is sufficient, not the sharp exponent of the
Morse--Sard theorem.

TauCeti.addHaar_image_criticalPoints_eq_.signature:
TauCeti.addHaar_image_criticalPoints_eq_zero_of_finrank_le_add_two.{u, v} {E : Type u}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {F : Type v}
  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [FiniteDimensional ℝ F] [MeasurableSpace F]
  [BorelSpace F] {U : Set E} {f : E → F} (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure F) [ν.IsAddHaarMeasure]
  {n : WithTop ℕ∞} (hf : ∀ x ∈ U, ContDiffAt ℝ n f x)
  (hcodim : Module.finrank ℝ E ≤ Module.finrank ℝ F + 2)
  (hk : ↑(Module.finrank ℝ E - Module.finrank ℝ F + 1) ≤ n) :
  ν (f '' (U ∩ {x | ¬Function.Surjective ⇑(fderiv ℝ f x)})) = 0
TauCeti.addHaar_image_criticalPoints_eq_.doc:
**The Morse--Sard theorem at the sharp regularity, in codimension at most two.** If
`finrank ℝ E ≤ finrank ℝ F + 2` and the map is `C^n` at every point of `U` with
`finrank ℝ E - finrank ℝ F < n`, then the values taken at the points of `U` where the Fréchet
derivative is not surjective form a set of additive Haar measure zero. The set need not be open.

This is the regularity of Sard's theorem. It cannot be lowered in general: Whitney's `C¹`
function on the plane that is not constant along a connected arc of critical points has critical
values of positive measure.

**The Morse--Sard theorem** on a set. The values taken at the points of `U` where the Fréchet
derivative is not surjective form a set of additive Haar measure zero, provided the map is
sufficiently smooth at every point of `U`. The set need not be open, and no relation between the
two finite dimensions is required.

TauCeti.addAwayDecomposition.doc:
For a finite set `S` of indices, the decomposition of a
restricted product of additive groups as the plain product of the factors at `S` times the
restricted product away from `S`, coordinatewise the identity in both directions: `x` goes to
`((x i)_{i ∈ S}, (x i)_{i ∉ S})`, and `(y, z)` goes to the element with coordinate `y ⟨i, _⟩` at
`i ∈ S` and `z ⟨i, _⟩` at `i ∉ S`.

It is the composite of the reindexing along `Equiv.sumCompl (· ∈ S)`, the splitting over the sum
`S ⊕ {i // i ∉ S}`, and the collapse of the restricted product over the finite index type `S`.

projective height one if and only if, for every nonzero coordinate `x j`, each ratio `x i / x j`
is zero or of finite multiplicative order. This includes the zero tuple.

**The marked presentation of `G_{ℚ₂}(2)`.** There is an isomorphism
`e : G_{ℚ₂}(2) ≃ D₀ = ⟨A, S, Y ∣ A²S⁴(S,Y)⟩` along which the standard orientation of `D₀` pulls
back to the cyclotomic orientation of `G_{ℚ₂}(2)`, and the cyclotomic orientation is surjective.

**The marked presentation of `G_{ℚ₂(√-2)}(2)`.** The maximal pro-`2` Galois group of
`ℚ₂(√-2)` is isomorphic to `⟨x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄ ∣ x₁⁶ (x₁, x₂) x₃⁸ (x₃, x₄)⟩`, the even dyadic
Demushkin group with `α = 4` and `f = 3`, and under this isomorphism the cyclotomic orientation
satisfies `χ(x₂) · (1 + 4) = -1` and `χ(x₄) · (1 - 8) = 1` and is trivial on `x₁` and `x₃`.

This is `absoluteGaloisGroupProP_two_marked_of_degree_even_principal` at `N = 2`, with `k = 2`
read off the cyclotomic image `closure⟨-1 + 2²⟩`
(`range_localCyclotomicCharacter_ratPadicSqrtNegTwo`).

`TauCeti.absoluteGaloisGroupProP_two_marked_of_degree_odd`, the target must have the same odd degree
over `ℚ₂` as the source; an isomorphism of local fields over `ℚ₂` provides that

**Functoriality of the marked presentation in even degree.** The two even dyadic marked
theorems `TauCeti.absoluteGaloisGroupProP_two_marked_of_degree_even_plusMinus` and
`TauCeti.absoluteGaloisGroupProP_two_marked_of_degree_even_principal` present `G_K(2)` by the same
word `demushkinWordTwoEven a f (N + 2)` on `N + 2` generators and record the same values on the
second and fourth marked generators, the value `-(1 + a)⁻¹` and the value `(1 - 2^f)⁻¹`; they differ
only in the hypotheses that select the parameters `a` and `f`. Hence the transport of their marking
is a single statement. For `e : K ≃+* K'` an isomorphism of fields, the transported isomorphism
`(absoluteGaloisGroupProPCongr e).trans m` of a marked presentation of `G_K(2)` of the even form
presents `G_{K'}(2)` by the same relator word and takes the same values.

Only the transport of the recorded values is claimed, and it uses no property of `e` beyond being an
isomorphism of fields; the transport is the naturality of the cyclotomic orientation along the
induced isomorphism of the absolute Galois groups
(`TauCeti.cyclotomicOrientation_trans_absoluteGaloisGroupProPCongr`). For the transported
presentation to be *the* marked presentation of `G_{K'}(2)` in the sense of
`TauCeti.absoluteGaloisGroupProP_two_marked_of_degree_even_plusMinus` or
`TauCeti.absoluteGaloisGroupProP_two_marked_of_degree_even_principal`, the target must have the
same even degree over `ℚ₂` and the same cyclotomic image as the source; an isomorphism of local
fields over `ℚ₂` provides that (`TauCeti.isDyadicEvenPlusMinusCase_iff_of_algEquiv` and
`TauCeti.isDyadicEvenPrincipalCase_iff_of_algEquiv`).

TauCeti.abs_sub_taylorWithinEval_le.doc:
**Taylor's theorem with a bounded remainder.** If `f` is `C^(n+1)` and its `(n+1)`st
derivative is bounded in absolute value by `M`, then its Taylor polynomial of order `n` about `x₀`
approximates `f x` with error at most `M * |x - x₀|^(n+1) / (n+1)!`.

function such that `ĝ = u ^ (4 / (n - 2)) g` is a smooth metric. Then the scalar curvature of `ĝ`

The **conformal Laplacian** `L_g u = aₙ Δ⁺_g u + Scal_g u` of a function `u` on a smooth
Riemannian manifold of dimension `n`, where `aₙ = 4 (n - 1) / (n - 2)`, `Δ⁺_g = -Δ_g` is the
nonnegative Laplacian and `Scal_g` is the scalar curvature.

TauCeti.Yamabe.conformalCoefficient_mul_.doc:
**The bubbles attain the Yamabe constant of the sphere**: in dimension `n > 2`, for Lebesgue
measure, `aₙ ∫ ‖dU_{t,b}‖² = Y(Sⁿ) (∫ U_{t,b} ^ pₙ) ^ (2 / pₙ)`. This is the equality case of the
sharp Euclidean Sobolev inequality.

TauCeti.X_pow_two_pow_sub_C_irreducible.doc:
**The two-power case of Capelli's theorem.** Over any field `K`, if `a` is not a square
in `K` and, when `k ≥ 2`, `a` is not of the form `-4b⁴`, then `X^(2ᵏ) - a` is irreducible.
The second condition cannot be dropped: `X⁴ + 4` is reducible over `ℚ`.

**Capelli's theorem**, sufficiency: over any field `K`, if `n ≠ 0`, `a` is not a `p`-th
power for any prime `p ∣ n`, and `a` is not of the form `-4b⁴` when `4 ∣ n`, then `Xⁿ - a` is
irreducible.

**Capelli's theorem.** Over any field `K` and for `n ≠ 0`, the binomial `Xⁿ - a` is
irreducible if and only if `a` is not a `p`-th power for any prime `p ∣ n` and, when `4 ∣ n`,
`a` is not of the form `-4b⁴`. For odd `n` this is Mathlib's
`X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_iff_forall_prime_of_odd`.

**Orbit-torus weights are local zeta factors.** Let `P` be a `2 × 2` matrix of determinant
one all of whose iterates are nondegenerate, `det (1 - P ^ k) ≠ 0` for `k ≥ 1`. Read off the label
`σ = (0 < det (1 - P))` and `i = 1` if `det (1 + P) < 0`, `i = 0` otherwise. Then the local series
`f = f_(σ, i)` satisfies `t f' = f ∑_{k ≥ 1} sgn det (1 - P ^ k) t ^ k`; over `ℚ` this says
`log f = ∑_{k ≥ 1} sgn det (1 - P ^ k) t ^ k / k`.

TauCeti.WorkedExamples.nonempty_addEquiv.doc:
**The Mordell–Weil group of `y² = x³ - x + 1` over `ℚ` is `ℤ`.** It is finitely generated,
torsion-free and of rank one.

TauCeti.Wkp.dense_contDiffOn_representat.doc:
**Meyers–Serrin: `H = W` in `W^{k,p}(Ω)`.** For `1 ≤ p < ∞`, every order `k` and an
arbitrary open set `Ω`, the elements of `W^{k,p}(Ω)` represented by functions smooth on `Ω` are
dense in `W^{k,p}(Ω)`, in the full Sobolev norm.

TauCeti.Wkp.doc:
The arbitrary-order, real-valued weak Sobolev space `W^{k,p}(Ω)`.  At order zero this is
`Lᵖ(Ω)`; order one is `W1p`; every further order adjoins the weak derivative of the highest
derivative field from the preceding order.

for all radii `ρ₁ ≤ ρ₂`: each completed Huber algebra `B^I⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩` is the Gauss-normed ring
`B^I{X₁, …, Xₙ}` of unit-radius restricted series, which is noetherian by
`TauCeti.WittVector.isNoetherianRing_isRestricted_subring_intervalRing`.

**The interval ring `B^I` is stably sheafy** for all radii `0 < ρ₁ ≤ ρ₂ < 1`: every complete
Hausdorff Huber ring topologically of finite type over `B^I` is sheafy. The ring `B^I` is a
complete Hausdorff Tate ring that is strongly noetherian by Kedlaya's Theorem 4.10
(`TauCeti.WittVector.isStronglyNoetherian_intervalRing`), so this is Wedhorn's Corollary 8.35
(`TauCeti.Huber.isStablySheafyRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian`). In particular `B^I` is sheafy
(`TauCeti.Huber.IsStablySheafyRing.isSheafyRing`).

**The Schwarz reflection principle, weak form.** Let `U` be an open set mapped into itself by
the reflection `ρ` in the hyperplane `{a} × E`, and let `w` be weakly harmonic on `U ∩ H`, where
`H = {x | a < x.fst}`. Suppose that `w` is weakly differentiable on all of `U`, with weak gradient
`G` vanishing almost everywhere on `U` off `H`; for instance, `w` has zero trace on the flat
boundary `U ∩ {a} × E` and is extended by zero off `H`. Then the odd reflection
`x ↦ w x - w (ρ x)` is weakly harmonic on `U`.

TauCeti.WeaklyHarmonicOn.exists_harmonic.doc:
**The Schwarz reflection principle.** Let `U` be an open set mapped into itself by the
reflection `ρ` in the hyperplane `{a} × E`, and let `w` be weakly harmonic on `U ∩ H`, where
`H = {x | a < x.fst}`, and zero almost everywhere on `U` off `H`. Suppose that `w` is weakly
differentiable on all of `U`, with weak gradient `G` vanishing almost everywhere on `U` off `H`,
so that `w` vanishes on the flat boundary `U ∩ {a} × E` in the Sobolev sense. Then there is a
function `h` harmonic on `U` and odd under `ρ` that agrees almost everywhere on `U ∩ H` with `w`,
and whose gradient agrees almost everywhere on `U ∩ H` with `G`.

**Weyl's lemma with finite-dimensional coefficients.** A weakly harmonic function with
values in a finite-dimensional real normed space agrees almost everywhere with a function
harmonic on the same open set. No differentiability of the original function is assumed.

**The index of the trajectory operator is a difference of Morse indices.** Let `A` be a
continuous family of operators on a finite-dimensional real inner product space with invertible
symmetric limits `A±` at `±∞`. Then the index of the
trajectory operator `u ↦ u' + A u` from `W^{1,2}(ℝ, E)` to `L²(ℝ, E)` is the number of negative
eigenvalues of `A⁻` minus the number of negative eigenvalues of `A⁺`, counted with multiplicity:
the dimensions of the sums of their eigenspaces at negative eigenvalues.

**Uniqueness of Wasserstein geodesics.** Let `X` be a complete separable metric space and
`1 < p < ∞`. Suppose that every optimal coupling of `μ` and `ν` for the cost `d ^ p` is `π`, and
that `π`-almost every pair of points of `X` is joined by at most one geodesic path. Then any two
geodesic segments of `P_p (X)` from `μ` to `ν` agree on `[0, 1]`.

**Rellich--Kondrachov for zero-boundary Sobolev spaces.**  If `Ω` is bounded and
`1 ≤ p < ∞`, the canonical value map `W^{1,p}_0(Ω) → Lᵖ(Ω)` is a compact operator.

No boundary regularity is assumed.  The zero-boundary condition is what permits extension by zero
without creating a distributional boundary term.

TauCeti.W1p0.hasWeakFDerivOn_indicator.doc:
**The analytic content of the extension theorem.**  The zero-extension of `u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(Ω)`
is weakly differentiable on the larger open set `Ω'`, with weak gradient the zero-extension of the
weak gradient of `u`.  This is the statement that can *fail* for a general `u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω)`: with
no condition forcing `u` to vanish towards `∂Ω`, its zero-extension need not be weakly

`Ω ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}` is trapped between the hyperplanes `xᵢ = a` and `xᵢ = b`, then every
`u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(Ω)` satisfies `‖u‖_p ≤ (b - a) ‖∇u‖_p`.

enough. The endpoints may be in either order: reversed endpoints force `Ω` to be empty.

**The Poincaré inequality on `W^{1,p}_0(Ω)` for a bounded domain.** If `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞` and
`Ω ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}` is contained in a ball of radius `R`, then
`‖u‖_p ≤ 2R ‖∇u‖_p` for every `u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(Ω)`.

The constant `2R` is not sharp, but it is explicit and independent of the centre.

`p < ∞` and normalized `dim E`-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure on the frontier. It is
characterized by `TauCeti.W1p.frontierTrace_ae_eq_of_continuousOn` and

from `W^{1,p}(Ω)` to the whole space, and restriction to `Ω` recovers the original function.
Both endpoint exponents `p = 1` and `p = ∞` are included.

bounded, preconnected Lipschitz domain, let `S ⊆ Ω` have positive measure, and let `1 ≤ p < ∞`.

be a complete nonarchimedean field and `a, c ∈ K` with `c ≠ 0`. The closed unit disc
`Spa(K⟨T⟩, K⟨T⟩°)` is covered by the closed subdisc `R({T - a, c} / c) = {|T - a| ≤ |c|}` and by

Čech complex of the structure presheaf, as a presheaf of abelian groups, for this cover is exact
in every degree.

TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_presen.doc:
**Buzzard–Verberkmoes: stably uniform Tate pairs are sheafy.** Let `A` be a stably uniform
Tate ring, `P` a pair of definition whose ring of definition lies in `A⁺`, and `A⁺` a subring of
power-bounded elements. The presentation-limit structure presheaf of `Spa(A, A⁺)` is a sheaf of
complete separated topological rings on all opens. The ring need not be complete or Hausdorff.

TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isAdic_present.doc:
**The adic spectrum of a classical affinoid algebra is an affinoid adic space.** Let `K` be a
complete nonarchimedean field with a nontrivial absolute value and `B` a quotient of a Tate algebra
`K⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩`, carrying a complete ultrametric algebra norm, for instance the quotient Gauss norm.
Then for any pair of definition `P` of `B` and any plus ring `B⁺` of power-bounded elements
containing its ring of definition, such as `B°`, `Spa(B, B⁺)` is an affinoid adic space.

TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_eq_clas.doc:
**Every point of the closed unit disc is of one of Wedhorn's five types**, over an
algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field (Example 7.57): a classical point `x_a`
(type (1)), a point `η_{a,r}` (types (2) and (3)), the point attached to a decreasing sequence of
discs `D(aₙ, |cₙ|)` with no common point in `K` (type (4)), or a rank-two point `η_{a,r⁺}` or
`η_{a,r⁻}` with `r` the norm of an element of `K` (type (5)).

TauCeti.ValidLieTypeIndex.Group.doc:
The Lie-type candidate is the derived subgroup of the fixed points modulo its own centre.
No finiteness or simplicity instance is assumed or supplied.

TauCeti.ValidLieTypeIndex.AmbientGroup.doc:
**The ambient group of a valid Lie-type index**: the group of algebraic-closure-valued points
of the explicit carrier assigned to its family. It is generally infinite, and it is not identified
with the points of the pinned simply connected group scheme of the diagram. On the thirteen ordinary
and graph-twisted constructors it is `TauCeti.GraphTwistedIndex.AmbientGroup`; the Suzuki family
runs on the rank-two symplectic carrier, the Ree family of type `G₂` on the short-root `G₂` carrier
over `𝔽₃`, and the Ree family of type `F₄` and the Tits construction on the short-root `F₄`
carrier over `𝔽₂`.

TauCeti.UqSl2.triangularEquiv.doc:
**Triangular decomposition of `U_q(sl₂)`.**  Multiplication
`p ⊗ r ⊗ s ↦ p(F) * r(K) * s(E)` is a linear isomorphism
`ℂ[X] ⊗ ℂ[T, T⁻¹] ⊗ ℂ[X] ≃ UqSl2 q`, that is, `U⁻ ⊗ U⁰ ⊗ U⁺ ≃ U_q(sl₂)`.  It sends the
tensor product of monomial bases to the PBW basis.

TauCeti.UqSl2.sixJ_pentagon.doc:
**The Biedenharn–Elliott pentagon identity** for the `α₀ = 1` change-of-decomposition
(`F`-matrix) entries `sixJ` of `clebschGordanInclusion` across all signed ladder modules
`L_a^ε ⊗ L_b^δ ⊗ L_c^ζ ⊗ L_d^θ` at generic `q`.

  Polynomial ℂ ≃ₐ[ℂ] ↥(Subalgebra.center ℂ (TauCeti.UqSl2 q))
TauCeti.UqSl2.polynomialAlgEquivCenter.doc:
At a generic parameter, the center of `U_q(sl₂)` is a polynomial algebra in one variable:
evaluation at the Casimir element is an isomorphism `ℂ[X] ≃ₐ[ℂ] Z(U_q(sl₂))`.

TauCeti.UqSl2.pbwBasis.doc:
The Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt basis of `UqSl2 q`, indexed by the exponents `(a, b, c)`
of the ordered monomial `F ^ a * K ^ b * E ^ c`.

TauCeti.UqSl2.ladderModuleTensorHomEquiv.doc:
**The evaluation isomorphism.** At a generic parameter, a locally finite `UqSl2 q`-module `V`
is the direct sum over `(m, ε)` of `L_m^ε ⊗ Hom_U(L_m^ε, V)`, by `v ⊗ φ ↦ φ v`. Here `UqSl2 q`
acts on the left tensor factors, and the multiplicity spaces `Hom_U(L_m^ε, V)` may be
infinite-dimensional.

TauCeti.UqSl2.isTypeOne_and_isLocallyFin.doc:
**Type-1 locally finite modules.** At a generic parameter, a module is of type 1 and locally
finite exactly when it is isomorphic to a direct sum of positive signed ladder modules `L_m^+`.

TauCeti.UqSl2.isSemisimpleModule_of_fini.doc:
**Complete reducibility.** At a generic parameter, every finite-dimensional
`UqSl2 q`-module is semisimple.

TauCeti.UqSl2.isLocallyFiniteModule_iff_.doc:
At a generic parameter, a `UqSl2 q`-module is locally finite exactly when it is isomorphic to a
direct sum of signed ladder modules `L_m^ε`.

TauCeti.UqSl2.instIsDomain.doc:
For a nonzero parameter, `UqSl2 q` is a domain: both twists of its Ore tower are injective,
and an Ore extension of a domain by an injective twist is a domain. In particular the
presentation is nontrivial.

TauCeti.UqSl2.existsUnique_linearEquiv_l.doc:
**Classification of finite-dimensional simple `U_q(sl₂)`-modules.** At a generic parameter,
every finite-dimensional simple `UqSl2 q`-module is isomorphic to `L_m^ε` for exactly one
natural number `m` and sign `ε`.

TauCeti.UqSl2.VermaModule.ladderModuleEq.doc:
**The simple quotient of `M(ε q^m)`.** At a generic parameter, the quotient of `M(ε q^m)` by
the submodule generated by `v_(m + 1)` is isomorphic to the signed ladder module `L_m^ε`, by the
module map sending `v₀` to the class of `v₀`.

TauCeti.UqSl2.LadderModule.doc:
The underlying complex vector space `ℂ^(m + 1)` of the signed ladder module `L_m^ε` of
`UqSl2 q`. Its `UqSl2 q`-module structure, defined for nonzero `q`, is
`LadderModule.instModule`.

TauCeti.UpperHalfSpace.hyperbolicMetric.doc: The standard complete metric of constant curvature `-1` on upper half-space.

TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.volume_triangle.signature:
TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.volume_triangle {A B C : UpperHalfPlane} (hAB : A ≠ B)
  (hC :
    C ∉
      Set.range
        (TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.geodesicLine (TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.geodesicBetween A B))) :
  MeasureTheory.volume (A.triangle B C) =
    ENNReal.ofReal (Real.pi - A.interiorAngle B C - B.interiorAngle C A - C.interiorAngle A B)
TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.volume_triangle.doc:
**The Gauss–Bonnet formula**: the invariant area of a hyperbolic triangle is its angular
defect `π - α - β - γ`.

TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.vol.signature:
TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.volume_carrier_inter_strip {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]
  (P : TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon n) (h₀ : P.vertex 0 = Sum.inr OnePoint.infty)
  {i : Fin n} (hi : i ≠ 0) (hi' : i + 1 ≠ 0) :
  MeasureTheory.volume
      (P.carrier ∩
        {z |
          (TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.toComplex (P.vertex i)).re ≤ z.re ∧
            z.re ≤ (TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.toComplex (P.vertex (i + 1))).re}) =
    ENNReal.ofReal
      (Real.pi -
          TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.vertexAngle (P.vertex i) (Sum.inr OnePoint.infty)
            (P.vertex (i + 1)) -
        TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.vertexAngle (P.vertex (i + 1)) (P.vertex i) (Sum.inr OnePoint.infty))
TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.vol.doc:
**Gauss–Bonnet for the triangles of the fan from `∞`.** If `vertex 0` is `∞`, the part of
the carrier between the verticals through `vertex i` and `vertex (i + 1)`, for an side `i` not
ending at `∞`, has area `π` minus the angles at `vertex i` and `vertex (i + 1)` of the triangle
with vertices `∞`, `vertex i`, `vertex (i + 1)`. That part of the carrier is this triangle by
`exists_carrier_inter_strip_eq`.

TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.vol.signature:
TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.volume_carrier {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]
  (P : TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon n) :
  MeasureTheory.volume P.carrier = ENNReal.ofReal ((↑n - 2) * Real.pi - ∑ i, P.interiorAngle i)
TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.vol.doc:
**The Gauss–Bonnet formula for convex hyperbolic polygons with ideal vertices**: the area of
a convex polygon with `n` vertices in `ℍ ∪ ∂ℍ` is `(n - 2) π` minus the sum of its interior
angles, the angle at an ideal vertex being `0`.
Source: Walkden, *Hyperbolic geometry* (MATH32051), Theorem 7.2.2 and §7.1.

TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.ord.doc:
**The angle condition of Poincaré's theorem.** If every angle of `P` is `π / m` for a natural
number `m`, then at each finite vertex of the double the order of the cycle transformation times
the cycle angle sum is `2π`.

TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.isP.doc:
**The cusp condition of Poincaré's theorem.** The cycle transformations at the ideal vertices
of the double are parabolic.

TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.Sid.doc:
**Poincaré's presentation theorem.** For a locally finite fundamental polygon, every word in
the side generators evaluating to the identity is a consequence of the side relations and the
finite-vertex cycle relations.

TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.Sid.doc:
**The presentation part of Poincaré's polygon theorem.** If a side-paired polygon satisfies
the angle condition at every finite vertex cycle and has parabolic cycle transformations at its
ideal vertices, then evaluating the side generators at the side-pairing maps is an isomorphism
from the group presented by the side relations and the finite vertex cycle relations onto the
group generated by the side-pairing maps.

TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.Sid.doc:
**Poincaré's presentation theorem.** The group of a locally finite fundamental polygon is
presented by the side generators, the side relations, and the finite-vertex cycle relations.

TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.Sid.doc:
**The number of cusps of a locally finite fundamental polygon.** The number of cusp orbits
of `Γ` is the number of ideal vertex cycles of `P`.

TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.Sid.doc:
**Poincaré's presentation theorem**, as a description of the relations: the words in the
side generators evaluating to the identity in the group of a locally finite fundamental polygon
form the normal closure of the side and finite-vertex cycle relators.

satisfies the angle condition at every finite vertex cycle and has parabolic cycle
transformations at its ideal vertices, then it is a measurable fundamental domain for the group
generated by its side-pairing maps.

**The discreteness part of Poincaré's polygon theorem.** If a side-paired polygon satisfies
the angle condition at every finite vertex cycle and has parabolic cycle transformations at its
ideal vertices, then the group generated by its side-pairing maps is a cofinite Fuchsian group:
it is discrete and has finite covolume.

convex `n`-gon `P` by a group `Γ` containing the side-pairing maps be locally finite, with disjoint
interiors. Then the covolume of `Γ` is `2π ((n - k) / 2 - 1 - V + ∑ₑ (1 - 1 / mₑ))`, where `k` is

elliptic orbits of `Γ`, with stabilizer orders `mₑ`.

**The Gauss–Bonnet formula for compact convex hyperbolic polygons**: the area of a convex
polygon with `n` vertices, all in `ℍ` (no ideal vertices), is `(n - 2) π` minus the sum of its
interior angles.

`Γ_∞ = ⟨T⟩`.

Homogeneous coordinates identify the analytic realization of the standard projective-space
fan biholomorphically with complex projective space, the circle quotient of the unit sphere with
its standard homogeneous-ratio atlas.

TauCeti.Toric.IsLatticeRational.fg_dualS.doc:
**Gordan's lemma.** The dual semigroup of a lattice-rational cone in an integral lattice is
finitely generated. Salience is not required.

**The cone-by-cone properness criterion.** The analytic map of a morphism of regular fans
with nonempty source is proper exactly when, for every target cone `τ`, the inverse image of `τ`
under the real-linear map is the union of the source cones mapped into `τ`. The nonemptiness
hypothesis is necessary: the inclusion of the empty subfan is proper, but `0` lies in the inverse
image of every cone and in no cone of the empty fan. See
`TauCeti.Toric.FanHom.isProperMap_analyticMap_iff_isEmpty_or` for the form without it.

The fan of projective space attached to an integral basis `b` of an integral lattice: its
cones are spanned by the families of ray generators `projectiveSpaceGenerator b` omitting at least
one of them. For a basis indexed by a type with `n` elements it is the fan of `n`-dimensional
complex projective space.

The star subdivision of a regular fan `Φ` along a nonzero cone `σ` of `Φ` induces a proper
analytic map to the realization of `Φ`, because the two fans have the same support.

of the realization. There are a biholomorphism `e` from an open neighbourhood of `x` onto an open

lies in a boundary component exactly when that component passes through `x` and the coordinate

**Cartan's criterion.** Let `B` be a set of quasi-compact opens of `X` which is closed under
binary intersections and contains, inside each of its members, a basis of the topology of that
member. A sheaf of abelian groups which is Čech acyclic for the finite covers of members of `B` by
members of `B` has no cohomology in positive degrees on the members of `B`.

TauCeti.Topology.homologyCechComplexIsoH.doc:
**Leray's theorem.** Let `U` be a finite family of opens covering a topological space `X`, and
let `F` be a sheaf of abelian groups on `X` with no cohomology in positive degrees on any nonempty
finite intersection of members of `U`. Then the Čech cohomology `Hⁿ(U, F)`, the cohomology of the
Čech complex of `F` for `U`, is isomorphic to the sheaf cohomology `Hⁿ(X, F)`, for every `n`,
naturally in `F` (`TauCeti.Topology.homologyMap_comp_homologyCechComplexIsoH_hom`).

The colimit of a sequence of normal spaces in `TopCat` whose transition maps are closed
embeddings is normal.

TauCeti.TitsSystem.simple_mul_comm_of_br.doc:
**The key step of Tits's theorem on normal subgroups.** If `H` is normal, a simple reflection
whose Bruhat cell lies in `H ⊔ B` commutes with every simple reflection whose cell does not.

  {J : Set ↑T.simple} {g : G} :
  g ∈ T.standardParabolic J ↔ ∃ w ∈ Subgroup.closure (Subtype.val '' J), g ∈ T.bruhatCell w
TauCeti.TitsSystem.mem_standardParabolic.doc:
**The Bruhat decomposition of a standard parabolic:** an element lies in `P_J` exactly
when its Bruhat cell is indexed by the Weyl subgroup generated by `J`.

  [K.Normal] : K ≤ T.subgroupB.normalCore.subgroupOf (Subgroup.normalClosure ↑U) ∨ K = ⊤
TauCeti.TitsSystem.le_normalCore_subgrou.doc:
**Tits's theorem on normal subgroups of the normal closure of `U`.** Suppose the Weyl group is
irreducible, `U` is a solvable subgroup normalized by `B` with `B ≤ U (B ∩ N)`, and the normal
closure `H⁺` of `U` is perfect. Then every normal subgroup of `H⁺` either lies in `Z ∩ H⁺`, where
`Z = ⋂ g B g⁻¹` is the normal core of `B`, or is all of `H⁺`.

  [Group.IsSolvable ↥U] (hBU : T.subgroupB ≤ Subgroup.normalizer ↑U)

  H ≤ T.subgroupB.normalCore ∨ H = ⊤
TauCeti.TitsSystem.le_normalCore_or_eq_t.doc:
**Tits's simplicity theorem, for normal subgroups.** Suppose the Weyl group is irreducible,
`G` is perfect, and `U` is a solvable subgroup normalized by `B` whose conjugates generate `G`.
Then every normal subgroup of `G` either lies in the normal core `⋂ g B g⁻¹` of `B` or is `G`.

TauCeti.TitsSystem.isSimpleGroup_quotien.doc:
**Tits's simplicity criterion for the normal closure of `U`.** Under the hypotheses of
`TauCeti.TitsSystem.le_normalCore_subgroupOf_or_eq_top_of_normal`, the quotient `H⁺ / (Z ∩ H⁺)`
of the normal closure `H⁺` of `U` by its intersection with `Z = ⋂ g B g⁻¹` is simple whenever it is
nontrivial.

TauCeti.TitsSystem.isSimpleGroup_quotien.doc:
**Tits's simplicity theorem.** Suppose there is at least one simple reflection, the Weyl group
is irreducible, `G` is perfect, and `U` is a solvable subgroup normalized by `B` whose conjugates
generate `G`. Then the quotient of `G` by the normal core `⋂ g B g⁻¹` of `B` is simple.

TauCeti.TitsSystem.exists_standardParabo.signature:
TauCeti.TitsSystem.exists_standardParabolic_eq_sup_of_normal.{u} {G : Type u} [Group G]
  (T : TauCeti.TitsSystem G) (H : Subgroup G) [H.Normal] :
  ∃ J, T.standardParabolic J = H ⊔ T.subgroupB ∧ ∀ s ∈ J, ∀ t ∉ J, ↑s * ↑t = ↑t * ↑s
TauCeti.TitsSystem.exists_standardParabo.doc:
**Tits's theorem on normal subgroups.** For a normal subgroup `H`, the subgroup `H ⊔ B` is a
standard parabolic `P_J` for a set `J` of simple reflections that commutes elementwise with its
complement.

TauCeti.ThurstonEulerClassInequality.doc:
**Thurston's Euler class inequality**: on a closed orientable hyperbolic `3`-manifold `M`,
that is a compact connected orientable smooth `3`-manifold without boundary admitting a complete
Riemannian metric of constant curvature `-1`, every Euler class of a smooth taut codimension-one
foliation satisfies the Euler class inequality.

    TauCeti.TerminalCut.pairMinimumValue f s t
TauCeti.TerminalCut.min_pairMinimumValue.doc:
**Ultrametric inequality** for minimum cut values: every cut separating `s` from `t`
separates `s` from `v` or `v` from `t`. The intermediate vertex `v` is arbitrary.

  {f : Finset V → K} (hf : TauCeti.IsSymmSubmodular f) {𝒞 : Set (Finset V)}
  (h𝒞 : 𝒞.Pairwise fun Y Z => ¬Y.Crosses Z)

TauCeti.TerminalCut.exists_isMinimum_for.doc:
**Multi-cut non-crossing lemma.** Let `𝒞` be a pairwise non-crossing family of cuts, each a
minimum cut of a symmetric submodular `f` between some pair of vertices. If none of them
separates the distinct vertices `s` and `t`, then some minimum `s`–`t` cut crosses none of
them.

TauCeti.TerminalCut.exists_isCutTree.doc:
**Gomory–Hu theorem.** Every symmetric submodular set function on a nonempty finite vertex
type has a cut tree: a weighted tree on the vertices in which the minimum cut value between any
two distinct vertices is the minimum weight on the tree path between them, and deleting any tree
edge leaves a minimum cut between its ends.

TauCeti.TerminalCut.IsCutTree.isMinimum_.doc:
**Query theorem.** If `s(u, v)` has minimum weight on the tree path from `s` to `t`, and `s`
lies on the side of `u`, then that side is a minimum `s`–`t` cut. Since the two sides of a tree
edge cover the vertices, one of the orientations `(u, v)` and `(v, u)` applies.

**Serre's lemma on the Tate module.** An endomorphism of finite order of `T_p A` that induces
the identity on `A[p ^ k]`, with `p ^ k ≥ 3`, is the identity.

**Tate's isomorphism criterion**, on every subgroup. Let `G` be a finite group and `f : A ⟶ B`
a morphism of representations of `G`. If, for every subgroup `S` of `G` of prime-power order, the
map induced by `f` on the Tate cohomology of `S` is surjective in degree `q - 1`, bijective in
degree `q` and injective in degree `q + 1`, then it is bijective in every degree `n` for every
subgroup `S` of `G`.

**Tate's isomorphism criterion.** Let `G` be a finite group and `f : A ⟶ B` a morphism of
representations of `G`. If, for every subgroup `S` of `G` of prime-power order, the map induced by
`f` on the Tate cohomology of `S` is surjective in degree `q - 1`, bijective in degree `q` and
injective in degree `q + 1`, then `f` induces a bijection `Ĥⁿ(G, A) → Ĥⁿ(G, B)` in every
degree `n`.

TauCeti.TateCohomology.isZero_of_forall_.doc:
**Tate's cohomological triviality criterion** (Milne II 3.10). Let `G` be a finite group and
`A` a representation of `G`. If its Tate cohomology vanishes in degrees `q` and `q + 1` for every
subgroup `S` of `G` of prime-power order, then it vanishes in degree `n` for every subgroup `S`
of `G` and every integer `n`.

TauCeti.TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient_.signature:
TauCeti.TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient_eq_of_isBaseChange.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type} [Group G]
  [Fintype G] [IsCyclic G] {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [CommRing K] [Nontrivial K] [Algebra ℚ K]
  [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module K V] (ρ : Representation K G V) {M N : Rep.{0, 0, 0} ℤ G}
  [Module.Free ℤ ↑M] [Module.Finite ℤ ↑M] [Module.Free ℤ ↑N] {i : ↑M →ₗ[ℤ] V} {j : ↑N →ₗ[ℤ] V}
  (hi : IsBaseChange K i) (hj : IsBaseChange K j)
  (hiG : ∀ (g : G) (x : ↑M), i ((M.ρ g) x) = (ρ g) (i x))
  (hjG : ∀ (g : G) (y : ↑N), j ((N.ρ g) y) = (ρ g) (j y)) :
  TauCeti.TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient M = TauCeti.TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient N
TauCeti.TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient_.doc:
**Tate's lattice lemma.** Let `G` be a finite cyclic group, `K` a nontrivial commutative
`ℚ`-algebra (classically `ℝ`) and `ρ` a representation of `G` on a `K`-module `V`. If `M` and `N`
are integral representations of `G`, free over `ℤ` with `M` of finite rank, and `G`-equivariant
maps `i : M → V` and `j : N → V` exhibit `V` as the base change of `M` and of `N` to `K`, then `M`
and `N` have the same Herbrand quotient. The rank of `N` is then finite as well, being that of
`V`.

TauCeti.TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient_.signature:
TauCeti.TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient_coind.{u} {R G : Type u} [CommRing R] [Group G] [Fintype G]
  [IsCyclic G] (S : Subgroup G) [Fintype ↥S] (A : Rep.{u, u, u} R ↥S) :
  TauCeti.TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient (Rep.coind.{u, u, u, u} S.subtype A) =
    TauCeti.TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient A
TauCeti.TateCohomology.herbrandQuotient_.doc:
**Shapiro's lemma for Herbrand quotients.** For a subgroup `S` of a finite cyclic group `G` and
a representation `A` of `S`, the coinduced representation `Coind_S^G A` has the same Herbrand
quotient over `G` as `A` has over `S`. Both quotients are ratios `|H²| / |H¹|` of ordinary group
cohomology, `S` being cyclic as well, and Shapiro's lemma `groupCohomology.coindIso` identifies the
cohomology of `Coind_S^G A` with that of `A` in every degree.

This computes the Herbrand quotient of a module whose factors are permuted transitively by `G`
from that of the stabilizer of one factor. For a cyclic extension `L/K` of number fields and a
place `v` of `K`, the module `∏_{w ∣ v} L_wˣ` is coinduced in this way from the decomposition group
of one place `w` acting on `L_wˣ`.

TauCeti.TateCohomology.cup_bijective_of_.doc:
**The Tate–Nakayama theorem** (Nakayama, Ann. of Math. 65 (1957); Serre, *Local Fields*, IX §8).
Let `G` be a finite group, `C` a representation of `G` over `ℤ` and `u ∈ H²(G, C)`.
Suppose that for every subgroup `S` of `G` of prime-power order

* `H¹(S, C) = 0`,
* the restriction of `u` generates `H²(S, C)`, and
* `H²(S, C)` has `|S|` elements.

Then for every representation `M` with `Tor₁^ℤ(M, C) = 0`, in the form that `M ⊗ X → M ⊗ Y` is
injective for every short exact sequence `0 → X → Y → C → 0` of abelian groups, cup product with
`u` is a bijection `H^r(G, M) → H^{r+2}(G, M ⊗ C)` in every integer degree `r`.

  (hgen : ∀ (y : ↑(tateCohomology N 2)), ∃ m, m • u = y)
  (hcardG : Nat.card ↑(tateCohomology N 2) = Nat.card G)
  (h1 :

      IsPGroup p ↥S → CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (tateCohomology (Rep.res S.subtype N) 1))
  (hcard :
    ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (S : Subgroup G) [inst : Fintype ↥S],
      IsPGroup p ↥S → Nat.card ↑(tateCohomology (Rep.res S.subtype N) 2) = Nat.card ↥S)
  (r r' : ℤ) (h : r + 2 = r') :

TauCeti.TateCohomology.cup_bijective_of_.doc:
**Tate's theorem.** Let `G` be a finite group, `N` a representation of `G` over `ℤ` and
`u ∈ H²(G, N)`. Suppose that

* `u` generates `H²(G, N)`, a group of order `|G|`;
* for every subgroup `S` of `G` of prime-power order, `H¹(S, N) = 0` and `H²(S, N)` has order
  `|S|`.

Then cup product with `u` is a bijection `H^r(G, ℤ) → H^{r+2}(G, ℤ ⊗ N)` in every integer degree
`r`. The classical hypothesis that the restriction of `u` to each subgroup generates its `H²` is
a consequence of these and is not assumed.

TauCeti.TateCohomology.cup_bijective_of_.doc:
**Tate's theorem**, with the degree-zero injection as hypothesis. Let `G` be a finite group,
`N` a representation of `G` over `ℤ` and `u ∈ H²(G, N)`. Suppose that

* cup product with `u` is injective `H⁰(G, ℤ) → H²(G, N)`;
* for every subgroup `S` of `G` of prime-power order, `H¹(S, N) = 0` and `H²(S, N)` has order
  `|S|`.

Then cup product with `u` is a bijection `H^r(G, ℤ) → H^{r+2}(G, ℤ ⊗ N)` in every integer degree
`r`.

an open neighbourhood of a rectangle `[a₁, b₁] × [a₂, b₂]`, the integral of the Floer energy

`K(u) = K_s(u) ds + K_t(u) dt` over the positively oriented boundary, minus the integral of the
curvature `R_K(u)`.

parametrized by the end coordinates:

`∫_{S_R} u^*ω = ∑ q, ±a(t ↦ u(φ_q(±R + i t)))`,

with the sign `+` on the input ends `0` and `1` and `-` on the output end `∞`.

constant symplectic form equals the outer boundary action. The value of the map at the puncture
is unrestricted, and the map need not be holomorphic.

`s ↦ ½ ω(u, ∂s u)`.

TauCeti.SymplecticForm.exists_isSymplect.doc:
**Linear Darboux theorem.** Two symplectic vector spaces of the same finite dimension are
linearly symplectomorphic.

TauCeti.SymplecticForm.IsSymplectic.signature:

TauCeti.SymplecticForm.IsSymplectic.doc:
A submodule is **symplectic** if it meets its symplectic complement only in zero,
equivalently (`isSymplectic_iff_nondegenerate_restrict`) `ω` restricts to it nondegenerately.

TauCeti.SymplecticForm.Invariant.complex.doc:
**The Hermitian form of a `J`-invariant symplectic form is twice the pullback of the induced
Hermitian form along `v ↦ v^(1,0)`**: with `g = ω (·, J ·)` and `h` its sesquilinear
complexification, `ω (v, J w) + i ω (v, w) = 2 h (v^(1,0), w^(1,0))`.

TauCeti.SymplecticForm.Compatible.sq_ass.doc:
**Cauchy--Schwarz along a complex line.** For a compatible pair, the squares of the
components `g(v, w)` and `ω(v, w) = g(J v, w)` of `w` along the orthogonal pair `v`, `J v` add up
to at most `g(v, v) g(w, w)`.

TauCeti.SymplecticForm.Compatible.apply_.doc:
**The Wirtinger inequality.** A symplectic form compatible with `J` calibrates the associated
metric: `ω(v, w) ≤ |v ∧ w|_g`.

TauCeti.Symplectic.IsotropicFlag.exists_.doc:
**Lie--Kolchin for `Sp₂ₘ`-valued points.**

Let `Q` be the coordinate algebra of a reduced, geometrically connected, geometrically solvable
affine group of finite type over an algebraically closed field `k`. For every bialgebra morphism
`π : O(Sp₂ₘ) → Q` some rational symplectic matrix `P` conjugates the `Q`-valued point `π` into the
stabilizer of the standard complete isotropic flag. The columns of `P` form a symplectic basis
whose isotropic half is a Lie--Kolchin basis of an invariant Lagrangian subspace.

limiting at every level. In particular, the limiting maps respect the sphere action.

Symmetric spectra of pointed simplicial sets: the modules over the commutative monoid
`SymmetricSequence.sphere` of symmetric sequences. A symmetric spectrum is a symmetric sequence
`X` with an action `S ⊗ X ⟶ X` for the Day convolution product, satisfying the unit and
associativity laws.

TauCeti.SymmetricSequence.doc:
Symmetric sequences of pointed simplicial sets: functors from the finite-bijection groupoid
to pointed simplicial sets, with the Day convolution product along the block sum.

TauCeti.Sym.norm_le_norm_coeffEquiv_ofFn.doc:
**Cauchy's bound** on the symmetric power: the points of an unordered tuple are bounded by one
more than the sup-norm of its elementary symmetric chart, because each of them is a root of the
monic polynomial those coordinates present.

**Vieta's formulas** on the symmetric power: the `k`-th coefficient of the monic polynomial of
an unordered `n`-tuple is the `(n - k)`-th elementary symmetric function of the tuple, up to the
sign `(-1) ^ (n - k)`.

is a product of the standard generators. A fixed point fixing `∞` is a torus element times a
unipotent generator, and any other is carried to one by `w u(a, b)` for the unipotent generator
moving its last column onto the line through `e₀`.

TauCeti.Suzuki.mem_borelSubgroupOf_or_me.doc: **The rank-one Bruhat decomposition** `Sz(q) = B ∪ B w B`, for `m ≠ 0`.

TauCeti.Subgroup.CuspDatum.im_scaling_sm.doc:

`Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ)`. If `g ∈ Γ` does not carry the cusp of `D'` to the cusp of `D`, then the height of

orientations at the origin and have the same centre are smoothly isotopic relative to that centre.

**Euclidean disc theorem.** Smooth embeddings with a common centre and derivative
equivalences with positive relative determinant are smoothly isotopic relative to that centre.
The source is finite-dimensional; the target needs neither an orientation nor a completeness
instance.

**Euclidean disc theorem.** Smooth self-embeddings with a common centre and the
same derivative orientation there are smoothly isotopic relative to that centre.

TauCeti.SmoothEmbedding.exists_smoothIso.doc:
**The disc theorem in a manifold.** Two smooth embeddings of `E` into a boundaryless manifold
modelled on `E`, with the same centre `f 0 = g 0` and derivatives at `0` of the same orientation,
are smoothly isotopic relative to that centre. The orientations are compared in the chart at the
centre: the product of the derivative determinants there is positive. This condition does not
depend on the chart, since a change of chart multiplies both determinants by the same nonzero
number. For `M = E` it is the hypothesis of the Euclidean disc theorem
`TauCeti.SmoothEmbedding.exists_smoothIsotopy_of_det_mul_pos`.

at its centre, with the same derivative orientation there, are smoothly isotopic relative to the
centre through embeddings with values in the ball.

**The relative ambient disc theorem.** Let `f` and `g` be smooth embeddings of `E` into a
Hausdorff boundaryless manifold `M` modelled on `E`, preserving the orientations `o` of `E` and
`oM` of `M` at the origin, with images in a preconnected open set `U`. On every compact subset `A`
of `E`, `g` is `f` followed by the final diffeomorphism of a smooth diffeotopy of `M` fixing every
point outside a compact subset of `U`. Points outside `U`, for instance protected discs and
collars, are not moved.

smooth embedding is diffeomorphic to an arbitrarily small open neighbourhood of its image,

of a smooth embedding is diffeomorphic to an open neighbourhood inside any prescribed open

compactness nor closedness of the embedded image nor completeness of the ambient metric
is required.

components: if `g` is a homotopy inverse of the inclusion `O(4) → Diff(S³)`, then every `f` is
joined to the image of `g f` by the homotopy from the composite to the identity.

commutator relations in an associative `ℚ`-algebra, then the product of a raising divided power
and a lowering divided power is an integral sum in PBW order `F`, `H`, `E`.

coerced to the algebra, so this is the standard coefficient `(H - m - n + 2k choose k)`.

continuous semigroup with growth bound `(omega, M)` if and only if `1 ≤ M`, its domain is dense,
the half-line `(omega, ∞)` lies in its resolvent set, and its resolvent powers satisfy the sharp

space, let `1 ≤ M`, and suppose that every real `lambda > omega` belongs to the resolvent set of
`A`, with the power estimates

Then `A` generates a strongly continuous semigroup with growth bound `(omega, M)`. The produced
semigroup is the exponential unshift of the exponent-zero Yosida limit for `A - omega I`.

  (LinearMap.trace ℂ E) (↑((TauCeti.SeibergWitten.quadraticEndPolar ψ) φ) * ↑T) =
    2 * ↑(inner ℂ (T ψ) φ).re
TauCeti.SeibergWitten.trace_quadraticEnd.doc:
Against a trace-free self-adjoint `T`, the polarization of `Q₀` pairs as
`tr (B(ψ, φ) T) = 2 Re⟪T ψ, φ⟫`: the formal adjoint of the derivative `B(ψ, ·)` of `Q₀` is
`T ↦ 2 T ψ`.

TauCeti.SeibergWitten.hasStrictFDerivAt_.signature:
TauCeti.SeibergWitten.hasStrictFDerivAt_quadraticEnd.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℂ E] (ψ : E) :
  HasStrictFDerivAt TauCeti.SeibergWitten.quadraticEnd (TauCeti.SeibergWitten.quadraticEndPolar ψ) ψ
TauCeti.SeibergWitten.hasStrictFDerivAt_.doc:
The real Fréchet derivative of `Q₀` at `ψ` is `B(ψ, ·)`, that is
`DQ₀|_ψ (φ) = φψ* + ψφ* - Re⟪ψ, φ⟫ Id`; this holds in the strict sense.

TauCeti.SchemeAction.exists_isClosed_orb.signature:
TauCeti.SchemeAction.exists_isClosed_orbit.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
  (G : CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec ↧k))
  {X : CategoryTheory.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec ↧k)} [CategoryTheory.GrpObj G]
  [CategoryTheory.ModObj G X] [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [CompactSpace ↥G.left]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [CompactSpace ↥X.left] [Nonempty ↥X.left] :
  ∃ y, IsClosed (TauCeti.SchemeAction.orbit G y)
TauCeti.SchemeAction.exists_isClosed_orb.doc:
**Existence of closed orbits.** A nonempty scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed
field, acted on by a group scheme of finite type, contains the closed orbit of a rational
point.

TauCeti.SU2.weyl_integration_formula.signature:
TauCeti.SU2.weyl_integration_formula {f : TauCeti.SU2 → ℂ} (hf : Continuous f)
  (hconj : ∀ (u g : TauCeti.SU2), f (u * g * u⁻¹) = f g) :
  ∫ (g : TauCeti.SU2), f g ∂TauCeti.haarProb TauCeti.SU2 =
    1 / (2 * ↑Real.pi) * ∫ (θ : ℝ) in 0..Real.pi, f (TauCeti.SU2.torusExp θ) * ↑(4 * Real.sin θ ^ 2)
TauCeti.SU2.weyl_integration_formula.doc:
**The Weyl integration formula for `SU(2)`.** For a continuous class function `f` on `SU(2)`,
the integral of `f` against the Haar probability measure is the integral over the Weyl chamber
`[0, π]` of the maximal torus against the Weyl density `(2π)⁻¹ · 4 sin²θ dθ`:

`∫ f dμ = (2π)⁻¹ ∫₀^π f (diag (e^{iθ}, e^{-iθ})) · 4 sin²θ dθ`.

The Weyl factor `4 sin²θ = |e^{iθ} - e^{-iθ}|²` is the squared modulus of the Weyl denominator,
and the density has total mass one (`TauCeti.SU2.weyl_integration_formula_normalized`).

TauCeti.SU2.sub_inv_mul_character_symPow.doc:
**The Weyl numerator identity.**  Multiplying the weight string of `Symᵈ(ℂ²)` by the Weyl
denominator `z - z⁻¹` telescopes to `z^{d+1} - z^{-(d+1)}`.

No hypothesis is needed on `z`: at the two points `z = ±1` where the denominator vanishes both
sides are `0`.

TauCeti.SU2.sin_mul_character_symPower_t.signature:
TauCeti.SU2.sin_mul_character_symPower_torusExp (d : ℕ) (θ : ℝ) :
  ↑(Real.sin θ) * (TauCeti.SU2.symPower d).character (TauCeti.SU2.torusExp θ) =
    ↑(Real.sin ((↑d + 1) * θ))
TauCeti.SU2.sin_mul_character_symPower_t.doc:
**The Weyl numerator identity in the angle parametrisation:** writing the torus element as
`diag (e^{iθ}, e^{-iθ})`, the identity of
`TauCeti.SU2.sub_inv_mul_character_symPower_torusHom` reads `sin θ · χ_d (θ) = sin ((d+1)θ)`.

As there, no hypothesis is needed on `θ`: at a multiple of `π` both sides vanish.

TauCeti.SU2.character_symPower_torusHom_.doc:
**The Weyl character formula for `SU(2)`.**  Away from the two points `z = ±1` of the maximal
torus, where the Weyl denominator vanishes, the character of `Symᵈ(ℂ²)` at `diag (z, z⁻¹)` is the
quotient of the Weyl numerator by the Weyl denominator.

TauCeti.SU2.character_symPower_torusExp_.signature:
TauCeti.SU2.character_symPower_torusExp_eq_sin_div_sin (d : ℕ) {θ : ℝ} (hθ : Real.sin θ ≠ 0) :
  (TauCeti.SU2.symPower d).character (TauCeti.SU2.torusExp θ) =
    ↑(Real.sin ((↑d + 1) * θ) / Real.sin θ)
TauCeti.SU2.character_symPower_torusExp_.doc:
**The Weyl character formula in the angle parametrisation.**  Off the multiples of `π`, where
the Weyl denominator `2i·sin θ` vanishes, the character of `Symᵈ(ℂ²)` at `diag (e^{iθ}, e^{-iθ})`
is `sin ((d+1)θ) / sin θ`.  In particular it is real.

TauCeti.RoughForm.apply_mlieBracket_eq_n.doc:
**Cartan's formula for the Levi form.** For vector fields `V` and `W` tangent to the kernel of
a one-form `α` near `x`, `α_x ([V, W]_x) = -dα_x (V_x, W_x)`.

TauCeti.Ring.mem_jacobson_iff_forall_gel.signature:
TauCeti.Ring.mem_jacobson_iff_forall_gelfandRadius_mul_eq_zero.{u_3} {B : Type u_3} [NormedRing B]
  [NormedAlgebra ℂ B] [CompleteSpace B] {a : B} :
  a ∈ Ring.jacobson B ↔ ∀ (b : B), gelfandRadius (b * a) = 0
TauCeti.Ring.mem_jacobson_iff_forall_gel.doc:
An element of a complex Banach algebra lies in its Jacobson radical exactly when every
left multiple `b * a` is quasinilpotent, that is, `‖(b * a) ^ n‖ ^ (1 / n)` tends to zero.

TauCeti.Ring.IsNagata.doc:
A commutative ring `R` is *Nagata* if it is Noetherian and the quotient `R ⧸ p` by every prime
ideal `p` is a Japanese domain. Stacks, Definition 10.162.1 (032R).

TauCeti.Ring.IsJapanese.signature: TauCeti.Ring.IsJapanese.{u} (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] : Prop
TauCeti.Ring.IsJapanese.doc:
A domain `R` is *Japanese* (or *N-2*) if for every finite extension `L` of its fraction field,
the integral closure of `R` in `L` is a finite `R`-module; inseparable extensions are included.
Stacks, Definition 10.161.1 (032F). See `IsJapanese.finite_integralClosure` for an arbitrary model
of the fraction field and an extension in an arbitrary universe.

TauCeti.RiemannSurface.nhds_le_map_nhds_.signature:
TauCeti.RiemannSurface.nhds_le_map_nhds_of_not_eventuallyConst.{u_1, u_2} {X : Type u_1}
  {Y : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace X] [ChartedSpace ℂ X] [TopologicalSpace Y] [ChartedSpace ℂ Y]
  [IsManifold (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ ℂ) 1 X] [IsManifold (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ ℂ) 1 Y]
