            (↑L).wildExponent =

`∑_{M ∈ R} 1 / (#Aut_K(M) · q ^ c(M)) = 1`, is equivalent to the mass formula over `σ_K(n)`,
`∑_{L ∈ σ_K(n)} q ^ (-c(L)) = n`.

TauCeti.IsRepresentativeSet.tsum_one_div.signature:

TauCeti.IsRepresentativeSet.tsum_one_div.doc:
**Serre's second mass formula**: for `0 < n` and every set `R` of representatives of the
`K`-isomorphism classes in `σ_K(n)`, `∑_{M ∈ R} 1 / (#Aut_K(M) · q ^ c(M)) = 1`.

TauCeti.IsRegularRing.flat_frobenius.signature:
TauCeti.IsRegularRing.flat_frobenius.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (p : ℕ) [ExpChar R p]

TauCeti.IsRegularRing.flat_frobenius.doc:
**Kunz's theorem.** The Frobenius endomorphism of a regular ring of exponential characteristic
`p` is flat. Stacks, Lemma 51.17.6 (0EC0), the implication from regularity to flatness.

TauCeti.IsRegularLocalRing.of_hasProject.signature:
TauCeti.IsRegularLocalRing.of_hasProjectiveDimensionLE.{v, u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]

TauCeti.IsRegularLocalRing.of_hasProject.doc:
**Serre's theorem.** A Noetherian local ring whose residue field has finite projective
dimension is a regular local ring. Its dimension is then that projective dimension, by
`TauCeti.IsRegularLocalRing.projectiveDimension_quotient_maximalIdeal_eq_ringKrullDim`.

TauCeti.IsRegularLocalRing.of_globalDime.signature:
TauCeti.IsRegularLocalRing.of_globalDimension_lt_top.{v, u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]

  IsRegularLocalRing R
TauCeti.IsRegularLocalRing.of_globalDime.doc:
**Serre's theorem, global dimension form.** A Noetherian local ring of finite global dimension
is a regular local ring: its residue field has finite projective dimension.

TauCeti.IsRegularLocalRing.isRegular_pai.doc:
Over a two-dimensional regular local ring, every pair generating the maximal ideal is
regular on any finite injective normal local algebra, considered as a module over the base.

TauCeti.IsRegularLocalRing.isCohenMacaul.signature:

TauCeti.IsRegularLocalRing.isCohenMacaul.doc: **A regular local ring is Cohen–Macaulay.** Stacks, Lemma 10.106.3 (00NQ).

TauCeti.IsProP.topologicalGeneratorRank_.signature:
TauCeti.IsProP.topologicalGeneratorRank_eq_rank_continuousZModDual.{u} {p : ℕ}
  [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {G : Type u} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
  [CompactSpace G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G] (hG : TauCeti.IsProP p G) :
  TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRank G = Module.rank (ZMod p) (TauCeti.continuousZModDual p G)
TauCeti.IsProP.topologicalGeneratorRank_.doc:
**Burnside's basis theorem, cardinal form.** The topological generator rank of a profinite
pro-`p` group is the dimension of its continuous `𝔽_p`-dual over `𝔽_p`. No finiteness hypothesis is
needed, and the statement is an identity of cardinals.

TauCeti.IsProP.topologicalGeneratorRankN.signature:
TauCeti.IsProP.topologicalGeneratorRankNat_add_index.{u} {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)]
  {G : Type u} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G]
  [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G] (hG : TauCeti.IsProP p G)
  (hfg : TauCeti.IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated G)
  (h2 :
    ∀ (A : Type u) [inst : AddCommGroup A] [inst_1 : TopologicalSpace A]
      [inst_2 : DiscreteTopology A] [inst_3 : DistribMulAction G A] [inst_4 : ContinuousSMul G A]
      [Finite A],
      Nat.card A = p →
        (∀ (g : G) (a : A), g • a = a) → Subsingleton (TauCeti.ContCohomology.H2 G A))

    1 + (↑U).index * TauCeti.topologicalGeneratorRankNat G hfg
TauCeti.IsProP.topologicalGeneratorRankN.doc:
**The two-term Euler formula.** Let `G` be a topologically finitely generated profinite pro-`p`
group whose explicit `H²` vanishes on the discrete modules of order `p` with trivial action, and
let `U` be an open subgroup. Then `d(U) + [G : U] = 1 + [G : U] * d(G)`, the natural-number form
of `1 - d(U) = [G : U] * (1 - d(G))`.

The proof applies `TauCeti.IsProP.natCard_H1_mul_natCard` to the permutation module
`Coind_U^G 𝔽_p`, of order `p ^ [G : U]`, and reads both sides through Shapiro's lemma.

TauCeti.IsProP.topologicalClosure_normalClosure_eq_iff_quotient_pLowerCentralStep.{u} {p : ℕ}
  {F : Type u} [Group F] [TopologicalSpace F] [IsTopologicalGroup F] [CompactSpace F]

**Burnside's basis theorem for normal generation.** A subset `s` of a closed normal subgroup
`R` of a pro-`p` group `F` generates `R` as a closed normal subgroup of `F` exactly when its image
topologically generates the quotient `R ⧸ Rᵖ[R, F]`.

TauCeti.IsProP.surjective_of_forall_inv_.doc:
**Burnside's criterion modulo `λ_1`.** A continuous endomorphism of a pro-`p` group congruent
to the identity modulo `λ_1 = Φ` is surjective.

TauCeti.IsProP.surjective_iff_surjective.signature:

TauCeti.IsProP.surjective_iff_surjective.doc:
**Burnside's surjectivity criterion.** A continuous homomorphism from a compact group
to a profinite pro-`p` group is surjective exactly when its composites with all index-`p`
quotient maps are surjective.

TauCeti.IsProP.rank_H1_eq_topologicalGen.signature:
TauCeti.IsProP.rank_H1_eq_topologicalGeneratorRank.{u} {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {G : Type u}

**Burnside's basis theorem for `H¹`, cardinal form.** The dimension of `H¹(G, 𝔽_p)` over
`𝔽_p` is the topological generator rank of a profinite pro-`p` group `G`, as an identity of
cardinals and with no finiteness hypothesis.

TauCeti.IsProP.range_pi_mapQuotient_ker_.signature:
TauCeti.IsProP.range_pi_mapQuotient_ker_proPFrattini.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G]
  [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G] {p : ℕ}
  [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hG : TauCeti.IsProP p G)
  (hfg : TauCeti.IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated G) :
  (Set.range fun φ N => (TauCeti.ContinuousAut.mapQuotient ⋯) ↑φ) =
    {σ |
      (∀
          (N :
            { N //
              TauCeti.IsTopCharacteristic G ↑N.toOpenSubgroup ∧
                ↑N.toOpenSubgroup ≤ TauCeti.proPFrattini p G }),
          σ N ∈ (MulAut.mapQuotient (frattini (G ⧸ ↑(↑N).toOpenSubgroup))).ker) ∧
        ∀
          ⦃N M :
            { N //
              TauCeti.IsTopCharacteristic G ↑N.toOpenSubgroup ∧
                ↑N.toOpenSubgroup ≤ TauCeti.proPFrattini p G }⦄
          (hle : ↑N ≤ ↑M) (q : G ⧸ ↑(↑N).toOpenSubgroup),

topologically finitely generated pro-`p` group `G`, the coordinates on the quotients `G ⧸ N` by the
topologically characteristic open normal subgroups `N ≤ proPFrattini p G` identify the kernel of
`ContinuousAut G →* MulAut (G ⧸ proPFrattini p G)` with the families of automorphisms `σ N` of
the finite `p`-groups `G ⧸ N` that act trivially on the Frattini quotients of `G ⧸ N` and are
compatible with the quotient maps `G ⧸ N → G ⧸ M` for `N ≤ M`. The coordinate map is injective
and a topological embedding by `ContinuousAut.isEmbedding_pi_mapQuotient_ker_proPFrattini`.

generated exactly when its Frattini subgroup is open.

manifold structure modelled on the stable Hessian subspace, with its subspace topology and a
`C^n` inclusion into the ambient space. The dimension of the model plus the Morse index equals
the ambient dimension.

**The Morse lemma.** Near a nondegenerate critical point `x` of a `C^{n+2}` function `f`,
with `1 ≤ n ≤ ∞`, there is a `C^n` map `φ`, fixing `0` and with derivative the identity there,
in terms of which `f` is exactly its Hessian quadratic form:
`f (x + v) = f x + 2⁻¹ * fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x (φ v) (φ v)` for `v` near `0`.

`TauCeti.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint.exists_morse_chart` repackages this as a chart at
`x`.

**The Morse form of Łojasiewicz's gradient inequality.** Near a nondegenerate critical point
the absolute energy difference is bounded by a multiple of the squared norm of the gradient;
equivalently the Łojasiewicz inequality holds there with exponent `1 / 2`.
Smoothness alone does not guarantee such an inequality, and a gradient trajectory can spiral
forever without converging.

**The Morse form of Łojasiewicz's gradient inequality on a normed space.** Near a
nondegenerate critical point the absolute energy difference is bounded by a multiple of the
squared norm of the differential; equivalently the Łojasiewicz inequality holds there with
exponent `1 / 2`.

graph of this root. No polynomial equation or global semialgebraic domain is required.

TauCeti.IsMorse.exists_sublevel_union_ce.doc:
**Milnor's cell attachment theorem.** Let `f` be a Morse function on a Hausdorff manifold whose
band `f⁻¹[c - δ, c + δ]` is compact, for some `0 < δ`. Then there are a width `0 < ε₀ ≤ δ` and
normalized Morse charts `ψ p` with pairwise disjoint sources, indexed by the critical points `p`
on the level `f⁻¹(c)`, with `ψ p p = 0`, with the closed ball of radius `√(2ε₀)` in the target of
`ψ p`, and in which `f = c - Σ_{i < λ} yᵢ² + Σ_{i ≥ λ} yᵢ²`, where `λ` is the Morse index of `f`
at `p`. For every width `0 < ε ≤ ε₀`, the cell at `p` is the disc
`{‖y‖² ≤ ε, yᵢ = 0 for i ≥ λ}` of its negative coordinates, read in `M` through `ψ p`.

The lower sublevel `{f ≤ c - ε}` with these cells attached is a strong deformation retract of
`{f ≤ c + ε}`, for every such `ε`: there is a retraction of `{f ≤ c + ε}` onto it, and a
homotopy in `{f ≤ c + ε}` from this retraction to the identity which fixes it pointwise.

TauCeti.IsMorse.exists_relCWComplex_subl.doc:
**Milnor's cell attachment theorem in CW form.** Let `f` be a Morse function and `c` a value
with a compact band `f⁻¹[c - δ, c + δ]`. Then for some `0 < ε ≤ δ` the sublevel `{f ≤ c + ε}`
strong deformation retracts onto a finite CW complex `C ⊆ {f ≤ c + ε}` relative to the lower
sublevel `{f ≤ c - ε}`, whose `m`-cells correspond to the critical points of index `m` on the level
`c`. The complex is `TauCeti.morseRelCWComplex` built from normalized Morse charts at these
critical points.

TauCeti.IsMorse.exists_morseCellAttachme.doc:
**Milnor's cell attachment theorem, in pushout form.** Let `f` be a Morse function and `c` a
value with a compact band `f⁻¹[c - δ, c + δ]`. Then for some `0 < ε ≤ δ` there are normalized Morse
charts `ψ p` at the critical points `p` on the level `c`, with pairwise disjoint sources, such that
the comparison map `Φ : M_{c-ε} ∪_α ⨆ₚ D^{λ p} → M_{c+ε}` from the lower sublevel with one cell of
dimension the Morse index `λ p` attached at each `p` has a left inverse `g`, and `Φ ∘ g` is
homotopic to the identity of `M_{c+ε}` relative to the image of `Φ`, which contains the lower
sublevel `M_{c-ε}`.

TauCeti.IsMorse.exists_isZero_and_finran.doc:
**The weak Morse inequalities across a critical level.** Let `f` be a Morse function and `c` a
value with a compact band `f⁻¹[c - δ, c + δ]`. For some `0 < ε ≤ δ`, the relative singular
homology `Hₙ({f ≤ c + ε}, {f ≤ c - ε}; R)`, with coefficients in an object `R` of an abelian
category with coproducts, vanishes when no critical point on the level `c` has index `n`; and with
coefficients in a finite-dimensional module `V` over a division ring it is finite-dimensional, of
dimension at most `dim V` times the number of critical points of index `n` on the level `c`.

TauCeti.IsMorse.exists_admissible_morseC.doc:
**Admissible Morse charts at a critical level.** Let `f` be a Morse function on a Hausdorff
manifold whose band `f⁻¹[c - δ, c + δ]` is compact, for some `0 < δ`. Then there are a width
`0 < ε ≤ δ` and normalized Morse charts `ψ p`, indexed by the critical points `p` on the level
`f⁻¹(c)`, such that

* the only critical points in the band `f⁻¹[c - ε, c + ε]` are those on the level `f⁻¹(c)`;
* the chart sources are pairwise disjoint, and each lies in a prescribed neighbourhood `U p`;
* `ψ p p = 0`, and `f = c - Σ_{i < λ} (ψ p)ᵢ² + Σ_{i ≥ λ} (ψ p)ᵢ²` on the source of `ψ p`, where
  `λ` is the Morse index of `f` at `p`;
* the target of each chart contains the closed ball of radius `√(2ε)` about `0`.

The last condition places Milnor's ellipsoid `‖u‖² + 2‖v‖² ≤ 2ε` inside every chart. All of these
conditions persist when `ε` is decreased.

TauCeti.IsMcCallumWellOriented.doc:
A finite family `F` of real polynomials in `n` variables is *well-oriented* in McCallum's
sense if, when `n` is positive, singling out the distinguished variable `X 0` gives a family with
a squarefree basis `B` such that each member of `B` is nullified at only finitely many points of
`ℝ ^ (n - 1)`, and the McCallum projection of the family with respect to `B` is again
well-oriented. Every family of constants is well-oriented.

critical point `x` of a function `f` which is `C²` at `x` and strongly `q`-pseudoconvex at `x`, the

that is smooth at every point of a neighbourhood of `x`, on a manifold modelled on a
finite-dimensional real normed space `E`, there is a Morse chart: a chart `ψ` of the maximal atlas,
centred at `x`, and a linear change of coordinates `L : E ≃ (Fin n → ℝ)` such that on the source
of `ψ`

`f y = f x + (1/2) Σᵢ wᵢ (L (ψ y))ᵢ²`,

where every weight `wᵢ` is `-1` or `1` and the number of negative weights is the manifold Morse
index of `f` at `x`.

source of a normalized Morse chart: a partial diffeomorphism `ψ` onto an open subset of

`f y = f x - Σ_{i < λ} (ψ y)ᵢ² + Σ_{i ≥ λ} (ψ y)ᵢ²`

on its whole source, where `λ` is the manifold Morse index of `f` at `x`.

TauCeti.IsManifoldNondegenerateCriticalP.doc:
**The normalized Morse lemma on a manifold.** At a nondegenerate critical point `x` of a
function `f` which is smooth near `x`, on a manifold with a boundaryless model, there is a partial
diffeomorphism `ψ` onto an open subset of `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)`, `m = dim M`, with
`ψ x = 0` and

`f y = f x - Σ_{i < λ} (ψ y)ᵢ² + Σ_{i ≥ λ} (ψ y)ᵢ²`

on its whole source, where `λ` is the manifold Morse index of `f` at `x`.

**The Morse form of Łojasiewicz's gradient inequality on a Riemannian manifold.** Near a
nondegenerate critical point `p` of `f`, the absolute energy difference `|f y - f p|` is bounded by
a multiple of the squared Riemannian length of the gradient of `f` at `y`, for any continuous
Riemannian metric.

TauCeti.IsLocallyFlat.isBicollared_of_no.doc:
**Brown's bicollaring theorem for separating spheres.** For `n ≥ 1`, a locally flat embedding
of the `n`-sphere in the `(n + 1)`-sphere whose image has disconnected complement is bicollared.

The Jordan–Brouwer separation theorem says that the complement is always disconnected, so this
reduces `TauCeti.BrownBicollaring n` to it. The hypothesis `n ≠ 0` makes the source sphere
connected; the `0`-sphere is two points.

**Brown's collaring theorem**, for a compact domain: an injective, locally collared map from a
compact space into a Hausdorff space is collared. The local collars are assembled into one by
pushing an external collar inward along each of them in turn (Connelly's proof).

functions on an open set `U ⊆ ℂ` is equicontinuous on `U`.

Around a point `z₀ ∈ U` pick `r > 0` with `closedBall z₀ (2 * r) ⊆ U`; local boundedness supplies
one constant `C` bounding the whole family on that compact ball, and
`dist_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_two_mul_norm_le` then makes every member of the family
`C / r`-Lipschitz on `ball z₀ r`.  A single Lipschitz constant is a common continuity modulus.

into a Hausdorff space that is locally bicollared with disjoint open sides `A` and `B` has a

  (h : TauCeti.IsLocallyBicollared f) (hf : Function.Injective f) (hA : IsOpen A) (hB : IsOpen B)

TauCeti.IsLocallyBicollared.exists_isBic.doc:
**Brown's bicollaring theorem for separating maps.** Let `f` be an injective locally
bicollared map from a compact, preconnected, locally connected space into a preconnected
Hausdorff space, and write the complement of its image as the union of disjoint nonempty open
sets `A` and `B`. Then `f` has a global bicollar with positive side in `A` and negative side in
`B`.

TauCeti.IsLocalTiling.signature:
TauCeti.IsLocalTiling.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {X : Type u_2} [Group G] [MulAction G X]
  [TopologicalSpace X] (P : Set X) (N : X → Set G) : Prop
TauCeti.IsLocalTiling.doc:
A **local tiling** by a closed path-connected tile `P`: for each `x ∈ P`, `N x` is a set of
local neighbours, the elements `h` such that `h • P` is one of the tiles around `x`. The
identity is a neighbour, `x ∈ h • P` for each neighbour `h`, the neighbours of `x` seen from the
tile `h • P` are the translates `h⁻¹ • N x`, and each point of `P` lies in a tiling chart made of
its own neighbours.

TauCeti.IsLocalRing.sum_addVal_smul_sub_eq_finsum_card_ramificationGroup_sub_one.{u_1, u_2, u_3}
  {G : Type u_1} [Group G] {S : Type u_2} [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [IsDiscreteValuationRing S]
  [MulSemiringAction G S] {R : Type u_3} [CommSemiring R] [Algebra R S] [SMulCommClass G R S]
  [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] [FaithfulSMul G S] {ξ : S} (hξ : R[ξ] = ⊤) :
  ∑ σ ∈ Finset.univ.erase 1, (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal S) (σ • ξ - ξ) =

TauCeti.IsLocalRing.sum_addVal_smul_sub_.doc:
**Hilbert's counting identity.** Let a finite group `G` act faithfully on a discrete valuation
ring `S` generated over a base `R` fixed by `G` by a single element `ξ`. Then the sum over the
nontrivial `σ ∈ G` of the valuations `v (σ • ξ - ξ)` is `∑_{i ≥ 0} (#G_i - 1)`, where `G_i` is
the `i`-th ramification group: each `σ ≠ 1` lies in exactly `v (σ • ξ - ξ)` of the groups
`G_0, G_1, …`, and the sum is finite because the filtration is eventually trivial.

TauCeti.IsLocalRing.mem_ramificationGrou.doc:
**Serre's criterion** for the ramification filtration: when `S` is generated over `R` by a set
`s` and `G` acts by `R`-algebra automorphisms, membership in `G_i` is decided on `s` alone. This
is `TauCeti.Ideal.mem_inertia_iff_of_adjoin_eq_top` at a power of the maximal ideal.

  ∃ f c,
    ∃ (hf : ∀ (x : M), f x = c → ContMDiffAt I (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ) 1 f x) (hreg :
      TauCeti.IsRegularValue I (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ) f c),

TauCeti.IsLiouvilleDomain.exists_isRestr.doc:
**The boundary of a Liouville domain is of restricted contact type.** On a finite-dimensional
manifold without boundary, a Liouville domain `W` is the sublevel set `{f ≤ c}` of a function `f`,
`C¹` along the level `f⁻¹(c)`, of which `c` is a regular value; the frontier of `W` is exactly the
level; and the level, with its atlas `TauCeti.regularLevelChartedSpace`, is a hypersurface
of restricted contact type for the primitive `α`.

TauCeti.IsLiouvilleDomain.doc:
A subset `W` of a manifold `M` is a **Liouville domain** for the smooth two-form `ω`, with
primitive `α`, when `ω` is nondegenerate, `dα = ω`, `W` is compact and lies in the interior of
`M`, and the Liouville field of `α` points strictly outwards along the boundary of `W`: some smooth
vector field `Z` with `ι_Z ω = α` and some continuous function `f` and value `c` satisfy
`W = {f ≤ c}`, with `f` smooth and `df(Z) > 0` at every point of the level `f⁻¹(c)`. The
nondegeneracy of `ω` makes `Z` unique, and the condition along `f⁻¹(c)` makes `c` a regular value
of `f`, so that `W` is a compact domain with smooth boundary `f⁻¹(c)`.

TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.not_isPreconnected.doc:
**The Jordan separation theorem on the Riemann sphere.** The complement of a Jordan curve in
`OnePoint ℂ` is not preconnected.

**The Jordan separation theorem.** The complement of a Jordan curve in the plane is not
preconnected.

TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.natCard_zerothHomo.doc:
**The Jordan curve theorem on the Riemann sphere.** The complement of a Jordan curve in
`OnePoint ℂ` has exactly two path components.

TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.natCard_connectedC.doc:
**The Jordan curve theorem.** The complement of a Jordan curve in the plane has exactly two
connected components: by `TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.connectedComponentIn_eq_filledHull_sdiff_or_compl`
they are its inside `filledHull C \ C` and its unbounded outside `(filledHull C)ᶜ`.

TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.frontier_connected.signature:
TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.frontier_connectedComponentIn {C : Set ℂ} (h : TauCeti.IsJordanCurve C)
  {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∉ C) : frontier (connectedComponentIn Cᶜ x) = C
TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.frontier_connected.doc:
**The frontier of a complementary component of a Jordan curve is the whole curve**: for
`x ∉ C`, the component of `Cᶜ` containing `x` has frontier `C`.

TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.exists_homeomorph_.signature:
TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.exists_homeomorph_image_sphere_of_mem {C : Set ℂ} {p : ℂ}
  (hC : TauCeti.IsJordanCurve C) (hp : p ∈ TauCeti.filledHull C \ C) :
  ∃ e,

TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.exists_homeomorph_.doc:
**The Schoenflies theorem, centred at a point of the inside.** For a Jordan curve `C ⊆ ℂ` and a
point `p` of its inside `filledHull C \ C`, there is a homeomorphism `e` of `ℂ` with `e 0 = p`
carrying the unit circle onto `C`, the open unit disc onto the inside of `C`, and the closed unit
disc onto `filledHull C`.

TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.exists_homeomorph_.signature:
TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.exists_homeomorph_image_sphere {C : Set ℂ} (hC : TauCeti.IsJordanCurve C) :
  ∃ e,
    ⇑e '' Metric.sphere 0 1 = C ∧
      ⇑e '' Metric.ball 0 1 = TauCeti.filledHull C \ C ∧
        ⇑e '' Metric.closedBall 0 1 = TauCeti.filledHull C
TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.exists_homeomorph_.doc:
**The Schoenflies theorem.** For every Jordan curve `C ⊆ ℂ` there is a homeomorphism of `ℂ`
carrying the unit circle onto `C`, the open unit disc onto the inside `filledHull C \ C` of `C`, and
the closed unit disc onto `filledHull C`.

**The Schoenflies theorem on the 2-sphere.** Let `C` be a Jordan curve in the unit sphere of a
three-dimensional real inner product space, and `v` a point of the sphere off `C`. Then some
homeomorphism of the sphere fixing `v` carries the great circle `⟪x, v⟫ = 0` onto `C`.

TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.exists_homeomorph_.signature:
TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.exists_homeomorph_compl_ball_compl_filledHull_sdiff {C : Set ℂ}
  (hC : TauCeti.IsJordanCurve C) :
  ∃ h,
    ContinuousOn h (Metric.ball 0 1)ᶜ ∧
      DifferentiableOn ℂ h (Metric.closedBall 0 1)ᶜ ∧
        Set.BijOn h (Metric.closedBall 0 1)ᶜ (TauCeti.filledHull C)ᶜ ∧
          Set.BijOn h (Metric.sphere 0 1) C ∧

TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.exists_homeomorph_.doc:
**Carathéodory's theorem for the outside of a Jordan curve.** For a Jordan curve `C ⊆ ℂ` there
is a map `h`, holomorphic off the closed unit disc and tending to infinity at infinity, carrying the
exterior of the closed disc bijectively onto the outside `(filledHull C)ᶜ` and the unit circle
bijectively onto `C`, which restricts to a homeomorphism of the closed exterior `(ball 0 1)ᶜ` onto
the complement of the inside, the closure of the outside
(`TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.closure_compl_filledHull`).

TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.exists_homeomorph_.doc:
**Carathéodory's theorem for the inside of a Jordan curve.** For a Jordan curve `C ⊆ ℂ` and a
point `p` of its inside `filledHull C \ C`, there is a map `g`, holomorphic on the open unit disc
with `g 0 = p`, carrying the disc bijectively onto the inside and the unit circle bijectively onto
`C`, which restricts to a homeomorphism of the closed disc onto `filledHull C`.

TauCeti.IsInvolutiveDistribution.exists_.signature:
TauCeti.IsInvolutiveDistribution.exists_flatChart.{u, u_1, u_2} {E : Type u} {H : Type u_1}
  {M : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace H]
  {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [IsManifold I 1 M] {m : ℕ∞} (hm : 1 ≤ m) {n : WithTop ℕ∞} (hmn : ↑m + 1 ≤ n) [IsManifold I n M]
  {k : ℕ} {D : (x : M) → Submodule ℝ (TangentSpace I x)}
  (hinv : TauCeti.IsInvolutiveDistribution I D) (hD : TauCeti.IsContMDiffDistribution I (↑m) k D)
  {x : M} (hx : I.IsInteriorPoint x) :
  ∃ e W,
    e ∈ IsManifold.maximalAtlas I (↑m) M ∧
      x ∈ e.source ∧
        Module.finrank ℝ ↥W = k ∧ ∀ y ∈ e.source, Submodule.map (↑(mfderiv% (↑I ∘ ↑e) y)) (D y) = W
TauCeti.IsInvolutiveDistribution.exists_.doc:
**The local Frobenius theorem.** An involutive `C^m` distribution `D` of rank `k`, for `1 ≤ m`,
on a `C^n` manifold with `m + 1 ≤ n`, modelled on a finite-dimensional real space, is constant in a
suitable chart around any interior point `x`: there are a chart `e` of the `C^m` maximal atlas whose
domain contains `x` and a `k`-dimensional subspace `W` of the model space such that the differential
of `I ∘ e` carries `D y` onto `W` at every point `y` of the domain of `e`. On a boundaryless
manifold `BoundarylessManifold.isInteriorPoint` gives the interior hypothesis at every point.

**The Frobenius theorem in coordinates.** Let `f` be of class `C^(n+1)` near `(x₀, y₀)`, with
an involutive graph distribution. Then the distribution has an integral manifold through
`(x₀, y₀)`: the graph of a function `u`, of class `C^(n+1)` at `x₀`, with `u x₀ = y₀` and
`D u x = f (x, u x)` near `x₀`, so that the tangent space of the graph at `(x, u x)` is the graph
of `f (x, u x)`.

  (hinv : TauCeti.IsInvolutiveDistribution (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (E × F)) D)
  (hD :
    TauCeti.IsContMDiffDistribution (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ (E × F)) (↑n + 1) (Module.finrank ℝ E)
      D)
  {x₀ : E} {y₀ : F} (h₀ : Disjoint (D (x₀, y₀)) (LinearMap.fst ℝ E F).ker) :
  ∃ u,
    u x₀ = y₀ ∧
      ContDiffAt ℝ (↑n + 1) u x₀ ∧
        ∀ᶠ (x : E) in nhds x₀, DifferentiableAt ℝ u x ∧ D (x, u x) = (↑(fderiv ℝ u x)).graph
TauCeti.IsInvolutiveDistribution.exists_.doc:
**The Frobenius theorem for transverse distributions.** Let `D` be an involutive `C^(n+1)`
distribution of rank `finrank ℝ E` on `E × F` such that `D (x₀, y₀)` meets the vertical subspace
`0 × F` only in `0`. Then `D` has an integral manifold through `(x₀, y₀)`: the graph of a function
`u`, of class `C^(n+1)` at `x₀`, with `u x₀ = y₀`, whose tangent space at `(x, u x)`, the graph of
`fderiv ℝ u x`, is `D (x, u x)` for every `x` near `x₀`.

  [IsScalarTower A C L] [IsIntegralClosure C A L] : IsNoetherianRing C
TauCeti.IsIntegralClosure.isNoetherianRi.doc:
**Krull–Akizuki.** Let `A` be a Noetherian domain of Krull dimension at most one with fraction
field `K`, and let `L` be a domain containing `A` that is a finite-dimensional `K`-vector space
compatibly with `A`, such as a finite extension of `K`. Then an integral closure `C` of `A` in `L`
is a Noetherian ring. No separability over `K` is assumed, and `C` need not be a finite
`A`-module.

TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule.isNilpote.signature:
TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule.isNilpotent_or_isUnit.{u, v} {A : Type u} {M : Type v} [Ring A]

  (h : TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule A M) (f : Module.End A M) : IsNilpotent f ∨ IsUnit f
TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule.isNilpote.doc:
**Fitting's lemma**, restated: an endomorphism of an indecomposable module that is both
Noetherian and Artinian is either nilpotent or a unit of the endomorphism ring.

TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule.isNilpote.signature:
TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule.isNilpotent_or_bijective.{u, v} {A : Type u} {M : Type v} [Ring A]
  [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module A M] [IsNoetherian A M] [IsArtinian A M]
  (h : TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule A M) (f : Module.End A M) :
  IsNilpotent f ∨ Function.Bijective ⇑f
TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule.isNilpote.doc:
**Fitting's lemma**: an endomorphism of an indecomposable module that is both Noetherian and
Artinian is either nilpotent or bijective.

For a large enough exponent `m`, Mathlib's Fitting decomposition splits `M` as
`ker (f ^ m) ⊕ range (f ^ m)`. Indecomposability collapses one of the two summands: if the range
vanishes then `f ^ m = 0`, and if the kernel vanishes then `f` is injective while the range, being
everything, forces `f` to be surjective.

TauCeti.IsGoodDixonPrime.two_mul_natAbs_.signature:
TauCeti.IsGoodDixonPrime.two_mul_natAbs_lt_of_natAbs_le_sqrt.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] {p : ℕ}

TauCeti.IsGoodDixonPrime.two_mul_natAbs_.doc:
**Dixon's size bound in the shape the residue window asks for.** An integer of absolute value
at most `⌊√|G|⌋` lies strictly inside the window of half-width `p / 2`, since `2⌊√|G|⌋ < p`.

TauCeti.IsGoodDixonPrime.nonempty_center.signature:
TauCeti.IsGoodDixonPrime.nonempty_center_algEquiv_conjClasses.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] {p : ℕ}
  (hp : TauCeti.IsGoodDixonPrime G p) :
  Nonempty
    (↥(Subalgebra.center (ZMod p) (MonoidAlgebra (ZMod p) G)) ≃ₐ[ZMod p] ConjClasses G → ZMod p)
TauCeti.IsGoodDixonPrime.nonempty_center.doc:
**The good-prime structure theorem.** At a good Dixon prime the centre of `ZMod p [G]` is the
algebra of `ZMod p`-valued functions on the conjugacy classes of `G`.

This is what guarantees that the class-multiplication matrices are simultaneously diagonalizable
over `ZMod p` with exactly `r` distinct common eigenrows, so that the eigenvector search of the
Burnside--Dixon--Schneider algorithm terminates in one-dimensional common eigenspaces, with no
bad-prime merging of distinct central characters.

TauCeti.IsGoodDixonPrime.isSemisimpleRin.signature:

  (hp : TauCeti.IsGoodDixonPrime G p) : IsSemisimpleRing (MonoidAlgebra (ZMod p) G)
TauCeti.IsGoodDixonPrime.isSemisimpleRin.doc:
**Maschke's theorem at a good Dixon prime**: the modular group algebra `ZMod p [G]` is a
semisimple ring.

TauCeti.IsGoodCycle.apply_self_eq_zero_o.doc: An image occurring with multiplicity at least two has square zero.

TauCeti.IsGoodCycle.signature:
TauCeti.IsGoodCycle.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {H : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {P : Type u_3} [AddCommGroup H]
  [Fintype ι] [Fintype P] (B : LinearMap.BilinForm ℤ H) (κ e : H) (C : ι → H) (m δ : ι → ℕ)
  (pts : ι → Finset P) : Prop
TauCeti.IsGoodCycle.doc:
The numerical properties of a positive cycle `∑ m i • C i` of distinct simple
pseudoholomorphic images in a good class `e` of a symplectic four-manifold with canonical class
`κ`, passing through generic points indexed by `P`, read in the intersection form `B` on
integral homology. The image `C i` has singularity number `δ i` and contains the points `pts i`.
The fields say: the multiplicities are positive; distinct images meet nonnegatively; the number
of points on an image is at most half the index `d(C i) - 2 δ i` of simple curves in its class,
where `d(x) = x · x - κ · x`; the good class `e` is at least `-1` on every image of negative
square; the cycle represents `e`; every point lies on some image; and the number of points is
half the virtual dimension of `e`. The square `-1` of an image of negative square, which
adjunction forces for an exceptional sphere, then follows (`IsGoodCycle.apply_self_eq_neg_one`).

TauCeti.IsFunctionField.exists_polynomia.doc:
**Belyi's theorem, existence direction, for a given function**: over a field `k` algebraic
over `ℚ`, let `F / k` be a function field with exact constant field `k` and `x ∈ F` transcendental
over `k`. Then there is a nonconstant polynomial `q` with rational coefficients such that `F` is an
algebraic Belyi pair over `k(t)` for every structure in which `t` acts as `q(x)`: the composite of
`x` with `q` is a Belyi map. Such a structure exists, see
`TauCeti.IsFunctionField.exists_isAlgebraicBelyiPair`.

TauCeti.IsFunctionField.exists_isAlgebra.signature:
TauCeti.IsFunctionField.exists_isAlgebraicBelyiPair.{u, v} {k : Type u} {F : Type v} [Field k]

  ∃ β, ∃ (hβ : Transcendental k β), TauCeti.IsAlgebraicBelyiPair k F
TauCeti.IsFunctionField.exists_isAlgebra.doc:
**Belyi's theorem, existence direction**: over a field `k` algebraic over `ℚ`, such as an
algebraic closure of `ℚ` or a number field, every function field `F / k` with exact constant field
`k` admits a Belyi map: there is `β ∈ F` transcendental over `k` such that `F` over `k(t)`, with
`t` acting as `β`, is an algebraic Belyi pair.

TauCeti.IsFreelyIndependentElements.tend.doc:
**The weak free central limit theorem.** Centered free selfadjoint elements whose moments
are uniformly bounded in each degree and whose average variance tends to `v ≥ 0` have
normalized-sum laws converging weakly to `semicircleReal 0 v`. No common compact support of the
approximating laws is required.

**The weak free central limit theorem for identically distributed elements.** If centered
free selfadjoint elements have the same scalar moments and variance `v ≥ 0`, the laws of their
normalized sums converge weakly to `semicircleReal 0 v`. Equality of scalar moments suffices;
no trace or faithfulness is needed.

Freeness determines the joint distribution from the individual ones: two normalised
functionals for which `B` is free and which agree on each `B i` agree on the subalgebra
generated by the `B i`.

TauCeti.IsFreelyIndependent.doc:
Subalgebras `B i` of `A` are *freely independent* with respect to a linear functional `φ` if
`φ (a₁ * ⋯ * aₙ) = 0` for every nonempty word `[(i₁, a₁), …, (iₙ, aₙ)]` whose consecutive labels
are distinct and whose letters satisfy `aⱼ ∈ B iⱼ` and `φ aⱼ = 0`. Labels that are not adjacent
may coincide.

TauCeti.IsFiniteEtaleSplit.of_henselianL.doc:
A Henselian local ring with separably closed residue field, that is, a strictly Henselian local
ring, has no nonsplit finite étale covers: a faithfully flat finite étale algebra has a point over
the separably closed residue field, which lifts to a section.

TauCeti.IsFiniteEtaleSplit.doc:
A ring `R` *has no nonsplit finite étale covers* if every finite étale `R`-algebra is totally
split. This is the conclusion of Scholze's Lemma 15.3 for the perfectoid tower `A_∞`.

**The local Frobenius theorem in product coordinates.** Let `D` be a family of subspaces of
`E × F` with a `C^(n+1)` local frame of `finrank ℝ E` vector fields on an open neighbourhood `U` of
`p₀`, involutive on `U`, such that `D p₀` meets the vertical subspace `0 × F` only in `0`. Then some
`C^(n+1)` change of coordinates `φ`, with `C^(n+1)` inverse and fixing `p₀`, carries `D` onto the
horizontal subspace `E × 0`, the kernel of the second projection, at each point of its domain. So
`φ` is a flat chart of `D`, and the preimages under `φ` of the horizontal slices are integral
manifolds of `D`.

Serre, Theorem 3.2). For a Demushkin group `G` of even rank `n`, the image `A` of its canonical
character has `(A : A^p) < p ^ n` as supernatural numbers. For `q(G) ≠ 2` this is

For `q(G) = 2`, so `p = 2`, the index `(A : A²)` is `1`, `2` or `4`, and it is `4` only for the
non-procyclic images `{±1} × U^(f)`, which do not occur at rank two; so `(A : A²) ≤ 2 < 2 ^ n`, or
`(A : A²) = 4 < 2 ^ n` with `n ≥ 4`.

**The necessity half of the existence theorem for `q ≠ 2`** (Labute, Theorem 1). For a
Demushkin group `G` of rank `n` with `q(G) ≠ 2`, the image `A` of its canonical character has
`(A : A^p) < p ^ n`. Indeed `A` is trivial, with `(A : A^p) = 1`, or the principal unit group
`1 + qℤ_p`, with `(A : A^p) = p`, while `n ≥ 2`. Together with the parity of the rank
(`TauCeti.IsDemushkin.even_demushkinRank_of_demushkinQ_ne_two`), this places `(n, A)` in the first
situation of the existence theorem.

**An open subgroup of an infinite Demushkin group is Demushkin** (Serre's exposé, §9.2). The
subgroup is pro-`p` and topologically finitely generated with `G`; its `H²(U, 𝔽_p)` is
one-dimensional by `TauCeti.IsDemushkin.finrank_cohomFp_two_openSubgroup`; and its cup product is
nondegenerate because a nonzero class of `H¹(U, 𝔽_p) ≅ H¹(G, Coind_U^G 𝔽_p)` is paired
nontrivially by Tate's duality map `α₁` of `G`, a pairing which is the corestriction of a cup
product of `U`.

group `G` of rank `n` with `q`-invariant `q`,

`G^{ab} ≃ₜ* ℤ_p^{n-1} × ℤ_p ⧸ q ℤ_p`

as topological groups. When `q = 0` the second factor is `ℤ_p` and `G^{ab} ≅ ℤ_p^n` is torsion-free;
otherwise it is the cyclic group of order `q`, which is the torsion subgroup of `G^{ab}`.

infinite Demushkin group `G` is topologically isomorphic to a Demushkin group `H` if and only if
`H` has rank `2 + [G : U] (n(G) - 2)` and the canonical character of `H` has image `χ(U)`, where
`χ` is the canonical character of `G`.

isomorphic if and only if they have the same rank and their canonical characters have the same
image. The forward direction is the invariance of both invariants under isomorphism; the
converse is `TauCeti.IsDemushkin.nonempty_continuousMulEquiv_of_range_demushkinCharacter_eq`.

TauCeti.IsDemushkin.existsUnique_hasPres.doc:
**Labute's Theorem 4: a Demushkin group has exactly one continuous character with the
prescription property.**

bijective** on every finite discrete `G`-module `M` killed by `pⁱ`:
`H¹(G, M) × H¹(G, Hom(M, I(χ)/pⁱ)) → H²(G, I(χ)/pⁱ)` is a perfect pairing.

**Tate's theorem: an infinite Demushkin group has `p`-cohomological dimension exactly `2`.**
The lower bound is `H²(G, 𝔽_p) ≠ 0`; the upper bound is the right exactness of `H²` on the finite
`𝔽_p[G]`-modules, which Tate's perfect duality provides.

TauCeti.IsDemushkin.doc:
**The Demushkin predicate** (Labute, p. 106), for a prime `p` and a topological group `G`: a
pro-`p` group whose `H¹(G, 𝔽_p)` is finite-dimensional, whose `H²(G, 𝔽_p)` is one-dimensional, and
on which the cup product `H¹(G, 𝔽_p) × H¹(G, 𝔽_p) → H²(G, 𝔽_p)` is nondegenerate on both sides.
The primality of `p` is a hypothesis of the predicate. Profiniteness is not: no field mentions
`CompactSpace G` or `TotallyDisconnectedSpace G`, so Lean leaves those section instances out of
the structure, and the predicate is also defined for topological groups that are not profinite.
The presentation results below assume both; on profinite groups, its intended mathematical
domain, this is Labute's notion. The pro-`p` hypothesis is a field, so that no theorem about
Demushkin groups applies to a group that satisfies only the cohomological clauses. Finite
generation is a consequence, `IsDemushkin.isTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated`, and is not assumed.

TauCeti.IsCyclicallyMonotone.exists_isCC.doc:
**The theorem of Rockafellar and Rüschendorf.** Every `c`-cyclically monotone set is
contained in the `c`-superdifferential of a `c`-concave potential: there is a `φ` with
`φ x + φᶜ y = c (x, y)` at every point `(x, y)` of the set, where `φᶜ` is the infimal
`c`-transform of `φ`.

TauCeti.IsCyclicallyMonotone.exists_fenc.doc:
**Rockafellar's theorem.** A cyclically monotone set lies in the graph of the
subdifferential of a Legendre–Fenchel conjugate `g⋆`, hence of a convex function that is lower
semicontinuous for every topology compatible with the pairing, and is never `⊥` as soon as the
set is nonempty (`TauCeti.apply_ne_bot_of_mem_subdifferential`).

**Rockafellar's theorem for the quadratic cost.** A `c`-cyclically monotone set for the cost
`‖x - y‖ ^ 2 / 2` lies in the subdifferential graph of a Legendre–Fenchel conjugate `u = g⋆` for
the inner product: `y ∈ ∂u(x)` for every `(x, y)` in the set.

TauCeti.IsCoupling.klDiv_eq_klDiv_add_kl.doc:
**The Pythagorean identity of the Schrödinger problem.** Let `π` be a coupling of `μ` and `ν`
whose density against the finite reference `R` is `exp (φ(x) + ψ(y))`, for measurable potentials
`φ ∈ L¹(μ)` and `ψ ∈ L¹(ν)`. Then every coupling `γ` of `μ` and `ν` satisfies
`klDiv γ R = klDiv γ π + klDiv π R`.

**The Schachermayer--Teichmann theorem.** For a finite-valued lower semicontinuous cost on a
product of Polish spaces, a coupling of finite cost between two probability measures is optimal
if and only if it is concentrated on a measurable `c`-cyclically monotone set.

The finite-cost hypothesis is used only for the forward implication: when every coupling has
infinite cost, every coupling is optimal.

`π` of finite measures `μ` and `ν` with finite second moments is an optimal plan for the cost

semicontinuous `u : E → EReal` such that `y ∈ ∂u(x)` for `π`-almost every `(x, y)`.

**The Benamou–Brenier lower bound.** Let `t ↦ νₜ` be a curve of finite measures, narrowly
continuous on `[a, b]` with `a ≤ b`, solving the continuity equation with velocity `v` on
`(a, b)`, whose initial law `ν_a` is a probability measure (by conservation of mass, so is `ν_b`).
Then for `1 ≤ p < ∞` the `p`-Wasserstein distance between the endpoint laws is controlled by the
`p`-action of `v`: `W_p (ν_a, ν_b) ^ p ≤ (b - a) ^ (p - 1) * ∫_a^b ∫ ‖vₜ‖ ^ p dνₜ dt`.

On `[0, 1]` the factor is `1`, and this is the inequality `W_p (ν₀, ν₁) ^ p ≤ ∫₀¹ ∫ ‖vₜ‖ ^ p dνₜ dt`
of the Benamou–Brenier formula.

TauCeti.IsCompleteBernsteinFunction.exis.doc:
**The complete Bernstein representation theorem, uniqueness form.** A complete Bernstein
function has exactly one representing triple `(a, b, μ)`.

TauCeti.IsCAD.exists_isCAD_lazardValuati.doc:
**CAD lifting by Lazard delineations in a reordered base.** Suppose every cell `C` of a
cylindrical algebraic decomposition of `ℝ ^ n` is an analytic submanifold, and its reordering
`(· ∘ e.symm) ⁻¹' C` by a permutation `e` of the base coordinates carries a Lazard delineation
of a fixed polynomial family. Then the stacks of those delineations, pulled back to the
original cells, form a cylindrical algebraic decomposition of `ℝ ^ (n + 1)` with the original
decomposition as its projection.

Every lifted cell is an analytic submanifold. On it, every family member has constant Lazard
valuation when the base coordinates are read through `e` and the new coordinate is read last.

      ∃ F, Function.Surjective ⇑F ∧ TauCeti.IsAdmissibleIdeal (RingHom.ker F.toRingHom)
TauCeti.IsBasic.exists_surjective_pathAl.doc:
**Gabriel's presentation theorem for basic algebras.** A finite-dimensional basic algebra over
an algebraically closed field is a quotient of the path algebra of a finite quiver by an
admissible ideal: there is a surjective algebra map `kQ → A` whose kernel is admissible.

TauCeti.IsAspherical.exists_homotopyEquiv.{u} {X Y : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [TopologicalSpace Y] [TauCeti.CWType X] [TauCeti.CWType Y] {x : X} {y : Y}

TauCeti.IsAspherical.exists_homotopyEqui.doc:
**Uniqueness of aspherical spaces of CW type.** Two aspherical spaces of CW type are homotopy
equivalent by a homotopy equivalence realizing any prescribed isomorphism `φ` of their fundamental
groups: there is a homotopy equivalence `e` and a path `γ` from `e x` to `y` such that the map
induced by `e` on fundamental groups, followed by basepoint change along `γ`, is `φ`.

The hypothesis of CW type on both spaces cannot be dropped: a point and the Warsaw circle are
aspherical with trivial fundamental groups, but they are not homotopy equivalent.

TauCeti.IsAlgebraicBelyiPair.of_mapRingE.doc:
**The Galois conjugate of an algebraic Belyi pair is an algebraic Belyi pair**: if `F` is an
algebraic Belyi pair over `k`, and `τ : F ≃+* F'` carries `k(t)` onto `k'(t)` by the coefficient
map of `σ : k ≃+* k'`, then `F'` is an algebraic Belyi pair over `k'`.

Taking `F' = F` with its structure maps precomposed with `σ⁻¹` and `τ` the identity, this is the
conjugation of a Belyi pair by an automorphism `σ` of the constants.

TauCeti.IsAlgebraicBelyiPair.signature:
TauCeti.IsAlgebraicBelyiPair.{u_1, u_2} (k : Type u_1) (F : Type u_2) [Field k] [CharZero k]
  [Field F] [Algebra k F] [Algebra (RatFunc k) F] [IsScalarTower k (RatFunc k) F]
  [FiniteDimensional (RatFunc k) F] : Prop
TauCeti.IsAlgebraicBelyiPair.doc:
An **algebraic Belyi pair** over a field `k` of characteristic zero: a function field `F / k`
with exact constant field `k`, finite over the rational function field `k(t)` through the given
`Algebra (RatFunc k) F` structure, in which every place lying over a place of `k(t)` other than
`t = 0`, `t = 1` and `t = ∞` has ramification index `1`.

The branch locus is only required to be contained in the three marked places. The base field is
pinned to characteristic zero, where `F / k(t)` is automatically separable; in characteristic `p`
the power map `t ↦ t ^ p` is inseparable and `4t(1 - t)` is constant in characteristic `2`.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.toContinuousAl.doc:
**Equivalence of complete affinoid norms.** An algebra isomorphism between completely normed
affinoid algebras is a homeomorphism, whatever complete ultrametric algebra norms they carry.
Applied to two such norms on one algebra, this says that they define the same topology.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.supSeminorm_eq.doc:
**The supremum seminorm is the spectral value of the minimal polynomial.** Let `B` be an
affinoid algebra which is integral and torsion-free over an integrally closed domain `A`. For
`f : B` with minimal polynomial `X ^ d + ∑_{i < d} aᵢ X ^ i` over `A`,
`|f|sup = max_{i < d} |aᵢ|sup ^ (1 / (d - i))`.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.isRestricted_s.doc:
**Restricted series over an affinoid algebra form an affinoid algebra.** For an affinoid
algebra `A` with a complete ultrametric algebra norm, the Gauss-normed algebra `A⟨X₁, …, Xₘ⟩` of
unit-radius restricted series is affinoid: a Tate presentation `K⟨Y₁, …, Yₙ⟩ → A` induces a
presentation `K⟨X₁, …, Xₘ, Y₁, …, Yₙ⟩ → A⟨X₁, …, Xₘ⟩`.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.height_eq_ring.signature:

  ↑m.height = ringKrullDim A
TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.height_eq_ring.doc:
**Heights of maximal ideals of affinoid domains.** Every maximal ideal of an affinoid domain
`A` has height `dim A`.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_pointNo.signature:
TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_pointNorm_eq_supSeminorm.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1}
  [NontriviallyNormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] {A : Type u_2} [CommRing A]

  ∃ x, TauCeti.pointNorm K x f = TauCeti.supSeminorm K f
TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_pointNo.doc:
**The maximum modulus principle.** On a nonzero affinoid algebra the supremum seminorm is
attained at a classical point: for every `f : A` there is a maximal ideal `x` of `A` with
`|f(x)| = |f|sup`.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_finite_.signature:
TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_finite_injective.{u, u_1} {K : Type u} [NormedField K]
  [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A] [Algebra K A] [Nontrivial A]
  (hA : TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) : ∃ n g, Function.Injective ⇑g ∧ g.Finite
TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_finite_.doc:
**Affinoid Noether normalisation.** Every nonzero affinoid algebra over a complete
ultrametric field is finite over an injectively embedded finite-variable Tate algebra.
Finiteness uses the algebra structure induced by the displayed map.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.existsUnique_a.doc:
**The universal property of restricted series over an affinoid algebra.** Let `A` and `B` be
affinoid algebras with complete ultrametric algebra norms. A `K`-algebra map `φ : A → B` and
power-bounded `b₁, …, bₖ ∈ B` extend to exactly one `K`-algebra map `A⟨X₁, …, Xₖ⟩ → B` sending
each `Xᵢ` to `bᵢ`, namely `TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.restrictedLift`. It is continuous, as is every
algebra map between such algebras (`TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.continuous_algHom`).

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.continuous_alg.doc:
Every homomorphism from a noetherian ultrametric Banach algebra to a completely normed
affinoid algebra is continuous. The affinoid presentation is purely algebraic.

TauCeti.IsAdicComplete.existsUnique_eval.signature:

TauCeti.IsAdicComplete.existsUnique_eval.doc:
**Hensel's lemma with a derivative dividing `π ^ k`.** Let `R` be `π`-adically complete with
`π` a non-zero-divisor, and let `f` be a polynomial with `f'(t) ∣ π ^ k` and
`f(t) ≡ 0 mod π ^ (2k + 1)`. Then `f` has exactly one root congruent to `t` modulo `π ^ (k + 1)`.

TauCeti.InternalGrading.exists_linearIndependent_isCompl_torsion.{u, u_1} {k : Type u_1}

**The free part of the structure theorem.** In a finitely generated graded `k[X]`-module over
a field on which `X` lowers degree by `d ≠ 0`, the torsion submodule has a complement spanned by a
`k[X]`-linearly independent family of homogeneous elements: `M` is its torsion submodule plus a
graded free module, one `X`-tower for each element of the family.

  [Module.Finite (Polynomial k) M] (hd : d ≠ 0)

    ∃ (_ : Finite ι) (_ : Finite κ),

TauCeti.InternalGrading.exists_isInterna.doc:

by `d ≠ 0` in a finitely generated graded `k[X]`-module `M` over a field. Then `M` is the internal
direct sum of cyclic submodules `k[X] ∙ t i` generated by homogeneous elements `t i`, indexed by
the disjoint union of two finite types: for `i` in the first, `t i` has zero annihilator, so
`k[X] ∙ t i` is a free `X`-tower; for `j` in the second, `t j` has annihilator `(X ^ m j)` with
`m j ≠ 0`, so `k[X] ∙ t j ≅ k[X] ⧸ (X ^ m j)`.

TauCeti.InternalGrading.exists_iSupIndep.doc:
**The torsion part of the structure theorem.** Let `X` lower degree by `d ≠ 0` in a finitely
generated graded `k[X]`-module over a field. Then every homogeneous `k[X]`-submodule `L` contained
in the torsion submodule is the independent sum of finitely many cyclic submodules `k[X] ∙ t i`,
where each `t i` is homogeneous with annihilator `(X ^ m i)` for some `m i ≠ 0`. Thus each summand
is isomorphic to `k[X] ⧸ (X ^ m i)` (`Ideal.quotTorsionOfEquivSpanSingleton`).

TauCeti.IntegralOrder.det_smul_mem_span.doc:
**Cramer's bound for subalgebras of integral elements.** Let `e` be an `F`-basis of `E` lying in
an `R`-subalgebra `Γ` all of whose elements are integral over the integrally closed domain `R`, and
let `r = det (Tr_F (e i * e j))` be the Gram determinant of the regular trace form. Then `r • x`
lies in the `R`-span of `e` for every `x ∈ Γ`.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.weylGroup_typeE₈.doc:
**The reflections in the 240 roots generate the isometry group of the E₈ lattice**: its Weyl
group is the whole of `O(E₈)`.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.typeE₈IsometryD8.doc:
**The `E₈` root lattice is isometric to the spinor glue lattice `D₈⁺`.**

The underlying rational equivalence sends the `i`-th simple root of `E₈` to the `i`-th vector of
Bourbaki's plate VII in Conway--Sloane coordinates.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.nonempty_isometr.doc:
**`E₈ ⊕ E₈ ⊕ U ≅ D₁₆⁺ ⊕ U`.** Adding the hyperbolic plane `U` makes the two non-isometric even
unimodular lattices of rank sixteen isometric.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.isLeast_form_sel.doc:
**The minimum norm of the discriminant class labelled `a : ZMod (n + 1)`.**  The class
`typeADiscriminantGroupEquiv n a = a.val • ω₁` of `Aₙ` has minimum norm
`a.val (n + 1 - a.val) / (n + 1)`, the shortest norm of the Conway–Sloane glue label `[a]` of an
`Aₙ` component.

Attained least norms in two discriminant cosets add to the attained least norm of the
corresponding coset of the orthogonal sum.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.infinite_isometr.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.infinite_isometry_of_isIndefinite.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup V]

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.infinite_isometr.doc:
**Indefinite lattices have infinite isometry groups.** A nondegenerate indefinite integral
lattice of rank at least three has infinitely many isometries.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.gaussSign_discri.doc:
**Milgram's theorem for `⟨2m⟩`**: the discriminant form of the rank-one lattice `⟨2m⟩` has
Gauss-sum invariant the sign of `m`.

**Milgram's theorem.** The Gauss-sum invariant of the discriminant form of an even
nondegenerate lattice is its signature `t₊ - t₋` modulo `8`.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.exists_ne_zero_m.doc:
**Minkowski's convex body theorem for a realized lattice.** Let `φ` realize a nondegenerate
integral lattice `L` in a real inner product space `E` of dimension `n`. A convex set `K ⊆ E`,
symmetric about the origin, of volume greater than `2ⁿ · √(det L)` contains `φ y` for some
nonzero `y ∈ L`.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.evenIntermediate.doc:
**Even overlattices correspond to quadratic-isotropic subgroups.** For an even lattice, the
intermediate-carrier order isomorphism restricts to the even carriers on one side and the
quadratic-isotropic subgroups of the discriminant group on the other.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.discriminantQuad.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.discriminantQuadraticModule.{u} {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V]

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.discriminantQuad.doc:
The discriminant group of an even nondegenerate integral lattice, equipped with its canonical
half-norm quadratic map and discriminant polar pairing.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.classNumber.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.classNumber.{u} {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module ℚ V]
  (L : TauCeti.IntegralLattice V) : ℕ
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.classNumber.doc:
The class number `h(L)`: the number of isometry classes in the genus of `L`. It is `0` when
the genus contains infinitely many classes.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.checkerboardDisc.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.checkerboardDiscriminantQuadraticIsometry (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (hn : Even n) :

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.checkerboardDisc.doc:
**The standard model is isometric to the discriminant quadratic module of an even-rank
checkerboard lattice**, by the identification carrying `(1, 0)` to the vector class and `(0, 1)`
to the spinor class.

This is the `Dₙ` row of the ADE table for even `n`: not only is the discriminant group `(ℤ/2)²`,
its quadratic form is the displayed one.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.unitNor.doc:
**A positive definite lattice is `I_k` plus a lattice without vectors of norm one.** The
standard lattice `I_k` is carried onto the unit-norm sublattice, with `k` its rank, and the second
summand is the complement `unitNormComplement L`.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.three_p.doc:
**Hermite's inequality for the minimum, without roots.** A positive definite integral lattice
of rank `n` satisfies `3 ^ (n choose 2) · (min L)ⁿ ≤ 4 ^ (n choose 2) · det L`.

integral lattice of rank `n` satisfy `(∏ᵢ λᵢ) · πⁿ ≤ 4ⁿ · Γ(n/2 + 1)² · det L`, that is,
`∏ᵢ λᵢ ≤ cₙⁿ · det L` with `cₙ = (4 / π) · Γ(n/2 + 1) ^ (2/n)` the constant of Minkowski's bound for
the minimum.

**Positive definite unimodular lattices of rank at most nine.** Such a lattice is the
standard lattice `Iₙ`, the root lattice `E₈`, or `I₁ ⊕ E₈`.

satisfies `min L ≤ (4 / 3) ^ ((n - 1) / 2) · (det L) ^ (1 / n)`.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.minimum.doc:
**Minkowski's bound for the minimum.** A positive definite integral lattice of rank `n`
satisfies `min L ≤ (4 / π) · Γ(n/2 + 1) ^ (2/n) · (det L) ^ (1/n)`.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.finite_.doc:
**A positive definite genus contains finitely many classes.** The lattices of the genus all
have the rank and determinant of `L`, so this is the finiteness of positive definite classes of
given rank and bounded determinant.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.signature: TauCeti.IntegralLattice.{u} (V : Type u) [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module ℚ V] : Type u
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.doc:
An integral symmetric lattice in a rational vector space.

The field `le_dual` says exactly that the form takes integer values on pairs of vectors in
`carrier`.

TauCeti.Int.Matrix.not_forall_exists_ne_.doc:
**The exponent in Siegel's lemma is optimal.** For an `m × (m + 1)` integer system, Siegel's
lemma `Int.Matrix.exists_ne_zero_int_vec_norm_le` gives a nonzero integer solution of sup norm at
most `((m + 1) · max 1 ‖A‖) ^ m`. For `0 < m` no exponent `e < m` works, with any constant `C`:
the system `b xᵢ = xᵢ₊₁` with `b` large has no nonzero integer solution of sup norm at most
`C · max 1 ‖A‖ ^ e`.

TauCeti.InjectiveTensor.doc:
The algebraic tensor product `E ⊗[𝕜] F` carrying the injective seminorm.

This wrapper distinguishes the injective seminorm from other norms on the same algebraic tensor
product, such as the projective norm or the Hilbert-space norm of inner product spaces.

The stage of the first `n` strands: the subalgebra generated by the generators
`T 0, …, T (n - 2)` that cross two of the strands `0, …, n - 1`. It is the image of the type-A
Hecke algebra on `n` strands.

TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.shift.doc:
The strand shift by `k`: the algebra endomorphism `T i ↦ T (i + k)` that moves every braid
`k` strands to the right.

TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.exists.doc:
**Ocneanu's theorem.** For every parameter `z` there is exactly one Markov trace with
parameter `z`.

The disjoint block map: the algebra map from the tensor product of the stages `a` and `b` to
the stage `a + b` that places the first factor on the first `a` strands and the second factor,
shifted by `a`, on the next `b` strands. Its injectivity, which would make it an embedding,
needs the basis theorem and is not proved here.

TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.doc:
The infinite type-A Hecke algebra over `R` with parameter `q`: the free `R`-algebra on `ℕ`
modulo `TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.Rel`. It is the union of its finite stages
`TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.stage R q n`; see the module docstring for what is proved about
them.

TauCeti.InfEquivAt.potentialIso.doc:
**Karp's theorem, converse direction.** Structures in a relational language that are both coded
into a carrier `κ` and satisfy the same infinitary sentences with carrier `κ` are potentially
isomorphic.

**Serre's criterion.** When `S` is generated over `R` by a set `s` and `G` acts by `R`-algebra
automorphisms, membership in the inertia subgroup of a two-sided ideal `I` is decided on `s` alone:
the elements moved into `I` form an `R`-subalgebra.

TauCeti.Hyperfunction.oneDimBoundaryPres.doc:
**The presheaf of one-dimensional hyperfunctions is separated**: a section that vanishes on
the members of an open cover vanishes.

TauCeti.Hyperfunction.OneDimBoundaryQuot.doc:
The space `O(ℂ ∖ ℝ) / O(W(U))` of one-dimensional hyperfunctions on an open set `U ⊆ ℝ`,
represented by holomorphic functions on `ℂ ∖ ℝ` modulo those extending holomorphically across
`U`.

TauCeti.HurewiczOne.hurewiczHomologyAddE.doc:
**The Hurewicz theorem in degree one**: for a path-connected space `X` with a base point `x`,
the Hurewicz map identifies the abelianization of `π₁(X, x)` with `H₁(X; ℤ)`, the first homology
group of the singular chain complex of `X` with integer coefficients.

TauCeti.HurewiczOne.hurewiczAddEquiv.doc:
**The Hurewicz theorem in degree one**: for a path-connected space, the Hurewicz map
identifies the abelianized fundamental group with the first homology group, written as the
explicit homology of the short complex `C₂ → C₁ → C₀`.

TauCeti.Huber.twoSidedRestrictedSubmodul.doc:
**Wedhorn's degree decomposition, Lemma 8.33(i).** A two-sided restricted family is the sum of
its non-negative part and its negative part: `A⟨z, z⁻¹⟩ = A⟨z⟩ + z⁻¹A⟨z⁻¹⟩` at the level of
coefficients. This is `twoSidedRestrictedSubmodule_eq_sup_compl` at the sign partition, which is
where the restrictedness of each summand is established.

TauCeti.Huber.tensorTopology.doc:
**The tensor topology** on `B ⊗[A] C`, for adic structure maps `A → B` and `A → C`: for any
compatible pairs of definition `(A₀, I)`, `(B₀, I B₀)` and `(C₀, I C₀)`, its neighbourhoods of
zero are generated by the images of `Iⁿ F`, where `F` is the image of `B₀ ⊗[A₀] C₀`
(`TauCeti.Huber.hasBasis_tensorTopology`). It is not an instance, since `B ⊗[A] C` may carry
other topologies.

TauCeti.Huber.isWeightBounded_of_isWeigh.doc:
**Wedhorn's coordinatewise hypothesis gives the uniform bound.** Each weighted monomial set is
a finite pointwise product of powers of the weighted variables, so it lies in the product of the
bounded sets containing those powers — and a finite pointwise product of bounded sets is bounded.

This is what makes `TauCeti.Huber.IsWeightBounded` the right hypothesis for the summability
theorem rather than a stronger one invented for it: the two are reached from the same place.

TauCeti.Huber.isTopologicallyFiniteType_.doc:
**Affinoid algebras are the algebras topologically of finite type.** A complete ultrametric
normed `K`-algebra `B` is topologically of finite type over `K` in Huber's sense (Wedhorn,
Definition 5.57) exactly when it is a quotient of a Tate algebra `K⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩` as a
`K`-algebra.

TauCeti.Huber.isSheafyRing_of_isStrongly.doc:
**Every strongly noetherian Tate ring is sheafy** in the sense of Wedhorn's Definition 8.26
(`TauCeti.Huber.IsSheafyRing`). This is Wedhorn's Theorem 8.28(b); `A` need not be complete or
Hausdorff. The identity of `Â` is topologically of finite type, so this is the case `B = Â` of
`TauCeti.Huber.isStablySheafyRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian`.

A ring with separately continuous multiplication in which the sets `ϖ ^ n A₀`, `n ≥ 0`, form
a neighbourhood basis of zero carries an ultrametric ring seminorm, equal to the Tate gauge, whose
open balls about zero form a neighbourhood basis of zero.

**Completion of a finite module is base change to the completed ring** (Huber, Lemma
2.3(iii)). If `A` is a Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition and `M` is a finitely
generated `A`-module with its natural topology, the canonical map `Â ⊗[A] M → M̂` is bijective.

TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStrictM.doc:
**Linear maps of finite modules over a Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition are
strict** (Huber, Lemma 2.3(i)). If `A₀` is noetherian, every `A`-linear map between finitely
generated `A`-modules with their natural topologies is continuous and open onto its image.

TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isClosed_.doc:
**Submodules of finite modules over a complete Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition
are closed** (Huber, Lemma 2.3(ii)). If `A` is complete and Hausdorff with a noetherian ring of
definition, every `A`-submodule of a finite `A`-module is closed in its natural topology.

**Huber's filtration** `K_i^p` of the term of degree `p`: for a set `N ⊆ M`, the product over
the faces `S`, `|S| = p + 1`, of the subgroups `Iⁱ · C[F_p / f_S] · N` of `M_{f_S}`.

The separated completion of the degree-`p` term of the rational-localization Čech complex,
for the product of the natural module topologies on its faces.

TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.of_isModuleTopology.{u_1, u_2} {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A]

**A finite algebra over a Tate ring is a Tate ring.** If `B` is a commutative `A`-algebra,
finite as an `A`-module and carrying its natural topology, then `B` is a Tate ring; the image of a
pseudouniformiser of `A` is a pseudouniformiser of `B`.

TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoCoherentOver.signature:

  [_root_.Module R M] (m : ℕ∞) : Prop
TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoCoherentOver.doc:
`M` is *`m`-pseudocoherent* over `R`: it has a resolution `⋯ → F₁ → F₀ → M → 0` by finite free
modules `Fᵢ = Fin (n i) → R`, with augmentation `ε` and differentials `d i : Fᵢ₊₁ → Fᵢ`, which is
exact at `M, F₀, …, F_{m-1}`. Thus `0`-pseudocoherent means finitely generated,
`1`-pseudocoherent means finitely presented, and for `m = ⊤` the whole resolution is exact
(Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 1.1.1; Stacks, Tag 064T, with the index negated).

a Huber ring.

subgroup `N` of an affine group `G` of finite type over a field of characteristic zero,
restriction to the invariant functions identifies the fppf homogeneous quotient `G/N` with the
sheaf of points of `Spec O(G)^N`.

`f : O(G) ⟶ O(N)` be a surjection of finite-type commutative Hopf algebras over a field of
characteristic zero, representing a closed immersion of a reductive group `N` into `G`. Then
restriction to the functions on `G` invariant under right translation by `N` identifies the fppf
homogeneous quotient `G/N` with the sheaf of points of `Spec O(G)^N`.

generated defining ideal is the stabilizer, over every commutative value algebra, of a line in
a finite-dimensional exterior-power representation. The line lies in the weight space of a
unique character of the subgroup, including when the subgroup is nonreduced.

**Chevalley's coset criterion.** A closed subgroup with finitely generated defining ideal
admits a finite exterior-power representation and a unimodular vector whose matrix coefficients
detect its left cosets over every commutative value algebra, including nonreduced algebras.

TauCeti.HopfIdeal.IsParabolic.doc:
A Hopf ideal defines a **parabolic subgroup** when its base change to an algebraic closure
defines a smooth closed subgroup of the geometric fibre containing a Borel subgroup.

The order is contravariant: `I ≤ J` says that the subgroup cut out by `I` contains the subgroup
cut out by `J`.

TauCeti.HopfIdeal.IsBorelOverAlgClosed.e.doc:
**Borel conjugacy.** Any two Borel subgroups of a finite-type affine group over an
algebraically closed field are conjugate by a rational point. The ambient group need not
be smooth, reduced, or connected.

TauCeti.Homologous.homotopyEquiv.doc:
**Homologous twisting cocycles give homotopy equivalent twisted complexes**: for every
differential graded right module `(ℳ, dM)`, the twisted complexes of `mP` and `mQ` are
homotopy equivalent.

TauCeti.Hodge.exists_isCompl_of_isPolari.doc:
**Semisimplicity of polarizable rational Hodge structures.** Every rational Hodge substructure
of a polarizable pure Hodge structure has a complement, both over `ℚ` and after complexification,
orthogonal to it for some polarization.

TauCeti.Hodge.Polarization.exists_comp_t.doc:
**Self-duality is invertible up to a nonzero integer.** For a polarization of `V`, there is a
Hodge morphism `g : V^*(-n) → V` such that composing it with self-duality, in either order, is
multiplication by a nonzero natural number `c`. Over `ℚ`, `c⁻¹ • g` is the inverse of
self-duality.

TauCeti.Hodge.PolarizableHodgeStructureC.doc:
**Categorical semisimplicity of polarizable rational Hodge structures.** Every object is
isomorphic to a finite biproduct of simple objects induced by rational Hodge substructures.

The category of finite-dimensional polarizable rational Hodge structures of weight `n`, with
integral, rational, and complex models in `Type u`.

The integral model is a finitely generated free lattice and determines the conjugation on the
complexification. The rational model is the carrier on which morphisms are defined. Polarizability
is retained only as a property, so no particular polarizing form is part of an object.

TauCeti.Hodge.MixedHodgeStructureCat.abe.doc: Mixed Hodge structures, with rational Hodge morphisms, form an abelian category.

TauCeti.Hodge.MixedHodgeStructure.map_la.doc:
**Deligne's fine conjugation relation.** Conjugation exchanges `I^{p,q}` and `I^{q,p}`
modulo the sum of the components `I^{r,s}` with `r < q` and `s < p`.

TauCeti.Hodge.MixedHodgeStructure.isInte.doc:
**Deligne's theorem.** The pieces `I^{p,q}` of Deligne's bigrading form an internal direct sum
of the complex vector space underlying a mixed Hodge structure.

**The Hodge decomposition of a complex graded piece**: the Hodge components of
`WC_k / WC_{k-1}` are an internal direct sum.

TauCeti.Hodge.MixedHodgeStructure.Hom.ra.doc:
**Strictness of a morphism of mixed Hodge structures for the Hodge filtration.** A complex
vector lying both in the image of `f` and in the target's Hodge step `F^p` is the image of a
vector of the source's `F^p`.

The two filtration steps are the sums of the bigrading pieces of first index at least `p`, and `f`
respects the bigrading, so a preimage may be truncated to its components of first index at least
`p` without changing its image.

TauCeti.Hodge.IsPolarization.doc:
The **Hodge–Riemann bilinear relations** for a fixed integral bilinear form `Q` on the lattice
of a weight-`n` Hodge structure.

The form is `(-1)^n`-symmetric and nondegenerate; its complexification annihilates
`F p × F (n + 1 - p)`; and `i^(p-q) Q x (conj x)` is a positive real number for every nonzero `x`
in the Hodge component `H^{p,q}`, where `q = n - p`.

TauCeti.Hodge.IsPolarizable.internalHom.doc:
**Polarizable pure Hodge structures are closed under internal homs.** The internal hom of
weights `n₁` and `n₂` is polarizable of weight `n₂ - n₁`.

TauCeti.Hodge.IsPolarizable.dual.doc: **The dual of a polarizable pure Hodge structure is polarizable.**

TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.isInterna.doc:
**The Hodge decomposition.** The Hodge components `H^{p,n-p}` form an internal direct sum of
the ambient complex vector space.

TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.finsum_ho.doc:
**The Hodge numbers partition the dimension**: the Hodge numbers of a weight-`n` Hodge
structure on a finite-dimensional complex vector space sum to its dimension.

TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.signature:
TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.{u} (W : Type u) [AddCommGroup W] [_root_.Module ℂ W]

TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.doc:
A pure Hodge structure of weight `n` on a complex vector space with conjugation `ω`.

The decreasing filtration `F` is bounded and `n`-opposed to its conjugate: for every `p`,
`F p` is complementary to the conjugate of `F (n + 1 - p)`.

map of pairs from `(R, I)`, there is a unique `R`-algebra map from the henselization of
`(R, I)` to `S` carrying the extended ideal into `J`.

**The universal property of the henselization of a local ring.** Every local homomorphism
from a local ring `R` to a henselian local ring `S` factors through a unique local
`R`-algebra map from the henselization of `R` along its maximal ideal. Every `R`-algebra map
from the henselization to `S` is in fact local and equal to this one (`eq_lift`).

TauCeti.HeisenbergDGA.minimalModel_m_thr.doc:
**The transferred ternary operation on `([a], [a], [b])`**: `m₃^H ([a], [a], [b]) = [a c]`.
Of the Kontsevich--Soibelman/Merkulov tree sum only the term
`-p m₂ (i (τ [a]), h m₂ (i [a], i [b]))` survives, with `h (a b) = c` and the Koszul twist

`ZMod 2`-linear endomorphism of the free module on generators whose coefficient from `x` to `y`
is the number, modulo two, of nonnegative domains of Maslov index one from `x` to `y` avoiding
the basepoints (`TauCeti.HeegaardRegionSystem.hatCoefficient`).

TauCeti.HeegaardRegionSystem.IsNice.doc:
A pointed Heegaard diagram, with region Euler characteristics `χ`, is *nice* when every
region containing no basepoint is a bigon or a square: a disk, of Euler characteristic one, with
two or four corners.

its composite with `f` is.

additive homomorphism out of a topological group is continuous as soon as it is continuous at `0`
(`continuous_of_continuousAt_zero`), so `hfc` is the same assumption the open-mapping theorem
makes. This is the form behind `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology`, which pins down the
topology of a finite module over a Tate ring.

first-countable nonarchimedean group to a Baire space is open, when `A` has a zero sequence of
units.

the action, in the form `hc` that the Baire step already uses.

**The fundamental theorem of calculus for weak derivatives.** If `u'` is the weak derivative
of `u` on `Ioo a b` and `t₀ ∈ Ioo a b`, then `u` is almost everywhere on `Ioo a b` equal to a
constant plus the primitive `t ↦ ∫ s in t₀..t, u' s`.

TauCeti.HasWeakFDerivOn.lintegral_ofReal.doc:
**Jensen's bound for the gradient of a mollification.** If `U` is a weak derivative field of
`u` on the whole space and `rho` is a smooth compactly supported probability kernel, then
`∫ Φ(‖D(u ⋆ rho)‖) ≤ ∫ Φ(‖U‖)` for every `Φ` convex and monotone on `[0, ∞)`, in extended
nonnegative form.

TauCeti.HasWeakConjWirtingerDerivOn.exis.doc:
**Weyl's lemma for `\bar∂`.** A distributional solution with finite-dimensional complex
coefficients agrees almost everywhere on its domain with a holomorphic function.

TauCeti.HasNodalReduction.of_genus_eq_ze.signature:
TauCeti.HasNodalReduction.of_genus_eq_zero_of_divisor_degree_eq_one.{u} {R K : Type u} [CommRing R]

  (C : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme) [C.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec ↧K)]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsCurveOver K]
  [∀ (y : TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.CodimensionOnePoint C),

  (hk : IsIntegrallyClosedIn K ↑C.functionField)
  (hg :

        (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology
          (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf.trivial C).obj 1) =
      0)
  {D : TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.SchemeWeilDivisor C}

    (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.SchemeWeilDivisor.relativeDegree (C ↘ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec ↧K)) D =

TauCeti.HasNodalReduction.of_genus_eq_ze.doc:
**A curve of genus zero with a divisor of degree one has nodal reduction.** Let `C` be a
regular proper curve over the fraction field `K` of a discrete valuation ring `R`, with `K`
integrally closed in `K(C)`. If `dim_K H¹(C, 𝒪_C) = 0` and some divisor on `C` has degree one,
then `C` has a proper at-worst-nodal model over `R`; indeed `C ≅ ℙ¹_K`, which has the smooth proper
model `ℙ¹_R`.

TauCeti.HasMinMaxLowerBound.kyFanGauge_a.doc:
**Ky Fan triangle inequality from the converse min–max localization.** On a pair of inner
product spaces with the property `HasMinMaxLowerBound`, the Ky Fan gauges are subadditive:
`Kₖ(S + T) ≤ Kₖ(S) + Kₖ(T)`.

**Cauchy-Laurent coefficient formula.** For any convergent Laurent series on
`Metric.eball c R \ Metric.closedBall c r` and any interior circle radius `ρ ∈ (r, R)`, the
`n`-th Laurent coefficient is `circleLaurentCoeff f c ρ n`.

TauCeti.HasHomotopyLiftingProperty.of_pa.signature:
TauCeti.HasHomotopyLiftingProperty.of_partitionOfUnity.{w, u, v, u_1} {ι : Type u_1} {E : Type u}
  {B : Type v} {A : Type w} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B] [TopologicalSpace A]
  {p : E → B} {U : ι → Set B} (ρ : PartitionOfUnity ι B)
  (hρ : ∀ (i : ι), Function.support ⇑(ρ i) ⊆ U i)
  (hlift :
    ∀ (i : ι) (W : Set A),
      IsOpen W →

TauCeti.HasHomotopyLiftingProperty.of_pa.doc:
**Dold's local-to-global homotopy lifting theorem.** Let `p : E → B` be a map and
`(U i)_{i ∈ ι}` a numerable cover of `B`, witnessed by a partition of unity
`ρ : PartitionOfUnity ι B` with `support (ρ i) ⊆ U i` for every `i`. If each restriction
`p ⁻¹' U i → U i` has the homotopy lifting property with respect to every open subset of `A`, then
`p` has the homotopy lifting property with respect to `A`.

TauCeti.HasHomotopyExtensionProperty.pro.doc:
**Strøm's product theorem**: if closed subsets `A ⊆ X` and `B ⊆ Y` have the homotopy
extension property, then so does `A × Y ∪ X × B ⊆ X × Y`.

TauCeti.HasGaloisLabel.signature:

  (j : TauCeti.TransitiveGroupIndex n) : Prop
TauCeti.HasGaloisLabel.doc:
The Galois group of `f` carries the transitive-group label `j` of degree `n`: `f` is
separable of degree `n`, and some numbering of its roots in the splitting field by `Fin n` carries
the image of the Galois action on the roots to a conjugate of the reference subgroup
`referenceSubgroup n j`. By `TauCeti.hasGaloisLabel_iff_forall`, every numbering then does.

TauCeti.HasApproximationProperty.doc:
The identity can be approximated uniformly on every norm-compact set by bounded operators
with finite-dimensional range.

TauCeti.HaagerupZsido.integral_norm_reci.doc: **The exact mass of the Haagerup–Zsidó kernel.** `∫_ℝ ‖k(t)‖ dt = π / 2`.

TauCeti.HaagerupZsido.integral_exp_mul_I.signature:
TauCeti.HaagerupZsido.integral_exp_mul_I_mul_reciprocalKernel {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 ≤ |x|) :

TauCeti.HaagerupZsido.integral_exp_mul_I.doc:
**The exterior reciprocal Fourier identity.** For `|x| ≥ 1`, the Fourier integral of the
Haagerup–Zsidó kernel is `∫ e^{itx} k(t) dt = 1 / x`.

TauCeti.GroupPresentation.homEquiv.{u_1} (P : TauCeti.GroupPresentation) {G : Type u_1} [Group G] :

TauCeti.GroupPresentation.homEquiv.doc:
Homomorphisms from a finite presentation correspond to generator assignments satisfying
its transcribed relators. No generation or injectivity condition is imposed on the assignment.

TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.zariskiTopology.signature:
TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.zariskiTopology.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {G : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [Group G]

TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.zariskiTopology.doc: The Zariski topology generated by the complements of algebraic sets over `G`.

TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.isEquationallyNoeth.doc:
**Linear groups are equationally Noetherian.** Over a commutative Noetherian ring `R`, the
general linear group `GL n R` is equationally Noetherian over any coefficients: every system of
equations in finitely many variables has a finite subsystem with the same solutions in
`GL n R`.

TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.IsGDomain.of_isCSA.signature:
TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.IsGDomain.of_isCSA.{u_1, u_3} {G : Type u_1} {H : Type u_3} [Group G] [Group H]

  TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.IsGDomain ι
TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.IsGDomain.of_isCSA.doc:
**CSA groups are domains** (Baumslag–Myasnikov–Remeslennikov, Proposition 1). A CSA group in
which the images of two coefficients do not commute is a domain over these coefficients.

TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.CoordGroup.signature:
TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.CoordGroup.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {G : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} {X : Type u_3}

TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.CoordGroup.doc: The coordinate group `G_{R(S)} = G[X] ⧸ Rad_H(S)` of a system `S` over `H`.

TauCeti.GromovWassersteinSpace.signature:
TauCeti.GromovWassersteinSpace.{u, v} (p : ENNReal) (Z : Type v) [MetricSpace Z] [Fact (1 ≤ p)] :
  Type (max (u + 1) v)
TauCeti.GromovWassersteinSpace.doc:
Finite-size standard Borel measured kernels modulo weak isomorphism, with the full
Gromov–Wasserstein metric. The carrier universe is fixed, but is independent of the target.

TauCeti.GridLink.unknottingNumber.doc:
The unknotting number of a grid link: the least number of crossing changes turning it into
the unknot, or `⊤` if no sequence of crossing changes does.

TauCeti.GridDiagram.unblockedHomologyCom.signature:
