TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.hungerbuhlerWasem_.doc:
**The Hungerbühler–Wasem generalized residue theorem for a contour cycle** (HW Thm 3.3).
Let `U` be open, `S ⊆ U` finite, `f` holomorphic on `U ∖ S` and meromorphic at each point of
`S`, and let `C` be a contour cycle in `U`, **null-homologous** in `U`, whose curves are
piecewise-`C¹` immersions rooted off `S` and satisfy conditions (A′) and (B). Then the Cauchy
principal value of `f` along `C` exists and

`PV ∮_C f = 2πi · ∑_{s ∈ S} n_s(C) · Res_s f`,

each singularity weighted by the **generalized** winding number of `C` about it. The
singularities are allowed to lie **on** `C`, where those weights are in general not integers and
the contour integral only exists as a principal value.

Null-homology is asked of the cycle only, never of its generators, so the theorem covers the
combinations that make cycles worth having: a difference of two homologous loops around a hole of
`U`, neither of them null-homologous, is null-homologous. Its `S = ∅` case is the homology Cauchy
theorem for cycles
(`TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.homologyCauchyTheorem`), and its one-generator case is the single-curve
theorem `TauCeti.Contour.hungerbuhlerWasem_residueTheorem`. Where the trace of `C` avoids `S`
the principal value is an ordinary integral and the statement is the classical residue theorem
for cycles (`TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.classicalResidueTheorem_nullHomologous`), which needs neither
immersions nor the conditions.

TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.homologyCauchyTheo.doc:
**The homology Cauchy theorem for contour cycles.** Let `C` be a finite formal integer
combination of closed piecewise-`C¹` curves whose trace lies in an open set `U`. If `C` is
null-homologous in `U` and `f` is holomorphic on `U`, with values in any complex normed space,
then the contour integral of `f` over the whole cycle vanishes.

The null-homology assumption is imposed only on `C`, not on each supported curve, so the theorem
includes cancellations between different generators.

`∮_C f = 2πi · ∑_{s ∈ S} n_s(C) · Res_s f`.

TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.classicalResidueTh.doc:
**The classical residue theorem for a null-homologous contour cycle.** Let `U` be open, `S` a
finite set, `f` differentiable on `U ∖ S` and meromorphic at each point of `S` lying in `U`, and let
`C` be a contour cycle in `U`, **null-homologous** in `U`, whose trace **avoids** `S`. Then

`Cycle.integral f C = 2πi · ∑_{s ∈ S} n_s(C) · Res_s f`,

each pole weighted by the generalized winding number of `C` about it.

Null-homology is asked of the cycle only, never of its generators, so the theorem covers the
combinations that make cycles worth having: a difference of two loops around a hole of `U`, neither
of them null-homologous, is. Points of `S` outside `U` are harmless rather than excluded, their
winding number vanishing by null-homology, and `S` may list regular points of `f`, whose residues
are `0`.

Its `S = ∅` case is the homology Cauchy theorem for cycles
(`TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.homologyCauchyTheorem`), and its one-generator case is the single-curve
theorem `TauCeti.Contour.classicalResidueTheorem_nullHomologous`.

TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.cauchyTheorem_star.doc:
**Cauchy's theorem for a cycle in a star-shaped open set.** A holomorphic function integrates
to zero along every contour cycle contained in an open set star-shaped about some point.

TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.cauchyIntegralForm.doc:
**Cauchy's integral formula for a cycle** (roadmap Layer 3). For `f` holomorphic on an open `U`,
`C` a contour cycle in `U` that is null-homologous there, and `z ∈ U` off the trace of `C`,

`Cycle.integral (fun w ↦ f w / (w − z)) C = 2πi · n_z(C) · f z`,

so that `f z · n_z(C) = (2πi)⁻¹ ∮_C f(w)/(w − z) dw`: the Cauchy-type integral over the cycle
recovers the value of `f` at `z`, counted with the multiplicity with which `C` winds around it. The
`S = ∅` companion of this statement is the homology Cauchy theorem for cycles
(`TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.homologyCauchyTheorem`).

function.** Let `f` be holomorphic on an open `U` with values in a complex Banach space, let `C` be
a contour cycle in `U` that is null-homologous there, and let `z ∈ U` lie off the trace of `C`.

**Cauchy's integral formula for a cycle, for the `k`-th derivative.** Let `f` be holomorphic on
an open `U`, let `C` be a contour cycle in `U` that is null-homologous there, and let `z ∈ U` lie
off the trace of `C`. Then for every `k`,

`Cycle.integral (fun w ↦ f w / (w − z) ^ (k + 1)) C = 2πi · n_z(C) · f⁽ᵏ⁾(z) / k !`.

Cauchy kernel `w ↦ f w / (w − z) ^ (k + 1)`, whose only possible singularity in `U` is at `z`.

path of a simply connected open set `U` issuing from `z₀` is the germ at `z₀` of a single function
analytic on all of `U`.

So on a simply connected domain analytic continuation produces no new branches, and a
"multi-valued analytic function" there is single-valued after all.

`C^n` on an open set `s`, with `1 ≤ n`, and whose derivative at `a ∈ s` is a continuous linear
equivalence, coincides on a neighbourhood of `a` with an `OpenPartialHomeomorph` whose source is
contained in `s` and whose inverse is `C^n` on its target.

which all iterated derivatives of order `1 ≤ i ≤ k` vanish is null, provided
`finrank ℝ E < (k + 1) * finrank ℝ F`.

reductive commutative bialgebra, the invariants of the symmetric algebra `Sym V` form a finitely
generated algebra.

TauCeti.Colored3Graph.IsTopRegularOverPo.doc:
**Slicing lemma.** If `H` is `(δ, r)`-top-regular over `P` at a positive rank, then it is
`(max (2δ) (δ / α), r)`-top-regular over every polyad `P'` whose pair graphs lie in those of `P`
and whose support is at least an `α`-fraction of the support of `P`. The polyad `P'` may live
over a different skeleton, so this is how top regularity passes to a refined lower skeleton.

`H` is `(δ, r)`-top-regular over the polyad `P` when, for every top color `c` and every
family of `r` subpolyads of `P` whose union support has at least `δ` times the size of the
support of `P`, the relative density of `c` on that union is within `δ` of the relative density
of `c` over `P`. Members of the family may repeat, so this tests unions of at most `r`
subpolyads.

profinite pro-`p` group `G` with `cd_p G ≤ 2` and `H²(G, 𝔽_p)` finite, and an open

point of its unipotent part times a point of its Levi part.

isomorphic to one of the explicitly constructed groups on the classification list.

TauCeti.ClassFunction.natCard_nsmul_mem_.doc:
**Artin's sharp induction theorem, read for the elementary subgroups.** Every cyclic subgroup
is elementary, so the sharp cyclic theorem gives the explicit multiplier `|G|` here too.

When `Nat.card G` vanishes in `k`, the multiple is zero; the intended nonvacuous content is the
characteristic-zero specialization.

This is *weaker* than Brauer's induction theorem, which asserts the same with multiplier `1`. By
`TauCeti.ClassFunction.indVirtualCharacters_eq_virtualCharacters_iff`, Brauer's theorem is
equivalent to `1` being induced from the elementary subgroups, which is not proved here.

**Artin's induction theorem, sharp form, through the canonical API.** For every virtual
character `f` of a finite group `G`, the explicit multiple `|G| • f` belongs to the subgroup
generated by virtual characters induced from cyclic subgroups.  When `Nat.card G` vanishes in `k`,
the multiple is zero; the intended nonvacuous content is the characteristic-zero specialization.

**Artin's induction theorem with its induced-character-span target.** Over a
algebraically closed field in which `|G|` is invertible (in particular, in characteristic zero),
`|G| • f` belongs to the additive subgroup generated by characters induced from irreducible
characters of cyclic subgroups.

TauCeti.ClassFunction.indVirtualCharacte.doc:
**Brauer's induction theorem.** Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero,
every virtual character of a finite group is an integral combination of virtual characters
induced from elementary subgroups.

**An induction theorem, one prime at a time and with coefficients in a subring.** Let `A` be a
subring of `k` admitting an additive map `t : A → ℤ` with `t 1 = 1`; for example `ℤ[ζ]` for a root
of unity `ζ` in characteristic zero (`PowerBasis.exists_linearMap_apply_one`). The virtual
characters induced from a family of subgroups exhaust `R(G)` exactly when, for every prime `p`,
some multiple `m • 1` with `p ∤ m` is an `A`-linear combination of them.

This reduces an induction theorem to a separate statement for each prime `p`. In Serre's proof of
Brauer's induction theorem, that statement is supplied, for the elementary subgroups, by the
`p`-elementary subgroups with coefficients in `ℤ[ζ]`, `ζ` a primitive `|G|`-th root of unity; this
declaration does not prove it.

TauCeti.ClassFunction.indVirtualCharacte.doc:
**An induction theorem is a single membership.**  The virtual characters induced from a family
of subgroups exhaust `R(G)` exactly when the constant function `1`, the character of the trivial
representation, is one of them.

Brauer's induction theorem is this statement for the elementary subgroups, and its whole content is
therefore the membership `1 ∈ V_G`.

TauCeti.ClassFunction.character_mem_indC.doc:
**Brauer's induction theorem, character form.** Every character is an integral combination of
characters induced from irreducible characters of elementary subgroups.

  (u : ↑(L.H F 2)) (h1 : ∀ (H : Subgroup L.Gal), Subsingleton ↑((L.subgroupLayer H).H F 1))
  (hcard : ∀ (H : Subgroup L.Gal), Nat.card ↑((L.subgroupLayer H).H F 2) = Nat.card ↥H)
  (hgen :

**Tate's theorem** (J. Tate, *The higher dimensional cohomology groups of class field theory*,
Ann. of Math. 56 (1952); Artin–Tate, Chapter XIV §4), with its hypotheses stated one by one over
the finite quotient system `H ↦ L.subgroupLayer H`:

* `h1`: `H¹(H, A^V) = 0` for every subgroup `H ≤ U/V`;
* `hcard`: `H²(H, A^V)` has exactly `#H` elements;
* `hgen`: the restriction of `u` to the layer of `H` generates that layer's `H²`.

degree `r`; its underlying homomorphism is `cupClass F L u r` (`tateTheorem_toAddMonoidHom`).

field `ℚ(ζ_n)`.

an element `a ∈ Kˣ` lies in `N_{L/K}(Lˣ)` exactly when, at every finite place `v` and every

it is the invariant `TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.unramifiedInv K E` of the layer
(`invMap_relBrInfl`).

finite and infinite places of the number field `K` sum to zero.

**The global invariant is injective**, because the idele-class `H¹` vanishes and the sum of
the local invariants vanishes only on the classes that die in the idele classes.

`Kˢ`: the invariant of a class is the sum of the local invariants of a lift to the ideles of its
inflation to some refinement of the layer. By `globalInv_eq` it does not depend on the refinement
or on the lift, and `globalInv_unique` characterizes it by the equations `globalInv_ideleToClassH2`
and `globalInv_infl`.

invariant on a layer is the global invariant (`globalClassFormation_inv`).

      Subsingleton
        ↑((TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.NormalLayer.ofOpenNormal V).H
            (TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalFormation K) 1)) :
  Function.Injective ⇑(TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.brLocalization K)
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.brLocalization_.doc:
**The Hasse principle from the vanishing of `H¹` on the idele-class formation**: if `H¹`
vanishes on every layer `V ◁ G_K` of `globalFormation K`, then a Brauer class of `K` whose
localizations all vanish is zero: `Br K → ⨁_v Br K_v` is injective.

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.brLocalization_.signature:
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.brLocalization_injective_of_subsingleton_groupCohomology_one (K : Type)
  [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (h :
    ∀ (L : Type) [inst : Field L] [inst_1 : NumberField L] [inst_2 : Algebra K L] [IsGalois K L],
      Subsingleton ↑(groupCohomology (TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ideleClassRep K L) 1)) :
  Function.Injective ⇑(TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.brLocalization K)
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.brLocalization_.doc:
**The Hasse principle for Brauer classes, from idele-class `H¹`.** If `H¹(Gal(L/K), C_L)`
vanishes for every finite Galois extension `L/K`, then a Brauer class of `K` whose localizations
at all places vanish is zero: `Br K → ⨁_v Br K_v` is injective.

**The Hasse principle for the Brauer group** (Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether). A Brauer class of
the number field `K` whose localizations at all places vanish is zero: `Br K → ⨁_v Br K_v` is
injective.

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation..doc:
**Tate's isomorphism of a class formation commutes with conjugation**: conjugating
`x ∪ u_{U/V}` by `g` gives the cup product of the conjugate of `x` with the fundamental class of
the conjugate layer.

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation..signature:
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation.tateIso {G : Type} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation..doc:
**Tate's theorem for a class formation**, in every integer degree: the generic theorem applied
to the fundamental class, with the three hypotheses discharged by the three individually named
consequences of the axioms. This is Artin–Tate's Main Theorem (Chapter XIV §4, Theorem 1).

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation..signature:
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation.groundInclusion_mem_normSubgroup_of_range_eq_commutator
  {G : Type} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G]
  [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G] {F : TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.Formation G}
  (cf : TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation F)
  {small big : TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.NormalLayer G}
  (T : TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.LayerRestriction small big)
  (hT : T.galHom.range = commutator big.Gal) (a : ↥(F.level big.ground)) :
  (T.groundInclusion F) a ∈ small.normSubgroup F
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation..doc:
**The principal ideal theorem for a class formation.** Let `V ◁ U` be a layer, `K/F` in field
notation, and restrict it to the ground subgroup `U'` whose image `U'/V` is the commutator subgroup
of `U/V`, the layer `K/E` over the maximal abelian subextension `E`. Then every element of the
ground level `A^U` is, in `A^{U'}`, a norm from `A^V`.

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation..signature:
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation.artinEquiv_layerHom {G : Type} [Group G]

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation..doc: **Artin reciprocity is carried along a layer morphism matching the fundamental classes.**

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation..signature:
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation.artinEquiv_conj {G : Type} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation..doc:
**Artin reciprocity commutes with conjugation**: Artin reciprocity of the conjugate layer,
applied to the conjugate of a class modulo norms, is the conjugate of its Artin symbol.

TauCeti.CkHolderSpace.signature:
TauCeti.CkHolderSpace.{u, v} (k : ℕ) (α : NNReal) (E : Type u) (F : Type v) [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] : Type (max u v)
TauCeti.CkHolderSpace.doc:
The space of bounded `C^k` maps whose iterated Fréchet derivatives through order `k` are
bounded and whose `k`-th iterated derivative is globally `α`-Hölder. Its norm is

`∑_{i ≤ k} ‖D^i f‖_∞ + [D^k f]_α`.

TauCeti.CircleSobolev.weight_add_le.signature:
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.weight_add_le (s : ℝ) (m n : ℤ) :
  TauCeti.CircleSobolev.weight s (m + n) ≤
    TauCeti.CircleSobolev.weight |s| m * TauCeti.CircleSobolev.weight s n
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.weight_add_le.doc:
**Peetre's inequality**: `(1 + |m + n|) ^ s ≤ (1 + |m|) ^ |s| (1 + |n|) ^ s` for every real
`s`. Shifting frequencies by `m` therefore changes the weights of every order `s` by at most the
factor `(1 + |m|) ^ |s|`.

TauCeti.CircleSobolev.norm_mul_le.signature:
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.norm_mul_le.{u_4} {s : ℝ} {A : Type u_4} [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra ℂ A]
  [CompleteSpace A] [hs : Fact (1 / 2 < s)] (a b : TauCeti.CircleSobolev s A) :
  ‖a * b‖ ≤ 2 ^ (s + 1) * √(∑' (n : ℤ), TauCeti.CircleSobolev.weight (-(2 * s)) n) * ‖a‖ * ‖b‖

TauCeti.CircleSobolev.mulFourierSeriesEq.signature:
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.mulFourierSeriesEquiv.{u_1} {s : ℝ} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E] {T : ℝ} [Fact (0 < T)] (f : AddCircle T → ℂ)
  (hf : ContDiff ℝ ↑⊤ fun x => f ↑x) (hf₀ : ∀ (x : AddCircle T), f x ≠ 0) :
  TauCeti.CircleSobolev s E ≃L[ℂ] TauCeti.CircleSobolev s E
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.mulFourierSeriesEq.doc:
For a smooth function `f` on the circle that vanishes nowhere, multiplication by `f` as a
continuous linear automorphism of `H^s`, for every real `s`; its inverse is multiplication by
`f⁻¹`.

TauCeti.CircleSobolev.isUnit_iff_forall_.signature:
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.isUnit_iff_forall_ne_zero {s : ℝ} [hs : Fact (1 / 2 < s)] (T : ℝ)
  [Fact (0 < T)] {a : TauCeti.CircleSobolev s ℂ} :
  IsUnit a ↔ ∀ (x : AddCircle T), ((TauCeti.CircleSobolev.toContinuousMap T ⋯) a) x ≠ 0
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.isUnit_iff_forall_.doc:
**Wiener's lemma for `H^s`, `s > 1/2`.** An element of `H^s(ℂ)` is a unit if and only if its
continuous representative vanishes nowhere.

TauCeti.CircleSobolev.isUnit_iff_forall_.signature:
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.isUnit_iff_forall_isUnit.{u_1} {s : ℝ} {A : Type u_1} [NormedCommRing A]
  [NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] [hs : Fact (1 / 2 < s)] (T : ℝ) [Fact (0 < T)]
  {a : TauCeti.CircleSobolev s A} :
  IsUnit a ↔ ∀ (x : AddCircle T), IsUnit (((TauCeti.CircleSobolev.toContinuousMap T ⋯) a) x)
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.isUnit_iff_forall_.doc:
**Wiener's lemma for `H^s(A)`, `s > 1/2`.** An element of `H^s(A)` is a unit if and only if
its continuous representative takes invertible values at every point of the circle.

TauCeti.CircleSobolev.isCompactOperator_.doc:
**Rellich's theorem** on the circle: the inclusion `H^s → H^t` is a compact operator for
`t < s` when `E` is finite-dimensional.

TauCeti.CircleSobolev.exists_norm_inclus.signature:
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.exists_norm_inclusion_le.{u_1} {s t : ℝ} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℂ E] {r : ℝ} (hrt : r ≤ t) (hts : t < s) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ C,
    0 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (a : TauCeti.CircleSobolev s E),
        ‖(TauCeti.CircleSobolev.inclusion ⋯) a‖ ≤
          ε * ‖a‖ + C * ‖(TauCeti.CircleSobolev.inclusion ⋯) a‖
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.exists_norm_inclus.doc:
**Ehrling's inequality** on the circle: for `r ≤ t < s`, the `H^t` norm is bounded by an
arbitrarily small multiple of the `H^s` norm plus a multiple of the weaker `H^r` norm.

TauCeti.CircleSobolev.exists_analyticAt_.signature:
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.exists_analyticAt_hardyGraph {s : ℝ} [hs : Fact (1 / 2 < s)] :
  ∃ ψ,
    ψ 0 = 0 ∧
      AnalyticAt ℂ ψ 0 ∧
        ∃ W ∈ nhds 0,
          ∀ᶠ (y :
            ℂ ×
              ↥(TauCeti.CircleSobolev.supported s ℂ (Set.Ici 0)) ×
                ↥(TauCeti.CircleSobolev.supported s ℂ (Set.Ici 0))) in
            nhds 0,
            ψ y ∈ W ∧
              ∀ p ∈ W,
                p ∈ TauCeti.CircleSobolev.neckGraph s ℂ y.1 ∧
                    (TauCeti.CircleSobolev.indicator (Set.Ici 0))
                          (TauCeti.CircleSobolev.nemytskii Complex.exp p.1) =
                        1 + ↑y.2.1 ∧
                      (TauCeti.CircleSobolev.indicator (Set.Ici 0))
                          (TauCeti.CircleSobolev.nemytskii Complex.exp p.2) =
                        1 + ↑y.2.2 ↔
                  p = ψ y
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.exists_analyticAt_.doc:
**The nonlinear Hardy graph theorem at a plumbing node.** For `s > 1/2` there are a
neighbourhood `W` of `0` in `H^s × H^s` and a map `ψ`, analytic at the origin with `ψ 0 = 0`, such
that for all data `y = (a, p, q)` near `0`, with `p` and `q` of nonnegative frequencies, `ψ y` is
the unique `(F, G) ∈ W` with

* `(F, G)` in the neck graph of the plumbing `xy = a`, and
* nonnegative parts of `e^F` and `e^G` equal to `1 + p` and `1 + q`.

In terms of the boundary maps `ξ = x e^F` and `η = y e^G`, the conditions say that `(ξ, η)` solves
the node equation `ξ(x) η(a / x) = b` with `b = a e^{F₀ + G₀}`
(`CircleSobolev.mul_exp_mul_mul_exp_eq_of_mem_neckGraph`), and that the positive Fourier
coefficients of `ξ` and `η` are those of `x (1 + p)` and `y (1 + q)`. So the solution, its
nonpositive coefficients and `b` depend holomorphically on `a` and on these positive coefficients,
also at the node `a = 0`.

TauCeti.CircleSobolev.analyticOnNhd_nemy.signature:
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.analyticOnNhd_nemytskii {s : ℝ} (T : ℝ) [hT : Fact (0 < T)]
  [hs : Fact (1 / 2 < s)] {F : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} (hU : IsOpen U) (hF : DifferentiableOn ℂ F U) :
  AnalyticOnNhd ℂ (TauCeti.CircleSobolev.nemytskii F)
    {u | ∀ (x : AddCircle T), ((TauCeti.CircleSobolev.toContinuousMap T ⋯) u) x ∈ U}
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.analyticOnNhd_nemy.doc:
**The holomorphic Nemytskii map is holomorphic.** If `F` is holomorphic on an open set `U`,
then `u ↦ nemytskii F u` is analytic on the open subset of `H^s`, `s > 1/2`, of elements with
values in `U` (`isOpen_setOf_forall_toContinuousMap_mem`).

TauCeti.ChainComplex.kronecker_bijective.signature:
TauCeti.ChainComplex.kronecker_bijective_succ_of_projective_homology.{v_1, u_1, u_3} {C : Type u_1}
  [CategoryTheory.Category.{v_1, u_1} C] [CategoryTheory.Abelian C] {k : Type u_3} [CommRing k]
  [CategoryTheory.Linear k C] [∀ (V : C), CategoryTheory.HasProjectiveDimensionLE V 1]
  {X : ChainComplex C ℕ} {Y : C} [∀ (n : ℕ), CategoryTheory.Projective (X.X n)] (n : ℕ)
  [CategoryTheory.Projective (HomologicalComplex.homology X n)] :
  Function.Bijective ⇑(TauCeti.ChainComplex.kronecker k X Y (n + 1))
TauCeti.ChainComplex.kronecker_bijective.doc:
**The universal coefficient theorem above a projective homology object**, when every object
has projective dimension at most one, as for modules over a principal ideal domain: for a chain
complex `X` indexed by `ℕ` with projective terms whose homology `Hₙ(X)` is projective, the
Kronecker map `Hⁿ⁺¹(Hom(X, Y)) →ₗ[k] (Hₙ₊₁(X) ⟶ Y)` is bijective, for every object `Y`. Nothing
is assumed about the homology in the other degrees.

TauCeti.ChainComplex.kronecker_bijective.signature:
TauCeti.ChainComplex.kronecker_bijective_of_projective_homology_of_add_one_eq.{v_1, u_1, u_2, u_3}
  {C : Type u_1} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v_1, u_1} C] [CategoryTheory.Abelian C] {α : Type u_2}
  [AddRightCancelSemigroup α] [One α] {k : Type u_3} [CommRing k] [CategoryTheory.Linear k C]
  {X : ChainComplex C α} {Y : C} {i j : α} (hij : j + 1 = i)
  [CategoryTheory.Projective (HomologicalComplex.cycles X j)]
  [CategoryTheory.IsSplitMono (HomologicalComplex.iCycles X j)]
  [CategoryTheory.IsSplitMono (HomologicalComplex.iCycles X i)]
  [CategoryTheory.Projective (HomologicalComplex.homology X j)] :
  Function.Bijective ⇑(TauCeti.ChainComplex.kronecker k X Y i)
TauCeti.ChainComplex.kronecker_bijective.doc:
**The universal coefficient theorem in one degree with projective homology below it**: in
degree `i = j + 1`, if the cycles `Zⱼ` are projective, the inclusions `Zⱼ ⟶ Xⱼ` and `Zᵢ ⟶ Xᵢ`
are split, and `Hⱼ(X)` is projective, then the Kronecker map `Hⁱ(Hom(X, Y)) →ₗ[k] (Hᵢ(X) ⟶ Y)` is
bijective, for every object `Y`: the `Ext¹(Hⱼ(X), Y)` term of the universal coefficient sequence
vanishes.

**The universal coefficient theorem below the first non-projective homology**: for a chain
complex `X` indexed by `ℕ` with projective terms whose homology objects are projective below
degree `n`, the Kronecker map `Hⁿ(Hom(X, Y)) →ₗ[k] (Hₙ(X) ⟶ Y)` is bijective, for every object
`Y`. In particular this holds when `X` is exact below degree `n`.

**The universal coefficient theorem with projective homology**: for a chain complex `X`
indexed by `ℕ` whose terms and homology objects are all projective, the Kronecker map
`Hⁿ(Hom(X, Y)) →ₗ[k] (Hₙ(X) ⟶ Y)` is bijective in every degree, for every object `Y`.

**The universal coefficient theorem for injective coefficients**: for an injective object `Y`,
the Kronecker map `Hⁱ(Hom(X, Y)) →ₗ[k] (Hᵢ(X) ⟶ Y)` is bijective.

TauCeti.CayleyDickson.mul_assoc_of_mem_a.signature:
TauCeti.CayleyDickson.mul_assoc_of_mem_adjoin.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R]
  {x y a b c : TauCeti.CayleyDickson (Quaternion R)} (ha : a ∈ NonUnitalAlgebra.adjoin R {1, x, y})
  (hb : b ∈ NonUnitalAlgebra.adjoin R {1, x, y}) (hc : c ∈ NonUnitalAlgebra.adjoin R {1, x, y}) :
  a * b * c = a * (b * c)
TauCeti.CayleyDickson.mul_assoc_of_mem_a.doc:
**Artin's theorem** for the double of the quaternions: the subalgebra generated by two elements
`x` and `y` is associative.

TauCeti.CayleyDickson.moufang_right.signature:
TauCeti.CayleyDickson.moufang_right.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R]
  (x y z : TauCeti.CayleyDickson (Quaternion R)) : x * (z * y * z) = x * z * y * z
TauCeti.CayleyDickson.moufang_right.doc: **The right Moufang identity**: `x * (z * y * z) = ((x * z) * y) * z`.

TauCeti.CayleyDickson.moufang_middle.signature:
TauCeti.CayleyDickson.moufang_middle.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R]
  (x y z : TauCeti.CayleyDickson (Quaternion R)) : z * x * (y * z) = z * (x * y) * z
TauCeti.CayleyDickson.moufang_middle.doc: **The middle Moufang identity**: `(z * x) * (y * z) = (z * (x * y)) * z`.

TauCeti.CayleyDickson.moufang_left.signature:
TauCeti.CayleyDickson.moufang_left.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R]
  (x y z : TauCeti.CayleyDickson (Quaternion R)) : z * x * z * y = z * (x * (z * y))
TauCeti.CayleyDickson.moufang_left.doc: **The left Moufang identity**: `(z * x * z) * y = z * (x * (z * y))`.

TauCeti.CStarAction.isKMSState_iff_of_de.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.isKMSState_iff_of_dense.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A]
  {α : TauCeti.CStarAction (Multiplicative ℝ) A} {β : ℝ} [PartialOrder A] [StarOrderedRing A]
  {ω : A →P[ℂ] ℂ} {s : Set A} (hs : Dense s) (hinv : IsInvariant (fun t a => (α t) a) s)
  (hentire : ∀ b ∈ s, α.IsEntireAnalytic b) :
  α.IsKMSState β ω ↔
    ‖ω.toContinuousLinearMap‖ = 1 ∧
      ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s, ω (a * α.entireExtension b (↑β * Complex.I)) = ω (b * a)
TauCeti.CStarAction.isKMSState_iff_of_de.doc:
**Dense analytic KMS criterion.** A state is β-KMS if and only if the analytic KMS
identity holds for pairs in a norm-dense invariant set of entire analytic elements.
In particular, the set can be a norm-dense invariant star subalgebra.

TauCeti.CStarAction.isCompact_kmsStates.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.isCompact_kmsStates.{u_2} {B : Type u_2} [CStarAlgebra B] [PartialOrder B]
  [StarOrderedRing B] {α : TauCeti.CStarAction (Multiplicative ℝ) B} {β : ℝ} :
  IsCompact (α.kmsStates β)
TauCeti.CStarAction.isCompact_kmsStates.doc: **Weak-* compactness of `K_β`.** For unital `B`, the set of β-KMS states is weak-* compact.

TauCeti.CStarAction.entireAnalytic.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.entireAnalytic.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A]
  (α : TauCeti.CStarAction (Multiplicative ℝ) A) : NonUnitalStarSubalgebra ℂ A
TauCeti.CStarAction.entireAnalytic.doc: The entire analytic elements of a real action, as a nonunital star subalgebra.

TauCeti.CStarAction.dense_entireAnalytic.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.dense_entireAnalytic.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A]
  (α : TauCeti.CStarAction (Multiplicative ℝ) A) : Dense ↑α.entireAnalytic
TauCeti.CStarAction.dense_entireAnalytic.doc:
**Density of entire analytic elements.** The entire analytic elements of a point-norm
continuous real action are dense, since every element is a limit of its Gaussian smearings.

TauCeti.CStarAction.convex_kmsStates.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.convex_kmsStates.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A] [PartialOrder A]
  [StarOrderedRing A] {α : TauCeti.CStarAction (Multiplicative ℝ) A} {β : ℝ} :
  Convex ℝ (α.kmsStates β)
TauCeti.CStarAction.convex_kmsStates.doc: **Convexity of `K_β`.** Convex combinations of β-KMS states are β-KMS states.

TauCeti.CStarAction.IsKMSState.of_tendst.doc:
**Pointwise limits of KMS states.** If β-KMS states converge pointwise to a positive
functional of norm one, then the limit is a β-KMS state.

TauCeti.CStarAction.IsKMSState.apply_act.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.IsKMSState.apply_action.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A]
  {α : TauCeti.CStarAction (Multiplicative ℝ) A} {β : ℝ} [PartialOrder A] [StarOrderedRing A]
  {ω : A →P[ℂ] ℂ} (hω : α.IsKMSState β ω) (hβ : β ≠ 0) (t : Multiplicative ℝ) (a : A) :
  ω ((α t) a) = ω a
TauCeti.CStarAction.IsKMSState.apply_act.doc:
**KMS states are invariant.** For `β ≠ 0`, every β-KMS state `ω` is invariant under the
dynamics: `ω (α_t(a)) = ω a`. At `β = 0` the KMS states are the tracial states, which need not
be invariant.

TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentat.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentation.regular.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {G : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2}
  {H : Type u_3} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A] [NormedAddCommGroup H]

TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentat.doc:
The regular covariant representation on `L²(G, H)` induced by a representation `ρ` of `A` on
`H`: `a` acts by `ξ ↦ (r ↦ ρ (α_{r⁻¹}(a)) (ξ r))` and `s` by left translation
`ξ ↦ (r ↦ ξ (s⁻¹ r))`.

TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentat.doc: The integrated form is bounded by the coefficient function's L¹ norm.

TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentation.integratedOperator_convolution.{u_1, u_2, u_3}

TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentat.doc:
The integrated form of a covariant pair is multiplicative for twisted convolution with respect
to a left-invariant measure: `(π ⋊ U) (f ⋆ g) = (π ⋊ U) f * (π ⋊ U) g`.

TauCeti.CStarAction.ConvolutionAlgebra.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.ConvolutionAlgebra.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} [Group G]
  [TopologicalSpace G] [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A] [MeasurableSpace G] (α : TauCeti.CStarAction G A)

TauCeti.CStarAction.ConvolutionAlgebra.doc:
The convolution ⋆-algebra of the C⋆-dynamical system `(A, G, α)` with respect to `μ`: the
compactly supported continuous functions `G → A`, with twisted convolution as product and the
twisted involution as star. Use `ConvolutionAlgebra.toConv` and `ConvolutionAlgebra.ofConv` to
pass to and from `C_c(G, A)`, whose own product and star are pointwise.

TauCeti.BoundedHolomorphicFunctions.rest.signature:
TauCeti.BoundedHolomorphicFunctions.restrict_injective.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℂ V] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]
  {U U' : TopologicalSpace.Opens V} [FiniteDimensional ℂ V] [CompleteSpace E] (h : U' ≤ U)

  Function.Injective ⇑(TauCeti.BoundedHolomorphicFunctions.restrict h)
TauCeti.BoundedHolomorphicFunctions.rest.doc:
**Identity theorem.** If `V` is finite-dimensional, `E` is complete, and every connected
component of `U` meets `U'`, then restriction `H^∞(U, E) → H^∞(U', E)` is injective.

TauCeti.BoundedHolomorphicFunctions.isCo.signature:
TauCeti.BoundedHolomorphicFunctions.isCompactOperator_restrict.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1}
  {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℂ V] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]
  {U U' : TopologicalSpace.Opens V} [ProperSpace E] {K : Set V} (hK : IsCompact K) (hU'K : ↑U' ⊆ K)
  (hKU : K ⊆ ↑U) : IsCompactOperator ⇑(TauCeti.BoundedHolomorphicFunctions.restrict ⋯)
TauCeti.BoundedHolomorphicFunctions.isCo.doc:
**Montel's theorem for bounded holomorphic maps.** If `U'` lies in a compact subset `K` of
`U` and `E` is proper, restriction `H^∞(U, E) → H^∞(U', E)` is a compact operator.

TauCeti.BoundedHolomorphicFunctions.dist.doc:
**Cauchy estimate.** On a ball of radius `R` inside `U`, a bounded holomorphic map `f` is
Lipschitz at the centre with constant `2 * ‖f‖ / R`.

TauCeti.BoundedFlow.exists_val_eq_cutBou.signature:
TauCeti.BoundedFlow.exists_val_eq_cutBound.{u, v, w} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v} {K : Type w}
  [Fintype V] [(v w : V) → Fintype (Q v w)] [AddCommGroup K] [LinearOrder K] [IsOrderedAddMonoid K]
  {lo hi : TauCeti.Assignment Q K} {s t : V} [DecidableEq V] (hst : s ≠ t)
  (f : TauCeti.BoundedFlow lo hi s t) : ∃ g S, s ∈ S ∧ t ∉ S ∧ g.val = TauCeti.cutBound lo hi S
TauCeti.BoundedFlow.exists_val_eq_cutBou.doc:
**Max-flow/min-cut theorem for bounded assignments.** If some bounded `s`–`t` assignment
between distinct terminals exists, then some bounded `s`–`t` assignment has value equal to the cut
bound of some vertex set containing `s` but not `t`. By weak duality
(`TauCeti.BoundedFlow.val_le_cutBound`) this assignment is maximum and this cut bound is
minimum.

TauCeti.BoundedFlow.IsMaximum.minimizers.doc:
**The poset of minimum cuts.** For a maximum bounded `s`–`t` assignment `f` between distinct
terminals, the minimum cuts, ordered by inclusion, are order isomorphic to the upper sets of the
poset of free residual components, ordered by inclusion. A minimum cut corresponds to the free
components contained in it, and an upper set to the vertices of its components together with the
vertices forced onto the source side.

TauCeti.BlackScholes.riskNeutralPrice_pu.signature:
TauCeti.BlackScholes.riskNeutralPrice_put {s r σ K τ : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hσ : 0 < σ) (hK : 0 < K)
  (hτ : 0 < τ) :
  TauCeti.BlackScholes.riskNeutralPrice (fun x => (K - x)⁺) s r σ τ =
    TauCeti.BlackScholes.putPrice s r σ K τ
TauCeti.BlackScholes.riskNeutralPrice_pu.doc:
**The Black–Scholes put formula.** The discounted risk-neutral expectation of the put payoff
`(K - S_τ)⁺` is `K e^{-rτ} Φ(-d₋) - s Φ(-d₊)`.

TauCeti.BlackScholes.riskNeutralPrice_ca.signature:
TauCeti.BlackScholes.riskNeutralPrice_call {s r σ K τ : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hσ : 0 < σ) (hK : 0 < K)
  (hτ : 0 < τ) :
  TauCeti.BlackScholes.riskNeutralPrice (fun x => (x - K)⁺) s r σ τ =
    TauCeti.BlackScholes.callPrice s r σ K τ
TauCeti.BlackScholes.riskNeutralPrice_ca.doc:
**The Black–Scholes call formula.** The discounted risk-neutral expectation of the call payoff
`(S_τ - K)⁺` is `s Φ(d₊) - K e^{-rτ} Φ(d₋)`.

TauCeti.BlackScholes.riskNeutralPrice.signature: TauCeti.BlackScholes.riskNeutralPrice (h : ℝ → ℝ) (s r σ τ : ℝ) : ℝ
TauCeti.BlackScholes.riskNeutralPrice.doc:
The discounted risk-neutral expectation `exp (-r τ) * E[h (S_τ)]` of a payoff `h` of the
terminal spot `S_τ = terminalSpot s r σ τ Z`, `Z ∼ N(0, 1)`. For a non-integrable payoff the
Bochner integral, and hence this value, is zero.

TauCeti.BlackScholes.putPrice_pde.signature:
TauCeti.BlackScholes.putPrice_pde {s r σ K : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hK : 0 < K) (hσ : σ ≠ 0) {T t : ℝ}
  (ht : t < T) :
  deriv (fun u => TauCeti.BlackScholes.putPrice s r σ K (T - u)) t +
        σ ^ 2 * s ^ 2 / 2 * deriv (deriv fun x => TauCeti.BlackScholes.putPrice x r σ K (T - t)) s +
      r *
        (s * deriv (fun x => TauCeti.BlackScholes.putPrice x r σ K (T - t)) s -
          TauCeti.BlackScholes.putPrice s r σ K (T - t)) =
    0
TauCeti.BlackScholes.putPrice_pde.doc:
**The Black–Scholes equation for the put.** In calendar time `t < T`, the put price
`P(s, t) = putPrice s r σ K (T - t)` satisfies
`∂P/∂t + σ² s² / 2 ∂²P/∂s² + r (s ∂P/∂s - P) = 0` at every spot `s > 0`.

TauCeti.BlackScholes.mul_gaussianPDFReal.signature:
TauCeti.BlackScholes.mul_gaussianPDFReal_dPlus {s r σ K τ : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hK : 0 < K)
  (hσ : σ ≠ 0) (hτ : 0 < τ) :
  s * ProbabilityTheory.gaussianPDFReal 0 1 (TauCeti.BlackScholes.dPlus s r σ K τ) =
    K * Real.exp (-r * τ) *
      ProbabilityTheory.gaussianPDFReal 0 1 (TauCeti.BlackScholes.dMinus s r σ K τ)
TauCeti.BlackScholes.mul_gaussianPDFReal.doc:
The Black–Scholes density identity `s φ(d₊) = K e^{-rτ} φ(d₋)`, where `φ` is the standard
Gaussian density. It expresses that `d₊² - d₋² = 2 (log (s / K) + r τ)`.

TauCeti.BlackScholes.deriv_callPrice_spo.signature:
TauCeti.BlackScholes.deriv_callPrice_spot_mem_Ioo {s r σ K τ : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hK : 0 < K)
  (hσ : σ ≠ 0) (hτ : 0 < τ) :
  deriv (fun x => TauCeti.BlackScholes.callPrice x r σ K τ) s ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1
TauCeti.BlackScholes.deriv_callPrice_spo.doc: The call delta lies strictly between `0` and `1`.

TauCeti.BlackScholes.callPrice_sub_putPr.signature:
TauCeti.BlackScholes.callPrice_sub_putPrice (s r σ K τ : ℝ) :
  TauCeti.BlackScholes.callPrice s r σ K τ - TauCeti.BlackScholes.putPrice s r σ K τ =
    s - K * Real.exp (-r * τ)
TauCeti.BlackScholes.callPrice_sub_putPr.doc: **Put–call parity** for the closed-form prices: `C - P = s - K e^{-rτ}`.

TauCeti.BlackScholes.callPrice_pde.signature:
TauCeti.BlackScholes.callPrice_pde {s r σ K : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hK : 0 < K) (hσ : σ ≠ 0) {T t : ℝ}
  (ht : t < T) :
  deriv (fun u => TauCeti.BlackScholes.callPrice s r σ K (T - u)) t +
        σ ^ 2 * s ^ 2 / 2 *
          deriv (deriv fun x => TauCeti.BlackScholes.callPrice x r σ K (T - t)) s +
      r *
        (s * deriv (fun x => TauCeti.BlackScholes.callPrice x r σ K (T - t)) s -
          TauCeti.BlackScholes.callPrice s r σ K (T - t)) =
    0
TauCeti.BlackScholes.callPrice_pde.doc:
**The Black–Scholes equation for the call.** In calendar time `t < T`, the call price
`C(s, t) = callPrice s r σ K (T - t)` satisfies
`∂C/∂t + σ² s² / 2 ∂²C/∂s² + r (s ∂C/∂s - C) = 0` at every spot `s > 0`.

TauCeti.BinaryQuadraticForm.posDefProper.doc:
**Distinct proper classes of primitive positive definite forms have distinct Picard classes.**
This is the injective half of the correspondence between proper classes of primitive positive
definite forms of discriminant `-n` and the Picard group of the order of discriminant `-n`.

**The Picard class of a proper class of primitive positive definite forms**, the class of
`aℤ + ((-b + √(-n))/2)ℤ` in the Picard group of the quadratic order of discriminant `-n`.

TauCeti.BinaryGolay.weightEnumerator_cod.signature:
TauCeti.BinaryGolay.weightEnumerator_code :
  (↑TauCeti.BinaryGolay.code).weightEnumerator =
    MvPolynomial.X 0 ^ 24 + 759 * MvPolynomial.X 0 ^ 16 * MvPolynomial.X 1 ^ 8 +
          2576 * MvPolynomial.X 0 ^ 12 * MvPolynomial.X 1 ^ 12 +
        759 * MvPolynomial.X 0 ^ 8 * MvPolynomial.X 1 ^ 16 +
      MvPolynomial.X 1 ^ 24
TauCeti.BinaryGolay.weightEnumerator_cod.doc:
The homogeneous weight enumerator is
`X²⁴ + 759 X¹⁶Y⁸ + 2576 X¹²Y¹² + 759 X⁸Y¹⁶ + Y²⁴`.

TauCeti.BinaryGolay.thirtyTwo_le_sum_sq.doc:
**The norm bound for the Leech lattice in congruence coordinates.** Let `m ∈ {0, 1}` and let
`b` be an integer vector reducing to a Golay codeword modulo two, and put `a = 2b + m 𝟙`. If
`∑ aᵢ ≡ 4m (mod 8)` and `a ≠ 0`, then `∑ aᵢ² ≥ 32`. These are the congruence conditions that
describe the Leech lattice in the coordinates `x = a / 2`, in which the halved dot product of `x`
with itself is `∑ aᵢ² / 8`; so the bound says that such an `x` has norm at least `4`.

TauCeti.BinaryGolay.rootLatticeIsometry.doc:
**The Golay root lattice is `A₁²⁴`.** The zero-code lattice generated by all Golay roots
is isometric to the orthogonal sum of twenty-four copies of the existing `A₁` lattice.
The ambient isometry doubles every coordinate.

TauCeti.BinaryGolay.isUnimodular_ofIsotr.doc:
**Gluing `2 ℤ²⁴` along the Golay code gives a unimodular lattice**, because the glue is
Lagrangian.

TauCeti.BinaryGolay.isEven_ofIsotropicSu.doc:
**Gluing `2 ℤ²⁴` along the Golay code gives an even lattice**, because the glue is
quadratic-isotropic.

TauCeti.BinaryCode.IsTypeII.eight_dvd_ca.signature:
TauCeti.BinaryCode.IsTypeII.eight_dvd_card.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι]
  {C : TauCeti.LinearCode (ZMod 2) ι} (hC : TauCeti.BinaryCode.IsTypeII C) : 8 ∣ Fintype.card ι
TauCeti.BinaryCode.IsTypeII.eight_dvd_ca.doc: A Type II binary code has length divisible by eight.

TauCeti.BalancedCategory.signature:
TauCeti.BalancedCategory.{v, u} (C : Type u) [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C]
  [CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory C] [CategoryTheory.BraidedCategory C] : Type (max u v)
TauCeti.BalancedCategory.doc:
A *balanced* structure on a braided monoidal category: a twist `θ : 𝟭 C ≅ 𝟭 C`, a natural
automorphism of the identity functor, satisfying the balancing axiom
`θ_{X ⊗ Y} = (θ_X ⊗ θ_Y) ≫ β_{X,Y} ≫ β_{Y,X}`.

TauCeti.BFEquiv.realize_iff_of_qrank_le.doc:
**Back-and-forth equivalence at level `α` gives agreement up to quantifier rank `α`.** Tuples
that are back-and-forth equivalent at level `α` satisfy the same infinitary formulas of quantifier
rank at most `α`, at every carrier. The rank and the level are compared after lifting them to a
common universe.

TauCeti.BFEquiv.doc:
Ordinal back-and-forth equivalence of tuples. At successors the previous level is retained,
in addition to the forth and back requirements. The language is relational.

TauCeti.AuxTerminalHom.signature:
TauCeti.AuxTerminalHom.{u, v} {V : Type u} (Q : V → V → Type v) (A B : Finset V) :
  V ⊕ Bool → V ⊕ Bool → Type v
TauCeti.AuxTerminalHom.doc:
The arrow family of `Q` with auxiliary terminals for the vertex sets `A` and `B`, on the
vertex type `V ⊕ Bool`. The arrows between original vertices `Sum.inl v` and `Sum.inl w` are those
of `Q v w`; the fresh source `σ = Sum.inr false` has one arrow to each `Sum.inl a` with `a ∈ A`; the
fresh sink `τ = Sum.inr true` has one arrow from each `Sum.inl b` with `b ∈ B`; and there are no
other arrows.

TauCeti.ArtinSchreierMonomial.ramificati.doc:
**The tame different theorem fails at infinity**: the different exponent `d` is at least the
ramification index `e`, so `e ≠ d + 1`, unlike at every tame place.

TauCeti.ArrowWalk.splitEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.ArrowWalk.splitEquiv.{u, v} {V : Type u} (Q : V → V → Type v) (s t : V) (b : Bool) :
  TauCeti.ArrowWalk Q s t ≃ TauCeti.ArrowWalk (TauCeti.SplitHom Q) (s, false) (t, b)
TauCeti.ArrowWalk.splitEquiv.doc:
Lifting identifies the walks from `s` to `t` with the walks in the split network from the
entrance of `s` to the entrance (`b = false`) or exit (`b = true`) of `t`; the inverse is
projection.

TauCeti.AnalyticStage.transition.signature:
TauCeti.AnalyticStage.transition.{u_1, u_2} {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {h : ℕ} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module ℤ_[p] E] [IsBoundedSMul ℤ_[p] E] [IsUltrametricDist E]
  [CompleteSpace E] (S : Type u_2) [Semiring S] [_root_.Module S E] [ContinuousConstSMul S E]
  [SMulCommClass ℤ_[p] S E] : TauCeti.AnalyticStage p h E →L[S] TauCeti.AnalyticStage p (h + 1) E
TauCeti.AnalyticStage.transition.doc:
The transition `LA_h(E) → LA_{h+1}(E)`. The disc of `a ∈ ZMod (pʰ)` is the union of the discs
of the classes `a' = a + pʰ b`, `0 ≤ b < p`, in `ZMod (p ^ (h + 1))`, where `b = ⌊a'.val / pʰ⌋`.
On the disc of `a'` the coordinates are related by `w = b + p v`, and the transition re-expands
`∑ₖ c(a, k) wᵏ` in powers of `v`:

`d(a', j) = ∑ₖ (k choose j) b^(k - j) pʲ • c(a, k)`.

TauCeti.AnalyticStage.norm_amiceMap.signature:
TauCeti.AnalyticStage.norm_amiceMap.{u_1, u_2} {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {h : ℕ}
  {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module ℤ_[p] E] [IsBoundedSMul ℤ_[p] E]
  [IsUltrametricDist E] [CompleteSpace E] (S : Type u_2) [Semiring S] [_root_.Module S E]
  [ContinuousConstSMul S E] [SMulCommClass ℤ_[p] S E] (c : ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap ℕ E) :
  ‖(TauCeti.AnalyticStage.amiceMap p h S) c‖ = ‖c‖
TauCeti.AnalyticStage.norm_amiceMap.doc: **Amice's theorem.** Amice's map preserves norms: `‖∑ₙ e_{h,n} • cₙ‖ = supₙ ‖cₙ‖`.

TauCeti.AnalyticStage.isOrthonormalBasis.signature:
TauCeti.AnalyticStage.isOrthonormalBasis_amiceTerm (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (h : ℕ) :
  TauCeti.IsOrthonormalBasis ℤ_[p] fun n => TauCeti.AnalyticStage.amiceTerm p h n 1
TauCeti.AnalyticStage.isOrthonormalBasis.doc:
**Amice's basis theorem.** The disc expansions `amiceTerm p h n 1` of Amice's polynomials
`e_{h,n}(x) = ⌊n / pʰ⌋! (x choose n)` form an orthonormal basis of `LA_h(ℤ_p)`.

TauCeti.AnalyticStage.amiceMap_surjectiv.signature:
TauCeti.AnalyticStage.amiceMap_surjective.{u_1, u_2} (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (h : ℕ)
  {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module ℤ_[p] E] [IsBoundedSMul ℤ_[p] E]
  [IsUltrametricDist E] [CompleteSpace E] (S : Type u_2) [Semiring S] [_root_.Module S E]
  [ContinuousConstSMul S E] [SMulCommClass ℤ_[p] S E] :
  Function.Surjective ⇑(TauCeti.AnalyticStage.amiceMap p h S)
TauCeti.AnalyticStage.amiceMap_surjectiv.doc:
**Amice's theorem: surjectivity.** Every coefficient vector of `LA_h(E)` is the expansion of
a series `∑ₙ e_{h,n} • cₙ` with `cₙ → 0`.

TauCeti.AnalyticStage.amiceEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.AnalyticStage.amiceEquiv.{u_1, u_2} (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (h : ℕ) {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module ℤ_[p] E] [IsBoundedSMul ℤ_[p] E] [IsUltrametricDist E]
  [CompleteSpace E] (S : Type u_2) [Semiring S] [_root_.Module S E] [ContinuousConstSMul S E]
  [SMulCommClass ℤ_[p] S E] : ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap ℕ E ≃ₗᵢ[S] TauCeti.AnalyticStage p h E
TauCeti.AnalyticStage.amiceEquiv.doc:
**Amice's theorem.** Amice's map `(cₙ) ↦ ∑ₙ e_{h,n} • cₙ`, where
`e_{h,n}(x) = ⌊n / pʰ⌋! (x choose n)`, is an isometric isomorphism from the null sequences in `E`
onto the analytic stage `LA_h(E)`.

TauCeti.AnalyticBelyiPair.nonempty_iso_s.signature:
TauCeti.AnalyticBelyiPair.nonempty_iso_superelliptic_iff {P : TauCeti.AnalyticBelyiPair}
  (ν : ↑(P.restrict ⁻¹' {TauCeti.ThricePuncturedSphere.basePt}) ≃ Fin 4) :
  Nonempty (P.Iso TauCeti.AnalyticBelyiPair.superelliptic) ↔
    TauCeti.PermutationTriple.IsoClass.mk (⋯.monodromyTriple ν) =
      TauCeti.PermutationTriple.IsoClass.mk TauCeti.PermutationTriple.torusTriple
TauCeti.AnalyticBelyiPair.nonempty_iso_s.doc:
**The superelliptic curve is the analytic Belyi pair of the torus triple**: an analytic Belyi
pair is isomorphic to the superelliptic curve exactly when its monodromy triple is isomorphic to
`TauCeti.PermutationTriple.torusTriple`, for any numbering of its fibre over `1/2`.

TauCeti.AnalyticBelyiPair.isoClassEquivC.signature:
TauCeti.AnalyticBelyiPair.isoClassEquivConnectedCoverClass (n : ℕ) :
  Quotient (TauCeti.AnalyticBelyiPair.isoSetoid n) ≃
    TauCeti.ConnectedCoverClass TauCeti.ThricePuncturedSphere.basePt n
TauCeti.AnalyticBelyiPair.isoClassEquivC.doc:
**Analytic Belyi pairs are classified by finite covers of the thrice-punctured sphere.**
Restricting the Belyi map over `ℂ ∖ {0, 1}` and filling the punctures are inverse bijections between
isomorphism classes of analytic Belyi pairs of degree `n` and isomorphism classes of connected
degree-`n` covers of `ℂ ∖ {0, 1}`.

TauCeti.Amenable.of_tendsto.signature:
TauCeti.Amenable.of_tendsto.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
  [IsTopologicalGroup G] {ι : Type u_2} {l : Filter ι} [l.NeBot] {ms : ι → TauCeti.Mean G}
  (h :
    ∀ (g : G) (f : TauCeti.UCB G),
      Filter.Tendsto (fun i => (ms i) ((TauCeti.UCB.leftTranslation g) f) - (ms i) f) l (nhds 0)) :
  TauCeti.Amenable G
TauCeti.Amenable.of_tendsto.doc:
Cluster-point criterion: a topological group is amenable when it carries means `ms i` which
are approximately left invariant along a nontrivial filter, that is, `ms i (L_g f) - ms i f → 0`
for every `g` and `f`.

TauCeti.Amenable.of_isColimit.doc:
The apex of a colimit cocone over a filtered diagram of amenable topological groups in `GrpCat`
is amenable, provided the legs of the cocone are continuous.

TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure.spinPolar.signature:
TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure.spinPolarizationData.{u} {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V]
  [_root_.Module ℝ V] (J : TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure V) {Q : QuadraticForm ℝ V}
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] (hQJ : ∀ (v : V), Q (J.toLinearMap v) = Q v)
  (hQ : QuadraticMap.Nondegenerate) : TauCeti.SpinPolarizationData (QuadraticForm.baseChange ℂ Q)
TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure.spinPolar.doc:
**The polarization of a complexified quadratic space by a complex structure.** For a
nondegenerate quadratic form `Q` on a finite-dimensional real vector space and an almost complex
structure `J` preserving `Q`, the `i`- and `-i`-eigenspaces of the complexification of `J` are the
two isotropic summands of a polarization of `Q.baseChange ℂ`, with no orthogonal remainder. Its
pairing field identifies the `-i`-eigenspace with the dual of the `i`-eigenspace through the
polar form.

TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure.isRiemann.doc:
**Every form polarizing the weight-one Hodge structure of `J` is a Riemann form for `J`**, with
no flatness assumption: `J`-invariance of `E_ℝ` says that the Weil operator is an isometry of the
polarization, and positivity of `E_ℝ (J x) x` is positivity of the Hodge form on real vectors.

TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure.isRiemann.signature:
TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure.isRiemannForm_iff_isPolarization.{u, v} {V : Type u} {Vℂ : Type v}
  [AddCommGroup V] [AddCommGroup Vℂ] [_root_.Module ℂ Vℂ] {ιℂ : V →ₗ[ℤ] Vℂ} [Module.Flat ℤ V]
  (J : TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure (TauCeti.Hodge.Realification V)) (hℂ : IsBaseChange ℂ ιℂ)
  (E : LinearMap.BilinForm ℤ V) :
  J.IsRiemannForm E ↔ TauCeti.Hodge.IsPolarization hℂ (J.latticeHodgeStructure hℂ) E
TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure.isRiemann.doc:
**When `V` is flat over `ℤ`, the Riemann forms for `J` are exactly the forms polarizing its
weight-one Hodge structure.** Flatness is used only in the forward direction, for nondegeneracy.

TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure.fockActio.signature:
TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure.fockAction_ι_one_tmul.{u} {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V]
  [_root_.Module ℝ V] (J : TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure V) {Q : QuadraticForm ℝ V}
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] (hQJ : ∀ (v : V), Q (J.toLinearMap v) = Q v)
  (hQ : QuadraticMap.Nondegenerate) (v : V) :
  (J.fockAction hQJ hQ) ((CliffordAlgebra.ι (QuadraticForm.baseChange ℂ Q)) (1 ⊗ₜ[ℝ] v)) =
    ↑√2 •
      ((J.spinPolarizationData hQJ hQ).wedge ⟨J.holomorphicPart v, ⋯⟩ +
        2⁻¹ • (J.spinPolarizationData hQJ hQ).contract ⟨J.antiholomorphicPart v, ⋯⟩)
TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure.fockActio.doc:
**The normalized Fock action of a real vector**: `c(v)` is `√2` times exterior multiplication
by `v^(1,0)` plus `√2 / 2` times contraction against
`QuadraticMap.polar (Q.baseChange ℂ) · v^(0,1)`. In the geometric convention `Q (v) = -g (v, v)`
that contraction is `-2 ι(v^(0,1))` for the contraction `ι` against `g_ℂ`, so this is
`c(v) = √2 (ε(v^(1,0)) - ι(v^(0,1)))`.

TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure.degreeSca.signature:
TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure.degreeScaling_comp_spinAction_eq_fockAction_comp.{u} {V : Type u}
  [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module ℝ V] (J : TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure V)
  {Q : QuadraticForm ℝ V} [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] (hQJ : ∀ (v : V), Q (J.toLinearMap v) = Q v)
  (hQ : QuadraticMap.Nondegenerate) {r : ℂˣ} (hr : ↑r = ↑√2)
  (a : CliffordAlgebra (QuadraticForm.baseChange ℂ Q)) :
  (TauCeti.ExteriorAlgebra.degreeScaling r).toLinearMap ∘ₗ
      (TauCeti.spinAction (QuadraticForm.baseChange ℂ Q) (J.spinPolarizationData hQJ hQ)) a =
    (J.fockAction hQJ hQ) a ∘ₗ (TauCeti.ExteriorAlgebra.degreeScaling r).toLinearMap
TauCeti.AlmostComplexStructure.degreeSca.doc:
**The degree scaling by `√2` intertwines the native and the normalized Fock actions**:
`T ∘ spinAction a = fockAction a ∘ T`, where `T` multiplies `⋀^p W` by `√2 ^ p`
(`TauCeti.ExteriorAlgebra.degreeScaling_of_mem_exteriorPower`).

TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture.exis.signature:
TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture.exists_sq_le_mul_radical_rpow
  (h : TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ C,
    ∀ (A B : ℤ),
      IsCoprime A B →
        4 ∣ A + 1 →
          32 ∣ B →
            B ≠ 0 →
              ↑(A * B * (A + B)) ^ 2 ≤
                C * ↑(UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical (A * B * (A + B))) ^ (6 + ε)
TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture.exis.doc:
**Szpiro's conjecture for Frey curves.** Under `TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture`, for
every `ε > 0` there is a constant `C` such that `(A B (A + B))² ≤ C rad (A B (A + B)) ^ (6 + ε)`
for all coprime integers `A` and `B` with `A ≡ -1 (mod 4)`, `32 ∣ B` and `B ≠ 0`. The Frey curve
`y² = x (x - A) (x + B)` of such a pair has minimal discriminant `(A B (A + B))² / 2⁸` and
algorithmic conductor `rad (A B (A + B))`.

TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture.exis.signature:
TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture.exists_sq_le (h : TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture) {ε : ℝ}
  (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ C,
    ∀ (A B : ℤ),
      IsCoprime A B →
        A * B * (A + B) ≠ 0 →
          ↑(A * B * (A + B)) ^ 2 ≤
            C * ↑(UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical (A * B * (A + B)).natAbs) ^ (6 + ε)
TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture.exis.doc:
**Szpiro's conjecture for Frey curves.** Under `TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture`, for every
`ε > 0` there is a constant `C` such that `(A B (A + B))² ≤ C rad (A B (A + B)) ^ (6 + ε)` for all
coprime integers `A` and `B` with `A B (A + B) ≠ 0`. This applies Szpiro's conjecture to the curve
of `TauCeti.exists_natAbs_sq_le_absNorm_minimalDiscriminantIdeal`.

TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture.asym.doc:
**Szpiro's conjecture implies asymptotic Fermat.** If `TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture`
holds, there is an `N` such that `aⁿ + bⁿ = cⁿ` has no solution in positive integers for any
exponent `n ≥ N`. The bound `N` depends on the constant of Szpiro's conjecture for `ε = 1`, so it
is ineffective.

TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture.abcC.doc:
**Szpiro's conjecture implies the abc conjecture with exponent `3 / 2`**: under
`TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture`, for every `ε > 0` there is a constant `C` with
`max (|a|, |b|, |c|) ≤ C rad (a b c) ^ (3 / 2 + ε)` for all coprime `a + b = c`. For coprime
positive integers `a + b = c`, Szpiro's bound for Frey curves gives
`(a b c)² ≪_ε rad (a b c) ^ (6 + 4 ε)` (`TauCeti.AlgorithmicSzpiroConjecture.exists_sq_le`), and
`c² ≤ 2 a b c` because `a + b ≤ 2 a b`.

TauCeti.AlgorithmicModifiedSzpiroConject.doc:
**The modified Szpiro conjecture implies Szpiro's conjecture**, with the same constants: the
relation `1728 Δ = c₄³ - c₆²` on the reduced minimal model gives `|Δ_min| ≤ max (|c₄|³, c₆²)`.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.twoChartModel..doc:
**The Riemann–Roch theorem on `X_F` in dimension form**: when `k` is integrally closed in `F`,
`dim_k H⁰(X_F, 𝒪(D)) - dim_k H¹(X_F, 𝒪(D)) = deg D + 1 - g(F)`.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowu.signature:

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowu.doc:
**The blowup of a finitely generated submodule is proper.** If `F` is finite, the structure
morphism `Proj R(J) ⟶ Spec C` is proper.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowu.signature:

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowu.doc:
**The affine charts of the blowup of a submodule.** For a nonempty finite subset `S ⊆ F` with
product `t`, the standard open `D₊(t T^{#S})` of `Proj R(J)` is isomorphic to `Spec C[F/S]`, the
spectrum of the `C`-subalgebra of `B_t` generated by the fractions `f/f'` with `f ∈ F` and
`f' ∈ S`. It is Mathlib's `Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec` followed by the spectrum of
`awayEquivFractionSubalgebra`.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.relativeSpecSy.doc:
**`Spec_X (Sym F)` represents linear functionals.** For a quasicoherent sheaf `F` on `X` and a
scheme `q : T ⟶ X` over `X`, morphisms `T ⟶ Spec_X (Sym F)` over `X` correspond to morphisms of
`𝒪_T`-modules `q^* F ⟶ 𝒪_T`. It is `relativeSpecSymmetricAlgebraHomEquiv` followed by the
adjunction between pullback and pushforward of modules.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.relativeSpecPullbackIso_comp.{u} {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}

        (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.relativeSpecPu.doc:
**Relative Spec commutes with base change, compatibly with composition.** For `g : Z ⟶ Y`
and `f : Y ⟶ X`, the isomorphism `Spec_Z ((g ≫ f)^* A) ≅ Z ×_X Spec_X A` is the composite of the

and the canonical isomorphism `Z ×_Y (Y ×_X Spec_X A) ≅ Z ×_X Spec_X A`.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.relativeSpecEq.doc:
Relative Spec and the algebra of regular functions give an anti-equivalence between
quasi-coherent commutative algebras and affine schemes over an arbitrary base scheme. Its unit
and counit are the canonical section and affine-chart comparisons.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.relativeSpecBa.doc:
**Relative Spec commutes with base change, naturally in the algebra.** For `f : Y ⟶ X`,
taking the relative spectrum of the pullback of a quasicoherent algebra is naturally isomorphic
to base changing its relative spectrum along `f`.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.relativePicard.doc:
The **relative Picard fppf sheaf** of `f : X ⟶ S`, obtained by sheafifying the presheaf
`T ↦ Pic(X_T) / Pic(T)` on the fppf site of schemes over `S`.

This definition does not assert that the resulting sheaf is representable.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.relativePicard.signature:
TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.relativePicardDegreeZeroFunctor.{u} {S X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  (f : X ⟶ S) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f] [AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f]
  [AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyConnected f] :
  CategoryTheory.Functor (CategoryTheory.Over S)ᵒᵖ CommGrpCat
TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.relativePicard.doc:
**The degree-zero Picard functor `Pic⁰_{X/S}`** of a smooth proper geometrically connected
family of curves `f : X ⟶ S`, as a presheaf of commutative groups on schemes over `S`: it sends
`T` to the subgroup `relativePicardDegreeZeroSubgroup f T` of `Pic(X_T) / Pic(T)`, and a morphism
over `S` to the restriction of the pullback map of the relative Picard presheaf.

Over an exact constant field, the dual of `H¹(X, L)` is linearly equivalent to
`H⁰(X, Ω_{X/k} ⊗ L⁻¹)`, by the identification of the differential line bundle with the canonical
bundle. This asserts only the existence of a noncanonical linear equivalence, not a natural
duality pairing.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.isRegular_norm.doc:
**Resolution of curves: regularity of the normalization.** Let `Y` be an integral locally
Noetherian scheme of dimension at most one, and suppose that the normalization of `Y` in its
function field, along `Spec k(Y) ⟶ Y`, is finite over `Y`. Then this normalization is a regular
scheme.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.isModification.doc:
**Resolution of curves: the normalization is a modification.** If the normalization of an
integral scheme `Y` in its function field, along `Spec k(Y) ⟶ Y`, is finite over `Y`, then it is a
modification of `Y`: it is proper, and an isomorphism over a dense open of `Y` with dense preimage.
Stacks, Lemma 33.41.1 (0C45) over a field.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_pullback.signature:
TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_pullbackSymmetricPowerComparison_app.{u}

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_pullback.doc:
**Symmetric powers commute with pullback of quasicoherent sheaves**: for every morphism of
schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` and every quasicoherent `𝒪_Y`-module `M`, the canonical comparison
`f^* (Symⁿ M) ⟶ Symⁿ (f^* M)` is an isomorphism.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.gradedSymmetri.doc:
The graded symmetric algebra functor is an equivalence between quasicoherent sheaves and
graded quasicoherent algebras freely generated in degree one. Its inverse takes the degree-one
component, and its unit is the identification `F ≅ Sym¹ F`.

The graded symmetric algebra functor is left adjoint to the degree-one functor: morphisms of
graded quasicoherent algebras `Sym F ⟶ A` correspond to morphisms of quasicoherent sheaves
`F ⟶ A₁`, by restriction to degree one along `F ≅ Sym¹ F` and by `gradedSymmetricAlgebraLift`.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.gradedRelative.doc:
Graded relative Spec is an anti-equivalence between graded quasicoherent algebras and graded
affine schemes over `X`. The functor sends `A` to the relative spectrum of `⨁ₙ Aₙ`, graded through
the relative-Spec unit `p_* 𝒪 ≅ ⨁ₙ Aₙ`, and the inverse reads off the grading. The unit is the
identity, and the counit is, on underlying schemes, relative Spec of the grading isomorphism
followed by the relative-Spec counit.

every line bundle `L` satisfies

`dim H⁰(X, L) - dim H⁰(X, Ω_{X/k} ⊗ L⁻¹) = deg L + 1 - g`,

where `deg L = χ(L) - χ(𝒪_X)` is the Euler-characteristic degree and `g = dim H¹(X, 𝒪_X)`.

extension.** Let `X` be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus `g ≥ 1` over a
field `k`, with a rational point `x₀`. For every field extension `K / k`, two `K`-points of `X`
with the same class `𝒪(Γₓ - x₀)` in `Pic(X_K) / Pic(Spec K)` are equal. Taking `K`
algebraically closed, the Abel–Jacobi map is injective on geometric points.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.abelJacobiMapT.doc:

`x : T ⟶ X` to the fppf-local class of `𝒪(Γₓ - x₀,T)`.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.doc:
**Algebraic Hartogs principle.** Let `a, b` be a weakly `M`-regular sequence. If `D(a)` and
`D(b)` lie in the open subset `U` of `Spec R`, then `M → M~(U)` is bijective: every section of `M~`
over `U` comes from a unique element of `M`.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.coheigh.doc:
**Krull's principal ideal theorem on a scheme.** A maximal point of the zero locus of a
nonzero global function on an integral locally Noetherian scheme, that is, the generic point of
an irreducible component of that zero locus, has coheight one.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Cartier.doc:
**The Cartier–Picard dictionary.** On any integral scheme, Cartier divisors modulo
principal divisors form the Picard group of line-bundle classes under tensor product.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularProperC.doc:
**The anti-equivalence between regular proper curves and algebraic function fields** over a
field `k`: the function-field functor `X ↦ k(X)` is an equivalence
`RegularProperCurveCat k ≌ (FunctionFieldCat k)ᵒᵖ` with inverse the model functor
`F ↦ twoChartModel F`.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentS.doc:
A quasicoherent sheaf on any scheme has a left dual in `QuasicoherentSheaf X` if and only
if it is finite locally free.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.ModuliProblem..doc:
**`[Γ(N)]` is rigid for `N ≥ 3` where `N` is invertible** (Katz–Mazur, 2.7.2). Over a base `B`
on which `N` is invertible, `[Γ(N)]` is isomorphic to the rigid naive problem `[Γ(N)]_naive`
(`ModuliProblem.isRigid_gammaNaive`).

**The moduli problem `[Γ(N)]` is étale over `Ell/B` when `N` is invertible on `B`**
(Katz–Mazur, 3.7.1): where `N` is invertible on `B`, `[Γ(N)]` is isomorphic to `[Γ(N)]_naive`,
whose representing schemes are étale over their bases. Together with
`ModuliProblem.hasProperty_isFinite_gammaRelRepData`, this makes `[Γ(N)]` finite étale over
`Ell/B`.

**The integral moduli problem `[Γ(N)]` is relatively representable** (Katz–Mazur, 3.6.0).
For an elliptic curve `E/S`, it is represented by the closed Drinfeld-basis locus in
`E[N] ×_S E[N]`.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.ModuliProblem..doc:
For `N ≥ 4` invertible on `B`, the existing fine curve `Y₁(N)` also represents the
integral Drinfeld `[Γ₁(N)]` problem restricted to `B`.

**The moduli problem `[Γ₁(N)]` is relatively representable** (Katz–Mazur, 3.6.0). For an
object `X = (E/S)` of `Ell/B`, the functor `T ↦ [Γ₁(N)](E_T/T)` on schemes over `S` is represented
by the exact-order scheme `E.exactOrderScheme N`, the closed subscheme of `E` of points of exact
order `N`, through `gammaOneBaseChangeEquiv`. No hypothesis is placed on `B`, and `N` need not be
invertible on it.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.ModuliProblem..doc:
**`Y₁(N)` is a fine moduli scheme for `N ≥ 4`.** For `N ≥ 4`, the naive moduli problem
`[Γ₁(N)]` over `Ell/B` is represented by the universal elliptic curve over `Y₁(N)`
(`EllObj.yOne B N`): the naive `[Γ₁(N)]`-structures on an object `X` of `Ell/B` correspond to
the arrows `X ⟶ EllObj.yOne B N`, by pulling back the point `(0, 0)`
(`naiveLevelEquiv_gammaOneNaiveRepresentableBy_homEquiv`).

**Serre duality for line bundles.** The dual of `H¹(X, L)` is linearly isomorphic to
`H⁰(X, ω ⊗ L⁻¹)` for any representative `ω` of the canonical line-bundle class.
The existence statement does not select a canonical pairing.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleShea.doc:
**The Riemann–Roch theorem for line bundles, in Serre-duality form.** For every line bundle
`L` and every representative `ω` of the canonical class,

`dim H⁰(X, L) - dim H⁰(X, ω ⊗ L⁻¹) = deg L + 1 - g`,

where `deg L = χ(L) - χ(𝒪_X)` is the Euler-characteristic degree and `g = dim H¹(X, 𝒪_X)`. No
rational point is needed: it is the integral closedness of `k` in `k(X)` that makes
`H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` one-dimensional.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleShea.doc:
**The Riemann–Roch theorem for a line bundle.** On a proper integral curve over a field `k`
whose codimension-one local rings are discrete valuation rings, with a `k`-rational point and with
`H¹(X, 𝒪_X)` finite-dimensional, a line bundle `L ≅ 𝒪_X(D)` satisfies
`χ(L) = deg D + 1 - g`.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteLocallyF.signature:
TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteLocallyFreeSheaf.pullbackDeterminantIso.{u}

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteLocallyF.doc:
Pulling back the determinant of a finite locally free sheaf of constant rank `r` is naturally
isomorphic to taking the determinant of its pullback: `f^* (det E) ≅ det (f^* E)`. The forward map
is the canonical exterior-power comparison `f^* (⋀ʳ E) ⟶ ⋀ʳ (f^* E)`, which is invertible because
`E` is quasicoherent.

The identity functor on finite locally free sheaves is naturally isomorphic to
internal-Hom dualization applied twice.

The full category of finite locally free sheaves on a scheme, that is, of locally free and
finitely presented `𝒪_X`-modules. Its morphisms are morphisms of `𝒪_X`-modules.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteFlatComm.doc:
**Deligne's theorem.** Let `G` be a finite locally free commutative group scheme over `S`
whose rank is `n` at every point of `S`. Then every point `x : X ⟶ G` over `S` is killed by
`n`: its `n`-th power in the group of `X`-valued points of `G` is the unit.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurveG.doc: **Multiplication by a nonzero integer `n` is an isogeny of degree `n²`.**

**The `n`-torsion of an elliptic curve is étale where `n` is invertible** (Katz–Mazur 2.3.1).
For an elliptic curve `E` over a scheme `S` and an integer `n` invertible in every residue field of
`S`, the `n`-torsion `E[n]` is étale over `S`. It is also finite over `S`
(`EllipticCurveGeom.isFinite_torsion_hom`), so `E[n]` is finite étale over `S`.

  [NeZero N] (hN : ∀ (b : ↥B), ↑N ≠ 0) (h4 : 4 ≤ N) :
  AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.EllObj.yOne B N).structureMap
TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.EllObj.smooth_.doc:
**`Y₁(N)` is smooth over `B`.** For `N ≥ 4` invertible on `B`, the structure morphism of the
fine moduli scheme `Y₁(N)` to `B` is smooth; for example `Y₁(N)` is smooth over `ℤ[1/N]`.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AtWorstNodalOf.doc:
Being at worst nodal of relative dimension one is the affine-local extension of the
scheme-theoretic criterion over spectra.

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.signature:

TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.doc:
A pointed morphism `a : X ⟶ J.toOver` from a scheme `X` over `K` with a `K`-rational point
`x₀` to an abelian variety `J` has the **Albanese property** if every morphism `f : X ⟶ A.toOver`
to an abelian variety sending `x₀` to the identity factors as `f = a ≫ φ` through a unique
homomorphism `φ : J ⟶ A` of abelian varieties.

TauCeti.Algebra.isUnit_discr_localizatio.doc:
The discriminant of a basis of a finite free algebra is a unit at a prime `𝔭` iff the base
change to the localization `A_𝔭` is étale over `A_𝔭`.

TauCeti.Algebra.isFiniteEtaleTorsor_iff.signature:

TauCeti.Algebra.isFiniteEtaleTorsor_iff.doc:
**Chase–Harrison–Rosenberg.** `B` is a finite étale `G`-torsor over `A` if and only if
`A → B` is injective, `A` is the ring of invariants, and the action is free: for each `g ≠ 1` the
elements `g • b - b` generate the unit ideal of `B`.

**Hensel's lemma for the norm.** Let `S` be a finite free algebra over a ring `R` Henselian at
an ideal `I`, containing a unit `w` whose trace is a unit. If a unit `v` of `R` is congruent to the
norm of `a` modulo `I`, then `v` is the norm of some `y` congruent to `a` modulo `IS`.

TauCeti.Algebra.etale_of_isUnramifiedAt_.doc:
A finite flat algebra over a Noetherian local ring of dimension at least two is étale
everywhere if it is unramified at each prime not lying over the closed point. This is the finite
flat case of local purity, with no regularity or normality assumptions.

TauCeti.Algebra.etale_iff_traceForm_nondegenerate.{u_1, u_2} (K : Type u_1) (B : Type u_2) [Field K]

TauCeti.Algebra.etale_iff_traceForm_nond.doc:
A finite-dimensional algebra over a field is étale iff its trace form is nondegenerate. The
fibre case in the proof of Stacks, Lemma 49.3.1 (0BJF).

TauCeti.Algebra.etale_iff_isUnit_discr.doc:
**The discriminant criterion.** A finite free algebra is étale iff the discriminant of a basis
is a unit. Stacks, Lemma 49.3.1 (0BJF), affine form.

TauCeti.Algebra.etale_iff_etale_fiber_of.signature:

TauCeti.Algebra.etale_iff_etale_fiber_of.doc:
A finite free algebra over a Noetherian ring is étale if and only if its fibres over all
primes of height at most one are étale. Minimal primes must be included; no generic étaleness
assumption is imposed.

TauCeti.AlgHom.convPow_finrank_eq_one.doc:
**Deligne's theorem, free case.** Every point of a commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebra
which is free of finite rank `n` over `R` is killed by `n`.

TauCeti.AlgHom.convPow_eq_one_of_rankAtS.doc:
**Deligne's theorem.** Every point of a commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebra which is
finite flat of constant stalk rank `n` over `R` is killed by `n`.

**Newton's formula for the determinant**, without division:
`6 det A = T(A)³ - 3 T(A) T(A ∘ A) + 2 T(A ∘ (A ∘ A))`.

TauCeti.AlbertAlgebra.det_eq_invOf_two_m.doc:
**Newton's formula for the determinant**: when `2` and `3` are invertible,
`det A = (T(A)³ - 3 T(A) T(A ∘ A) + 2 T(A ∘ (A ∘ A))) / 6`.

TauCeti.AdicSpace.mono_of_isClosedImmers.signature:
TauCeti.AdicSpace.mono_of_isClosedImmersion.{u} {X Y : TauCeti.AdicSpace} (f : X ⟶ Y)

TauCeti.AdicSpace.mono_of_isClosedImmers.doc:
**Closed immersions of adic spaces are monomorphisms**: a morphism into an adic space factors
through a closed immersion in at most one way.

TauCeti.AdditiveGroup.exists_ne_zero_coa.signature:

TauCeti.AdditiveGroup.exists_ne_zero_coa.doc:
**Kolchin's theorem for `𝔾ₐ`**: every nonzero vector of a comodule over the coordinate
algebra of the additive group produces a nonzero fixed vector, over an arbitrary base and with no
finiteness hypothesis. The witness is the top nonvanishing divided-power component `Nᵢ v`: by the
binomial composition rule each further component of it is a component of `v` of strictly larger
index, which vanishes by maximality.

TauCeti.AddCircle.denseRange_coe_add_mul.signature:
TauCeti.AddCircle.denseRange_coe_add_mul_iff.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] {p : ℝ} (hp : p ≠ 0)

TauCeti.AddCircle.denseRange_coe_add_mul.doc:
**Kronecker's theorem for linear flows on tori.** A line `t ↦ θ + t ν` in the torus
`(ℝ / pℤ)^ι` is dense exactly when its velocity `ν` is nonresonant: `∑ i, k i * ν i ≠ 0` for every
nonzero integer vector `k`.

TauCeti.AbsolutelySumming.signature:
TauCeti.AbsolutelySumming.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (𝕜 : Type u_1) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] (p : ENNReal)

TauCeti.AbsolutelySumming.doc:
The operator ideal `Πₚ(E, F)` of absolutely `p`-summing operators, normed by the
`p`-summing norm `πₚ`. It is a Banach space when `F` is complete, and its inclusion
`OperatorGauge.Carrier.toContinuousLinearMapL` into the bounded operators is a contraction.

TauCeti.AbelianK0.eulerChar_eq_homologyEulerChar.{w, v, u} {A : Type u}

TauCeti.AbelianK0.eulerChar_eq_homologyE.doc:
**The Euler–Poincaré theorem in abelian `K₀`.** For a cochain complex that is strictly
supported in degrees `a` to `b`, and any finite range of degrees containing `[a, b]`, the
alternating sum of the classes of the terms equals the alternating sum of the classes of the
cohomology objects.

TauCeti.AbelianK0.AdditiveInvariant.sum_.doc:
**The Euler–Poincaré theorem for an additive invariant.** For a cochain complex that is
strictly supported in degrees `a` to `b`, any finite range of degrees containing `[a, b]`, and any
invariant additive on short exact sequences, the alternating sum of the values on the terms equals
the alternating sum of the values on the cohomology objects.

TauCeti.AInfinityRightModule.yonedaHomot.signature:
TauCeti.AInfinityRightModule.yonedaHomotopyEquiv.{u} {R A M : Type u} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup A]

TauCeti.AInfinityRightModule.yonedaHomot.doc:
**The Yoneda lemma for right `A∞` modules.**  Over an `A∞` algebra with a strict unit `e`,
for a module on which `e` is a right unit for the binary operation, evaluation at `e` is a
homotopy equivalence from the morphism complex out of the free module of rank one to the
underlying complex of the module, with homotopy inverse the Yoneda cochains.

TauCeti.AInfinityFunctor.signature:
TauCeti.AInfinityFunctor.{u₁, u₂, v₁, v₂, w} {R : Type w} [CommRing R] {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂}

TauCeti.AInfinityFunctor.doc:
An **`A∞` functor** between nonunital `A∞` categories `ℬ` on `C` and `𝒞` on `D`: a map of
objects `obj : C → D` together with an `A∞` morphism from the total algebra of morphisms of `ℬ` to
that of the induced category `𝒞.induced obj`, whose components send a composable string of `C` to
a morphism between the images of its endpoints and every other string to zero.  Its component of
arity `n` on a composable string `X₀, …, Xₙ` is the functor component
`fₙ : Hom(Xₙ₋₁, Xₙ) ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ Hom(X₀, X₁) ⟶ Hom(obj X₀, obj Xₙ)` of degree `1 - n`.

The **transferred `A∞` category**: the `A∞` structure transferred from the total algebra of
morphisms of `𝒞` along a special contraction onto the total module of morphisms of `D` which is
compatible with the hom modules along a bijection of objects `e : D ≃ C`.  Its differential is the
differential `d_D` of the retract (`homInclusion_homDifferential_transfer`), its composition is
`g ∘ f = p m₂(i g, i f)` (`homInclusion_comp_transfer`), and its higher operations are those of the

suspended degree zero concentrated on the words of length `n - 1`.

degree `q`.

graded algebra, presented as a minimal `A∞` algebra without operations above arity two, and
suppose that `HH^{n, 2 - n}(H, H) = 0` for every `n ≥ 3`: every Hochschild cocycle of `ℋ` of

polynomial algebra is integral.

subspace `V` of `EuclideanSpace ℝ ι` has volume at least `2 ^ finrank ℝ V`, computed in `V`.

of a subspace is its norm closure.

subspaces of `ι → K` of absolute height at most `B`, of all dimensions together.

**Nakayama's lemma with weighted generators.** If `b` spans `M` and `e i • b i ∈ I • M` for

**Stiemke's theorem.** A subspace `S` of `ι → K` contains no nonzero nonnegative vector

and let `A, B ∈ SL(2, ℝ)` lift elements of `Γ`, with `A` hyperbolic: `|tr A| > 2`. Unless `B`
conjugates the class of `A` to itself or to its inverse, that is, unless `B` fixes or exchanges
the two fixed points of `A` on the ideal boundary,

and let `A, B ∈ SL(2, ℝ)` lift elements of `Γ`, with `A` elliptic: `|tr A| < 2`. Unless `B`
commutes with `A` in `PSL(2, ℝ)`, that is, unless `B` fixes the fixed point of `A` in `ℍ`,
`|tr² A - 4| + |tr [A, B] - 2| ≥ 1`.

**Jørgensen's inequality.** Let `Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ)` be a discrete subgroup and let
`A, B ∈ SL(2, ℝ)` lift elements of `Γ`. Unless `B` conjugates the class of `A` to itself or to
its inverse, `|tr² A - 4| + |tr [A, B] - 2| ≥ 1`.

and let `A, B ∈ SL(2, ℝ)` lift elements of `Γ`, with `A` parabolic, so that `tr² A = 4`. Unless `B`

boundary, `|tr [A, B] - 2| ≥ 1`. This is Shimizu's lemma in trace form.

Subgroup.inv_le_abs_apply_one_zero_of_up.doc:
**Shimizu's lemma.** Let `Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ)` be a discrete subgroup containing the translation
`z ↦ z + w` with `w ≠ 0`, and let `A ∈ SL(2, ℝ)` lift an element of `Γ`. If the lower-left entry
of `A` does not vanish, that is, if the element does not fix `∞`, then that entry has absolute
value at least `|w|⁻¹`. Both lifts of the element give the same absolute value.

**Dedekind's modular law**: if the join `H ⊔ N` is the product set `H * N` (for example
when `H` normalizes `N`) and `N ≤ K`, then `(K ⊓ H) ⊔ N = K ⊓ (H ⊔ N)`.

Subgroup.indClassFun_mackey.{u_1, u_2} {k : Type u_1} [Semiring k] {G : Type u_2} [Group G]

finite-index subgroup `H` and an element `x` of a subgroup `K`, the induced class function
`Ind_H^G f` evaluated at `x` is the sum, over the double cosets `K \ G / H`, of the class functions
induced to `K` from the Mackey subgroups.

Subgroup.im_smul_mul_im_le_sq_of_upperRi.signature:
Subgroup.im_smul_mul_im_le_sq_of_upperRightHom_mem

Subgroup.im_smul_mul_im_le_sq_of_upperRi.doc:
**Shimizu's lemma, geometric form.** Let `Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ)` be a discrete subgroup containing
the translation `z ↦ z + w` with `w ≠ 0`. An element of `Γ` that does not fix `∞` moves every
point `z` of the upper half-plane to a point with `(g • z).im * z.im ≤ w ^ 2`; in particular it
cannot keep a point of imaginary part greater than `|w|` that high.

Subgroup.im_smul_mul_im_le_abs_mul_of_up.signature:
Subgroup.im_smul_mul_im_le_abs_mul_of_upperRightHom_mem

Subgroup.im_smul_mul_im_le_abs_mul_of_up.doc:
**Shimizu's lemma for two parabolic fixed points, geometric form.** Let `Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ)` be
a discrete subgroup containing the translation `z ↦ z + w` with `w ≠ 0`, and let
`h ∈ PSL(2, ℝ)` conjugate the translation `z ↦ z + w'`, `w' ≠ 0`, into `Γ`. If `h` does not fix
`∞`, then `(h • z).im * z.im ≤ |w * w'|` for every `z` in the upper half-plane.

Applied to `h = σ g σ'⁻¹`, where `σ` and `σ'` send two cusps of `Γ` to `∞` and `g ∈ Γ`, this
bounds the heights above two cusps simultaneously; for `h ∈ Γ` and `w' = w` it is
`Subgroup.im_smul_mul_im_le_sq_of_upperRightHom_mem`.

Subgroup.exists_sidePairing_relatorQuoti.signature:
Subgroup.exists_sidePairing_relatorQuotientTo_bijective_of_compactSpace
  (Γ : Subgroup (Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) ℝ)) [DiscreteTopology ↥Γ]

Subgroup.exists_sidePairing_relatorQuoti.doc:
**Dirichlet presentations of cocompact Fuchsian groups.** Let `Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ)` be discrete
with compact orbit space, and let `p ∈ ℍ` have trivial stabilizer. The Dirichlet domain of `Γ`
centred at `p` is a compact convex polygon `P` with a side pairing by elements of `Γ`, and `Γ` is
presented by the side-pairing maps, subject to the side relations and the vertex-cycle
relations.

Subgroup.exists_finset_card_le_one_add_i.signature:
Subgroup.exists_finset_card_le_one_add_index_mul.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G)

Subgroup.exists_finset_card_le_one_add_i.doc:
**Schreier's index formula.** If `H` has finite index `n` in a group generated by a finite set
`S` of `d` elements, then `H` is generated by at most `1 + n * (d - 1)` elements. This sharpens
Mathlib's `Subgroup.exists_finset_card_le_mul`, which gives `n * d`.

Subgroup.degree_compactifiedQuotientMap.signature:
Subgroup.degree_compactifiedQuotientMap

Subgroup.degree_compactifiedQuotientMap.doc:
**The degree of a finite-index map of compactified Fuchsian quotients is the index.** For
`Δ ≤ Γ` discrete of finite index, the map `X(Δ) → X(Γ)` induced by the inclusion has degree
`[Γ : Δ]`.

Subgroup.conj_eq_or_conj_eq_inv_of_dist_le

Subgroup.conj_eq_or_conj_eq_inv_of_dist_.doc:
**The Margulis lemma for Fuchsian groups.** Let `Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ)` be a discrete subgroup and let
`g, h ∈ Γ` both move a point `z ∈ ℍ` a distance at most `1 / 4`. If `g` fixes no point of `ℍ`, that
is, if `g` is parabolic or hyperbolic, then `h g h⁻¹ = g` or `h g h⁻¹ = g⁻¹`.

Subgroup.compactSpace_compactifiedQuotie.signature:
Subgroup.compactSpace_compactifiedQuotient_of_isBounded_truncation.{u_1}

**Compactness from a Dirichlet domain with a bounded cusp truncation.** If a discrete
subgroup `Γ` has finitely many cusp orbits, and some Dirichlet domain of `Γ` is bounded after
removing finitely many cusp horodiscs of positive heights, then the quotient `Γ \ ℍ` with its cusp
orbits adjoined is compact.

Subgroup.IsCofinite.isCompact_image_thic.signature:
Subgroup.IsCofinite.isCompact_image_thickPart
