Subgroup.IsCofinite.isCompact_image_thic.doc:
**The thick part of the quotient of a cofinite group is compact.** For a cofinite
`Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ)` and `ε > 0`, the image in `Γ \ ℍ` of the points moved a hyperbolic distance at
least `ε` by every nonidentity element of `Γ` is compact.

Subgroup.IsCofinite.exists_sidePairing_c.signature:
Subgroup.IsCofinite.exists_sidePairing_closure_range_map_eq
  {Γ : Subgroup (Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) ℝ)} (hΓ : Γ.IsCofinite)
  {p : UpperHalfPlane} (hp : p ∈ TauCeti.freeLocus (↥Γ) UpperHalfPlane) :
  ∃ n,
    ∃ (x : NeZero n),
      ∃ P σ,
        P.carrier = TauCeti.dirichletDomain (↥Γ) p ∧

Subgroup.IsCofinite.exists_sidePairing_c.doc:
**The converse of Poincaré's polygon theorem.** Every cofinite `Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ)` arises from
Poincaré's polygon theorem. For a centre `p` with trivial stabilizer, the Dirichlet domain of `Γ`
centred at `p` is the carrier of a convex polygon with finitely many vertices and a side pairing
whose maps generate `Γ`. The cycle transformation of each finite vertex has finite order `m` and
the interior angles along its cycle add up to `2π / m`, and the cycle transformation of each ideal
vertex is parabolic. These are the hypotheses of
`TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane.ConvexPolygon.SidePairing.isCofinite_of_isParabolic`.

Subgroup.FG.inf_of_isFreeGroup.signature:
Subgroup.FG.inf_of_isFreeGroup.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [IsFreeGroup G] {H K : Subgroup G}

Subgroup.FG.inf_of_isFreeGroup.doc:
**Howson's theorem**: in a free group, the intersection of two finitely generated subgroups
is finitely generated.

Subgroup.CompactifiedQuotient.doc:
The compactified quotient of `Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ)`: the coarse orbit space `Γ \ ℍ` with one point
adjoined for each cusp orbit of `Γ`.

Subalgebra.centralizer_centralizer_of_is.signature:
Subalgebra.centralizer_centralizer_of_isSemisimpleModule.{u_3, u_4} {K : Type u_3} [CommRing K]
  {N : Type u_4} [AddCommGroup N] [_root_.Module K N] (A : Subalgebra K (Module.End K N))
  [Module.Finite (Module.End (↥A) N) N] [IsSemisimpleModule (↥A) N] :
  Subalgebra.centralizer K ↑(Subalgebra.centralizer K ↑A) = A
Subalgebra.centralizer_centralizer_of_is.doc:
**The double centralizer theorem inside an endomorphism algebra.** Let `A` be a `K`-subalgebra
of `Module.End K N`, and suppose `N` is semisimple as an `A`-module and finite over
`Module.End A N`. Then `A` is its own double centralizer: an endomorphism commuting with everything
that commutes with `A` already lies in `A`.

The inclusion `A ≤ A''` is formal (`Subalgebra.le_centralizer_centralizer`); the content is the
reverse one, which is Jacobson density. The centralizer `A'` is the ring of `A`-linear
endomorphisms of `N`, so an element of `A''` is an `A'`-linear endomorphism, and density writes
every such endomorphism as the action of an element of `A`.

Finiteness is over `Module.End A N`, the hypothesis density actually needs; a caller with a finite
`K`-module `N` gets it from `Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite`.

StrongDual.norm_sum_apply_comp_single_le.signature:

`κ → E` pairs bidual vectors `z i` of norm at most one with its coordinate functionals
`f ∘ single i` to a value of norm at most one.

StrongDual.exists_pos_norm_sub_ofReal_sm.signature:

StrongDual.exists_norm_lt_and_forall_mem.signature:

StrongDual.exists_norm_lt_and_forall_app.signature:

functionals `f i` on `E` and `ε > 0`, some `x : E` with `‖x‖ < ‖φ‖ + ε` satisfies

StrongDual.bipolar_eq_closedAbsConvexHul.signature:
StrongDual.bipolar_eq_closedAbsConvexHull.{u_1, u_2} (𝕜 : Type u_1) {E : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜]

convex hull of the set together with zero, including when the set is empty.

StarSubalgebra.exists_forall_norm_sub_ap.doc:
**The von Neumann density theorem.** An operator `x` in the double commutant of a unital star
subalgebra `S` of the bounded operators on a Hilbert space is a strong-operator limit of elements
of `S`: for every finite family of vectors `v i` and every `ε > 0` there is `s ∈ S` with
`‖x (v i) - s (v i)‖ < ε` for all `i`.

StarSubalgebra.double_commutant_iff_isCl.signature:
StarSubalgebra.double_commutant_iff_isClosed_image_ofCLM.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2}
  [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (S : StarSubalgebra 𝕜 (H →L[𝕜] H)) :
  (↑S).centralizer.centralizer = ↑S ↔ IsClosed (ContinuousLinearMapWOT.ofCLM '' ↑S)
StarSubalgebra.double_commutant_iff_isCl.doc:
**The bicommutant theorem:** a unital star subalgebra equals its double commutant
if and only if it is weak operator closed.

StarSubalgebra.apply_mem_closure_of_mem_.signature:
StarSubalgebra.apply_mem_closure_of_mem_centralizer_centralizer.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1}
  {H : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (S : StarSubalgebra 𝕜 (H →L[𝕜] H)) {x : H →L[𝕜] H} (hx : x ∈ (↑S).centralizer.centralizer)
  (v : H) : x v ∈ closure ((fun s => s v) '' ↑S)
StarSubalgebra.apply_mem_closure_of_mem_.doc:
**The von Neumann density theorem for one vector.** An operator in the double commutant of a
unital star subalgebra `S` maps each vector `v` into the closure of the orbit `S v`.

StarConvex.extDeriv_poincareHomotopy.signature:
StarConvex.extDeriv_poincareHomotopy.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]

  {ω : E → E [⋀^Fin (n + 1)]→L[ℝ] F} [CompleteSpace F] (hs : StarConvex ℝ x₀ s) (hso : IsOpen s)
  (hω : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ω s) (hclosed : ∀ y ∈ s, extDeriv ω y = 0) {x : E} (hx : x ∈ s) :
  extDeriv (TauCeti.poincareHomotopy x₀ ω) x = ω x
StarConvex.extDeriv_poincareHomotopy.doc:
**The Poincaré lemma.** On an open set star-convex with respect to `x₀`, the Poincaré
homotopy operator with centre `x₀` of a closed `C¹` form is a primitive of it.

StarConvex.exists_invariant_contDiffOn_f.signature:
StarConvex.exists_invariant_contDiffOn_forall_extDeriv_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {E : Type u_1}
  {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
  [CompleteSpace F] {n : ℕ} {x₀ : E} {s : Set E} {ω : E → E [⋀^Fin (n + 1)]→L[ℝ] F} {G : Type u_3}
  [Monoid G] {ρ : ContRepresentation ℝ G E} (hs : StarConvex ℝ x₀ s) (hso : IsOpen s)
  (hρx₀ : ∀ (g : G), (ρ g) x₀ = x₀) (hρs : ∀ (g : G), Set.MapsTo (⇑(ρ g)) s s) {r : ℕ∞} (hr : 1 ≤ r)
  (hωr : ContDiffOn ℝ (↑r) ω s) (hclosed : ∀ y ∈ s, extDeriv ω y = 0)
  (hω : ∀ (g : G), ∀ y ∈ s, (ω ((ρ g) y)).compContinuousLinearMap (ρ g) = ω y) :

        (∀ (g : G), ∀ y ∈ s, (α ((ρ g) y)).compContinuousLinearMap (ρ g) = α y) ∧
          ∀ y ∈ s, extDeriv α y = ω y
StarConvex.exists_invariant_contDiffOn_f.doc:
**The Poincaré lemma for invariant forms.** Let a monoid `G` act on `E` through a continuous
representation `ρ`, fixing `x₀` and preserving an open set `s` star-convex with respect to `x₀`.
A closed `C^r` form of positive degree on `s`, `r ≥ 1`, invariant under every `ρ g` on `s`, is the
exterior derivative on `s` of an invariant `C^r` form vanishing at `x₀`.

StarConvex.exists_contDiffOn_forall_extD.doc:
**The Poincaré lemma.** A closed `C^r` form, `r ≥ 1`, on an open star-convex set is the
exterior derivative of a `C^r` form, which can be chosen to vanish at the centre.

SimpleGraph.walkEquivOfSimpleGraph.signature:
SimpleGraph.walkEquivOfSimpleGraph.{u} {α : Type u} (H : SimpleGraph α) (x y : α) :
  H.Walk x y ≃ (Graph.ofSimpleGraph H).Walk x y
SimpleGraph.walkEquivOfSimpleGraph.doc: Walks in a simple graph are equivalent to edge-labelled walks in its associated `Graph`.

SimpleGraph.vertexConnectivity_le_edgeCo.signature:
SimpleGraph.vertexConnectivity_le_edgeConnectivity.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} :
  G.vertexConnectivity ≤ G.edgeConnectivity
SimpleGraph.vertexConnectivity_le_edgeCo.doc:
**Whitney's inequality**: the vertex connectivity of a simple graph is at most its edge
connectivity.

SimpleGraph.szemeredi_regularity_le.signature:
SimpleGraph.szemeredi_regularity_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
  (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] {ε : ℝ} {P₁ : Finpartition Finset.univ}
  (hP₁ : P₁.IsEquipartition) (hP₇ : 7 ≤ P₁.parts.card) (hPε : 100 ≤ 4 ^ P₁.parts.card * ε ^ 5)
  (hα :
    SzemerediRegularity.stepBound^[⌊4 / ε ^ 5⌋₊] P₁.parts.card *
        16 ^ SzemerediRegularity.stepBound^[⌊4 / ε ^ 5⌋₊] P₁.parts.card ≤
      Fintype.card α) :
  ∃ P ≤ P₁,
    P.IsEquipartition ∧
      P.IsUniform G ε ∧
        P.parts.card ≤ SzemerediRegularity.stepBound^[⌊4 / ε ^ 5⌋₊ + 1] P₁.parts.card
SimpleGraph.szemeredi_regularity_le.doc:
**Szemerédi's regularity lemma below a starting equipartition.** If `P₁` is an equipartition
with at least `7` parts and `100 ≤ 4 ^ #P₁.parts * ε ^ 5`, and the graph is large enough, then
some `ε`-uniform equipartition refines `P₁` and has at most
`stepBound^[⌊4 / ε ^ 5⌋₊ + 1] #P₁.parts` parts.

SimpleGraph.nonempty_stNumbering_of_isVe.signature:
SimpleGraph.nonempty_stNumbering_of_isVertexConnected_two_sup_edge.{u} {V : Type u} [Fintype V]
  {G : SimpleGraph V} {s t : V} (hst : s ≠ t)
  (hG : (G ⊔ SimpleGraph.edge s t).IsVertexConnected 2) : Nonempty (G.STNumbering s t)
SimpleGraph.nonempty_stNumbering_of_isVe.doc:
**Lempel–Even–Cederbaum theorem (existence).** Let `s ≠ t` be distinct vertices of a finite
simple graph `G` such that `G ⊔ SimpleGraph.edge s t` is `2`-vertex-connected. Then `G` admits an
`st`-numbering.

SimpleGraph.nonempty_stNumbering_iff_isV.signature:
SimpleGraph.nonempty_stNumbering_iff_isVertexConnected_two_sup_edge.{u} {V : Type u} [Fintype V]
  {G : SimpleGraph V} (h3 : 3 ≤ Fintype.card V) {s t : V} (hst : s ≠ t) :
  Nonempty (G.STNumbering s t) ↔ (G ⊔ SimpleGraph.edge s t).IsVertexConnected 2
SimpleGraph.nonempty_stNumbering_iff_isV.doc:
**Lempel–Even–Cederbaum theorem.** On a finite vertex type with at least three vertices, a
simple graph `G` admits an `st`-numbering for distinct vertices `s ≠ t` if and only if
`G ⊔ SimpleGraph.edge s t` is `2`-vertex-connected.

SimpleGraph.nonempty_stNumbering_iff_isV.signature:
SimpleGraph.nonempty_stNumbering_iff_isVertexConnected_two.{u} {V : Type u} [Fintype V]
  {G : SimpleGraph V} (h3 : 3 ≤ Fintype.card V) {s t : V} (hst : G.Adj s t) :
  Nonempty (G.STNumbering s t) ↔ G.IsVertexConnected 2
SimpleGraph.nonempty_stNumbering_iff_isV.doc:
**Lempel–Even–Cederbaum theorem for adjacent endpoints.** On a finite vertex type with at least
three vertices, a simple graph `G` with `G.Adj s t` admits an `st`-numbering if and only if `G` is
`2`-vertex-connected.

SimpleGraph.isVertexReachable_iff_exists.signature:
SimpleGraph.isVertexReachable_iff_exists_paths.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} [Finite V]
  {s t : V} (hst : s ≠ t) (hadj : ¬G.Adj s t) (k : ℕ) :
  G.IsVertexReachable (↑k) s t ↔
    ∃ P, (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧ Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)
SimpleGraph.isVertexReachable_iff_exists.doc:
**Menger's theorem for vertex reachability.** Two distinct nonadjacent vertices `s` and `t` of
a simple graph on a finite vertex type are `k`-vertex-reachable exactly when there are `k` paths
from `s` to `t` pairwise sharing no vertex other than `s` and `t`.

SimpleGraph.isVertexConnected_iff_forall.signature:
SimpleGraph.isVertexConnected_iff_forall_exists_paths.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V}
  [Finite V] {k : ℕ} (hk : k < Nat.card V) :
  G.IsVertexConnected ↑k ↔
    ∀ (s t : V),
      s ≠ t →
        ∃ P,
          Function.Injective P ∧
            (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧ Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)
SimpleGraph.isVertexConnected_iff_forall.doc:
**The global form of Menger's theorem.** A simple graph on a finite vertex type with more than
`k` vertices is `k`-vertex-connected exactly when every two distinct vertices `s` and `t`,
adjacent or not, are joined by `k` distinct paths pairwise sharing no vertex other than `s` and
`t`.

SimpleGraph.isEdgeReachable_iff_exists_p.signature:
SimpleGraph.isEdgeReachable_iff_exists_paths.{u} {α : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph α} {s t : α}
  [Finite α] (k : ℕ) :
  G.IsEdgeReachable (↑k) s t ↔
    ∃ P, (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧ Pairwise fun i j => (P i).edges.Disjoint (P j).edges
SimpleGraph.isEdgeReachable_iff_exists_p.doc:
**Menger's theorem for edge-disjoint paths in a simple graph, predicate form.** In a finite
simple graph, `s` and `t` stay reachable after deleting any fewer than `k` edges exactly when there
are `k` `s`–`t` paths, no two of which traverse a common edge.

SimpleGraph.graphonPartitionEnergy_finit.signature:
SimpleGraph.graphonPartitionEnergy_finiteGraphGraphon {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] (G : SimpleGraph (Fin m))
  [DecidableRel G.Adj] (P : Finpartition Finset.univ) :
  TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.graphonPartitionEnergy MeasureTheory.volume P.cellPartition ⋯
      (TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.finiteGraphGraphon G) =
    G.weightedEnergy P
SimpleGraph.graphonPartitionEnergy_finit.doc:
**Finite partition energy is graphon partition energy.** For a graph `G` on `Fin m` with
`0 < m` and a partition `P` of its vertices, the size-weighted energy of `P` is the partition
energy of the graphon of `G` over the partition of the unit interval grouping the vertex cells by
the parts of `P`.

SimpleGraph.g0_dichotomy.signature:
SimpleGraph.g0_dichotomy.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] [PolishSpace X]
  [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (G : SimpleGraph X)
  (hG : MeasureTheory.AnalyticSet {p | G.Adj p.1 p.2}) :
  Xor (∃ c, Measurable ⇑c) (∃ φ, Continuous ⇑φ)
SimpleGraph.g0_dichotomy.doc:
**The Kechris–Solecki–Todorcevic G₀ dichotomy.** A simple graph on a Polish space whose edge
relation is analytic has a measurable coloring by `ℕ`, or receives a continuous homomorphism from
`gZero`, and not both.

SimpleGraph.frieze_kannan.signature:
SimpleGraph.frieze_kannan.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
  [DecidableRel G.Adj] {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ P,
    P.parts.card ≤ 4 ^ ⌈1 / ε ^ 2⌉₊ ∧
      ∀ (A B : Finset V),
        |↑(G.interedges A B).card - G.steppedCount P A B| ≤ ε * ↑(Fintype.card V) ^ 2
SimpleGraph.frieze_kannan.doc:
**Finite Frieze–Kannan weak regularity.** For `ε > 0`, the vertices of `G` have a partition
`P` into at most `4 ^ ⌈1 / ε²⌉` parts such that, for all vertex sets `A` and `B`, the number of
edges from `A` to `B` is within `ε * (card V) ^ 2` of its stepped prediction
`G.steppedCount P A B`.

SimpleGraph.forall_reachable_induce_iff_.signature:
SimpleGraph.forall_reachable_induce_iff_exists_paths.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} {s t : V}
  [Finite V] (hst : s ≠ t) (hadj : ¬G.Adj s t) (k : ℕ) :
  (∀ (X : Finset V) (hs : s ∉ X) (ht : t ∉ X),
      X.card < k → (SimpleGraph.induce (↑X)ᶜ G).Reachable ⟨s, hs⟩ ⟨t, ht⟩) ↔
    ∃ P, (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧ Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)
SimpleGraph.forall_reachable_induce_iff_.doc:
**Menger's theorem for internally vertex-disjoint paths, predicate form.** Let `s` and `t` be
distinct nonadjacent vertices of a simple graph on a finite vertex type. Then `t` stays reachable
from `s` after deleting any fewer than `k` vertices other than `s` and `t` exactly when there are
`k` paths from `s` to `t` pairwise sharing no vertex other than `s` and `t`.

SimpleGraph.forall_exists_walk_iff_exist.signature:
SimpleGraph.forall_exists_walk_iff_exists_paths.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} [Finite V]
  (A B : Finset V) (k : ℕ) :
  (∀ (X : Finset V), X.card < k → ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, ∃ p, ∀ v ∈ p.support, v ∉ X) ↔
    ∃ a b P,
      (∀ (i : Fin k), a i ∈ A) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), b i ∈ B) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
            (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ v ∈ (P i).support, v ≠ a i → v ≠ b i → v ∉ A ∧ v ∉ B) ∧
              Pairwise fun i j => (P i).support.Disjoint (P j).support
SimpleGraph.forall_exists_walk_iff_exist.doc:
**Menger's theorem for vertex-disjoint paths between vertex sets, predicate form.** Let `A` and
`B` be sets of vertices of a simple graph on a finite vertex type. For every set `X` of fewer than
`k` vertices, some walk from a vertex of `A` to a vertex of `B` avoids `X`, exactly when there are
`k` pairwise vertex-disjoint paths, each from a vertex of `A` to a vertex of `B` with its other
vertices in neither `A` nor `B`.

SimpleGraph.forall_exists_walk_iff_exist.signature:
SimpleGraph.forall_exists_walk_iff_exists_fan.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} {x : V}
  {U : Finset V} [Finite V] (hx : x ∉ U) (k : ℕ) :
  (∀ (X : Finset V), X.card < k → x ∉ X → ∃ y ∈ U, ∃ p, ∀ v ∈ p.support, v ∉ X) ↔
    ∃ u P,
      Function.Injective u ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), u i ∈ U) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
            (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ v ∈ (P i).support, v ≠ u i → v ∉ U) ∧
              Pairwise fun i j => ∀ v ∈ (P i).support, v ∈ (P j).support → v = x
SimpleGraph.forall_exists_walk_iff_exist.doc:
**Menger's theorem for fans, predicate form.** Let `x` be a vertex outside a set `U` of vertices
of a simple graph on a finite vertex type. For every set `X` of fewer than `k` vertices other than
`x`, some walk from `x` to a vertex of `U` avoids `X`, exactly when there are `k` paths, the `i`-th
from `x` to `u i ∈ U` with its other vertices outside `U`, any two of which share only the vertex
`x`.

SimpleGraph.forall_exists_reachable_dele.signature:
SimpleGraph.forall_exists_reachable_deleteEdges_iff_exists_paths.{u} {α : Type u}
  {G : SimpleGraph α} [Finite α] {A B : Finset α} (hAB : Disjoint A B) (k : ℕ) :
  (∀ (F : Finset (Sym2 α)), F.card < k → ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, (G.deleteEdges ↑F).Reachable a b) ↔
    ∃ a b P,
      (∀ (i : Fin k), a i ∈ A) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), b i ∈ B) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
            (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ v ∈ (P i).support, v ≠ a i → v ≠ b i → v ∉ A ∧ v ∉ B) ∧
              Pairwise fun i j => (P i).edges.Disjoint (P j).edges
SimpleGraph.forall_exists_reachable_dele.doc:
**Menger's theorem for edge-disjoint paths between vertex sets in a simple graph, predicate
form.** For disjoint finite vertex sets `A` and `B` in a finite simple graph, deleting fewer than
`k` edges always leaves an `A`–`B` connection exactly when there are `k` pairwise edge-disjoint
`A`–`B` paths with no internal terminal vertex.

SimpleGraph.exists_strong_regular.signature:
SimpleGraph.exists_strong_regular.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
  (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (P₀ : Finpartition Finset.univ)
  (hP₀ : P₀.IsEquipartition) {l : ℕ} (hl : l ≤ Fintype.card α) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) {F : ℕ → ℝ}
  (hF : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < F n) :
  ∃ P Q, G.StrongRegular P Q ε F (max l P₀.parts.card) ∧ P.AlmostRefines P₀ ε ∧ l ≤ P.parts.card
SimpleGraph.exists_strong_regular.doc:
**Strong graph regularity.** Let `ε > 0` and let `F : ℕ → ℝ` be a positive schedule. Every
equipartition `P₀` of a finite graph `G` is almost refined, up to `ε`, by the coarse partition `P`
of a strong regularity witness `(P, Q)`, where `P` has at least `l` parts for any requested
`l ≤ card α`, and `Q` has at most `strongGraphRegularityBound ε F (max l #P₀.parts)` parts.

SimpleGraph.exists_regular_exact_refinin.signature:
SimpleGraph.exists_regular_exact_refining_equipartition.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α]
  [DecidableEq α] (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (P : Finpartition Finset.univ)
  (hP : P.IsEquipartition) {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) :
  ∃ Q ≤ P,
    Q.IsEquipartition ∧
      Q.IsUniform G δ ∧ Q.parts.card ≤ TauCeti.nestedRefinementBound δ P.parts.card
SimpleGraph.exists_regular_exact_refinin.doc:
**Szemerédi's regularity lemma refining an equipartition exactly.** Every equipartition `P` of a
finite graph is refined exactly by a `δ`-uniform equipartition with at most
`nestedRefinementBound δ #P.parts` parts.

SimpleGraph.exists_regular_equipartition.signature:
SimpleGraph.exists_regular_equipartition_almost_refining.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α]
  [DecidableEq α] (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] {ε : ℝ} (P₀ : Finpartition Finset.univ)
  (hP₀ : P₀.IsEquipartition) (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ P,
    P.IsEquipartition ∧
      P.IsUniform G ε ∧
        P.AlmostRefines P₀ ε ∧ P.parts.card ≤ TauCeti.refiningRegularityBound ε P₀.parts.card
SimpleGraph.exists_regular_equipartition.doc:
**Szemerédi's regularity lemma relative to a seed.** Every equipartition `P₀` of a finite
graph is almost refined, up to `ε`, by an `ε`-uniform equipartition with at most
`refiningRegularityBound ε #P₀.parts` parts.

SimpleGraph.exists_regular_almostRefines.signature:
SimpleGraph.exists_regular_almostRefines_le_card.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
  (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] {ε : ℝ} (P₀ : Finpartition Finset.univ)
  (hP₀ : P₀.IsEquipartition) {l : ℕ} (hl : l ≤ Fintype.card α) (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ P,
    P.IsEquipartition ∧
      P.IsUniform G ε ∧
        P.AlmostRefines P₀ ε ∧
          l ≤ P.parts.card ∧
            P.parts.card ≤
              TauCeti.nestedRefinementBound ε
                (max (max l P₀.parts.card) ⌈2 * ↑(max l P₀.parts.card) / ε⌉₊)
SimpleGraph.exists_regular_almostRefines.doc:
**Szemerédi's regularity lemma relative to a seed, with a minimum number of parts.** Every
equipartition `P₀` of a finite graph is almost refined, up to `ε`, by an `ε`-uniform equipartition
with at least `l` parts, for any requested `l ≤ card α`. It is obtained by refining exactly an
equipartition into `max l₀ ⌈2 * l₀ / ε⌉₊` parts almost refining `P₀`, where
`l₀ = max l #P₀.parts`, so it has at most `nestedRefinementBound ε (max l₀ ⌈2 * l₀ / ε⌉₊)`
parts.

SimpleGraph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator.signature:
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_sum_eq.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} {s t : V}
  [Finite V] [DecidableEq V] (c : V → ℕ) (hst : s ≠ t) (hadj : ¬G.Adj s t) :
  ∃ k P X,
    (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
      (∀ (v : V), v ≠ s → v ≠ t → {i | v ∈ (P i).support}.card ≤ c v) ∧
        ∃ (hs : s ∉ X) (ht : t ∉ X),
          ¬(SimpleGraph.induce (↑X)ᶜ G).Reachable ⟨s, hs⟩ ⟨t, ht⟩ ∧ ∑ v ∈ X, c v = k
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator.doc:
**Vertex-capacitated Menger's theorem.** Let `s` and `t` be distinct nonadjacent vertices of a
simple graph on a finite vertex type, and let `c v` be a capacity on every vertex. Some family of
`k` paths from `s` to `t`, in which every vertex `v` other than `s` and `t` lies on at most `c v`
members, and some set `X` of vertices other than `s` and `t`, whose deletion separates `s` from
`t`, satisfy `∑ v ∈ X, c v = k`. By `SimpleGraph.card_le_sum_of_not_reachable_induce`, the family is
then largest and the separator of least weight.

SimpleGraph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator.signature:
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_card_eq.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} {s t : V}
  [Finite V] (hst : s ≠ t) (hadj : ¬G.Adj s t) :
  ∃ k P X,
    Function.Injective P ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)) ∧
          ∃ (hs : s ∉ X) (ht : t ∉ X),
            ¬(SimpleGraph.induce (↑X)ᶜ G).Reachable ⟨s, hs⟩ ⟨t, ht⟩ ∧ X.card = k
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator.doc:
**Menger's theorem for internally vertex-disjoint paths.** Let `s` and `t` be distinct
nonadjacent vertices of a simple graph on a finite vertex type. Some family of `k` distinct paths
from `s` to `t`, pairwise sharing no vertex other than `s` and `t`, and some set of `k` vertices
other than `s` and `t`, whose deletion separates `s` from `t`, exist. By
`SimpleGraph.card_le_card_of_not_reachable_induce`, the family is then largest and the separator
smallest.

SimpleGraph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator.signature:
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_card_add_one_eq.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V}
  {s t : V} [Finite V] (h : G.Adj s t) :
  ∃ k P X,
    Function.Injective P ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin (k + 1)), (P i).IsPath) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)) ∧
          P (Fin.last k) = h.toWalk ∧
            ∃ (hs : s ∉ X) (ht : t ∉ X),
              ¬(SimpleGraph.induce (↑X)ᶜ (G.deleteEdges {s(s, t)})).Reachable ⟨s, hs⟩ ⟨t, ht⟩ ∧
                X.card = k
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator.doc:
**Menger's theorem for internally vertex-disjoint paths between adjacent vertices.** Let `s` and
`t` be adjacent vertices of a simple graph on a finite vertex type. For some `k`, there are a
family of `k + 1` distinct paths from `s` to `t`, pairwise sharing no vertex other than `s` and
`t`, whose last member is the path consisting of the edge `s(s, t)`, and a set of `k` vertices
other than `s` and `t` whose deletion, together with that of the edge `s(s, t)`, separates `s` from
`t`. By `SimpleGraph.card_le_card_add_one_of_not_reachable_induce_deleteEdges`, the family is then
largest and the separator smallest.

SimpleGraph.exists_paths_setSeparator_su.signature:
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_setSeparator_sum_eq.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} [Finite V]
  [DecidableEq V] (c : V → ℕ) (A B : Finset V) :
  ∃ k a b P X,
    (∀ (i : Fin k), a i ∈ A) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin k), b i ∈ B) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ v ∈ (P i).support, v ≠ a i → v ≠ b i → v ∉ A ∧ v ∉ B) ∧
            (∀ (v : V), {i | v ∈ (P i).support}.card ≤ c v) ∧
              (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ B, ∀ (p : G.Walk a b), ∃ v ∈ p.support, v ∈ X) ∧ ∑ v ∈ X, c v = k
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_setSeparator_su.doc:
**Vertex-capacitated Menger's theorem between vertex sets.** Let `A` and `B` be sets of vertices
of a simple graph on a finite vertex type, and let `c v` be a capacity on every vertex. Some family
of `k` paths, the `i`-th from `a i ∈ A` to `b i ∈ B` with its other vertices in neither `A` nor
`B`, in which every vertex `v` lies on at most `c v` members, and some set `X` of vertices meeting
every walk from a vertex of `A` to a vertex of `B` satisfy `∑ v ∈ X, c v = k`. By
`SimpleGraph.card_le_sum_of_forall_exists_mem_support`, the family is then largest and the
separator of least weight.

SimpleGraph.exists_paths_setSeparator_ca.signature:
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_setSeparator_card_eq.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} [Finite V]
  (A B : Finset V) :
  ∃ k a b P X,
    (∀ (i : Fin k), a i ∈ A) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin k), b i ∈ B) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ v ∈ (P i).support, v ≠ a i → v ≠ b i → v ∉ A ∧ v ∉ B) ∧
            (Pairwise fun i j => (P i).support.Disjoint (P j).support) ∧
              (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ B, ∀ (p : G.Walk a b), ∃ v ∈ p.support, v ∈ X) ∧ X.card = k
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_setSeparator_ca.doc:
**Menger's theorem for vertex-disjoint paths between vertex sets.** Let `A` and `B` be sets of
vertices of a simple graph on a finite vertex type. Some family of `k` pairwise vertex-disjoint
paths, the `i`-th from `a i ∈ A` to `b i ∈ B` with its other vertices in neither `A` nor `B`, and
some set of `k` vertices meeting every walk from a vertex of `A` to a vertex of `B` exist. By
`SimpleGraph.card_le_card_of_forall_exists_mem_support`, the family is then largest and the
separator smallest.

SimpleGraph.exists_paths_setEdgeSeparato.signature:
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_setEdgeSeparator_card_eq.{u} {α : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph α} [Finite α]
  {A B : Finset α} (hAB : Disjoint A B) :
  ∃ k a b P F,
    (∀ (i : Fin k), a i ∈ A) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin k), b i ∈ B) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ v ∈ (P i).support, v ≠ a i → v ≠ b i → v ∉ A ∧ v ∉ B) ∧
            (Pairwise fun i j => (P i).edges.Disjoint (P j).edges) ∧
              ↑F ⊆ G.edgeSet ∧ (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(G.deleteEdges ↑F).Reachable a b) ∧ F.card = k
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_setEdgeSeparato.doc:
**Menger's theorem for edge-disjoint paths between vertex sets in a simple graph.** For
disjoint finite vertex sets `A` and `B` in a finite simple graph, some family of pairwise
edge-disjoint `A`–`B` paths with no internal terminal vertex and some separating edge set have the
same cardinality. Shared endpoints are allowed.

SimpleGraph.exists_paths_edgeSeparator_c.signature:
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_edgeSeparator_card_eq.{u} {α : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph α} {s t : α}
  [Finite α] (hst : s ≠ t) :
  ∃ k P F,
    (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
      (Pairwise fun i j => (P i).edges.Disjoint (P j).edges) ∧
        ↑F ⊆ G.edgeSet ∧ ¬(G.deleteEdges ↑F).Reachable s t ∧ F.card = k
SimpleGraph.exists_paths_edgeSeparator_c.doc:
**Menger's theorem for edge-disjoint paths in a simple graph.** For distinct vertices `s` and
`t` of a finite simple graph, some family of `s`–`t` paths, no two of which traverse a common edge,
has as many members as some set of edges of `G` whose deletion leaves `s` and `t` unreachable. By
`SimpleGraph.card_le_encard_of_not_reachable_deleteEdges`, the family is then largest and the set
of edges smallest.

SimpleGraph.exists_fan_separator_card_eq.signature:
SimpleGraph.exists_fan_separator_card_eq.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} {x : V} {U : Finset V}
  [Finite V] (hx : x ∉ U) :
  ∃ k u P X,
    Function.Injective u ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin k), u i ∈ U) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ v ∈ (P i).support, v ≠ u i → v ∉ U) ∧
            (Pairwise fun i j => ∀ v ∈ (P i).support, v ∈ (P j).support → v = x) ∧
              x ∉ X ∧ (∀ y ∈ U, ∀ (p : G.Walk x y), ∃ v ∈ p.support, v ∈ X) ∧ X.card = k
SimpleGraph.exists_fan_separator_card_eq.doc:
**Menger's theorem for fans.** Let `x` be a vertex outside a set `U` of vertices of a simple
graph on a finite vertex type. Some family of `k` paths, the `i`-th from `x` to `u i ∈ U` with its
other vertices outside `U`, any two of which share only the vertex `x`, and some set of `k`
vertices other than `x` meeting every walk from `x` to a vertex of `U` exist. By
`SimpleGraph.card_le_card_of_fan`, the fan is then largest and the separator smallest.

SimpleGraph.cutDiscrepancy.signature:
SimpleGraph.cutDiscrepancy.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
  [DecidableRel G.Adj] (P : Finpartition Finset.univ) : ℝ
SimpleGraph.cutDiscrepancy.doc:
The cut discrepancy of `G` with respect to `P`: the largest deviation, over all rectangles
`(A, B)`, between the number of edges from `A` to `B` and its stepped prediction. It is
count-scaled, so it lies between `0` and `(card V) ^ 2`.

SimpleGraph.abs_card_induced_fin_three_s.signature:
SimpleGraph.abs_card_induced_fin_three_sub_le.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_2} [Field 𝕜]
  [LinearOrder 𝕜] [IsStrictOrderedRing 𝕜] {G : SimpleGraph α} [DecidableRel G.Adj] {ε : 𝕜}
  (J : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) [DecidableRel J.Adj] {A : Fin 3 → Finset α}
  (hA : ∀ (i j : Fin 3), i < j → G.IsUniform ε (A i) (A j)) :
  |↑{g ∈ Fintype.piFinset A | ∀ (i j : Fin 3), J.Adj i j ↔ G.Adj (g i) (g j)}.card -
        (∏ i, ↑(A i).card) * ∏ p, G.patternDensity (J.Adj (↑p).1 (↑p).2) (A (↑p).1) (A (↑p).2)| ≤
    3 * ε * ∏ i, ↑(A i).card
SimpleGraph.abs_card_induced_fin_three_s.doc:
**Induced counting lemma for three cells.** Let `A 0`, `A 1`, `A 2` be pairwise `ε`-uniform
cells of `G`, and `J` a graph on `Fin 3`. Then the number of maps `g` with `g i ∈ A i` such that
`g i` and `g j` are adjacent in `G` exactly when `i` and `j` are adjacent in `J` differs from
`|A 0| |A 1| |A 2|` times the product, over the pairs `i < j`, of the edge density of
`(A i, A j)` (if `i` and `j` are adjacent in `J`) or of its nonedge density `1 - d(A i, A j)`
(otherwise), that is `SimpleGraph.patternDensity`, by at most `3 ε |A 0| |A 1| |A 2|`.

SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.isEdgeConn.signature:
SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.isEdgeConnected.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} {k : ℕ∞}
  (h : G.IsVertexConnected k) : G.IsEdgeConnected k
SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.isEdgeConn.doc:
**Whitney's inequality**, predicate form: a `k`-vertex-connected graph is
`k`-edge-connected.

SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.exists_isO.doc:
**Whitney's theorem with prescribed initial cycle.** For any cycle `c` in a `2`-vertex-connected
simple graph on a finite vertex type, there is an open ear decomposition of `⊤` whose initial
subgraph is `c.toSubgraph`.

SimpleGraph.IsVertexConnected.exists_isC.doc:
**Dirac's theorem.** For `2 ≤ k`, every set of at most `k` vertices of a `k`-vertex-connected
simple graph on a finite vertex type lies on a common cycle.

Setoid.silver_dichotomy_standardBorel.signature:
Setoid.silver_dichotomy_standardBorel.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace X]
  [StandardBorelSpace X] (E : Setoid X) (hE : MeasurableSet {p | E p.1 p.2}) :
  Countable (Quotient E) ∨ ∃ f, MeasurableEmbedding f ∧ ∀ (a b : ℕ → Bool), a ≠ b → ¬E (f a) (f b)
Setoid.silver_dichotomy_standardBorel.doc:
**Silver's theorem on a standard Borel space.** A Borel equivalence relation on a standard
Borel space has countably many classes, or a measurable embedding of Cantor space sending distinct
points to inequivalent points.

Setoid.silver_dichotomy.signature:
Setoid.silver_dichotomy.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] [PolishSpace X]
  [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (E : Setoid X) (hE : MeasurableSet {p | E p.1 p.2}) :
  Countable (Quotient E) ∨ E.HasCantorAntichainOn Set.univ
Setoid.silver_dichotomy.doc:
**Silver's theorem.** A Borel equivalence relation on a Polish space has countably many
classes, or a Cantor antichain on the whole space: a continuous map of Cantor space sending
distinct points to inequivalent points.

Setoid.mk_quotient_le_aleph0_or_eq_conti.signature:
Setoid.mk_quotient_le_aleph0_or_eq_continuum.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace X]
  [StandardBorelSpace X] (E : Setoid X) (hE : MeasurableSet {p | E p.1 p.2}) :
  Cardinal.mk (Quotient E) ≤ Cardinal.aleph0 ∨ Cardinal.mk (Quotient E) = Cardinal.continuum
Setoid.mk_quotient_le_aleph0_or_eq_conti.doc:
**The cardinality form of Silver's theorem.** A Borel equivalence relation on a standard Borel
space has at most `ℵ₀` or exactly `𝔠` classes.

Setoid.hasCantorAntichainOn_range_of_for.signature:
Setoid.hasCantorAntichainOn_range_of_forall_gSGraph_adj.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} {S : Set (List Bool)}
  {φ : (ℕ → Bool) → X} [TopologicalSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (E : Setoid X)
  (hE : MeasurableSet {p | E p.1 p.2}) (hS : TauCeti.DenseWords S) (hφ : Continuous φ)
  (hφE : ∀ ⦃y z : ℕ → Bool⦄, (TauCeti.gSGraph S).Adj y z → ¬E (φ y) (φ z)) :
  E.HasCantorAntichainOn (Set.range φ)
Setoid.hasCantorAntichainOn_range_of_for.doc:
**The category route to Silver's theorem.** Let `E` be a Borel equivalence relation and `φ` a
continuous map from Cantor space sending the edges of `gSGraph S` to `E`-inequivalent pairs. If `S`
is dense, the range of `φ` carries a Cantor antichain for `E`.

Setoid.countable_or_hasCantorAntichainOn.signature:
Setoid.countable_or_hasCantorAntichainOn_of_measurableSet.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [PolishSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] {A : Set X} (hA : MeasurableSet A)
  (R : Setoid X) (F : Setoid ↑A) (hRF : ∀ (x y : ↑A), R ↑x ↑y → F x y)
  (hF : MeasurableSet {p | F p.1 p.2}) : Countable (Quotient F) ∨ R.HasCantorAntichainOn A
Setoid.countable_or_hasCantorAntichainOn.doc:
**Silver's theorem relative to a Borel subset.** Let `A` be a Borel subset of a Polish space
`X`, `F` a Borel equivalence relation on `A`, and `R` any equivalence relation on `X` whose
restriction to `A` refines `F`. Then `F` has countably many classes, or `A` carries a Cantor
antichain for `R`, continuous for the topology of `X`.

Setoid.borelReducible_bot_iff_not_counta.signature:
Setoid.borelReducible_bot_iff_not_countable_quotient.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace X]
  [StandardBorelSpace X] (E : Setoid X) (hE : MeasurableSet {p | E p.1 p.2}) :
  ⊥.BorelReducible E ↔ ¬Countable (Quotient E)
Setoid.borelReducible_bot_iff_not_counta.doc:
**Silver's theorem in reducibility form.** Equality on Cantor space is Borel reducible to a
Borel equivalence relation on a standard Borel space exactly when the latter has uncountably many
classes.

SetRel.exists_measurableSet_isIndependen.signature:
SetRel.exists_measurableSet_isIndependent_superset.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} {G : SetRel X X} {A : Set X}
  [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]
  (hG : MeasureTheory.AnalyticSet G) (hA : MeasureTheory.AnalyticSet A) (hind : G.IsIndependent A) :
  ∃ B, MeasurableSet B ∧ A ⊆ B ∧ G.IsIndependent B
SetRel.exists_measurableSet_isIndependen.doc:
**The Kechris–Solecki–Todorcevic lemma.** In a Hausdorff space with its Borel σ-algebra, an
analytic independent set of an analytic relation is contained in a Borel independent set.

Set.weightEnumerator.signature:
Set.weightEnumerator.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {β : ι → Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [(i : ι) → Zero (β i)]
  [(i : ι) → DecidableEq (β i)] (C : Set ((i : ι) → β i)) : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℤ
Set.weightEnumerator.doc:
The homogeneous Hamming weight enumerator `W_C(X, Y) = ∑_w A_w(C) X^(n-w) Y^w`, where `n`
is the length, `A_w(C)` is the weight distribution, and the variables `0, 1` are `X, Y`.

SchwartzMap.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier_span_or.signature:
SchwartzMap.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier_span_orthonormalBasis.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] {ι : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] (f : SchwartzMap E ℂ)
  (o : OrthonormalBasis ι ℝ E) [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (v : E) :
  ∑' (ℓ : ↥(Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range ⇑o))), f (v + ↑ℓ) =
    ∑' (m : ↥(Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range ⇑o))),
      FourierTransform.fourier ⇑f ↑m * Complex.exp (2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I * ↑(inner ℝ v ↑m))
SchwartzMap.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier_span_or.doc:
**Poisson's summation formula** over the lattice `L` spanned by an orthonormal basis `o` of a
finite-dimensional real inner product space: for a Schwartz function `f` and `v : E`,
`∑' ℓ : L, f (v + ℓ) = ∑' m : L, 𝓕 f m * exp (2πi ⟪v, m⟫)`. For the standard basis of
`EuclideanSpace ℝ ι` this is Poisson summation over `ℤ^ι`.

SchwartzMap.tsum_eq_tsum_dual_fourier.signature:
SchwartzMap.tsum_eq_tsum_dual_fourier.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  (f : SchwartzMap E ℂ) (L : Submodule ℤ E) [DiscreteTopology ↥L] [IsZLattice ℝ L] (v : E) :
  ∑' (ℓ : ↥L), f (v + ↑ℓ) =
    (↑(ZLattice.covolume L MeasureTheory.volume))⁻¹ *
      ∑' (m : ↥(ZLattice.dual L)),
        FourierTransform.fourier ⇑f ↑m * Complex.exp (2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I * ↑(inner ℝ v ↑m))
SchwartzMap.tsum_eq_tsum_dual_fourier.doc:
**Poisson's summation formula** over a full lattice `L` of a finite-dimensional real inner
product space: for a Schwartz function `f` and `v : E`,
`∑' ℓ : L, f (v + ℓ) = (covolume L)⁻¹ * ∑' m : L^∨, 𝓕 f m * exp (2πi ⟪v, m⟫)`.
The sign of the phase is the one forced by Mathlib's `𝓕 f w = ∫ x, exp (-2πi ⟪x, w⟫) f x`.

SchwartzMap.norm_fourierInv_toL2_eq.signature:
SchwartzMap.norm_fourierInv_toL2_eq.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℂ F] [CompleteSpace F] (f : SchwartzMap E F) :
  ‖(FourierTransformInv.fourierInv f).toLp 2 MeasureTheory.volume‖ = ‖f.toLp 2 MeasureTheory.volume‖
SchwartzMap.norm_fourierInv_toL2_eq.doc: **Plancherel's theorem** for the inverse Fourier transform of Schwartz functions.

SchwartzMap.integral_norm_pow_mul_norm_f.signature:
SchwartzMap.integral_norm_pow_mul_norm_fourierInv_sq_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {V : Type u_1}
  {H : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [FiniteDimensional ℝ V]
  [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]

      ∑ i, ‖((LineDeriv.lineDerivOp (b i))^[N] σ).toLp 2 MeasureTheory.volume‖ ^ 2
SchwartzMap.integral_norm_pow_mul_norm_f.doc:
**The weighted Plancherel bound**: for a Schwartz function `σ`, an orthonormal basis `b` of
`V` indexed by `ι`, and `N ≠ 0`,

`(2π) ^ (2N) ∫ ‖x‖ ^ (2N) ‖𝓕⁻ σ x‖² dx ≤ (#ι) ^ (N - 1) ∑ᵢ ‖∂_{bᵢ}^N σ‖²_{L²}`.

SchwartzMap.integral_inner_pow_mul_norm_.signature:
SchwartzMap.integral_inner_pow_mul_norm_fourierInv_sq.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] [MeasurableSpace V]

SchwartzMap.integral_inner_pow_mul_norm_.doc:
**The weighted Plancherel identity**: for a Schwartz function `σ`,

`(2π) ^ (2N) ∫ ⟪x, m⟫ ^ (2N) ‖𝓕⁻ σ x‖² dx = ‖∂_m^N σ‖²_{L²}`.

SchwartzMap.integral_bilinear_laplacian_.signature:
SchwartzMap.integral_bilinear_laplacian_right_eq_neg_sum.{u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {E : Type u_3}
  {F₁ : Type u_4} {F₂ : Type u_5} {F₃ : Type u_6} {ι : Type u_7} [NormedAddCommGroup E]

**Green's identity on Schwartz space**: for a continuous bilinear map `B` and an orthonormal
basis `b`, `∫ B(f, Δg) = -∑ᵢ ∫ B(∂_{bᵢ} f, ∂_{bᵢ} g)`.

SchauderBasis.surjective_inclusionInDoub.signature:
SchauderBasis.surjective_inclusionInDoubleDual_iff.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2}

SchauderBasis.surjective_inclusionInDoub.doc:
**James's basis criterion.** A Banach space with a Schauder basis is reflexive
if and only if that basis is shrinking and boundedly complete.

**Moore's theorem**: a simplicial set whose sets of simplices are groups, with simplicial

SSet.kanComplex_of_addGroup.{u} {X : _root_.SSet} [(n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) → AddGroup (X.obj n)]

SSet.kanComplex_of_addGroup.doc:
**Moore's theorem** for additive groups: a simplicial set whose sets of simplices are additive
groups, with simplicial operators additive, is a Kan complex.

SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory.doc:
The full enhanced subcategory of a simplicial set `X` on a predicate `P` on its vertices: the
subcomplex of the simplices all of whose vertices satisfy `P`.

**The Eilenberg–Zilber theorem**: the Alexander–Whitney map
`C(K × L; R ⊗ S) ⟶ C(K; R) ⊗ C(L; S)` is a chain homotopy equivalence, with homotopy inverse the
shuffle map.

`ω` of the longest element `w₀` and a weight `λ`,

`Δ · D_{w₀}(e^λ) = ∑_{w ∈ W} sgn(w) e^{w λ - (ρ - w ρ)}`,

the alternating sum over the dot orbit `w ⬝ λ = w(λ + ρ) - ρ`.

RootPairing.weylDenominator_mul_prod_map.doc:
**Demazure's formula for the longest element**: for a reduced word `ω` of the longest element
`w₀` (an element of which every simple reflection is a left descent),

`Δ · D_{w₀}(f) = ∑_{w ∈ W} sgn(w) e^{-(ρ - w ρ)} w(f)`,

where `D_{w₀}` is the product of the Demazure operators along `ω`, `Δ` is the Weyl denominator and
the right-hand side is the dot alternatization (`RootPairing.dotAlternatization_apply`). Since `Δ`
is not a zero divisor, this determines `D_{w₀}(f)`.

RootPairing.reflectionBond.doc:
The **bond** of two weights related by a reflection in a positive root: if `y = s_β x` for a
positive root `β`, it is `⟨y, β^∨⟩ = -⟨x, β^∨⟩`. For `y ≠ x` and a reduced root pairing the
positive root `β` is unique (`TauCeti.eq_of_isPos_of_reflection_eq`), so the bond is well defined
(`RootPairing.reflectionBond_eq_coroot'`). If no reflection in a positive root sends `x` to `y`, the
bond is `0`. For a cover `y ⋖ x` of the parabolic quotient `W / W_λ`, the bond of `x λ` and `y λ`
is the positive cover bond `b_λ(x, y)`.

RootPairing.parabolic_wallIndices_eq_sta.doc:
**The stabilizer of a dominant weight is a standard parabolic subgroup**: the one generated by
the simple reflections in the walls through it.

**The localization identity** of the Demazure operator:
`(1 - e^{-αᵢ}) Dᵢ(f) = f - e^{-αᵢ} sᵢ(f)`, where `sᵢ` reindexes `ℤ[M]` along the reflection of
`M`. Equivalently, `Dᵢ(e^x) = (e^x - e^{-αᵢ} e^{sᵢ x}) / (1 - e^{-αᵢ})`.

RootPairing.existsUnique_nonempty_equiv_.doc:
**The Cartan-Killing classification.** Every irreducible reduced crystallographic finite root
system over `ℚ` is isomorphic to the model root system `TauCeti.DynkinType.rationalRootSystem t` of
a unique valid Dynkin type `t`.

RootPairing.dotAlternatization_one.doc:
**The Weyl denominator identity for a root datum**:

`∑_{w ∈ W} sgn(w) e^{-(ρ - w ρ)} = ∏_{α > 0} (1 - e^{-α})`,

where `ρ - w ρ = ∑_{β > 0, w⁻¹ β < 0} β`. Unlike `TauCeti.weylDenominator_eq_weylNumerator_zero`,
this needs neither `ρ` to be a weight nor the roots to span.

**Kostant's multiplicity formula**, stated before any module is named: an element of `ℤ[M]`
whose product with the Weyl denominator is the Weyl numerator of `λ` has `μ`-th coefficient
`∑_{w ∈ W} sgn(w) P(w ⬝ λ - μ)`.

The hypothesis is exactly the Weyl character formula, so this turns that formula into a closed
expression for one weight multiplicity at a time.

**Johnson's uniqueness-of-norm theorem.** On a complex algebra `A` with zero Jacobson radical,
not necessarily unital, any two ring norms compatible with scalars, under which `A` is complete,
are equivalent.

RingHom.isHomeomorph_kerLift.signature:
RingHom.isHomeomorph_kerLift.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace R]

RingHom.isHomeomorph_kerLift.doc:
**The topological first isomorphism theorem for rings.** A ring homomorphism that is a
quotient map presents its target as the quotient of its source by its kernel, topologically as
well as algebraically.

A continuous surjection is not enough on its own. Surjectivity of `f` makes the lift bijective and
continuity of `f` makes it continuous, but a continuous bijection is open only when the topology it
lands in is no coarser than the one it carries; that `f` is a quotient map is exactly the statement
that it is not coarser.

`IsHomeomorph.homeomorph` turns this into `R ⧸ ker f ≃ₜ S`. What it bundles is `RingHom.kerLift`,
which is a ring homomorphism, so a consumer needing the isomorphism of rings has it already —
`RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective` is that same map.

RingEquiv.trivialF2Map1Equiv_kummerSquar.doc:
**The Kummer isomorphism on square classes is natural in field isomorphisms**: transport of
`H¹(-, 𝔽₂)` along `G_L ≃ G_K` corresponds to pushforward of square classes along `e`.

Ring.SatisfiesSerreR.signature: Ring.SatisfiesSerreR.{u} (n : ℕ) (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : Prop
Ring.SatisfiesSerreR.doc:
A ring `R` satisfies *Serre's condition* `(R_n)` if every prime of height at most `n` lies in
the regular locus, that is, `R_p` is a regular local ring whenever `ht p ≤ n`. Stacks,
Definition 10.157.1 (031P).

**Henselian pairs are stable under directed colimits.** If every `(G i, I i)` is a
Henselian pair and the transition maps carry `I i` into `I j`, then the directed colimit
`Ring.DirectLimit G f` is Henselian along the colimit ideal `⨆ i, (I i).map (of G f i)`.

Representation.symmetricAlgebraReynolds.doc:
The **Reynolds operator** `p ↦ #G⁻¹ • ∑ g, g • p`, from `Sym M` onto the invariant subalgebra.
It is linear over the invariant subalgebra and restricts to the identity on it, but it is
generally not multiplicative.

Representation.symmetricAlgebraInvariant.doc:
**The homogeneous Noether bound.** The invariants of a finite linear group over a rational
algebra are generated by homogeneous invariants of positive degree at most the group order.
This holds without finite generation or freeness of the underlying module.

The invariant subalgebra `Sym(M)^G`: the elements of `Sym M` fixed by the induced action of
every element of `G`, that is, the fixed subalgebra `FixedPoints.subalgebra` of the bundled
action.

**Graded Nakayama lemma for the coinvariant algebra.** Homogeneous elements of `Sym M` whose
images span the coinvariant algebra `Sym M ⧸ A₊ · Sym M` over `R` generate `Sym M` as a module
over the invariant subalgebra `A = Sym(M)^G`.

Representation.radical_symmetricAlgebraH.doc:
For a finite group over a reduced base, the radical of the Hilbert ideal is the irrelevant
ideal.

**The converse of the Chevalley–Shephard–Todd theorem.** Let a finite group `G` act faithfully
and linearly on a finite-dimensional vector space `V` over a field `K` of characteristic zero. If
the polynomial invariants `Sym(V*)^G` form a polynomial algebra on homogeneous invariants, then `G`
is generated by its pseudoreflections, the elements whose fixed space is a hyperplane.

Representation.pseudoreflectionSubgroup_.doc:
**The Chevalley–Shephard–Todd theorem.** Let a finite group `G` act faithfully and linearly on a
finite-dimensional vector space `V` over a field `K` of characteristic zero. Then `G` is generated
by pseudoreflections, the elements whose fixed space is a hyperplane, if and only if the
polynomial invariants `Sym(V*)^G` form a polynomial algebra on homogeneous invariants
`f₁, …, fₙ` of positive degree, where necessarily `n = dim V`.

**Chevalley's theorem: the coinvariant algebra of a reflection group is the regular
representation.** If a finite group `G` acts faithfully on a finite-dimensional vector space `V`
over a field of characteristic zero and is generated by pseudoreflections, then the coinvariant
algebra of the polynomial functions `Sym(V*)`, as an ungraded representation, is equivalent to the
regular representation `K[G]`.

**Finiteness of the coinvariant algebra.** For a finite group acting on a finitely generated
module, the coinvariant algebra `Sym M ⧸ A₊ · Sym M` is a finite `R`-module: it is of finite type,
and generated by nilpotent, hence integral, elements.

this determines the Hilbert series.

**Molien's formula**, trace form: the image in `K⟦X⟧` of the Hilbert series of the invariant
subalgebra (its coefficients are the dimensions of the homogeneous components, cast into `K`) is
the average over the group of the graded traces `∑ₙ tr(g | Symⁿ M) tⁿ`. In characteristic zero
this determines the Hilbert series.

Representation.forall_mem_symmetricAlgebraInvariants_lift_eval_eq_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1}

Representation.forall_mem_symmetricAlgeb.doc:
**Invariant polynomials detect orbits.** Two vectors have the same value on every invariant
polynomial function exactly when they lie in the same orbit.

Representation.forall_homogeneous_mem_sy.doc:
**The fibre over the vertex is the origin.** Every homogeneous invariant polynomial function
of positive degree vanishes at `v` exactly when `v = 0`.

**Molien's formula, degreewise.** The dimension of the degree-`n` part of the invariant
subalgebra, cast into `K`, is equal in `K` to the average over the group of the traces
`tr(g | Symⁿ M)`. In characteristic zero this determines the dimension; in characteristic `p` it
determines it only modulo `p`.

This is the instance on `Symⁿ M` of the character formula
`Representation.card_inv_mul_sum_char_eq_finrank` for the dimension of the invariants, stated
with the normalisation `⅟#G` of the Reynolds operator and the degree-`n` maps
`homogeneousSubmoduleMapₛₗ (ρ g) n`.

Representation.finrank_linearMap_eq_of_i.doc:
**Clifford's theorem, multiplicity form, for two minimal subspaces.**  The hom spaces of any
two minimal `N`-stable subspaces of an irreducible representation have the same dimension; over a
splitting field this says that the two constituents occur in the restriction with the same
multiplicity.

Representation.finrank_linearMap_eq_of_i.signature:
Representation.finrank_linearMap_eq_of_isAtom.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {G : Type u_2}

Representation.finrank_linearMap_eq_of_i.doc:
**Clifford's theorem, multiplicity form.**  Every simple `k[N]`-submodule of the restriction of
an irreducible representation has a hom space of the same dimension as that of a given minimal
`N`-stable subspace; over a splitting field this says that the two constituents occur in the
restriction with the same multiplicity.  By the single-orbit theorem the submodule is isomorphic to
a translate of the subspace, and a translate transports.

  Algebra.FiniteType R ↥ρ.symmetricAlgebraInvariants
Representation.finiteType_symmetricAlgeb.doc:
**Noether's finiteness theorem** for the invariants of a finite group acting on a finitely
generated module over a Noetherian ring: the invariant subalgebra is of finite type.

Representation.exists_forall_finrank_lin.signature:
Representation.exists_forall_finrank_linearMap_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {G : Type u_2}

Representation.exists_forall_finrank_lin.doc:
**Clifford's theorem, the common multiplicity.**  For a finite-dimensional irreducible `ρ`
there is a positive natural number `e` such that the hom space of every irreducible
`N`-constituent of the restriction has dimension `e`.  The restriction is semisimple
(`TauCeti.Representation.isSemisimpleRepresentation_comp_subtype`), so over a splitting field this
`e` is the `e` of the classical decomposition `Res_N W ≅ e · ⨁ᵢ {}^{gᵢ} V`.

Representation.exists_forall_apply_eq_mu.doc:
**Schur's lemma for contravariant forms.** Over an algebraically closed field, a contravariant
form on a finite-dimensional irreducible representation is a scalar multiple of any separating
contravariant form.

Representation.exists_common_fixed_vecto.signature:
Representation.exists_common_fixed_vector_of_isUnipotent.{u, v, w} {K : Type u} {G : Type w}

  ∃ v, v ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ (g : G), (ρ g) v = v
Representation.exists_common_fixed_vecto.doc:
**Kolchin's common fixed vector theorem.** If every element of a monoid acts unipotently on a
nonzero finite-dimensional vector space over a field, then the monoid fixes a nonzero vector.

Representation.exists_bijective_aeval_sy.signature:
Representation.exists_bijective_aeval_symmetricAlgebraInvariants_dual_of_pseudoreflectionSubgroup_eq_top.{u_1,

Representation.exists_bijective_aeval_sy.doc:
**The Chevalley–Shephard–Todd theorem.** Let a finite group `G`, whose order is invertible in
the field `K`, act linearly on a finite-dimensional vector space `V`, and suppose that `G` is
generated by pseudoreflections, the elements whose fixed space is a hyperplane. Then the
polynomial invariants `Sym(V*)^G` form a polynomial algebra on `dim V` homogeneous invariants
`f₁, …, fₙ` of positive degree: `K[X₁, …, Xₙ] → Sym(V*)^G`, `Xᵢ ↦ fᵢ`, is an isomorphism.

Representation.eq_zero_of_isEmpty_equiv.signature:

Representation.eq_zero_of_isEmpty_equiv.doc:
**Schur's lemma for pairings of nonisomorphic representations.** A contravariant pairing of two
irreducible representations that are not isomorphic vanishes, provided the source carries a
separating contravariant form.

Representation.char_eq_zero_or_norm_char.doc:
**Burnside's vanishing theorem.** If the conjugacy class of `g` has size coprime to the degree
of an irreducible complex representation `ρ`, then its character either vanishes at `g` or attains
there the maximum absolute value `χ(1)` that any character value can have.

The average `χ(g) / χ(1)` is an algebraic integer (`Representation.isIntegral_char_div_finrank`)
and `χ(g)` is a sum of `χ(1)` roots of unity, so Kronecker's theorem leaves no other
possibility.

Representation.char_eq_zero_or_exists_ap.doc:
**Burnside's vanishing theorem, scalar form** (Isaacs, Theorem 3.8). If the conjugacy class of
`g` has size coprime to the degree of an irreducible complex representation `ρ`, then either its
character vanishes at `g`, or `ρ g` is a scalar `μ • 1`, that is, `g` lies in the centre `Z(χ)` of
the character (Isaacs, Lemma 2.27).

Representation.asAlgebraHom_surjective_o.signature:
Representation.asAlgebraHom_surjective_of_isIrreducible.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1}
  {G : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3} [Field k] [Monoid G] [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module k V]
  [IsAlgClosed k] [FiniteDimensional k V] (ρ : Representation k G V) (hρ : ρ.IsIrreducible) :
  Function.Surjective ⇑ρ.asAlgebraHom
Representation.asAlgebraHom_surjective_o.doc:
**Burnside density theorem.** The monoid algebra of a finite-dimensional irreducible
representation over an algebraically closed field exhausts the full endomorphism algebra.

Jacobson density gives all endomorphisms linear over the representation's commuting endomorphism
ring. Schur's lemma identifies that ring with the base field, so these are exactly the
`k`-linear endomorphisms.

Representation.adjoin_range_eq_top_of_le.doc:
**Graded Nakayama lemma for polynomial invariants.** Homogeneous invariants of positive degree
whose classes span `A₊ ⧸ A₊²`, where `A₊` is the ideal of invariants with zero constant term,
generate the invariant algebra `Sym(M)^G` as an `R`-algebra.

Representation.IsIrreducible.exists_forall_apply_eq_smul.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1}

Representation.IsIrreducible.exists_fora.doc:
**Schur's lemma, scalar form.** Over an algebraically closed field, a linear endomorphism of a
finite-dimensional irreducible representation commuting with the action is multiplication by a
scalar.  This is `Representation.IsIrreducible.algebraMap_intertwiningMap_bijective_of_isAlgClosed`
read pointwise on an unbundled endomorphism.

Representation.IntertwiningMap.exists_le.signature:
Representation.IntertwiningMap.exists_leftInverse_of_injective.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {k : Type u_1}
  {G : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3} {W : Type u_4} [Field k] [Group G] [Finite G] [NeZero ↑(Nat.card G)]

Representation.IntertwiningMap.exists_le.doc:
**Maschke's theorem for intertwining maps.**  Over a field in which the order of the finite
group `G` is invertible, an injective intertwining map `f : ρ → σ` has an intertwining left
inverse `p : σ → ρ`, that is, `p ∘ f = id`.

Rep.projective_of_isZero_res_sylow.signature:
Rep.projective_of_isZero_res_sylow.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] [Finite G]
  (A : Rep.{u, u, u} k G) [Module.Projective k ↑A]
  (h :
    ∀ (p : ℕ),
      Nat.Prime p →
        p ∣ Nat.card G →
          ∃ P x,
            IsUnit ↑p ∨
              (Ideal.span {↑p}).IsMaximal ∧
                (∀ (v : ↑A), ↑p • v = 0 → v = 0) ∧
                  CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (tateCohomology (Rep.res (↑P).subtype A) 0) ∧
                    CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (tateCohomology (Rep.res (↑P).subtype A) (-1))) :
  Module.Projective (MonoidAlgebra k G) A.ρ.asModule
Rep.projective_of_isZero_res_sylow.doc:
**Nakayama–Rim, Sylow form** (Serre, *Local Fields*, IX §§3–5; Rim, Ann. of Math. 69 (1959)).
Let `k` be a commutative ring, `G` a finite group, and `A` a representation of `G` on a
projective `k`-module. Suppose that for each prime `p` dividing `|G|` some Sylow `p`-subgroup `P`
satisfies: `p` is a unit in `k`, or `pk` is a maximal ideal, multiplication by `p` is injective
on `A`, and `H_Tate⁰(P, A) = H_Tate⁻¹(P, A) = 0`. Then `A` is projective over `k[G]`.

Rep.projective_of_isZero_res.signature:
Rep.projective_of_isZero_res.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] [Finite G] [IsDomain k]
  [CharZero k] (hk : ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → IsUnit ↑p ∨ (Ideal.span {↑p}).IsMaximal)
  (A : Rep.{u, u, u} k G) [Module.Projective k ↑A]
  (hA :
    ∀ (S : Subgroup G) [inst : Fintype ↥S] (n : ℤ),
      CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (tateCohomology (Rep.res S.subtype A) n)) :
  Module.Projective (MonoidAlgebra k G) A.ρ.asModule
Rep.projective_of_isZero_res.doc:
**Nakayama–Rim, lattice form** (Serre, *Local Fields*, IX §§3–5; Rim, Ann. of Math. 69
(1959)). Over an integral domain of characteristic zero in which every prime number is a unit or
generates a maximal ideal (for instance `ℤ`, `ℤ_[p]` or `ℤ_(p)`), a cohomologically trivial
representation of a finite group whose underlying `k`-module is projective — for instance free, of
any rank — is projective over `k[G]`.

Rep.projective_ker_of_isZero_res.signature:
Rep.projective_ker_of_isZero_res.{u, u_1} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] [Finite G]
  [IsDomain k] [IsPrincipalIdealRing k] [CharZero k]
  (hk : ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → IsUnit ↑p ∨ (Ideal.span {↑p}).IsMaximal) (A : Rep.{u, u, u} k G)
  (hA :
    ∀ (S : Subgroup G) [inst : Fintype ↥S] (n : ℤ),
      CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (tateCohomology (Rep.res S.subtype A) n))
  {P : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup P] [_root_.Module (MonoidAlgebra k G) P]
  [Module.Projective (MonoidAlgebra k G) P] (f : P →ₗ[MonoidAlgebra k G] A.ρ.asModule)
  (hf : Function.Surjective ⇑f) : Module.Projective (MonoidAlgebra k G) ↥f.ker
Rep.projective_ker_of_isZero_res.doc:
**Nakayama–Rim: cohomological triviality gives projective dimension at most one.** If `A` is
cohomologically trivial, the kernel of every surjection onto `A.ρ.asModule` from a projective
`k[G]`-module is projective. Here `k` is a principal ideal domain of characteristic zero in which
every prime number is a unit or generates a maximal ideal; no finiteness is assumed of `A` or of
the projective module.

Real.isEquivalent_Gamma_natCast_add_one_.doc:
**Euler's limit formula in ratio form.** For every real `s`, `Γ(n + 1 + s)` is asymptotic to
`n ^ s * n!` as the natural number `n` tends to infinity.

Real.infinite_setOf_mul_abs_mul_sub_roun.doc:
**Dirichlet's theorem, nearest-integer form.** For every real `α`, infinitely many natural
numbers `q ≥ 1` satisfy `q ‖q α‖ ≤ 1`.

Real.fourierInv_mul_convolution_eq.signature:

  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [NormedRing R]
  [NormedSpace ℂ R] [IsScalarTower ℂ R R] [SMulCommClass ℂ R R] [CompleteSpace R] {f₁ f₂ : E → R}
  (hf₁ : MeasureTheory.Integrable f₁ MeasureTheory.volume)
  (hf₂ : MeasureTheory.Integrable f₂ MeasureTheory.volume) (x : E) :
  FourierTransformInv.fourierInv
      (MeasureTheory.convolution f₁ f₂ (ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℂ R) MeasureTheory.volume) x =
    FourierTransformInv.fourierInv f₁ x * FourierTransformInv.fourierInv f₂ x
Real.fourierInv_mul_convolution_eq.doc:
**The convolution theorem for the inverse Fourier transform.** The inverse Fourier transform
of the convolution of two integrable functions is the product of their inverse Fourier
transforms.

Real.exp_le_one_add_add_sq_div_of_le.signature:
Real.exp_le_one_add_add_sq_div_of_le {x c : ℝ} (hxc : x ≤ c) (hc0 : 0 ≤ c) (hc3 : c < 3) :

Real.exp_le_one_add_add_sq_div_of_le.doc:
**Bernstein's exponential bound.** If `x ≤ c` with `0 ≤ c < 3`, then
`exp x ≤ 1 + x + x ^ 2 / (2 * (1 - c / 3))`. Only an upper bound on `x` is needed: negative `x`
are covered by `Real.exp_le_one_add_add_sq_div_two_of_nonpos`.

QuotientGroup.quotientQuotientEquivQuoti.signature:
QuotientGroup.quotientQuotientEquivQuotientSup.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] (H N : Subgroup G)
  [N.Normal] : (G ⧸ N) ⧸ Subgroup.map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) H ≃ G ⧸ H ⊔ N
QuotientGroup.quotientQuotientEquivQuoti.doc:
**The third isomorphism theorem for coset spaces.** For a normal `N` and an *arbitrary*
subgroup `H`, the cosets of the image of `H` in `G ⧸ N` are the cosets of `H ⊔ N` in `G`, both
directions sending the class of `g` to the class of `g`.

Mathlib's `QuotientGroup.quotientQuotientEquivQuotient` is the group isomorphism this
generalises: it asks for `N ≤ M` with `M` normal, so that both sides are groups and the map is a
homomorphism. Here neither side need be a group — `H` is unconstrained — and what survives is the
bijection of coset spaces, which is what a coset-indexed sum or family needs.

QuotientAddGroup.quotientQuotientEquivQu.doc:
**The third isomorphism theorem for coset spaces**, additive version: for a
normal `N` and an arbitrary subgroup `H`, the cosets of the image of `H` in `G ⧸ N` are the
cosets of `H ⊔ N` in `G`.

    (a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + c ^ 2 + d ^ 2) • (Q x + Q y + Q z + Q w)
QuadraticMap.euler_four_squares.doc:
**Euler's four-square identity for a quadratic map.** Multiplying `(x, y, z, w)` by the
quaternion `a + bi + cj + dk` multiplies `Q x + Q y + Q z + Q w` by `a² + b² + c² + d²`. For
`Q = x ↦ x²` on a commutative ring this is `euler_four_squares`.

QuadraticMap.IsometryEquiv.exists_extens.doc:
**Witt's extension theorem** (Lam I.4.9). An isometry between regular subspaces of a
finite-dimensional quadratic space extends to an isometry of the whole space. No regularity
hypothesis on the ambient form is needed.

regular quaternary form over a number field `K` whose discriminant is a square and which is
isotropic at every finite and real place. If every regular diagonal ternary form over `K` that is
isotropic at every finite and real place is isotropic over `K`, then `Q` is isotropic over `K`.

QuadraticForm.not_anisotropic_of_isLocal.doc:
**The quaternary case of the Hasse–Minkowski theorem.** Let `Q` be a regular quaternary form
over a number field `K` which is isotropic at every finite and real place. If, over every number
field, every regular diagonal ternary form that is isotropic at every finite and real place is
isotropic, then `Q` is isotropic over `K`.

The ternary hypothesis is quantified over number fields because it is needed not only over `K` but
also over the quadratic field `K(√d)`, for `d` a nonsquare representative of the discriminant of
`Q`.

form of rank `n ≥ 5` over a number field that is isotropic at every finite and real place. If every
diagonal regular form of rank `n - 1` that is isotropic at every finite and real place is isotropic
over `K`, then `Q` is isotropic over `K`.

every finite and every real place exactly when they have the same rank, the images of their global
discriminants agree at every finite place, and they have the same Hasse sign at every finite place
and the same positive index at every real place.

A submodule on which `Q` is nonpositive is totally real for a linear endomorphism `J` if
`Q(v) + Q(Jv)` is positive for every nonzero `v`.

QuadraticForm.globalInvariants_hasseProd.doc:
**The Hasse product formula.** For every regular form `Q` over a number field `K`, the
product of the finite Hasse signs and of the real Hasse signs of `Q` is `1`.

QuadraticForm.globalInvariants.doc:
**The system of local invariants of a regular quadratic form** `Q` over a number field: its
rank, its plain discriminant `d(Q) ∈ Kˣ/(Kˣ)²`, its Hasse sign at every finite place and its
positive index at every real place.

**Witt decomposition** for a regular form: a nondegenerate quadratic form on a
finite-dimensional space is isometric to the orthogonal sum of `m` hyperbolic planes and an
anisotropic diagonal form, and `m` is the Witt index of its class.

QuadraticForm.equivalent_iff_sigPos_eq_a.doc:
**Sylvester's law of inertia** for regular forms: two nondegenerate real quadratic forms are
isometric exactly when their signatures agree.

QuadraticForm.equivalent_iff_finrank_eq_.signature:
QuadraticForm.equivalent_iff_finrank_eq_and_sigPos_eq_and_sigNeg_eq.{u_1, u_2} {M : Type u_1}

QuadraticForm.equivalent_iff_finrank_eq_.doc:
**Sylvester's law of inertia**, classification form: two real quadratic forms on
finite-dimensional spaces are isometric exactly when their dimensions agree and both indices of
inertia agree.  The dimension is a genuine third condition: it records the number of zero weights
in a diagonalization, which the two indices do not see.

QuadraticForm.equivalent_atRealPlace_iff.doc:
**Sylvester's law of inertia at a real place.** Two regular quadratic forms become isometric
at a real place exactly when their signatures there agree.

QuadraticAlgebra.span_natCast_omega_sub_.doc:
**Dedekind's criterion for a quadratic order.** Let `r` be a root of `X² - b X - a` modulo
`p`, so that `b - r` is the second root. Then `p` factors as `(p) = (p, ω - r) (p, ω - (b - r))`
in `ℤ[ω]` if and only if `p` does not divide both the derivative `2r - b` and the quotient
`(r² - b r - a)/p`, that is, unless `p ∣ 2r - b` and `p² ∣ r² - b r - a`.

QuadraticAlgebra.ringHom_eq_or_eq_conjug.doc:
**The two complex embeddings of an imaginary quadratic field.** For a nonsquare `a ≤ 0`, every
complex embedding of the field `QuadraticAlgebra ℚ a 0` is the distinguished embedding or its
complex conjugate.

QuadraticAlgebra.nrComplexPlaces_eq_one.doc: An imaginary quadratic field has exactly one complex place, so its signature is `(0, 1)`.

QuadraticAlgebra.complexEmbedding.doc:
**The distinguished complex embedding of `ℚ(√a)`** for `a ≤ 0`: the `ℚ`-algebra map
`QuadraticAlgebra ℚ a 0 →ₐ[ℚ] ℂ` sending `ω` to `√(-a) · i`, the square root of `a` with
nonnegative imaginary part.

Projectivization.instIsManifold.doc:
Projective space over a nontrivially normed field, with its standard affine charts, is a
`C^r` manifold for every `r`; for `r = ω` it is an analytic manifold. Over `ℂ` this is the
standard complex manifold structure on `ℂℙⁿ`.

ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun.mgf_sum_le_e.doc:
**Bernstein's moment-generating-function bound for independent sums.** If the `Xᵢ`, `i ∈ s`,
are independent with mean zero, finite second moments and `Xᵢ ≤ b` almost surely, then for
`0 ≤ t` with `t * b < 3` the moment-generating function of `∑ i ∈ s, Xᵢ` at `t` is at most
`exp (v * t ^ 2 / (2 * (1 - t * b / 3)))`, where `v = ∑ i ∈ s, E Xᵢ²`.

ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun.measureReal_.doc:
**One-sided sub-exponential Bernstein inequality.** For independent centered variables with
common parameter `K`, this bounds the upper tail of a finite sum.

**Bernstein's inequality.** Let the `Xᵢ`, `i ∈ s`, be independent with mean zero, finite
second moments and `Xᵢ ≤ b` almost surely, and let `v = ∑ i ∈ s, E Xᵢ²`. Then for `0 ≤ ε`,
`P(ε ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, Xᵢ) ≤ exp (-ε ^ 2 / (2 * (v + b * ε / 3)))`.

**Sub-exponential Bernstein inequality.** If the `Xᵢ`, `i ∈ s`, are independent, centered
and sub-exponential with common parameter `K`, then for `t > 0`

`P(|∑ i ∈ s, Xᵢ| ≥ t) ≤ 2 * exp (-t^2 / (4 * (|s| * K^2 + K * t)))`.

The constants follow directly from the centered MGF bound `E exp (λ Xᵢ) ≤ exp (K ^ 2 * λ ^ 2)`
for `|λ| ≤ 1 / K`.

**Bernstein's inequality, two-sided form.** Let the `Xᵢ`, `i ∈ s`, be independent and
almost-everywhere measurable with mean zero and `|Xᵢ| ≤ b` almost surely, and let
`v = ∑ i ∈ s, E Xᵢ²`. Then for `0 ≤ ε`,
`P(ε ≤ |∑ i ∈ s, Xᵢ|) ≤ 2 * exp (-ε ^ 2 / (2 * (v + b * ε / 3)))`.

ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.pow_apply_singl.doc:
**Chapman–Kolmogorov lower bound.** The `m + n`-step mass of a measurable set `s` is at least
the mass of the paths that sit at the intermediate state `y` at time `m`.

ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.markovChainKern.signature:
ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.markovChainKernel.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace α]
  (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α) [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] :
  ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α (ℕ → α)
ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.markovChainKern.doc:
**The path-law kernel of a homogeneous Markov chain**: the kernel sending a state `x` to the law
`markovChainLaw (Measure.dirac x) κ` of the chain started at `x` (`markovChainKernel_apply`). Being
a kernel, it records that this law depends measurably on the starting state, and every path law of
the chain is its mixture over the initial law (`markovChainLaw_eq_comp`).

ProbabilityTheory.IsGaussian.lintegral_e.doc:
**The Maurey–Pisier inequality.** For a centred Gaussian measure `μ` and a `C¹` function `f`,
`∫∫ exp (t (f y - f x)) dμ(x) dμ(y) ≤ ∫ exp (π² t² / 8 · Var[f' x; μ]) dμ(x)`.

ProbabilityTheory.CondIndepFun.exists_in.signature:
ProbabilityTheory.CondIndepFun.exists_independent_coding.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {Ω : Type u_1}

ProbabilityTheory.CondIndepFun.exists_in.doc:
**Conditional independence as a functional representation.** If `X` and `Y` are conditionally
independent given `Z`, then their joint law with `Z` is obtained by keeping `Z` and applying two
measurable coding functions to separate uniform coordinates. When `μ` is a probability measure,
the noises are independent both of one another and of the original sample carrying `Z`.

PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.IsCombinato.doc:
The weak realization of a positive-dimensional combinatorial manifold is a PL manifold,
possibly with boundary: it has an atlas modelled on the half-space in `(Fin n → ℝ) × ℝ` whose
chart transitions lie in the PL groupoid. No finiteness or countability of the complex is
assumed.

PowerSeries.radius_inv_eq_limsup.signature:
PowerSeries.radius_inv_eq_limsup.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [NormedRing R] {f : PowerSeries R} :

PowerSeries.radius_inv_eq_limsup.doc:
**Cauchy–Hadamard formula**: the inverse of the radius of `∑ aₙ Xⁿ` is
`limsup ‖aₙ‖ ^ (1 / n)`.

PowerSeries.radius_eq_liminf.signature:
PowerSeries.radius_eq_liminf.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [NormedRing R] {f : PowerSeries R} :

PowerSeries.radius_eq_liminf.doc:
**Cauchy–Hadamard formula**, `liminf` form: the radius of `∑ aₙ Xⁿ` is
`liminf 1 / ‖aₙ‖ ^ (1 / n)`.

PowerSeries.norm_coeff_colemanDBounded_trunc_le.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [NormedCommRing R]
  [NormOneClass R] [IsUltrametricDist R] {F B : PowerSeries R} {ρ : ℕ → ℝ}
  (hρ₀ : ∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ ρ i) (hρ : Antitone ρ)
  (hF : ∀ (j : ℕ), ‖(PowerSeries.coeff j) F‖ ≤ ∏ i ∈ Finset.range j, ρ i)
  (hB : ∀ (i : ℕ), PowerSeries.IsRestricted (ρ i) B) (hB₀ : (PowerSeries.coeff 0) B = 0)

  ‖(((PowerSeries.trunc a) B).colemanDBounded ((PowerSeries.trunc b) F) n m).coeff k‖ ≤

PowerSeries.norm_coeff_colemanDBounded_t.doc:
**Coleman's bound for truncations.** Let `ρ` be a nonnegative antitone Newton majorant of a
power series `F`, `‖coeff j F‖ ≤ ∏ i < j, ρ i`, and let `B` be restricted at every radius `ρ i`
with `B(0) = 0`. Then the Coleman transforms of the truncations of `F` along the truncations of
`B` satisfy `‖coeff k D_(n,m)(trunc a B, trunc b F)‖ ≤ ∏ i < k, β_B(ρ i)`, uniformly in the ranks,
degree bounds and truncation orders. In particular this bounds
`D_(N,M)(trunc (M + 1) B, trunc (N + 1) F)`.

PowerSeries.henselianLocalRing.signature: PowerSeries.henselianLocalRing.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] : HenselianLocalRing (PowerSeries K)
PowerSeries.henselianLocalRing.doc:
**Hensel's lemma for `K⟦t⟧`.** Over a field `K`, the power series ring `K⟦t⟧` is a Henselian
local ring. If `a₀` is a root modulo `t` of a monic polynomial `f` with `f' (a₀)` a unit, its
constant coefficient `c` is a simple root of the reduction of `f`, which therefore factors as
`(X - c) * h` with `X - c` coprime to `h`; lifting this factorization
(`Polynomial.Monic.exists_monic_mul_eq_of_isCoprime`) gives a linear factor `X - a` of `f` with
`a ≡ a₀ mod t`.

PowerSeries.height_eq_one_iff_of_isDiscr.doc:
**The height-one primes of `O⟦X⟧`.** Over a discrete valuation ring `O` with uniformiser `ϖ`,
complete for its maximal ideal, a prime ideal of `O⟦X⟧` has height one if and only if it is
generated by `C ϖ` or by an irreducible polynomial distinguished at the maximal ideal.
