  (hrow :
    ∀ (n : ℕ),
      HasSum (fun m => (PowerSeries.coeff m) ((PowerSeries.hasseDeriv n) f) • a ^ m)
        (((PowerSeries.hasseDeriv n) f).evalAt a)) :
  (PowerSeries.taylor a f).evalAt b = f.evalAt (b + a)
PowerSeries.evalAt_taylor_of_summable.doc:
**The Taylor identity from the double series.** If the double series
`∑ₙ,ₘ coeff m (Δⁿ f) aᵐ bⁿ` is summable and each of its rows `∑ₘ coeff m (Δⁿ f) aᵐ` converges to
`(Δⁿ f)(a)`, then the Taylor translate at `a` evaluated at `b` is `f(b + a)`. Grouping the terms
by `n` gives the translate at `b`, and grouping them by `n + m` gives `f` at `b + a`, by the
binomial theorem.

PowerSeries.aeval_multiset_esymm_add_mul.signature:
PowerSeries.aeval_multiset_esymm_add_multiplicativeSequence.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R]
  (Q : PowerSeries R) (n k : ℕ) {S : Type u_2} [CommSemiring S] [Algebra R S] {m : ℕ}
  (s t : Multiset S) (hs : s.card = n) (ht : t.card = m) :
  (MvPolynomial.aeval fun j => (s + t).esymm (↑j + 1)) (Q.multiplicativeSequence (n + m) k) =
    ∑ p ∈ Finset.HasAntidiagonal.antidiagonal k,
      (MvPolynomial.aeval fun j => s.esymm (↑j + 1)) (Q.multiplicativeSequence n p.1) *
        (MvPolynomial.aeval fun j => t.esymm (↑j + 1)) (Q.multiplicativeSequence m p.2)
PowerSeries.aeval_multiset_esymm_add_mul.doc:
**The Whitney formula for roots**: on the union of a family `s` of `n` roots and a family `t`
of `m` roots, `Kₖ` is the convolution of the values of the multiplicative sequence on `s` and
on `t`.

PowerSeries.IsWeierstrassFactorizationAt.doc:
For a Weierstrass factorization `g = f * h`, the power basis of `A⟦X⟧ ⧸ (g)` over `A`
generated by the class of `X`: the classes of `1, X, …, X ^ (deg f - 1)` form a basis. It is the
monic power basis of `A[X] ⧸ (f)` transported along `algEquivQuotient`.

PowerSeries.IsRestricted.norm_evalAt_le_.doc:
**The Schwarz lemma for distinct zeros with multiplicities.** Let `f` be a power series over a
complete ultrametric normed field `K`, restricted at a radius `c > 0`, and let `s` be a finite set
of points of the closed disc of radius `c` at each of which the Hasse derivatives `(D⁽ᵗ⁾ f)(b)`
vanish for `t < T b`. Then at every point `x` of the closed disc of radius `c` in a complete normed
field extension `L` of `K`,

```text
‖f(x)‖ ≤ ‖f‖_c * ∏_{b ∈ s} (‖x - b‖ / c) ^ T b.
```

PowerSeries.IsRestricted.norm_evalAt_le_.signature:
PowerSeries.IsRestricted.norm_evalAt_le_gaussNorm_mul_prod.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [NormedField K]
  [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] {c : ℝ} {f : PowerSeries K} [DecidableEq K] {L : Type u_2}
  [NormedField L] [NormedAlgebra K L] [CompleteSpace L] (hf : PowerSeries.IsRestricted c f)
  (hc : 0 < c) {Z : Multiset K} (hZ : ∀ b ∈ Z, ‖b‖ ≤ c)
  (hzero : ∀ b ∈ Z, ∀ t < Multiset.count b Z, ((PowerSeries.hasseDeriv t) f).evalAt b = 0) {x : L}
  (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ c) :
  ‖f.evalAt x‖ ≤
    PowerSeries.gaussNorm norm c f * (Multiset.map (fun b => ‖x - (algebraMap K L) b‖ / c) Z).prod
PowerSeries.IsRestricted.norm_evalAt_le_.doc:
**The Schwarz lemma for restricted series.** Let `f` be a power series over a complete
ultrametric normed field `K`, restricted at a radius `c > 0`. Let `Z` be a finite multiset of
points of the closed disc of radius `c` such that `f` vanishes at each `b ∈ Z` to at least the
multiplicity of `b` in `Z`, in the sense that the Hasse derivatives `(D⁽ᵗ⁾ f)(b)` vanish for `t`
below that multiplicity. Then at every point `x` of the closed disc of radius `c` in a complete
normed field extension `L` of `K`,

```text
‖f(x)‖ ≤ ‖f‖_c * ∏_{b ∈ Z} ‖x - b‖ / c,
```

where `‖f‖_c` is the Gauss norm of `f` at `c`.

PowerSeries.IsRestricted.norm_evalAt_le_.signature:
PowerSeries.IsRestricted.norm_evalAt_le_gaussNorm_mul_norm_prod.{u_1} {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)]
  {K : Type u_1} [NormedField K] [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[p] K] [CompleteSpace K] {c : ℝ}
  {f : PowerSeries K} (hf : PowerSeries.IsRestricted c f) (hc : 1 ≤ c) {s : Finset ℤ_[p]} {T : ℕ}
  (hzero : ∀ b ∈ s, ∀ t < T, ((PowerSeries.hasseDeriv t) f).evalAt ((algebraMap ℚ_[p] K) ↑b) = 0)
  (x : ℤ_[p]) :
  ‖f.evalAt ((algebraMap ℚ_[p] K) ↑x)‖ ≤
    PowerSeries.gaussNorm norm c f * (‖∏ b ∈ s, (x - b)‖ / c ^ s.card) ^ T
PowerSeries.IsRestricted.norm_evalAt_le_.doc:
**The Schwarz lemma on a grid of `p`-adic integers.** Let `K` be a complete normed field
extension of `ℚ_p` and `f` a power series over `K` restricted at a radius `c ≥ 1`. If the Hasse
derivatives `(D⁽ᵗ⁾ f)(b)` vanish for `t < T` at every point `b` of a finite set `s` of `p`-adic
integers, then at every `p`-adic integer `x`

```text
‖f(x)‖ ≤ ‖f‖_c * (‖∏_{b ∈ s} (x - b)‖ / c ^ #s) ^ T.
```

**The Schwarz lemma on the integers not divisible by `q`.** Let `K` be a complete normed field
extension of `ℚ_p`, `f` a power series over `K` restricted at a radius `c ≥ 1`, and `q` an integer
prime to `p`. If the Hasse derivatives `(D⁽ᵗ⁾ f)(j)` vanish for `t < T` at every integer
`0 ≤ j < N` not divisible by `q`, a grid of `S` points, then at every `p`-adic integer `x`

```text
‖f(x)‖ ≤ ‖f‖_c * (‖⌊N / q⌋!‖ ^ (q - 1) / c ^ S) ^ T.
```

PowerSeries.IsRestricted.norm_evalAt_le_.signature:
PowerSeries.IsRestricted.norm_evalAt_le_gaussNorm_mul_norm_factorial.{u_1} {p : ℕ}
  [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {K : Type u_1} [NormedField K] [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[p] K] [CompleteSpace K]
  {c : ℝ} {f : PowerSeries K} (hf : PowerSeries.IsRestricted c f) (hc : 1 ≤ c) (a : ℤ_[p])
  {d : ℤ_[p]} (hd : IsUnit d) {n T : ℕ}
  (hzero :
    ∀ j < n,
      ∀ t < T, ((PowerSeries.hasseDeriv t) f).evalAt ((algebraMap ℚ_[p] K) ↑(a + ↑j * d)) = 0)
  (x : ℤ_[p]) :
  ‖f.evalAt ((algebraMap ℚ_[p] K) ↑x)‖ ≤
    PowerSeries.gaussNorm norm c f * (‖↑n.factorial‖ / c ^ n) ^ T
PowerSeries.IsRestricted.norm_evalAt_le_.doc:
**The Schwarz lemma on a progression of `p`-adic integers.** Let `K` be a complete normed field
extension of `ℚ_p` and `f` a power series over `K` restricted at a radius `c ≥ 1`. If the Hasse
derivatives `(D⁽ᵗ⁾ f)(a + j d)` vanish for `t < T` and `j < n`, where `d` is a unit of `ℤ_p`, then
at every `p`-adic integer `x`

```text
‖f(x)‖ ≤ ‖f‖_c * (‖n!‖ / c ^ n) ^ T.
```

PowerSeries.IsRestricted.norm_evalAt_add.signature:
PowerSeries.IsRestricted.norm_evalAt_add_le_max.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [NormedCommRing R]
  [IsUltrametricDist R] {c : ℝ} {f : PowerSeries R} {a : R} [CompleteSpace R]
  (hf : PowerSeries.IsRestricted c f) (hc : 0 < c) (ha : ‖a‖ ≤ c) {y : R} (hy : ‖y‖ ≤ c) {T : ℕ}
  {ε : ℝ} (h : ∀ t < T, ‖((PowerSeries.hasseDeriv t) f).evalAt a‖ * ‖y‖ ^ t ≤ ε) :
  ‖f.evalAt (y + a)‖ ≤ max ε (PowerSeries.gaussNorm norm c f * (‖y‖ / c) ^ T)
PowerSeries.IsRestricted.norm_evalAt_add.doc:
**The Taylor remainder estimate.** Over a complete ultrametric normed ring, let `f` be
restricted at a radius `c > 0` and let `‖a‖ ≤ c`, `‖y‖ ≤ c`. If `ε` bounds the first `T` terms
`‖(Δᵗ f)(a)‖ ‖y‖ᵗ`, `t < T`, of the expansion of `f` at `a`, then

```text
‖f(y + a)‖ ≤ max ε (‖f‖_c * (‖y‖ / c) ^ T).
```

For `ε = 0` this is the Schwarz lemma at a single zero of order `T`.

PowerSeries.IsRestricted.evalAt_taylor.signature:
PowerSeries.IsRestricted.evalAt_taylor.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [NormedCommRing R] [IsUltrametricDist R]
  {c : ℝ} {f : PowerSeries R} {a b : R} [CompleteSpace R] (hf : PowerSeries.IsRestricted c f)
  (ha : ‖a‖ ≤ c) (hb : ‖b‖ ≤ c) : (PowerSeries.taylor a f).evalAt b = f.evalAt (b + a)
PowerSeries.IsRestricted.evalAt_taylor.doc:
**The Taylor identity for restricted series.** Over a complete ultrametric normed ring, if `f`
is restricted at the radius `c` and `‖a‖ ≤ c`, `‖b‖ ≤ c`, then the expansion of `f` at `a`
evaluated at `b` is `f(b + a)`.

PowerSeries.IsRestricted.evalAt_eq_zero_.signature:
PowerSeries.IsRestricted.evalAt_eq_zero_iff.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [NormedCommRing R] [NormOneClass R]
  [IsUltrametricDist R] [CompleteSpace R] {c : ℝ} {f : PowerSeries R}
  (hf : PowerSeries.IsRestricted c f) (hc : 0 < c) {a : R} (ha : ‖a‖ ≤ c) :
  f.evalAt a = 0 ↔ ∃ q, PowerSeries.IsRestricted c q ∧ f = (PowerSeries.X - PowerSeries.C a) * q
PowerSeries.IsRestricted.evalAt_eq_zero_.doc:
**Factor theorem for restricted series.** Over a complete ultrametric normed commutative ring,
a series restricted at a radius `c > 0` vanishes at a point `a` of the closed disc of radius `c`
exactly when it is `X - a` times a series restricted at `c`.

PowerSeries.IsGoodZero.signature:
PowerSeries.IsGoodZero.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R] (f : PowerSeries R)
  (a : R) (h : ℕ) : Prop
PowerSeries.IsGoodZero.doc:
A power series `f` has a **good zero of order `h`** at `a` if its Hasse derivatives of order
less than `h` vanish at `a` and its Hasse derivative of order `h` is a unit at `a`. For `h = 0`
this says that `f(a)` is a unit. Values at `a` are the infinite sums `PowerSeries.evalAt`, so the
notion is meaningful for entire series over a complete normed ring.

PowerSeries.IsEntire.tendsto_norm_coeff_.signature:
PowerSeries.IsEntire.tendsto_norm_coeff_rpow_inv_natCast.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [NormedRing R]
  {F : PowerSeries R} (hF : F.IsEntire) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ‖(PowerSeries.coeff n) F‖ ^ (↑n)⁻¹) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
PowerSeries.IsEntire.tendsto_norm_coeff_.doc:
**Cauchy–Hadamard for entire series.** The `n`-th roots `‖aₙ‖ ^ (1 / n)` of the coefficient
norms of an entire series tend to zero.

PowerSeries.IsEntire.evalAt_taylor.doc:
**The Taylor identity.** For an entire series `f`, the Taylor translate at `a` evaluated at
`b` is `f(b + a)`.

PowerSeries.IsEntire.evalAt_eq_zero_iff.doc:
**Factor theorem for entire series.** An entire series vanishes at `a` exactly when it is
`X - a` times an entire series.

PositiveLinearMap.law_integralPositiveLi.signature:
PositiveLinearMap.law_integralPositiveLinearMap_comap_restrict_id {K : Set ℝ} [CompactSpace ↑K]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hμ : μ Kᶜ = 0) :
  (ContinuousMap.integralPositiveLinearMap (MeasureTheory.Measure.comap Subtype.val μ)).law
      (ContinuousMap.realToRCLike ℂ (ContinuousMap.restrict K (ContinuousMap.id ℝ))) =
    μ
PositiveLinearMap.law_integralPositiveLi.doc:
**Realization of compactly supported laws.** A finite measure `μ` on `ℝ` concentrated on a
compact set `K` is the law of the coordinate function `x ↦ x` in the commutative C⋆-algebra
`C(K, ℂ)`, with respect to integration against `μ` on `K`. This functional is a state when `μ` is
a probability measure (`ContinuousMap.integralPositiveLinearMap_one`).

PositiveLinearMap.law_eq_law_iff_forall_.signature:
PositiveLinearMap.law_eq_law_iff_forall_apply_pow.{u_1, u_2} {A : Type u_1} [CStarAlgebra A]
  [PartialOrder A] [StarOrderedRing A] (φ : A →ₚ[ℂ] ℂ) {a : A} {B : Type u_2} [CStarAlgebra B]
  [PartialOrder B] [StarOrderedRing B] (ψ : B →ₚ[ℂ] ℂ) {b : B} (ha : IsSelfAdjoint a)
  (hb : IsSelfAdjoint b) : φ.law a = ψ.law b ↔ ∀ (n : ℕ), φ (a ^ n) = ψ (b ^ n)
PositiveLinearMap.law_eq_law_iff_forall_.doc:
Two selfadjoint elements, possibly in different C⋆-algebras and with respect to different
positive functionals, have the same law exactly when they have the same moments:
`μ_a = μ_b ↔ ∀ n, φ (a ^ n) = ψ (b ^ n)`.

PositiveLinearMap.law.signature:
PositiveLinearMap.law.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [CStarAlgebra A] [PartialOrder A] [StarOrderedRing A]
  (φ : A →ₚ[ℂ] ℂ) (a : A) : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ
PositiveLinearMap.law.doc:
The **law** `μ_a` of an element `a` of a C⋆-algebra with respect to a positive linear
functional `φ`: for selfadjoint `a`, the finite Borel measure on `ℝ`, concentrated on
`spectrum ℝ a` (`law_compl_spectrum`), with `∫ f dμ_a = φ (cfc f a)` for every `f` continuous on
the spectrum (`ofReal_integral_law`), and characterized by this property (`eq_law_iff`). For `a`
not selfadjoint it is the zero measure (`law_of_not_isSelfAdjoint`).

PolynomialLaw.coeff.doc:
The coefficients of polynomial laws `M →ₚₗ[R] N` at the generic combination `∑ⱼ Xⱼ ⊗ mⱼ`:
`coeff m f k` is the coefficient of the monomial `Xᵏ` in `f (∑ⱼ Xⱼ ⊗ mⱼ)`, computed over the
polynomial ring `R[Xⱼ]`.

PolynomialLaw.algHomEquiv.doc:
Algebra maps `A →ₐ[R] B` are identified with the multiplicative polynomial laws
`A →ₚₗ[R] B` homogeneous of degree one, by `φ ↦ φ.toLinearMap.toPolynomialLaw` with inverse
`IsHomogeneousOfDegree.toAlgHom`.

PolynomialLaw.IsMultiplicative.signature:
PolynomialLaw.IsMultiplicative.{u, u_1, u_2} {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R] {A : Type u_1}
  {B : Type u_2} [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] [Semiring B] [Algebra R B] (f : A →ₚₗ[R] B) : Prop
PolynomialLaw.IsMultiplicative.doc:
A polynomial law `f : A →ₚₗ[R] B` between `R`-algebras is multiplicative if `f 1 = 1` and
`f (x * y) = f x * f y` for every commutative `R`-algebra `S` and all `x y : S ⊗[R] A`. See
`IsMultiplicative.toFun_one` and `IsMultiplicative.toFun_mul` for algebras in other universes.

Polynomial.taylorExp_smul_derivative'.signature:
Polynomial.taylorExp_smul_derivative'.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] [Algebra ℚ R] (r : R) :
  (r • Polynomial.derivative').taylorExp ⋯ = Polynomial.taylorAlgHom r
Polynomial.taylorExp_smul_derivative'.doc:
**Taylor's formula for polynomials.** Over a `ℚ`-algebra, the Taylor exponential of the
scaled derivative `r • d / dX` is the Taylor shift `p ↦ p (X + r)`.

Polynomial.tarskiQuery_eq_signVariations.signature:
Polynomial.tarskiQuery_eq_signVariationsAtBot_sub_signVariationsAtTop.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [Field R]
  [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] [IsRealClosed R] (p q : Polynomial R) :
  p.tarskiQuery q =
    ↑(TauCeti.Sturm.signVariationsAtBot (p.sturmSeq (Polynomial.derivative p * q))) -
      ↑(TauCeti.Sturm.signVariationsAtTop (p.sturmSeq (Polynomial.derivative p * q)))
Polynomial.tarskiQuery_eq_signVariations.doc:
**Sturm–Tarski on the whole line.** The Tarski query of `q` at the distinct roots of `p` is
the drop in sign variations from `-∞` to `+∞` of the Sturm sequence of `p` and `p' * q`. No
squarefreeness assumption is needed. For `p = 0` both sides are zero.

Polynomial.subresultant_eq_zero_of_getEl.signature:
Polynomial.subresultant_eq_zero_of_getElem?_sturmSeq.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [DecidableEq K]
  {p q s t : Polynomial K} {m i j : ℕ} (hp : p.natDegree ≤ m) (hs : (p.sturmSeq q)[i + 1]? = some s)
  (ht : (p.sturmSeq q)[i + 2]? = some t) (htj : t.natDegree < j) (hjs : j + 1 < s.natDegree) :
  p.subresultant q m q.natDegree j = 0
Polynomial.subresultant_eq_zero_of_getEl.doc:
**Structure theorem for subresultants**, degree gap. For consecutive entries `s, t` of the
signed remainder sequence of `p` and `q` after the first, the subresultants of `p` and `q` at
the indices strictly between `deg t` and `deg s - 1` vanish.

Polynomial.splits_of_nodup_newtonSlopes.signature:
Polynomial.splits_of_nodup_newtonSlopes.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [NormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K]
  [CompleteSpace K] (v : AddValuation K (WithTop ℝ)) {b : ℝ} (hb : 1 < b)
  (hv : ∀ (x : K), x ≠ 0 → ‖x‖ = b ^ (-(v x).untop₀)) {f : Polynomial K}
  (hf : (f.newtonSlopes v).Nodup) : f.Splits
Polynomial.splits_of_nodup_newtonSlopes.doc:
**Distinct-slopes splitting theorem.** Over a complete ultrametric normed field, any polynomial
whose finite Newton slopes have multiplicity one splits into linear factors over the base field.

Polynomial.rootMultiplicity_mul_logHeigh.signature:
Polynomial.rootMultiplicity_mul_logHeight₁_le.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (P : Polynomial K) (β : K) :
  ↑(Polynomial.rootMultiplicity β P) * Height.logHeight₁ β ≤
    P.logHeight + ↑(Module.finrank ℚ K) * ↑P.natDegree * Real.log 2
Polynomial.rootMultiplicity_mul_logHeigh.doc:
**Roth's lemma in one variable**, multiplicity form: the multiplicity of a root `β` of a
polynomial `P` over a number field, times the relative logarithmic height of `β`, is at most
`h(P) + [K : ℚ] * deg P * log 2`. The zero polynomial has root multiplicity zero.

Polynomial.preimage_thomEncoding_subsing.signature:
Polynomial.preimage_thomEncoding_subsingleton_or_eq_Ioo.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [Field R]
  [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] [IsRealClosed R] (p : Polynomial R)
  (τ : Fin p.natDegree → SignType) :
  (p.thomEncoding ⁻¹' {τ}).Subsingleton ∨ ∃ a b, p.thomEncoding ⁻¹' {τ} = {x | a < ↑x ∧ ↑x < b}
Polynomial.preimage_thomEncoding_subsing.doc:
**Thom's lemma for finite Thom encodings.** For any signs `τ` prescribed for the
derivatives of orders `1, …, natDegree p`, the set of points where `p` realizes them is empty,
a single point, or an open interval with endpoints `a ∈ WithBot R` and `b ∈ WithTop R`.

Polynomial.preimage_derivativeSign_subsi.doc:
**Thom's lemma.** For any signs `σ k` prescribed for the derivatives of every order of `p`,
including order zero, the set of points where `p` realizes them is empty, a single point, or an
open interval with endpoints `a ∈ WithBot R` and `b ∈ WithTop R`.

Polynomial.norm_hermiteIntegral_le.doc:
**Hermite's estimate**: if `C` bounds `‖f‖` on the closed disc of radius `‖z‖`, then
`‖F_f(z)‖ ≤ ‖z‖ exp ‖z‖ C`.

Polynomial.norm_coeff_colemanDBounded_le.signature:
Polynomial.norm_coeff_colemanDBounded_le.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [SeminormedCommRing R]
  {B P : Polynomial R} {n m : ℕ} [NormOneClass R] [IsUltrametricDist R] {ρ β : ℕ → ℝ}
  (hB₀ : B.coeff 0 = 0) (hρ₀ : ∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ ρ i) (hρ : Antitone ρ)
  (hP : ∀ j ≤ n, ‖P.coeff j‖ ≤ ∏ i ∈ Finset.range j, ρ i)
  (hβ : ∀ (t j : ℕ), ‖B.coeff (j + 1)‖ * ρ t ^ (j + 1) ≤ β t) (k : ℕ) :
  ‖(B.colemanDBounded P n m).coeff k‖ ≤ ∏ t ∈ Finset.range k, β t
Polynomial.norm_coeff_colemanDBounded_le.doc:
**Coleman's coefficient bound.** Let `P` and `B` be polynomials over an ultrametric seminormed
ring with `‖1‖ = 1` and `B(0) = 0`. If `ρ` is a nonnegative antitone sequence with
`‖coeff j P‖ ≤ ∏ i < j, ρ i` for `j ≤ n`, and `‖coeff l B‖ * ρ t ^ l ≤ β t` for every `t` and every
`l ≥ 1`, then the `k`-th coefficient of Coleman's transform `D_(n,m)(B, P)` has norm at most
`∏ t < k, β t`, for all ranks `n` and degree bounds `m`.

Polynomial.mul_dvd_eval_sub_eval_sub_mul.signature:
Polynomial.mul_dvd_eval_sub_eval_sub_mul.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (f : Polynomial R)
  {d e t x x' : R} (hx : d ∣ x - t) (hde : d ∣ e) (hxx' : e ∣ x' - x) :
  d * e ∣
    Polynomial.eval x' f - Polynomial.eval x f -
      Polynomial.eval t (Polynomial.derivative f) * (x' - x)
Polynomial.mul_dvd_eval_sub_eval_sub_mul.doc:
**Taylor's estimate.** If `d ∣ x - t`, `d ∣ e` and `e ∣ x' - x`, then the derivative at `t`
linearises the polynomial `f` from `x` to `x'` up to an error divisible by `d * e`.

Polynomial.linearIndependent_iff_hasseWr.signature:
Polynomial.linearIndependent_iff_hasseWronskian_ne_zero.{u_3} {m : ℕ} {K : Type u_3} [Field K]
  [CharZero K] {g : Fin m → Polynomial K} : LinearIndependent K g ↔ Polynomial.hasseWronskian g ≠ 0
Polynomial.linearIndependent_iff_hasseWr.doc:
**The Wronskian criterion.** Over a field of characteristic zero, a family of polynomials is
linearly independent if and only if its Hasse Wronskian is nonzero.

Polynomial.irreducible_of_forall_mem_new.signature:
Polynomial.irreducible_of_forall_mem_newtonSlopes_eq_div.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  {v : AddValuation K (WithTop ℝ)} (hint : ∀ (x : K), x ≠ 0 → ∃ n, v x = ↑↑n) {f : Polynomial K}
  (hf : f.coeff 0 ≠ 0) (hdeg : 0 < f.natDegree) {a : ℤ} (hcop : a.natAbs.Coprime f.natDegree)
  (ha : ∀ m ∈ f.newtonSlopes v, m = ↑a / ↑f.natDegree) : Irreducible f
Polynomial.irreducible_of_forall_mem_new.doc:
**Newton polygon irreducibility criterion**, coprime form. If the valuation takes integer
values on nonzero elements, a polynomial `f` of degree `d > 0` with nonzero constant coefficient
whose finite slopes all equal `a / d`, for an integer `a` coprime to `d`, is irreducible.

Polynomial.irreducible_of_forall_mem_new.signature:
Polynomial.irreducible_of_forall_mem_newtonSlopes_eq.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  {v : AddValuation K (WithTop ℝ)} (hint : ∀ (x : K), x ≠ 0 → ∃ n, v x = ↑↑n) {f : Polynomial K}
  (hf : f.coeff 0 ≠ 0) {q : ℚ} (hq : ∀ m ∈ f.newtonSlopes v, m = ↑q) (hden : q.den = f.natDegree) :
  Irreducible f
Polynomial.irreducible_of_forall_mem_new.doc:
**Newton polygon irreducibility criterion.** If the valuation takes integer values on
nonzero elements, a polynomial `f` with nonzero constant coefficient whose finite slopes all
equal a rational number `q`, and whose degree is the denominator of `q`, is irreducible.

Polynomial.inv_le_norm_ratCast_sub.signature:
Polynomial.inv_le_norm_ratCast_sub (f : Polynomial ℤ) {α : ℂ}
  (hα : (Polynomial.map (Int.castRingHom ℂ) f).IsRoot α) {ξ : ℚ} (hξ : (Polynomial.aeval ξ) f ≠ 0) :
  (2 ^ (f.natDegree - 1) * (Polynomial.map (Int.castRingHom ℂ) f).mahlerMeasure *
        Height.mulHeight₁ ξ ^ f.natDegree)⁻¹ ≤
    ‖↑ξ - α‖
Polynomial.inv_le_norm_ratCast_sub.doc:
**Liouville's inequality.** Let `f ∈ ℤ[X]` have degree `d` and a complex root `α`. Every
rational number `ξ` with `f(ξ) ≠ 0` satisfies `|ξ - α| ≥ (2 ^ (d - 1) M(f) H(ξ) ^ d)⁻¹`, where
`M(f)` is the Mahler measure of `f` and `H(ξ)` the height of `ξ`.

Polynomial.hermiteIntegral_eq_sumIDeriv.signature:
Polynomial.hermiteIntegral_eq_sumIDeriv (f : Polynomial ℂ) (z : ℂ) :
  f.hermiteIntegral z =
    Complex.exp z * Polynomial.eval 0 (Polynomial.sumIDeriv f) -
      Polynomial.eval z (Polynomial.sumIDeriv f)
Polynomial.hermiteIntegral_eq_sumIDeriv.doc:
**Hermite's identity**: integration by parts evaluates Hermite's integral as
`F_f(z) = exp z * (sumIDeriv f)(0) - (sumIDeriv f)(z)`.

Polynomial.finite_setOf_natDegree_le_sup.signature:
Polynomial.finite_setOf_natDegree_le_supNorm_le (n : ℕ) (B : ℝ) :
  {P | P.natDegree ≤ n ∧ P.supNorm ≤ B}.Finite
Polynomial.finite_setOf_natDegree_le_sup.doc:
**Northcott's theorem for integer polynomials.** Only finitely many integer polynomials
have degree at most `n` and coefficient sup norm (naive height) at most `B`.

Polynomial.exists_subresultant_natDegree.signature:
Polynomial.exists_subresultant_natDegree_sub_one_eq_C_mul_of_getElem?_sturmSeq.{u_1} {K : Type u_1}
  [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {p q s t : Polynomial K} {m i : ℕ} (hp : p.natDegree ≤ m)
  (hq : i = 0 → q.natDegree ≤ m) (hs : (p.sturmSeq q)[i + 1]? = some s)
  (ht : (p.sturmSeq q)[i + 2]? = some t) :
  ∃ c, c ≠ 0 ∧ p.subresultant q m q.natDegree (s.natDegree - 1) = Polynomial.C c * t
Polynomial.exists_subresultant_natDegree.doc:
**Structure theorem for subresultants**, upper index. For consecutive entries `s, t` of the
signed remainder sequence of `p` and `q` after the first, the subresultant of `p` and `q` at
index `deg s - 1` is a nonzero multiple of `t`. Only the initial pair additionally requires
`q.natDegree ≤ m`.

Polynomial.exists_subresultant_natDegree.signature:
Polynomial.exists_subresultant_natDegree_eq_C_mul_of_getElem?_sturmSeq.{u_1} {K : Type u_1}
  [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {p q s t : Polynomial K} {m i : ℕ} (hp : p.natDegree ≤ m)
  (hq : i = 0 → q.natDegree ≤ m) (hs : (p.sturmSeq q)[i + 1]? = some s)
  (ht : (p.sturmSeq q)[i + 2]? = some t) :
  ∃ c, c ≠ 0 ∧ p.subresultant q m q.natDegree t.natDegree = Polynomial.C c * t
Polynomial.exists_subresultant_natDegree.doc:
**Structure theorem for subresultants**, lower index. For consecutive entries `s, t` of the
signed remainder sequence of `p` and `q` after the first, the subresultant of `p` and `q` at
index `deg t` is a nonzero multiple of `t`. Only the initial pair additionally requires
`q.natDegree ≤ m`.

Polynomial.exists_isRoot_sub_mem.signature:
Polynomial.exists_isRoot_sub_mem.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] {J : Ideal R} [HenselianRing R J]
  (f : Polynomial R) {a₀ : R} (h₁ : Polynomial.eval a₀ f ∈ J)
  (h₂ : IsUnit ((Ideal.Quotient.mk J) (Polynomial.eval a₀ (Polynomial.derivative f)))) :
  ∃ a, f.IsRoot a ∧ a - a₀ ∈ J
Polynomial.exists_isRoot_sub_mem.doc:
**Hensel's lemma without monicity.** Over a Henselian pair `(R, J)`, a simple root of a
polynomial modulo `J` lifts to a root with the same image in `R ⧸ J`, whether or not the polynomial
is monic.

Polynomial.exists_isRoot_addVal_eval_eq.signature:
Polynomial.exists_isRoot_addVal_eval_eq.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
  [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [HenselianLocalRing A] (F : Polynomial A) (y₀ : A)
  (hlt :
    (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval y₀ (Polynomial.derivative F)) +
        (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval y₀ (Polynomial.derivative F)) <
      (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval y₀ F)) :
  ∃ z,
    F.IsRoot z ∧
      (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval y₀ F) =
        (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval y₀ (Polynomial.derivative F)) +
          (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (z - y₀)
Polynomial.exists_isRoot_addVal_eval_eq.doc:
**Hensel's lemma with an estimate** over a Henselian discrete valuation ring. If the order of
`F` at `y₀` exceeds twice the order of its derivative there, then `F` has a root `z` whose
distance to `y₀` has order exactly `addVal (F(y₀)) - addVal (F'(y₀))`. This is the existence
part of Mathlib's `hensels_lemma` in `addVal` spelling; the uniqueness of `z` in that ball is
`Polynomial.existsUnique_isRoot_addVal_lt`.

Polynomial.exists_C_entireResultant_eq.signature:
Polynomial.exists_C_entireResultant_eq.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [NormedCommRing R] [CompleteSpace R]
  {P : Polynomial R} {F : PowerSeries R} (hP : P.Monic) (hF : F.IsEntire) :
  ∃ G,
    G.IsEntire ∧
      ∃ H, H.degree < ↑P.natDegree ∧ PowerSeries.C (P.entireResultant F) = ↑P * G + ↑H * F
Polynomial.exists_C_entireResultant_eq.doc:
**The Bézout identity for the entire resultant.** For monic `P` and entire `F` there are an
entire series `G` and a polynomial `H` of degree less than `deg P` with
`Res(P, F) = P * G + H * F`.

Polynomial.existsUnique_isRoot_addVal_lt.signature:
Polynomial.existsUnique_isRoot_addVal_lt.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
  [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [HenselianLocalRing A] (F : Polynomial A) (y₀ : A)
  (hlt :
    (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval y₀ (Polynomial.derivative F)) +
        (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval y₀ (Polynomial.derivative F)) <
      (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval y₀ F)) :
  ∃! z,
    F.IsRoot z ∧
      (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval y₀ (Polynomial.derivative F)) <
        (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (z - y₀)
Polynomial.existsUnique_isRoot_addVal_lt.doc:
**Hensel's lemma with uniqueness** over a Henselian discrete valuation ring. If the order of
`F` at `y₀` exceeds twice the order of its derivative there, then `F` has exactly one root `z`
whose distance to `y₀` has order larger than that of `F'(y₀)`. Its distance to `y₀` is given by
`Polynomial.exists_isRoot_addVal_eval_eq`.

Polynomial.dist_coeff_colemanDBounded_mu.signature:
Polynomial.dist_coeff_colemanDBounded_mul_le.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [NormedCommRing R]
  [NormOneClass R] [IsUltrametricDist R] {B₁ B₂ P₁ P₂ : Polynomial R} {n m : ℕ} {ρ β : ℕ → ℝ}
  {r : ℝ} (hB₁ : B₁.coeff 0 = 0) (hB₂ : B₂.coeff 0 = 0) (hρ₀ : ∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ ρ i) (hρ : Antitone ρ)
  (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hP₁ : ∀ j ≤ n, ‖P₁.coeff j‖ ≤ ∏ i ∈ Finset.range j, ρ i)
  (hP : ∀ j ≤ n, ‖(P₂ - P₁).coeff j‖ * r ≤ ∏ i ∈ Finset.range j, ρ i)
  (hβ₁ : ∀ (t j : ℕ), ‖B₁.coeff (j + 1)‖ * ρ t ^ (j + 1) ≤ β t)
  (hβ : ∀ (t j : ℕ), ‖(B₂ - B₁).coeff (j + 1)‖ * r * ρ t ^ (j + 1) ≤ β t) (k : ℕ) :
  dist ((B₂.colemanDBounded P₂ n m).coeff k) ((B₁.colemanDBounded P₁ n m).coeff k) * r ≤
    ∏ t ∈ Finset.range k, β t
Polynomial.dist_coeff_colemanDBounded_mu.doc:
**Coleman's perturbation bound.** Let `ρ` be a nonnegative antitone sequence and `r ≥ 1`. If
`P₁` has Newton majorant `ρ` up to degree `n`, the perturbation `P₂ - P₁` satisfies the same
bound after multiplication by `r`, and the coefficients of positive degree of `B₁` and of
`r (B₂ - B₁)` are bounded by `β` at every radius `ρ t`, where `B₁(0) = B₂(0) = 0`, then the
coefficients of the bounded Coleman transforms satisfy
`dist (coeff k D_(n,m)(B₂, P₂)) (coeff k D_(n,m)(B₁, P₁)) * r ≤ ∏ t < k, β t`.

Thus perturbing the inputs by a factor `r⁻¹` relative to their majorants moves every coefficient
of the transform by at most `r⁻¹` times its coefficient bound
`Polynomial.norm_coeff_colemanDBounded_le`, uniformly in the ranks `n` and degree bounds `m`.

Polynomial.card_roots_eq_sum_ite_of_addV.signature:
Polynomial.card_roots_eq_sum_ite_of_addVal_lt.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
  [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] (F : Polynomial A) (C : Finset A) {r : ℕ}
  (hcover : ∀ x ∈ F.roots, ∃ c ∈ C, ↑r ≤ (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (x - c))
  (hdisj : (↑C).PairwiseDisjoint fun c => {x | ↑r ≤ (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (x - c)})
  (hder :
    ∀ x ∈ F.roots,
      (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.derivative F)) < ↑r) :
  F.roots.card =
    ∑ c ∈ C, if ∃ x ∈ F.roots, ↑r ≤ (IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal A) (x - c) then 1 else 0
Polynomial.card_roots_eq_sum_ite_of_addV.doc:
Count roots by a finite disjoint family of balls covering them. If the derivative order at
each root is smaller than the ball order, each occupied ball contributes exactly one root.
The derivative bound also excludes repeated rational roots, so no separability hypothesis is
needed.

Polynomial.IsRootEnumeration.aeval_esymm.doc:
**Vieta's formulas, read through a root enumeration.** If `x` enumerates the roots in `L` of
the monic polynomial `f` of degree `Fintype.card ι`, then for every `k ≤ Fintype.card ι` the
`k`-th elementary symmetric polynomial evaluated at `x` is `(-1) ^ k` times the coefficient of `f`
in degree `Fintype.card ι - k`.

Polynomial.IsPrimitive.gaussNorm_map_eq_.signature:
Polynomial.IsPrimitive.gaussNorm_map_eq_one.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [Ring R] [Nontrivial R]
  {v : AbsoluteValue R ℝ} (hna : IsNonarchimedean ⇑v) {p : Polynomial ℤ} (hp : p.IsPrimitive) :
  Polynomial.gaussNorm v 1 (Polynomial.map (Int.castRingHom R) p) = 1
Polynomial.IsPrimitive.gaussNorm_map_eq_.doc:
**Gauss's lemma at a nonarchimedean absolute value.** A primitive polynomial with integer
coefficients has Gauss norm of radius one equal to `1` at every nonarchimedean absolute value,
in any characteristic.

Polynomial.Gal.sign.signature: Polynomial.Gal.sign.{u} {F : Type u} [Field F] (p : Polynomial F) : p.Gal →* ℤˣ
Polynomial.Gal.sign.doc:
The parity character of the action of `p.Gal` on the distinct roots of `p` in its splitting
field. It takes values in `ℤˣ`, independently of the characteristic of the base field.

PeriodPair.weierstrassP_add.signature:
PeriodPair.weierstrassP_add (L : PeriodPair) {z w : ℂ} (hz : z ∉ L.lattice) (hw : w ∉ L.lattice)
  (h : L.weierstrassP z ≠ L.weierstrassP w) :
  L.weierstrassP (z + w) =
    ((L.derivWeierstrassP z - L.derivWeierstrassP w) / (L.weierstrassP z - L.weierstrassP w)) ^ 2 /
          4 -
        L.weierstrassP z -
      L.weierstrassP w
PeriodPair.weierstrassP_add.doc:
**The addition theorem for `℘`.** If `z, w ∉ Λ` and `℘(z) ≠ ℘(w)`, then
`℘(z + w) = ((℘'(z) - ℘'(w)) / (℘(z) - ℘(w)))² / 4 - ℘(z) - ℘(w)`.

PeriodPair.exists_g₂_g₃_eq.signature: PeriodPair.exists_g₂_g₃_eq {a b : ℂ} (hab : a ^ 3 - 27 * b ^ 2 ≠ 0) : ∃ L, L.g₂ = a ∧ L.g₃ = b
PeriodPair.exists_g₂_g₃_eq.doc:
**The uniformization theorem**: for all `a, b ∈ ℂ` with `a³ - 27 b² ≠ 0` there is a lattice `Λ`
with `g₂(Λ) = a` and `g₃(Λ) = b`.

PeriodPair.derivWeierstrassP_add.signature:
PeriodPair.derivWeierstrassP_add (L : PeriodPair) {z w : ℂ} (hz : z ∉ L.lattice)
  (hw : w ∉ L.lattice) (h : L.weierstrassP z ≠ L.weierstrassP w) :
  L.derivWeierstrassP (z + w) =
    -((L.derivWeierstrassP z - L.derivWeierstrassP w) / (L.weierstrassP z - L.weierstrassP w)) *
        (L.weierstrassP (z + w) - L.weierstrassP z) -
      L.derivWeierstrassP z
PeriodPair.derivWeierstrassP_add.doc:
**The addition theorem for `℘'`.** If `z, w ∉ Λ` and `℘(z) ≠ ℘(w)`, then
`℘'(z + w) = -m (℘(z + w) - ℘(z)) - ℘'(z)` with `m = (℘'(z) - ℘'(w)) / (℘(z) - ℘(w))`: the points
`(℘(z), ℘'(z))`, `(℘(w), ℘'(w))` and `(℘(z + w), -℘'(z + w))` lie on a line of slope `m`.

Path.IsCrosscut.natCard_connectedCompone.doc:
**A crosscut of a simply connected domain has exactly two sides.** If `γ` is a crosscut of a
simply connected open set `U ⊆ ℂ`, then `U \ range γ` has exactly two connected components.

PadicInt.vanDerPutEquiv.signature:
PadicInt.vanDerPutEquiv.{u_1, u_2} {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (S : Type u_1) (E : Type u_2)
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [IsUltrametricDist E] [CompleteSpace E] [Semiring S] [_root_.Module S E]
  [ContinuousConstSMul S E] : C(ℤ_[p], E) ≃ₗᵢ[S] ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap ℕ E
PadicInt.vanDerPutEquiv.doc:
**Van der Put's theorem**, as an isometric isomorphism between the continuous functions on
`ℤ_[p]` with values in a complete ultrametric normed group `E` and the null sequences in `E`,
sending a function to its van der Put coefficients. It is linear over any scalars `S` acting
continuously on `E`.

PadicInt.mahlerLinearIsometryEquiv.signature:
PadicInt.mahlerLinearIsometryEquiv.{u_1, u_2} {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (S : Type u_1)
  (E : Type u_2) [Semiring S] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module ℤ_[p] E] [IsBoundedSMul ℤ_[p] E]
  [IsUltrametricDist E] [CompleteSpace E] [_root_.Module S E] [ContinuousConstSMul S E] :
  C(ℤ_[p], E) ≃ₗᵢ[S] ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap ℕ E
PadicInt.mahlerLinearIsometryEquiv.doc:
**Mahler's theorem, scalar-linear form.** Mathlib's Mahler isometry
`mahlerEquiv E : C(ℤ_[p], E) ≃ₗᵢ[ℤ_[p]] C₀(ℕ, E)` is linear over any semiring `S` acting on the
coefficient module `E`.

PadicInt.hasSum_vanDerPut.doc:
**Van der Put's theorem**: a continuous function on `ℤ_[p]` with values in an ultrametric
normed group is the uniformly convergent sum of its van der Put terms, without assuming
completeness.

OrthonormalBasis.volume_weighted_crosspo.signature:
OrthonormalBasis.volume_weighted_crosspolytope.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]
  [DecidableEq ι] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (o : OrthonormalBasis ι ℝ E) (b : Module.Basis ι ℝ E)
  (a : ι → ℝ) (ha : ∀ (i : ι), 0 < a i) :
  MeasureTheory.volume {x | ∑ i, a i * |(b.repr x) i| ≤ 1} =
    ENNReal.ofReal
      (2 ^ Fintype.card ι / ↑(Fintype.card ι).factorial * |o.toBasis.det ⇑b| / ∏ i, a i)
OrthonormalBasis.volume_weighted_crosspo.doc:
The canonical Euclidean volume of a weighted cross-polytope in an arbitrary real basis.
The index type may be empty, in which case the volume and the empty products are one.

OrthonormalBasis.sum_sq_norm_apply_eq_no.doc:
**Parseval's identity for a functional.** The squared values of a continuous linear functional
on a finite orthonormal basis sum to the square of its operator norm: by the Riesz representation,
they are the squared coordinates of the representing vector.

OrthonormalBasis.norm_det_le_prod_norm.doc:
**Hadamard's inequality.** The determinant of a family `v` in the coordinates of an
orthonormal basis has norm at most the product of the norms of the vectors. The family may be
linearly dependent.

Orthonormal.summable_norm_apply_sq.doc:
**Bessel's inequality for a functional.** The values of a continuous linear functional `φ` on
an orthonormal family are square summable. The space need not be complete.

Orthonormal.norm_starProjection_sq_eq_su.doc:
**Parseval's identity** on the span `U` of a finite orthonormal family: the orthogonal
projection of `x` onto `U` has squared norm `∑ᵢ ‖⟪vᵢ, x⟫‖²`.

Orthonormal.norm_analysisMap_le.doc:
**Bessel's inequality** for the analysis map of an orthonormal family: the coefficient vector
`(⟪vᵢ, x⟫)ᵢ` has norm at most `‖x‖`.

Orientation.integrationCurrent_extDerivC.signature:
Orientation.integrationCurrent_extDerivCLM.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] {k : ℕ}
  (o : Orientation ℝ E (Fin (k + 1))) (Ω : TopologicalSpace.Opens E)
  (ω : TestFunction Ω (E [⋀^Fin k]→L[ℝ] ℝ) ⊤) :
  (o.integrationCurrent Ω) (TestFunction.extDerivCLM ω) = 0
Orientation.integrationCurrent_extDerivC.doc:
**Stokes' theorem for test forms**: the integration current annihilates every exact test
form.

Orientation.integrationCurrent.signature:
Orientation.integrationCurrent.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] {m : ℕ} {n : ℕ∞}
  (o : Orientation ℝ E (Fin m)) (Ω : TopologicalSpace.Opens E) :
  TestFunction Ω (E [⋀^Fin m]→L[ℝ] ℝ) n →L[ℝ] ℝ
Orientation.integrationCurrent.doc:
The **oriented integration current** `[[Ω]]` of an open set `Ω` of an oriented real vector
space `E` of dimension `m`: the continuous linear functional `ω ↦ ∫_Ω ω` on test `m`-forms on `Ω`.
For any basis `b` of orientation `o` it is `ω ↦ ∫ x, ω x b ∂b.addHaar`
(`Orientation.integrationCurrent_apply`). If `m` is not the dimension of `E`, it is zero.

Orientation.hodgeStar.signature:
Orientation.hodgeStar.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] {n : ℕ} [_i : Fact (Module.finrank ℝ V = n)] (o : Orientation ℝ V (Fin n))
  {k l : ℕ} (hkl : k + l = Module.finrank ℝ V) : ↥(⋀[ℝ]^k V) ≃ₗ[ℝ] ↥(⋀[ℝ]^l V)
Orientation.hodgeStar.doc:
The Hodge star `⋀ᵏ V ≃ ⋀ˡ V`, `k + l = finrank ℝ V`, of an oriented real inner product space:
Mathlib's `exteriorPower.hodgeStar` for the inner product and `Orientation.volumeEquiv`. It is
characterized by `⟪⋆x, y⟫ = vol (x ∧ y)` (`Orientation.inner_hodgeStar_apply`).

Orientation.existsUnique_eq_smul_integra.signature:
Orientation.existsUnique_eq_smul_integrationCurrent_of_finrank_eq_zero.{u_1} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  [BorelSpace E] {Ω : TopologicalSpace.Opens E} (o : Orientation ℝ E (Fin 0))
  (hE : Module.finrank ℝ E = 0) (hΩ : IsConnected ↑Ω)
  (T : TestFunction Ω (E [⋀^Fin 0]→L[ℝ] ℝ) ⊤ →L[ℝ] ℝ) : ∃! c, T = c • o.integrationCurrent Ω
Orientation.existsUnique_eq_smul_integra.doc:
**The constancy theorem in degree zero.** On a zero-dimensional oriented real vector space
every `0`-current on a connected open set, which is then the whole point, is a unique real multiple
of the integration current, the signed Dirac current at the origin. No boundary condition enters:
the boundary of a `0`-current is zero.

**The constancy theorem.** On a connected open subset `Ω` of an oriented real vector space of
dimension `k + 1`, a top-degree current with zero boundary, `T ∘ d = 0`, is a unique real multiple
of the oriented integration current `[[Ω]]`.

Orientation.existsUnique_comp_monoCLM_eq.doc:
**The local constancy theorem.** A top-degree current with zero boundary on an arbitrary open
subset `Ω` of an oriented real vector space of dimension `k + 1` restricts, on every connected open
subset `U ⊆ Ω`, to a unique real multiple of the integration current `[[U]]`.

OpenSubgroup.exact_cor_cup_of_index_two.signature:
OpenSubgroup.exact_cor_cup_of_index_two.{u} {G : Type u} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
  [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G] (U : OpenSubgroup G)
  (hU : (↑U).index = 2) (n : ℕ) :
  Function.Exact ⇑(CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom (TauCeti.trivialF2CorMap G ↑U ⋯ n)) fun x =>
    (((TauCeti.trivialF2TopPairing G).cup n 1) x) (U.indexTwoCharacterClass hU)
OpenSubgroup.exact_cor_cup_of_index_two.doc:
**The index-two corestriction--cup sequence is exact in every degree.** The kernel of
cupping with the subgroup character consists exactly of the corestrictions from `U`.

OpenPartialHomeomorph.exists_eq_sum_holo.signature:

OpenPartialHomeomorph.exists_eq_sum_holo.doc:
**Hadamard's lemma for holomorphic germs.** A holomorphic germ vanishing at `x` is a
combination `∑ i, zᵢ * qᵢ` of the centered coordinate germs `zᵢ` along the coordinate functionals
of a basis `b`, whose coefficients `qᵢ` take at `x` the values of the partial derivatives
`∂φ/∂zᵢ` of any representative `φ`, read in the chart `e`.

OnePoint.instContMDiffConstSMul.signature:
OnePoint.instContMDiffConstSMul.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [DecidableEq 𝕜]
  [ProperSpace 𝕜] : ContMDiffConstSMul (modelWithCornersSelf 𝕜 𝕜) ⊤ (GL (Fin 2) 𝕜) (OnePoint 𝕜)
OnePoint.instContMDiffConstSMul.doc:
**Möbius transformations of the projective line are analytic.** For `𝕜 = ℂ`, every
transformation `z ↦ (a * z + b) / (c * z + d)` of the Riemann sphere is holomorphic, and hence a
biholomorphism `Diffeomorph.constSmul 𝓘(ℂ) ω g` with inverse the transformation of `g⁻¹`.

NumberField.unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMult.signature:
NumberField.unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative.{u_1} (F : Type u_1) [Field F] [NumberField F] :
  (NumberField.RingOfIntegers F)ˣ ≃*
    ↥(NumberField.Units.torsion F) × Multiplicative (Fin (NumberField.Units.rank F) → ℤ)
NumberField.unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMult.doc:
**Dirichlet's unit theorem, structural form.** The unit group of the ring of integers of a
number field is the product of its torsion subgroup and the free abelian group generated by the
fundamental system: a unit corresponds to its unique decomposition as a root of unity times a
product of powers of fundamental units (`NumberField.Units.exist_unique_eq_mul_prod`).

NumberField.one_le_norm_mul_house_pow.doc:
**Liouville's inequality** in a number field `K` of degree `d`: a nonzero algebraic integer
`x ∈ K` satisfies `1 ≤ ‖σ x‖ ⌈x⌉ᵈ⁻¹` for every embedding `σ : K →+* ℂ`, since its norm is a
nonzero integer.

NumberField.nonempty_algEquiv_iff_of_squ.signature:
NumberField.nonempty_algEquiv_iff_of_squarefree.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [NumberField K] [Field L] [NumberField L] {d e : ℤ} (hK : Module.finrank ℚ K = 2)
  (hL : Module.finrank ℚ L = 2) {θ : NumberField.RingOfIntegers K}
  {η : NumberField.RingOfIntegers L} (hθ : minpoly ℤ θ = Polynomial.X ^ 2 - Polynomial.C d)
  (hη : minpoly ℤ η = Polynomial.X ^ 2 - Polynomial.C e) (hd : Squarefree d) (he : Squarefree e) :
  Nonempty (K ≃ₐ[ℚ] L) ↔ d = e
NumberField.nonempty_algEquiv_iff_of_squ.doc:
**The squarefree radicand is an isomorphism invariant.** Two quadratic fields presented by
square roots of squarefree integers `d` and `e` are `ℚ`-isomorphic exactly when `d = e`. Taking
`L = K` and the identity shows that the squarefree radicand of a quadratic field does not depend on
the presentation.

NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensiona.signature:
NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le.{u_1} (A : Type u_1) [Field A]
  [CharZero A] (N : ℕ) :
  {K | |NumberField.discr ↥↑K| ≤ ↑N}.ncard ≤
    (2 * NumberField.coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N + 1) ^
        (NumberField.hermiteTheorem.rankOfDiscrBdd N + 1) *
      NumberField.hermiteTheorem.rankOfDiscrBdd N
NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensiona.doc:
**Effective Hermite--Minkowski.** Inside a fixed extension `A / ℚ`, the number of number fields
`K` (finite extensions of `ℚ`) with `|discr K| ≤ N` is at most
`(2 * coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N + 1) ^ (rankOfDiscrBdd N + 1) * rankOfDiscrBdd N`, an explicit function
of `N` alone. This upgrades Mathlib's `NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd` from finiteness to an
explicit count.

NumberField.hermiteCountBound.doc:
The elementary polynomial count appearing in effective Hermite--Minkowski: if every field is
generated by a root of an integer polynomial of degree at most `D` and coefficient height at most
`C`, then the number of possible generated fields is bounded by
`(2 * C + 1) ^ (D + 1) * D`.

NumberField.fg_units_integralClosure.signature:
NumberField.fg_units_integralClosure.{u_1, u_2} (K : Type u_1) (L : Type u_2) [Field K] [Field L]
  [Algebra K L] [NumberField K] [FiniteDimensional K L] :
  Group.FG (↥(integralClosure (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) L))ˣ
NumberField.fg_units_integralClosure.doc:
**Dirichlet's unit theorem** (finite generation) for the integral closure of `𝓞 K` in a
finite extension `L` of the number field `K`: its unit group is finitely generated.

NumberField.exists_ne_zero_mul_eq_mul_ri.signature:
NumberField.exists_ne_zero_mul_eq_mul_ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  [NumberField K] {θ : NumberField.RingOfIntegers K} {d : ℤ}
  (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = Polynomial.X ^ 2 - Polynomial.C d) (hgen : ℚ[↑θ] = ⊤)
  {x y : NumberField.RingOfIntegers K} (hx : x ≠ 0)
  (hnorm :
    x * (NumberField.ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj hmin hgen) x =
      y * (NumberField.ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj hmin hgen) y) :
  ∃ ε, ε ≠ 0 ∧ x * ε = y * (NumberField.ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj hmin hgen) ε
NumberField.exists_ne_zero_mul_eq_mul_ri.doc:
**Hilbert's Theorem 90 for quadratic conjugation.** Let `σ` be the quadratic conjugation of a
quadratic number field and let `x y : 𝓞 K` with `x ≠ 0` have equal norms, `x σx = y σy`. Then there
is a nonzero `ε : 𝓞 K` with `x ε = y σε`; equivalently `y / x = ε / σε` is a "coboundary". The
construction is explicit: `ε = σx (x + y)` works unless `x + y = 0`, and then `ε = σx θ x` does.

NumberField.exists_ne_zero_int_vec_abs_l.signature:
NumberField.exists_ne_zero_int_vec_abs_le_of_house_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  [NumberField K] {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
  (a : Matrix α β (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) {A : ℝ} (hA : 1 ≤ A)
  (hcard : Module.finrank ℚ K * Fintype.card α < Fintype.card β)
  (ha : ∀ (i : α) (j : β), NumberField.house ↑(a i j) ≤ A) :
  ∃ x,
    x ≠ 0 ∧
      (a.mulVec fun j => ↑(x j)) = 0 ∧
        ∀ (j : β),
          |↑(x j)| ≤
            (3 * ↑(Fintype.card β) * A) ^
              (↑(Module.finrank ℚ K) * ↑(Fintype.card α) /
                (↑(Fintype.card β) - ↑(Module.finrank ℚ K) * ↑(Fintype.card α)))
NumberField.exists_ne_zero_int_vec_abs_l.doc:
**Siegel's lemma over a number field, with rational integer unknowns** (Evertse,
Theorem 3.20). Let `K` be a number field of degree `d` and `a` a matrix over `𝓞 K` with `M` rows
and `N` columns, whose entries have house at most `A ≥ 1`. If `d * M < N`, there is a nonzero
`x ∈ ℤ^N` with `a x = 0` and `|xⱼ| ≤ (3 N A) ^ (d M / (N - d M))` for every `j`.

NumberField.exists_evertse_unweighted.signature:
NumberField.exists_evertse_unweighted.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K] (m : ℕ) :
  ∃ C,
    ∀ (V : Type u_2) [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module K V]
      (Sfin : Finset (NumberField.FinitePlace K)) (L : AbsoluteValue K ℝ → Fin m → Module.Dual K V)
      (x : Module.Basis (Fin m) K V) (μ : AbsoluteValue K ℝ → Fin m → ℝ),
      (∀ (v : NumberField.InfinitePlace K), LinearIndependent K (L ↑v)) →
        (∀ v ∈ Sfin, LinearIndependent K (L ↑v)) →
          (∀ (v : NumberField.InfinitePlace K), Monotone (μ ↑v)) →
            (∀ v ∈ Sfin, Monotone (μ ↑v)) →
              (∀ (v : NumberField.InfinitePlace K) (k j : Fin m), v ((L (↑v) k) (x j)) ≤ μ (↑v) j) →
                (∀ v ∈ Sfin, ∀ (k j : Fin m), v ((L (↑v) k) (x j)) ≤ μ (↑v) j) →
                  ∃ ξ π,
                    (∀ (j l : Fin m), ∀ u ∉ Sfin, u (ξ j l) ≤ 1) ∧
                      (∀ (v : NumberField.InfinitePlace K) (i j : Fin m),
                          v ((L (↑v) ((π ↑v) i)) (x j + ∑ l with l < j, ξ j l • x l)) ≤
                            C * min (μ (↑v) i) (μ (↑v) j)) ∧
                        ∀ v ∈ Sfin,
                          ∀ (i j : Fin m),
                            v ((L (↑v) ((π ↑v) i)) (x j + ∑ l with l < j, ξ j l • x l)) ≤
                              min (μ (↑v) i) (μ (↑v) j)
NumberField.exists_evertse_unweighted.doc:
**Evertse's lemma without weights** (Evertse; Bombieri–Gubler, Lemma 7.5.29): the case
`ν = 1` of `NumberField.exists_evertse`. If `|L v k (x j)|_v ≤ μ v j` with `μ v` nondecreasing,
then the corrected basis satisfies `|L v (π v i) (y j)|_v ≤ C * min (μ v i) (μ v j)` at the
infinite places and `|L v (π v i) (y j)|_v ≤ min (μ v i) (μ v j)` at the places of `S₀`.

NumberField.exists_evertse.signature:
NumberField.exists_evertse.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K] (m : ℕ) :
  ∃ C,
    ∀ (V : Type u_2) [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module K V]
      (Sfin : Finset (NumberField.FinitePlace K)) (L : AbsoluteValue K ℝ → Fin m → Module.Dual K V)
      (x : Module.Basis (Fin m) K V) (ν μ : AbsoluteValue K ℝ → Fin m → ℝ),
      (∀ (v : NumberField.InfinitePlace K), LinearIndependent K (L ↑v)) →
        (∀ v ∈ Sfin, LinearIndependent K (L ↑v)) →
          (∀ (v : NumberField.InfinitePlace K) (k : Fin m), 0 < ν (↑v) k) →
            (∀ v ∈ Sfin, ∀ (k : Fin m), 0 < ν (↑v) k) →
              (∀ (v : NumberField.InfinitePlace K), Monotone (μ ↑v)) →
                (∀ v ∈ Sfin, Monotone (μ ↑v)) →
                  (∀ (v : NumberField.InfinitePlace K) (k j : Fin m),
                      v ((L (↑v) k) (x j)) ≤ ν (↑v) k * μ (↑v) j) →
                    (∀ v ∈ Sfin, ∀ (k j : Fin m), v ((L (↑v) k) (x j)) ≤ ν (↑v) k * μ (↑v) j) →
                      ∃ ξ π,
                        (∀ (j l : Fin m), ∀ u ∉ Sfin, u (ξ j l) ≤ 1) ∧
                          (∀ (v : NumberField.InfinitePlace K) (i j : Fin m),
                              v ((L (↑v) ((π ↑v) i)) (x j + ∑ l with l < j, ξ j l • x l)) ≤
                                C * (ν (↑v) ((π ↑v) i) * min (μ (↑v) i) (μ (↑v) j))) ∧
                            ∀ v ∈ Sfin,
                              ∀ (i j : Fin m),
                                v ((L (↑v) ((π ↑v) i)) (x j + ∑ l with l < j, ξ j l • x l)) ≤
                                  ν (↑v) ((π ↑v) i) * min (μ (↑v) i) (μ (↑v) j)
NumberField.exists_evertse.doc:
**Evertse's lemma** (Evertse; Bombieri–Gubler, Lemma 7.5.29). There is a constant `C`,
depending only on `K` and `m`, with the following property. Let `S₀` be a finite set of finite
places, `x` a basis of a `K`-vector space `V` indexed by `Fin m`, and at every infinite place and
every place of `S₀` let the forms `L v k` be linearly independent, the weights `ν v k` positive
and `μ v` nondecreasing, with `|L v k (x j)|_v ≤ ν v k * μ v j`. Then there are `ξ j l ∈ K`,
integral outside `S₀`, and permutations `π v`, such that `y j = x j + ∑ l < j, ξ j l • x l`
satisfies `|L v (π v i) (y j)|_v ≤ C * (ν v (π v i) * min (μ v i) (μ v j))` at every infinite
place and `|L v (π v i) (y j)|_v ≤ ν v (π v i) * min (μ v i) (μ v j)` at every place of `S₀`.

NumberField.existsUnique_neg_squarefree_.signature:
NumberField.existsUnique_neg_squarefree_algEquiv.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  [NumberField.IsTotallyComplex K] (hK : Module.finrank ℚ K = 2) :
  ∃! d, d < 0 ∧ Squarefree d ∧ Nonempty (K ≃ₐ[ℚ] QuadraticAlgebra ℚ (↑d) 0)
NumberField.existsUnique_neg_squarefree_.doc:
**The radicand classification of imaginary quadratic fields.** Every totally complex number
field of degree `2` over `ℚ` is isomorphic to `QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0` for exactly one negative
squarefree integer `d`.

NumberField.eq_zero_of_norm_le_exp_of_ho.signature:
NumberField.eq_zero_of_norm_le_exp_of_house_le_exp.{u_3} {K : Type u_3} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (σ : K →+* ℂ) {y : K} {m : ℤ} (hm : m ≠ 0) {N : ℕ} (hint : IsIntegral ℤ (↑m ^ N * y)) {A B C : ℝ}
  (hσ : ‖σ y‖ ≤ Real.exp A) (hy : NumberField.house y ≤ Real.exp B) (hmC : |↑m| ^ N ≤ Real.exp C)
  (h : C + A + ↑(Module.finrank ℚ K - 1) * (C + B) < 0) : y = 0
NumberField.eq_zero_of_norm_le_exp_of_ho.doc:
**Liouville's inequality in exponential form.** Let `K` be a number field of degree `d`,
`σ : K →+* ℂ`, `y ∈ K` and `m ≠ 0` an integer with `m ^ N y` an algebraic integer. If
`‖σ y‖ ≤ exp A`, `⌈y⌉ ≤ exp B` and `|m| ^ N ≤ exp C` with `C + A + (d - 1) (C + B) < 0`,
then `y = 0`.

NumberField.coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd.doc:
An explicit height bound for the integer minimal polynomial of a primitive generator of a number
field of discriminant `≤ N`. It is `⌈M ^ D * (D.choose (D / 2))⌉₊` where `D = rankOfDiscrBdd N` is
Mathlib's degree bound and `M = max √(1 + boundOfDiscBdd N ^ 2) 1` dominates the per-conjugate bound
of both the real and complex primitive elements of `finite_of_discr_bdd`.

NumberField.card_ideal_absNorm_le.signature:
NumberField.card_ideal_absNorm_le.{u_1} (F : Type u_1) [Field F] [NumberField F] {X : ℝ}
  (hX : 1 ≤ X) :
  {I | I ≠ ⊥ ∧ ↑(Ideal.absNorm I) ≤ X}.Finite ∧
    ↑{I | I ≠ ⊥ ∧ ↑(Ideal.absNorm I) ≤ X}.ncard ≤ X ^ 2 * 2 ^ Module.finrank ℚ F
NumberField.card_ideal_absNorm_le.doc:
In any number field `F`, the set of nonzero integral ideals with norm at most `X` is
finite, and for `X ≥ 1` its cardinality is at most `X² * 2^[F:ℚ]`.

NumberField.Units.regulator_eq_one_of_ra.signature:
NumberField.Units.regulator_eq_one_of_rank_eq_zero.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (h : NumberField.Units.rank K = 0) : NumberField.Units.regulator K = 1
NumberField.Units.regulator_eq_one_of_ra.doc:
**The regulator of a number field of unit rank zero is `1`.** When the unit rank is zero,
the unit lattice sits inside the zero-dimensional log space, and the regulator — its covolume,
computed by `NumberField.Units.regulator_eq_det'` as a determinant indexed by the infinite
places other than the distinguished one — is the determinant of the empty matrix, `1`.

NumberField.NarrowClassGroup.signature: NumberField.NarrowClassGroup.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [NumberField K] : Type u_1
NumberField.NarrowClassGroup.doc:
The **narrow class group** `Cl⁺(K)`: invertible fractional ideals of `𝓞 K` modulo the principal
ones with a totally positive generator.

NumberField.InfinitePlace.infiniteSemilo.signature:
NumberField.InfinitePlace.infiniteSemilocalUnitsTateCohomologyIsoPos {K L : Type} [Field K]
  [NumberField K] [Field L] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L] [IsGalois K L]

    tateCohomology (Rep.ofAlgebraAutOnUnits v.Completion w.Completion) ↑n
NumberField.InfinitePlace.infiniteSemilo.doc:
**Shapiro's lemma for infinite semi-local units in positive degrees.** For any finite
Galois extension `L/K` of number fields and an infinite place `w` above `v`, the semi-local
Tate cohomology at `v` is the cohomology of `L_wˣ` over `Gal(L_w/K_v)` in every degree `n > 0`.

NumberField.InfinitePlace.even_nrComplex.signature:
NumberField.InfinitePlace.even_nrComplexPlaces_iff_zero_lt_discr.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K]
  [NumberField K] : Even (NumberField.InfinitePlace.nrComplexPlaces K) ↔ 0 < NumberField.discr K
NumberField.InfinitePlace.even_nrComplex.doc:
**Brill's theorem, parity form.** The number of complex places is even exactly when the
discriminant is positive.

NumberField.Chebotarev.tendsto_frobenius.signature:
NumberField.Chebotarev.tendsto_frobeniusPsi.{u_1, u_2} (K : Type u_1) (L : Type u_2) [Field K]

    (nhds (↑(Nat.card ↑C.carrier) / ↑(Nat.card Gal(L/K))))
NumberField.Chebotarev.tendsto_frobenius.doc:
**The Chebotarev density theorem, for Chebyshev's `ψ`, as a limit.** For a finite Galois
extension `L / K` of number fields and a conjugacy class `C` of `Gal(L/K)`,
`ψ_C(x) / x → #C / #Gal(L/K)`.

NumberField.Chebotarev.primeCount_primes.signature:
NumberField.Chebotarev.primeCount_primesCongruent_isEquivalent_logIntegral (m a : ℕ) [NeZero m]
  (ha : IsUnit ↑a) :
  Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop
    (fun x => TauCeti.primeCount ℚ {p | Ideal.absNorm p.asIdeal % m = a % m} x) fun x =>
    1 / ↑m.totient * TauCeti.Real.logIntegral x
NumberField.Chebotarev.primeCount_primes.doc:
**The prime number theorem for arithmetic progressions.** At every nonzero level `m`, the
number of primes of `𝒪 ℚ` whose norms are congruent to an invertible residue `a` modulo `m`
is asymptotic to `Li(x) / φ(m)`.
This is the logarithmic-integral form of equidistribution among the invertible residue classes.

NumberField.Chebotarev.hasNaturalDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet.{u_1, u_2} (K : Type u_1) (L : Type u_2)

    (↑(Nat.card ↑C.carrier) / ↑(Nat.card Gal(L/K)))
NumberField.Chebotarev.hasNaturalDensity.doc:
Natural-density Chebotarev: among the primes of `K`, the primes with arithmetic Frobenius
class `C` have density `#C / #Gal(L/K)`.

NumberField.Chebotarev.hasDirichletDensi.signature:
NumberField.Chebotarev.hasDirichletDensity_setOf_map_inertiaDeg_eq.{u_1, u_2} (K : Type u_1)
  (L : Type u_2) [Field K] [NumberField K] [Field L] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L] [IsGalois K L]
  (E : IntermediateField K L) (μ : Multiset ℕ) :
  NumberField.Set.HasDirichletDensity
    {𝔭 | Multiset.map (fun P => (↑P).inertiaDeg (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) Finset.univ.val = μ}
    (∑ C with (MulAction.toPerm (Quotient.out C)).fullCycleType = μ,

NumberField.Chebotarev.hasDirichletDensi.doc:
**Non-Galois Chebotarev for splitting types.** The primes with residue-degree multiset `μ`
in `E` have density the total proportion of elements whose action on `Gal(L/K) ⧸ Gal(L/E)`
has full cycle type `μ`, expressed as a sum of conjugacy-class proportions. No normality of
`E/K` or realizability hypothesis on `μ` is needed.

NumberField.Chebotarev.hasDirichletDensi.signature:
NumberField.Chebotarev.hasDirichletDensity_primesCongruent (m a : ℕ) [NeZero m] (ha : IsUnit ↑a) :
  NumberField.Set.HasDirichletDensity {𝔭 | Ideal.absNorm 𝔭.asIdeal % m = a % m} (1 / ↑m.totient)
NumberField.Chebotarev.hasDirichletDensi.doc:
**Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions, with Dirichlet density.** For
`m ≠ 0` and `a` a unit modulo `m`, the primes of `𝓞 ℚ` whose absolute norm is congruent to `a`
modulo `m` have Dirichlet density `1 / φ(m)`.

NumberField.Chebotarev.hasDirichletDensi.signature:
NumberField.Chebotarev.hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet.{u_1, u_2} (K : Type u_1)
  (L : Type u_2) [Field K] [NumberField K] [Field L] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L] [IsGalois K L]

NumberField.Chebotarev.hasDirichletDensi.doc:
**The Chebotarev density theorem.** For a finite Galois extension `L / K` of number fields
and a conjugacy class `C` of `Gal(L/K)`, the primes of `𝓞 K` whose Frobenius in `L` lies in `C`
have Dirichlet density `#C / #Gal(L/K)`.

NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPsi_asym.signature:
NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPsi_asymptotic_of_mul_comm.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2}

  (hab : ∀ (σ τ : Gal(L/K)), σ * τ = τ * σ) (σ : Gal(L/K)) :

    fun x => x
NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPsi_asym.doc:
**Weighted Chebotarev for abelian extensions.** If `Gal(L/K)` is abelian, then for every
`σ ∈ Gal(L/K)` the Frobenius `ψ` function of `σ` satisfies `ψ_σ(x) = x / #Gal(L/K) + o(x)`.

NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPsi_asymptotic.{u_1, u_2} (K : Type u_1) (L : Type u_2) [Field K]
  [NumberField K] [Field L] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L] [IsGalois K L]

NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPsi_asym.doc:
**The Chebotarev density theorem, for Chebyshev's `ψ`.** For a finite Galois extension `L / K`
of number fields and a conjugacy class `C` of `Gal(L/K)`, the Frobenius `ψ` function of `C`
satisfies `ψ_C(x) = (#C / #Gal(L/K)) x + o(x)`.

NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet.{u_1, u_2} (K : Type u_1) (L : Type u_2) [Field K]
  [NumberField K] [Field L] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L] [IsGalois K L]
  (C : ConjClasses Gal(L/K)) :

NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet.doc:
**The primes of `K` with Artin class `C` in `L`.** A height-one prime `𝔭` of `𝓞 K` belongs to
`frobeniusPrimeSet K L C` when `𝔭` is unramified in `L` — so that `artinSymbol` is applicable —
and its Artin class is `C`.

The unramifiedness proof is packaged existentially rather than assumed, because `artinSymbol`
takes it as an argument and no value is assigned at a ramified prime. See
`mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_iff_artinSymbol_eq` for the form used once such a proof is available.

The carrier and this membership condition are taken from
`TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev/Suggested.lean`, lines 64–76, described in the section
`Frobenius prime sets and finite exceptional sets` of `TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev/README.md`.

NumberField.Chebotarev.fixedField_froben.signature:
NumberField.Chebotarev.fixedField_frobenius_fiber_card.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2}
  [Field K] [NumberField K] [Field L] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L] [IsGalois K L]
  (C : ConjClasses Gal(L/K)) (sigma : Gal(L/K)) (hsigma : sigma ∈ C.carrier)
  (p : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K))
  (hp : p ∈ NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet K L C) :
  Nat.card
      { P //
        IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.under (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) P = p ∧
          P ∈
            NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet
              (↥(IntermediateField.fixedField (Subgroup.zpowers sigma))) L
              (ConjClasses.mk sigma.toFixedFieldAlgEquiv) } =
    Nat.card Gal(L/K) / (Nat.card ↑C.carrier * orderOf sigma)
NumberField.Chebotarev.fixedField_froben.doc:
**The fixed-field Frobenius fiber count.** Let `sigma` represent the conjugacy class `C`, and
let `p` be an unramified prime with Artin class `C`.  The number of primes of
`L ^ <sigma>` above `p` whose relative Artin class in `L / L ^ <sigma>` is represented by
`sigma.toFixedFieldAlgEquiv` is

```text
#Gal(L/K) / (#C * orderOf sigma).
```

The division is exact by `ConjClasses.card_carrier_mul_orderOf_dvd`.

truncations of the exponential leaves monomials of degree at least three.

image in the closed unit ball of its bidual.

under the canonical embedding into the bidual is the closed ball of radius `r` about the image
of `x`.

**Johnson's theorem.** A surjective homomorphism `θ : A → B` of complex Banach algebras, not
assumed continuous, is continuous when `B` is unital with zero Jacobson radical.

semisimple complex Banach algebra is continuous. Neither algebra needs a unit.

**Šilov's theorem** for a unital target. Every homomorphism, not necessarily unital, from a
complex Banach algebra into a commutative unital complex Banach algebra with zero Jacobson radical
is continuous.

Nat.sum_range_sub_ceilDiv.signature: Nat.sum_range_sub_ceilDiv (r : ℕ) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, (r - i) ⌈/⌉ n = r
Nat.sum_range_sub_ceilDiv.doc:
**Hermite's identity** in truncated ceiling-division form: for `0 < n`, the ceilings of
`(r - i) / n` over a complete block `0 ≤ i < n` of shifts add up to `r`. The subtraction is
truncated, so the terms with `r ≤ i` vanish. Compare the floor form `Int.sum_range_add_ediv`.

Nat.sub_one_mul_sum_div_pow_succ_eq_sub_.signature:
Nat.sub_one_mul_sum_div_pow_succ_eq_sub_sum_digits {b f a : ℕ} (ha : a < b ^ f) :
  (b - 1) * ∑ i ∈ Finset.range f, a / b ^ (i + 1) = a - (b.digits a).sum
Nat.sub_one_mul_sum_div_pow_succ_eq_sub_.doc:
**Legendre's identity over a fixed range.** For `a < b ^ f`,
`(b - 1) ∑_{i < f} ⌊a / b ^ (i + 1)⌋ = a - s(a)`, where `s(a)` is the base-`b` digit sum of `a`.
This is `Nat.sub_one_mul_sum_log_div_pow_eq_sub_sum_digits` with the sum extended by zero terms
from `log b a + 1` to `f`.

Nat.dvd_choose_add_mul_iff.signature:
Nat.dvd_choose_add_mul_iff {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {q r a b : ℕ} (hr : r < p)

Nat.dvd_choose_add_mul_iff.doc:
**Lucas' theorem for divisibility, one digit at a time.** For last digits `r, a < p`, the
prime `p` divides `(r + p q) choose (a + p b)` exactly when `r < a` or `p` divides
`q choose b`.

Nat.card_filter_not_dvd_choose.signature:
Nat.card_filter_not_dvd_choose {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (n : ℕ) :
  {k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) | ¬p ∣ n.choose k}.card = (List.map (fun x => x + 1) (p.digits n)).prod
Nat.card_filter_not_dvd_choose.doc:
**Fine's theorem.** The number of `k ≤ n` for which `p ∤ n choose k` is `∏ⱼ (nⱼ + 1)`, the
product over the base-`p` digits `nⱼ` of `n`.

Nat.Partition.schurPoly_eq_det_esymmInt.signature:
Nat.Partition.schurPoly_eq_det_esymmInt.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] {σ : Type u_2}

  TauCeti.schurPoly σ R μ =

**The dual Jacobi--Trudi identity for partitions.**  In a finite alphabet `σ`, the Schur
polynomial of a partition `μ` is `det (e_{μ'ᵢ - i + j})_{0 ≤ i, j < r}`, where `μ'ᵢ` is the length
of the `i`-th column of the Young diagram of `μ`, for every `r` at least the largest part of `μ`,
and `e_m = 0` for `m < 0`.

MvPowerSeries.norm_restrictedHasseDeriv_.signature:
MvPowerSeries.norm_restrictedHasseDeriv_le.{u_1, u_2} {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [NormedRing R]

**The Cauchy estimate on the restricted-series ring.** At a positive polyradius `c`,
`‖∂^d f‖ ≤ (∏ᵢ cᵢ ^ dᵢ)⁻¹ ‖f‖` for the Gauss norm.

MvPowerSeries.isNormMulUnit_of_norm_sub_.signature:
MvPowerSeries.isNormMulUnit_of_norm_sub_C_lt.{u_1, u_2} {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [NormedRing R]

MvPowerSeries.isNormMulUnit_of_norm_sub_.doc:
**Neumann series criterion.** Over a complete ultrametric norm-one ring, a restricted series
whose distance from a constant multiplicative unit `a` is less than `‖a‖` is a multiplicative
unit.

MvPowerSeries.exists_gaussNorm_primitive.signature:
MvPowerSeries.exists_gaussNorm_primitive_le.{u_1, u_2} {σ : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [NormedField K]

**The Gauss norm bound for primitives.** Over a normed field of characteristic zero, for
polyradii `0 ≤ c' ≤ c` with `c'ᵢ < cᵢ`, there is `C ≥ 0` such that for every `f` with a Gauss norm
at `c`, `∫ f dXᵢ` has a Gauss norm at `c'` and `gaussNorm c' (∫ f dXᵢ) ≤ C * gaussNorm c f`.

with `deg P ≤ r i`. If `r i * h(a i) ≥ s⁻¹ * (h(P) + [K : ℚ] * r i * log 2)` for some `s > 0`,

`log 2` by a larger constant, such as Pottmeyer's `4`, only strengthens the hypothesis.

MvPolynomial.weightedIndex.doc:
The weighted index is the least reciprocal-weighted order of a nonzero Hasse jet;
the infimum of the empty set is `⊤`.

MvPolynomial.linearIndependent_iff_exist.signature:
MvPolynomial.linearIndependent_iff_exists_genWronskian_ne_zero.{u_3, u_4} {σ : Type u_3} {m : ℕ}

multivariate polynomials is linearly independent if and only if some generalized Wronskian with
admissible rows `|D k| ≤ k` is nonzero.

harmonic one and `r²` times a homogeneous polynomial of degree `e`. The sum is direct by
`MvPolynomial.disjoint_ker_laplacian_map_mulLeft_normSq`.

MvPolynomial.exists_ne_zero_forall_aeval.signature:

Fewer than `#σ` polynomials in `k[X_σ]` vanishing at the origin have a common zero in `K^σ` other
than the origin.

**The Fischer decomposition**, disjointness: a harmonic polynomial divisible by `r²` with
homogeneous quotient is zero.

**Vieta's formulas for an indexed family of roots**: the `k`-th elementary symmetric
polynomial, evaluated at `x : σ → S`, is `(-1) ^ k` times the coefficient of the monic polynomial
`∏ i, (X - C (x i))` in degree `card σ - k`.

MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.finite_setOf_.signature:
MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.finite_setOf_eval_ne_zero_and_abs_le_of_three_le_card_roots

that `F(X, 1)` has at least three distinct complex zeros. Then for every bound `B`, the
inequality `0 < |F(x, y)| ≤ B` has only finitely many integer solutions. Like Roth's theorem,
the proof is ineffective.

MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.finite_setOf_.doc:
**The Thue inequality for square-free binary forms** (Evertse, Corollary 6.4, square-free
case). Let `F ∈ ℤ[X₀, X₁]` be a binary form of degree `d ≥ 3` with no squared linear factor over
`ℂ`. Then for every bound `B`, the inequality `0 < |F(x, y)| ≤ B` has only finitely many integer
solutions. Like Roth's theorem, the proof is ineffective.

MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.finite_setOf_.signature:
MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.finite_setOf_eval_eq_of_three_le_card_roots {F : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℤ}

MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.finite_setOf_.doc:
**Thue's theorem** (Thue 1909; Evertse, Corollary 6.4). Let `F ∈ ℤ[X₀, X₁]` be a binary form
such that `F(X, 1)` has at least three distinct complex zeros, and let `m ≠ 0`. Then the Thue
equation `F(x, y) = m` has only finitely many integer solutions. Like Roth's theorem, the proof
is ineffective.

MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.finite_setOf_.doc:
**Thue's theorem for square-free binary forms** (Evertse, Corollary 6.4, square-free case).
Let `F ∈ ℤ[X₀, X₁]` be a binary form of degree `d ≥ 3` with no squared linear factor over `ℂ`,
and let `m ≠ 0`. Then the Thue equation `F(x, y) = m` has only finitely many integer solutions.
Like Roth's theorem, the proof is ineffective.

MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.exists_pos_mu.signature:
MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.exists_pos_mul_max_abs_rpow_le_abs_eval {F : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℤ}

MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.exists_pos_mu.doc:
**The Thue–Roth inequality for binary forms** (Evertse, Theorem 6.3). Let `F ∈ ℤ[X₀, X₁]` be
a binary form of degree `d` with no squared linear factor over `ℂ`, and let `κ > 2`. Then there
is `c > 0` with `|F(x, y)| ≥ c max(|x|, |y|) ^ (d - κ)` for all integers `x`, `y` with
`F(x, y) ≠ 0`. The proof is ineffective: it gives no value of `c`.

Multiset.mul_esymm_eq_sum.doc:

the elements of `s` is an explicit combination of the lower elementary symmetric functions and
the power sums `(s.map (· ^ j)).sum`. This is `MvPolynomial.mul_esymm_eq_sum` evaluated at the
elements of `s`.

MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup.signature:
MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup_quotient_center.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2}
  [Group G] [MulAction G α] [MulAction.IsQuasiPreprimitive G α]

MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup.doc:
**Iwasawa's criterion for the central quotient.** Let a nontrivial perfect group `G` have an
Iwasawa structure on a quasiprimitive action. If every element acting trivially is central, then
`G` modulo its centre is simple.

MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup.signature:
MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup_quotient.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [Group G]

  (hker : ∀ (g : G), (∀ (x : α), g • x = x) → g ∈ N) : IsSimpleGroup (G ⧸ N)
MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup.doc:
**Iwasawa's criterion for a quotient.** Let a perfect group `G` have an Iwasawa structure on a
quasiprimitive action. If a proper normal subgroup `N` contains every element acting trivially,
then `G ⧸ N` is simple.

MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup.signature:
MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup_derivedCentralQuotient.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1}
  {α : Type u_2} [Group G] [MulAction G α] [MulAction.IsQuasiPreprimitive G α]

  IsSimpleGroup (TauCeti.DerivedCentralQuotient G)
MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup.doc:
**Iwasawa's criterion for the derived central quotient.** Let a nontrivial perfect group `G`
have an Iwasawa structure on a quasiprimitive action whose kernel is central. Then the derived
subgroup of `G` modulo its centre, `TauCeti.DerivedCentralQuotient G`, is simple.

MulAction.IwasawaStructure.fixedPoints_e.signature:
MulAction.IwasawaStructure.fixedPoints_eq_univ_or_eq_top.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2}
  [Group G] [MulAction G α] [MulAction.IsQuasiPreprimitive G α]

  MulAction.fixedPoints (↥N) α = Set.univ ∨ N = ⊤
MulAction.IwasawaStructure.fixedPoints_e.doc:
**Iwasawa's normal-subgroup theorem for a perfect group.** If a perfect group has an Iwasawa
structure on a quasiprimitive action, each of its normal subgroups either fixes every point or is
the whole group.

MonomialOrder.isGroebnerBasis_span_of_is.doc:
**Buchberger's criterion.** If the nonzero members of `G` have unit leading coefficients and
the S-polynomial of any two members of `G` has remainder `0` on division by `G`, then `G` is a
Gröbner basis of the ideal it generates.

MonomialOrder.isGroebnerBasis_span_iff_i.doc:
**Buchberger's criterion.** A set `G` whose nonzero members have unit leading coefficients is a
Gröbner basis of the ideal it generates if and only if the S-polynomial of any two members of `G`
has remainder `0` on division by `G`.

MonomialOrder.isGroebnerBasis_iff_span_e.doc:
**Buchberger's criterion.** A set `G` whose nonzero members have unit leading coefficients is a
Gröbner basis of `I` if and only if it generates `I` and the S-polynomial of any two members of `G`
has remainder `0` on division by `G`.

MonomialOrder.IsGroebnerBasis.comap_rena.doc:
**The elimination theorem for the lexicographic order.** If `e : τ → σ` is strictly monotone
with image an upper set of variables, then the members of a lexicographic Gröbner basis of `I` in
the variables `e τ` form a lexicographic Gröbner basis of the elimination ideal.

MonomialOrder.IsGroebnerBasis.comap_rena.signature:
MonomialOrder.IsGroebnerBasis.comap_rename.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2}
  {R : Type u_3} [CommSemiring R] {m : MonomialOrder σ} {m' : MonomialOrder τ} {e : τ → σ}
  {G : Set (MvPolynomial σ R)} {I : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ R)} (h : m.IsGroebnerBasis G I)
  (hm :
    ∀ (a b : τ →₀ ℕ),

  (helim :
    ∀ (a b : σ →₀ ℕ), m.toSyn a ≤ m.toSyn b → ↑b.support ⊆ Set.range e → ↑a.support ⊆ Set.range e) :
  m'.IsGroebnerBasis (⇑(MvPolynomial.rename e) ⁻¹' G) (Ideal.comap (MvPolynomial.rename e) I)
MonomialOrder.IsGroebnerBasis.comap_rena.doc:
**The elimination theorem.** Let `m` be an elimination order for the variables `e τ`: every
monomial below a monomial in these variables is again a monomial in these variables. If `G` is a
Gröbner basis of `I` for `m`, then the members of `G` in the variables `e τ` form a Gröbner basis
of the elimination ideal `I.comap (rename e)` for every monomial order `m'` on `τ` which `e`
carries to `m`.

MonoidHom.universalGSpaceChainComplexToS.signature:
MonoidHom.universalGSpaceChainComplexToStandardComplex_naturality.{u} {k G H : Type u} [Group G]
  [Group H] [CommRing k] (φ : G →* H) :

MonoidHom.universalGSpaceChainComplexToS.doc:
**The join-to-standard comparison is natural in the group.** Relabelling simplices before
forgetting their indices agrees with first forgetting indices and then relabelling the tuples.
This is an equality of chain maps in `Rep k G`, with target actions restricted along `φ`.

MonoidHom.transfer_commutator_eq_one.signature:
MonoidHom.transfer_commutator_eq_one.{u_1} {G : Type} [Group G] [Group.FG ↥(commutator G)]
  [(commutator G).FiniteIndex] {A : Type u_1} [CommGroup A] (ϕ : ↥(commutator G) →* A) :
  ϕ.transfer = 1
MonoidHom.transfer_commutator_eq_one.doc:
**Furtwängler's theorem**, the group-theoretic principal ideal theorem: if the commutator
subgroup `G'` of `G` is finitely generated and of finite index (for instance if `G` is finite),
the transfer `G → A` of every homomorphism `ϕ : G' →* A` to a commutative group is trivial. For
`ϕ` the abelianization map, this says that the transfer `G → G' ⧸ G''` is trivial.

MonoidHom.restrictScalarsMonoidalLeftAct.doc:
The left action of a monoid `H` on `ModuleCat A` by twisting along a homomorphism
`a : H →* RingAut A`: an element `h` acts by restricting scalars along `(a h)⁻¹`. The associator
`(g * h) ⊙ₗ M ≅ g ⊙ₗ h ⊙ₗ M` and the unitor `1 ⊙ₗ M ≅ M` are the comparison isomorphisms
of restriction of scalars, with identity underlying linear maps.

MonoidHom.exists_comp_eq_and_closure_ran.doc:
**Gaschütz's lemma.** Let `f : G →* H` be a surjective homomorphism from a finite group, and
let `G` be generated by an `ι`-tuple. Then every generating `ι`-tuple of `H` lifts along `f` to a
generating `ι`-tuple of `G`.

MonoidHom.card_comp_eq_and_closure_range.doc:
**Gaschütz's counting lemma.** For a subgroup `K` of a finite group `G`, the number of
`ι`-tuples that generate `K` and lift a given generating tuple of `H` along `f` does not depend on
that generating tuple.

MonoidAlgebra.isSemisimpleRing_tensor.signature:
MonoidAlgebra.isSemisimpleRing_tensor.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] (k : Type u_2)
  [Field k] [Algebra R k] (G : Type u_3) [Group G] [Finite G] [NeZero ↑(Nat.card G)] :
  IsSemisimpleRing (TensorProduct R (MonoidAlgebra R G) k)
MonoidAlgebra.isSemisimpleRing_tensor.doc:
**Maschke's theorem after base change.** If `k` is a field in which the order of the finite
group `G` is nonzero, then the base change `R[G] ⊗[R] k` of the group algebra over any commutative
ring `R` mapping to `k` is a semisimple ring, being isomorphic to `k[G]`.

ModuleCat.projectiveDimension_add_depth_.signature:
ModuleCat.projectiveDimension_add_depth_eq_depth.{v, u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
  [IsNoetherianRing R] [Small.{v, u} R] (M : ModuleCat R) [Module.Finite R ↑M] [Nontrivial ↑M]

  CategoryTheory.projectiveDimension M + ↑(IsLocalRing.depth M) = ↑(IsLocalRing.depth ↧R)
ModuleCat.projectiveDimension_add_depth_.doc:
**The Auslander–Buchsbaum formula.** For a nonzero finite module `M` of finite projective
dimension over a Noetherian local ring `R`, `projectiveDimension M + depth M = depth R`.
Stacks, Proposition 10.111.1 (090V).

ModuleCat.exists_isAlmostSplit_of_not_in.signature:
ModuleCat.exists_isAlmostSplit_of_not_injective.{u, v, w} (k : Type u) {A : Type v} [Field k]

ModuleCat.exists_isAlmostSplit_of_not_in.doc:
**The Auslander–Reiten theorem, existence on the left.** Over a finite-dimensional algebra, a
finitely generated indecomposable non-injective module `N` starts an almost-split sequence
`0 → N → E → M → 0` of `A`-modules with `E` and `M` finitely generated.

ModuleCat.exists_isAlmostSplit_arTransla.signature:
ModuleCat.exists_isAlmostSplit_arTranslate.{u, v, w} (k : Type u) {A : Type v} [Field k] [Ring A]

ModuleCat.exists_isAlmostSplit_arTransla.doc:
**The Auslander–Reiten theorem, existence.** Over a finite-dimensional algebra, a finitely
generated indecomposable non-projective module `M` ends an almost-split sequence
`0 → τ M → E → M → 0` of `A`-modules whose left-hand end is the translate `τ M` and whose middle
term is finitely generated.

ModuleCat.exists_isAlmostSplit_X₃_eq_iff.signature:
ModuleCat.exists_isAlmostSplit_X₃_eq_iff.{u, v, w} (k : Type u) {A : Type v} [Field k] [Ring A]
  [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] (M : ModuleCat A) [Module.Finite A ↑M] :
  (∃ S, S.X₃ = M ∧ S.IsAlmostSplit) ↔ CategoryTheory.Indecomposable M ∧ ¬CategoryTheory.Projective M
ModuleCat.exists_isAlmostSplit_X₃_eq_iff.doc:
Over a finite-dimensional algebra, a finitely generated module ends an almost-split sequence
of `A`-modules exactly when it is indecomposable and non-projective.

Module.exists_finset_card_le_finrank_and.signature:
Module.exists_finset_card_le_finrank_and_smul_mem_span.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2}

      ∃ r, (algebraMap R F) r ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ (x : M), r • x ∈ Submodule.span R ↑s
Module.exists_finset_card_le_finrank_and.doc:
**Nakayama's lemma at a field-valued point.** If the fibre `F ⊗[R] M` of a finite module at a
field-valued point `R → F` has dimension `d`, then `M` is generated by `d` elements after inverting
some element of `R` that does not vanish at that point.

Module.SatisfiesSerreS.signature:
Module.SatisfiesSerreS.{u, v} (n : ℕ) (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M]
  [_root_.Module R M] : Prop
Module.SatisfiesSerreS.doc:
An `R`-module `M` satisfies *Serre's condition* `(S_n)` if for every prime `p` of `R` the depth
of `M_p` over `R_p` is at least `min (n, dim Supp M_p)`. This is meant for finite modules over a
Noetherian ring. Since the zero module has depth `⊤`, primes outside the support impose nothing.
Stacks, Definition 10.157.1 (031P).

Module.End.mk_trace_homogeneousSubmodule.signature:
Module.End.mk_trace_homogeneousSubmoduleMapₛₗ_mul_reverse_charpoly_of_pow_eq_one.{u_1, u_2}

**The graded trace formula for an endomorphism of finite order** of a finite-dimensional
vector space over an arbitrary field: if `f ^ n = 1` with `n` nonzero in `K`, then
`(∑ₘ tr(f | Symᵐ V) tᵐ) * det(1 - t f) = 1`.

No eigenvalue of `f` need lie in `K`: over an algebraic closure `f` becomes diagonalizable, and
both factors commute with scalar extension
(`Module.End.trace_homogeneousSubmoduleMapₛₗ_baseChange`, `LinearMap.charpoly_baseChange`).

Module.Basis.reflTransGen_isOrtho_isCont.signature:
Module.Basis.reflTransGen_isOrtho_isContiguous.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [Field K]

Module.Basis.reflTransGen_isOrtho_isCont.doc:
**Serre's connectivity theorem for orthogonal bases.** Orthogonal bases of a regular
quadratic space in dimension at least three are joined by a finite chain whose every step
consists of two orthogonal bases with a vector in common.

Module.Basis.existsUnique_ringHom_nonneg.signature:
Module.Basis.existsUnique_ringHom_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]

Module.Basis.existsUnique_ringHom_nonneg.doc:
**The Frobenius–Perron character.** A ring with a finite nonempty `ℤ`-basis with nonnegative
structure constants, such that every basis element occurs in `b j * ∑ i, b i` for every `j`, has
exactly one character to `ℝ` which is nonnegative on the basis.
