IsSimpleModule.algebraMap_end_bijective_.doc:
**Rickart's scalar-commutant theorem**: the scalar map from the complex numbers
to the algebraic endomorphism ring of a simple Banach module is bijective.

IsSelfAdjoint.exists_isUnitary_complexGe.doc:
**Stone's theorem, converse direction (existence).** A self-adjoint operator `A` on a complex
Hilbert space is `-i` times the complex generator of a unitary C₀-group.

IsSelfAdjoint.existsUnique_isUnitary_com.doc:
**Stone's theorem, converse direction.** A self-adjoint operator `A` on a complex Hilbert
space is `-i` times the complex generator of exactly one unitary C₀-group.

IsSelfAdjoint.add_of_isRelativelyBounded.signature:
IsSelfAdjoint.add_of_isRelativelyBounded.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜]

  (hb : b < 1) : IsSelfAdjoint (A + V)
IsSelfAdjoint.add_of_isRelativelyBounded.doc:
**The Kato–Rellich theorem.** Let `A` be a self-adjoint partial linear map on a Hilbert space
and `V` a symmetric partial linear map that is relatively bounded with respect to `A` with
constants `a` and `b < 1`, that is `dom A ⊆ dom V` and `‖V x‖ ≤ a * ‖x‖ + b * ‖A x‖` on `dom A`.
Then `A + V`, whose domain is `dom A`, is self-adjoint.

IsQuotientCoveringMap.cwComplexQuotient.signature:
IsQuotientCoveringMap.cwComplexQuotient.{u, u_1} {E : Type u} [TopologicalSpace E] {G : Type u_1}
  {B : Type u} [TopologicalSpace B] [Topology.CWComplex Set.univ] [Group G] [MulAction G E]
  [T2Space E] {p : E → B} (hp : IsQuotientCoveringMap p G)

IsQuotientCoveringMap.cwComplexQuotient.doc:
**The orbit space of a free cellular action is a CW complex.** Let `p : E → B` be the quotient
covering map of an action of `G` on the Hausdorff CW complex `E` that carries every open `n`-cell
onto an open `n`-cell, and carries an open cell onto itself only by `1`. Then `B` is a CW complex
whose `n`-cells are the `G`-orbits of `n`-cells of `E`
(`IsQuotientCoveringMap.cellQuotientEquiv`). The characteristic map of an orbit is `p ∘ φ`, for
`φ` the characteristic map of the chosen representative of the orbit
(`IsQuotientCoveringMap.map_cellQuotientEquiv_symm`).

IsPGroup.sq_topologicalGeneratorRankNat_.signature:
IsPGroup.sq_topologicalGeneratorRankNat_lt_four_mul_finrank_cohomFp_two.{u} {p : ℕ}
  [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {G : Type u} [Group G] [Finite G] [Nontrivial G] [TopologicalSpace G]
  [DiscreteTopology G] (hG : IsPGroup p G) :

IsPGroup.sq_topologicalGeneratorRankNat_.doc:
**The Golod–Shafarevich inequality.** A nontrivial finite `p`-group `G`, with the discrete
topology, satisfies `d(G)² < 4 r(G)`, where `d(G)` is its generator rank and
`r(G) = dim_{𝔽_p} H²(G, 𝔽_p)` is its relation rank. Finite generation follows from
`TauCeti.isTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated_of_fg`.

IsManifold.restrictScalars_of_ne_zero.signature:
IsManifold.restrictScalars_of_ne_zero.{u_1, u_4} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℂ E] [FiniteDimensional ℂ E] {m : WithTop ℕ∞} (n : WithTop ℕ∞) {M : Type u_4}
  [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M] (hm : m ≠ 0)
  (h : IsManifold (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ E) m M) : IsManifold (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ E) n M
IsManifold.restrictScalars_of_ne_zero.doc:
**A complex manifold is a real-analytic manifold.** A complex manifold modelled on
`𝓘(ℂ, E)`, of class `C^m` for some `m ≠ 0` with `E` finite-dimensional, is with the same charts a
real `C^n` manifold modelled on `𝓘(ℝ, E)` for every `n`; for `n = ω` it is real-analytic.

IsLocalRing.mem_range_algebraMap_of_two_.signature:
IsLocalRing.mem_range_algebraMap_of_two_le_depth.{u, u_1} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
  [IsNoetherianRing R] (K : Type u_1) [CommRing K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
  (hdepth : 2 ≤ IsLocalRing.depth ↧R) {x : K}

IsLocalRing.mem_range_algebraMap_of_two_.doc:
**Algebraic Hartogs principle for fractions.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring of depth at
least two with total ring of fractions `K`. An element of `K` that lies in the image of `R_p` for
every prime `p` other than the maximal ideal lies in `R`: if for every such `p` some `t ∉ p` has
`t x ∈ R`, then `x ∈ R`.

IsLocalExtr.mem_criticalPoints.doc: **Fermat's theorem on a manifold.** A local extremum is a critical point.

IsIntegralCurveOn.exists_tendsto_atTop_o.doc:
**The Morse form of the convergence theorem.** A negative gradient trajectory confined to a
compact set on which `fderiv ℝ f` is continuous and every critical point of `f` is nondegenerate
converges to a critical point of `f` in that set.

Nondegeneracy enters only through the finiteness of the critical locus, which is
`TauCeti.HasNondegenerateCriticalPointsOn.finite_setOfPred_fderiv_eq_zero`; the differentiability
and the continuity of the gradient are read off the continuity of `fderiv ℝ f` on `K`, the
gradient being the differential transported by the Riesz isometry.

IsIdempotentElem.exists_smul_eq_mul_of_m.signature:
IsIdempotentElem.exists_smul_eq_mul_of_mul_sub_smul_mem.{u_2, u_3} {S : Type u_2} {T : Type u_3}

IsIdempotentElem.exists_smul_eq_mul_of_m.doc:
**Nakayama's lemma for an idempotent.** Let `T` be a module-finite `S`-algebra and `J` an
ideal of `S` in the Jacobson radical. If an idempotent `e` of `T` satisfies `e T ⊆ S e + JT`, then
`e T = S e`.

IsFreeGroup.maximal_isMulCommutative_iff.signature:
IsFreeGroup.maximal_isMulCommutative_iff.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [IsFreeGroup G]

IsFreeGroup.maximal_isMulCommutative_iff.doc:
The maximal abelian subgroups of a nontrivial free group are exactly the cyclic subgroups
generated by elements that are not proper powers.

IsFreeGroup.isGDomain_id.signature:
IsFreeGroup.isGDomain_id.{u_1} {F : Type u_1} [Group F] [IsFreeGroup F] (hF : ¬IsMulCommutative F) :

IsFreeGroup.isCSA.doc: **Free groups are CSA**: every maximal abelian subgroup of a free group is malnormal.

IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.semil.signature:
IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.semilocalUnitsTateCohomologyIsoPos {K L : Type} [Field K]
  [NumberField K] [Field L] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L] [IsGalois K L]
  (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K))
  (w : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers L))

        (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.adicCompletion L w))
      ↑n
IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.semil.doc:
**Shapiro's lemma for semi-local units in positive degrees.** For any finite Galois
extension `L/K` of number fields and a place `w` above a finite place `v`, the semi-local
Tate cohomology at `v` is the cohomology of `L_wˣ` over `Gal(L_w/K_v)` in every degree `n > 0`.

IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.neg_l.signature:
IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.neg_log_valuation_aeval_mul_log_absNorm_le.{u_1, u_2}
  {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] {K : Type u_2} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) {P : MvPolynomial ι ℤ}
  {L : ι → ℕ} (hL : ∀ (i : ι), MvPolynomial.degreeOf i P ≤ L i) (x : ι → K) :
  -↑((IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation K v) ((MvPolynomial.aeval x) P)).log *
      Real.log ↑(Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal) ≤
    ↑(Module.finrank ℚ K) * Real.log (∑ s ∈ P.support, |↑(P.coeff s)|) +
      ∑ i, ↑(L i) * Height.logHeight₁ (x i)
IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.neg_l.doc:
**Liouville's inequality for values of integer polynomials at a finite place.** Let `P` be an
integer polynomial with partial degrees `degreeOf i P ≤ L i` and let `x` be a point of a number
field `K`. The order of `P(x)` at a finite place `v`, weighted by `log N(v)`, is at most
`[K : ℚ] log ℓ(P) + ∑ i, L i * h(x_i)`, where `ℓ(P)` is the sum of the absolute values of the
coefficients of `P` and `h` is the logarithmic height `logHeight₁`, relative to `K`.

The bound is meaningful for `P(x) ≠ 0`; for `P(x) = 0` the left side is `0`. Writing
`N(v) = p ^ f` and `h(x_i) = [K : ℚ] h_abs(x_i)` with the absolute height, this is
`ord_v P(x) ≤ [K : ℚ] / (f log p) * (log ℓ(P) + ∑ i, L i * h_abs(x_i))`.

  {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [Field K] [NumberField K] [Field L] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L]

IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.multi.doc:
**Hilbert's formula for a number-field different exponent.** For a finite Galois extension
`L/K`, the multiplicity of a prime `w` in the global different is the sum of the orders of the
nonnegative-index lower ramification groups, minus one in each degree.

IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.abs_l.signature:

IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.abs_l.doc:
**Liouville's inequality at a finite place.** The absolute value of the order
`-WithZero.log (v.valuation K x)` of an element `x` of a number field at a finite place `v`,
weighted by the logarithm of the norm of `v`, is at most the logarithmic height of `x`. Both sides
vanish at `x = 0`.

The **`S`-integral finite adeles** `∏_{v ∈ S} K_v × ∏_{v ∉ S} 𝒪_v`: the finite adeles that are
integral at every finite place outside `S`, as an `R`-subalgebra of the finite adele ring. For
`S = ∅` these are the integral finite adeles, and every finite adele is `S`-integral for some
finite `S`.

IsCyclic.card_filter_dvd_orderOf_eq_mul_prod_primeFactors.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Group α] [Fintype α]
  [IsCyclic α] {f : ℕ} (hf : f ∣ Fintype.card α) :
  ↑{τ | f ∣ orderOf τ}.card =
    ↑(Fintype.card α) *
      ∏ p ∈ f.primeFactors,
        (1 - (↑p ^ ((Fintype.card α).factorization p - f.factorization p + 1))⁻¹)
IsCyclic.card_filter_dvd_orderOf_eq_mul_.doc:
**Euler's product formula for the elements of order divisible by `f`.** For `f` dividing the
order `h` of a cyclic group, the elements of order divisible by `f` are a proportion
`∏ p ∣ f, (1 - p ^ -(v_p h - v_p f + 1))` of the group, the product running over the primes of
`f`.

IsCompactOperator.precomp.signature:
IsCompactOperator.precomp.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3}
  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [ProperSpace 𝕜] [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
  [SeminormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] {T : E →L[𝕜] F} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑T) :
  IsCompactOperator ⇑(ContinuousLinearMap.precomp 𝕜 T)
IsCompactOperator.precomp.doc:
**Schauder's theorem**, forward direction: the adjoint of a compact operator is compact. It
holds over every proper nontrivially normed field, without completeness hypotheses, because the
dual of a normed space is complete.

IsCompactOperator.of_precomp.signature:
IsCompactOperator.of_precomp.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3} [RCLike 𝕜]
  [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
  [CompleteSpace F] {T : E →L[𝕜] F} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑(ContinuousLinearMap.precomp 𝕜 T)) :
  IsCompactOperator ⇑T
IsCompactOperator.of_precomp.doc:
**Schauder's theorem**, reverse direction: an operator into a Banach space over `ℝ` or `ℂ`
whose adjoint is compact is itself compact.

IsCompactOperator.exists_norm_le_mul_nor.doc:
**Ehrling's inequality.** If `i : X → Y` is a compact operator and `j : Y → Z` is an injective
continuous linear map, then for every `ε > 0` there is `C ≥ 0` with
`‖i x‖ ≤ ε * ‖x‖ + C * ‖j (i x)‖` for all `x`.

IsCompact.isPolynomiallyConvex_of_forall.doc: Every compact subset of the real locus `ℝⁿ ⊆ ℂⁿ` is polynomially convex.

IsCompact.harnack_inequality.signature:
IsCompact.harnack_inequality.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {K U : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K) (hU : IsOpen U) (hUc : IsPreconnected U)
  (hKU : K ⊆ U) :
  ∃ C,
    0 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (u : E → ℝ),
        InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd u U → (∀ z ∈ U, 0 ≤ u z) → ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, u x ≤ C * u y
IsCompact.harnack_inequality.doc:
**Harnack's inequality.** Let `K` be a compact subset of a preconnected open set `U`. There
is a constant `C`, depending only on `K` and `U`, such that every function `u` harmonic and
nonnegative on `U` satisfies `u x ≤ C * u y` for all `x, y ∈ K`; that is,
`sup_K u ≤ C * inf_K u`.

IsCompact.exists_holderOnWith_thickening.doc:
**Local Hölder bounds near a compact set are uniform on a thickening.** If `f` is `α`-Hölder on
a ball around each point of a compact set `K`, with radii and constants depending on the point, then
on some open thickening of `K` the function `f` is `α`-Hölder with one constant and is bounded.

IsCoercive.orthogonalComplement_iSup_eig.signature:
IsCoercive.orthogonalComplement_iSup_eigenspaces_formSolutionOperator_eq_bot.{u_9, u_10}
  {V : Type u_9} {H : Type u_10} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [CompleteSpace V]
  [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] {B : V →L[ℝ] V →L[ℝ] ℝ} (hB : IsCoercive B)
  {J : V →L[ℝ] H} (hJ : IsCompactOperator ⇑J) (hsymm : ∀ (u v : V), (B u) v = (B v) u) :
  (⨆ mu, Module.End.eigenspace (↑(hB.formSolutionOperator J)) mu)ᗮ = ⊥
IsCoercive.orthogonalComplement_iSup_eig.doc:
**The spectral theorem for the solution operator**: its eigenspaces have trivial orthogonal
complement in `H`, even when `H` is incomplete.

IsCoercive.isLeast_rayleighQuotient.signature:
IsCoercive.isLeast_rayleighQuotient.{u_3, u_4} {V : Type u_3} {H : Type u_4} [NormedAddCommGroup V]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [CompleteSpace V] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]
  {B : V →L[ℝ] V →L[ℝ] ℝ} (hB : IsCoercive B) {J : V →L[ℝ] H} (hJ : IsCompactOperator ⇑J)
  (hsymm : ∀ (u v : V), (B u) v = (B v) u) (hJne : J ≠ 0) :
  IsLeast {r | ∃ v, J v ≠ 0 ∧ (B v) v / ‖J v‖ ^ 2 = r} ‖hB.formSolutionOperator J‖⁻¹
IsCoercive.isLeast_rayleighQuotient.doc:
**The Rayleigh principle**: the least variational eigenvalue `‖S‖⁻¹` is the *minimum* of the
Rayleigh quotient `B v v / ‖J v‖²` over the vectors with `J v ≠ 0`.  The minimum is attained at
an eigenfunction, which is why compactness of `J` is assumed.

IsCoercive.inv_norm_formSolutionOperator.signature:
IsCoercive.inv_norm_formSolutionOperator_mul_norm_apply_sq_le.{u_1, u_2} {V : Type u_1}
  {H : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [CompleteSpace V]
  [SeminormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] {B : V →L[ℝ] V →L[ℝ] ℝ} (hB : IsCoercive B)
  (J : V →L[ℝ] H) (hsymm : ∀ (u v : V), (B u) v = (B v) u) (v : V) :
  ‖hB.formSolutionOperator J‖⁻¹ * ‖J v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (B v) v
IsCoercive.inv_norm_formSolutionOperator.doc:
**The Rayleigh lower bound**: `‖S‖⁻¹ ‖J v‖² ≤ B v v` for every `v : V`.  For the Dirichlet
problem this is the Poincaré inequality with the reciprocal solution-operator norm as its
constant.  Beyond coercivity, only symmetry is needed: when `S = 0` the left-hand side vanishes
and the bound is the nonnegativity of the energy.

IsCoercive.fredholmAlternative_formPertu.doc:
**The variational Fredholm alternative.**  For a compact continuous linear map `J`, either the
homogeneous perturbation of `B` by `κ ⟪J ·, J ·⟫` has a nonzero solution, or every represented
forcing has a unique solution.

IsBaseChange.bilinForm.signature:
IsBaseChange.bilinForm.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3}
  {N : Type u_4} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A] [AddCommMonoid M]
  [_root_.Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [_root_.Module R N] [_root_.Module A N]
  [IsScalarTower R A N] {f : M →ₗ[R] N} (h : IsBaseChange A f) (B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M) :
  LinearMap.BilinForm A N
IsBaseChange.bilinForm.doc:
Extend a bilinear form to an abstract base change, transporting Mathlib's tensor-product
base change along the canonical equivalence.

IsAlgebraic.not_liouvilleWith.signature:
IsAlgebraic.not_liouvilleWith {α : ℝ} (hα : IsAlgebraic ℚ α) {p : ℝ} (hp : 2 < p) :
  ¬LiouvilleWith p α
IsAlgebraic.not_liouvilleWith.doc:
**Roth's theorem** in terms of Liouville exponents: a real algebraic number is not a
Liouville number with any exponent `p > 2`.

IsAlgebraic.mahlerExponent_le.signature:
IsAlgebraic.mahlerExponent_le {ξ : ℝ} (hξ : IsAlgebraic ℚ ξ) (n : ℕ) :
  TauCeti.mahlerExponent n ξ ≤ ↑((minpoly ℚ ξ).natDegree - 1)
IsAlgebraic.mahlerExponent_le.doc:
**Liouville's bound for Mahler's exponent.** If `ξ` is a real algebraic number of degree `D`
over `ℚ`, then `wₙ(ξ) ≤ D - 1` for every `n`.

IsAlgebraic.irrationalityExponent_eq_two.signature:
IsAlgebraic.irrationalityExponent_eq_two {α : ℝ} (hα : IsAlgebraic ℚ α) (hirr : Irrational α) :
  TauCeti.irrationalityExponent α = 2
IsAlgebraic.irrationalityExponent_eq_two.doc: The irrationality exponent of a real algebraic irrational number is two.

IsAlgebraic.inv_le_norm_ratCast_sub.signature:
IsAlgebraic.inv_le_norm_ratCast_sub {α : ℂ} (hα : IsAlgebraic ℚ α) {ξ : ℚ} (hξ : ↑ξ ≠ α) :
  (2 ^ ((minpoly ℚ α).natDegree - 1) *
          (Polynomial.map (Int.castRingHom ℂ) (TauCeti.primitiveMinpoly α)).mahlerMeasure *
        Height.mulHeight₁ ξ ^ (minpoly ℚ α).natDegree)⁻¹ ≤
    ‖↑ξ - α‖
IsAlgebraic.inv_le_norm_ratCast_sub.doc:
**Liouville's inequality** for an algebraic number. Let `α ∈ ℂ` be algebraic of degree `d`
with primitive minimal polynomial `F_α ∈ ℤ[X]`. Every rational number `ξ ≠ α` satisfies
`|ξ - α| ≥ (2 ^ (d - 1) M(F_α) H(ξ) ^ d)⁻¹`, where `M(F_α)` is the Mahler measure of `F_α` (the
Mahler measure of `α`) and `H(ξ)` the height of `ξ`.

IsAlgebraic.finite_setOfPred_abs_sub_le_.signature:
IsAlgebraic.finite_setOfPred_abs_sub_le_mulHeight₁_rpow_neg {α : ℝ} (hα : IsAlgebraic ℚ α) {κ : ℝ}
  (hκ : 2 < κ) : {ξ | |↑ξ - α| ≤ Height.mulHeight₁ ξ ^ (-κ)}.Finite
IsAlgebraic.finite_setOfPred_abs_sub_le_.doc:
**Roth's theorem** (Roth, 1955). If `α` is a real algebraic number and `κ > 2`, then only
finitely many rational numbers `ξ` satisfy `|ξ - α| ≤ H(ξ) ^ (-κ)`, where `H` is the
multiplicative height on `ℚ`.

IsAlgebraic.exists_pos_mul_mulHeight₁_rp.signature:
IsAlgebraic.exists_pos_mul_mulHeight₁_rpow_neg_le_norm_sub {α : ℂ} (hα : IsAlgebraic ℚ α) {κ : ℝ}
  (hκ : 2 < κ) : ∃ c, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (ξ : ℚ), ↑ξ ≠ α → c * Height.mulHeight₁ ξ ^ (-κ) ≤ ‖↑ξ - α‖
IsAlgebraic.exists_pos_mul_mulHeight₁_rp.doc:
**Roth's theorem** for a complex algebraic number (Evertse, remarks after Theorem 6.2). If
`α ∈ ℂ` is algebraic and `κ > 2`, then there is `c > 0` with `c H(ξ) ^ (-κ) ≤ ‖ξ - α‖` for every
`ξ ∈ ℚ` with `ξ ≠ α`. For real `α` this is
`IsAlgebraic.exists_pos_mul_mulHeight₁_rpow_neg_le_abs_sub`; a non-real `α` is at distance at
least `|im α|` from every rational number.

IsAlgebraic.exists_pos_mul_mulHeight₁_rp.signature:
IsAlgebraic.exists_pos_mul_mulHeight₁_rpow_neg_le_abs_sub {α : ℝ} (hα : IsAlgebraic ℚ α) {κ : ℝ}
  (hκ : 2 < κ) : ∃ c, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (ξ : ℚ), ↑ξ ≠ α → c * Height.mulHeight₁ ξ ^ (-κ) ≤ |↑ξ - α|
IsAlgebraic.exists_pos_mul_mulHeight₁_rp.doc:
**Roth's theorem** as a lower bound (Evertse, Theorem 6.2). If `α` is a real algebraic
number and `κ > 2`, then there is `c > 0` with `c H(ξ) ^ (-κ) ≤ |ξ - α|` for every `ξ ∈ ℚ` with
`ξ ≠ α`. For irrational `α` the condition `ξ ≠ α` always holds, by `Irrational.ne_rat`.

IsAlgebraic.exists_pos_mul_max_abs_rpow_.doc:
**Roth's theorem for a linear form.** If `α ∈ ℂ` is algebraic and `κ > 2`, then there is
`c > 0` with `‖x - α y‖ ≥ c max(|x|, |y|) ^ (1 - κ)` for all integers `x`, `y` with `x ≠ α y`.

IsAlgebraic.exists_pos_le_norm_aeval_mul.signature:
IsAlgebraic.exists_pos_le_norm_aeval_mul_supNorm_pow {ξ : ℂ} (hξ : IsAlgebraic ℚ ξ) (n : ℕ) :
  ∃ c > 0,
    ∀ (P : Polynomial ℤ),
      P.natDegree ≤ n →
        (Polynomial.aeval ξ) P ≠ 0 →
          c ≤ ‖(Polynomial.aeval ξ) P‖ * P.supNorm ^ ((minpoly ℚ ξ).natDegree - 1)
IsAlgebraic.exists_pos_le_norm_aeval_mul.doc:
**Liouville's inequality for the value of an integer polynomial.** Let `ξ ∈ ℂ` be algebraic
of degree `D` over `ℚ` and let `n ∈ ℕ`. There is `c > 0` such that every `P ∈ ℤ[X]` of degree at
most `n` with `P(ξ) ≠ 0` satisfies `c ≤ |P(ξ)| H(P) ^ (D - 1)`, where `H(P)` is the coefficient
sup norm of `P`.

IsAddCyclic.card_filter_dvd_addOrderOf_e.signature:
IsAddCyclic.card_filter_dvd_addOrderOf_eq_add_sum_primeFactors.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [AddGroup α]
  [Fintype α] [IsAddCyclic α] {f : ℕ} (hf : f ∣ Fintype.card α) :
  ↑{τ | f ∣ addOrderOf τ}.card =
    ↑(Fintype.card α) *
      ∏ p ∈ f.primeFactors,
        (1 - (↑p ^ ((Fintype.card α).factorization p - f.factorization p + 1))⁻¹)
IsAddCyclic.card_filter_dvd_addOrderOf_e.doc:
**Euler's product formula for the elements of additive order divisible by `f`.** This is the
additive counterpart of `IsCyclic.card_filter_dvd_orderOf_eq_mul_prod_primeFactors`.

Irrational.badlyApproximable_of_aeval_eq.doc:
**Liouville's theorem in degree two.** An irrational root of a nonzero integer polynomial of
degree at most `2` is badly approximable.

IntermediateField.wildExponent_le_mul_na.signature:
IntermediateField.wildExponent_le_mul_natCastValuation.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  [ValuativeRel K] [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] {n : ℕ}
  {L : IntermediateField K (SeparableClosure K)} (hL : L ∈ TauCeti.totallyRamifiedOfDegree K n)
  (hnK : ↑n ≠ 0) : L.wildExponent ≤ n * TauCeti.natCastValuation K n hnK
IntermediateField.wildExponent_le_mul_na.doc:
**The wild exponent is bounded on `σ_K(n)` away from equal characteristic `p ∣ n`**: if `n`
is nonzero in `K`, every `L ∈ σ_K(n)` has `c(L) ≤ n · v_K(n)`. In equal characteristic, where
`v_K(n) = 0`, this recovers `c(L) = 0` for `p ∤ n`.

IntermediateField.wildExponent.signature:
IntermediateField.wildExponent.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [ValuativeRel K] [TopologicalSpace K]
  [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] (L : IntermediateField K (SeparableClosure K)) : ℕ
IntermediateField.wildExponent.doc:
The wild exponent `c(L) = d(L) - [L : K] + 1` of a subextension `L` of `SeparableClosure K`,
written `d(L) + 1 - [L : K]` in truncated subtraction. For `L ∈ σ_K(n)` the truncation is
faithful by `IntermediateField.sub_one_le_discriminantExponent`, and `c(L)` is Serre's nonnegative
integer `d(L) - n + 1`.

IntermediateField.rootCount.signature:
IntermediateField.rootCount.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Field K] [Field E]
  [Algebra K E] (L : IntermediateField K E) {n : ℕ} (a : Fin n → K) : ℕ
IntermediateField.rootCount.doc:
The root count of a coefficient vector `a : Fin n → K` in a subextension `L`: the number of
roots of the monic polynomial `monicOfCoeff a` lying in `L`, counted with multiplicity.

IntermediateField.isGalois_fixedField.signature:
IntermediateField.isGalois_fixedField.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Field K] [Field M]
  [Algebra K M] (H : Subgroup Gal(M/K)) [Finite ↥H] : IsGalois (↥(IntermediateField.fixedField H)) M
IntermediateField.isGalois_fixedField.doc:
**Artin's theorem**: `M` is Galois over the field fixed by a finite group of automorphisms,
Mathlib's `IsGalois.of_fixed_field` on the fixed field of the Galois correspondence.

IntermediateField.finrank_fixedField_eq_.signature:
IntermediateField.finrank_fixedField_eq_natCard.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [Field M] [Algebra K M] (H : Subgroup Gal(M/K)) [Finite ↥H] :
  Module.finrank (↥(IntermediateField.fixedField H)) M = Nat.card ↥H
IntermediateField.finrank_fixedField_eq_.doc:
**Artin's theorem, degree form**: the degree of `M` over the field fixed by a finite group of
automorphisms is the order of the group.

Mathlib's `IntermediateField.finrank_fixedField_eq_card` is the same conclusion under
`[FiniteDimensional K M]`, which a subgroup of the automorphism group of an infinite extension does
not supply.

IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_fixe.signature:
IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_fixedField.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [Field M] [Algebra K M] (H : Subgroup Gal(M/K)) [Finite ↥H] :
  FiniteDimensional (↥(IntermediateField.fixedField H)) M
IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_fixe.doc:
**Artin's theorem**: `M` is finite over the field fixed by a finite group of automorphisms.

Mathlib has this for `FixedPoints.subfield H M`; the fixed field of the Galois correspondence is
the same subfield, and this is the instance on that form, with no hypothesis on `M / K`.

Int.IsFundamentalDiscr.existsUnique_fins.signature:
Int.IsFundamentalDiscr.existsUnique_finset_primeDiscriminant {D : ℤ} (hD : D.IsFundamentalDiscr) :
  ∃! s, (∀ P ∈ s, TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsPrimeDiscriminant P) ∧ ∏ P ∈ s, P = D
Int.IsFundamentalDiscr.existsUnique_fins.doc:
**Unique prime-discriminant factorization of a fundamental discriminant.** Every fundamental
discriminant is the product of a unique finite set of prime discriminants.

InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd.norm_sub.signature:
InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd.norm_sub_le_of_norm_le.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F]
  [NormedSpace ℝ F] [CompleteSpace F] {u : E → F} {y z : E} {s M : ℝ}
  (hy : InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd u (Metric.closedBall y s))
  (hz : InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd u (Metric.closedBall z s))
  (hM : ∀ x ∈ Metric.ball y s ∪ Metric.ball z s, ‖u x‖ ≤ M) (hs : 0 < s) (hyz : dist y z ≤ s) :
  ‖u y - u z‖ ≤ 2 ^ Module.finrank ℝ E * ↑(Module.finrank ℝ E) * M * dist y z / s
InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd.norm_sub.doc:
**The Lipschitz bound for bounded harmonic functions.** Let `u` be harmonic on neighbourhoods
of the closed balls `closedBall y s` and `closedBall z s`, with `0 < s` and `dist y z ≤ s`, and let
`‖u‖ ≤ M` on the open balls `ball y s` and `ball z s`. Then

`‖u y - u z‖ ≤ 2ⁿ n M dist y z / s`,

where `n` is the dimension of `E`. This is the difference form of the interior gradient estimate
`|∇u| ≤ C M / s` for harmonic functions.

InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd.le_three.doc:
**The local Harnack inequality.** If `u` is harmonic and nonnegative on `ball c (4 * r)`, then
any two of its values on `ball c r` are within the factor `3 ^ n` of each other, where `n` is the
dimension of `E`.

InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd.harnack_.signature:
InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd.harnack_inequality_center {f : ℂ → ℝ} {c w : ℂ} {R : ℝ}
  (hf : InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd f (Metric.ball c R))
  (hnonneg : ∀ z ∈ Metric.ball c R, 0 ≤ f z) (hw : w ∈ Metric.ball c R) :
  (R - ‖w - c‖) / (R + ‖w - c‖) * f c ≤ f w ∧ f w ≤ (R + ‖w - c‖) / (R - ‖w - c‖) * f c
InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd.harnack_.doc:
**The centered Harnack inequality on an open planar disk.**

If `f` is harmonic and nonnegative throughout the open disk of radius `R` about `c`, then
every `w` in the disk satisfies the sharp two-sided comparison with `f c`

`(R - ‖w - c‖) / (R + ‖w - c‖) * f c ≤ f w
  ≤ (R + ‖w - c‖) / (R - ‖w - c‖) * f c`.

**Harnack's inequality on a smaller closed disk.**

If `f` is harmonic and nonnegative throughout `ball c R` and `r < R`, then for any
`x, y ∈ closedBall c r`,

`f x ≤ ((R + r) / (R - r)) ^ 2 * f y`.

InnerProductSpace.HarmonicContOnCl.harna.doc:
**Harnack's inequality on a smaller closed disk, from boundary nonnegativity.**

If `f` is harmonic on `ball c R`, continuous on its closure and nonnegative on its boundary
circle, and `r < R`, then for any `x, y ∈ closedBall c r`,

`f x ≤ ((R + r) / (R - r)) ^ 2 * f y`.

InnerProductSpace.HarmonicContOnCl.harna.signature:
InnerProductSpace.HarmonicContOnCl.harnack_inequality_center_of_nonneg_on_sphere {f : ℂ → ℝ}
  {c w : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hf : InnerProductSpace.HarmonicContOnCl f (Metric.ball c R))
  (hnonneg : ∀ z ∈ Metric.sphere c R, 0 ≤ f z) (hw : w ∈ Metric.ball c R) :
  (R - ‖w - c‖) / (R + ‖w - c‖) * f c ≤ f w ∧ f w ≤ (R + ‖w - c‖) / (R - ‖w - c‖) * f c
InnerProductSpace.HarmonicContOnCl.harna.doc:
**The centered Harnack inequality on a planar disk.**

If `f` is harmonic on the open disk of radius `R` about `c`, continuous on its closure and
nonnegative on its boundary circle, then every `w` in the open disk satisfies

`(R - ‖w - c‖) / (R + ‖w - c‖) * f c ≤ f w
  ≤ (R + ‖w - c‖) / (R - ‖w - c‖) * f c`.

ImplicitFunctionData.analyticAt_implicit.signature:
ImplicitFunctionData.analyticAt_implicitFunction.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1}
  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
  [CompleteSpace E] {F : Type u_3} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] [CompleteSpace F]
  {G : Type u_4} [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace 𝕜 G] [CompleteSpace G]
  {φ : ImplicitFunctionData 𝕜 E F G} (hl : AnalyticAt 𝕜 φ.leftFun φ.pt)
  (hr : AnalyticAt 𝕜 φ.rightFun φ.pt) :
  AnalyticAt 𝕜 (Function.uncurry φ.implicitFunction) (φ.prodFun φ.pt)
ImplicitFunctionData.analyticAt_implicit.doc:
**The analytic implicit function theorem**, general form: the implicit function defined by
analytic `leftFun` and `rightFun` is analytic.

Ideal.mem_iInf_map_algebraMap_pow_iff.signature:
Ideal.mem_iInf_map_algebraMap_pow_iff.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [Ring A]
  [Algebra R A] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite R A] (I : Ideal R) (x : A) :
  x ∈ ⨅ n, Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I ^ n ↔ ∃ r ∈ I, (algebraMap R A) r * x = x
Ideal.mem_iInf_map_algebraMap_pow_iff.doc:
**The Krull intersection theorem for an extended ideal.** If `R` is Noetherian and `A` is a
finite `R`-module, an element of every power of the two-sided ideal of `A` generated by `I` is
fixed by multiplication by some scalar in `I`.

Ideal.isRegularLocalRing_localization_of.doc:
**The Jacobian criterion for a hypersurface.** Let `f ∈ A` and let `P` be a prime of
`A ⧸ (f)` lying over the prime `Q` of `A`, with `A_Q` a regular local ring. If some derivation `D`
of `A` maps `f` outside `Q`, then the localization of `A ⧸ (f)` at `P` is a regular local ring.

Ideal.isNoetherianRing_of_isAdicComplete.signature:
Ideal.isNoetherianRing_of_isAdicComplete.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.FG)
  [IsAdicComplete I R] [IsNoetherianRing (R ⧸ I)] : IsNoetherianRing R
Ideal.isNoetherianRing_of_isAdicComplete.doc:
**Noetherianity of complete rings.** A ring that is `I`-adically complete for a finitely
generated ideal `I` is Noetherian as soon as `R ⧸ I` is Noetherian.

Ideal.exists_pow_eq_mk_iff_pow_sub_one_m.doc:
**Euler's criterion in a finite residue domain.** Let `P` be a prime of `R` with finite
quotient and `n ∣ #(R ⧸ P) - 1`. For `a ∉ P`, the class of `a` is an `n`-th power in `R ⧸ P`
exactly when `a ^ ((#(R ⧸ P) - 1) / n) ≡ 1 (mod P)`.

Ideal.exists_pow_add_smul_inf_eq_pow_smu.doc:
**Artin–Rees for a finitely generated submodule.** If `N₀` is a finitely generated submodule
over a noetherian ring, there is a shift `k` such that `I ^ (n + k) • N₀ ⊓ L` equals
`I ^ n • (I ^ k • N₀ ⊓ L)` for every submodule `L` and every `n`. The ambient module need not be
finite: only `N₀` is, so Mathlib's `Ideal.exists_pow_inf_eq_pow_smul` is applied inside `N₀`.
In particular `I ^ (n + k) • N₀ ⊓ L ≤ I ^ n • L`; when `L ≤ N₀`, this shows that the
filtration `N₀` induces on `L` is cofinal in the `I`-adic filtration of `L`.

group `G`, a subgroup `H` of `G`, the integral closures `B` and `C` of `A` in `M` and in `M ^ H`,

indexed by the double cosets `H \ G / D`.

`Ideal.doubleCosetQuotientEquivPrimesOverOfIsIntegralClosure_mk`.

HomotopyGroup.bijective_hurewicz.doc:
**The Hurewicz theorem.** If `πₖ(X, x)` is trivial for every `k < n + 2`, then the Hurewicz
map `πₙ₊₂(X, x) → Hₙ₊₂(X; ℤ)`, `[p] ↦ p_*[Iⁿ⁺²]`, is bijective.

HomologicalComplex.reidemeisterTorsion_e.signature:

HomologicalComplex.reidemeisterTorsion_e.doc: The torsion of a bounded based complex vanishes if and only if the complex is not acyclic.

chain complexes of vector spaces, with `C₁` and `C₃` acyclic, and with compatible bases: the basis
`c₂ i` of `C₂ᵢ` is the image of the basis `c₁ i` of `C₁ᵢ` followed by lifts of the basis `c₃ i` of
`C₃ᵢ`. Then `τ(C₂) = ε · τ(C₁) · τ(C₃)`, with the sign `ε = ∏ⱼ (-1) ^ (dim B₃,ⱼ₊₁ · dim B₁,ⱼ)`
given by the dimensions of the boundaries `Bₖ,ⱼ ⊆ Cₖ,ⱼ`. This also holds when the complexes are
unbounded, both sides being `0`.

The basis-change formula for the torsion: replacing the bases `c i` of `C` by `c' i`
multiplies the torsion by `∏ᵢ [c'ᵢ / cᵢ] ^ ((-1) ^ i)`, where `[c'ᵢ / cᵢ]` is the determinant of

not acyclic or is unbounded.

HomologicalComplex.isIso_homologyKunneth_of_isSplitMono_of_isSplitEpi.{u, u_3} {R : Type u}

HomologicalComplex.isIso_homologyKunneth.doc:
**The Künneth theorem for split complexes**: for complexes `K` and `L` of modules over a
commutative ring `R` whose cycles split off their terms and whose homology splits off their cycles,
the Künneth map `⨁_{p + q = n} Hₚ(K) ⊗ H_q(L) ⟶ Hₙ(K ⊗ L)` is an isomorphism.  This applies to
complexes of semisimple modules, for instance of vector spaces over a field
(`HomologicalComplex.isSplitMono_iCycles_of_isSemisimpleModule`), and to complexes whose cycles
split off and whose homology is projective
(`HomologicalComplex.isSplitEpi_homologyπ_of_projective`).

HomologicalComplex.isIso_homologyKunneth.signature:
HomologicalComplex.isIso_homologyKunneth_of_d_eq_zero_of_flat_right.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]

  CategoryTheory.IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyKunneth K L n)
HomologicalComplex.isIso_homologyKunneth.doc:
**The Künneth theorem when the second factor has zero differentials and flat terms**: if `L`
is a complex of flat modules with zero differentials, so that `H_q(L) = L_q`, then for every
complex `K` the Künneth map `⨁_{p + q = n} Hₚ(K) ⊗ H_q(L) ⟶ Hₙ(K ⊗ L)` is an isomorphism.  This
is `HomologicalComplex.isIso_homologyKunneth_of_d_eq_zero_of_flat` with the factors interchanged.

HomologicalComplex.isIso_homologyKunneth_of_d_eq_zero_of_flat.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]

HomologicalComplex.isIso_homologyKunneth.doc:
**The Künneth theorem when one factor has zero differentials and flat terms.**  If `K` is a
complex of flat modules with zero differentials, so that `Hₚ(K) = Kₚ`, then for every complex `L`
the Künneth map `⨁_{p + q = n} Hₚ(K) ⊗ H_q(L) ⟶ Hₙ(K ⊗ L)` is an
isomorphism.  For instance, for a flat module `M` placed in degree zero this says that tensoring
`L` with `M` commutes with homology.

HomologicalComplex.finrank_homology_le_finrank_X.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} [DivisionRing k]

HomologicalComplex.finrank_homology_le_f.doc:
**The weak Morse inequality.**  In a homological complex of vector spaces, a homology group
has dimension at most that of the finite-dimensional term it is computed from.

HomologicalComplex.eulerChar_forgetFG_eq.doc:
**Euler--Poincaré for a bounded cochain complex of finitely generated modules.**  Over a
Noetherian ring with the rank-nullity property, Mathlib's Euler characteristic of the terms agrees
with its homology Euler characteristic after forgetting a bounded complex from `FGModuleCat R` to
`ModuleCat R`.

The source category makes every term and homology object finitely generated, hence of finite
rank, while the explicit bounds make both `finsum`s finite.  Consequently this equality does not
rely on either totalized junk value.

Homeomorph.pullbackDiffeomorph.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {H : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace H]

A homeomorphism onto a charted space is a `C^n` diffeomorphism for the pulled-back structure:
read in a pulled-back chart and in the corresponding chart of `M`, both it and its inverse are the
identity.

Homeomorph.pullbackChartedSpace.doc:
The charted-space structure on `N` pulled back along a homeomorphism `e : N ≃ₜ M`: the atlas
is `{e.transOpenPartialHomeomorph c | c ∈ atlas H M}` and the chart at `x` is the chart of `M` at
`e x` precomposed with `e`.

Homeomorph.alexanderIsotopyClosedBall.signature:
Homeomorph.alexanderIsotopyClosedBall.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]

  TauCeti.AmbientIsotopy ↑(Metric.closedBall 0 1)
Homeomorph.alexanderIsotopyClosedBall.doc:
**Alexander's lemma.** A homeomorphism of the closed unit ball fixing the unit sphere is
joined to the identity through homeomorphisms of the ball fixing the sphere.

HolderWith.heatCauchyPotential.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]

**The spatial Hölder estimate of the Cauchy heat potential.** If `g` is continuous and
`α`-Hölder with constant `H`, then so is every time slice of its Cauchy potential, with the same
constant.

HolderOnWith.norm_image_sub_sub_le_of_ha.doc:
**First-order Taylor bound for a Hölder derivative.** If `g` has derivative `g'` within `s`
and `g'` is `α`-Hölder with constant `H` on `s`, then for a segment from `x` to `x + w` contained
in `s`, the error of the linear approximation is at most `H ‖w‖^(1 + α)`.

HilbertBasis.tsum_enorm_sq_inner.doc:
**Parseval's identity, extended-nonnegative form.** The squared extended norms of the
coordinates of `x` in a Hilbert basis sum to `‖x‖ₑ²`.

HilbertBasis.prod.doc:
**The product Hilbert basis.** Pointwise products of two Hilbert bases form a Hilbert basis of
`L²(μ ⊗ ν)`, indexed by the product of the index types.

HilbertBasis.hilbertSchmidtNorm_columnOp.signature:
HilbertBasis.hilbertSchmidtNorm_columnOperator.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2}

HilbertBasis.hilbertSchmidtNorm_columnOp.doc:
**Hilbert–Schmidt norm identity.** The Hilbert–Schmidt norm of `T_f` is the `ℓ²` norm of
`f`.

HilbertBasis.hasSum_norm_sq_inner.doc:
**Parseval's identity, norm-square form.** The squared coordinates of `x` in a Hilbert basis
sum to `‖x‖²`, as a convergent series of real numbers.

HeckeRing.GLn.range_evalHom.signature:
HeckeRing.GLn.range_evalHom (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] {p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) :
  (HeckeRing.GLn.evalHom n p).range = HeckeRing.GLn.pLocalSubring n p
HeckeRing.GLn.range_evalHom.doc:
**The generators generate `R_p`** (Shimura, Theorem 3.20): for `p` prime, the polynomials in
the generators `heckeGen k` are exactly the elements of the `p`-local Hecke ring.

HeckeRing.GL2.peterssonInnerCosets_hecke.signature:
HeckeRing.GL2.peterssonInnerCosets_heckeTCuspNat_right {N n : ℕ} [NeZero N] [NeZero n] (k : ℤ)

HeckeRing.GL2.peterssonInnerCosets_hecke.doc:
**The Petersson adjoint formula in the second argument.** For `n` coprime to `N`,

`⟪f, Tₙ g⟫ = ⟪⟨n⟩⁻¹ Tₙ f, g⟫`.

This is the Hermitian transpose of
`peterssonInnerCosets_heckeTCuspNat_left`.

HeckeRing.GL2.degree_diagCoset_of_ratio_.doc:
**The prime-power degree** (Shimura, Theorem 3.24, degree count): for prime `p` and
`k ≥ 1`, a divisibility chain `a` of ratio `a₁ / a₀ = pᵏ` has `deg T(a₀, a₁) = pᵏ⁻¹ (p + 1)`.
The archetype is `a = (pⁱ, pⁱ⁺ᵏ)`.

HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.heckeUCuspNat_eq_q.doc:
**A newform is an eigenvector of `U_p` at every prime `p` dividing the level, with eigenvalue
`a_p(f)`** (Atkin–Lehner; Li; Diamond–Shurman, Theorem 5.8.2; Miyake, Theorem 4.6.13). Together
with the good eigensystem this makes a newform a full Hecke eigenform (`Newform.toEigenform`).
The statement is on the bad-prime operator `heckeUCuspNat`, matching the `U_p`-spelled API of
`HeckeSlash/BadPrime`; `Newform.heckeTCuspNat_eq_qExpansion_coeff_smul` is the statement at
every prime.

HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.eq_of_forall_notMe.doc:
**Strong multiplicity one** (Miyake, Theorem 4.6.12, fixed level): two newforms of level `N`
and weight `k` whose eigenvalues agree at every index coprime to `N` outside a finite set are
equal. No assumption is made on the nebentypus.

HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.atkinLehnerPseudoEigenvalue {N Q : ℕ} [NeZero N] {k : ℤ}
  (f : HeckeRing.GL2.Newform N k) (h : TauCeti.Nat.IsExactDivisor Q N) : ℂ
HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.atkinLehnerPseudoE.doc:
**The Atkin–Li pseudo-eigenvalue** `λ_Q(f)` of a newform `f` at an exact divisor `Q` of the
level: the scalar with `𝒲_Q f = λ_Q(f) • g`, where `𝒲_Q` is the slash by the Atkin–Li matrix
`atkinLiMatrix N Q` normalized by `(√Q) ^ (2 - k)` and `g = f.atkinLehnerTransform h` is the
transported newform. Since `g` has first Fourier coefficient `1`, it is the first Fourier
coefficient of `𝒲_Q f`.

HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.L_eulerProduct.signature:
HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.L_eulerProduct {N : ℕ} [NeZero N] {k : ℤ} (f : HeckeRing.GL2.Newform N k)
  (hk : 0 < k) {s : ℂ} (hs : ↑k / 2 + 1 < s.re) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun n =>
      ∏ p ∈ n.primesBelow,
        (1 - (PowerSeries.coeff p) (UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion 1 ⇑f.toCuspForm) * ↑p ^ (-s) +
            f.dirichletLift ↑p * ↑p ^ (k - 1) * ↑p ^ (-2 * s))⁻¹)
    Filter.atTop (nhds (ModularForm.L hk f.toCuspForm s))
HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.L_eulerProduct.doc: Finite Euler products converge to Mathlib's `ModularForm.L` for a newform.

HeckeCosetModule.mul_comm_of_antiInvolut.signature:
HeckeCosetModule.mul_comm_of_antiInvolution.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] (R : Type u_2)
  {Δ : Submonoid G} {H : Subgroup G} [IsHeckeTriple Δ H H] [CommSemiring R]
  (ι : HeckeAntiInvolution Δ H) (h_fix : ∀ (D : HeckeCoset Δ H H), ι.onHeckeCoset D = D)
  (f g : HeckeRing Δ H R) : f * g = g * f
HeckeCosetModule.mul_comm_of_antiInvolut.doc:
**Shimura's commutativity criterion** (Proposition 3.8 of [Shimura][shimura1971]): the
Hecke ring over a commutative semiring is commutative when an anti-involution fixes every
double coset.

HeckeCoset.heckeSum_eq_sum_of_rightCoset.signature:
HeckeCoset.heckeSum_eq_sum_of_rightCosets.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6} {G : Type u_1} [Group G]
  {Δ Δ' : Submonoid G} {Γ₁ Γ₂ : Subgroup G} (D : HeckeCoset Δ Γ₁ Γ₂) {R : Type u_2} {S : Type u_3}
  {V : Type u_4} {W : Type u_5} [Semiring R] [Semiring S] [AddCommMonoid V] [_root_.Module R V]
  [AddCommMonoid W] [_root_.Module S W] {σ : R →+* S} (ρ : Representation R (↥Δ') V)
  (hD : ↑(Quotient.out D) ∈ Δ') (hΓ₂ : Γ₂.toSubmonoid ≤ Δ') {q : V →ₛₗ[σ] W}
  [Finite (DoubleCoset.DecompQuotient Γ₂ Γ₁ (↑(Quotient.out D))⁻¹)] (hΓ₁ : Γ₁.toSubmonoid ≤ Δ')
  (hq : ∀ (γ : G) (hγ : γ ∈ Γ₁), q ∘ₛₗ ρ ⟨γ, ⋯⟩ = q) {ι : Type u_6} [Fintype ι] (a : ι → G)
  (ha : ∀ (i : ι), a i ∈ Δ')
  (hcover : DoubleCoset.doubleCoset ↑(Quotient.out D) ↑Γ₁ ↑Γ₂ = ⋃ i, MulOpposite.op (a i) • ↑Γ₁)
  (hinj : Function.Injective fun i => MulOpposite.op (a i) • ↑Γ₁) :
  D.heckeSum ρ hD hΓ₂ q = ∑ i, q ∘ₛₗ ρ ⟨a i, ⋯⟩
HeckeCoset.heckeSum_eq_sum_of_rightCoset.doc:
**The Hecke sum of a `Γ₁`-invariant map is the sum over any decomposition of the double coset
into right cosets.** If the right cosets `Γ₁ aᵢ` are pairwise distinct and cover `Γ₁ D.out Γ₂`,
then `heckeSum D ρ q = ∑ᵢ q ∘ ρ(aᵢ)`.

So the map is attached to the double coset itself: the representatives `D.out` and `v.out` that
`heckeSum` happens to pick are one such family, and every other family gives the same map. The
hypothesis `ha` records that the family lies in the monoid `ρ` acts through; it is automatic
when the family lies in the double coset and `Γ₁ ≤ Δ'`.

HasStrictFDerivAt.isNashAt_implicitFunct.doc:
**Nash implicit function theorem for systems.** If the coordinates of a finite system are
Nash at `u` and its partial derivative in the unknown variables is invertible, every coordinate
of Mathlib's chosen implicit function is a Nash germ at the parameter point.

HasStrictFDerivAt.contDiffOn_toOpenParti.signature:

    (HasStrictFDerivAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph f hf).target
HasStrictFDerivAt.contDiffOn_toOpenParti.doc:
**The inverse function theorem produces a `C^n` inverse.** If `f` is `C^n` on the source of the
homeomorphism built by the inverse function theorem, then the inverse is `C^n` on the target.

HasStrictFDerivAt.analyticAt_implicitFun.signature:
HasStrictFDerivAt.analyticAt_implicitFunctionOfProdDomain.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1}

HasStrictFDerivAt.analyticAt_implicitFun.doc:
**The analytic implicit function theorem.** If `f : E₁ × E → F` is analytic at `u` and its
partial derivative in the second variable is invertible there, the implicit function `ψ` with
`f (x, ψ x) = f u` near `u.1` is analytic at `u.1`.

HasFDerivAt.finrank_range_lt_of_infinite.signature:
HasFDerivAt.finrank_range_lt_of_infinite_of_norm_eq.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ F] {g h : E → F} {g' h' : E →L[ℝ] F} {x : E} (hh : HasFDerivAt h h' x)
  (hg : HasFDerivAt g g' x) (hn : ∀ᶠ (y : E) in nhds x, ‖h y‖ = ‖h x‖) (h0 : h x ≠ 0) {p : ℕ}
  (hp :

        Module.finrank ℝ ↥(↑(fderiv ℝ (fun q => g q.1 + q.2 • h q.1) (x, t))).range ≤ p}.Infinite) :
  Module.finrank ℝ ↥(↑h').range < p
HasFDerivAt.finrank_range_lt_of_infinite.doc:
**The Lefschetz–Whitehead rank estimate for unit directions.** Let `g` and `h` be
differentiable at `x`, where `h x ≠ 0` and `‖h‖` is constant near `x`, for instance a map into the
unit sphere. If the swept map `(y, t) ↦ g y + t • h y` has rank at most `p` at `(x, t)` for
infinitely many `t`, then `h` has rank less than `p` at `x`.

HasFDerivAt.finrank_range_lt_of_infinite.signature:
HasFDerivAt.finrank_range_lt_of_infinite.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]

  [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] {g h : E → F} {g' h' : E →L[𝕜] F} {x : E} [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 F]

  Module.finrank 𝕜 ↥(↑h').range < p
HasFDerivAt.finrank_range_lt_of_infinite.doc:
**The Lefschetz–Whitehead rank estimate.** Let `g` and `h` be differentiable at `x`, with
`h x` outside the range of the derivative `h'` of `h`. If the swept map
`(y, t) ↦ g y + t • h y` has rank at most `p` at `(x, t)` for infinitely many `t`, for instance
for every `t` near `0`, then `h` has rank less than `p` at `x`.

HasCompactSupport.two_pi_inv_smul_integr.doc:
**The Cauchy–Pompeiu formula** for a compactly supported `C¹` map `u : ℂ → F`: `u` is the
Cauchy transform of `∂ₓ u + i ∂ᵧ u = 2 \bar∂ u`,
`u w = (2π)⁻¹ ∫ (w - z)⁻¹ • (∂ₓ u z + i ∂ᵧ u z)`, the integral being over the whole plane.

HasCompactSupport.exists_norm_iteratedFD.signature:
HasCompactSupport.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_sub_sub_add_fderiv_le.{u_4, u_5} {E : Type u_4}
  {F : Type u_5} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
  {n : WithTop ℕ∞} {f : E → F} (hfc : HasCompactSupport f) (hf : ContDiff ℝ n f) {i : ℕ}

HasCompactSupport.exists_norm_iteratedFD.doc:
**Uniform first-order Taylor estimate for all derivatives.** If `f` is `C^{i+1}` with compact
support, then the `i`-th derivative of the first-order Taylor remainder
`z ↦ f (z - h) - f z + Df(z) h` is `o(‖h‖)` as `h → 0`, uniformly on the whole space.

HasCompactSupport.exists_norm_iteratedFD.signature:
HasCompactSupport.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_prod_right_sub_sub_le.{u_4, u_5, u_6} {P : Type u_4}
