HasCompactSupport.exists_norm_iteratedFD.doc:
**Uniform first-order Taylor estimate in a parameter.** If `g : P × E → F` is `C^{i+1}` with
compact support, then the `i`-th derivative in the second variable of the first-order Taylor
remainder `x ↦ g (p + h, x) - g (p, x) - Dg(p, x) (h, 0)` in the first variable is `o(‖h‖)` as
`h → 0`, uniformly on the whole space.

HahnModule.instLieRing.doc: Hahn series with coefficients in a Lie ring form a Lie ring under the convolution bracket.

Group.ResiduallyFinite.injective_of_surj.signature:
Group.ResiduallyFinite.injective_of_surjective.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [Group.FG G]
  [Group.ResiduallyFinite G] {f : G →* G} (hf : Function.Surjective ⇑f) : Function.Injective ⇑f
Group.ResiduallyFinite.injective_of_surj.doc:
**Malcev's theorem.** A surjective endomorphism of a finitely generated residually finite
group is injective: such a group is Hopfian.

Group.IsPrimitive.signature: Group.IsPrimitive.{u} {G : Type u} [Group G] (x : G) : Prop
Group.IsPrimitive.doc: An element of a group is primitive when it belongs to some free basis of the group.

Graph.vertexConnectivity_le_edgeConnecti.signature:
Graph.vertexConnectivity_le_edgeConnectivity.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β} :
  G.vertexConnectivity ≤ G.edgeConnectivity
Graph.vertexConnectivity_le_edgeConnecti.doc: **Whitney's inequality for multigraphs**: vertex connectivity is at most edge connectivity.

Graph.isVertexReachable_iff_exists_paths.signature:
Graph.isVertexReachable_iff_exists_paths.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β}
  [Finite ↑G.vertexSet] {s t : ↑G.vertexSet} (hst : s ≠ t) (hadj : ¬G.Adj ↑s ↑t) (k : ℕ) :
  G.IsVertexReachable k s t ↔
    ∃ P, (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧ Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)
Graph.isVertexReachable_iff_exists_paths.doc:
**Menger's theorem for the vertex-reachability predicate.** For distinct nonadjacent actual
vertices of a multigraph with finitely many actual vertices, `k`-vertex-reachability is equivalent
to the existence of `k` internally vertex-disjoint native paths. No finite-edge assumption is
needed.

Graph.isEdgeReachable_iff_exists_paths.signature:
Graph.isEdgeReachable_iff_exists_paths.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β} {s t : α}
  [Finite ↑G.vertexSet] [Finite ↑G.edgeSet] (hs : s ∈ G.vertexSet) (k : ℕ) :
  G.IsEdgeReachable k s t ↔
    ∃ P, (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧ Pairwise fun i j => (P i).edges.Disjoint (P j).edges
Graph.isEdgeReachable_iff_exists_paths.doc:
**Menger's theorem for edge-disjoint paths in a multigraph, predicate form.** For an actual
vertex `s` of a multigraph with finitely many actual vertices and edges, `s` and `t` stay reachable
after deleting any fewer than `k` edges exactly when there are `k` `s`–`t` paths, no two of which
traverse a common edge.

Graph.isBridge_iff_forall_cycle_notMem.signature:
Graph.isBridge_iff_forall_cycle_notMem.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β} {e : β}
  (he : e ∈ G.edgeSet) : G.IsBridge e ↔ ∀ ⦃u : α⦄ (p : G.Walk u u), p.IsCycle → e ∉ p.edges
Graph.isBridge_iff_forall_cycle_notMem.doc: An actual edge is a bridge exactly when it lies on no cycle.

Graph.isBridge_iff_componentCount_delete.doc:
**Bridges by component counts.**  With finitely many connected components, an edge is a
bridge exactly when deleting it increases the number of connected components by one.

Graph.forall_reachable_deleteVerts_iff_e.signature:
Graph.forall_reachable_deleteVerts_iff_exists_paths.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β}
  {s t : α} [Finite ↑G.vertexSet] (hst : s ≠ t) (hadj : ¬G.Adj s t) (k : ℕ) :
  (∀ (X : Finset α), s ∉ X → t ∉ X → X.card < k → (G.deleteVerts ↑X).Reachable s t) ↔
    ∃ P, (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧ Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)
Graph.forall_reachable_deleteVerts_iff_e.doc:
**Menger's theorem for internally vertex-disjoint paths in a multigraph, predicate form.** Let
`s ≠ t` be points of a multigraph with finitely many actual vertices, joined by no edge. Then `s`
and `t` stay reachable after deleting any fewer than `k` vertices other than `s` and `t` exactly
when there are `k` paths from `s` to `t` pairwise sharing no vertex other than `s` and `t`.

Graph.forall_reachable_deleteEdges_delet.signature:
Graph.forall_reachable_deleteEdges_deleteVerts_iff_exists_paths.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v}
  {G : Graph α β} {s t : α} [Finite ↑G.vertexSet] [Finite { e // G.IsLink e s t }] (hst : s ≠ t)
  (k : ℕ) :
  (∀ (X : Finset α),
      s ∉ X →
        t ∉ X → X.card < k → ((G.deleteEdges {e | G.IsLink e s t}).deleteVerts ↑X).Reachable s t) ↔
    ∃ P,
      Function.Injective P ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k ⊕ { e // G.IsLink e s t }), (P i).IsPath) ∧
          Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)
Graph.forall_reachable_deleteEdges_delet.doc:
**Menger's theorem for adjacent vertices, predicate form.** For distinct points,
after deleting every direct edge, every set of fewer than `k` nonterminal points leaves
the terminals reachable exactly when there are distinct internally disjoint paths indexed by
`Fin k ⊕ {e // G.IsLink e s t}`.

Graph.forall_exists_reachable_deleteVert.signature:
Graph.forall_exists_reachable_deleteVerts_iff_exists_paths.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v}
  {G : Graph α β} [Finite ↑G.vertexSet] (A B : Finset α) (hA : ↑A ⊆ G.vertexSet)
  (hB : ↑B ⊆ G.vertexSet) (k : ℕ) :
  (∀ (X : Finset α), X.card < k → ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, (G.deleteVerts ↑X).Reachable a b) ↔
    ∃ a b P,
      (∀ (i : Fin k), a i ∈ A) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), b i ∈ B) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
            (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ x ∈ (P i).support, x ≠ a i → x ≠ b i → x ∉ A ∧ x ∉ B) ∧
              Pairwise fun i j => (P i).support.Disjoint (P j).support
Graph.forall_exists_reachable_deleteVert.doc:
**Menger's theorem for vertex-disjoint paths between vertex sets in a multigraph, predicate
form.** Let `A` and `B` be finite sets of actual vertices of a multigraph with finitely many actual
vertices. Deleting any set of fewer than `k` vertices leaves some vertex of `B` reachable from
some vertex of `A` exactly when there are `k` pairwise vertex-disjoint `A`–`B` paths whose
interiors avoid both terminal sets.

Graph.forall_exists_reachable_deleteEdge.signature:
Graph.forall_exists_reachable_deleteEdges_iff_exists_paths.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v}
  {G : Graph α β} [Finite ↑G.vertexSet] [Finite ↑G.edgeSet] {A B : Finset α} (hAB : Disjoint A B)
  (k : ℕ) :
  (∀ (F : Finset β), F.card < k → ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, (G.deleteEdges ↑F).Reachable a b) ↔
    ∃ a b P,
      (∀ (i : Fin k), a i ∈ A) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), b i ∈ B) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
            (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ v ∈ (P i).support, v ≠ a i → v ≠ b i → v ∉ A ∧ v ∉ B) ∧
              Pairwise fun i j => (P i).edges.Disjoint (P j).edges
Graph.forall_exists_reachable_deleteEdge.doc:
**Menger's theorem for edge-disjoint paths between vertex sets in a multigraph, predicate
form.** For disjoint finite sets `A` and `B` in a finite multigraph, deleting fewer than `k` edges
always leaves some vertex of `B` reachable from some vertex of `A` exactly when there are `k`
pairwise edge-disjoint `A`–`B` paths with no internal terminal vertex.

Graph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_sum_e.signature:
Graph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_sum_eq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β} {s t : α}
  [Finite ↑G.vertexSet] [DecidableEq α] (c : α → ℕ) (hst : s ≠ t) (hadj : ¬G.Adj s t) :
  ∃ k P X,
    (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
      (∀ (v : α), v ≠ s → v ≠ t → {i | v ∈ (P i).support}.card ≤ c v) ∧
        ↑X ⊆ G.vertexSet ∧ s ∉ X ∧ t ∉ X ∧ ¬(G.deleteVerts ↑X).Reachable s t ∧ ∑ v ∈ X, c v = k
Graph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_sum_e.doc:
**Vertex-capacitated Menger's theorem for multigraphs.** Let `s ≠ t` be points of a multigraph
with finitely many actual vertices, joined by no edge, and let `c v` be a capacity on every vertex.
Some family of `k` paths from `s` to `t`, in which every vertex `v` other than `s` and `t` lies on
at most `c v` members, and some set `X` of actual vertices avoiding `s` and `t`, whose deletion
leaves `s` and `t` unreachable, satisfy `∑ v ∈ X, c v = k`. By
`Graph.card_le_sum_of_not_reachable_deleteVerts`, the family is then largest and the separator of
least weight.

Graph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_card_.signature:
Graph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_card_eq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β}
  {s t : α} [Finite ↑G.vertexSet] (hst : s ≠ t) (hadj : ¬G.Adj s t) :
  ∃ k P X,
    Function.Injective P ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)) ∧
          ↑X ⊆ G.vertexSet ∧ s ∉ X ∧ t ∉ X ∧ ¬(G.deleteVerts ↑X).Reachable s t ∧ X.card = k
Graph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_card_.doc:
**Menger's theorem for internally vertex-disjoint paths in a multigraph.** Let `s ≠ t` be
points of a multigraph with finitely many actual vertices, joined by no edge. Some family of `k`
distinct paths from `s` to `t`, pairwise sharing no vertex other than `s` and `t`, and some set of
`k` actual vertices avoiding `s` and `t`, whose deletion leaves `s` and `t` unreachable, exist. By
`Graph.card_le_encard_of_not_reachable_deleteVerts`, the family is then largest and the separator
smallest.

Graph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_card_.signature:
Graph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_card_add_card_eq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β}
  {s t : α} [Finite ↑G.vertexSet] [Finite { e // G.IsLink e s t }] (hst : s ≠ t) :
  ∃ k P X,
    Function.Injective P ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin k ⊕ { e // G.IsLink e s t }), (P i).IsPath) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)) ∧
          (∀ (e : { e // G.IsLink e s t }), P (Sum.inr e) = ⋯.toWalk) ∧
            ↑X ⊆ G.vertexSet ∧
              s ∉ X ∧
                t ∉ X ∧
                  ¬((G.deleteEdges {e | G.IsLink e s t}).deleteVerts ↑X).Reachable s t ∧ X.card = k
Graph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_card_.doc:
**Menger's theorem for internally vertex-disjoint paths between possibly adjacent vertices.**
Let `s ≠ t` be points of a multigraph with finitely many actual vertices and finitely many edges
joining the terminals.  For some `k`, there are distinct internally disjoint paths
indexed by `Fin k ⊕ {e // G.IsLink e s t}`.  The path indexed by a direct edge is that one-edge
path.  There is also a set `X` of `k` actual vertices such that deleting `X` and all direct edges
separates `s` from `t`.

Graph.exists_paths_setSeparator_sum_eq.signature:
Graph.exists_paths_setSeparator_sum_eq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β}
  [Finite ↑G.vertexSet] [DecidableEq α] (c : α → ℕ) (A B : Finset α) (hA : ↑A ⊆ G.vertexSet)
  (hB : ↑B ⊆ G.vertexSet) :
  ∃ k a b P X,
    (∀ (i : Fin k), a i ∈ A) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin k), b i ∈ B) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ x ∈ (P i).support, x ≠ a i → x ≠ b i → x ∉ A ∧ x ∉ B) ∧
            (∀ (x : α), {i | x ∈ (P i).support}.card ≤ c x) ∧
              ↑X ⊆ G.vertexSet ∧
                (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(G.deleteVerts ↑X).Reachable a b) ∧ ∑ x ∈ X, c x = k
Graph.exists_paths_setSeparator_sum_eq.doc:
**Vertex-capacitated Menger's theorem between vertex sets in a multigraph.** Let `A` and `B`
be finite sets of actual vertices of a multigraph with finitely many actual vertices. Some family
of `k` paths, the `i`-th from `a i ∈ A` to `b i ∈ B` with its other vertices in neither terminal
set, and some set `X` of actual vertices satisfy the following: every vertex `v` lies on at most
`c v` members, deleting `X` destroys all `A`–`B` reachability, and `∑ v ∈ X, c v = k`.

Graph.exists_paths_setSeparator_card_eq.signature:
Graph.exists_paths_setSeparator_card_eq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β}
  [Finite ↑G.vertexSet] (A B : Finset α) (hA : ↑A ⊆ G.vertexSet) (hB : ↑B ⊆ G.vertexSet) :
  ∃ k a b P X,
    (∀ (i : Fin k), a i ∈ A) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin k), b i ∈ B) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ x ∈ (P i).support, x ≠ a i → x ≠ b i → x ∉ A ∧ x ∉ B) ∧
            (Pairwise fun i j => (P i).support.Disjoint (P j).support) ∧
              ↑X ⊆ G.vertexSet ∧ (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(G.deleteVerts ↑X).Reachable a b) ∧ X.card = k
Graph.exists_paths_setSeparator_card_eq.doc:
**Menger's theorem for vertex-disjoint paths between vertex sets in a multigraph.** Let `A`
and `B` be finite sets of actual vertices of a multigraph with finitely many actual vertices.
Some family of `k` pairwise vertex-disjoint paths, the `i`-th from `a i ∈ A` to `b i ∈ B` with
its other vertices in neither terminal set, and some set `X` of `k` actual vertices whose deletion
destroys all `A`–`B` reachability exist.

Graph.exists_paths_setEdgeSeparator_card.signature:
Graph.exists_paths_setEdgeSeparator_card_eq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β}
  [Finite ↑G.vertexSet] [Finite ↑G.edgeSet] {A B : Finset α} (hAB : Disjoint A B) :
  ∃ k a b P F,
    (∀ (i : Fin k), a i ∈ A) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin k), b i ∈ B) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin k), ∀ v ∈ (P i).support, v ≠ a i → v ≠ b i → v ∉ A ∧ v ∉ B) ∧
            (Pairwise fun i j => (P i).edges.Disjoint (P j).edges) ∧
              ↑F ⊆ G.edgeSet ∧ (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(G.deleteEdges ↑F).Reachable a b) ∧ F.card = k
Graph.exists_paths_setEdgeSeparator_card.doc:
**Menger's theorem for edge-disjoint paths between vertex sets in a multigraph.** Let `A` and
`B` be disjoint finite vertex sets of a multigraph with finitely many actual vertices and edges.
Some family of pairwise edge-disjoint paths from `A` to `B`, with no internal vertex in
either terminal set, has as many members as some set of actual edges whose deletion separates
`B` from `A`. Shared endpoints are allowed.

Graph.exists_paths_edgeSeparator_card_eq.signature:
Graph.exists_paths_edgeSeparator_card_eq.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β} {s t : α}
  [Finite ↑G.vertexSet] [Finite ↑G.edgeSet] (hst : s ≠ t) :
  ∃ k P F,
    (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
      (Pairwise fun i j => (P i).edges.Disjoint (P j).edges) ∧
        ↑F ⊆ G.edgeSet ∧ ¬(G.deleteEdges ↑F).Reachable s t ∧ F.card = k
Graph.exists_paths_edgeSeparator_card_eq.doc:
**Menger's theorem for edge-disjoint paths in a multigraph.** For distinct points `s` and `t`
of a multigraph with finitely many actual vertices and edges, some family of `s`–`t` paths, no two
of which traverse a common edge, has as many members as some set of actual edges whose deletion
leaves `s` and `t` unreachable. By `Graph.card_le_encard_of_not_reachable_deleteEdges`, the family
is then largest and the set of edges smallest.

Graph.exists_orientation_indegree_eq_iff.signature:
Graph.exists_orientation_indegree_eq_iff.{u, v} {V : Type u} {E : Type v} {G : Graph V E}
  [Fintype ↑G.edgeSet] [Fintype ↑G.vertexSet] (d : ↑G.vertexSet → ℕ) :
  (∃ o, ∀ (x : ↑G.vertexSet), o.indegree x = d x) ↔
    ∑ x, d x = Fintype.card ↑G.edgeSet ∧
      ∀ (S : Finset ↑G.vertexSet), (G.internalEdges S).card ≤ ∑ x ∈ S, d x
Graph.exists_orientation_indegree_eq_iff.doc:
**Hakimi's theorem.** A finite multigraph has an orientation with indegree `d` exactly when
`d` sums to the number of actual edges and every vertex set `S` has at most `d(S)` internal
edges.

Graph.exists_flow_val_eq_edgeCutCapacity.signature:
Graph.exists_flow_val_eq_edgeCutCapacity_mem.{u, v, w} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {K : Type w}
  {G : Graph α β} [Fintype ↑G.vertexSet] [Fintype ↑G.edgeSet]
  [(x y : ↑G.vertexSet) → Fintype (G.BidirectedHom x y)] [AddCommGroup K] [LinearOrder K]
  [IsOrderedAddMonoid K] {c : ↑G.edgeSet → K} {s t : ↑G.vertexSet} (hst : s ≠ t) (hc : 0 ≤ c)
  (H : AddSubgroup K) (hcH : ∀ (e : ↑G.edgeSet), c e ∈ H) :
  ∃ f,
    f.toFun.IsAcyclic ∧
      (∀ ⦃x y : ↑G.vertexSet⦄ (a : G.BidirectedHom x y), f.toFun a ∈ H) ∧
        ∃ S, s ∈ S ∧ t ∉ S ∧ f.val = G.edgeCutCapacity c S
Graph.exists_flow_val_eq_edgeCutCapacity.doc:
**Undirected max-flow/min-cut theorem with integrality.** For nonnegative capacities on the
edges of a multigraph, all lying in an additive subgroup `H`, and distinct actual vertices `s` and
`t`, some acyclic `s`–`t` flow with all values in `H` has value equal to the capacity of some set of
actual vertices containing `s` but not `t`. By `TauCeti.Flow.val_le_edgeCutCapacity` this flow is
maximum and this cut is minimum. Being acyclic, the flow vanishes on every loop arrow and on one of
the two arrows of every nonloop edge.

Graph.exists_flow_val_eq_edgeCutCapacity.signature:
Graph.exists_flow_val_eq_edgeCutCapacity.{u, v, w} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {K : Type w}
  {G : Graph α β} [Fintype ↑G.vertexSet] [Fintype ↑G.edgeSet]
  [(x y : ↑G.vertexSet) → Fintype (G.BidirectedHom x y)] [AddCommGroup K] [LinearOrder K]
  [IsOrderedAddMonoid K] {c : ↑G.edgeSet → K} {s t : ↑G.vertexSet} (hst : s ≠ t) (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
  ∃ f, f.toFun.IsAcyclic ∧ ∃ S, s ∈ S ∧ t ∉ S ∧ f.val = G.edgeCutCapacity c S
Graph.exists_flow_val_eq_edgeCutCapacity.doc:
**Undirected max-flow/min-cut theorem.** For nonnegative capacities on the edges of a
multigraph and distinct actual vertices `s` and `t`, some acyclic `s`–`t` flow has value equal to
the capacity of some set of actual vertices containing `s` but not `t`. By
`TauCeti.Flow.val_le_edgeCutCapacity` this flow is maximum and this cut is minimum.

Graph.Walk.signature: Graph.Walk.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (G : Graph α β) : α → α → Type (max u v)
Graph.Walk.doc:
An edge-labelled walk in a multigraph. Each step records an edge together with its
incidence; a zero-length walk may be based at any ambient point.

Graph.IsVertexConnected.isEdgeConnected.signature:
Graph.IsVertexConnected.isEdgeConnected.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β} {k : ℕ}
  (h : G.IsVertexConnected k) : G.IsEdgeConnected k
Graph.IsVertexConnected.isEdgeConnected.doc:
**Whitney's inequality for multigraphs**, predicate form: a `k`-vertex-connected multigraph
is `k`-edge-connected. Parallel edges count separately toward edge connectivity, while loops
affect neither side.

Graph.IsBipartition.exists_isCapacitated.doc:
**Kőnig's theorem for multiset capacitated matchings.** Let `L` and `R` form a bipartition of a
multigraph with finitely many actual edges, and let `b v : ℕ` be a capacity on every actual vertex.
Some multiset capacitated matching `x` and some vertex cover `C` satisfy
`∑ e, x e = ∑ v ∈ C, b v`. By `Graph.IsCapacitatedMatching.sum_le_sum_of_isVertexCover`, the
matching is then largest and the cover of least weight.

Geometry.SimplicialComplex.space_cone_of.doc:
Coning a triangulation of the intrinsic frontier of a compact convex set `C` to a point of the
intrinsic interior of `C` triangulates `C`: every point of `C` is either the apex or lies on a
segment from the apex to a point of the intrinsic frontier.

Geometry.SimplicialComplex.cone.signature:
Geometry.SimplicialComplex.cone.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Field 𝕜] [LinearOrder 𝕜]
  [IsStrictOrderedRing 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module 𝕜 E] [DecidableEq E]
  (K : Geometry.SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E) (p : E) (h : K.IsConeApex p) : Geometry.SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E
Geometry.SimplicialComplex.cone.doc:
The cone `pK` on a simplicial complex `K` with apex `p`. Its faces are the nonempty finite sets
whose vertices other than `p` form a face of `K` or are empty: the faces of `K`, the faces of `K`
with `p` adjoined, and the vertex `{p}`.

Geometry.SimplicialComplex.IsConeApex.signature:
Geometry.SimplicialComplex.IsConeApex.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Field 𝕜]
  [LinearOrder 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module 𝕜 E] (K : Geometry.SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E)
  (p : E) : Prop
Geometry.SimplicialComplex.IsConeApex.doc:
A point `p` is a *cone apex* for a geometric simplicial complex `K` if `p ∉ |K|` and every
segment from `p` to a point `y ∈ |K|` meets `|K|` only at `y`. These are the conditions under
which joining `p` to the faces of `K` gives a simplicial complex, the cone `K.cone p h`.

Function.Involutive.orbitCount_finRotate.signature:
Function.Involutive.orbitCount_finRotate_mul_add_orbitCount_eq_iff {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]
  {σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)} (hinv : Function.Involutive ⇑σ) :
  TauCeti.orbitCount (finRotate n * σ) + TauCeti.orbitCount σ = n + 1 ↔ σ.IsNoncrossingMatching
Function.Involutive.orbitCount_finRotate.doc:
**The boundary-count criterion for noninterleaving.** A chord diagram on a nonempty boundary
circle, with matching an involution `σ` and `m = n - orbitCount σ` bands, has exactly `m + 1`
boundary cycles if and only if no two of its bands interleave.

FreeGroup.isConj_iff_isRotated_reduceCyc.signature:
FreeGroup.isConj_iff_isRotated_reduceCyclically.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [DecidableEq α]
  {x y : FreeGroup α} :
  IsConj x y ↔ FreeGroup.reduceCyclically x.toWord ~r FreeGroup.reduceCyclically y.toWord
FreeGroup.isConj_iff_isRotated_reduceCyc.doc:
**Conjugacy criterion in free groups.** Two elements of a free group are conjugate exactly
when the cyclic reductions of their reduced words are cyclic rotations of each other.

FormalGroup.logIso.signature:
FormalGroup.logIso.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (F : FormalGroup R) [Algebra ℚ R] :
  TauCeti.FormalGroupIso F FormalGroup.𝔾ₐ
FormalGroup.logIso.doc:
The normalized logarithm is a strict isomorphism from `F` to the additive formal group,
with the formal exponential as its inverse.

FormalGroup.height_eq_height_iff_nonempt.signature:
FormalGroup.height_eq_height_iff_nonempty_formalGroupIso.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  [IsSepClosed K] {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP K p] (F G : FormalGroup K) [F.IsComm]
  [G.IsComm] : F.height p = G.height p ↔ Nonempty (TauCeti.FormalGroupIso F G)
FormalGroup.height_eq_height_iff_nonempt.doc:
**Lazard's classification of formal group laws by height.** Over a separably closed field `K`
of characteristic `p`, two commutative formal group laws are isomorphic exactly when they have the
same height. In height `⊤` both are isomorphic to the additive formal group law.

FormalGroup.height.signature: FormalGroup.height.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] (F : FormalGroup K) (p : ℕ) : ℕ∞
FormalGroup.height.doc:
The **height** of a formal group law `F` over a field `K` of characteristic `p`: `⊤` if
multiplication by `p` on `F` is zero, and otherwise the exponent `h` such that the first nonzero
term of `[p]_F(T)` has degree `p ^ h` (see `FormalGroup.height_eq_natCast_iff`).

FormalGroup.exists_order_nsmulSeries_eq_.signature:
FormalGroup.exists_order_nsmulSeries_eq_pow.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (F : FormalGroup R)
  [F.IsComm] {p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hpR : ↑p = 0) (h0 : F.nsmulSeries p ≠ 0) :
  ∃ h, h ≠ 0 ∧ (F.nsmulSeries p).order = ↑(p ^ h)
FormalGroup.exists_order_nsmulSeries_eq_.doc:
**The `p`-series has order a power of `p`** in characteristic `p`: if `p` is a prime with
`p = 0` in `R` and `F` is commutative, then either `[p]_F = 0` or the first nonzero term of
`[p]_F` has degree `p ^ h` for some `h ≥ 1`.

FormalGroup.TopNilpotentPoint.signature:
FormalGroup.TopNilpotentPoint.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (F : FormalGroup R)
  (A : Type u_2) [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] : Type u_2
FormalGroup.TopNilpotentPoint.doc:
The **points of a formal group law `F` in `A`**: the elements of a topological ring `A`
satisfying `PowerSeries.HasEval`, that is, the topologically nilpotent elements. Evaluation of
power series over `R` at these elements converges when `A` is a complete, Hausdorff, linearly
topologised `R`-algebra; under those assumptions they form a group under `x +_F y = F(x, y)`.
This is the analogue for `A` of the power-series carrier `F.Point σ`.

This is a structure rather than a subtype of `A` so that its group law, which depends on `F`, is
not confused with the ring operations of `A`.

FirstOrder.Language.aElementary_of_tarsk.signature:
FirstOrder.Language.aElementary_of_tarskiVaught.{u, v, w, w'} {L : FirstOrder.Language} {M : Type w}
  {N : Type w'} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] {A : L.Fragment} (f : L.Embedding N M)
  (htv :
    ∀ {n : ℕ} (φ : L.BoundedFormulaω Empty (n + 1)),
      ⟨n, FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.all φ⟩ ∈ A →
        ∀ (a : Fin n → N),
          (∃ m, ¬FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.Realize φ Empty.elim (Fin.snoc (⇑f ∘ a) m)) →
            ∃ b,
              ¬FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.Realize φ Empty.elim
                  (Fin.snoc (⇑f ∘ a) (f b))) :
  FirstOrder.Language.AElementary A f
FirstOrder.Language.aElementary_of_tarsk.doc:
**The fragment Tarski–Vaught criterion.** If, for every universal member `∀ x, φ` of `A` and
every tuple `a` from `N`, whenever `φ` has a counterexample at `f ∘ a` in `M` it has one in the
image of `f`, then `f` is `A`-elementary.

FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.realize_conj.doc:
**A countable theory is one sentence.** A structure satisfies the conjunction of a countable
theory exactly when it is a model of the theory.

FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.exists_count.doc:
**The omitting types theorem for a countable formation-closed fragment.** A satisfiable theory
of sentences of the fragment has a countable nonempty model, in any universe, omitting any
countable family of partial types in the fragment, none isolated over the theory in the fragment.
Countability of the language follows from countability and formation closure of the fragment.

FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.conjunction.signature:
FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.conjunction.{u, v} {L : FirstOrder.Language} (T : L.Theoryω)
  (hT : Set.Countable T) : L.Sentenceω
FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.conjunction.doc:
The **conjunction of a countable theory**: its sentences, enumerated into the carrier `ℕ`
along `IndexCoding.ofEncodableWith`, joined by one countable conjunction. Indices that code no
sentence carry `⊤`.

FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.Model.signature:
FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.Model.{u, v, w} {L : FirstOrder.Language} (T : L.Theoryω) (M : Type w)
  [L.Structure M] : Prop
FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.Model.doc:
A structure is a **model** of an `L_{ω₁ω}` theory when it satisfies every sentence of the
theory.

FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.signature: FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.{u, v} (L : FirstOrder.Language) : Type (max u v)
FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.doc: An `L_{ω₁ω}` theory: a set of `L_{ω₁ω}` sentences.

FirstOrder.Language.StrongHomClass.theor.doc: Isomorphic structures are models of the same `L_{ω₁ω}` theories.

FirstOrder.Language.ConsistencyProperty..signature:
FirstOrder.Language.ConsistencyProperty.model_existence_omitting.{u, v, w, u_1}
  {L : FirstOrder.Language} [Countable ((n : ℕ) × L.Functions n)]
  [Countable ((n : ℕ) × L.Relations n)] (C : L.ConsistencyProperty) {ι : Type u_1} [Countable ι]
  {n : ι → ℕ} (p : (i : ι) → Set ((L.withConstants ℕ).BoundedFormulaω Empty (n i)))
  (hp : ∀ (i : ι), (p i).Countable)
  (hC :
    ∀ (i : ι),
      ∀ t ∈ C.sets,
        ∀ (c : Fin (n i) → ℕ),
          ∃ ψ ∈ p i,
            insert
                (FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.substBounds (fun j => (L.con (c j)).term)
                    ψ).not
                t ∈
              C.sets)
  {s : (L.withConstants ℕ).Theoryω} (hs : s ∈ C.sets) (hsc : Set.Countable s) :
  ∃ M x,
    Countable M ∧
      Nonempty M ∧
        s.Model M ∧
          (Function.Surjective fun c => ↑(L.con c)) ∧
            ∀ (i : ι), FirstOrder.Language.OmitsType M (p i)
FirstOrder.Language.ConsistencyProperty..doc:
**The model existence theorem with omitted types.** Over a language with countably many
function and relation symbols, let `p i` be countably many countable partial types such that
every member `t` of the consistency property `C` and every tuple `c` of Henkin constants admit
some `ψ ∈ p i` for which `t` together with the refutation `¬ψ[c]` is again a member. Then every
countable member `s` of `C` has a countable nonempty model, in any universe `w`, in which every
element is the interpretation of a Henkin constant and which omits every `p i`.

FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.re.doc:
**Transport a formula along a coding of its carrier**: each `ι`-indexed conjunction or
disjunction becomes the corresponding coded connective at carrier `κ`.

FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.fr.signature:
FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.freeVarSupport.{u, v, u', uι} {L : FirstOrder.Language}
  {α : Type u'} {ι : Type uι} {n : ℕ} : L.BoundedFormulaInf ι α n → Set α
FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.fr.doc:
The **free-variable support** of an infinitary formula: the set of free variables that occur
in one of its atoms. Infinitary connectives take the union over all their branches, so the support
may be infinite.

FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.signature:
FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.{u, v, u', uι} (L : FirstOrder.Language) (ι : Type uι)
  (α : Type u') : ℕ → Type (max u v u' uι)
FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.doc:
An infinitary bounded formula of `L_{∞ω}`, with infinitary conjunctions and disjunctions
branching over the fixed carrier `ι`, free variables indexed by `α`, and `n` additional bound
variables available.

Finset.two_mul_sum_range_choose_add_sum_.signature:
Finset.two_mul_sum_range_choose_add_sum_sum_tsub.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} (s : Finset ι) (k : ι → ℕ) :
  2 * ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (s.sup k), ({i ∈ s | j < k i}.card + 1).choose 2 +
      ∑ i ∈ s, ∑ i' ∈ s, (k i' - k i) =
    (s.card + 1) * ∑ i ∈ s, k i
Finset.two_mul_sum_range_choose_add_sum_.doc:
**The Conway–Sloane exponent identity.** Twice `∑_{j < max k} binom(Nⱼ + 1, 2)`, where
`Nⱼ = #{i ∈ s | j < kᵢ}`, plus `∑_{i, i' ∈ s} (k_{i'} - kᵢ)` (truncated subtraction) is
`(#s + 1) ∑_{i ∈ s} kᵢ`. The first sum is the exponent of `p` in the local density of the
diagonal Jordan form `diag(uᵢ pᵏⁱ)` at an odd prime, the second is the exponent of `√p` in the
cross terms of its Conway–Sloane `p`-mass.

Finset.sum_pow_of_commute_of_mul_self_eq.signature:
Finset.sum_pow_of_commute_of_mul_self_eq_zero.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [Semiring R] {ι : Type u_2}
  (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → R) (hc : (↑s).Pairwise (Function.onFun Commute x))
  (hx : ∀ i ∈ s, x i * x i = 0) (n : ℕ) :
  (∑ i ∈ s, x i) ^ n = n.factorial • ∑ t, (↑t).noncommProd x ⋯
Finset.sum_pow_of_commute_of_mul_self_eq.doc:
**Multinomial theorem for square-zero elements.** If the `x i` commute pairwise and square to
zero on `s`, then `(∑ i ∈ s, x i) ^ n` is `n !` times the sum, over the `n`-element subsets `t` of
`s`, of the products of the `x i` with `i ∈ t`.

Finset.sum_piAntidiag_prod_choose.signature:
Finset.sum_piAntidiag_prod_choose.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (K : ι → ℕ)
  (n : ℕ) : ∑ k ∈ s.piAntidiag n, ∏ i ∈ s, (K i).choose (k i) = (∑ i ∈ s, K i).choose n
Finset.sum_piAntidiag_prod_choose.doc:
**Vandermonde's identity** for finitely many groups: the ways of choosing `n` objects from
groups of sizes `K i`, `i ∈ s`, sorted by how many come from each group.

Finset.sum_filter_piAntidiag_prod_choose.signature:
Finset.sum_filter_piAntidiag_prod_choose_fiberwise.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} [DecidableEq ι]
  {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] (f : ι → κ) (K : ι → ℕ) (m : κ → ℕ) :
  ∑ k ∈ Finset.univ.piAntidiag (∑ j, m j) with ∀ (j : κ), ∑ i with f i = j, k i = m j,
      ∏ i, (K i).choose (k i) =
    ∏ j, (∑ i with f i = j, K i).choose (m j)
Finset.sum_filter_piAntidiag_prod_choose.doc:
**Vandermonde's identity** grouped along a map `f : ι → κ`: the ways of choosing objects from
groups of sizes `K i` so that, for every `j`, exactly `m j` objects come from the groups in the
fibre of `f` over `j`.  Merging the groups of each fibre into one group of size
`∑ i with f i = j, K i` counts these choices as a product of binomial coefficients.

Finset.norm_le_integral_norm_sum_smul_ra.signature:
Finset.norm_le_integral_norm_sum_smul_rademacher.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2}
  {E : Type u_3} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] {ε : ι → Ω → ℝ} (s : Finset ι) (v : ι → E)
  (hε : ∀ i ∈ s, ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw (ε i) TauCeti.Probability.rademacherMeasure P)
  (hind : (↑s).Pairwise fun i j => ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (ε i) (ε j) P) {j : ι} (hj : j ∈ s) :
  ‖v j‖ ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω), ‖∑ i ∈ s, ε i ω • v i‖ ∂P
Finset.norm_le_integral_norm_sum_smul_ra.doc:
**Rademacher convexity inequality.** Every summand's norm is bounded by the expected
norm of the signed sum. Pairwise independence of the Rademacher signs suffices.

Finset.integerProjection.signature:
Finset.integerProjection {n : ℕ} (P : Finset (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) ℤ)) :
  Finset (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ)
Finset.integerProjection.doc:
The Collins projection of a finite family `P` of integer polynomials in the variables
`X 0, …, X n`, computed over `ℤ`: single out the distinguished variable `X 0` and take the Collins
projection of the resulting family of polynomials in `X 0` over `ℤ[X 1, …, X n]`.

Finset.image_map_integerProjection.signature:
Finset.image_map_integerProjection {n : ℕ} [DecidableEq (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℝ)]
  (P : Finset (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) ℤ)) :
  Finset.image (⇑(MvPolynomial.map (Int.castRingHom ℝ))) P.integerProjection =
    P.integerFamily.collinsProjection
Finset.image_map_integerProjection.doc:
**The integer projection computes the real projection.** Mapping the integer projection of
`P` to `ℝ` gives the Collins projection of the real family of `P`.

Finset.exists_injective_of_mul_card_le_c.signature:
Finset.exists_injective_of_mul_card_le_card_smul.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [SMul α β]
  [DecidableEq β] {D : Finset α} {k : ℕ} (h : ∀ (F : Finset β), k * F.card ≤ (D • F).card) :
  ∃ j, Function.Injective j ∧ ∀ (p : β × Fin k), ∃ d ∈ D, d • p.1 = j p
Finset.exists_injective_of_mul_card_le_c.doc:
**Hall's theorem for expanding sets.** If a finite set `D` acting on `β` satisfies
`k · |F| ≤ |D • F|` for every finite `F ⊆ β`, then there is an injective map
`j : β × Fin k → β` moving each point by an element of `D`: `j (x, i) = d • x` for some `d ∈ D`.

This applies Hall's marriage theorem to the neighbour sets `D • {x}` indexed by `β × Fin k`.

Finset.IsSquarefreeBasis.signature: Finset.IsSquarefreeBasis.{u_1} {D : Type u_1} [CommRing D] (F B : Finset (Polynomial D)) : Prop
Finset.IsSquarefreeBasis.doc:
`B` is a squarefree basis of the finite family `F` of polynomials over `D`: its members
are primitive, squarefree, of positive degree and pairwise relatively prime, and every member
of `F` is a constant times a product of powers of members of `B`.

FGModuleCat.isLocalRing_end_of_indecompo.doc:
**Fitting's lemma** in `FGModuleCat A`: a finitely generated indecomposable module of finite
length (Noetherian and Artinian) has a local endomorphism ring.

FGModuleCat.abelian_isFrobenius.signature:
FGModuleCat.abelian_isFrobenius.{u, v, w} (k : Type w) [Field k] {A : Type u} [Ring A] [Algebra k A]
  [FiniteDimensional k A] [Small.{v, u} A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (hl : Module.Injective A A)
  (hr : Module.Injective Aᵐᵒᵖ A) : (TauCeti.ExactStructure.abelian (FGModuleCat A)).IsFrobenius
FGModuleCat.abelian_isFrobenius.doc:
**The module-category Frobenius theorem.** For a finite-dimensional algebra `A` over a field
which is self-injective on both sides, the canonical exact structure on the category of finitely
generated (equivalently, finite-dimensional) `A`-modules is Frobenius.

FDRep.trace_eq_smul.signature:
FDRep.trace_eq_smul.{u, v} {k : Type u} {G : Type v} [Field k] [Group G] {V : FDRep k G}
  (f : V ⟶ V) :
  TauCeti.trace f =
    (LinearMap.trace k ↑V.V) (ModuleCat.Hom.hom f.hom.hom) •
      CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id
        (CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorUnit (FDRep k G))
FDRep.trace_eq_smul.doc:
The categorical trace of an equivariant endomorphism of a finite-dimensional representation
is its linear trace, acting on the trivial representation by scalar multiplication.

FDRep.exists_pos_finrank_hom_tensorPower.signature:
FDRep.exists_pos_finrank_hom_tensorPower_lt_card_conjClasses.{v} {G : Type v} [Group G] [Finite G]
  (V X : FDRep ℂ G) (hV : Function.Injective ⇑V.ρ) (hX : 0 < Module.finrank ℂ ↑X.V) :
  ∃ n < Nat.card (ConjClasses G), 0 < Module.finrank ℂ (X ⟶ V.tensorPower n)
FDRep.exists_pos_finrank_hom_tensorPower.doc:
**Burnside–Brauer, conjugacy-class bound.** Every nonzero finite-dimensional complex
representation has a nonzero map into a tensor power of a faithful representation, with exponent
strictly smaller than the number of conjugacy classes.

FDRep.clifford_restrict_iso_of_isAtom.signature:
FDRep.clifford_restrict_iso_of_isAtom.{u, v} {k : Type u} {G : Type v} [Field k] [Group G]
  {N : Subgroup G} [N.Normal] [IsAlgClosed k] (W : FDRep k G) [CategoryTheory.Simple W]
  (σ : Subrepresentation (W.ρ.comp N.subtype)) (hσ : IsAtom σ) :
  ∃ (hfinite : Finite (G ⧸ TauCeti.inertia (FDRep.of σ.toRepresentation))),
    have x := hfinite;
    ∃ e, e ≠ 0 ∧ Nonempty (N.resFDRep W ≅ (FDRep.of σ.toRepresentation).cliffordSum e)
FDRep.clifford_restrict_iso_of_isAtom.doc:
**Clifford's theorem for a specified constituent.** Given a simple constituent `σ` of the
restriction of an irreducible representation to a normal subgroup, the restriction is isomorphic
to `e` copies of every conjugate of `σ`, with the distinct conjugates indexed by the left cosets
of its inertia group.

Algebraic closure makes `k` a splitting field, so the Hom-space dimension in the multiplicity
theorem is the actual number of copies. Finite dimensionality makes the set of isotypic components,
and hence the inertia quotient indexing the sum, finite.

FDRep.clifford_restrict_iso.doc:
**Clifford's theorem, representation form.** The restriction of an irreducible
representation to a normal subgroup is isomorphic to `e` copies of every conjugate of one simple
constituent, with the distinct conjugates indexed by the left cosets of its inertia group.

Algebraic closure makes `k` a splitting field, so the Hom-space dimension in the multiplicity
theorem is the actual number of copies. The conclusion includes the finite inertia quotient that
indexes the sum.

FDRep.clifford_restrict_finrank.signature:
FDRep.clifford_restrict_finrank.{u, v} {k : Type u} {G : Type v} [Field k] [Group G]
  {N : Subgroup G} [N.Normal] [IsAlgClosed k] (W : FDRep k G) [CategoryTheory.Simple W] :
  ∃ V,
    ∃ (_ : CategoryTheory.Simple V) (hfinite : Finite (G ⧸ TauCeti.inertia V)),
      have x := hfinite;
      ∃ e,
        e ≠ 0 ∧
          Nonempty (N.resFDRep W ≅ V.cliffordSum e) ∧
            Module.finrank k ↑W.V = e * (TauCeti.inertia V).index * Module.finrank k ↑V.V
FDRep.clifford_restrict_finrank.doc:
**Clifford's theorem, dimension form.**  The dimension of an irreducible representation of `G`
is the common multiplicity `e` of the constituents of its restriction to `N`, times the number
`[G : inertia V]` of those constituents, times the dimension of one of them.

The decomposition `Res_N W ≅ V.cliffordSum e` that `FDRep.clifford_restrict_iso` supplies is
returned alongside the identity, so that `V` is exhibited as a constituent of the restriction and
not merely named by it.

In particular the index of the inertia group of a constituent divides the dimension of `W`; that
is the arithmetic that `FDRep.clifford_restrict_dvd_finrank` reads off and that
`FDRep.clifford_restrict_inertia_eq_top_of_coprime` exploits.

FDRep.clifford_restrict_dvd_finrank.signature:
FDRep.clifford_restrict_dvd_finrank.{u, v} {k : Type u} {G : Type v} [Field k] [Group G]
  {N : Subgroup G} [N.Normal] [IsAlgClosed k] (W : FDRep k G) [CategoryTheory.Simple W] :
  ∃ V,
    ∃ (_ : CategoryTheory.Simple V) (hfinite : Finite (G ⧸ TauCeti.inertia V)),
      have x := hfinite;
      ∃ e,
        e ≠ 0 ∧
          Nonempty (N.resFDRep W ≅ V.cliffordSum e) ∧
            (TauCeti.inertia V).index ∣ Module.finrank k ↑W.V ∧
              Module.finrank k ↑V.V ∣ Module.finrank k ↑W.V ∧
                (TauCeti.inertia V).index ∣ N.index ∧
                  (TauCeti.inertia V).index ∣ Module.finrank k ↑W.V / (e * Module.finrank k ↑V.V)
FDRep.clifford_restrict_dvd_finrank.doc:
**The divisibilities in Clifford's theorem.**  For an irreducible constituent `V` of the
restriction of an irreducible `W` to a normal subgroup, both the index of the inertia group of `V`
and the dimension of `V` divide the dimension of `W`; the index divides `[G : N]`, and it divides
the quotient `dim W / (e * dim V)` that the dimension identity leaves.

The decomposition `Res_N W ≅ V.cliffordSum e` is carried along from
`FDRep.clifford_restrict_finrank`, so that `V` is exhibited as a constituent of the restriction and
the divisibilities are read as statements about that constituent rather than about some unrelated
irreducible representation of `N`.

This is the form in which the dimension identity of `FDRep.clifford_restrict_finrank` is used.  The
number of distinct conjugates occurring in the restriction is `[G : inertia V]`, and it is
constrained from two sides at once: by the degree of `W`, through the dimension identity, and by
the index of `N`, through `TauCeti.le_inertia`.  Neither constraint mentions the multiplicity `e`,
which the last divisibility divides out instead: `dim W / (e * dim V)` counts the distinct
conjugates.

FDRep.char_eq_zero_or_norm_char_eq_finra.signature:
FDRep.char_eq_zero_or_norm_char_eq_finrank.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [Finite G] (X : FDRep ℂ G)
  [Representation.IsIrreducible X.ρ] {g : G}
  (h : (Nat.card ↑(ConjClasses.mk g).carrier).Coprime (Module.finrank ℂ ↑X.V)) :
  X.character g = 0 ∨ ‖X.character g‖ = ↑(Module.finrank ℂ ↑X.V)
FDRep.char_eq_zero_or_norm_char_eq_finra.doc: **Burnside's vanishing theorem**, for a bundled finite-dimensional complex representation.

FDRep.char_eq_zero_or_exists_apply_eq_sm.signature:
FDRep.char_eq_zero_or_exists_apply_eq_smul.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [Finite G] (X : FDRep ℂ G)
  [Representation.IsIrreducible X.ρ] {g : G}
  (h : (Nat.card ↑(ConjClasses.mk g).carrier).Coprime (Module.finrank ℂ ↑X.V)) :
  X.character g = 0 ∨ ∃ μ, X.ρ g = μ • 1
FDRep.char_eq_zero_or_exists_apply_eq_sm.doc:
**Burnside's vanishing theorem, scalar form**, for a bundled finite-dimensional complex
representation.

Equiv.isSemianalytic_image_iff.signature:
Equiv.isSemianalytic_image_iff.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] {s : Set E} (e : E ≃ F)
  (he : AnalyticOnNhd ℝ (⇑e) Set.univ) (he' : AnalyticOnNhd ℝ (⇑e.symm) Set.univ) :
  TauCeti.IsSemianalytic (⇑e '' s) ↔ TauCeti.IsSemianalytic s
Equiv.isSemianalytic_image_iff.doc:
**Analytic isomorphisms.** For a bijection `e` that is analytic with analytic inverse, the
image `e '' s` is semianalytic if and only if `s` is semianalytic.

Equiv.Perm.rsk_inv.signature:
Equiv.Perm.rsk_inv {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
  (TauCeti.rsk n) σ⁻¹ =
    ⟨((TauCeti.rsk n) σ).fst, (((TauCeti.rsk n) σ).snd.2, ((TauCeti.rsk n) σ).snd.1)⟩
Equiv.Perm.rsk_inv.doc:
**Schützenberger's symmetry theorem.** The Robinson--Schensted correspondence of the
inverse permutation exchanges the insertion and recording tableaux.

Equiv.Perm.orbitCount_add_orbitCount_add.signature:
Equiv.Perm.orbitCount_add_orbitCount_add_orbitCount_mul_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Finite α]
  (σ τ : Equiv.Perm α) :
  TauCeti.orbitCount σ + TauCeti.orbitCount τ + TauCeti.orbitCount (τ * σ) ≤
    Nat.card α + 2 * Nat.card (MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient (↥(Subgroup.closure {σ, τ})) α)
Equiv.Perm.orbitCount_add_orbitCount_add.doc:
**The Euler bound for a pair of permutations.** For permutations `σ` and `τ` of a finite type,
the orbits of `σ`, of `τ` and of `τ * σ` together number at most the number of points plus twice
the number of orbits of the group generated by `σ` and `τ`. For the rotation and edge involution
of a ribbon graph these count vertices, edges and faces, and this is the bound `χ ≤ 2` on each
connected component; equality holds exactly when every component is a sphere.

Equidecomp.exists_iff_exists_finpartitio.signature:
Equidecomp.exists_iff_exists_finpartition.{u_1, u_2} {X : Type u_1} {G : Type u_2} [Group G]
  [MulAction G X] {A B : Set X} :
  (∃ f, f.source = A ∧ f.target = B) ↔
    ∃ P γ, ((↑P.parts).PairwiseDisjoint fun s => γ s • s) ∧ ⋃ s ∈ P.parts, γ s • s = B
Equidecomp.exists_iff_exists_finpartitio.doc:
**Equidecompositions as partitions.** Two sets `A` and `B` are related by an
equidecomposition exactly when there are a finite partition of `A` and a group element `γ s` for
each part `s`, such that the translates `γ s • s` are pairwise disjoint with union `B`.

Equidecomp.Equipartition.signature: Equidecomp.Equipartition.{u_1, u_2} (X : Type u_1) (G : Type u_2) [SMul G X] : Type (max u_1 u_2)
Equidecomp.Equipartition.doc:
An *equipartition* of `X` for an action of `G`: a finite set of pairs `(Aᵢ, gᵢ)` of a nonempty
source piece `Aᵢ : Set X` and a group element `gᵢ : G`, such that the source pieces `Aᵢ` are
pairwise disjoint and the target pieces `gᵢ • Aᵢ` are pairwise disjoint. When `G` is a group
acting on `X`, moving each `Aᵢ` by `gᵢ` is then an equidecomposition of the union of the `Aᵢ` with
the union of the `gᵢ • Aᵢ` (see `Equidecomp.Equipartition.toEquidecomp`).

ENNReal.inner_le_Lp_mul_Lq_tsum.doc:
**Hölder's inequality** for unconditional sums in `ℝ≥0∞`: for conjugate exponents `p` and `q`,
`∑' i, f i * g i ≤ (∑' i, f i ^ p) ^ (1 / p) * (∑' i, g i ^ q) ^ (1 / q)`.
No summability hypotheses are needed; both sides may be infinite.

ENNReal.Lp_add_le_tsum.signature:
ENNReal.Lp_add_le_tsum.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} (f g : ι → ENNReal) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) :
  (∑' (i : ι), (f i + g i) ^ p) ^ (1 / p) ≤
    (∑' (i : ι), f i ^ p) ^ (1 / p) + (∑' (i : ι), g i ^ p) ^ (1 / p)
ENNReal.Lp_add_le_tsum.doc:
**Minkowski's inequality** for unconditional sums in `ℝ≥0∞`: for `1 ≤ p`,
`(∑' i, (f i + g i) ^ p) ^ (1 / p) ≤ (∑' i, f i ^ p) ^ (1 / p) + (∑' i, g i ^ p) ^ (1 / p)`.
No summability hypotheses are needed; both sides may be infinite.

DoubleCoset.doubleCoset_mul_doubleCoset_.signature:
DoubleCoset.doubleCoset_mul_doubleCoset_eq_iUnion_rightCosets.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {G : Type u_1}
  [Group G] {Γ₁ Γ₂ Γ₃ : Subgroup G} {δ₁ δ₂ : G} {ι : Type u_2} {κ : Type u_3} (a : ι → G)
  (b : κ → G) (hcover₁ : DoubleCoset.doubleCoset δ₁ ↑Γ₁ ↑Γ₂ = ⋃ i, MulOpposite.op (a i) • ↑Γ₁)
  (hcover₂ : DoubleCoset.doubleCoset δ₂ ↑Γ₂ ↑Γ₃ = ⋃ j, MulOpposite.op (b j) • ↑Γ₂) :
  DoubleCoset.doubleCoset δ₁ ↑Γ₁ ↑Γ₂ * DoubleCoset.doubleCoset δ₂ ↑Γ₂ ↑Γ₃ =
    ⋃ p, MulOpposite.op (a p.1 * b p.2) • ↑Γ₁
DoubleCoset.doubleCoset_mul_doubleCoset_.doc:
**Shimura's covering identity for a product of double cosets** (§3.4). If `Γ₁ δ₁ Γ₂` is the
union of the right cosets `Γ₁ aᵢ` and `Γ₂ δ₂ Γ₃` is the union of the right cosets `Γ₂ bⱼ`, then
the pointwise product `Γ₁ δ₁ Γ₂ · Γ₂ δ₂ Γ₃` is the union of the right cosets `Γ₁ aᵢ bⱼ`.

The two double cosets splice because `Γ₂ Γ₂ = Γ₂`: an element of the product is `u v` with
`u ∈ Γ₁ δ₁ Γ₂` and `v ∈ Γ₂ δ₂ Γ₃`; writing `v = g bⱼ` with `g ∈ Γ₂` moves `g` into `u`, and `u g`
is again in `Γ₁ δ₁ Γ₂`, hence in some `Γ₁ aᵢ`.

⚠ The union is **not** disjoint, and the family `(i, j) ↦ Γ₁ aᵢ bⱼ` is in general far from
injective. Any repetitions here are right-coset collisions; this theorem neither counts them nor
identifies them with `DoubleCoset.multiplicity`, which uses left-coset representatives. The
identity supplies coverage only, exactly as
`doubleCoset_eq_iUnion_rightCosets_of_forall_exists` does for a single double coset.

DoubleCoset.doubleCoset_eq_iUnion_rightC.signature:
DoubleCoset.doubleCoset_eq_iUnion_rightCosets.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] (Γ₁ Γ₂ : Subgroup G)
  (g : G) :
  DoubleCoset.doubleCoset g ↑Γ₁ ↑Γ₂ = ⋃ v, MulOpposite.op (g * (↑(Quotient.out v))⁻¹) • ↑Γ₁
DoubleCoset.doubleCoset_eq_iUnion_rightC.doc:
**Shimura's decomposition of a double coset into right cosets.** `Γ₁gΓ₂` is the union of the
right cosets `Γ₁ · (g τᵥ⁻¹)`, where `τᵥ` runs over representatives of `Γ₂ ⧸ (Γ₂ ∩ g⁻¹Γ₁g)` — the
mirror of `DoubleCoset.doubleCoset_eq_iUnion_leftCosets`, and of Mathlib's
`doubleCoset_union_rightCoset`, which is indexed by all of `Γ₂` and so repeats each coset.

The inverse on `τᵥ` is what converts the *left*-coset quotient `Γ₂ ⧸ (Γ₂ ∩ g⁻¹Γ₁g)` into an index
for the right cosets: `Γ₁ g τ = Γ₁ g τ'` exactly when `τ'τ⁻¹ ∈ Γ₂ ∩ g⁻¹Γ₁g`.

It lives here rather than beside `doubleCoset_eq_iUnion_leftCosets` because it is phrased with
`DecompQuotient`, which this file defines.

DoubleCoset.doubleCoset_eq_iUnion_rightC.signature:
DoubleCoset.doubleCoset_eq_iUnion_rightCosetRep.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] {Δ : Submonoid G}
  {Γ₁ Γ₂ : Subgroup G} (D : HeckeCoset Δ Γ₁ Γ₂) :
  DoubleCoset.doubleCoset ↑(Quotient.out D) ↑Γ₁ ↑Γ₂ =
    ⋃ v, MulOpposite.op (DoubleCoset.rightCosetRep D v) • ↑Γ₁
DoubleCoset.doubleCoset_eq_iUnion_rightC.doc:
**Shimura's decomposition of the double coset**, in the `rightCosetRep` spelling:
`Γ₁ δ Γ₂ = ⋃ᵥ Γ₁ (δ τᵥ⁻¹)`. Since `rightCosetRep` is not `@[expose]`, this is how a downstream
module reads `DoubleCoset.doubleCoset_eq_iUnion_rightCosets` at the representatives the slash sum
is defined with.

DividedPowerAlgebra.isInternal_homogeneo.doc:
The homogeneous pieces of the divided power algebra form an internal direct sum: the sum
map `⨁ d, Γ^d_R(M) → Γ_R(M)` is bijective.

DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousLawEquiv.signature:
DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousLawEquiv.{u, u_1, u_2} (R : Type u) [CommSemiring R] (M : Type u_1)
  (N : Type u_2) [AddCommMonoid M] [_root_.Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [_root_.Module R N]
  (d : ℕ) :
  (↥(DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousSubmodule d) →ₗ[R] N) ≃ₗ[R]
    ↥(PolynomialLaw.homogeneousSubmodule R M N d)
DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousLawEquiv.doc:
**Roby representability**: composition with the universal law `γ_d` is a linear equivalence
between linear maps `Γ^d_R(M) → N` and homogeneous polynomial laws `M → N` of degree `d`.

DividedPowerAlgebra.gamma.signature:
DividedPowerAlgebra.gamma.{u, u_1} (R : Type u) [CommSemiring R] (M : Type u_1) [AddCommMonoid M]
  [_root_.Module R M] (d : ℕ) : M →ₚₗ[R] ↥(DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousSubmodule d)
DividedPowerAlgebra.gamma.doc:
The universal homogeneous polynomial law `γ_d : M → Γ^d_R(M)` of degree `d`. After scalar
extension to a commutative `R`-algebra `S` it sends `∑ⱼ sⱼ ⊗ mⱼ` to
`∑_{∑ⱼ nⱼ = d} (∏ⱼ sⱼ ^ nⱼ) ⊗ ∏ⱼ dp R nⱼ mⱼ` (see `gamma_toFun_sum_tmul`), and its ground value is
`m ↦ dp R d m` (see `ground_gamma_apply`).

DividedPowerAlgebra.baseChangeHomogeneou.signature:
DividedPowerAlgebra.baseChangeHomogeneousEquiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (R : Type u_1) [CommSemiring R]
  (M : Type u_2) [AddCommMonoid M] [_root_.Module R M] (S : Type u_3) [CommSemiring S] [Algebra R S]
  (d : ℕ) :
  TensorProduct R S ↥(DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousSubmodule d) ≃ₗ[S]
    ↥(DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousSubmodule d)
DividedPowerAlgebra.baseChangeHomogeneou.doc:
**Base change of homogeneous divided powers**: for a commutative `R`-algebra `S`, the base
change isomorphism restricts to an `S`-linear isomorphism
`S ⊗[R] Γ^d_R(M) ≃ₗ[S] Γ^d_S(S ⊗[R] M)` taking `1 ⊗ dp R d m` to `dp S d (1 ⊗ m)`
(`baseChangeHomogeneousEquiv_one_tmul_dp`). No flatness is assumed.

DividedPowerAlgebra.baseChangeEquiv.signature:
DividedPowerAlgebra.baseChangeEquiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (R : Type u_1) [CommSemiring R] (M : Type u_2)
  [AddCommMonoid M] [_root_.Module R M] (S : Type u_3) [CommSemiring S] [Algebra R S] :
  TensorProduct R S (DividedPowerAlgebra R M) ≃ₐ[S] DividedPowerAlgebra S (TensorProduct R S M)
DividedPowerAlgebra.baseChangeEquiv.doc:
**Base change of divided power algebras**: for a commutative `R`-algebra `S`, the canonical
map `S ⊗[R] Γ_R(M) → Γ_S(S ⊗[R] M)` is an isomorphism of `S`-algebras. No flatness is
assumed.

Distribution.translatePairing_eq_of_line.doc:
**Distributions with vanishing derivatives have locally constant regularizations.** If every
directional derivative of `T` vanishes, then `x ↦ T (ρ (· - x))` is constant on every
preconnected open set of translations for which `ρ (· - x)` is supported in `Ω`.

Distribution.fderiv_translatePairing_app.signature:
Distribution.fderiv_translatePairing_apply.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
  {Ω V : TopologicalSpace.Opens E} [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (T : Distribution Ω F ⊤)
  (ρ : TestFunction V ℝ ⊤) {x : E} (hx : Set.MapsTo (fun x_1 => x_1 + x) (tsupport ⇑ρ) ↑Ω) (v : E) :
  (fderiv ℝ (T.translatePairing ρ) x) v = (LineDeriv.lineDerivOp v T).translatePairing ρ x
Distribution.fderiv_translatePairing_app.doc:
**The derivative of a regularization.** At every admissible translation, the derivative of
`x ↦ T (ρ (· - x))` in the direction `v` is the regularization of the distributional derivative
`∂_{v} T`.

Distribution.exists_norm_apply_le.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] {Ω : TopologicalSpace.Opens E}
  (T : Distribution Ω F ⊤) {K : TopologicalSpace.Compacts E} (hK : ↑K ⊆ ↑Ω) :
  ∃ N C,
    0 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (φ : TestFunction Ω ℝ ⊤),
        tsupport ⇑φ ⊆ ↑K →
          ∀ (M : ℝ), 0 ≤ M → (∀ i ≤ N, ∀ (x : E), ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ i (⇑φ) x‖ ≤ M) → ‖T φ‖ ≤ C * M
Distribution.exists_norm_apply_le.doc:
**A distribution has finite order on each compact set.** For a compact `K ⊆ Ω` there are an
order `N` and a constant `C` such that `‖T φ‖ ≤ C * M` for every test function `φ` supported in
`K` whose derivatives of order at most `N` are all bounded by `M`.

DiscreteConvolution.tsum_addRingConvolut.signature:

    (∑' (x : G), f x) ^ 2 * ∑' (x : G), g x ^ 2
DiscreteConvolution.tsum_addRingConvolut.doc:
**Young's inequality** in the other orientation, `‖f ⋆ g‖₂ ≤ ‖f‖₁ ‖g‖₂`, for families in
`ℝ≥0∞` on an additive group, in squared form. On a noncommutative group it does not follow from
`tsum_addRingConvolution_sq_le` by commutativity; it is that inequality on the opposite group.

DiscreteConvolution.tsum_addRingConvolution_sq_le.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [AddGroup G]
  (f g : G → ENNReal) :

    (∑' (x : G), g x) ^ 2 * ∑' (x : G), f x ^ 2
DiscreteConvolution.tsum_addRingConvolut.doc:
**Young's inequality** `‖f ⋆ g‖₂ ≤ ‖g‖₁ ‖f‖₂` for families in `ℝ≥0∞` on an additive group,
in squared form. No summability hypotheses are needed.

DirichletCharacter.LFunction_apply_one_p.doc:
The value at `s = 1` of the `L`-function of a nontrivial quadratic Dirichlet character is a
positive real number.

  (∀ (X : Finset V), s ∉ X → t ∉ X → X.card < k → TauCeti.ReachableAvoiding D.AdjHom (↑X) s t) ↔
    ∃ P, (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧ Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)
Digraph.forall_reachableAvoiding_iff_exi.doc:
**Menger's theorem for vertex deletion in a digraph, predicate form.** Distinct nonadjacent
vertices remain joined after deleting any fewer than `k` other vertices exactly when there are
`k` pairwise internally vertex-disjoint directed paths between them.

Digraph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_sum.signature:
Digraph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_sum_eq.{u} {V : Type u} {D : Digraph V} {s t : V} [Finite V]
  [DecidableEq V] (c : V → ℕ) (hst : s ≠ t) (hadj : ¬D.Adj s t) :
  ∃ k P X,
    (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
      (∀ (v : V), v ≠ s → v ≠ t → {i | v ∈ (P i).vertices}.card ≤ c v) ∧
        s ∉ X ∧ t ∉ X ∧ ¬TauCeti.ReachableAvoiding D.AdjHom (↑X) s t ∧ ∑ v ∈ X, c v = k
Digraph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_sum.doc:
**Vertex-capacitated Menger's theorem for a digraph.** Let `s` and `t` be distinct vertices
with no arrow from `s` to `t`, and let `c v` be the capacity of vertex `v`. Some family of `k`
directed `s`-to-`t` paths respects every nonterminal vertex capacity, and some terminal-excluding
vertex separator has total capacity `k`.

  (hst : s ≠ t) (hadj : ¬D.Adj s t) :
  ∃ k P X,
    Function.Injective P ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin k), (P i).IsPath) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => (P i).InternallyDisjoint (P j)) ∧
          s ∉ X ∧ t ∉ X ∧ ¬TauCeti.ReachableAvoiding D.AdjHom (↑X) s t ∧ X.card = k
Digraph.exists_paths_vertexSeparator_car.doc:
**Menger's theorem for internally vertex-disjoint paths in a digraph.** Between distinct
nonadjacent vertices of a finite digraph, some family of pairwise internally vertex-disjoint
directed paths has the same cardinality as a terminal-excluding vertex separator.

DifferentiableOn.torusIntegral_prod_sub_.doc:
**The Cauchy integral formula on a polydisc.** If `f` is complex differentiable on the closed
polydisc with center `c` and polyradius `R`, then for every `w` in the open polydisc, the integral
of `(∏ i, (z i - w i))⁻¹ • f z` over the distinguished boundary `T(c, R)` is `(2πi)ⁿ • f w`.

DifferentiableOn.hasLaurentSeriesOnAnnul.signature:
DifferentiableOn.hasLaurentSeriesOnAnnulus.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E] {f : ℂ → E} {c : ℂ} {r ρ : ℝ} {R : ENNReal}

DifferentiableOn.hasLaurentSeriesOnAnnul.doc:
**Laurent's theorem on an open concentric annulus.** Every function `f : ℂ → E` into a complex
Banach space that is complex-differentiable on `Metric.eball c R \ Metric.closedBall c r` (`0 ≤ r`,
`r < ρ`, `ENNReal.ofReal ρ < R`) expands in a convergent Laurent series with coefficients
`circleLaurentCoeff f c ρ`.

DifferentiableOn.eqOn_of_eqOn_re_gt.signature:
DifferentiableOn.eqOn_of_eqOn_re_gt.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]

DifferentiableOn.eqOn_of_eqOn_re_gt.doc:
**Identity theorem on a right half-plane.** Two functions holomorphic on `Re s > a` that
agree on some right half-plane `Re s > b` agree throughout `Re s > a`.

Diffeomorph.restrictScalars.doc:
A `C^n` diffeomorphism for boundaryless models over `𝕜'` is a `C^n` diffeomorphism for
their scalar restrictions to `𝕜`, with the same underlying equivalence. For instance, a
biholomorphism between complex manifolds is a diffeomorphism of the underlying real manifolds.

Diffeomorph.mpullback_cotangent_symplect.doc:
**Cotangent lifts are symplectic.** The cotangent lift of a smooth diffeomorphism pulls the
canonical symplectic form of `T*N` back to the canonical symplectic form of `T*M`.

Diffeomorph.isTopologicalGroup.doc:
Self-diffeomorphisms of a compact Hausdorff manifold with a locally compact model space
form a topological group for the weak Whitney topology.

DiffContOnCl.circleAverage_herglotzRiesz.signature:
DiffContOnCl.circleAverage_herglotzRieszKernel_smul_re_add {f : ℂ → ℂ} {c w : ℂ} {R : ℝ}
  (hf : DiffContOnCl ℂ f (Metric.ball c R)) (hw : w ∈ Metric.ball c R) :

DiffContOnCl.circleAverage_herglotzRiesz.doc:
**The Herglotz formula** on a disc: a function holomorphic on a disc and continuous up to its
boundary is the Herglotz–Riesz integral of its boundary real part, plus the imaginary constant
`(f c).im * I`. Unlike the Poisson formula, which recovers `f` from all of its boundary values,
this recovers `f` from the boundary values of its real part alone.

  (M : Matrix n n A) : D M.det = (M.adjugate * M.map ⇑D).trace
Derivation.leibniz_det.doc:
**Jacobi's formula**: a derivation `D` differentiates the determinant of `M` as the trace of
the adjugate of `M` times the entrywise derivative of `M`.

CoxeterSystem.exists_wordProd_alternatin.signature:
CoxeterSystem.exists_wordProd_alternatingWord_mul_of_isLeftDescent_pair.{u_1, u_2} {B : Type u_1}
  {W : Type u_2} [Group W] {M : CoxeterMatrix B} (cs : CoxeterSystem M W) {i i' : B} (hne : i ≠ i')
  {w : W} (hd : cs.IsLeftDescent w i) (hd' : cs.IsLeftDescent w i') :
  ∃ v,
    0 < orderOf (cs.simple i * cs.simple i') ∧
      w =
          cs.wordProd (CoxeterSystem.alternatingWord i i' (orderOf (cs.simple i * cs.simple i'))) *
            v ∧
        w =
            cs.wordProd
                (CoxeterSystem.alternatingWord i' i (orderOf (cs.simple i * cs.simple i'))) *
              v ∧
          cs.length w = orderOf (cs.simple i * cs.simple i') + cs.length v
CoxeterSystem.exists_wordProd_alternatin.doc:
**Tits' lemma.** If `i ≠ i'` are both left descents of `w`, then `w` splits as a rank-two
parabolic factor times a remainder, the lengths adding, and the parabolic factor is spelled by
*both* alternating words of length `orderOf (s i * s i')`.

Classically the exponent is the Coxeter-matrix entry `M i i'`; the order of `s i * s i'` divides it
(`CoxeterSystem.simple_mul_simple_pow`), which gives the bound
`CoxeterSystem.length_le_of_isLeftDescent_pair`, and the two agree by Tits' theorem on the
geometric representation — see the module docstring.

CoxeterSystem.MinimalCosetRepCovBy.signature:
CoxeterSystem.MinimalCosetRepCovBy.{u_1, u_2} {B : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} [Group W]
  {M : CoxeterMatrix B} (cs : CoxeterSystem M W) (J : Set B) (y x : W) : Prop
CoxeterSystem.MinimalCosetRepCovBy.doc:
`y` is **covered by** `x` in the Bruhat order of the parabolic quotient `W / W_J`, modelled on
the minimal coset representatives: both are minimal coset representatives, `y < x`, and no minimal
coset representative lies strictly between them.

CoxeterSystem.IsMinimalCosetRep.simple_m.doc:
**Deodhar's lemma.** Let `u` be a minimal coset representative for `cs.parabolic J` and let
`s i` be a simple reflection. Then either `s i * u` is again a minimal coset representative, or
`s i * u = u * s j` for some `j ∈ J`, so that `s i * u` lies in the coset of `u`. The second case
can only occur when `s i * u` is longer than `u`.

**The Koszul formula** for Mathlib's Levi-Civita connection
`CovariantDerivative.leviCivitaConnection`, in terms of `TauCeti.Manifold.koszul`.

  [(x : M) → _root_.Module ℝ (V x)] [(x : M) → TopologicalSpace (V x)]
  [∀ (x : M), IsTopologicalAddGroup (V x)] [∀ (x : M), ContinuousSMul ℝ (V x)] [FiberBundle F V]
  [VectorBundle ℝ F V] (cov : CovariantDerivative I F V) [cov.ContMDiffCovariantDerivative ↑⊤]

**The Ricci identity.** For a torsion-free connection `∇ᵀ` on the tangent bundle, the
antisymmetric part of the second covariant derivative of a smooth section `σ` is the curvature
of `∇` applied to `σ`: `∇²σ(u, v) - ∇²σ(v, u) = R(u, v) σ`.

antisymmetric part of its second covariant derivative is the curvature of `∇` applied to `σ`,
corrected by the covariant derivative of `σ` along the torsion of `∇ᵀ`:

`∇²σ(u, v) - ∇²σ(v, u) = R(u, v) σ - ∇_{T(u, v)} σ`.

CovariantDerivative.mfderiv_eq_zero_of_r.doc:
**Einstein's constancy theorem**, local form. Let a metric-compatible torsion-free connection
have Ricci tensor `Ric = a g` near a point `x`, for a function `a`, in dimension other than two.
Then `da` vanishes at `x`.

  [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} {M : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace H M] [T2Space M] [IsManifold I (↑⊤) M]

  (hcov : cov.IsMetricCompatible) (ht : cov.torsion = 0) (hdim : 3 ≤ Module.finrank ℝ E) {κ : M → ℝ}

CovariantDerivative.mfderiv_eq_zero_of_c.doc:
**Schur's theorem**, local form. Let a metric-compatible torsion-free connection have
curvature tensor of the pointwise constant-curvature form `R(w, u)v = κ(y) (⟨u, v⟩ w - ⟨w, v⟩ u)`
at every point `y` near `x`, in dimension at least three. Then `dκ` vanishes at `x`. No
differentiability of `κ` is assumed: near `x`, `κ` is the smooth scalar curvature divided by
`n (n - 1)`.

**Schur's theorem**, global form. If a metric-compatible torsion-free connection on a
preconnected manifold of dimension at least three has, at every point `x`, the same sectional
curvature `κ x` on all tangent two-planes at `x`, then it has constant sectional curvature
`κ x₀` for any point `x₀`.

CovariantDerivative.hasConstantSectional.doc:
A metric-compatible torsion-free connection has constant sectional curvature `κ` if and only
if its curvature tensor is the constant-curvature tensor `R(w, u)v = κ (⟨u, v⟩ w - ⟨w, v⟩ u)` at
every point. Applied to the Levi-Civita connection, this identifies constant sectional curvature
of a Riemannian manifold with the constant-curvature equation.

CovariantDerivative.eq_of_ricciTensor_eq.doc:
**Einstein's constancy theorem.** Let a metric-compatible torsion-free connection on a
preconnected manifold, of dimension other than two, have Ricci tensor `Ric = a g` for a function
`a`. Then `a` is constant.

CovariantDerivative.eq_of_forall_hasSect.doc:
**Schur's theorem.** Let a metric-compatible torsion-free connection on a preconnected
manifold of dimension at least three have, at every point `x`, the same sectional curvature `κ x`
on all tangent two-planes at `x`. Then `κ` is constant.

torsion-free connection `∇ᵀ` on the tangent bundle,

is minus the cyclic curvature contraction with the torsion of the tangent connection. The

CovariantDerivative.cottonTensor.doc:
The Cotton tensor `C(u, v, w) = (∇_w P)(u, v) - (∇_v P)(u, w)` of a smooth connection, where
`P` is the Schouten tensor and `∇P` is `CovariantDerivative.derivSchoutenTensor`. The usual
formula on vector fields holds for a smooth metric (see
`CovariantDerivative.cottonTensor_apply_of_mdifferentiableAt`); otherwise `∇P`, and hence the
Cotton tensor, may be `0`.

`(∏ i, a i) · vol K ≤ 2ⁿ`, where `vol K` is the real-valued volume (zero if `K` has infinite
volume). Neither monotonicity of `a` nor `0 ∈ interior K` is assumed.

Convex.mul_volume_preimage_prodMk_rpow_a.doc:
**Brunn's concavity principle**, extended form: the dimension root of the fiber volume of
a convex set is concave along segments joining points with nonempty fibers. Fibers may have
infinite volume, and no dimension assumption is needed.

Convex.mul_volume_hyperplaneSection_rpow.doc:
**Brunn's concavity principle** for hyperplane sections, extended form. Along a unit vector
`e` in a space of dimension `n`, the `(n - 1)`-th root of the section volume of a convex set is
concave on the heights at which the section is nonempty.

Convex.mem_closure_setOf_ne_zero_isMaxOn.doc:
**The Bishop–Phelps theorem for support functionals**, in Phelps' general form. Let `C` be a
nonempty complete convex subset of a normed space. Every nonzero functional whose real part is
bounded above on `C` is a norm limit of support functionals of `C`, namely of nonzero functionals
whose real part attains its supremum on `C`. No boundedness of `C` is assumed: the support
functionals of `C` are norm dense among the nonzero functionals whose real part is bounded above
on `C`.

Convex.logConcave_measure_preimage_prodM.doc:
**Brunn's principle, in log-concave form.** For a measurable convex set `s ⊆ E × F` and a
measure `ν` with the Prékopa–Leindler property at every weight, the measure of the slices,
`x ↦ ν (Prod.mk x ⁻¹' s)`, is log-concave.

Convex.isClosed_iff_forall_isClosed_inte.doc:
**Krein–Šmulian theorem.** A convex subset of the dual of a Banach space is weak-star closed if
and only if its intersection with every closed ball centred at zero is weak-star closed.

Convex.frontier_subset_closure_setOf_isM.doc:
**The Bishop–Phelps theorem for support points.** The support points of a complete convex
subset `C` of a normed space, namely the points of `C` at which the real part of some nonzero
functional attains its supremum on `C`, are dense in the boundary of `C`. They all lie on the
boundary by `StrongDual.mem_frontier_of_isMaxOn_re`.

Convex.extDerivWithin_poincareHomotopy.doc:
**The relative Poincaré lemma.** On a convex set with unique derivatives, the Poincaré
homotopy operator, centred in the set, of a form closed within the set is a primitive of it
within the set.

support functional `h`, nonzero and with real part positive on the open cone
`{w | k * ‖f‖ * ‖w‖ < re (f w)}`.

derivatives, which need not be open. A `C^r` form of positive degree, `r ≥ 1`, closed within `s`
and invariant under every `ρ g` on `s`, is the exterior derivative within `s` of an invariant
`C^r` form. The primitive is the Poincaré homotopy operator centred at the average of an orbit in
`s`, a point fixed by `G`.

a Banach space whose intersection with every closed ball centred at zero is weak-star closed. If
every element of `C` has norm greater than some `r > 0`, then evaluation at a single point `x`
separates `C` from zero: `1 ≤ re (f x)` for every `f ∈ C`.

positive degree whose restriction to the zero section vanishes has a primitive of the same
regularity, vanishing there as a full ambient tensor. The neighborhood must be stable under
scaling the normal coordinate towards zero.

**The relative Poincaré lemma.** A `C^r` form, `r ≥ 1`, closed within a convex set with unique
derivatives is the exterior derivative within the set of a `C^r` form, which can be chosen to
vanish at any given point of the set. The set need not be open: a closed half-ball, the image of
a boundary chart, is allowed.

Convex.dense_setOf_ne_zero_isMaxOn_re.doc:
**The Bishop–Phelps theorem for support functionals.** The support functionals of a nonempty
bounded complete convex subset `C` of a nonzero normed space, namely the nonzero functionals whose
real part attains its supremum on `C`, are norm dense in the dual. This is the case of
`Convex.mem_closure_setOf_ne_zero_isMaxOn_re_of_bddAbove` in which every functional is bounded on
`C`.

**Brunn's concavity principle**: if every fiber of a convex set has finite volume, the
dimension root of the fiber volume is concave on the projection of the set.

convex set along a unit vector `e` have finite volume, then in a space of dimension `n` the

operator norms `‖T - R‖` over all bounded linear maps `R` of rank at most `n`. The indexing is
zero-based, so `a₀(T) = ‖T‖` (`singularValue_zero`).

On finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces these are the singular values of `T`.

spaces has closed range, then the range of its adjoint is exactly the annihilator of its
kernel.

the gauge of its sum is at most the sum of the gauges, even when that sum is infinite.

`c + g` and that of `B` is at most `c`, then `g ‖X‖ ≤ ‖A X - X B‖` for every bounded operator `X`.

linear operator on `L²(ℝⁿ)` of Hilbert space valued functions whose adjoint `T†` satisfies the
cancellation condition with dilation factor `c`: for every `b ∈ L²` vanishing off a closed ball
`closedBall y r` with integral zero, `∫_{ℝⁿ \ closedBall y (c r)} ‖T† b‖ ≤ B ‖b‖₁`. Then for every
`2 < p < ∞` and every `f ∈ L²`,

`‖T f‖_p ≤ (p · 2 C + p / (p - 2) · 4 ‖T‖²) ^ (1 - 1 / p) ‖f‖_p`,

where `C = 4 · 2ⁿ ‖T‖² + cⁿ + 4 B`. This is the bound of
`ContinuousLinearMap.eLpNorm_le_of_setLIntegral_compl_closedBall_le` for `T†` at the conjugate
exponent `p / (p - 1) ∈ (1, 2)`, transferred to `T` by duality.

**The Calderón–Zygmund theorem** for an operator whose adjoint is given by a kernel, strong
type `(p, p)` for `2 < p < ∞`. Let `T` be a bounded linear operator on `L²(ℝⁿ)` of Hilbert space
valued functions such that `T† b x = ∫ k x y (b y) dy` for almost every `x` off any closed ball
outside which `b` vanishes, where `k` satisfies Hörmander's condition
`∫_{dist x y' > 2 dist y y'} ‖k x y - k x y'‖ dx ≤ B` for all `y`, `y'`. Then for every
`2 < p < ∞` and every `f ∈ L²`,

`‖T f‖_p ≤ (p · 2 (2ⁿ (4 ‖T‖² + 1) + 4 B) + p / (p - 2) · 4 ‖T‖²) ^ (1 - 1 / p) ‖f‖_p`.

Formally, if `T` has kernel `K`, then `T†` has kernel `k x y = (K y x)†`, and the hypothesis is
Hörmander's condition for `K` with the roles of its two variables exchanged.

ContinuousLinearMap.eLpNorm_le_of_horman.doc:
**The Calderón–Zygmund theorem** for an operator given by a kernel, strong type `(p, p)` for
`1 < p < 2`. Let `T` be a bounded linear operator on `L²(ℝⁿ)` such that `T b x = ∫ K x y (b y) dy`

Hörmander's condition `∫_{dist x y' > 2 dist y y'} ‖K x y - K x y'‖ dx ≤ B` for all `y`, `y'`.

`‖T f‖_p ≤ (p / (p - 1) · 2 (2ⁿ (4 ‖T‖² + 1) + 4 B) + p / (2 - p) · 4 ‖T‖²) ^ (1 / p) ‖f‖_p`.

(Pr): the principal-minor series of the extension `i ∘ u ∘ r` of `u` through a retract
presentation `r ∘ i = id` of `M` by a model space `C₀(J, R)`, fixed by choice. If `u` is row

series is `1`.

**Gantmacher's theorem**, reverse direction: an operator into a Banach space whose adjoint is

ContinuousLinearMap.IsRowCompact.rowHodg.doc:

on an ultrametric normed field with `‖x‖ = b ^ (-v x)` for `x ≠ 0`, where `b > 1`. For a
row-compact endomorphism `u` of `C₀(I, K)`, the row Hodge polygon of its row norms lies below
the Newton polygon of its principal-minor series `u.matrixCoeff.charPowerSeries`. When `K` is
complete, these principal-minor sums converge and the series is the Fredholm series
`det (1 - T u)`.

**The Riesz identity at a good zero.** Let `u` be row compact, put `C = 1 - a • u`, and
suppose `ΔʲH_u(a) = 0` for `j < h` while `c = ΔʰH_u(a)` is a unit, so that `a` is a good zero
of order `h` of the Fredholm determinant. Then `b = c⁻¹ • ΔʰV(a)` satisfies
`C ^ (h + 1) b = C ^ h`, that is, `C ^ h (C b - 1) = 0`. This is the identity from which the
Riesz projector `1 - (C b) ^ h` at `a` and its complementary projector `(C b) ^ h` are built.

ContinuousLinearMap.IsRowCompact.mem_spe.doc:
**The nonzero spectrum of a row-compact operator.** For a row-compact endomorphism `u` of
`C₀(I, K)` over a complete ultrametric field and `μ ≠ 0`, `μ` lies in the spectrum of `u` if and
only if `μ⁻¹` is a zero of the Fredholm series `det (1 - T u)`.

the operator `1 - a • u` is invertible if and only if the value `H_u(a)` of the Fredholm series
`det (1 - T u)` is a unit of `R`.

order `h` of its Fredholm determinant `H_u`: `ΔʲH_u(a) = 0` for `j < h` and `ΔʰH_u(a)` is a unit.

`det (1 - T u)` is a restricted power series at every radius.

nonzero eigenvalues. This conclusion concerns eigenvalues in the given coefficient field.

and let its Fredholm series `H_u` be distinguished of degree `s` at the radius `ε⁻¹`. Then the
extension of `u` to `C₀(I, L)`, for a complete normed field extension `L` of `K`, has at most `s`
spectral values of norm at least `ε`.

**Strassmann's bound for the spectrum** over the coefficient field: if the Fredholm series of
a row-compact endomorphism `u` of `C₀(I, K)` is distinguished of degree `s` at the radius `ε⁻¹`,
then `u` has at most `s` spectral values of norm at least `ε`.

ContinuousLinearMap.IsRowCompact.doc:
A continuous linear map between model spaces is **row compact** if the entries of its matrix
are uniformly bounded and its row norms tend to zero along the cofinite filter of output indices.
The bound is automatic over Tate scalars (`ContinuousLinearMap.isRowCompact_iff_tendsto_rowNorm`);
it is part of the definition so that the real suprema defining the row norms are meaningful.

ContinuousLinearMap.IsCompletelyContinuo.doc:
A completely continuous perturbation of the identity is a Fredholm operator, over any
complete nontrivially normed field.

**Bounded Inverse Theorem**: a bijective continuous linear map from a complete ultrametric
seminormed module to a complete normed module over a Tate ring is a continuous linear
equivalence.

the unit cube is the boundary sum of the cofactor pullback `H = L.affineFluxPullback p F`: the sum
over `j` of the integral of `H j` over the front face `u j = 1` minus that over the back face
`u j = 0`. The determinant is signed.

**Scalar curvature is continuous in the second-order jet of the metric.** The scalar curvature
of a coordinate jet depends continuously on the jet at every jet whose Gram matrix is invertible.

ContinuousAlgHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurje.doc:
**The continuous first isomorphism theorem** for Banach algebras: a continuous surjective
algebra homomorphism `f : A → B` induces an isomorphism of topological algebras
`A ⧸ ker f ≃ B`. Its inverse is continuous by the open mapping theorem; it need not be an
isometry.

ContinuousAddEquiv.quotientKerEquivOfSur.doc:
**The first isomorphism theorem for a surjective strict homomorphism** of
topological additive groups: `G ⧸ f.ker ≃ₜ+ H`.

**The Frobenius-Schur reality trichotomy for compact groups.** The indicator of an irreducible
unitary representation of a compact group on a finite-dimensional complex inner product space is
`1`, `0` or `-1`.

The indicator is the difference `dim (Sym²V)ᴳ - dim (Λ²V)ᴳ`
(`ContRepresentation.frobeniusSchurIndicator_eq_sub_finrank_invariants`) and those two dimensions
add up to at most `1` (`ContRepresentation.finrank_invariants_squares_le_one`), so the difference
is one of the three values.

strongly continuous unitary representation `π` of a locally compact abelian group `G` on a
Hilbert space `H` and a vector `ξ`, the matrix coefficient `g ↦ ⟪ξ, π(g) ξ⟫` is the
Fourier–Stieltjes transform of a finite inner regular measure on the Pontryagin dual of `G`.

ContRepresentation.exists_orthogonal_irr.signature:
ContRepresentation.exists_orthogonal_irreducible_decomposition_of_finite.{u_1, u_2, u_3}
  {𝕜 : Type u_1} {G : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3} [RCLike 𝕜] [Group G] [Finite G]
  [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 V] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 V]
  (π : ContRepresentation 𝕜 G V) :
  ∃ e n U,
    (e.congr π).IsUnitary ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin n), (U i).toRepresentation.IsIrreducible) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j =>
            ∀ v ∈ (U i).toSubmodule, ∀ w ∈ (U j).toSubmodule, inner 𝕜 (e v) (e w) = 0) ∧
          (DirectSum.IsInternal fun i => (U i).toSubmodule) ∧
            Module.finrank 𝕜 V = ∑ i, Module.finrank 𝕜 ↥(U i).toSubmodule
ContRepresentation.exists_orthogonal_irr.doc:
**Maschke's theorem in orthogonal form.** A finite-dimensional representation `π` of a finite
group on an inner product space is an internal direct sum of finitely many irreducible
subrepresentations, of dimensions adding up to `dim V`, which are moreover pairwise *orthogonal*
for an invariant inner product `⟪e ·, e ·⟫` obtained from the given one by a continuous linear
automorphism `e` of the carrier.

This is the finite shadow of complete reducibility, and all that is finite about it is the
production of `e`: unitarity is not assumed but produced, by the finite unitarian trick
`ContRepresentation.exists_isUnitary_congr_of_finite`, and the decomposition of `π` itself is then
`ContRepresentation.IsUnitary.exists_orthogonal_irreducible_decomposition_of_congr`, which
decomposes the unitary model and carries every block back along the equivalence of representations
`ContRepresentation.congrEquiv : π.Equiv (congr e π)` for an arbitrary group. The blocks are
therefore subrepresentations of `π` itself.

Distorting the inner product by `e` is unavoidable and is what "Maschke" costs here: Lean fixes one
inner product on `V`, and a representation of a finite group need not preserve it, only the average
`|G|⁻¹ ∑ g, ⟪π g ·, π g ·⟫` of its translates. So the blocks need not be orthogonal for `⟪·, ·⟫`,
and orthogonality is stated for the invariant form `⟪e ·, e ·⟫` that the unitarian trick produces —
equivalently, their images under `e` are the orthogonal family decomposing the unitary model
`congr e π`. It is that orthogonality which the compact theory contributes over Mathlib's Maschke,
which produces complements but no inner product; the plain semisimplicity is not restated here,
being already a Mathlib instance for every field in which `|G|` is invertible.

ContRepresentation.exists_eq_smul_one_of.doc:
**Schur's lemma, scalar half.** Every continuous self-intertwiner of an irreducible
finite-dimensional representation over an algebraically closed field is a scalar multiple of the
identity.

finite-dimensional Hausdorff continuous representations is zero.

Inequivalence is asked of the continuous representations, which by
`ContRepresentation.nonempty_equiv_iff` is the same condition as inequivalence of the underlying
algebraic representations. The field need not be algebraically closed.

ContMDiffVectorBundle.symmetricBilinearM.doc:
When two is invertible, the symmetric bilinear maps on the fibres of a `C^n` vector bundle
form a `C^n` vector bundle.
